'use client'

import type { ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Accordion as BaseAccordion } from '@base-ui/react/accordion'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Accordion.module.css'

export interface AccordionItem {
  value: string
  title: ReactNode
  content: ReactNode
  disabled?: boolean
}

export interface AccordionProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>
  items: AccordionItem[]
  /** Controlled: the values of the open items. */
  value?: string[]
  defaultValue?: string[]
  /** Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string[]) => void
  /** Allow more than one item open at once. */
  multiple?: boolean
  appearance?: 'outlined' | 'flush'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** The heading element each trigger sits in. Match it to the page's outline. */
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6
  disabled?: boolean
  className?: string
}

export function Accordion({
  items,
  onValueChange,
  appearance = 'outlined',
  size = 'md',
  headingLevel = 3,
  className,
  ...props
}: AccordionProps) {
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  return (
    <BaseAccordion.Root
      {...props}
      onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next as string[]))}
      // Collapsed panels stay in the DOM as hidden="until-found", so the
      // browser's find-in-page can reach text inside them and open them.
      hiddenUntilFound
      className={cn(styles.accordion, styles[appearance], styles[size], className)}
    >
      {items.map((item) => (
        <BaseAccordion.Item key={item.value} value={item.value} disabled={item.disabled} className={styles.item}>
          <BaseAccordion.Header render={<Heading />} className={styles.header}>
            <BaseAccordion.Trigger className={styles.trigger}>
              <span className={styles.title}>{item.title}</span>
              <Icon name="chevron-down" className={styles.chevron} />
            </BaseAccordion.Trigger>
          </BaseAccordion.Header>
          <BaseAccordion.Panel className={styles.panel}>
            <div className={styles.content}>{item.content}</div>
          </BaseAccordion.Panel>
        </BaseAccordion.Item>
      ))}
    </BaseAccordion.Root>
  )
}

# Accordion A stack of headings that each show or hide a section of content: FAQs, setting...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as AccordionStories from './Accordion.stories'

<Meta of={AccordionStories} />

# Accordion

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A stack of headings that each show or hide a section of content: FAQs,
settings groups, long forms split into parts.

<Status of={AccordionStories} />

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Default} />

## Variants

`appearance` chooses the frame, `size` the scale. By default one item is
open at a time; `multiple` lets several stay open.

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `outlined` | A self-contained block on the page: an FAQ, a settings group. The items sit in a bordered panel. |
| `flush` | Sections inside something that already has a frame, such as a card or a sidebar. Edge to edge, no side padding. |

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Open} />

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Flush} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | The default: 32px triggers, 14px text. |
| `sm` | Dense panels and side columns: 24px triggers, 12px text. |

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Small} />

| Mode | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Single (default) | Sections a reader compares one at a time. Opening one closes the other. |
| `multiple` | Sections a reader may want side by side, such as settings groups. |

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Multiple} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Accordion } from 'zweihander/accordion'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/accordion.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Accordion.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Accordion.tsx)
- Spec: the kit's own. uiguideline.com has no page for it yet.
- Behaviour: [Base UI Accordion](https://base-ui.com/react/components/accordion)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={AccordionStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={AccordionStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

## Measurements

Each size takes its trigger height from a control tier (Foundations /
Sizing). `flush` drops the inline padding to 0 at both sizes, so the
title lines up with the text around it.

Dividers and the outlined frame are 1px. The title is medium weight (500)
and wraps; the chevron keeps its size.

## Color

The two appearances share their colours; they differ only in where the
lines go. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="outlined"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Divider', token: '--border' },

    { part: 'Chevron', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Text colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Trigger, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="flush"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Divider, and a line under the last item', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Chevron', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Text colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Trigger, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' }]} />

The lines are `--border`, the lighter border for things that are not
controls. The trigger has no fill at rest.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={AccordionStories.Open} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={AccordionStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={AccordionStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills the trigger with `--accent`. A disabled trigger does not
  change on hover.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline. In `outlined` it sits 2px inside
  the trigger, because the frame clips anything outside; in `flush` there
  is no clipping and no side padding, so it sits 2px outside instead.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own: the trigger keeps its hover fill
  while the pointer is down.
- **Open** turns the chevron to point up, and the panel's height animates
  from 0 to its content's height over `--duration-base`.
- **Disabled** dims the trigger to 50% opacity, on one item
  (`disabled` in `items`) or on all of them (`disabled` on the accordion).

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AccordionStories} />
</div>

`ref` reaches the container.

The props are the kit's own, since there is no spec to follow. `items` is
flat, per the kit's "flat props" convention. `value` is an array in single
mode too, because that is Base UI's model and it keeps the type the same
when `multiple` is switched on. `headingLevel` exists because a heading
level must follow the page's outline, which the component cannot know.

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Controlled} />

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Accordion for several related sections that most readers only
need some of: an FAQ, groups of settings, the parts of a long form. Each
title should say what is inside, so a reader can pick without opening
every item.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={AccordionStories.DoRelatedSections} />}
  doCaption="Several related sections, each title naming what is inside."
  dont={<Story of={AccordionStories.DontSingleItem} />}
  dontCaption="One item is not a list of sections. Use a Collapse."
/>

Set `headingLevel` to fit the page: under an `h2`, the items are `h3`, the
default.

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Headings} />

## When not to use

- **For one section.** Use a
  [Collapse](?path=/docs/components-data-display-collapse--docs): a text
  button that belongs to the content around it.
- **For views of the same thing, one at a time.** Use
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs).
- **For content most readers need.** An accordion trades a shorter page for
  an extra click on everything inside it. Show that content.

## Accessibility

- Each trigger is a `<button>` inside a real heading, with
  `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; each panel is a region labelled by
  its trigger.
- `headingLevel` sets the heading element, `h3` by default.
- **Every trigger is a tab stop.** Enter and Space toggle. There is no
  arrow-key movement between triggers, following the current APG
  guidance (Base UI dropped it too).
- A disabled item's trigger has `aria-disabled` and does not open.
- Collapsed panels are `hidden="until-found"`: the browser's find-in-page
  reaches their text and opens the item.
- Triggers are 32px (`sm` 24px), the compact control scale. On touch
  (`pointer: coarse`) they grow to 44px rather than overlapping each
  other with invisible hit areas.
- The open/close animation stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Card, type CardProps } from '../../data-display/Card'
import styles from './ActionPanel.module.css'

export interface ActionPanelProps extends Omit<CardProps, 'title' | 'onClick' | 'render' | 'orientation'> {
  title: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  action: ReactNode
  actionPlacement?: 'below' | 'end'
  variant?: 'default' | 'danger'
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4
}

/**
 * A card that offers one action: what it is, what it does, and the control
 * that does it. The panel is a group named by its title and described by
 * its description, so the control is announced with that context.
 */
export function ActionPanel({
  title,
  description,
  action,
  actionPlacement = 'below',
  variant = 'default',
  headingLevel = 2,
  className,
  ...props
}: ActionPanelProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  return (
    <Card
      role="group"
      aria-labelledby={`${id}title`}
      aria-describedby={description ? `${id}description` : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.actionPanel, styles[actionPlacement], variant === 'danger' && styles.danger, className)}
      {...props}
    >
      <div className={styles.text}>
        <Heading id={`${id}title`} className={styles.title}>
          {title}
        </Heading>
        {description && (
          <div id={`${id}description`} className={styles.description}>
            {description}
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
      <div className={styles.action}>{action}</div>
    </Card>
  )
}

# Action Panel A [Card](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) that offers one ac...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ActionPanelStories from './ActionPanel.stories'

<Meta of={ActionPanelStories} />

# Action Panel

A [Card](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) that offers one action:
a title saying what it does, a description of what happens when you take
it, and the control that does it. For actions that stand on their own on a
settings or detail page, such as exporting data, renewing a plan or
deleting a workspace. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Forms: Action
panels.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/action-panel.json
```

## Simple

A button under the description. The default, and the right one when the
description runs to two lines or more.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.Simple} />

## Button at the end

`actionPlacement="end"` puts the action beside the text, for a short
description. It drops under the text when the card gets narrow.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.ButtonAtEnd} />

## With a switch

A setting that takes effect the moment it changes, so there is no Save
button. Give the Switch an `aria-label` that matches the title: the
panel's title is not its label.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.WithSwitch} />

## With an input

A small form, one field and its button, for an action that needs one
value. The form is yours: the panel lays out what you pass.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.WithInput} />

## Danger

`variant="danger"` edges the panel in the destructive colour, in every
appearance, flat surface included. Use it only for what cannot be undone,
with a destructive Button, and confirm in a
[Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs) before acting. Put it
last on the page.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.Danger} />

## Without a description

The description is optional; several actions wrap onto more rows rather
than overflow.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.TitleOnly} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={ActionPanelStories} />

Every other Card prop and `<div>` attribute passes through, except
`onClick`, `render` and `orientation`: the panel is not itself a control,
and its placement prop sets the direction.

## Layout

- **Below** stacks the text and the action, in the Card's gap.
- **End** keeps the text at least 16rem wide, then wraps the action under
  it, keeping its order.
- The description stops at 65 characters a line; long titles and words
  break anywhere rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

- **With link**: no slot of its own. Pass a [Link](?path=/docs/components-navigation-link--docs)
  as the `action`.
- **Simple well, with well**: not a variant. The tinted inset is the
  Card's look; pick it with `appearance` so the panel matches the other
  blocks on the page.
- **Danger** is added: Tailwind leaves a danger zone to a red button.

## Accessibility

- The panel is a `group` named by its title, so a screen reader names
  it when focus enters the control. The description is linked with
  `aria-describedby`; screen readers differ on reading a group's
  description, so the control's own name must make sense alone. The title
  is heard twice in reading order, as the heading and the group's name.
- The title is an `h2` by default. Use `headingLevel={3}` or `4` under a
  section heading, so the outline has no gaps.
- The danger edge is not the only warning: the title and the destructive
  button say it too, so it does not rest on colour.
- The control keeps its own name: a Switch needs an `aria-label`, a
  button names its action ("Delete workspace", not "Delete"), a field
  has its label.

import type { ComponentProps, MouseEvent, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon, type IconName } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Alert.module.css'

export interface AlertProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'title'> {
  variant?: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'
  appearance?: 'subtle' | 'outlined' | 'solid'
  title?: ReactNode
  /** Replaces the variant's icon; `false` shows none. */
  icon?: ReactNode | false
  /** Buttons or links under the message, e.g. "Retry". */
  action?: ReactNode
  /** Shows a close button that calls this. The alert does not hide itself: remove it when this fires. */
  onClose?: (event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void
  /** Accessible name of the close button. */
  closeLabel?: string
  /**
   * Announce the alert when it appears. `danger` and `warning` interrupt
   * (`role="alert"`), the others wait their turn (`role="status"`). Leave it
   * off for an alert that is on the page from the start.
   */
  isLive?: boolean
}

const icons: Record<NonNullable<AlertProps['variant']>, IconName> = {
  info: 'info-filled',
  success: 'success-filled',
  warning: 'warning-filled',
  danger: 'danger-filled',
}

export function Alert({
  variant = 'info',
  appearance = 'subtle',
  title,
  icon,
  action,
  onClose,
  closeLabel = 'Dismiss',
  isLive = false,
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: AlertProps) {
  const urgent = variant === 'danger' || variant === 'warning'
  return (
    <div
      role={isLive ? (urgent ? 'alert' : 'status') : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.alert, styles[variant], styles[appearance], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {icon !== false && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {icon ?? <Icon name={icons[variant]} />}
        </span>
      )}
      <div className={styles.body}>
        {title && <div className={styles.title}>{title}</div>}
        {children && <div className={styles.description}>{children}</div>}
        {action && <div className={styles.action}>{action}</div>}
      </div>
      {onClose && (
        <button type="button" aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close} onClick={onClose}>
          <Icon name="close" />
        </button>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

# Alert A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes or the ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as AlertStories from './Alert.stories'

<Meta of={AlertStories} />

# Alert

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes
or the reader dismisses it: something went wrong, needs attention, or worked.

<Status of={AlertStories} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithAction} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour, by meaning; `appearance` is the emphasis. Any
variant takes any appearance.

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `info` | Something worth knowing that changes nothing: a plan change, scheduled maintenance. |
| `success` | Something finished and stays true: a domain verified, an import done. |
| `warning` | Something that will go wrong if nobody acts: a card expiring, a quota nearly used. |
| `danger` | Something that went wrong and needs a next step: a failed upload, a lost connection. |

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Appearances} />

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `subtle` | The default. Sits on the page without shouting. |
| `outlined` | On a tinted or busy background, where a tint would disappear. |
| `solid` | The one message nobody should miss, such as an outage banner. Rarely more than one per page. |

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Dismissible} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithoutIcon} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Alert } from 'zweihander/alert'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/alert.json
```

- Source: [src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/alert](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/alert)
- Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={AlertStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={AlertStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Only the description is required. The icon is one line of body text tall,
so it sits on the title's line.

## Measurements

One size. The text is body text, so an alert sits in running content
without a jump in size.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every alert"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-md' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap, icon to text', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Action', property: 'Space above, and between actions', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Minimum hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset (inside)', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
  ]}
/>

The border is always there, 1px and transparent unless `outlined`, so
switching appearance never moves the content.

## Color

Each variant reads four tokens, the same four as a Tag of that variant, so
the two always agree. Subtle and outlined keep the description in
`--foreground`: a paragraph in the variant's colour is tiring to read, so
the colour goes on the icon and the title.

<SpecTable
  caption="info"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--info-subtle' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--info-text' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--info-text' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--info' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--info-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="success"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--success-subtle' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--success' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="warning"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--warning-subtle' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--warning-text' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--warning-text' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--warning' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--warning-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="danger"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--danger-subtle' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--danger' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Description, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

## States

The alert itself has no states. Its close button does.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Close hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Close focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={AlertStories.Dismissible} />
</States>

- **Hover** tints the close button with 15% of the alert's own text
  colour, so it reads on every variant and appearance.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, inside the button's edge.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AlertStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **Placed in the content, not at the top of the screen.** The spec
  describes a prominent message at the top; here an alert goes where the
  thing it is about is. An outage banner is a `solid` alert placed at the
  top by the page.
- **Closing is the parent's job.** `onClose` reports the click and the
  alert stays until whoever rendered it removes it, so "dismissed" lives in
  your state and can be remembered across visits.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Alert for a message about a page or a section that should stay put
until it is dealt with: a failed save, a card about to expire, an import
that finished. The title says what happened; the description says what it
means and what to do.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={AlertStories.DoSayWhatHappened} />}
  doCaption="Say what happened and offer the next step."
  dont={<Story of={AlertStories.DontVague} />}
  dontCaption="“Something went wrong” leaves the red box to do the talking, and the reader with nothing to do."
/>

The icon is decorative, so the variant has to be clear from the words too:
"Upload failed", not just a red box.

## When not to use

- **For news about something that just happened and needs nothing more.**
  Use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): it goes
  away by itself.
- **For a one-line message under a form or a group of fields.** Use an
  [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs).
- **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and
  `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`.
- **For a decision the reader must make before going on.** Use a Modal.

## Accessibility

- A plain `<div>` by default: an alert on the page when it loads is read in
  order, like the text around it, and does not interrupt.
- An alert that **appears** in response to something (a failed save) needs
  `isLive`. `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at
  once; `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait for the screen
  reader to finish.

  <Canvas of={AlertStories.Live} />

- The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning.
- The close button is a native `<button>` named `Dismiss` (change it with
  `closeLabel`). Tab reaches it, Enter and Space press it.
- Focus ring: 2px `--ring` on the close button. On touch screens its hit
  area grows to 44×44px without the button growing.
- Every variant and appearance passes the story tests' contrast check
  (light mode).

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './AppContent.module.css'

export interface AppContentProps extends ComponentProps<'main'> {
  /**
   * A column beside the page for a summary, a status or activity, in an
   * `aside` landmark. From 80rem of shell width it sits to the right and
   * scrolls on its own; below that it follows the page.
   */
  aside?: ReactNode
  /** The aside's accessible name. Give one when the page has more than one `aside`. */
  asideLabel?: string
}

/**
 * The page region of an App Shell: the `main` landmark, as one flat card
 * surface or as blocks on the canvas, whichever the Theme's `contentStyle`
 * picks, with an optional aside column. The shell renders it around its
 * children; it reads the shell's grid and canvas values, so it is not used
 * on its own.
 */
export function AppContent({ aside, asideLabel, className, children, ...props }: AppContentProps) {
  // `null`, `false` and `undefined` render nothing, so they are no aside either.
  const hasAside = aside != null && aside !== false
  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.content, hasAside && styles.withAside)}>
      <main tabIndex={-1} className={cn(styles.main, className)} {...props}>
        {children}
      </main>
      {hasAside && (
        // Focusable: side by side it scrolls on its own, and an aside of
        // plain text has nothing else a keyboard could scroll it with.
        <aside tabIndex={0} aria-label={asideLabel} className={styles.aside}>
          {aside}
        </aside>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

# App Content The page region of an app: the `main` landmark. One of the three pieces the ...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as AppContentStories from './AppContent.stories'

<Meta of={AppContentStories} />

# App Content

The page region of an app: the `main` landmark. One of the three pieces
the [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) template places;
the shell puts it around its children, so you rarely render it yourself.
It reads the shell's grid and canvas, so it is not used on its own.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/app-content.json
```

## Flat

The Theme's `contentStyle="flat"` (the default): one card surface, inset
8px from the shell's edges at every density. Blocks inside are
[Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) with
`appearance="surface"`, which become sections ruled off at the top.

<Canvas of={AppContentStories.Flat} />

## On the canvas

`contentStyle="card"`: no surface; the page sits on the canvas and each
surface Card is raised.

<Canvas of={AppContentStories.OnCanvas} />

## Props

Any `main` attribute; the App Shell passes the `id` its skip link targets.
`aside` takes a column for beside the page, in an `aside` landmark named by
`asideLabel`; the App Shell passes both through
([With an aside](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs)).

## Layout

- Below 48rem the flat surface drops its inset, edge and rounding and goes
  flush.
- The page padding is `--space-container`, `--space-section` from 64rem.
  App Content sets no maximum width: to cap and centre a page, put a
  [Container](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-container--docs) inside it.
- Only the page scrolls; the shell's other pieces stay put. With an aside,
  from 80rem the page and the aside scroll on their own, side by side;
  under 80rem the aside follows the page and they scroll as one.
- The surface restates `--background` as `--card` (flat) or as the
  canvas's solid colour (card), so components that draw "the surface under
  me" match it.

## Accessibility

- The `main` landmark, focusable (`tabIndex={-1}`) so the shell's skip
  link can move focus to it.
- An aside is a `complementary` landmark after `main`, focusable so a
  keyboard can scroll it.
- On a canvas, text takes the canvas text colours (the Theme's
  `canvas-foreground` and `canvas-muted-foreground` tokens); the kit checks
  them for its own canvases.

'use client'

import { useId, useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode, type RefObject } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { AppContent } from '../../patterns/application-ui/AppContent'
import { ShellContext, TopBar } from '../../patterns/application-ui/TopBar'
import styles from './AppShell.module.css'

export type AppShellLayout = 'sidebar' | 'top-bar'
export type AppShellSurface = 'solid' | 'transparent'

/** `null`, `false` and `undefined` render nothing, so they are no navigation either. */
const given = (node: ReactNode) => node != null && node !== false

export interface AppShellProps extends ComponentProps<'div'> {
  /**
   * `sidebar`: the sidebar runs the full height and there is no top bar on
   * wide screens, so search and the account go in the NavSidebar's header
   * and footer. `top-bar`: the header runs the full width above the sidebar and
   * the content.
   */
  layout?: AppShellLayout
  /** The header: `solid` on the card colour, or `transparent` on the canvas. */
  topBarSurface?: AppShellSurface
  /** The sidebar: `solid` on the card colour, or `transparent` on the canvas. */
  sidebarSurface?: AppShellSurface
  /** The logo. The shell places it, in the same spot in either layout. */
  brand?: ReactNode
  /** A NavSidebar. Beside the page at every width; below 64rem it is the icon rail. */
  sidebar?: ReactNode
  /**
   * A TopBar. Above the page in `top-bar`; in `sidebar` only below 64rem,
   * where the rail has no room for search or the account.
   */
  header?: ReactNode
  /**
   * A column beside the page for a summary, a status or activity, in an
   * `aside` landmark. From 80rem of shell width it sits right of the page,
   * as wide as the expanded sidebar, and each column scrolls on its own;
   * below that it follows the page and the two scroll as one.
   */
  aside?: ReactNode
  /** The aside's accessible name. Give one when the page has more than one `aside`. */
  asideLabel?: string
  /** The `id` of the `main` element, which the skip link targets. Generated if not given. */
  mainId?: string
  children: ReactNode
}

/**
 * The frame of an application, a template. It only places three patterns,
 * the TopBar, the NavSidebar and the AppContent, on the Theme's canvas, with no padding or gap of its
 * own; the Theme's `contentStyle` decides whether the page is one flat
 * surface or blocks on the canvas. The sidebar stays put while the content
 * scrolls; on narrow screens it narrows to the icon rail.
 */
export function AppShell({
  layout = 'sidebar',
  topBarSurface = 'solid',
  sidebarSurface = 'transparent',
  brand,
  sidebar,
  header,
  aside,
  asideLabel,
  mainId,
  children,
  className,
  ...props
}: AppShellProps) {
  const autoId = useId()
  const mainRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null)
  const id = mainId ?? `${autoId}main`
  const hasSidebar = given(sidebar)
  const hasBrand = given(brand)
  // The logo is rendered once, in the place it shows: in the NavSidebar's top
  // row for the sidebar layout while the sidebar is expanded, else in the
  // header.
  // CSS alone would need two copies, and a logo can hold an id or a menu.
  const frameRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const isWide = useIsWide(frameRef)
  const brandInSidebar = hasBrand && layout === 'sidebar' && hasSidebar && isWide
  const top = given(header) ? header : hasBrand ? <TopBar /> : null
  return (
    <ShellContext.Provider
      value={{
        brand: brandInSidebar ? null : brand,
        brandCell: layout === 'top-bar' && hasSidebar,
        isNarrow: !isWide,
        sidebarBrand: brandInSidebar ? brand : null,
      }}
    >
      <div
        className={cn(
          styles.shell,
          layout === 'top-bar' ? styles.topBarLayout : styles.sidebarLayout,
          hasSidebar && styles.withSidebar,
          hasBrand && styles.withBrand,
          className,
        )}
        {...props}
      >
        {/* Focus is moved by hand: the browser's own jump would also scroll
            the window, and a generated id is not a tidy URL fragment. */}
        <a
          href={`#${id}`}
          className={styles.skip}
          onClick={(e) => {
            e.preventDefault()
            mainRef.current?.focus()
          }}
        >
          Skip to content
        </a>
        {/* The shell is the size container and the frame its grid, so the
            layout follows the shell's own width: an element cannot query itself. */}
        <div ref={frameRef} className={styles.frame}>
          {top && (
            <div className={styles.top} data-surface={topBarSurface}>
              {top}
            </div>
          )}
          {hasSidebar && (
            <div className={styles.sidebar} data-surface={sidebarSurface}>
              {sidebar}
            </div>
          )}
          <AppContent ref={mainRef} id={id} aside={aside} asideLabel={asideLabel}>
            {children}
          </AppContent>
        </div>
      </div>
    </ShellContext.Provider>
  )
}

/** Whether the element is at least 64rem wide, where the sidebar is expanded (the CSS container query's twin). */
function useIsWide(ref: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>) {
  const [isWide, setIsWide] = useState(true)
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const element = ref.current
    if (!element) return
    const rem = Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize)
    // Measured now too, before the first paint, so a phone never sees the expanded sidebar.
    setIsWide(element.clientWidth >= 64 * rem)
    const observer = new ResizeObserver(([entry]) => setIsWide(entry.contentRect.width >= 64 * rem))
    observer.observe(element)
    return () => observer.disconnect()
  }, [ref])
  return isWide
}

# App Shell A template: the frame of an application. It only places three patterns, the [T...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as AppShellStories from './AppShell.stories'

<Meta of={AppShellStories} />

# App Shell

A template: the frame of an application. It only places three patterns,
the [Top Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-top-bar--docs) (`TopBar`,
with `TopBarNav` for links across it), the
[Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs)
(`NavSidebar`) and the
[App Content](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-app-content--docs)
(`AppContent`, which the shell puts around its children), on the Theme's
canvas, with no padding or gap of its own. The navigation stays put while
the page scrolls, and on a phone the sidebar narrows to its icon rail.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/app-shell.json
```

## Sidebar layout

The default, `layout="sidebar"`: the sidebar runs the full height and
there is **no top bar** on wide screens. What a top bar would hold goes in
the NavSidebar, laid out as in the Claude apps: the logo and the collapse
button in its top row, the tenant switcher and search in its `header`,
notifications, help and the account in its `footer`. Below 64rem the
sidebar is the rail: its header and footer rows stay, as icons, and the
header comes back above the page with the logo.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.WithSidebar} />

## Top bar layout

`layout="top-bar"`: the header runs the full width above the sidebar and
the page.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.TopBarLayout} />

## The logo

Pass the logo as `brand`, not inside the NavSidebar or the TopBar. The
shell places it in the same spot in both layouts: its left edge on the
sidebar icons' left edge, centred in a row as tall as the top bar. It does
not move when the sidebar collapses, and it follows density. In the
sidebar layout the shell hands it to the NavSidebar's top row, next to the
collapse button; a collapsed rail cuts the logo to the rail's width, so lead
the logo with its mark. It is rendered once, wherever it shows. A sidebar
that is not a NavSidebar gets no logo in the sidebar layout.

## Canvas and content style

Two settings on the `Theme`, so a
whole app takes them at once:

- **`canvas`**: what the shell sits on. `plain` (the card colour),
  `neutral` (the page gray, the default) or `tinted` (the accent's subtle
  step). For any other colour or a gradient, pass
  `tokens={{ canvas, 'canvas-solid', 'canvas-foreground', 'canvas-muted-foreground' }}`,
  where `canvas-solid` is one colour standing for the canvas (for a
  gradient, a colour from its middle): components on the canvas use it as
  the surface under them, for a Badge's ring or a Checkbox's fill.
  The kit checks contrast for its own three canvases only; a custom canvas,
  in light and in dark (use `var(--use-light, …) var(--use-dark, …)`), is
  yours to check.
- **`contentStyle`**: how the page meets the canvas. `flat` (the default)
  puts it on one card surface, inset 8px from the edges at every density
  and flush below 48rem. `card` leaves it on the canvas, and each block is
  a [Card](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) with
  `appearance="surface"`, which is raised under `card` and a ruled-off
  section under `flat`.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.CardOnTint} />

Each piece of the shell is `solid` (the card colour, with an edge where it
meets the page) or `transparent` (the canvas, its text in the canvas
colours): `topBarSurface` (default `solid`) and `sidebarSurface` (default
`transparent`). On a `plain` canvas a transparent piece keeps its edge,
since nothing else marks it. That edge keys off `canvas="plain"`: with a
custom canvas from `tokens`, set `canvas` to the preset closest to it
(`plain` for a white one) so the edges follow.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.TransparentOnPlain} />

### Sidebar surfaces

The NavSidebar takes each surface's colours from the shell:

- **Gray**: `transparent` on the `neutral` canvas, the sidebar's own look.
- **White**: `solid`. The current item takes the brand's light tint
  (`--primary-subtle`), since a gray fill on white reads as hover.
- **Transparent on a deep canvas of your own**: a colour or gradient dark
  enough for white text. Beside `canvas`, `canvas-solid`, `canvas-foreground`
  and `canvas-muted-foreground`, the Theme tokens `canvas-hover`,
  `canvas-selected`, `canvas-field`, `canvas-field-border`, `canvas-badge`
  and `canvas-badge-foreground` set the sidebar's fills on it. Dark veils
  (black at 12–24%) for hover, the current item and the search field deepen
  the canvas under white text; a white badge with red text stands out on
  any hue, a red canvas included. On a canvas of the brand's own hue, give
  a brand avatar the `subtle` variant, or it vanishes.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.SidebarSurfaces} />

## Combinations

Of the 36 combinations of layout, the two surfaces, canvas and content
style, 24 occur in real products. The other 12 render but should not be
used:

- no `plain` canvas with `flat` content;
- no `transparent` top bar over a `solid` sidebar (on a `plain` canvas it
  looks the same as a solid one, so that case is fine);
- no `solid` full-height sidebar (`layout="sidebar"`) with `flat` content.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.Combinations} />

## Collapsed rail

NavSidebar's `isCollapsible` turns it into an icon rail that the reader can
expand. The links keep their names, and show them as tooltips; the header
and footer stay, as icons.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.CollapsedRail} />

## Top navigation

No sidebar: a logo and `TopBarNav` links in the header. On a phone the
links stay in the bar and scroll sideways when they do not fit.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.TopNavigationMobile} />

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.TopNavigation} />

## With an aside

Three columns, after Tailwind UI's multi-column layouts: the sidebar, the
page and an `aside` on the right for what supports the page, such as a
summary, a status or recent activity. Pass it as `aside`, and name it with
`asideLabel`. From 80rem of shell width it sits beside the page, as wide as
the expanded sidebar (`--sidebar-width`), and each column scrolls on its
own, so the summary stays in view while the page scrolls. It takes the
page's surface: a second card under `flat`, the canvas under `card`.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.WithAside} />

Under 80rem there is no room for a third column next to a usable page, so
the aside follows the page and the two scroll as one. Nothing is hidden,
but the aside now comes after the whole page, so keep what the reader
needs first in the page itself.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.WithAsideStacked} />

## On a phone

Under 64rem of shell width the sidebar stays beside the page as the icon
rail, and cannot expand: 16rem would cover most of a phone. The links keep
their names, as tooltips. There is no menu button and no drawer.

<Canvas of={AppShellStories.Mobile} />

## Props

**AppShell**

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | `sidebar`, `top-bar` | `sidebar` | Full-height sidebar with no top bar, or a full-width top bar. |
| `topBarSurface` | `solid`, `transparent` | `solid` | The header on the card colour or on the canvas. |
| `sidebarSurface` | `solid`, `transparent` | `transparent` | The sidebar on the card colour or on the canvas. |
| `brand` | node | – | The logo, placed by the shell. |
| `sidebar` | node | – | A NavSidebar. Beside the content at every width; the icon rail below 64rem. |
| `header` | node | – | A TopBar. In `sidebar` it shows only below 64rem; without one the shell adds a plain TopBar there for the logo. |
| `aside` | node | – | A column beside the page, in an `aside` landmark. Right of the page from 80rem, below it under 80rem. |
| `asideLabel` | string | – | The aside's accessible name. |
| `mainId` | string | generated | The `id` of the `main` element, the skip link's target. |
| `children` | node | – | The page, inside `<main>`. |

`sidebar={isAdmin && <NavSidebar … />}` works: `false` and `null` count as
no sidebar, so there is no empty column.

**TopBar** takes `start` (breadcrumbs, or a logo and TopBarNav), `end`
(search, notifications, the account menu) and `children` for the middle.

**TopBarNav** takes `items` (`{ label, href }[]`) and `currentHref`.

## Layout

- **The shell fills the viewport** (`block-size: 100dvh`) and only the
  page scrolls, so the sidebar and the header stay in place. Set
  `block-size` on it to put it in a smaller box.
- **The sidebar sits beside the page at every width.** From 64rem, in
  `layout="sidebar"`, it runs the full height and the top bar is hidden,
  because the sidebar holds what the bar would. Below 64rem it is the icon
  rail and the top bar comes back in both layouts, for the logo, search and
  the account.
- **An aside** sits right of the page from 80rem, `--sidebar-width` wide,
  and the page and the aside each scroll on their own. Under 80rem it goes
  below the page and the two scroll together; below 48rem it is flush too,
  ruled off from a flat page at the top.
- **Below 48rem** a flat page drops its 8px inset, edge and rounding and
  goes flush, since a frame around it only costs width on a phone.
- **Everything follows density**: the top bar is `--control-md` plus two
  `--space-cluster` tall, the sidebar is `--sidebar-width` wide, the page
  padding is `--space-section`. The 8px inset of a flat page does not
  change.
- **Breakpoints are the shell's own width**, which in an app is the
  viewport's. That is also what lets the stories show the phone layout in
  a 390px box.
- **The shell is a size container** (`container-type: inline-size`), so
  it takes its width from where it sits, never from its content. In a
  block it fills the line as usual; as a flex or grid item that would
  otherwise shrink to fit, give it a width (`inline-size: 100%` or
  `flex: 1`), or it collapses.

## Accessibility

- A "Skip to content" link is the first thing in the shell, visible when
  focused. It moves focus past the navigation to the `main` element. Give
  `mainId` when something else should link there too; otherwise the id is
  generated, so two shells in one page (as in these docs) never share it.
- The page is the `main` landmark; the sidebar and TopBarNav are `nav`
  landmarks named "Main".
- The aside is a `complementary` landmark, after the page in reading and
  focus order. Name it with `asideLabel`. It takes focus (`tabIndex={0}`)
  with a visible ring, so a keyboard can scroll it when it scrolls on its
  own and holds nothing focusable.
- In the rail each link keeps its name, so the navigation reads the same
  on a phone.
- The current page is marked `aria-current="page"` in both kinds of
  navigation, and shown by more than colour.

'use client'

import { useState, type ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import type { AccentColor } from '@/theme/palettes'
import { Tooltip, TooltipGroup } from '../overlays/Tooltip'
import { Badge, type BadgeProps } from './Badge'
import styles from './Avatar.module.css'

type AvatarStatus = 'online' | 'away' | 'busy' | 'offline'

// Badge's presence colours, so a dot on an avatar and a dot beside a name match.
const STATUS: Record<AvatarStatus, { variant: BadgeProps['variant']; label: string }> = {
  online: { variant: 'success', label: 'Online' },
  away: { variant: 'warning', label: 'Away' },
  busy: { variant: 'destructive', label: 'Busy' },
  offline: { variant: 'secondary', label: 'Offline' },
}

export interface AvatarProps extends ComponentProps<'span'> {
  size?: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  imageSrc?: string
  /** Who this is. Without it the avatar is decorative and hidden from assistive tech. */
  imageAlt?: string
  /** Shown when there is no image, or it fails to load. One or two letters. */
  initials?: string
  /** Any accent hue. Unset is the neutral gray. */
  color?: AccentColor
  /** `subtle` is a tint of the hue; `solid` is its 600 step (400 in dark). */
  variant?: 'subtle' | 'solid'
  /** A presence dot at the bottom-end corner. Joins the name as ", Online" when there is `imageAlt`. */
  status?: AvatarStatus
  /** The status word in the name, for another language. Defaults to Online, Away, Busy or Offline. */
  statusLabel?: string
}

export function Avatar({
  size = 'md',
  imageSrc,
  imageAlt,
  initials,
  color,
  variant = 'subtle',
  status,
  statusLabel = status && STATUS[status].label,
  className,
  ...props
}: AvatarProps) {
  // Keyed by src, so a new imageSrc gets a fresh attempt instead of staying
  // on the fallback from the last one that failed.
  const [failedSrc, setFailedSrc] = useState<string>()
  // An empty string is no image, not a request for the page's own URL.
  const showImage = !!imageSrc && failedSrc !== imageSrc

  return (
    <span
      // The label lives on the container so the image, the initials and the silhouette
      // all announce the same thing: the person, not "S R" or nothing.
      role={imageAlt ? 'img' : undefined}
      // Children of role="img" are not read, so the status joins the name.
      aria-label={imageAlt && status ? `${imageAlt}, ${statusLabel}` : imageAlt}
      aria-hidden={imageAlt ? undefined : true}
      // The Theme's own palette switch: on the avatar it remaps --primary and
      // its tints to this hue, already measured for contrast.
      data-accent={color}
      className={cn(styles.avatar, styles[size], styles[variant], status && styles.hasStatus, className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {showImage ? (
        <img
          src={imageSrc}
          alt=""
          className={styles.image}
          onError={() => setFailedSrc(imageSrc)}
        />
      ) : initials ? (
        <span className={styles.initials}>{initials}</span>
      ) : (
        // Drawn to the container's edge, not an icon with a margin: the body
        // runs off the bottom and the circle crops it.
        <svg viewBox="0 0 64 64" className={styles.silhouette}>
          <circle cx="32" cy="26" r="12" />
          <rect x="12" y="42" width="40" height="30" rx="20" />
        </svg>
      )}
      {status && (
        <Badge
          isDot
          variant={STATUS[status].variant}
          size={size === 'xs' || size === 'sm' ? 'sm' : 'md'}
          className={styles.status}
        />
      )}
    </span>
  )
}

export interface AvatarGroupProps extends ComponentProps<'span'> {
  /** The people, in order. Each takes Avatar's props; the group's `size` wins. */
  avatars: AvatarProps[]
  /** The most circles in the row, the "+n" included. Unset shows everyone. */
  max?: number
  size?: AvatarProps['size']
  /** The name of the "+n" avatar, for another language. Used only when the avatars are named. */
  moreLabel?: (count: number) => string
  /** Each named avatar shows its name on hover, and the "+n" lists the people it stands for, on hover or focus. */
  hasTooltips?: boolean
}

/** Avatars overlapping in a row, with a "+n" for the ones past `max`. */
export function AvatarGroup({
  avatars,
  max,
  size = 'md',
  moreLabel = (count) => `${count} more`,
  hasTooltips = false,
  className,
  ...props
}: AvatarGroupProps) {
  // The "+n" takes the last slot, so it always stands for two or more: never "+1"
  // where the person would have fitted.
  const shown = max !== undefined && avatars.length > max ? avatars.slice(0, Math.max(max - 1, 0)) : avatars
  const hidden = avatars.length - shown.length
  // Named avatars get a named "+n"; decorative ones (the names are printed) a decorative one.
  const isNamed = avatars.some((a) => a.imageAlt)

  // With tooltips, the "+n" lists who it stands for, and takes focus so
  // that list can be read by keyboard too.
  const hiddenNames = hasTooltips
    ? avatars
        .slice(shown.length)
        .map((a) => a.imageAlt)
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(', ')
    : ''
  const more = hidden > 0 && (
    // ponytail: past +99 the text outgrows an xs circle; shorten the count if a list that long turns up.
    <Avatar
      size={size}
      initials={`+${hidden}`}
      imageAlt={isNamed ? moreLabel(hidden) : undefined}
      tabIndex={hiddenNames ? 0 : undefined}
    />
  )

  const group = (
    <span className={cn(styles.group, className)} {...props}>
      {shown.map((avatar, i) => {
        const el = <Avatar {...avatar} size={size} style={{ zIndex: shown.length - i, ...avatar.style }} />
        return hasTooltips && avatar.imageAlt ? (
          <Tooltip key={i} content={avatar.imageAlt}>
            {el}
          </Tooltip>
        ) : (
          <Avatar key={i} {...avatar} size={size} style={{ zIndex: shown.length - i, ...avatar.style }} />
        )
      })}
      {more && hiddenNames ? <Tooltip content={hiddenNames}>{more}</Tooltip> : more}
    </span>
  )
  // One shared delay: once a name shows, the next shows as the pointer moves on.
  return hasTooltips ? <TooltipGroup>{group}</TooltipGroup> : group
}

# Avatar A picture of a person or account, with initials or a silhouette when there is no ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from './Avatar'
import * as AvatarStories from './Avatar.stories'

<Meta of={AvatarStories} />

# Avatar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A picture of a person or account, with initials or a silhouette when there
is no picture, an optional presence dot, and a group that overlaps several.

<Status of={AvatarStories} />

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Fallbacks} />

## Variants

Neutral by default. `color` picks any accent hue, and `variant` how strong
it is. Behind a photo the colour only shows while it loads or where the
image is transparent.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Colors} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Avatar initials="SR" /> `subtle` | Most places: lists, comments, a byline. A tint that sits quietly next to text. |
| <Avatar initials="SR" variant="solid" /> `solid` | Where the avatar has to stand out on its own: a header, an account menu trigger. |

Colour tells people apart in a list; it carries no meaning. Pick it from the
person (a hash of their id), never from a status.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Sizes} />

### Status

`status` puts a presence dot on the bottom-end corner, in Badge's presence
colours: online, away, busy, offline.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Status} />

### Group

`AvatarGroup` overlaps a row of avatars, for the people on a record or a
thread. `max` is the most circles in the row, the "+n" included.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Group} />

With `hasTooltips`, each named avatar shows its name on hover, and the
"+n" lists the people it stands for, on hover or keyboard focus:

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.GroupTooltips} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from 'zweihander/avatar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/avatar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Avatar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Avatar.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/avatar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/avatar)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={AvatarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={AvatarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

One avatar shows one of image, initials or silhouette, in that order of
preference. A broken image falls back to the next. The status dot and the
group are optional.

## Measurements

The circle ignores the Theme's radius preset: a circle is the shape, not a
corner setting.

<SpecTable
  caption="xs"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-xs' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-sm' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-md' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="lg"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-lg' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-lg' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every size" rows={[{ part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' }]} />

The image and the silhouette fill the circle edge to edge.

The status dot is a Badge dot: `sm` on the xs and sm avatars, `md` on md and
lg. It sits on the corner of the avatar's box, outside the curve.

<SpecTable
  caption="Status dot and group"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Status dot', property: 'Ring', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Group', property: 'Ring around each avatar', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Group', property: 'Overlap: a quarter of the size, md shown', token: '--avatar-md' },
  ]}
/>

The ring is 2px, as on a floating Badge.

## Color

`color` sets the Theme's own `data-accent` on the avatar, so a hue avatar
reads the accent tokens of that hue: switch the accent in the toolbar to see
the values for another one.

<SpecTable
  caption="subtle, neutral"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--secondary' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Colour', token: '--secondary-foreground' },
    { part: 'Silhouette', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="subtle, with a hue"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--primary-subtle' },
    { part: 'Initials and silhouette', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-subtle-text' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="solid, neutral"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--neutral-solid' },
    { part: 'Initials and silhouette', property: 'Colour', token: '--neutral-solid-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="solid, with a hue"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-foreground' },
    { part: 'Silhouette', property: 'Colour', token: '--neutral-solid-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

On `solid` the silhouette is always white, one look across hues; see
Accessibility for what that costs.

The status dot takes Badge's presence colours: online `success`, away
`warning`, busy `destructive`, offline `secondary`. The "+n" in a group is a
neutral subtle avatar.

## States

An avatar is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are
which part it can show.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Image', content: <Avatar size="lg" imageSrc={AvatarStories.default.args.imageSrc} imageAlt="Mary Thompson" /> },
    { label: 'Initials', content: <Avatar size="lg" initials="SR" imageAlt="Sam Rivera" /> },
    { label: 'Silhouette', content: <Avatar size="lg" imageAlt="Unknown user" /> },
    { label: 'Broken image', content: <Story of={AvatarStories.BrokenImage} /> },
    { label: 'Online', content: <Avatar size="lg" initials="SR" imageAlt="Sam Rivera" status="online" /> },
    { label: 'Offline', content: <Avatar size="lg" initials="SR" imageAlt="Sam Rivera" status="offline" /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Image** shows while `imageSrc` loads and after.
- **Broken image** drops the `<img>` and shows the initials, or the
  silhouette when there are none, instead of the browser's broken-image
  icon. A new `imageSrc` is tried again. An empty `imageSrc` is no image.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AvatarStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the container, including
`ref`.

### AvatarGroup

<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AvatarGroup} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the row.

### Differences from the spec

- **`initials` is added.** The spec's Anatomy has an Initials part but
  its prop list has no way to set them. Pass the letters, not a name:
  how to abbreviate a name depends on the language, and the kit should
  not guess.
- **A broken image falls back** to initials or the silhouette instead
  of showing the browser's broken-image icon.
- **No square, no `appearance`.** Always a circle, so a person never
  reads as a product or workspace logo.
- **The placeholder is a silhouette**, not the outline `user` icon: it
  fills the circle edge to edge and takes `color` and `variant` like
  initials do.
- **`color` and `variant` are added**, to tell people apart in a list.
- **The circle ignores the radius preset.**
- **`status` and `AvatarGroup` are added.** The status words and the
  "+n" name are English by default; `statusLabel` and `moreLabel` translate
  them.
- **`max` counts the "+n".** The row never grows past `max` circles, and
  the "+n" always stands for two or more: never "+1" where the person
  would have fitted.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Avatar to show who: the author of a comment, the people on a
project, the account that is signed in. Give it `imageAlt` when the avatar
is the only thing that says who it is. When the name is printed next to
it, leave `imageAlt` out: the avatar is decorative, and the name is read
once.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={AvatarStories.DoDecorativeBesideName} />}
  doCaption="The name is printed, so the avatar has no imageAlt. A screen reader hears “Mary Thompson” once."
  dont={<Story of={AvatarStories.DontRepeatName} />}
  dontCaption="imageAlt repeats the printed name: “Mary Thompson, image, Mary Thompson”."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a product, team or workspace logo.** An Avatar is always round, so
  it reads as a person. Use an image with its own shape.
- **For status through colour.** The avatar's `color` means nothing. Use
  `status` for presence, and print the status where people act on it (an
  assignee picker): a dot is a glance, not the only cue.
- **For a long list of people.** A group shows who at a glance; past a
  handful, show the count or a list of names instead.
- **For an icon in a circle.** Use the icon itself, or an icon-only
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) when it acts.

## Accessibility

- `imageAlt` names the **whole avatar** (`role="img"`), not just the
  image, so the image, the initials and the silhouette all announce the
  same person. The inner `<img>` has `alt=""`.
- Without `imageAlt` the avatar is **decorative** and hidden
  (`aria-hidden`), its status dot with it.
- With `status`, the status **joins the name**: "Mary Thompson, Online".
  The dot itself is not read.
- In a group, the "+n" is named "3 more" when the avatars are named, and
  decorative when they are not.
- With `hasTooltips`, the "+n" is the one avatar that takes focus, with
  the focus ring, and its tooltip of hidden names is its description. The
  other avatars' tooltips open on hover only: their names are already
  their accessible names.
- Initials are never read out: with `imageAlt` the avatar's name replaces
  them, without it the avatar is hidden. They are uppercased with CSS, so
  the text keeps the letters as passed.
- Initials meet 4.5:1 in every colour and variant, on every gray ramp in
  both modes, measured by the `Contrast` story. Neutral solid is gray 600
  under gray 50, 6.5:1 or more.
- On `subtle` the silhouette uses the initials colour (neutral uses
  `--muted-foreground`), past the 3:1 a graphic needs.
- On `solid` the silhouette is **always white**, by choice. In light mode
  that is under 3:1 on the warm hues (orange to lime); in dark mode, where
  the fill is the lighter 400 step, on most hues. It is accepted because
  the silhouette carries no information: the name is in `imageAlt` or
  printed beside the avatar.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Badge.module.css'

export interface BadgeProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'span'>, 'children'> {
  count?: number
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary' | 'destructive' | 'success' | 'warning'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** A dot with no number: "something new", not "how many". */
  isDot?: boolean
  /** Counts above this show as `maxCount+`. */
  maxCount?: number
  /** Pins the badge to a corner of `children` instead of sitting inline. */
  isFloating?: boolean
  floatingPlacement?: 'top-start' | 'top-end' | 'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end'
  /** The element a floating badge is pinned to. */
  children?: ReactNode
}

export function Badge({
  count,
  variant = 'primary',
  size = 'md',
  isDot = false,
  maxCount,
  isFloating = false,
  floatingPlacement = 'top-end',
  children,
  className,
  ...props
}: BadgeProps) {
  const hasBadge = isDot || count !== undefined
  const badge = hasBadge && (
    <span
      // A labelled badge is an image of a state: a plain span may not carry
      // aria-label. An unlabelled dot says nothing, and a floating badge sits
      // outside the element it describes, so both are hidden — the meaning
      // belongs in the anchor's own name.
      role={props['aria-label'] ? 'img' : undefined}
      aria-hidden={!props['aria-label'] && (isDot || isFloating) ? true : undefined}
      className={cn(
        styles.badge,
        styles[variant],
        styles[size],
        isDot && styles.dot,
        isFloating && [styles.floating, styles[floatingPlacement]],
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {isDot ? null : maxCount !== undefined && count! > maxCount ? `${maxCount}+` : count}
    </span>
  )

  if (children === undefined) return badge
  return (
    <span className={styles.anchor}>
      {children}
      {badge}
    </span>
  )
}

# Badge A small count or dot that flags something new on another element: unread messages ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Badge } from './Badge'
import * as BadgeStories from './Badge.stories'

<Meta of={BadgeStories} />

# Badge

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A small count or dot that flags something new on another element: unread
messages on an inbox, a status on an avatar.

<Status of={BadgeStories} />

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Variants} />

## Variants

Each variant comes as a count or, with `isDot`, a dot.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Badge count={8} /> `primary` | The default: new items in the brand colour. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="accent" /> `accent` | Strong and neutral, where the brand colour would clash. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="secondary" /> `secondary` | Low emphasis: a total, not news. As a dot, Offline. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="destructive" /> `destructive` | Something needs attention: failures, overdue items. As a dot, Busy. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="success" /> `success` | As a dot, Online. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="warning" /> `warning` | As a dot, Away or Pending. |

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Status} />

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Sizes} />

`maxCount` keeps a large number from stretching the badge past its anchor.

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.MaxCount} />

`isFloating` pins the badge to a corner of the element it wraps.

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Floating} />

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

import { Badge } from 'zweihander/badge'

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={BadgeStories.anatomyParts}>

The anchor only exists when the badge has `children`. A badge on its own
is just the container.

## Measurements

`md` is the xs control tier (Foundations / Sizing). Both sizes keep a
single digit a circle: the minimum width equals the height. `sm` pads the
count by 2px either side, below the spacing scale on purpose.

A dot has no text to carry it, so it must reach 3:1 against the page on its
own. That is why the `secondary` and `warning` dots step to a darker colour
than their pill.

## States

A badge is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are what
it shows.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Count', content: <Badge count={8} /> },
    { label: 'Over maxCount', content: <Badge count={120} maxCount={99} /> },
    { label: 'Zero', content: <Badge count={0} /> },
    { label: 'Dot', content: <Badge isDot /> },
  ]}
/>

`count={0}` shows "0". Hide the badge yourself if nothing new should mean
no badge.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={BadgeStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the badge, not to the
anchor.

### Differences from the spec

- **`children` is added.** A floating badge needs something to float on.
  The badge wraps it in a `position: relative` span rather than asking
  every consumer to position the anchor themselves.
- **`accent` is the inverted neutral.** The token set has one brand hue,
  which `primary` already uses, so `accent` is foreground-on-background:
  the strongest contrast available without inventing a colour.
- **`success` and `warning` are added** from the status tokens, for
  presence and state dots.
- **`floatingPlacement` defaults to `top-end`**, the usual notification
  corner; the spec gives no default.
- **Start and end are physical** (left and right). RTL pages would get
  mirrored placement.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Badge to say something is new, or how many, on the element it
belongs to: unread messages on an inbox button, a status dot on an avatar.
A floating badge is hidden from assistive tech, so the element it sits on
carries the meaning in its own name.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={BadgeStories.DoNameTheAnchor} />}
  doCaption="The button is named “Notifications, 4 unread”: the count reaches a screen reader too."
  dont={<Story of={BadgeStories.DontCountOnlyInBadge} />}
  dontCaption="The count lives only in the badge, which is hidden: a screen reader hears “Notifications”."
/>

Colour is never the only signal. A destructive badge still needs words
somewhere that say what is wrong, and a status dot needs `aria-label` or
a name beside it.

## When not to use

- **For a label or category.** Use a
  [Tag](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-tag--docs): it holds words,
  a badge holds a number.
- **For a message that needs reading.** Use an Alert or a Toast.
- **On every item of a list.** A badge flags what is new; if everything
  is, nothing stands out.

## Accessibility

- An **inline count** is plain text and is read where it sits. Inside a
  button it becomes part of the name ("Inbox 12").
- A **floating** badge is hidden from assistive tech: it sits *outside*
  the element it decorates, so it would be read as a stray number after
  it. Put the meaning in that element's name instead:
  `aria-label="Notifications, 4 unread"`.
- A **dot** has no text and is hidden too.
- Pass `aria-label` to any badge to expose it as an image with that name
  instead, e.g. a status dot on an avatar: `aria-label="Online"`.
- Contrast is checked by addon-a11y in error mode for every story.

</DocTab>

className?: string

/**
 * Flat rows, one per bucket: `{ time, ok: 120, error: 4 }`. A missing or null value is a gap, not a zero.

data: ChartRow[]

 */
layout?: 'stacked' | 'grouped' = 'stacked'

/**
 * What the legend shows beside each series: its sum, or its latest value (for rates and latencies, where a sum means nothing).
 */

 * Shown above the chart, and its accessible name.
 */

'use client'

import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type ComponentProps, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { useRender } from '@base-ui/react/use-render'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Breadcrumbs.module.css'

export interface BreadcrumbItem {
  label: ReactNode
  href?: string
  /** Replaces the `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link to="…" />`. */
  render?: ReactElement
}

export interface BreadcrumbsProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  /** From the top level down. The last one is the current page. */
  items: BreadcrumbItem[]
  /**
   * Collapse the middle when there are more than this many: the first item,
   * "…", and the last `maxItems - 1`. The "…" expands them in place.
   */
  maxItems?: number
  separator?: ReactNode
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

function Crumb({ item }: { item: BreadcrumbItem }) {
  return useRender({
    render: item.render,
    defaultTagName: 'a',
    props: { href: item.href, className: styles.link, children: item.label },
  })
}

export function Breadcrumbs({
  items,
  maxItems,
  separator,
  size = 'md',
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Breadcrumb',
  className,
  ...props
}: BreadcrumbsProps) {
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false)
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLOListElement>(null)
  // The "…" button is gone once pressed: move focus to the first item it
  // revealed, rather than dropping it on <body>.
  const justExpanded = useRef(false)
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!justExpanded.current) return
    justExpanded.current = false
    listRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('li')[1]?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('a, [href], button')?.focus()
  }, [expanded])
  const collapse = !expanded && maxItems !== undefined && maxItems >= 2 && items.length > maxItems
  const shown: (BreadcrumbItem | 'ellipsis')[] = collapse
    ? [items[0], 'ellipsis', ...items.slice(items.length - (maxItems - 1))]
    : items
  const sep = (
    <span className={styles.separator} aria-hidden="true">
      {separator ?? <Icon name="chevron-right" />}
    </span>
  )

  return (
    <nav aria-label={ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.breadcrumbs, styles[size], className)} {...props}>
      <ol ref={listRef} className={styles.list}>
        {shown.map((item, i) => {
          const last = i === shown.length - 1
          return (
            <li key={i} className={styles.item}>
              {item === 'ellipsis' ? (
                <button
                  type="button"
                  className={styles.ellipsis}
                  aria-label={`Show ${items.length - maxItems!} more`}
                  onClick={() => {
                    justExpanded.current = true
                    setExpanded(true)
                  }}
                >
                  <Icon name="more" />
                </button>
              ) : last ? (
                // The current page: text, not a link to itself.
                <span className={styles.current} aria-current="page">
                  {item.label}
                </span>
              ) : (
                <Crumb item={item} />
              )}
              {!last && sep}
            </li>
          )
        })}
      </ol>
    </nav>
  )
}

# Breadcrumbs The trail from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, each step a ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

# Breadcrumbs

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

The trail from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, each step a
link back up.

<Status of={BreadcrumbsStories} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Default} />

## Variants

Breadcrumbs has one look. What changes is the size, how a long trail
collapses, and what sits between the steps.

| Form | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Under a page title, at body size. The default. |
| `sm` | Dense headers, panels and side sheets, at `body-sm`. |
| `maxItems` | Deep hierarchies, or a trail in a narrow place: the middle collapses to "…", which expands in place. |
| `separator` | A slash or other glyph, where a chevron would clash with nearby icons. |

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Collapsed} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.CustomSeparator} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Breadcrumbs } from 'zweihander/breadcrumbs'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/breadcrumbs.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Breadcrumbs.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Breadcrumbs.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/breadcrumbs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/breadcrumbs)
- Behaviour: a plain `<nav>` and `<ol>`, after the [APG breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={BreadcrumbsStories.anatomyParts}>

</Anatomy>

Each step is a list item: its link (or the ellipsis), then a separator.
The last item has no separator after it.

Breadcrumbs is text, not a row of controls: its height is the line height
of its size.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.StatesExample} />
</States>

- **Hover** turns a link to `--foreground` and underlines it; on the
  ellipsis it fills an `--accent` chip.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the link or the
  ellipsis.
- There is no disabled state: a level the reader cannot open is left out
  of the trail.

## API
