</div>

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Breadcrumbs on pages three or more levels deep, under the page title,
so a reader can see where they are and jump back up any number of levels.
It is a secondary aid: the main navigation still has to get people
everywhere.

Keep the trail on one line. When it would wrap, collapse the middle with
`maxItems`; the first level and the nearest ones stay in view.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.DoCollapseLongTrail} />}
  doCaption="Collapse a long trail with maxItems: one line, and the levels that matter most stay visible."
  dont={<Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.DontWrapLongTrail} />}
  dontCaption="A trail that wraps reads as two rows and pushes the page down."
/>

Write each label as the title of the page it opens, short enough to scan.
The last item is the current page, as text: a link to the page you are on
does nothing useful.

## When not to use

- **For history.** Breadcrumbs shows where a page sits, not how the reader
  got there. For "go back", use a Back link or
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).
- **On a flat site.** One or two levels need no trail; the main
  navigation already says where you are.
- **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper: it shows the steps ahead
  too, and which are done.
- **As the main navigation.** Use a Nav Sidebar or Tabs.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Breadcrumb" (change it with `aria-label`),
  around an ordered list: screen readers announce the number of items and
  the position of each.
- Each level above the current page is a real `<a href>`, in the tab
  order.
- The last item is text with `aria-current="page"`, not a link.
- Separators are `aria-hidden`, so they are not read between items.
- The ellipsis is a button named "Show 3 more". Enter or Space expands the
  trail and moves focus to the first item it revealed, rather than
  dropping it on the page.
- The ellipsis is under 44px; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) its hit
  area grows to 44×44px without it growing.
- Focus ring: 2px `--ring`, 2px offset.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import docs from './docs.module.css'

const BREAKPOINTS = [
  { name: 'base', min: '0', px: '0px' },
  { name: 'sm', min: '40rem', px: '640px' },
  { name: 'md', min: '48rem', px: '768px' },
  { name: 'lg', min: '64rem', px: '1024px' },
  { name: 'xl', min: '80rem', px: '1280px' },
  { name: '2xl', min: '96rem', px: '1536px' },
] as const

// One row per breakpoint; each hides itself once the next one is reached, so
// exactly one is visible and it is the active one. Resize the preview to see
// it change.
const ACTIVE = [
  docs.bpBase,
  docs.bpSm,
  docs.bpMd,
  docs.bpLg,
  docs.bpXl,
  docs.bp2xl,
] as const

function ActiveBreakpoint() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.stack}>
      {BREAKPOINTS.map((bp, i) => (
        <div key={bp.name} className={`${ACTIVE[i]} ${docs.bpChip}`}>
          <span style={{ fontFamily: 'var(--font-mono)', fontSize: 'var(--text-body)', fontWeight: 500 }}>
            {bp.name}
          </span>
          <span style={{ fontSize: 'var(--text-body-sm)', opacity: 0.8 }}>
            active from {bp.min} ({bp.px}) up
          </span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

function Ladder() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.stack}>
      {BREAKPOINTS.filter((b) => b.name !== 'base').map((bp) => (
        <div key={bp.name} className={docs.row} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-3)' }}>
          <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '2.5rem', flexShrink: 0 }}>{bp.name}</span>
          <div
            style={{
              height: '1rem',
              borderRadius: 'var(--radius-sm)',
              background: 'var(--muted)',
              width: `calc(${bp.min} / 96 * 100%)`,
            }}
          />
          <span className={docs.caption}>{bp.px}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

# Breakpoints Five breakpoints, inherited from the underlying CSS framework without modifi...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as BreakpointsStories from './Breakpoints.stories'

<Meta of={BreakpointsStories} />

# Breakpoints

Five breakpoints, inherited from the underlying CSS framework without
modification. Zweihänder declares no `--breakpoint-*` of its own.

| Prefix | Min width | At a 16px root |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *(none)* | `0` | 0px |
| `sm:` | `40rem` | 640px |
| `md:` | `48rem` | 768px |
| `lg:` | `64rem` | 1024px |
| `xl:` | `80rem` | 1280px |
| `2xl:` | `96rem` | 1536px |

<Canvas of={BreakpointsStories.Scale} />

The box below reports the breakpoint currently in effect. Resize the
preview — or use Storybook's viewport toolbar — and it changes.

<Canvas of={BreakpointsStories.Active} />

## They are min-width, and that has a direction

`md:flex` means "flex at 768px **and above**". There is no maximum, so
rules outside a media query are the small-screen case and every
`@media (width >= …)` is an override for larger screens. Write the phone
layout first and widen it; writing the desktop layout first means every
breakpoint has to undo something.

The other direction is expressible — `@media (width < 48rem)` caps a rule
below a breakpoint — but mixing both in one component is where responsive
CSS usually becomes unreadable. Pick min-width and stay there.

## Breakpoints are in rem

`40rem`, not `640px`. A reader who raises their browser's default font
size gets the layout to break earlier, because the layout responds to how
large the text actually is rather than to the device. That is the correct
behaviour and it is worth not overriding: a `px` breakpoint holds a
multi-column layout together long after its text has stopped fitting.

The px column above is only true at the default 16px root.

## The kit has no opinion yet

**No component here uses a breakpoint.** Controls such as Button and Text
Input are inline-sized — they fill whatever their container gives them and have no
layout of their own to rearrange. The stories on this page are the only
responsive code in the repo.

That is expected at this stage: breakpoints are a **layout** concern, and
layout is the [Patterns](?path=/docs/patterns-overview--docs) tier, which
is empty. Marketing sections, dashboards and checkout flows are where
these will actually get used, and where the kit will need an opinion about
which of the five are load-bearing. Most design systems end up leaning on
two or three.

## Container queries are usually the better tool

A breakpoint asks how wide the *viewport* is. A component almost always
wants to know how wide **its own container** is — the same card is narrow
in a sidebar and wide in a main column at one identical viewport width.

Container queries are in every current browser, and they are plain CSS:

```css
.card {
  container-type: inline-size;
}

.cardBody {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
}

@container (width >= 28rem) {
  .cardBody {
    flex-direction: row;
  }
}
```

When a component is built here that needs to reflow, it should reach for
`@container` first and a viewport breakpoint only when the thing being
arranged really is the page.

## Customization

Breakpoints are theme keys like any other, redefined in the `@theme`
block:

```css
@theme {
  --breakpoint-sm: 30rem;
  --breakpoint-3xl: 120rem;
}
```

Two cautions. These generate utility *variants*, so they cannot be
overridden per-scope by `Theme` the way a color can — a variant is
compiled into a media query at build time, and there is no runtime
variable to swap. And removing a default breakpoint removes its prefix
entirely, so any existing `lg:` becomes a silent no-op rather than an
error.

'use client'

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Button as BaseButton } from '@base-ui/react/button'
import { mergeProps } from '@base-ui/react/merge-props'
import { useRender } from '@base-ui/react/use-render'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Button.module.css'

interface ButtonBaseProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'button'>, 'ref'> {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary' | 'destructive'
  appearance?: 'contained' | 'outlined' | 'ghost'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  startIcon?: ReactNode
  endIcon?: ReactNode
  /** Shows a spinner, blocks clicks and keeps focus, so a keyboard user is not dropped. On a link it behaves as disabled. */
  isLoading?: boolean
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Renders an `<a>` instead of a `<button>`: it navigates, it does not act. */
  href?: string
  target?: string
  rel?: string
  /** Replaces the rendered element, e.g. a router's `<Link />`. */
  render?: useRender.RenderProp
}

/** An icon-only button has no text to name it, so `aria-label` is required. */
export type ButtonProps =
  | (ButtonBaseProps & { isIconOnly?: false })
  | (ButtonBaseProps & { isIconOnly: true; 'aria-label': string })

export function Button({
  variant = 'primary',
  appearance = 'contained',
  size = 'md',
  startIcon,
  endIcon,
  isLoading = false,
  isFullWidth = false,
  isIconOnly = false,
  href,
  target,
  rel,
  render,
  disabled,
  type = 'button',
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: ButtonProps) {
  const content = (
    <>
      {isLoading && <span className={styles.spinner} aria-hidden="true" />}
      {startIcon && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {startIcon}
        </span>
      )}
      {children}
      {endIcon && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {endIcon}
        </span>
      )}
    </>
  )
  const own = {
    className: cn(
      styles.button,
      styles[variant],
      styles[appearance],
      styles[size],
      isIconOnly && styles.iconOnly,
      isFullWidth && styles.fullWidth,
      isLoading && styles.loading,
      className,
    ),
    'aria-busy': isLoading || undefined,
    children: content,
  }

  // `href` or `render` means someone else's element — an <a>, a router's
  // Link — whose semantics must survive: Base UI's Button would stamp
  // role="button" on it. Props are merged onto it instead.
  //
  // Disabled (or loading, which a link cannot show) drops the render
  // element too and leaves a bare <a> with no href: removing the href is
  // the only thing that stops an <a> navigating, and a router's Link keeps
  // its own. aria-disabled says why it is inert.
  const inert = disabled || isLoading
  const custom = useRender({
    enabled: href !== undefined || render !== undefined,
    render: inert ? undefined : render,
    defaultTagName: 'a',
    props: mergeProps<'a'>(own, props as ComponentProps<'a'>, {
      ...(!inert && href !== undefined && { href }),
      target,
      rel,
      'aria-disabled': inert || undefined,
    }),
  })
  if (custom) return custom

  return (
    <BaseButton
      {...props}
      {...own}
      type={type}
      disabled={disabled || isLoading}
      focusableWhenDisabled={isLoading}
    />
  )
}

# Button Triggers an action on the current page, or, with `href`, navigates. ## Variants `...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta of={ButtonStories} />

# Button

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Triggers an action on the current page, or, with `href`, navigates.

<Status of={ButtonStories} />

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour, by meaning; `appearance` is the emphasis. Any
variant takes any appearance.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Matrix} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Button>Primary</Button> | The next step: Save, Continue, Create. One per view. |
| <Button variant="accent">Accent</Button> | A strong action in neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. |
| <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button> | Everything else: Cancel, Back, Export. |
| <Button variant="destructive">Destructive</Button> | Deleting, or anything that cannot be undone. |

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Button>Contained</Button> | The action to take, filled so it is found first. |
| <Button appearance="outlined">Outlined</Button> | Actions that matter but are not the next step. |
| <Button appearance="ghost">Ghost</Button> | Low emphasis and dense places: toolbars, table rows, a card's corner. |

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.WithIcons} />

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.IconOnly} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js

```

npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/button.json

- Behaviour: [Base UI Button](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button)

Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). Buttons take the
spacious inline padding: a centred label needs more room either side than
a field's left-aligned text.

Each variant has a solid (the contained fill), a colour on that solid, and

Ghost and outlined have no fill at rest. Contained is lit from above: a
lighter top, a highlight on the top edge, a darker bottom edge and a
hairline border a step darker than the solid. Each is the variant's solid
moved in lightness, so it has no token of its own and follows the accent
and the mode.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={ButtonStories.Disabled} /> },
    { label: 'Loading', content: <Story of={ButtonStories.Loading} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ButtonStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover and pressed** are mixed from the variant's own colours, not a
  token each. A coloured solid (primary, destructive) moves away from its
  label and gains contrast; accent and secondary move toward it. Outlined
  and ghost tint the background with their tone, 8% on hover and 14% when
  pressed. Every state keeps the label at 4.5:1, measured by the
  `StateContrast` story under all seventeen accents in both modes.
- **Hover**, on contained, also draws a 1px hairline ring standing
  `--focus-offset` off the button, where the focus ring sits, so focus
  replaces it rather than adding a second ring. Inside a ButtonGroup the
  ring is left out: it would cut across the next button.
- **Pressed**, on contained, turns the light over: shade on the top edge,
  no drop shadow, no gradient, as if pushed in.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the button.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.
- **Loading** keeps the full colour: the button is busy, not unavailable.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ButtonStories} />
</div>

Every other `<button>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **Two sizes, not four.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`disabled`, not `isDisabled`**: the native attribute keeps its name.
- **`isIconOnly` is added.** The spec has no icon-only button, and a
  square button that still requires a name is common enough to need one.
- **`render` is added** for composition with routers and other elements,
  matching Base UI and shadcn. It replaced `asChild` in 0.8.
- **`accent` is the inverted neutral** (foreground on background), as on
  Badge: the token set has one brand hue and `primary` uses it.
- Outlined and ghost `primary` use `--primary-text`, a step of the accent
  measured to read at 4.5:1 on the page. The solid step would not, for
  warm accents.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Button for an action on the current page: save, submit, open a
dialog, delete. Use one `primary contained` button per view, for the thing
to do next. Everything else steps down to `outlined` or `ghost`, or to
`secondary`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ButtonStories.DoOnePrimary} />}
  doCaption="One primary button: the thing to do next. The rest step down."
  dont={<Story of={ButtonStories.DontTwoPrimaries} />}
  dontCaption="Two primary buttons compete for the same click."
/>

**Loading** keeps the button's width and focus and blocks it from acting
again, so a double-submit is impossible and a keyboard user is not dropped
back to the top of the page.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ButtonStories.Loading} />}
  doCaption="Show progress with isLoading: the button stays where focus is, and cannot fire twice."
  dont={<Story of={ButtonStories.DontDisableWhileSaving} />}
  dontCaption="Disabling it to show progress drops keyboard focus and reads as unavailable."
/>

## When not to use

- **To navigate.** A link is not a button. Pass `href` and Button renders a
  real `<a>`: it keeps link semantics, opens in a new tab on middle-click,
  and gets the link cursor. A plain Button with an `onClick` that changes
  the page does none of that.
- **For a setting that stays on or off.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs), a
  Switch or a Checkbox.
- **For a link inside running text.** Use Link.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Href} />

## Accessibility

- A native `<button>`, `type="button"` by default so it never submits a
  form by accident. Enter and Space both activate it.
- `isIconOnly` needs `aria-label`; TypeScript refuses it without one.
  Icons are `aria-hidden` everywhere else, so they never double the name.
- `isLoading` sets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` but keeps the button
  focusable. `disabled` removes it from the tab order, as native buttons
  do.
- A disabled or loading link renders a bare `<a>` with no `href` (the
  only thing that stops an `<a>` navigating) and `aria-disabled`. With
  `render`, the render element is dropped too, since a router's Link would
  keep its own `href`.
- `render` is for elements that are already interactive: a link or a
  router's Link. It merges props onto the element and adds no role or
  keyboard handling, so do not render a `<div>` through it.
- Hover and pressed keep the label at 4.5:1 too. The `StateContrast`
  story measures every variant × appearance × state under all seventeen
  accents in both modes, from the CSS that ships.
- `sm` and `md` are under 44px; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) the
  hit area grows to 44×44px without the button growing.
- Focus ring: 2px `--ring`, 2px offset, at 3:1 or better on the page.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState, type KeyboardEvent } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Calendar.module.css'

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ plain dates
   Calendar dates carry no time: every Date here is local midnight. */

export const startOfDay = (d: Date) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate())
export const isSameDay = (a: Date | null | undefined, b: Date | null | undefined) =>
  !!a && !!b && a.getFullYear() === b.getFullYear() && a.getMonth() === b.getMonth() && a.getDate() === b.getDate()
export const addDays = (d: Date, n: number) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate() + n)
/** Adds months, keeping the day where it exists: 31 Jan + 1 month is 28/29 Feb. */
export const addMonths = (d: Date, n: number) => {
  const first = new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth() + n, 1)
  const last = new Date(first.getFullYear(), first.getMonth() + 1, 0).getDate()
  return new Date(first.getFullYear(), first.getMonth(), Math.min(d.getDate(), last))
}
const startOfMonth = (d: Date) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), 1)
const clamp = (d: Date, min?: Date | null, max?: Date | null) =>
  min && d < startOfDay(min) ? startOfDay(min) : max && d > startOfDay(max) ? startOfDay(max) : d

/** The locale's first day of the week (0 = Sunday), where the browser knows it. */
export function firstDayOfWeek(locale?: string) {
  try {
    const l = new Intl.Locale(locale ?? navigator.language) as Intl.Locale & {
      getWeekInfo?: () => { firstDay: number }
      weekInfo?: { firstDay: number }
    }
    const info = l.getWeekInfo?.() ?? l.weekInfo
    if (info) return info.firstDay % 7
  } catch {
    /* fall through */
  }
  return 1
}

/** A span of days; `end` is null while only the first end is picked. */
export interface DateRange {
  start: Date | null
  end: Date | null
}

export interface CalendarProps {
  value?: Date | null
  defaultValue?: Date | null
  onValueChange?: (date: Date) => void
  /** The month shown; defaults to the value's, or today's. */
  month?: Date
  defaultMonth?: Date
  onMonthChange?: (month: Date) => void
  min?: Date | null
  max?: Date | null
  /** Rules out single dates, e.g. weekends or booked days. */
  isDateDisabled?: (date: Date) => boolean
  /** Shows a span instead of `value`: both ends selected, the days between banded. Clicks still report one day; the owner decides the span. */
  range?: DateRange | null
  /** BCP 47 tag, e.g. `vi-VN`. Defaults to the browser's. */
  locale?: string
  /** 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Defaults to the locale's. */
  weekStartsOn?: number
  /** Focus the selected (or today's) day on mount, e.g. when opened in a popover. */
  autoFocus?: boolean
  className?: string
}

export function Calendar({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  month: monthProp,
  defaultMonth,
  onMonthChange,
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  range,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  autoFocus = false,
  className,
}: CalendarProps) {
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const selected = range ? range.start : value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const rangeEnd = range?.end ?? null
  const [monthState, setMonthState] = useState(() => startOfMonth(defaultMonth ?? selected ?? today))
  const month = monthProp ? startOfMonth(monthProp) : monthState
  // The day with the roving tab stop, and where the keyboard moves from.
  const [focused, setFocused] = useState(() => clamp(selected ?? (isSameMonth(today, month) ? today : month), min, max))
  const gridRef = useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null)
  const moveFocus = useRef(autoFocus)

  const first = weekStartsOn ?? firstDayOfWeek(locale)
  const fmt = useMemo(() => {
    return {
      title: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { month: 'long', year: 'numeric', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      titleShort: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { month: 'short', year: 'numeric', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      weekday: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { weekday: 'short', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      weekdayNarrow: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { weekday: 'narrow', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      weekdayLong: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { weekday: 'long', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      day: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { day: 'numeric', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      full: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { dateStyle: 'full', calendar: 'gregory' }),
    }
  }, [locale])

  const disabled = (d: Date) =>
    (!!min && d < startOfDay(min)) || (!!max && d > startOfDay(max)) || (isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)

  const setMonth = (m: Date) => {
    const next = startOfMonth(m)
    setMonthState(next)
    onMonthChange?.(next)
  }
  const focusDay = (d: Date) => {
    const next = clamp(d, min, max)
    setFocused(next)
    if (!isSameMonth(next, month)) setMonth(next)
    moveFocus.current = true
  }
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!moveFocus.current) return
    moveFocus.current = false
    gridRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[tabindex="0"]')?.focus()
  })
  // Keep the tab stop inside the month when it changes from outside.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isSameMonth(focused, month)) setFocused(clamp(selected && isSameMonth(selected, month) ? selected : month, min, max))
  }, [month.getTime()]) // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps

  const select = (d: Date) => {
    if (disabled(d)) return
    setValueState(d)
    onValueChange?.(d)
    setFocused(d)
  }

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLElement>) => {
    const dow = (focused.getDay() - first + 7) % 7
    // Right to left mirrors the grid, so the arrows follow what is on screen.
    const ahead = getComputedStyle(e.currentTarget).direction === 'rtl' ? -1 : 1
    const moves: Record<string, () => Date> = {
      ArrowLeft: () => addDays(focused, -ahead),
      ArrowRight: () => addDays(focused, ahead),
      ArrowUp: () => addDays(focused, -7),
      ArrowDown: () => addDays(focused, 7),
      Home: () => addDays(focused, -dow),
      End: () => addDays(focused, 6 - dow),
      PageUp: () => addMonths(focused, e.shiftKey ? -12 : -1),
      PageDown: () => addMonths(focused, e.shiftKey ? 12 : 1),
    }
    if (moves[e.key]) {
      e.preventDefault()
      focusDay(moves[e.key]())
    } else if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
      e.preventDefault()
      select(focused)
    }
  }

  // Six rows of seven days, starting on the week's first day.
  const lead = (month.getDay() - first + 7) % 7
  const start = addDays(month, -lead)
  const weeks = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, w) => Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, d) => addDays(start, w * 7 + d)))
  const weekdays = weeks[0]
  // Two letters where the short names are short ("Mon" → "Mo", "lun." →
  // "lu"); the narrow ones where they are not ("Thứ 2" → "T2").
  const weekdayName = (d: Date) => {
    const short = fmt.weekday.format(d)
    return weekdays.every((w) => fmt.weekday.format(w).length <= 4) ? short.slice(0, 2) : fmt.weekdayNarrow.format(d)
  }
  const prevDisabled = !!min && startOfMonth(min) >= month
  const nextDisabled = !!max && startOfMonth(max) <= month

  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.calendar, className)}>
      <div className={styles.header}>
        {/* Not a heading: a calendar can sit anywhere in a page's outline.
            It announces the month as it changes. */}
        <div className={styles.title} aria-live="polite">
          {fmt.titleShort.format(month)}
        </div>
        <button
          type="button"
          className={styles.nav}
          aria-label="Previous month"
          disabled={prevDisabled}
          onClick={() => setMonth(addMonths(month, -1))}
        >
          <Icon name="chevron-left" className={styles.dirIcon} />
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          className={styles.nav}
          aria-label="Next month"
          disabled={nextDisabled}
          onClick={() => setMonth(addMonths(month, 1))}
        >
          <Icon name="chevron-right" className={styles.dirIcon} />
        </button>
      </div>
      <table ref={gridRef} role="grid" aria-label={fmt.title.format(month)} className={styles.grid} onKeyDown={onKeyDown}>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            {weekdays.map((d) => (
              <th key={d.getDay()} scope="col" abbr={fmt.weekdayLong.format(d)} className={styles.weekday}>
                {weekdayName(d)}
              </th>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {weeks.map((week, w) => (
            <tr key={w}>
              {week.map((d, col) => {
                const outside = !isSameMonth(d, month)
                // Selection and the band stay inside the month: a day of the month
                // either side is only there for shape, and two months side by
                // side would otherwise both draw the days where they overlap.
                const isSelected = !outside && (isSameDay(d, selected) || isSameDay(d, rangeEnd))
                const between = !outside && !!selected && !!rangeEnd && d > selected && d < rangeEnd
                const banded = !!rangeEnd && !isSameDay(selected, rangeEnd) && (isSelected || between)
                const isDisabled = disabled(d)
                return (
                  <td
                    key={d.getTime()}
                    role="gridcell"
                    aria-selected={isSelected || between || undefined}
                    className={cn(
                      styles.cell,
                      banded && styles.inRange,
                      banded && isSameDay(d, selected) && styles.rangeStart,
                      banded && isSameDay(d, rangeEnd) && styles.rangeEnd,
                      // Rounded off where a week or the month starts or ends.
                      banded && (col === 0 || d.getDate() === 1) && styles.bandStart,
                      banded && (col === 6 || addDays(d, 1).getDate() === 1) && styles.bandEnd,
                    )}
                  >
                    {outside ? (
                      // The months either side are shape, not content: hidden from
                      // assistive tech, not pickable, and faded past muted. Arrow
                      // keys still cross into them, by moving the month.
                      <span aria-hidden="true" data-outside="" className={cn(styles.day, styles.outside)}>
                        {fmt.day.format(d)}

                      <button
                        type="button"
                        tabIndex={isSameDay(d, focused) ? 0 : -1}
                        aria-label={fmt.full.format(d)}
                        aria-current={isSameDay(d, today) ? 'date' : undefined}
                        aria-disabled={isDisabled || undefined}
                        className={cn(

                          between && styles.between,
                          isSameDay(d, today) && styles.today,

                        onClick={() => select(d)}
                        onFocus={() => setFocused(d)}
                      >
                        {fmt.day.format(d)}
                      </button>
                    )}
                  </td>
                )
              })}
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  )
}

function isSameMonth(a: Date, b: Date) {
  return a.getFullYear() === b.getFullYear() && a.getMonth() === b.getMonth()
}

# Calendar A month grid to pick one day from, or to show one: a booking page, the inside o...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Calendar } from './Calendar'
import * as CalendarStories from './Calendar.stories'

<Meta of={CalendarStories} />

# Calendar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A month grid to pick one day from, or to show one: a booking page, the
inside of a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).

<Status of={CalendarStories} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Default} />

## Variants

Calendar has one look and one size. What changes is what it shows.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| One day (`value`) | Picking or showing a single day: a delivery date, a booking. |
| A span (`range`) | Showing a stay or a report period. Clicks still report one day; Date Range Picker decides the span. |
| Limits (`min`, `max`) | Booking windows: nothing before tomorrow, nothing after the season ends. |
| Ruled-out days (`isDateDisabled`) | Weekends, holidays, days already booked. |
| Locale (`locale`, `weekStartsOn`) | Month and weekday names in the reader's language, and their first day of the week. |

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Range} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.MinMax} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.NoWeekends} />

The locale decides the week: `vi-VN` and `en-GB` start on Monday, `en-US`
on Sunday, read from `Intl.Locale` where the browser knows it (Monday
otherwise). The grid is always Gregorian, so a locale whose own calendar is
not (Persian) still gets Gregorian days, in its own digits.

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Vietnamese} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Calendar } from 'zweihander/calendar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/calendar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/calendar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/calendar)
- Behaviour: a plain element, using `Intl` for names and the week's first day: no date library
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CalendarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CalendarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The grid always has six rows. Months span four to six weeks; a fixed height
keeps a popover or a page from jumping as you page through them.

Two more looks sit on the days: **today**, an orange disc, round where a
selected day takes the control's corners; and with `range`, the **band**, as tall as a day,
behind the days between the two ends. The band rounds off where a week or
the month starts or ends. Days of the months either side are never banded,
so two months side by side never draw the same day twice.

## Measurements

Calendar has one size. Days are 32px, 4px apart: each cell pads by half
of `--space-1` on every side, so a range's band runs unbroken under the
gap.

    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

Figures are tabular, so the columns of dates line up. On touch screens
(`pointer: coarse`) days grow to 44px, the touch target; the previous and
next buttons stay 32px.

## Color

One table per kind of day. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar:
the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="Header and weekdays"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Month', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Previous and next', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Weekdays', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Day"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Day', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Selected"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Day', property: 'Background', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Day', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Today"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Day', property: 'Background', token: '--orange' },
    { part: 'Day', property: 'Colour', token: '--orange-contrast' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Range"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Band', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Days between', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Today, between', property: 'Colour', token: '--orange-contrast' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Outside the month and unavailable"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Outside day', property: 'Colour, at 50%', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Unavailable day', property: 'Colour, at 60% opacity', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every part" rows={[{ part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' }]} />

- **Day** has no fill at rest.
- **Today's figure is dark**, not white: white on `--orange` is 3.4:1,
  under the 4.5:1 a 14px figure needs, while `--orange-contrast` clears
  4.9:1 in both modes. A selected today shows as selected.
- **Outside days** are `--muted-foreground` mixed 50% with transparent,
  about 2:1. No token is lighter, and WCAG allows it for decoration: they
  are hidden from assistive tech and cannot be picked.
- **Unavailable days** are struck through as well as faded, so they do not
  rely on colour.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CalendarStories.Default} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CalendarStories.Default} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={CalendarStories.MinMax} /> },
    { label: 'Today', content: <Calendar locale="en-GB" weekStartsOn={1} /> },
  ]}
/>

<States states={[{ label: 'Selected range', content: <Story of={CalendarStories.Range} /> }]} />

Each example forces the state on every day at once; on screen it is the
one under the pointer or the keyboard.

- **Hover** fills a day, or the previous and next buttons, with `--accent`
  behind `--accent-foreground`. The selected day and today keep their own
  colours; unavailable and outside days do not react.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the day.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click selects the day, and the
  selected look follows.
- **Disabled** is per day: before `min`, after `max`, or ruled out by
  `isDateDisabled`. The previous and next buttons disable at the limits,
  at 50% opacity.
- **Selected** is the brand fill, with the control's corners; **today** is the orange disc,
  round. With `range`, both ends are selected and the days between are
  banded.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CalendarStories} />
</div>

Also exported, for working with the same plain dates: `isSameDay`,
`addDays`, `addMonths`, `startOfDay`, `firstDayOfWeek` and the `DateRange`
type. Every date is local midnight; times are ignored.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Calendar where the day is picked by looking at the month: a booking
page, a delivery slot, a few weeks either side of today. Rule out the days
that cannot be picked with `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled`, rather than
refusing the choice after it is made.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CalendarStories.DoNearDate} />}
  doCaption="A date close to now, where seeing the week matters: unavailable days are struck through before anyone picks them."
  dont={<Story of={CalendarStories.DontFarDate} />}
  dontCaption="A date of birth is decades away: paging back a month, or even a year, at a time is slow. Type it in a Date Picker."
/>

Month steps keep the day where they can: 31 January plus a month is 28
February, not 3 March.

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.MonthEnds} />

## When not to use

- **For a date far from today**, or one people know by heart, like a date
  of birth. Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs):
  it takes the date typed, and opens this calendar when wanted.
- **For a span inside a form.** Use a
  [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs):
  it owns the two clicks that make a span and shows it here.
- **For a schedule of events.** A day here holds a number, not content.
  Use the [Event Calendar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-event-calendar--docs)
  pattern, or list the events in a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs).

## Accessibility

- A `role="grid"` named by the month and year ("September 2026"), with
  column headers that carry the full weekday name in `abbr`.
- Each day is a button named by its full date ("Friday 18 September
  2026"). The selected cell has `aria-selected`, and with `range` every
  cell from one end to the other does. Today has `aria-current="date"`.
- One tab stop: the selected day, or today when nothing is selected.
- Arrow keys move a day or a week, Home and End go to the week's ends,
  Page Up and Page Down move a month, and Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page
  Down a year. Enter or Space selects. Moving past the month shows the
  next one.
- Right to left, the arrows follow the screen (ArrowLeft is the next day)
  and the previous and next chevrons are mirrored.

  <Canvas of={CalendarStories.Keyboard} />

- The month and year are a polite live region, so paging is announced.
- The previous and next buttons are named "Previous month" and "Next
  month", and are disabled at `min` and `max`.
- Unavailable days stay focusable with `aria-disabled`, so they are found
  and announced as unavailable rather than skipped. Enter on one does
  nothing.
- Days of the months either side are not buttons and are hidden from
  assistive tech.
- Today's figure measures at least 4.5:1 on its disc, in both modes, on
  its own and inside a range.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Card A surface that groups related content: a summary, a person, a setting. ## Variants ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as CardStories from './Card.stories'

<Meta of={CardStories} />

# Card

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A surface that groups related content: a summary, a person, a setting.

<Status of={CardStories} />

<Canvas of={CardStories.Default} />

## Variants

`appearance` is how the surface stands off the page. Every appearance
takes every size and orientation.

<Canvas of={CardStories.Appearances} />

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `elevated` | The default panel: a white `--card` on the off-white page, with an edge and a faint shadow. |
| `outline` | Cards in a dense grid or inside another panel, where a shadow per card is too much. |
| `unstyled` | The card's padding and layout with nothing visible, e.g. inside a surface that already has its own. |
| `surface` | A block of an AppShell page. It follows the Theme's `contentStyle`: raised like `elevated` when the content is `card`, a section set off by a rule above when it is `flat`. See [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs). |

`size` sets the padding and the gap between children, from 12px (`xs`) to
32px (`lg`).

<Canvas of={CardStories.Sizes} />

`orientation="horizontal"` sets the children side by side: media, text and
an action.

<Canvas of={CardStories.Horizontal} />

With `onClick` the whole card is one button; with `render={<a href />}` it
is a link.

<Canvas of={CardStories.Clickable} />

<Canvas of={CardStories.NoBorderSquare} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Card } from 'zweihander/card'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/card.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Card.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Card.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/card](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/card)
- Composition: [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CardStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CardStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The card is only the container. Title and body are your own elements, at
the heading level the page needs.

## Measurements

Each size is a step of the spacing scale, padding on every side and the
gap between children.

<SpecTable
  caption="xs"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-3' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-2' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-cluster' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-container' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-group' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="lg"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-8' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-6' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Content', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Content', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

The border is 1px, transparent when `hasBorder` is off, so turning it on
or off never moves the content. `isRounded={false}` gives square corners.

## Color

Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="elevated"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-sm' },
    { part: 'Container, hover', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-md' },
    { part: 'Content', property: 'Colour', token: '--card-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="outline"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Container, hover', property: 'Border', token: '--control-border' },
    { part: 'Content', property: 'Colour', token: '--card-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

`unstyled` has no background, border or shadow, and its content takes the
colour of what it sits on.

`surface` takes `elevated`'s colours under `contentStyle="card"`. Under
`contentStyle="flat"` it has no background, radius or shadow, only `--border`
along its top edge.

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' }]} />

## States

A plain card is a container and has no states. A clickable or link card
has these:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Hover, outline', pseudo: 'hover', content: <Story of={CardStories.ClickableOutline} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CardStories.Clickable} />
</States>

- **Hover** never touches the surface: muted text sits on `--card` at
  4.5:1 with no margin to spare, and darkening it 6% took muted text to
  3.9:1. An `elevated` card lifts to `--shadow-md`; an `outline` card's
  edge strengthens to `--control-border`, the 3:1 control border. An
  `unstyled` card has no hover look.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the card.
- **Pressed and disabled** have no look of their own. A card has no
  `disabled` prop: a card that cannot act is a plain card.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CardStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **`children`, not `content`.** Arbitrary content is what React children
  are for.
- **`orientation` defaults to `vertical`.** The spec says `horizontal`,
  which would lay a title and its description side by side.
- **`render` is added** so a card can be a link, alongside `onClick` for
  a card that acts.
- **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's tinted card was dropped to match
  the Claude apps, where a panel is a white `--card` on the off-white
  page, with an edge or a faint shadow.
- **`unstyled`** keeps the padding and layout and drops every visual.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Card to group content about one thing, so it reads as a unit: a
person, a plan, a setting. Put headings inside at the level the page
needs; the card has none of its own.

A clickable card is one button, and a button may only hold phrasing
content: use spans for its title and text, not headings or paragraphs,
and put no links or buttons inside it. If a card needs its own actions,
leave it plain and put a button in it.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CardStories.Horizontal} />}
  doCaption="A plain card with its own Follow button: each control is reachable on its own."
  dont={<Story of={CardStories.DontNestButtons} />}
  dontCaption="A button inside a clickable card is invalid HTML, and neither control can be reached reliably."
/>

A card that navigates should be a link (`render={<a href />}`), not a
button with a click handler: a link opens in a new tab and shows its
address.

<Canvas of={CardStories.Link} />

## When not to use

- **For rows of data to compare.** Use a
  [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs): columns line
  values up, cards do not.
- **To show and hide content.** Use an
  [Accordion](?path=/docs/components-data-display-accordion--docs) or a
  [Collapse](?path=/docs/components-data-display-collapse--docs).
- **Just to add space or a background.** A plain `<div>` with padding
  does that without suggesting a unit.

## Accessibility

- A plain card is a `<div>`: no role, no tab stop, nothing added to the
  accessibility tree.
- **A clickable card is one `<button type="button">`, so everything inside
  becomes its label.** Click, Enter and Space all call `onClick`.
- A link card is a real `<a href>`, in the tab order, with no `type`.
- The card has no heading of its own.
- Muted text clears 4.5:1 on every appearance, in both modes, at rest and
  on hover: hover changes the shadow or the edge, never the surface under
  the text. The `Contrast` story measures it.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './CardHeading.module.css'

export interface CardHeadingProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'title'> {
  title: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  media?: ReactNode
  actions?: ReactNode
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4
}

/**
 * The top row of a card: what it is, and what you can do with it. Put it
 * first inside a Card; the card's padding and gap space it.
 */
export function CardHeading({
  title,
  description,
  media,
  actions,
  headingLevel = 2,
  className,
  ...props
}: CardHeadingProps) {
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.cardHeading, className)} {...props}>
      <div className={styles.lead}>
        {media && (
          <span className={styles.media} aria-hidden="true">
            {media}
          </span>
        )}
        <div className={styles.text}>
          <Heading className={styles.title}>{title}</Heading>
          {description && <p className={styles.description}>{description}</p>}
        </div>
      </div>
      {actions && <div className={styles.actions}>{actions}</div>}
    </div>
  )
}

import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as CardHeadingStories from './CardHeading.stories'

<Meta of={CardHeadingStories} />

# Card Heading

The top row of a card: what the card is, a line of context, and what you
can do with it. Put it first inside a [Card](?path=/docs/data-display-card--docs);
the card's padding and gap space it from the content. After Tailwind UI
Application UI, Headings: Card headings.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/card-heading.json
```

## Simple

A title and, optionally, one line of description.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.Simple} />

## With action

The card's main action at the end of the title row. One primary button at
most; a card is part of a page that has its own primary action.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.WithAction} />

## With avatar and menu

Who or what the card is about, as an Avatar or an Icon before the title.
Rarely used actions go in a Menu behind "More actions" so the row stays
short.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.WithAvatarAndMenu} />

## With a rule

The heading draws no line of its own. When the content needs setting off,
put a [Divider](?path=/docs/atomic-elements-divider--docs) after the heading,
inside the card.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.WithIconAndRule} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={CardHeadingStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **Actions wrap, the title does not squeeze.** The title and description
  keep the row down to 16rem, then the actions drop underneath them,
  keeping their order.
- **Long titles break anywhere** rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- The title is an `h2` by default: a card on a page sits under the
  page's `h1`. Use `headingLevel={3}` or `4` when the card sits under a
  section heading, so the outline has no gaps.
- The media is decorative and hidden from assistive tech: the title
  already says who or what the card is about.
- An icon-only action needs an `aria-label`, as on any Button. When a card
  repeats on a page, make action names unique, e.g. "Edit Chelsea Hagon".

import { Children, useCallback, useEffect, useId, useRef, useState, useSyncExternalStore, type CSSProperties, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Carousel.module.css'

export interface CarouselProps {
  /** One child per slide. */
  children: ReactNode
  /** Names the carousel, e.g. "Featured templates". Required: there may be several on a page. */
  label: string
  /** Slides in view at once. */
  slidesPerView?: number
  /** Show a dot per slide under the track. */
  showDots?: boolean
  /** Advance every this many milliseconds. Paused on hover and focus, and never under reduced motion. */
  autoPlay?: number
  /** Previous/next wrap around at the ends. */
  loop?: boolean
  index?: number
  defaultIndex?: number
  onIndexChange?: (index: number) => void
  className?: string
}

// Measured from the first slide, not the track: offsetLeft counts from the
// offset parent, and in right-to-left the distances (and scrollLeft) are negative.
const offsetOf = (track: HTMLElement, slide: HTMLElement) => slide.offsetLeft - (track.children[0] as HTMLElement).offsetLeft

const motionQuery = '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'
const prefersReducedMotion = () => window.matchMedia(motionQuery).matches
const subscribeMotion = (onChange: () => void) => {
  const query = window.matchMedia(motionQuery)
  query.addEventListener('change', onChange)
  return () => query.removeEventListener('change', onChange)
}

export function Carousel({
  children,
  label,
  slidesPerView = 1,
  showDots = true,
  autoPlay,
  loop = false,
  index: indexProp,
  defaultIndex = 0,
  onIndexChange,
  className,
}: CarouselProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const slides = Children.toArray(children)
  const count = slides.length
  const last = Math.max(0, count - slidesPerView)
  const trackRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const [indexState, setIndexState] = useState(defaultIndex)
  const index = Math.min(indexProp ?? indexState, last)
  const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(autoPlay !== undefined)
  const [paused, setPaused] = useState(false)
  const reducedMotion = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeMotion, prefersReducedMotion, () => false)

  const report = useCallback(
    (next: number) => {
      setIndexState(next)
      onIndexChange?.(next)
    },
    [onIndexChange],
  )

  // Where a scroll this component started is headed. A press mid-scroll
  // interrupts the old smooth scroll, and Firefox fires scrollend for it where
  // it stopped; reading that would report a slide nobody asked for.
  const heading = useRef<number | null>(null)
  const scrollTrack = useCallback(
    (track: HTMLElement, to: number) => {
      const slide = track.children[to] as HTMLElement | undefined
      if (!slide) return
      heading.current = to
      track.scrollTo({ left: offsetOf(track, slide), behavior: reducedMotion ? 'auto' : 'smooth' })
    },
    [reducedMotion],
  )
  // The reader taking over (swipe, wheel, arrow keys) ends the wait.
  const letGo = () => {
    heading.current = null
  }

  const goTo = useCallback(
    (next: number) => {
      const target = loop ? (next + last + 1) % (last + 1) : Math.min(Math.max(next, 0), last)
      if (trackRef.current) scrollTrack(trackRef.current, target)
      report(target)
    },
    [last, loop, report, scrollTrack],
  )

  // Swipes and trackpad scrolls move the track directly; read the index back
  // once it comes to rest. Reading it mid-scroll would report every slide a
  // smooth scroll passes, including the one it started from.
  const settle = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(undefined)
  useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(settle.current), [])
  // scrollend where the browser has it: Firefox pauses longer than 100ms
  // between the events of one smooth scroll, so the timer read a slide mid-way.
  // Safari has no scrollend and keeps the timer.
  const hasScrollEnd = typeof window !== 'undefined' && 'onscrollend' in window
  const onScroll = () => {
    if (hasScrollEnd) return
    clearTimeout(settle.current)
    settle.current = setTimeout(readIndex, 100)
  }
  const readIndex = () => {
    const track = trackRef.current
    if (!track) return
    const first = track.children[0] as HTMLElement | undefined
    if (!first) return
    const step = first.getBoundingClientRect().width + parseFloat(getComputedStyle(track).columnGap || '0')
    const next = Math.min(last, Math.max(0, Math.round(Math.abs(track.scrollLeft) / step)))
    if (heading.current !== null) {
      if (next !== heading.current) return
      heading.current = null
    }
    if (next !== index) report(next)
  }

  // Start at defaultIndex (or a controlled index) without animating there.
  const placed = useRef(false)
  useEffect(() => {
    if (placed.current) return
    placed.current = true
    const track = trackRef.current
    const slide = track?.children[index] as HTMLElement | undefined
    if (track && slide && index > 0) track.scrollTo({ left: offsetOf(track, slide), behavior: 'auto' })
  }, [index])

  // A controlled index that changes from outside scrolls the track.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (indexProp === undefined) return
    const track = trackRef.current
    const slide = track?.children[index] as HTMLElement | undefined
    if (track && slide && Math.abs(track.scrollLeft - offsetOf(track, slide)) > 1) scrollTrack(track, index)
  }, [indexProp, index, scrollTrack])

  const rotating = autoPlay !== undefined && playing && !paused && !reducedMotion
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!rotating) return
    const timer = setInterval(() => goTo(index >= last ? 0 : index + 1), autoPlay)
    return () => clearInterval(timer)
  }, [rotating, autoPlay, index, last, goTo])

  return (
    <section
      aria-roledescription="carousel"
      aria-label={label}
      className={cn(styles.carousel, className)}
      style={{ '--carousel-per-view': slidesPerView } as CSSProperties}
      onMouseEnter={() => setPaused(true)}
      onMouseLeave={() => setPaused(false)}
      onFocus={() => setPaused(true)}
      onBlur={(e) => {
        if (!e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget as Node)) setPaused(false)
      }}
    >
      <div className={styles.controls}>
        {autoPlay !== undefined && (
          <button
            type="button"
            className={styles.button}
            aria-label={playing ? 'Stop automatic slide show' : 'Start automatic slide show'}
            onClick={() => setPlaying(!playing)}
          >
            <Icon name={playing ? 'pause' : 'play'} />
          </button>
        )}
        <button
          type="button"
          className={styles.button}
          aria-label="Previous slide"
          aria-controls={`${id}-track`}
          disabled={!loop && index === 0}
          onClick={() => goTo(index - 1)}
        >
          <Icon name="chevron-left" className={styles.dirIcon} />
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          className={styles.button}
          aria-label="Next slide"
          aria-controls={`${id}-track`}
          disabled={!loop && index >= last}
          onClick={() => goTo(index + 1)}
        >
          <Icon name="chevron-right" className={styles.dirIcon} />
        </button>
      </div>
      <div
        id={`${id}-track`}
        ref={trackRef}
        className={styles.track}
        // Focusable so arrow keys scroll it, like any scrolling region.
        tabIndex={0}
        onScroll={onScroll}
        onPointerDown={letGo}
        onWheel={letGo}
        onKeyDown={letGo}
        onScrollEnd={hasScrollEnd ? readIndex : undefined}
      >
        {slides.map((slide, i) => (
          <div
            key={i}
            role="group"
            aria-roledescription="slide"
            aria-label={`${i + 1} of ${count}`}
            className={styles.slide}
          >
            {slide}
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
      {/* Every slide is always in the DOM, so a live region round the track
          would never change. This line does: polite while the reader drives
          it, silent while it rotates on its own. */}
      <p className={styles.srOnly} aria-live={rotating ? 'off' : 'polite'} aria-atomic="true">
        {slidesPerView > 1
          ? `Slides ${index + 1} to ${Math.min(index + slidesPerView, count)} of ${count}`
          : `Slide ${index + 1} of ${count}`}
      </p>
      {showDots && last > 0 && (
        <div className={styles.dots}>
          {Array.from({ length: last + 1 }, (_, i) => (
            <button
              key={i}
              type="button"
              className={cn(styles.dot, i === index && styles.dotActive)}
              aria-label={`Slide ${i + 1}`}
              aria-current={i === index ? 'true' : undefined}
              aria-controls={`${id}-track`}
              onClick={() => goTo(i)}
            />
          ))}
        </div>
      )}
    </section>
  )
}

# Carousel A row of slides seen one (or a few) at a time: featured items, a gallery, onboa...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as CarouselStories from './Carousel.stories'

<Meta of={CarouselStories} />

# Carousel

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A row of slides seen one (or a few) at a time: featured items, a gallery,
onboarding cards.

<Status of={CarouselStories} />

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Default} />

## Variants

The carousel has no `variant` prop. These are its configurations:

| Configuration | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| One in view (default) | Large slides that each need the full width: a feature, a photo. |
| `slidesPerView={3}` | Smaller items browsed in a row: templates, products. |
| `loop` | A short set with no natural first or last, where next from the end should wrap. |
| `autoPlay` | Rarely. A showcase where motion is the point; it adds a stop/start button. |

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.ThreeInView} />

With three in view, five slides have three stops (1-3, 2-4, 3-5), and the
dots count stops, not slides.

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Loop} />

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.AutoPlay} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Carousel } from 'zweihander/carousel'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/carousel.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Carousel.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Carousel.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/carousel](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/carousel)
- Behaviour: [WAI-ARIA carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CarouselStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CarouselStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The controls sit above the track, at its end, so they never cover a slide.
A visually hidden line after the track says where the reader is (see
Accessibility).

- **Native scrolling.** No transform maths and no gesture library: the
  track is `overflow-x: auto` with `scroll-snap-type`, so touch, trackpad
  and momentum behave as the platform does. The index is read back once
  the track comes to rest.
- **Right to left works.** Offsets are measured from the first slide, so
  the negative `scrollLeft` of a right-to-left track reads correctly, and
  the previous and next chevrons are mirrored.
- **`defaultIndex` starts there.** The track jumps to it on mount, without
  a scroll animation.

## Measurements

There is one size. Slide width follows from the carousel's width,
`slidesPerView` and the gap between slides.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every carousel"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Carousel', property: 'Gap between controls, track and dots', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Gap between slides', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Controls', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-8' },
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Dots', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Current dot', property: 'Width', token: '--space-6' },
    { part: 'Dot', property: 'Hit area', token: '--space-6' },
    { part: 'Button and dot', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

A dot is 6px round (1.5 × `--space-1`); the current one stretches to a
24px pill. Buttons have a 1px border.

## Color

The carousel has no variants: one table. Slides bring their own colours.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every carousel"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Icon colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Border', token: '--control-border' },
    { part: 'Button, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Button, hover', property: 'Icon colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Dot', property: 'Background', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Current dot', property: 'Background', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled, first stop' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Current slide 3', content: <Story of={CarouselStories.StartAtThird} /> },
    { label: 'Last stop', content: <Story of={CarouselStories.AtEnd} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CarouselStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills an enabled button with `--accent` and its icon with
  `--accent-foreground`. Dots have no hover look.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the track, a button or a
  dot.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own.
- **Disabled**: previous at the first stop and next at the last, unless
  `loop`. A disabled button is the enabled look at 50% opacity, with the
  disabled cursor and no hover.
- **Current slide**: the current stop's dot is the longer `--foreground`
  pill.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CarouselStories} />
</div>

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Everything in a carousel past the first slide is hidden until the reader
goes looking. Use one for content that is fine to miss: featured items,
examples, a gallery. Give it a `label` that names what is in it.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CarouselStories.Default} />}
  doCaption="Featured templates: browsing is optional, and missing one costs nothing."
  dont={<Story of={CarouselStories.DontHideImportant} />}
  dontCaption="Account notices the reader must act on, four of them hidden in slides most readers never reach."
/>

Prefer no `autoPlay`. Motion pulls the eye away from the rest of the page,
and a slide can move on before it has been read.

## When not to use

- **For content everyone must see.** Show it at once: a list, or
  [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) in a grid, show
  more and hide nothing.
- **For items to compare.** Use a
  [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs): side by side
  beats one at a time.
- **For steps in a flow.** Use a
  [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs): it shows how
  many steps there are and where you are.

## Accessibility

Follows the [WAI-ARIA carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/).

- A `<section>` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and your `label`;
  each slide is a group with `aria-roledescription="slide"` and a name
  like "2 of 5".
- Previous, next, stop/start and the dots are native buttons: Tab reaches
  them, Enter and Space press them.
- Previous and next are disabled at the ends unless `loop`. Dots are
  buttons named "Slide 3", with `aria-current` on the current stop.
- **Autoplay** (WCAG 2.2.2) pauses while the pointer is over the carousel
  or focus is inside it, has a stop/start button as its first control, and
  never runs under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- A visually hidden line says where you are ("Slide 3 of 5", or "Slides
  3 to 5 of 5"). It is `aria-live="polite"` when the reader moves the
  carousel, so a screen reader hears the change, and `off` while it
  rotates on its own. Every slide is in the DOM from the start, so a live
  region round the track would stay silent.
- The track is in the tab order (`tabindex="0"`), like any scrolling
  region.
- In right to left, the previous and next chevrons are mirrored.
- Buttons and dots have 44px touch targets on coarse pointers.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { CSSProperties } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Chart.module.css'

export interface ChartLegendItem {
  key: string
  label: string
  /** A CSS colour, usually from `colorVar`. */
  color: string
  /** Shown after the label, e.g. the series total "2.56K". */
  value?: string
}

export interface ChartLegendProps {
  items: ChartLegendItem[]
  /** Keys of series that are switched off. */
  hiddenKeys?: string[]
  /** Makes each item a toggle button. Without it the legend is a plain list. */
  onToggle?: (key: string) => void
  /** Called with the key under the pointer or focus, null when it leaves. Charts use it to fade the other series. */
  onFocusChange?: (key: string | null) => void
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  className?: string
}

/** Swatch, label and value per series. As toggles, it shows and hides series in the chart above it. */
export function ChartLegend({ items, hiddenKeys = [], onToggle, onFocusChange, orientation = 'horizontal', className }: ChartLegendProps) {
  const visibleCount = items.length - hiddenKeys.length
  return (
    <ul
      className={cn(styles.legend, orientation === 'vertical' && styles.legendVertical, className)}
      aria-label="Legend"
      onPointerLeave={() => onFocusChange?.(null)}
    >
      {items.map((item) => {
        const isHidden = hiddenKeys.includes(item.key)
        const content = (
          <>
            <span className={styles.swatch} style={{ '--swatch': item.color } as CSSProperties} aria-hidden="true" />
            <span className={styles.legendLabel}>{item.label}</span>
            {item.value !== undefined && <span className={styles.legendValue}>{item.value}</span>}
          </>
        )
        const focus = () => onFocusChange?.(isHidden ? null : item.key)
        const blur = () => onFocusChange?.(null)
        return (
          <li key={item.key} onPointerEnter={focus}>
            {onToggle ? (
              <button
                type="button"
                className={styles.legendItem}
                aria-pressed={!isHidden}
                // The last visible series cannot be hidden: an empty chart reads as "no data".
                aria-disabled={!isHidden && visibleCount === 1 ? true : undefined}
                onClick={() => (!isHidden && visibleCount === 1 ? undefined : onToggle(item.key))}
                onFocus={focus}
                onBlur={blur}
              >
                {content}
              </button>
            ) : (
              <span className={styles.legendItem}>{content}</span>
            )}
          </li>
        )
      })}
    </ul>
  )
}

'use client'

import { useCallback, useRef, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react'
import { Checkbox as BaseCheckbox } from '@base-ui/react/checkbox'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { ChoiceField, choiceStyles, type ValidationState } from './ChoiceField'
import styles from './Checkbox.module.css'

export interface CheckboxProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>
  checked?: boolean
  defaultChecked?: boolean
  /** The spec's `onChange`. Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean) => void
  /** Neither checked nor unchecked: a "select all" with some selected. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  name?: string
  /** Submitted when checked; "on" by default. */
  value?: string
  /** Colour of the checked box. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'neutral'
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  autoFocus?: boolean
  validationState?: ValidationState
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

export function Checkbox({
  ref,
  autoFocus,
  label,
  helperText,
  name,
  variant = 'neutral',
  isIndeterminate,
  disabled,
  required,
  validationState,
  className,
  onCheckedChange,
  ...props
}: CheckboxProps) {
  // The root is a focusable <span>, and React only honours autoFocus on form
  // elements, so it is done by hand — once, on mount, not on every render.
  const focused = useRef(false)
  const setRef = useCallback(
    (node: HTMLElement | null) => {
      if (node && autoFocus && !focused.current) {
        focused.current = true
        node.focus()
      }
      if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(node)
      else if (ref) ref.current = node
    },
    [autoFocus, ref],
  )
  return (
    <ChoiceField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      className={cn(styles.field, className)}
    >
      <BaseCheckbox.Root
        {...props}
        ref={setRef}
        indeterminate={isIndeterminate}
        required={required}
        onCheckedChange={onCheckedChange && ((next) => onCheckedChange(next))}
        className={cn(choiceStyles.control, styles.box, styles[variant])}
      >
        <BaseCheckbox.Indicator
          className={styles.indicator}
          render={(indicatorProps, state) => (
            <span {...indicatorProps}>
              <Icon name={state.indeterminate ? 'minus' : 'check'} />
            </span>
          )}
        />
      </BaseCheckbox.Root>
    </ChoiceField>
  )
}

# Checkbox Selects an option, or several from a list, to apply when a form is submitted. #...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Checkbox } from './Checkbox'
import * as CheckboxStories from './Checkbox.stories'

<Meta of={CheckboxStories} />

# Checkbox

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Selects an option, or several from a list, to apply when a form is
submitted.

<Status of={CheckboxStories} />

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the checked box. Each row: unchecked, checked,
indeterminate.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Checkbox defaultChecked label="Neutral" /> | The default: lists, forms, tables. The checked box is the foreground colour, so a column of them stays calm. |
| <Checkbox variant="primary" defaultChecked label="Primary" /> | One checkbox that carries the brand: an opt-in, a terms box beside a primary button. |

**Indeterminate** is for a parent whose children are partly selected. It
is a display state: clicking the parent chooses all or none, never
"mixed".

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.SelectAll} />

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Validation} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Checkbox } from 'zweihander/checkbox'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/checkbox.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/checkbox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/checkbox)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Checkbox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/checkbox) and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CheckboxStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CheckboxStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The label wraps the box, so the whole label is part of the click target.

## Measurements

One size. The box is control tier xs (Foundations / Sizing) and sits
centred on the first line of its label, however many lines the label
wraps to.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every checkbox"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--choice-box' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Check mark', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Gap from the box', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Gap from the label', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The box's corner is the radius step, not the control tier's radius: a box
that turned round under `radius="full-rounded"` would read as a radio.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Unchecked, every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--control-border' },
    { part: 'Container, hover', property: 'Border', token: '--foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="neutral, checked or indeterminate"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Check mark', property: 'Colour', token: '--background' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable

  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Check mark', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-foreground' },
