/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Container, error', property: 'Border', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Helper text, error', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Helper text, success', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Required asterisk', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Unchecked' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Checked', content: <Checkbox defaultChecked label="Remember me" /> },
    { label: 'Indeterminate', content: <Story of={CheckboxStories.Indeterminate} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Checkbox disabled defaultChecked label="Remember me" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Checkbox validationState="error" label="Remember me" /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CheckboxStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** anywhere on the label darkens an unchecked outline to
  `--foreground`. A checked box mixes 12% of the mark's colour into its
  fill, as Button does. An error outline stays red.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the box.
- **Disabled** dims the box and the label to 50%.
- **Read-only** looks enabled but has no hover and an arrow cursor.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CheckboxStories} />
</div>

`id`, `className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the box.

### Differences from the spec

- **Base UI's and HTML's names:** `defaultChecked` and `onCheckedChange`
  for the spec's `defaultValue` (a string there, which reads as the
  submitted value: that is `value`) and `onChange`; native `disabled`,
  `required`, `readOnly` for the `is…` forms.
- **`isIndeterminate` keeps its prefix.** Indeterminate is a DOM property,
  not an HTML attribute, so by the kit's naming rule it takes `is`; Base UI
  calls it `indeterminate`.
- **`autoFocus` is applied on mount by the component.** The box is a
  focusable `<span>`, which React's own `autoFocus` ignores.
- **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as checked, so only
  `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a checkbox for a choice that is submitted with a form: accepting
terms, opting in, picking several items from a list. Nothing happens
until the form is sent.

Write the label so that checked means yes.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CheckboxStories.DoPositiveLabel} />}
  doCaption="The label says what checking does: checked means yes."
  dont={<Story of={CheckboxStories.DontNegativeLabel} />}
  dontCaption="A negative label makes unchecked a double negative, and readers stop to work it out."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a setting that applies at once.** Use a
  [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs): it acts like a
  light switch, a checkbox waits for Submit.
- **For one choice out of several.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group; checkboxes
  are independent.
- **For a toggle in a toolbar.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs).

## Accessibility

- `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`, `mixed` when indeterminate.
  Space toggles it.
- The label wraps the box, so it names it and clicking it toggles the box.
- `helperText` is the box's description; the error state sets
  `aria-invalid`.
- The unchecked outline is `--control-border`, 3:1 on the page on every
  gray ramp.
- A hidden native input carries `name`, `value` and `required` into form
  submission and validation.
- 44×44px touch target on coarse pointers, without the box growing.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Collapsible } from '@base-ui/react/collapsible'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Collapse.module.css'

export interface CollapseProps {
  /** The trigger's text, e.g. "Show details". */
  label: ReactNode
  /** The trigger's text while open, e.g. "Hide details". Defaults to `label`. */
  openLabel?: ReactNode
  children: ReactNode
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  disabled?: boolean
  /**
   * Keep the closed content in the page as `hidden="until-found"`, so the
   * browser's find-in-page reaches it and opens it. On by default.
   */
  hiddenUntilFound?: boolean
  className?: string
}

/**
 * One show/hide section: a text button with a chevron and the content it
 * reveals. For a list of sections, use Accordion.
 */
export function Collapse({
  label,
  openLabel,
  children,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  size = 'md',
  disabled = false,
  hiddenUntilFound = true,
  className,
}: CollapseProps) {
  return (
    <Collapsible.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}
      disabled={disabled}
      className={cn(styles.collapse, styles[size], className)}
    >
      <Collapsible.Trigger className={styles.trigger}>
        <span className={styles.chevron} aria-hidden="true">
          <Icon name="chevron-right" />
        </span>
        {openLabel === undefined ? (
          label
        ) : (
          <>
            <span className={styles.closedLabel}>{label}</span>
            <span className={styles.openLabel}>{openLabel}</span>
          </>
        )}
      </Collapsible.Trigger>
      <Collapsible.Panel className={styles.panel} hiddenUntilFound={hiddenUntilFound}>
        <div className={styles.content}>{children}</div>
      </Collapsible.Panel>
    </Collapsible.Root>
  )
}

# Collapse One show/hide section, such as "Show details" or "Advanced settings": a text bu...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as CollapseStories from './Collapse.stories'

<Meta of={CollapseStories} />

# Collapse

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

One show/hide section, such as "Show details" or "Advanced settings": a
text button with a chevron, and the content it reveals under it.

<Status of={CollapseStories} />

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Open} />

## Variants

Collapse has one look. `size` matches it to the text around it, and
`openLabel` decides whether the label changes when it opens.

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Body text, 14px. The default. |
| `sm` | Small text, 12px: captions, dense panels, notes under a field. |

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Small} />

| Label | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| With `openLabel` | A label that names the action: "Show details" becomes "Hide details". |
| Without `openLabel` | A label that names the section: "Advanced settings" stays the same, and the chevron shows the state. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Collapse } from 'zweihander/collapse'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/collapse.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Collapse.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Collapse.tsx)
- Spec: the kit's own. uiguideline.com has no page for it.
- Behaviour: [Base UI Collapsible](https://base-ui.com/react/components/collapsible)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Measurements

The trigger has no padding: it is as tall as a line of its text, 20px at
`md` and 16px at `sm`.

line height too.

## Color

The trigger has no fill and no border in any state.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={CollapseStories.Open} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={CollapseStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CollapseStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** underlines the label, like a link.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the trigger.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own: the label stays underlined while the
  pointer is down.
- **Open** turns the chevron from right to down, shows `openLabel` if
  there is one, and animates the panel's height over `--duration-base`.
- **Disabled** dims the trigger to 50% opacity, with no underline on hover.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CollapseStories} />
</div>

The props are the kit's own, since there is no spec to follow. Closed
content is kept as `hidden="until-found"` by default: the browser's
find-in-page still matches it and opens the section.

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Searchable} />

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Collapse for one aside in running content: billing details under a
plan, advanced settings under a form. It is a text button, not a bar,
because it belongs to the content around it, and its trigger reads like a
link in a sentence.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CollapseStories.DoAsideInText} />}
  doCaption="One aside, under the text it belongs to. The label says what opening it does."
  dont={<Story of={CollapseStories.DontStackAsList} />}
  dontCaption="A stack of Collapses is a list of sections. Use an Accordion: its items are real headings, framed and divided."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a list of sections.** Use an
  [Accordion](?path=/docs/components-data-display-accordion--docs). Its
  items are full-width bars with dividers because they are the page's
  structure.
- **For a short hint about a control.** Use a
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) or a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs), which do not
  push the page down.
- **For content most readers need.** Hiding it costs everyone a click.
  Show it.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`
  pointing at the panel.
- Enter or Space toggles it. With `openLabel`, the button's name changes
  with its state ("Show details" / "Hide details"), and `aria-expanded`
  says it either way. Without it, the name stays the same.
- The chevron is decorative (`aria-hidden`), so it adds nothing to the
  name.
- Closed content is `hidden="until-found"` by default, so find-in-page
  reaches it.
- The trigger grows to a 44px target on coarse pointers.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the panel and chevron change without
  animating.

'use client'

import { useId, useState, type CSSProperties, type KeyboardEvent, type PointerEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { Popover } from '@base-ui/react/popover'
import { Slider } from '@base-ui/react/slider'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Select } from '../inputs/Select'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from '../inputs/InputField'
import styles from './ColorPicker.module.css'

/** Hue 0–360, saturation and brightness 0–1. */
interface Hsv {
  h: number
  s: number
  v: number
}

/**
 * `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`, with or without the `#`, to
 * lowercase `#rrggbb`, or `#rrggbbaa` when it is not opaque; anything else to `null`.
 */
export function normalizeHex(text: string): string | null {
  let m = text.trim().replace(/^#/, '').toLowerCase()
  if (!/^([0-9a-f]{3,4}|[0-9a-f]{6}|[0-9a-f]{8})$/.test(m)) return null
  if (m.length < 5) m = [...m].map((c) => c + c).join('')
  return `#${m.endsWith('ff') && m.length === 8 ? m.slice(0, 6) : m}`
}

let ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D | null | undefined
/**
 * Any CSS colour (hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `oklch()`, a name...) to the hex
 * normalizeHex gives; anything else to `null`. The browser does the parsing:
 * outside one (SSR), only hex is read.
 */
export function parseColor(text: string): string | null {
  const hex = normalizeHex(text)
  if (hex || typeof document === 'undefined' || !CSS.supports('color', text.trim())) return hex
  ctx ??= document.createElement('canvas').getContext('2d', { willReadFrequently: true })
  if (!ctx) return null
  ctx.fillStyle = '#000'
  ctx.fillStyle = text.trim()
  // Usually comes back as #rrggbb or rgba(r, g, b, a).
  const style = ctx.fillStyle
  const m = style.match(/^rgba?\(([\d.]+), ([\d.]+), ([\d.]+)(?:, ([\d.]+))?\)$/)
  if (m) return normalizeHex([m[1], m[2], m[3]].map(Number).map(byteHex).join('') + byteHex(Number(m[4] ?? 1) * 255))
  if (style.startsWith('#')) return normalizeHex(style)
  // Wide-gamut spaces keep their own syntax: paint a pixel and read it back in sRGB.
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, 1, 1)
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 1, 1)
  return normalizeHex([...ctx.getImageData(0, 0, 1, 1).data].map(byteHex).join(''))
}

/** parseColor, dropping the alpha when the picker has none. */
const readHex = (text: string, alpha: boolean) => {
  const n = parseColor(text)
  return n && !alpha ? n.slice(0, 7) : n
}

const toRgb = (hex: string) => {
  const n = parseInt(hex.slice(1, 7), 16)
  return [n >> 16, (n >> 8) & 255, n & 255]
}
const byteHex = (n: number) => Math.round(n).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')

function hexToHsv(hex: string): Hsv {
  const [r, g, b] = toRgb(hex).map((c) => c / 255)
  const max = Math.max(r, g, b)
  const d = max - Math.min(r, g, b)
  let h = 0
  if (d) {
    if (max === r) h = ((g - b) / d) % 6
    else if (max === g) h = (b - r) / d + 2
    else h = (r - g) / d + 4
  }
  return { h: (h * 60 + 360) % 360, s: max ? d / max : 0, v: max }
}

function hsvToHex({ h, s, v }: Hsv): string {
  const f = (k: number) => {
    const x = (k + h / 60) % 6
    return v - v * s * Math.max(0, Math.min(x, 4 - x, 1))
  }
  return `#${[f(5), f(3), f(1)].map((c) => byteHex(c * 255)).join('')}`
}

const hsvToHsl = ({ h, s, v }: Hsv) => {
  const l = v * (1 - s / 2)
  return { h, s: l === 0 || l === 1 ? 0 : (v - l) / Math.min(l, 1 - l), l }
}
const hslToHsv = ({ h, s, l }: { h: number; s: number; l: number }): Hsv => {
  const v = l + s * Math.min(l, 1 - l)
  return { h, s: v ? 2 * (1 - l / v) : 0, v }
}

const clamp = (n: number, max = 1) => Math.min(max, Math.max(0, n))
const pct = (n: number) => Math.round(n * 100)

export type ColorFormat = 'hex' | 'rgb' | 'hsl' | 'hsb'
const formats: { value: ColorFormat; label: string }[] = [
  { value: 'hex', label: 'Hex' },
  { value: 'rgb', label: 'RGB' },
  { value: 'hsl', label: 'HSL' },
  { value: 'hsb', label: 'HSB' },
]

/**
 * A compact text field for one channel. It keeps what is typed until Enter or
 * blur, and up/down step the value as in a design tool (Shift for 10).
 */
function ChannelInput({
  label,
  value,
  onCommit,
  onStep,
  disabled,
  className,
}: {
  label: string
  value: string
  /** Gets the typed text; ignore it if it does not parse. */
  onCommit: (text: string) => void
  onStep?: (delta: number) => void
  disabled?: boolean
  className?: string
}) {
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const commit = () => {
    if (draft !== null && draft.trim() !== '') onCommit(draft)
    setDraft(null)
  }
  return (
    <input
      type="text"
      inputMode={onStep ? 'numeric' : undefined}
      spellCheck={false}
      autoComplete="off"
      aria-label={label}
      className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.channel, className)}
      value={draft ?? value}
      disabled={disabled}
      onChange={(e) => setDraft(e.target.value)}
      onFocus={(e) => e.currentTarget.select()}
      onBlur={commit}
      onKeyDown={(e) => {
        if (e.key === 'Enter') commit()
        else if (onStep && (e.key === 'ArrowUp' || e.key === 'ArrowDown')) {
          e.preventDefault()
          setDraft(null)
          onStep((e.key === 'ArrowUp' ? 1 : -1) * (e.shiftKey ? 10 : 1))
        }
      }}
    />
  )
}

export type Swatch = string | { value: string; label: string }

export interface ColorPanelProps {
  /** `#rrggbb`, or `#rrggbbaa` when not opaque. */
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  onValueChange?: (hex: string) => void
  /** Show the opacity slider and field. Off, the value is always `#rrggbb`. */
  alpha?: boolean
  /** The format of the channel fields when the panel opens. */
  defaultFormat?: ColorFormat
  /** Preset colours under the pickers. A plain string is named by its hex. */
  swatches?: Swatch[]
  disabled?: boolean
  className?: string
}

/**
 * The picker on its own, laid out like Figma's: a saturation/brightness area,
 * hue and opacity strips, channel fields in a chosen
 * format, and optional swatches. Use it inline, or through ColorPicker, which
 * puts it in a popover under a hex field.
 */
export function ColorPanel({
  value,
  defaultValue = '#3b82f6',
  onValueChange,
  alpha = true,
  defaultFormat = 'hex',
  swatches,
  disabled = false,
  className,
}: ColorPanelProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(() => readHex(defaultValue, alpha) ?? '#000000')
  const hex = (value !== undefined ? readHex(value, alpha) : null) ?? valueState
  const rgbHex = hex.slice(0, 7)
  const a = hex.length > 7 ? parseInt(hex.slice(7), 16) / 255 : 1
  // Kept as HSV, not read back from hex: at zero saturation or brightness the
  // hex forgets the hue, and the strip would jump to red.
  const [hsv, setHsv] = useState(() => hexToHsv(hex))
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(hex)
  if (hex !== shown) {
    setShown(hex)
    if (hsvToHex(hsv) !== rgbHex) setHsv(hexToHsv(hex))
  }
  const [format, setFormat] = useState(defaultFormat)

  const change = (next: Hsv, nextA = a) => {
    setHsv(next)
    const byte = Math.round(clamp(nextA) * 255)
    const nextHex = hsvToHex(next) + (byte < 255 ? byteHex(byte) : '')
    setShown(nextHex)
    setValueState(nextHex)
    if (nextHex !== hex) onValueChange?.(nextHex)
  }
  // From an RGB colour, keeping the hue where the colour has none.
  const pickRgb = (rgb: string, nextA = a) => {
    const next = hexToHsv(rgb)
    change(next.s && next.v ? next : { ...next, h: hsv.h }, nextA)
  }

  const fromPointer = (e: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const box = e.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect()
    change({ ...hsv, s: clamp((e.clientX - box.left) / box.width), v: clamp(1 - (e.clientY - box.top) / box.height) })
  }

  // One tab stop for the area, and the keys move it the way the thumb looks:
  // left/right saturation, up/down brightness, Shift for steps of 10%.
  const onAreaKey = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    const step = e.shiftKey ? 0.1 : 0.01
    const keys: Record<string, Partial<Hsv>> = {
      ArrowRight: { s: hsv.s + step },
      ArrowLeft: { s: hsv.s - step },
      ArrowUp: { v: hsv.v + step },
      ArrowDown: { v: hsv.v - step },
      PageUp: { v: hsv.v + 0.1 },
      PageDown: { v: hsv.v - 0.1 },
      Home: { s: 0 },
      End: { s: 1 },
    }
    const move = keys[e.key]
    if (!move) return
    e.preventDefault()
    change({ ...hsv, s: clamp(move.s ?? hsv.s), v: clamp(move.v ?? hsv.v) })
  }

  // Each format as [label, shown value, max, apply]: apply takes a new number
  // for that channel and returns the colour, so typing and stepping share it.
  const rgb = toRgb(rgbHex)
  const hsl = hsvToHsl(hsv)
  const channels: [string, number, number, (n: number) => void][] =
    format === 'rgb'
      ? (['Red', 'Green', 'Blue'] as const).map((name, i) => [
          name,
          rgb[i],
          255,
          (n) => pickRgb(`#${rgb.map((c, j) => byteHex(j === i ? n : c)).join('')}`),
        ])
      : format === 'hsl'
        ? [
            ['Hue degrees', Math.round(hsl.h), 360, (n) => change({ ...hsv, h: n % 360 })],
            ['Saturation percent', pct(hsl.s), 100, (n) => change(hslToHsv({ ...hsl, s: n / 100 }))],
            ['Lightness percent', pct(hsl.l), 100, (n) => change(hslToHsv({ ...hsl, l: n / 100 }))],
          ]
        : format === 'hsb'
          ? [
              ['Hue degrees', Math.round(hsv.h), 360, (n) => change({ ...hsv, h: n % 360 })],
              ['Saturation percent', pct(hsv.s), 100, (n) => change({ ...hsv, s: n / 100 })],
              ['Brightness percent', pct(hsv.v), 100, (n) => change({ ...hsv, v: n / 100 })],
            ]
          : []
  const numeric = (label: string, shownValue: number, max: number, apply: (n: number) => void, className?: string) => (
    <ChannelInput
      key={label}
      label={label}
      value={String(shownValue)}
      className={className}
      disabled={disabled}
      onCommit={(text) => {
        const n = Number(text.replace('%', ''))
        if (Number.isFinite(n)) apply(clamp(Math.round(n), max))
      }}
      onStep={(d) => apply(clamp(shownValue + d, max))}
    />
  )

  const presets = swatches?.map((s) => (typeof s === 'string' ? { value: s, label: s } : s))

  return (
    <div
      className={cn(styles.panel, disabled && styles.disabled, className)}
      style={{ '--picker-hue': hsv.h, '--picker-color': hex, '--picker-rgb': rgbHex } as CSSProperties}
    >
      <div
        className={styles.area}
        data-disabled={disabled || undefined}
        onPointerDown={(e) => {
          if (disabled || e.button !== 0) return
          // Firefox throws on a pointer id it does not know (synthetic events);
          // the click still sets the colour, only the drag needs the capture.
          try {
            e.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)
          } catch {}
          e.preventDefault()
          e.currentTarget.querySelector('input')?.focus({ preventScroll: true })
          fromPointer(e)
        }}
        onPointerMove={(e) => e.currentTarget.hasPointerCapture(e.pointerId) && fromPointer(e)}
      >
        <div className={styles.areaThumb} style={{ left: `${hsv.s * 100}%`, top: `${(1 - hsv.v) * 100}%` }}>
          <input
            type="range"
            className={styles.srOnly}
            aria-label="Saturation"
            aria-valuetext={`Saturation ${pct(hsv.s)}%, brightness ${pct(hsv.v)}%`}
            min={0}
            max={100}
            value={pct(hsv.s)}
            disabled={disabled}
            onChange={(e) => change({ ...hsv, s: Number(e.target.value) / 100 })}
            onKeyDown={onAreaKey}
          />
          {/* Reachable by a screen reader's virtual cursor; the keyboard gets it through the arrows above. */}
          <input
            type="range"
            className={styles.srOnly}
            tabIndex={-1}
            aria-label="Brightness"
            aria-valuetext={`Brightness ${pct(hsv.v)}%`}
            min={0}
            max={100}
            value={pct(hsv.v)}
            disabled={disabled}
            onChange={(e) => change({ ...hsv, v: Number(e.target.value) / 100 })}
          />
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className={styles.strips}>
        <Slider.Root
          className={styles.strip}
          min={0}
          max={359}
          value={Math.round(hsv.h) % 360}
          disabled={disabled}
          onValueChange={(h) => change({ ...hsv, h: h as number })}
          thumbAlignment="edge"
        >
          <Slider.Control className={styles.stripControl}>
            <Slider.Track className={cn(styles.stripTrack, styles.hueTrack)}>
              <Slider.Thumb
                className={cn(styles.stripThumb, styles.hueThumb)}
                getAriaLabel={() => 'Hue'}
                getAriaValueText={(_, v) => `${v} degrees`}
              />
            </Slider.Track>
          </Slider.Control>
        </Slider.Root>
        {alpha && (
          <Slider.Root
            className={styles.strip}
            min={0}
            max={100}
            value={pct(a)}
            disabled={disabled}
            onValueChange={(n) => change(hsv, (n as number) / 100)}
            thumbAlignment="edge"
          >
            <Slider.Control className={styles.stripControl}>
              <Slider.Track className={cn(styles.stripTrack, styles.alphaTrack)}>
                <Slider.Thumb
                  className={cn(styles.stripThumb, styles.alphaThumb)}
                  getAriaLabel={() => 'Opacity'}
                  getAriaValueText={(_, v) => `${v}%`}
                />
              </Slider.Track>
            </Slider.Control>
          </Slider.Root>
        )}
      </div>

      <div className={styles.fields}>
        <Select
          aria-label="Colour format"
          className={styles.format}
          options={formats}
          value={format}
          disabled={disabled}
          onValueChange={(v) => v && setFormat(v as ColorFormat)}
        />
        <span className={cn(boxClass('md'), styles.channels)} data-disabled={disabled || undefined}>
          {format === 'hex' ? (
            <ChannelInput
              label="Hex"
              value={rgbHex.slice(1)}
              className={styles.hexChannel}
              disabled={disabled}
              onCommit={(text) => {
                // Any CSS colour; its alpha too, when it has one.
                const n = readHex(text, alpha)
                if (n) pickRgb(n.slice(0, 7), n.length > 7 ? parseInt(n.slice(7), 16) / 255 : a)
              }}
            />
          ) : (
            channels.map(([label, v, max, apply]) => numeric(label, v, max, apply))
          )}
          {alpha && numeric('Opacity percent', pct(a), 100, (n) => change(hsv, n / 100), styles.alphaChannel)}
          {alpha && (
            <span className={cn(inputStyles.affix, styles.unit)} aria-hidden>
              %
            </span>
          )}
        </span>
      </div>

      {presets && presets.length > 0 && (
        // Native radios: one choice at a time, one tab stop, arrows to move.
        // None is checked while the colour is not one of the swatches.
        <div role="radiogroup" aria-label="Swatches" className={styles.swatches}>
          {presets.map((s) => {
            const sv = readHex(s.value, alpha) ?? s.value
            return (
              <input
                key={s.value}
                type="radio"
                name={`${id}-swatch`}
                className={styles.swatch}
                style={{ '--swatch': sv } as CSSProperties}
                aria-label={s.label}
                checked={sv === hex}
                disabled={disabled}
                onChange={() => pickRgb(sv.slice(0, 7), sv.length > 7 ? parseInt(sv.slice(7), 16) / 255 : 1)}
              />
            )
          })}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

export interface ColorPickerProps extends Omit<ColorPanelProps, 'className'> {
  label?: ReactNode
  /**
   * Under the field. Replaced by a format hint while the typed text is not a
   * colour. The field reads any CSS colour and shows it back as hex.
   */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Submitted as the hex value. */
  name?: string
  required?: boolean
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/** A hex field with a swatch button that opens the ColorPanel. */
export function ColorPicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = '#3b82f6',
  onValueChange,
  alpha = true,
  defaultFormat,
  swatches,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: ColorPickerProps) {
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(() => readHex(defaultValue, alpha) ?? '#000000')
  const hex = (value !== undefined ? readHex(value, alpha) : null) ?? valueState
  const [text, setText] = useState(hex)
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  // Follow a controlled value that changes from outside.
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(hex)
  if (hex !== shown) {
    setShown(hex)
    setText(hex)
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const commit = (next: string) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(next)
    setInvalid(false)
    if (next !== hex) onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  const commitText = () => {
    const parsed = readHex(text, alpha)
    if (parsed) commit(parsed)
    else setInvalid(true)
  }

  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={invalid ? 'Enter a colour, e.g. #3b82f6, rgb(59 130 246) or hsl(217 91% 60%).' : helperText}
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <span className={boxClass(size)} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
        <Popover.Root>
          <Popover.Trigger
            className={cn(inputStyles.iconButton, styles.trigger)}
            style={{ '--swatch': hex } as CSSProperties}
            disabled={disabled}
            aria-label={`Choose colour, ${hex} selected`}
          />
          <Popover.Portal>
            <Popover.Positioner className={styles.positioner} side="bottom" align="start" sideOffset={6}>
              <Popover.Popup aria-label="Choose colour" className={styles.popup}>
                <ColorPanel value={hex} onValueChange={commit} alpha={alpha} defaultFormat={defaultFormat} swatches={swatches} />
              </Popover.Popup>
            </Popover.Positioner>
          </Popover.Portal>
        </Popover.Root>
        <Field.Control
          id={id}
          value={text}
          spellCheck={false}
          autoComplete="off"
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          required={required}
          className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.hexInput)}
          onChange={(e) => {
            setText(e.target.value)
            setInvalid(false)
          }}
          onBlur={commitText}
          onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === 'Enter' && commitText()}
        />
        {name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={hex} />}
      </span>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Color Picker Chooses a colour: type it in any CSS format, pick a swatch, find it on a sa...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { ColorPicker } from './ColorPicker'
import * as ColorPickerStories from './ColorPicker.stories'

<Meta of={ColorPickerStories} />

# Color Picker

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Chooses a colour: type it in any CSS format, pick a swatch, find it on a
saturation and brightness area and a hue strip, or type its channels in
Hex, RGB, HSL or HSB. The panel is laid out like Figma's colour picker.

<Status of={ColorPickerStories} />

<Canvas of={ColorPickerStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two exports.

| Export | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `ColorPicker` | A form field: the hex in a text field, with a swatch button that opens the panel in a popover. |
| `ColorPanel` | The panel on its own, always open: a sidebar, an inspector, a settings page about colour. |

<Canvas of={ColorPickerStories.Panel} />

`alpha` adds opacity; `defaultFormat` picks which channels the fields show
first.

<Canvas of={ColorPickerStories.FormatsAndOpacity} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ColorPicker, ColorPanel } from 'zweihander/color-picker'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/color-picker.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/ColorPicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/ColorPicker.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/color-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/color-picker)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover) and [Slider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/slider)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ColorPickerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ColorPickerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The panel here is shown open under its field; in a `ColorPicker` it opens
in a popover from the swatch button.

## Measurements

The field is a Text Input: the same tiers, padding and label. The panel is
the same at both field sizes.

<SpecTable
  caption="Field, sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius-field' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Field, md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Panel"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Swatch button', property: 'Size', token: '--control-xs' },
    { part: 'Swatch button and swatches', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Popover', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-3' },
    { part: 'Popover', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Gap between sections', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Area', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-md' },
    { part: 'Hue and opacity strips', property: 'Thickness', token: '--space-3' },
    { part: 'Hue and opacity strips', property: 'Gap between them', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Thumbs', property: 'Size', token: '--space-4' },
    { part: 'Format menu and channel fields', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Swatches', property: 'Minimum size', token: '--space-6' },

  ]}
/>

The panel is 16rem wide, so eight swatches fit in a row, and the area is
10rem tall. The format menu and the channels are the kit's md (32px)
Select and field box.

## Color

The area, the hue strip and the checkerboard are the colour model itself,
so they are fixed colours, not theme tokens. The thumbs are white rings
with a dark edge: one of the two is at least 3:1 against whatever colour
is under them.

<SpecTable
  rows={[
    { part: 'Popover', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Popover', property: 'Text', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Popover and swatch divider', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Popover', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-md' },
    { part: 'Swatch button', property: 'Inner edge', token: '--control-border' },
    { part: 'Chosen swatch', property: 'Ring', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Channel fields', property: 'Divider', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

Swatches have a faint inner edge, black 10% in light mode and white 10%
in dark, as in Figma. That is below the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11 round a white
swatch on white, accepted because the hex in the field, not the edge,
tells the colour.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <ColorPicker label="Brand colour" disabled /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <ColorPicker label="Brand colour" validationState="error" helperText="Pick a darker colour." /> },
  ]}
>
  <ColorPicker label="Brand colour" />
</States>

- **Focus** follows Text Input on the field. In the panel every thumb,
  swatch and field draws a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside.
- **Disabled** dims the field and disables the swatch button.
- **Error** is Text Input's. Typed text that is not a colour turns the
  field to error on its own, with a hint, and keeps the last good value.
- **Chosen swatch** has a 2px `--primary` ring; focused as well, the ring
  turns `--ring` and moves 1px further out.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ColorPickerStories} />
</div>

`ColorPanel` takes `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `alpha`,
`defaultFormat`, `swatches`, `disabled` and `className`.

`parseColor(text)` reads any CSS colour (`rgb(59 130 246)`,
`hsl(217 91% 60% / 50%)`, `oklch(...)`, `rebeccapurple`) to the same hex,
or `null`; the browser parses it, so outside one only hex is read.
`normalizeHex(text)` turns `#abc`, `ABC` or `#AABBCC` into `#aabbcc`,
keeps an alpha byte (`#3b82f680`, or `#abc8` as `#aabbcc88`) unless it is
`ff`, and turns anything else into `null`.

### Design notes

- **Hex in, hex out.** The value is lowercase `#rrggbb`, with an alpha
  byte only while opacity is under 100%. Typed text is read on Enter or
  blur: hex of 3, 4, 6 or 8 digits with or without `#`, or any CSS colour.
  It is shown back as hex.
- **Formats are a view, not a value.** RGB, HSL and HSB only change the
  fields; the value stays hex. Channel fields commit on Enter or blur, and
  up and down step by 1 (Shift by 10), as in a design tool.
- **The hue is remembered.** The picker keeps hue, saturation and
  brightness, so dragging to black and back leaves the hue strip where it
  was instead of jumping to red.
- **Not in this version:** Figma's library picker ("On this page"),
  gradients and an eyedropper.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a colour picker when any colour is a valid answer: a brand colour, a
chart series, a label someone defines. When there is a palette to follow,
offer it as named swatches.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ColorPickerStories.DoBrandSwatches} />}
  doCaption="The colours people should use, as named swatches: one click, and a screen reader says “Blue”, not a hex."
  dont={<Story of={ColorPickerStories.DontNoSwatches} />}
  dontCaption="A palette to follow but no swatches: people match it by eye and land a few steps off."
/>

<Canvas of={ColorPickerStories.Swatches} />

## When not to use

- **For a few fixed colours.** When only a set of colours is allowed (tag
  colours, a theme accent), use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group of swatches or
  a Select: the picker lets anyone type any colour.
- **To show a colour.** Use a swatch and its hex as text.

## Accessibility

- The field is a text input named by its label. The swatch button is
  named "Choose colour, #3b82f6 selected", and the popover is a dialog
  named "Choose colour" that returns focus to the button on Escape.
- The area is one tab stop: a slider named "Saturation" whose value text
  reads both numbers ("Saturation 76%, brightness 96%"). Left and right
  change saturation, up and down brightness, Shift moves 10%, Page Up and
  Page Down change brightness by 10%, Home and End set saturation to 0 or
  100%. A second "Brightness" slider is there for a screen reader's
  browse mode.
- The hue strip is a slider named "Hue", read as "217 degrees"; the
  opacity strip, "Opacity", read as "50%".
- The format menu is the kit's Select, named "Colour format". Channel
  fields are text inputs named for what they hold ("Red", "Hue degrees",
  "Lightness percent", "Opacity percent", "Hex"), so they do not share a
  name with the sliders.
- Swatches are native radios in a radio group named "Swatches": one tab
  stop, arrows move and choose, and the chosen one is checked. None is
  checked while the colour is not one of them. They are 24px with 8px
  between them, which meets WCAG 2.5.8 without a larger invisible target.
- A colour is never the only way to know the value: the hex is always in
  the field.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import docs from './docs.module.css'
import { PALETTE, STEPS } from './palette'

function BandSwatches({ pairs }: { pairs: readonly (readonly [string, string])[] }) {
  return (
    <div className={docs.grid}>
      {pairs.map(([bg, fg]) => (
        <div
          key={bg}
          className={docs.swatchPair}
          style={{ background: `var(--${bg})`, color: `var(--${fg})` }}
        >
          <span className={docs.swatchLabel}>--{bg}</span>
          <span className={docs.swatchLabel}>--{fg}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

const LINES = ['border', 'input', 'ring'] as const

function LineSwatches() {
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--space-6)' }}>
      {LINES.map((token) => (
        <div
          key={token}
          style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', alignItems: 'center', gap: 'var(--space-2)' }}
        >
          <div
            style={{
              height: '2.5rem',
              width: '6rem',
              borderRadius: 'var(--radius-md)',
              boxShadow: `inset 0 0 0 2px var(--${token})`,
            }}
          />
          <span className={docs.caption}>--{token}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

function PrimitiveSwatches() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.stack}>
      {Object.entries(PALETTE).map(([hue, values]) => (
        <div key={hue} className={docs.rampRow}>
          <span className={docs.rampName}>{hue}</span>
          <div className={docs.ramp}>
            {values.map((value, i) => (
              <div
                key={STEPS[i]}
                title={`${hue}-${STEPS[i]}`}
                className={docs.rampStep}
                style={{ background: value }}
              />
            ))}
          </div>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

# Colors Every color in the system is a CSS custom property declared in `src/tokens.css`, ...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ColorsStories from './Colors.stories'

<Meta of={ColorsStories} />

# Colors

Every color in the system is a CSS custom property declared in
`src/tokens.css`, with a counterpart under the `.dark` class. There is no
separate dark palette file and no JS theme object — one stylesheet holds
both modes.

**Read them with `var()`** — `background: var(--card)`,
`color: var(--muted-foreground)`, `border-color: var(--border)`. Because
the variable changes rather than the rule, a component written this way
switches theme without a single conditional: there is no light branch and
no dark branch anywhere in the kit's CSS.

**The swatches below read their values out of the live document**, so a
color shown here is the value the components actually get. The token
*names* are still listed by hand in `Colors.stories.tsx`, though — add a
token to `tokens.css` and it will not appear here until it is added there
too.

## Surfaces

`--background` is the page. `--card` and `--popover` are surfaces that sit
a level above it — a card inset in the page, a menu floating over it. In
light mode the page is gray-50, a cool off-white, and card/popover are
white: a panel separates from the page by being lighter, so it needs a
border at most, not a shadow. In dark mode `--background` sits at the
darkest step and card/popover are lifted one step toward the viewer.

Each surface has a `-foreground` partner, and the pair is the contract:
put `--card-foreground` on `--card`, never `--foreground`, even where the
two happen to be equal today.

<Canvas of={ColorsStories.Surfaces} />

## Subtle surfaces

`--muted` and `--accent` are the same value in both modes and differ only
in intent. `--muted` is for surfaces that recede — a disabled field's
fill, a table's zebra stripe — and is the only one of the two with a
foreground meant for *long-form* secondary text. `--accent` is for
surfaces that are reacting to the user: hover on a menu item, the
selected row in a list.

They are interchangeable in appearance, so nothing breaks visually if you
swap them, and nothing tells you that you did. The distinction is the
whole point: when a brand color eventually replaces one of them, only the
intent that should change will change.

<Canvas of={ColorsStories.SubtleSurfaces} />

## Solid actions

Filled controls. `--primary` is the default button and **the brand hue** —
blue out of the box, and the one token the
[`accentColor`](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs) setting moves. It
lightens in dark mode rather than darkening, so `--primary-foreground`
inverts with it.

`--destructive` is a hue too, but a fixed one: it stays red whatever the
accent is. A status colour that follows the brand stops being a status —
if the accent is already red, distinguish destructive actions by wording
and placement, not by colour alone.

A note on names: the token called `--accent` is **not** the brand hue. It
is a subtle surface (hover, selected row). The brand hue is `--primary`.
The collision is unfortunate and predates this kit — the names come from
the token contract the registry is compatible with.

<Canvas of={ColorsStories.SolidActions} />

## Lines and focus

`--border` is a divider or a container edge, `--input` is a form control's
edge, `--ring` is the focus indicator. None of them take a foreground —
they are only ever an outline color, never a fill behind text.

`--border` and `--input` are the same value in both modes and, like
muted/accent, are separated by intent rather than appearance. In dark mode
they stop being opaque neutrals and become white at 10% and 15% alpha
respectively, so an edge reads consistently whether it sits on
`--background` or on a lifted `--card`. That is the one place the palette
uses transparency.

<Canvas of={ColorsStories.LinesAndFocus} />

## Dark mode

Every token on this page has a counterpart under `.dark`, switched by a
class rather than a media query, and dark is not a mechanical inversion of
light — surfaces go *up* rather than down, and strong fills get lighter so
their foregrounds flip to dark text. The Light/Dark columns in the
contrast table below cover both.

The mechanism, the three places an inversion would have gone wrong, and
how to follow the OS setting are on their own page:
**[Dark mode](?path=/docs/foundations-dark-mode--docs)**.

## Contrast

Measured, not assumed — every pair below is computed from the OKLCH
values in `tokens.css`. WCAG AA wants 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for UI
component boundaries such as a focus ring.

| Pair | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `background` / `foreground` | 19.28:1 | 19.28:1 |
| `card` / `card-foreground` | 20.13:1 | 17.00:1 |
| `popover` / `popover-foreground` | 20.13:1 | 17.00:1 |
| `primary` / `primary-foreground` | 5.03:1 | 6.79:1 |
| `secondary` / `secondary-foreground` | 16.13:1 | 14.07:1 |
| `accent` / `accent-foreground` | 16.13:1 | 14.07:1 |
| `destructive` / `destructive-foreground` | 4.56:1 | 6.19:1 |
| `muted` / `muted-foreground` | 4.60:1 | 5.64:1 |
| `background` / `muted-foreground` | 4.85:1 | 7.73:1 |
| `background` / `ring` | 6.54:1 | 7.63:1 |

Measured on the defaults: blue accent, gray gray. The `primary` row is the default blue accent. Every one of the seventeen
accents is measured the same way and clears 4.5:1 for its own label — see
[Overview → Accent color](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs).

**`--muted-foreground` on `--muted` is 4.60:1 in light mode**, the
tightest pair it forms. It used to be 4.34:1, under AA: gray-500 on every
ramp has since been darkened to the lightest value that clears 4.6:1 on
its own gray-100, so muted text can now sit on a muted fill. On the page background, where secondary
text usually lives, the same token is 4.85:1.

**`--subtle-foreground` is a step between body text and muted text**
(gray-600 light, gray-300 dark): navigation labels that should recede
until hovered or current, as in the Claude apps' sidebar. It reads about
7.5:1 on the light page, so it is body-safe; use `--muted-foreground` for
genuinely secondary text.

**`--surface-filled` is a filled panel that muted text can sit on.**
Muted text reads 4.85:1 on it (gray-50) and 5.64:1 on gray-800 in dark — a step off `--card` so a filled panel still reads as filled. The build
measures `--muted-foreground` on `--background`, `--card`,
`--surface-filled` and `--muted` in both modes on all nine gray ramps, and
stops if any pair drops under 4.5:1. The tightest is neutral on `--muted`,
at 4.60:1.

**`--control-border` outlines a checkbox, radio or switch track.** Those
controls have nothing else that shows they are there, so WCAG 1.4.11 wants
3:1 against the page — and `--input` (gray-200) is about 1.3:1. The build
measures it on all nine gray ramps.

**`--field-border` is the text-field edge** (gray-300 light, white 18%
dark), about 1.5:1: the light hairline of the Claude apps, and a
deliberate exception to 3:1 for fields only. Fields lean on a white
`--card` fill, a faint drop, the label and the focus ring instead. A
product that needs 3:1 sets `--field-border: var(--control-border)`.

**`--primary-text` is the brand hue as text** — an outlined or ghost
primary button. The solid is picked for its label, not for being read on
the page, and amber-500 on white is barely 2:1, so the build measures a
third step per accent that clears 4.5:1 against the page.

**Two values are deliberately off the beaten path.** `--ring` follows the
accent at its `-700` step rather than being a neutral, because a focus
indicator has to clear 3:1 against the page under WCAG 1.4.11 and the
lighter solids miss it — yellow-600 measures 2.93:1, so the ring uses a
step darker than the fill for every accent.
And dark `--destructive-foreground` is neutral-900 rather than near-white:
dark mode inverts the destructive fill to red-400, and near-white on
red-400 is 2.77:1, which makes the label of a destructive button in dark
mode fail AA outright.

## Status

Four fixed hues for messages about state: `info` (blue), `success`
(green), `warning` (amber), `danger` (red). Like `--destructive`, they do
not follow the accent. Each comes as four tokens:

| Token | Use | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--{status}` | Solid fill | 600 (green 700, amber 500) | 400 |
| `--{status}-foreground` | Label on the solid | neutral-50 (amber: neutral-900) | neutral-900 |
| `--{status}-subtle` | Tinted fill | 100 | 950 |
| `--{status}-text` | Text, icon and border on the tint or the page | 800 | 300 |

The steps are pinned by hand, so `npm run tokens` measures them and fails
the build if any pair drops under 4.5:1:

| Pair | info | success | warning | danger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label on solid, light | 5.03:1 | 4.73:1 | 8.35:1 | 4.56:1 |
| text on subtle, light | 7.25:1 | 6.45:1 | 6.41:1 | 6.86:1 |
| text on page, light | 8.84:1 | 7.09:1 | 7.13:1 | 8.37:1 |
| label on solid, dark | 6.79:1 | 10.09:1 | 10.43:1 | 6.19:1 |
| text on subtle, dark | 8.13:1 | 10.67:1 | 10.37:1 | 8.40:1 |
| text on page, dark | 10.93:1 | 14.16:1 | 13.69:1 | 10.30:1 |

`danger` and `destructive` share red-600 but mean different things:
`destructive` is an action that destroys, `danger` is a state that is
wrong. Keep them apart so either can move without the other.

## Color is never the only signal

`--destructive` on a button does not say what will be destroyed, and a red
badge means nothing to a reader who cannot distinguish it from a neutral
one. Pair color with words, an icon, or a shape every time it carries
meaning. The contrast numbers above are a floor, not a design review.

## Where the values come from

**Every value is a step off a published ramp, digit for digit.** Nothing
here was hand-picked or eyeballed. Two ramps feed the palette and each is
swappable on its own: an **accent** (blue by default) for `--primary` and
`--ring`, and a **gray** (the `gray` ramp by default) for everything structural.

| Token | Light | Dark | Driven by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `background` | gray-50 | gray-950 | gray |
| `foreground` | gray-950 | gray-50 | gray |
| `card`, `popover` | white | gray-900 | gray |
| `card-foreground`, `popover-foreground` | gray-950 | gray-50 | gray |
| `primary` | accent-600 | accent-400 | **accent** |
| `primary-foreground` | white or near-black | near-black | **accent** |
| `secondary`, `muted`, `accent` | gray-100 | gray-800 | gray |
| `secondary-foreground`, `accent-foreground` | gray-900 | gray-50 | gray |
| `selected` | gray-200 | white 10% | gray |
| `hover-overlay` | black 5% | white 6% | fixed |
| `scrim` | black 50% | black 50% | fixed |
| `muted-foreground` | gray-500 | gray-400 | gray |
| `subtle-foreground` | gray-600 | gray-300 | gray |
| `surface-filled` | gray-50 | gray-800 | gray |
| `neutral-solid` | gray-600 | gray-600 | gray |
| `neutral-solid-foreground` | gray-50 | gray-50 | gray |
| `destructive` | red-600 | red-400 | fixed |
| `destructive-foreground` | neutral-50 | neutral-900 | fixed |
| `border`, `input` | gray-200 | white 10% / 15% | gray |
| `field-border` | gray-300 | white 18% | gray |
| `control-border` | gray-500 | gray-400 | gray |
| `ring` | accent-700 | accent-400 | **accent** |
| `primary-text` | first of accent-600…900 at 4.5:1 on the light page | first of accent-400…200 at 4.5:1 on the dark page | **accent** |

The light accent step is `-600` for most hues but `-700` for sky, fuchsia,
pink and rose, and the label is white or near-black depending on which one
clears 4.5:1 on that fill — the warm hues take dark labels. Exceptions to
the ramp rule: light `--card`/`--popover` (pure white, so a panel reads
lighter than the gray-50 page) and dark `--border`/`--input`/`--selected`, and `--hover-overlay` in both
(alpha, so they work over any surface — the sidebar's hover sits on
`--surface-filled`, which in dark equals the opaque `--accent` fill).

`--destructive` deliberately does **not** follow the accent. A status
colour that changes with the brand stops being a status.

## Naming

Token names describe a **role**, not a property or a color. `--primary` is
not "the brand color" and `--destructive` is not "red"; they are the
default action and the dangerous one. The names are also the common
contract most token-based kits share, which is what lets a component
copied out of Zweihänder resolve against tokens a target project already
has instead of arriving with its own private palette.

Figma, by contrast, conventionally names tokens by property —
`bg/primary`, `text/primary`, `border/default`. Those do not map one to
one: Figma's `text/primary` is this system's `--foreground`, and its
`bg/primary` is `--background`. Neither is `--primary`. Worth pinning down
before any Figma sync, since the collision is silent.

## Primitives

The full underlying palette — 22 hues × 11 shades. None of these
classes are referenced anywhere in the kit, so they are force-generated by
an `@source inline(...)` directive in `src/index.css` purely so this page
can render them.

This is raw material, not a palette to build UI from. Reach for a
primitive when you are defining the *next* semantic token; if a primitive
shows up in a component, a token is missing.

<Canvas of={ColorsStories.Primitives} />

## Customization

Swap the raw values in `:root` and `.dark` in `src/tokens.css`. Nothing
that reads `var(--primary)` or `var(--muted-foreground)` changes, because
every rule points at the variable rather than the value.

Two things to carry through a rebrand: re-measure the pairs in the
contrast table — a brand hue at the same *lightness* as neutral-900 will
not necessarily hit the same ratios — and keep light and dark as separate
decisions. Lifting a brand color for dark mode by reusing the light value
is what produces the 2.77:1 failure documented above.

Projects that install through the registry get these values merged into
their own stylesheet; projects on the npm package import
`zweihander/tokens.css` and override afterwards.

# Column Chooser A button above a table that opens a list of its columns, each with a chec...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as ColumnChooserStories from './ColumnChooser.stories'

<Meta of={ColumnChooserStories} />

# Column Chooser

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A button above a table that opens a list of its columns, each with a
checkbox to show or hide it, and a Reset that brings back the default set.

<Status of={ColumnChooserStories} />

<Canvas of={ColumnChooserStories.Open} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Every column shown (default) | Tables whose columns all matter at first, where people hide what they do not need. |
| `defaultVisibleKeys` | Tables with more columns than fit: show the essentials, let people add the rest. Reset goes back to this set. |

The chooser does not touch the table: it reports the shown keys and you
filter the Table's `columns` with them. That keeps the choice yours to
store, per user or per view. With a resizable Table, pass `onReset` to put
the widths back too:

<Canvas of={ColumnChooserStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={ColumnChooserStories.SomeHiddenByDefault} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ColumnChooser } from 'zweihander/column-chooser'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/column-chooser.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/ColumnChooser.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/ColumnChooser.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; built from the Application UI catalogue, whose source for widths is shadcn's Resizable. Widths are Table's `isResizable` instead, a handle in each header rather than resizable panels
- Behaviour: the kit's [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs), [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs) and [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ColumnChooserStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ColumnChooserStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open popovers on this tab and the next are pictures: real choosers
rendered in place with `container` and inert, the popup laid out under the
button where it opens.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Every chooser"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Checkbox list', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Reset', property: 'Gap above', token: '--space-3' },
  ]}
/>

The button is a medium Button and Reset a small one; the popover, its
padding and title are Popover's. Checkboxes keep their own sizes.

## Color

The chooser adds no colour of its own: the button is an outlined secondary
Button, Reset a ghost secondary Button, and the surface is Popover's
`--popover`. See those pages for their tokens.

## States

The chooser is open or closed. The button keeps Button's states; each box
keeps Checkbox's, and a locked column shows Checkbox's disabled look:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ColumnChooserStories.StateButton} />
</States>

- **Locked**: the row header column, and the last column left, are ticked
  and disabled: a table needs a name per row and at least one column.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ColumnChooserStories} />
</div>

### Differences from the spec

There is no uiguideline spec. The catalogue's anatomy lists drag to
reorder as optional; it is left out until a table needs it, because it
needs a keyboard way to move as well.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Column Chooser on a table with more columns than most people need at
once, typically six or more, where different people read different ones.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ColumnChooserStories.DoFewColumns} />}
  doCaption="A few optional columns beside a locked name column."
  dont={<Story of={ColumnChooserStories.DontTwoColumns} />}
  dontCaption="A chooser for two columns: one is locked, so there is nothing to choose."
/>

## When not to use

- **To switch between whole layouts** (a summary and a detailed set): use
  saved views, so one choice changes several columns at once.
- **To filter rows.** Hiding a column does not hide rows; use filters in
  the table's toolbar.
- **For a table that fits.** If every column fits on the screens it is
  used on, leave them all shown.

## Accessibility

- The button reports `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`. The
  popup is a `role="dialog"` named by the label, "Columns".
- Opening moves focus into the dialog; Escape closes it and returns focus
  to the button.
- Each column is a checkbox named by its header, in table order; Space
  toggles it, and the shown keys are reported in column order, the row
  header always among them.
- The row header column's checkbox, and the last checked one, are
  `aria-disabled`: ticked and unchangeable.
- Reset is a button named "Reset" that brings back the default columns.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

/** The first case-insensitive match of the query, marked. */
function Highlight({ text, query }: { text: string; query: string }) {
  const at = query ? text.toLowerCase().indexOf(query.toLowerCase()) : -1
  if (at < 0) return <>{text}</>
  return (

      {text.slice(0, at)}
      <mark className={styles.match}>{text.slice(at, at + query.length)}</mark>
      {text.slice(at + query.length)}
    </>
  )
}

  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: ComboboxProps) {
  const items: Item[] = options.map((o) => (typeof o === 'string' ? { value: o, label: o } : o))
  const find = (v: string | null | undefined) => (v == null ? v : (items.find((i) => i.value === v) ?? null))
  // Only for highlighting the typed text in each option; Base UI owns the
  // input's value and the filtering.
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('')
  // A pointer pick sends the field back to rest: no caret, no ring, as a
  // native select after a click. A keyboard pick keeps focus where the user is.
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null)
  const labelId = useId()

  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      labelId={labelId}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <BaseCombobox.Root
        items={items}
        value={find(value)}
        defaultValue={find(defaultValue)}
        onValueChange={(next, details) => {
          // After Base UI's own refocus of the input, hence the timeout.
          if (details.event instanceof MouseEvent) setTimeout(() => inputRef.current?.blur())
          onValueChange?.((next as Item | null)?.value ?? null)
        }}
        // Highlight only what was typed. When an option is chosen the input
        // takes its label, which is not a query to mark in other options.
        onInputValueChange={(next, details) => setQuery(details.reason === 'input-change' ? next : '')}
        // items are rebuilt each render, so compare by value, not identity,
        // or the selection loses its check on the next keystroke.
        isItemEqualToValue={(a: Item, b: Item) => a.value === b.value}
        readOnly={readOnly}
        required={required}
        autoHighlight
      >
        <BaseCombobox.InputGroup
          className={cn(boxClass(size), styles.group)}
        >
          <BaseCombobox.Input
            ref={(el) => {
              inputRef.current = el
              if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(el)
              else if (ref) ref.current = el
            }}
            id={id}
            placeholder={placeholder}
            autoFocus={autoFocus}
            aria-label={ariaLabel}
            aria-busy={isLoading || undefined}
            className={s.control}
          />
          {isLoading && <span className={cn(s.icon, s.spinner)} aria-hidden="true" />}
          {isClearable && !readOnly && (
            <BaseCombobox.Clear className={s.iconButton} aria-label="Clear selection">
              <Icon name="clear" />
            </BaseCombobox.Clear>
          )}
          <BaseCombobox.Trigger
            className={s.iconButton}
            // Field labels every control in it with the field's label; this
            // button is not the field, so it keeps its own name rather than
            // being a second "Team member".
            render={(props) => <button {...props} aria-labelledby={undefined} aria-label="Show options" />}
          >
            <Icon name="chevron-down" />
          </BaseCombobox.Trigger>
        </BaseCombobox.InputGroup>
        <BaseCombobox.Portal container={container}>
          <BaseCombobox.Positioner className={s.positioner} sideOffset={4}>
            <BaseCombobox.Popup
              className={s.popup}
              style={popupInset(size)}
            >
              {isLoading ? (
                <BaseCombobox.Status className={s.status}>Loading…</BaseCombobox.Status>
              ) : (
                <BaseCombobox.Empty className={s.empty}>{emptyText}</BaseCombobox.Empty>
              )}
              {/* A listbox needs a name of its own: the field's. */}
              <BaseCombobox.List aria-labelledby={label ? labelId : undefined} aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}>
                {(item: Item) => (
                  <BaseCombobox.Item key={item.value} value={item} disabled={item.disabled} className={s.option}>
                    <BaseCombobox.ItemIndicator className={s.check}>
                      <Icon name="check" />
                    </BaseCombobox.ItemIndicator>
                    <span>
                      <Highlight text={item.label} query={query} />
                    </span>
                  </BaseCombobox.Item>
                )}
              </BaseCombobox.List>
            </BaseCombobox.Popup>
          </BaseCombobox.Positioner>
        </BaseCombobox.Portal>
      </BaseCombobox.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Combobox

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A field you type into to filter a list of options, then choose one.

<Status of={ComboboxStories} />

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two sizes, and the field's validation states. Typing filters the list and
marks the match; the chosen option carries a check.

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and settings: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a toolbar filter, a table row, beside `sm` buttons. |

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Validation} />

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Clear} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Combobox } from 'zweihander/combobox'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/combobox.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/combobox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/combobox)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Combobox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ComboboxStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ComboboxStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The options list opens under the field, at least as wide as it:

- **Option**: the label, with the typed text marked by weight and
  underline. Options are inset by the field's padding, so their text
  starts where the input's does.
- **Check**: before the chosen option's label, in a column kept for every
  option so labels never shift.
- **Message**: "No matches" (`emptyText`) when nothing matches,
  "Loading…" while `isLoading`.

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.OpenButton} />

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). Fields take the normal
inline padding, so the value lines up with the label above it, and the
field radius, which never becomes a pill.

The field is 20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`; the list is at least as
wide as the field, 4px under it, and scrolls after 20rem (about ten
options).

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Field"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Border', token: '--field-border' },
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-2xs' },
    { part: 'Label, input', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Placeholder, helper, icons', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Required asterisk', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Validation and read-only"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Border, helper, focus ring, error', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Border, helper, success', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Field, read-only', property: 'Background', token: '--surface-filled' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Options list"
  rows={[
    { part: 'List', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'List', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'List', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-md' },
    { part: 'Option', property: 'Colour', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Option, highlighted', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Option, highlighted', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Check', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-text' },
    { part: 'No matches, Loading…', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

The field's edge is a light hairline, about 1.5:1, as in the Claude apps:
an approved exception to WCAG 1.4.11. The label, placeholder and focus
ring still mark the field. The matched text keeps the option's own colour,
so it holds full contrast on the highlighted row.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Filled', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Clear} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Validation} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <Fit><Combobox label="Team member" options={['Miya Burns']} defaultValue="Miya Burns" readOnly /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Disabled} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Loading', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Loading} /></Fit> },
  ]}
>
  <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Default} /></Fit>
</States>

- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the field, drawn while
  the input has focus, by pointer too: that is where typing goes. In the
  error state the ring is `--danger-text`. The clear and open buttons draw
  their own ring when tabbed to, so the field never shows two.
- **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the clear and open buttons
  darken from `--muted-foreground` to `--foreground`.
- **Error** turns the edge and the helper `--danger-text` together; the
  words are the message, the colour only points at it.
- **Read-only** fills the field with `--surface-filled`; there is no clear
  button.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.
- **Loading** adds a spinner before the buttons and says "Loading…" in the
  list.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ComboboxStories} />
</div>

### Differences from the spec

- **Labels must be strings**, not components: they are what is typed,
  matched and shown in the input.
- **`emptyText`** is added: an empty list needs to say why.
- **`onValueChange`, not `onChange`**, and native names (`disabled`,
  `readOnly`, `required`), as on Select.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Combobox to choose one option from a long list, when people already
know what they are looking for: a person, a country, a project. Typing a
few letters is faster than scrolling. It chooses from the list only; free
text that is not an option is not a value.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ComboboxStories.DoLongList} />}
  doCaption="A long list people know an entry of: type a few letters, pick it."
  dont={<Story of={ComboboxStories.DontFewOptions} />}
  dontCaption="Three options hidden behind typing. A Select or a radio group shows them all."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a handful of options.** Under about seven, use a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group when they
  should all be visible.
- **For free text.** If any answer is valid, use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs); to filter
  a page, use [Search](?path=/docs/components-inputs-search--docs).
- **For several values.** It holds one; a multi-select is not built yet.

## Accessibility

- The input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and
  `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox` named by the field's label (or
  `aria-label` when there is no visible label), as the input is.
- **Keyboard:** typing opens and filters; the first match is highlighted
  so Enter picks it; Up and Down move; Escape closes, then clears.
- The match is marked by weight and underline, not colour, so it keeps
  the option's full contrast on the highlighted row.
- The open button is named "Show options" and is out of the tab order
  (the input already opens the list); the clear button is "Clear
  selection".
- `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid`, and the helper text is
  the input's description.
- Loading and empty states are announced from the list.
- After an option is picked with the pointer, the input loses focus and the
  field returns to rest (no caret, no ring). A keyboard pick keeps focus in
  the input, so keyboard and screen reader users are not dropped to the page.
- Options are 32px tall; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) they grow to
  44px, and the clear and open buttons get a 44×44px hit area.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>
