'use client'

import { useEffect, useId, useRef, useState, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Autocomplete } from '@base-ui/react/autocomplete'
import { Dialog } from '@base-ui/react/dialog'
import { Kbd } from '../atomic-elements/Kbd'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './CommandPalette.module.css'

/** A command or an object: what is typed is matched against `label` and `keywords`. */
export interface CommandPaletteItem {
  value: string
  label: string
  icon?: ReactNode
  /** More words that find it: "bill" for "New invoice". Not shown. */
  keywords?: string[]
  /** Shown right-aligned, one key cap per key: `['⌘', 'N']`. Display only: it does not bind the key. */
  shortcut?: string[]
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Runs when the item is chosen, once the palette has closed and given focus back. */
  onSelect?: () => void
}

/** A titled run of items: Recent, Commands, Customers. A group with no match is left out. */
export interface CommandPaletteGroup {
  label: string
  items: CommandPaletteItem[]
}

export interface CommandPaletteProps {
  groups: CommandPaletteGroup[]
  /** The button that opens it, e.g. a search field in the sidebar. */
  trigger?: ReactElement
  /**
   * The letter that toggles it with ⌘ or Ctrl, anywhere on the page.
   * `false` binds nothing: only one palette on a page should own the key.
   */
  hotkey?: string | false
  /** Called with the chosen item, after its own `onSelect`. */
  onSelect?: (item: CommandPaletteItem) => void
  placeholder?: string
  /** Names the search input. */
  inputLabel?: string
  /** Shown when nothing matches. */
  emptyText?: string
  /** Names the dialog. */
  label?: string
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Trap focus, lock page scroll and make the page inert while open. `false` is for pictures of it. */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where it renders instead of `<body>`. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
}

export function CommandPalette({
  groups,
  trigger,
  hotkey = 'k',
  onSelect,
  placeholder = 'Search commands…',
  inputLabel = 'Search commands',
  emptyText = 'No results',
  label = 'Command palette',
  open,
  defaultOpen = false,
  onOpenChange,
  isModal = true,
  container,
  className,
}: CommandPaletteProps) {
  const [ownOpen, setOwnOpen] = useState(defaultOpen)
  const isOpen = open ?? ownOpen
  const setOpen = (next: boolean) => {
    if (open === undefined) setOwnOpen(next)
    onOpenChange?.(next)
  }
  const hintsId = useId()
  // Accent-insensitive, so "hoa don" finds "Hóa đơn".
  const { contains } = Autocomplete.useFilter({ sensitivity: 'base' })

  // Re-bound every render: the handler reads the current open state.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!hotkey) return
    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (e.repeat || e.isComposing) return
      if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && !e.altKey && !e.shiftKey && e.key.toLowerCase() === hotkey.toLowerCase()) {
        e.preventDefault()
        setOpen(!isOpen)
      }
    }
    document.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
    return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
  })

  // The choice runs after the close has finished and focus is back on the
  // trigger, so an action that opens a dialog or moves focus keeps it.
  const chosen = useRef<CommandPaletteItem | null>(null)
  const choose = (item: CommandPaletteItem) => {
    chosen.current = item
    setOpen(false)
  }
  const onClosed = (isOpenNow: boolean) => {
    const item = chosen.current
    if (isOpenNow || !item) return
    chosen.current = null
    item.onSelect?.()
    onSelect?.(item)
  }

  return (
    <Dialog.Root open={isOpen} onOpenChange={setOpen} onOpenChangeComplete={onClosed} modal={isModal}>
      {trigger && <Dialog.Trigger render={trigger} />}
      <Dialog.Portal container={container}>
        <Dialog.Backdrop className={styles.backdrop} />
        <Dialog.Viewport className={styles.viewport}>
          <Dialog.Popup className={cn(styles.popup, className)} aria-label={label}>
            {/* inline + open: the list is part of the dialog, not a popup of its own. */}
            <Autocomplete.Root
              items={groups}
              itemToStringValue={(item: CommandPaletteItem) => item.label}
              filter={(item: CommandPaletteItem, query) =>
                [item.label, ...(item.keywords ?? [])].some((text) => contains(text, query))
              }
              open
              inline
              autoHighlight="always"
              keepHighlight
            >
              <Autocomplete.InputGroup className={styles.search}>
                <Icon name="search" className={styles.searchIcon} />
                <Autocomplete.Input
                  className={styles.input}
                  placeholder={placeholder}
                  aria-label={inputLabel}
                  aria-describedby={hintsId}
                />
              </Autocomplete.InputGroup>
              <div className={styles.results}>
                <Autocomplete.Empty className={styles.empty}>{emptyText}</Autocomplete.Empty>
                <Autocomplete.List className={styles.list}>
                  {(group: CommandPaletteGroup) => (
                    <Autocomplete.Group key={group.label} items={group.items} className={styles.group}>
                      <Autocomplete.GroupLabel className={styles.groupLabel}>{group.label}</Autocomplete.GroupLabel>
                      <Autocomplete.Collection>
                        {(item: CommandPaletteItem) => (
                          <Autocomplete.Item
                            key={item.value}
                            value={item}
                            disabled={item.disabled}
                            className={styles.item}
                            onClick={() => choose(item)}
                          >
                            {item.icon && (
                              <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
                                {item.icon}
                              </span>
                            )}
                            <span className={styles.label}>{item.label}</span>
                            {/* Shown, not part of the name, as on a Menu item. */}
                            {item.shortcut && <Kbd size="sm" keys={item.shortcut} aria-hidden="true" />}
                          </Autocomplete.Item>
                        )}
                      </Autocomplete.Collection>
                    </Autocomplete.Group>
                  )}
                </Autocomplete.List>
              </div>
              {/* The keys, drawn for sight and said once to a screen reader as the input's description. */}
              <div className={styles.footer}>
                <span id={hintsId} className={styles.visuallyHidden}>
                  Arrow keys to move, Enter to choose, Escape to close.
                </span>
                <span className={styles.hint} aria-hidden="true">
                  <Kbd size="sm" keys={['↑', '↓']} /> Move
                </span>
                <span className={styles.hint} aria-hidden="true">
                  <Kbd size="sm">↵</Kbd> Choose
                </span>
                <span className={styles.hint} aria-hidden="true">
                  <Kbd size="sm">Esc</Kbd> Close
                </span>
              </div>
            </Autocomplete.Root>
          </Dialog.Popup>
        </Dialog.Viewport>
      </Dialog.Portal>
    </Dialog.Root>
  )
}

# Command Palette A search box over the page that finds a command or a record by typing an...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as CommandPaletteStories from './CommandPalette.stories'

<Meta of={CommandPaletteStories} />

# Command Palette

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A search box over the page that finds a command or a record by typing and
runs it with Enter, without a mouse. Opened by its trigger or by ⌘K
(Ctrl+K).

<Status of={CommandPaletteStories} />

<Canvas of={CommandPaletteStories.Default} />

## Variants

There is one palette; what changes is what you put in its groups.

| Content | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Commands | Actions a power user repeats: New invoice, Export ledger. Give each its `shortcut` when it has one, so the palette teaches the key. |
| Records | Objects to jump to, grouped by type: Customers, Invoices. Load them from your search as the user types, or pass the few that matter. |
| Recent | What the user opened last, as the first group. The palette does not remember it for you: pass it from your app's history. |

Typing matches the label and `keywords`, ignoring case and accents, so
"bill" finds New invoice and "hoa binh" finds Hòa Bình Trading.

<Canvas of={CommandPaletteStories.Matching} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { CommandPalette } from 'zweihander/command-palette'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/command-palette.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/CommandPalette.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/CommandPalette.tsx)
- Spec: uiguideline.com has no command palette; anatomy from Tailwind UI Command Palettes and shadcn/ui Command
- Behaviour: [Base UI Autocomplete](https://base-ui.com/react/components/autocomplete) (inline, inside a [Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog))
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CommandPaletteStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CommandPaletteStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open palettes on this tab and the next are pictures: real palettes
rendered in a frame with `container`, not modal (`isModal={false}`) and
inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Container"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-xl' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Margin to the screen edge', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Search row', property: 'Height', token: '--box-xl' },
    { part: 'Search row', property: 'Gap, icon to input', token: '--control-md-gap' },
    { part: 'Search icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Search input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-lg' },
    { part: 'List', property: 'Inset from the container', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Empty text', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-6' },
    { part: 'Key hints', property: 'Gap between hints', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Key hints', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-xs' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Item and group label"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-md-gap' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Group label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Group label', property: 'Padding above', token: '--control-xs-pad' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Minimum height on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The container is at most 40rem wide and never wider than the screen. It
sits near the top, at 12% of the screen height, not centred: the list
grows and shrinks as you type, and the input stays where the eye is. The
list shows about ten rows (24rem) and then scrolls; the search row and the
key hints stay. The search icon lines up with the item icons. Items are
the [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs)'s rows; shortcuts
are [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-kbd--docs) `sm`.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Every palette"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Backdrop', property: 'Background', token: '--scrim' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Container, rules', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Input, items', property: 'Colour', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Placeholder, icons, group labels, hints', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Highlighted item', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Highlighted item', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Results', content: <Story of={CommandPaletteStories.Results} /> },
    { label: 'No results', content: <Story of={CommandPaletteStories.NoResults} /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Highlighted** is where the arrow keys or the pointer are: an `--accent`
  fill, the icon taking the text colour. The first match is always
  highlighted, so Enter always does something. Focus stays in the input;
  the highlight is the list's `aria-activedescendant`.
- **Disabled** items are muted at 60% opacity. The arrow keys still reach
  them, so a screen reader hears that they exist, but Enter and a click do
  nothing.
- **No results** shows `emptyText` and no group labels.
- The input has no focus ring of its own: it is the palette's only field,
  and the caret shows where typing goes.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CommandPaletteStories} />
</div>

### Differences from the spec

The queue's anatomy lists the open shortcut, an empty state and recent
results as parts. Here the shortcut is behaviour (`hotkey`, and a Kbd on the
trigger), the empty state is a state (under States), and Recent is a group
you pass: the palette does not store history.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

In an app with many pages and actions, as a fast way around for people who
use it every day: jump to a record, run a command, without going through
the navigation. Open it from a search button in the sidebar
(`NavSidebarButton appearance="field"`) and from ⌘K.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CommandPaletteStories.DoGroup} />}
  doCaption="Group the results, start each command with a verb, and put records under their type. Recent first."
  dont={<Story of={CommandPaletteStories.DontMix} />}
  dontCaption="One list of bare nouns: Invoice could mean open one, create one or list them all."
/>

Keep the palette a shortcut, not the only way: everything in it must also
be reachable from the navigation or a button on the page.

## When not to use

- **To search inside one list or table.** Use a search field above it,
  which filters what is on the page.
- **To pick a value in a form.** Use a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs): it fills a
  field, the palette runs something.
- **For a handful of actions on one object.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) on that object.

## Accessibility

- The container is a `role="dialog"` named "Command palette" (`label`).
  Opening moves focus to the search input and traps it inside; closing
  returns focus to the trigger.
- The input is a `role="combobox"` named "Search commands" (`inputLabel`), its
  description the key hints: "Arrow keys to move, Enter to choose, Escape to
  close". The drawn hints are hidden, so they are read once.
- Each group is a `role="group"` named by its label; each item is a
  `role="option"`. A shortcut is drawn, not read: the item's name is its
  label.
- Up and Down move the highlight and the first match is highlighted; Enter
  chooses it, as does a click. A disabled item is reachable but Enter does
  nothing on it. The choice runs once the palette has closed and focus is
  back on the trigger.

  <Canvas of={CommandPaletteStories.Keyboard} />

- Escape closes it, as does a press outside.

  <Canvas of={CommandPaletteStories.Empty} />

- ⌘K or Ctrl+K toggles it from anywhere on the page; one palette per page
  should own that key, and the others set `hotkey={false}`.

  <Canvas of={CommandPaletteStories.Hotkey} />

Give the trigger `aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K"` when the palette
owns the key, as the trigger in these examples does.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Common Actions The actions every record and form shares (Create, Edit, Save, Cancel, Del...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as CommonActionsStories from './CommonActions.stories'

<Meta of={CommonActionsStories} />

# Common Actions

The actions every record and form shares (Create, Edit, Save, Cancel,
Delete and the rest), each with one label, one place, one button style,
one level of confirmation and, where the platform already has one, one
shortcut. After Carbon's Common actions pattern, cut to what an enterprise
app repeats on every object.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/common-actions.json
```

It installs `commonActions`, the table below as data, and
`CommonActionsTable`, which renders it. Place a button by reading its row:

```tsx
import { commonActions } from './CommonActions'

<Button type="submit" {...commonActions.save.button}>{commonActions.save.label}</Button>
```

There is no `<SaveButton>`: the buttons stay Button, Menu entries and
Confirm Dialogs, and the catalogue only decides which. Rename a label or
change a level in your copy, and the table follows. A pattern usually owns
no data; this one is conventions, not records, so it ships them as data
the table and your code can both read.

## Reference

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.Reference} />

## Placement

**Form footer.** Cancel, then Save, at the end. Save is the submit button
and the only primary one in the form. [Form
Layouts](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs)'
`FormActions` lays them out.

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.FormFooter} />

**List header.** Import and Export, then Create as the page's one primary
button, at the end of the [Card
Heading](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-card-heading--docs) or page
header.

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.ListHeader} />

**Record header.** Edit next to the title; everything else in the overflow
menu, Delete last after a separator so it is never the item under the
pointer when the menu opens. A list row puts the same entries in its ⋯
menu ([Stacked List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stacked-list--docs),
[Grid List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-grid-list--docs)).

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.RecordHeader} />

## Confirmation

Ask in proportion to what is lost. Each step up costs every user a click
on every use, so the level follows how hard the action is to reverse, not
how serious it sounds.

| Level | When | Built with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None | Easy to reverse, or nothing is lost: Edit, Duplicate, Export | The button |
| Undo toast | Reversible, but the result leaves the screen: Archive, Remove | [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs) with an Undo action |
| Confirm Dialog | Cannot be undone: Delete | [Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs) |
| Type to confirm | Cannot be undone and takes other records with it: a workspace, a ledger | Confirm Dialog with `confirmText`, from a danger [Action Panel](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-action-panel--docs) |

Delete is a Confirm Dialog by default and goes up to type to confirm when
it cascades, so no row of the table names that level. An Undo toast times
out: keep the action reachable elsewhere too (an Archived filter, the
record's menu) for anyone who misses it. The dialog's own Cancel is
outlined, beside its contained destructive button; that is Confirm
Dialog's, not a second Cancel style.

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.ArchiveWithUndo} />
<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.DeleteWithConfirm} />
<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.TypeToConfirm} />

## Labels

- **One verb, sentence case.** Add the object only when the page has more
  than one kind: "Create invoice" in a header, "Delete" in an invoice's own
  menu.
- **The pairs are not synonyms.** Create makes a record, Add puts one into
  a set; Delete destroys it, Remove takes it out of the set; Cancel throws
  input away, Close has none to throw.
- **The confirm button repeats the action** ("Delete invoice"), never
  "OK" or "Yes".

## Shortcuts

Only shortcuts the platform already teaches: ⌘S, Esc, ⌘Z. Shown as
[Kbd](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-kbd--docs) in Mac glyphs; show Ctrl for
⌘ on other systems. The app binds them; the catalogue only names them. A
shortcut for anything else belongs in the [Command
Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-command-palette--docs), where it can be
found.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={CommonActionsStories} />

`commonActions` is keyed by id (`save`, `delete`, …); each entry has
`label`, `purpose`, `placement`, `confirm` (`none`, `undo`, `dialog` or
`typed`), and optionally `button` (`variant` and `appearance`; left out
for an action that only lives in a menu) and `shortcut`.

## Layout

- **No breakpoint of its own.** The form footer and the headers wrap their
  buttons when the row runs out of room; Save stays last.
- **The reference table** scrolls sideways in a narrow container, as any
  [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs).

<Canvas of={CommonActionsStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

Carbon's Common actions, and where this departs from them:

- **Fewer actions.** Clear, Reset, Copy, Refresh, Search and a wizard's
  Back and Next are left out: they belong to Filter Bar, Search, Steps
  and their own components, which already place them.
- **Archive and Undo are added**, because an ERP keeps records with
  transactions and reverses rather than asks.
- **The trigger for Delete is outlined**, as on Action Panel; only the
  dialog's confirm button is filled.

## Accessibility

- Cancel comes before Save in the DOM as on screen, so Tab reaches the
  safe choice first and Save is the submit button that Enter in a field
  presses.
- The icon-only ⋯ button is named "More actions".
- A Confirm Dialog focuses Cancel when it opens, so Enter cannot delete;
  with type to confirm, it focuses the field.
- The reference table names each row by its action (a row header), so a
  screen reader announces "Save" with each cell.

# Confirm Dialog Asks before something that cannot be undone: a warning, the action as a q...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as ConfirmDialogStories from './ConfirmDialog.stories'

<Meta of={ConfirmDialogStories} />

# Confirm Dialog

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Asks before something that cannot be undone: a warning, the action as a
question, what it will destroy, then Cancel or the action. A press outside
does nothing, so the reader has to choose.

<Status of={ConfirmDialogStories} />

<Canvas of={ConfirmDialogStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Default | An everyday delete: a comment, a file, a saved view. One question, two buttons. |
| Type to confirm (`confirmText`) | A large delete that cannot be undone: a workspace, an account, a project with its files. The action waits until the reader types the name. |

<Canvas of={ConfirmDialogStories.TypeToConfirm} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ConfirmDialog } from 'zweihander/confirm-dialog'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/confirm-dialog.json
```

- Source: [src/components/overlays/ConfirmDialog.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/ConfirmDialog.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal) (the alert dialog)
- Built on: [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`, on [Base UI Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ConfirmDialogStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ConfirmDialogStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open dialogs on this tab and the next are pictures: rendered in a frame
with `container` and `isModal={false}`, inert, so they do not lock this page
or take its focus.

## Measurements

It is a Modal at `size="sm"` (at most 24rem wide): container, title,
description, body and footer take Modal's measurements. Its own parts:

<SpecTable
  caption="Icon and field"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Warning icon', property: 'Width', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Icon to title', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Text to type', property: 'Font family', token: '--font-mono' },
  ]}
/>

The icon is one line of the title tall, so it stays on the first line when
the title wraps.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Its own parts"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Warning icon', property: 'Colour', token: '--destructive' },
  ]}
/>

Everything else takes Modal's colours, and the buttons keep their own:
Cancel is `secondary` outlined, the action `destructive`.

## States

The dialog is open or closed. With `confirmText`, the action is disabled
until the field matches, then enabled; without it, it is enabled from the
start.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Waiting for the name', content: <Story of={ConfirmDialogStories.StateWaiting} /> },
    { label: 'Ready', content: <Story of={ConfirmDialogStories.DoEverydayDelete} /> },
  ]}
/>

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ConfirmDialogStories} />
</div>

### Differences from the spec

- **Destructive only.** There is no neutral variant: a decision that
  destroys nothing (sign out, leave without saving) is a
  [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`, where
  you choose the buttons.
- **No pending state.** The dialog closes on confirm. If the delete can fail,
  control `open` and keep it open until your request settles.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Before an action that destroys something the reader cannot get back. Put
the object's name in the title, say in the description what goes with it,
and name the action button after what it does.

Type to confirm is for the few deletes that are both large and final. Used
on every delete, it becomes a chore readers do without reading.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ConfirmDialogStories.DoEverydayDelete} />}
  doCaption="Ask once for an everyday delete, with the action on the button."
  dont={<Story of={ConfirmDialogStories.DontTypeForSmall} />}
  dontCaption="Do not make the reader type for a small delete: it teaches them to type without reading."
/>

## When not to use

- **When the action can be undone.** Do it, then offer Undo in a
  [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): no question
  is faster than a good one.
- **For a decision that destroys nothing**, such as Sign out or Leave
  without saving. Use a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs)
  with `isAlert`.
- **To show a warning.** Use an
  [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs).

## Accessibility

- `role="alertdialog"`, named by the title (the icon is hidden from
  assistive tech) and described by the consequence.
- Focus starts on Cancel, so Enter on open cannot delete. With
  `confirmText` it starts in the field, which is named "To confirm, type"
  and the name.
- The action stays disabled until the field matches exactly, case
  included; spaces around the text are ignored. Enter in the field confirms
  once it matches.
- A press outside does nothing. Cancel and Escape close it without
  confirming, and focus goes back to the trigger.
- Reopened, the field starts empty.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

./src/components/patterns/application-ui/Container.mdx
# Container Caps a page's content at a maximum width and centres it in the space it is giv...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ContainerStories from './Container.stories'

<Meta of={ContainerStories} />

# Container

Caps a page's content at a maximum width and centres it in the space it
is given. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Layout: Containers.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/container.json
```

Container only sets a width. Inside an [App
Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs), [App
Content](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-app-content--docs) owns the
page: its padding, its scroll and the aside column. Put a Container inside
it when a page should not stretch across a wide screen, a settings page or
a form; leave it out for a table that uses every column.

## Sizes

`size` is the widest the content gets: `sm` 48rem for a form or a settings
page, `md` (the default) 64rem for most pages, `lg` 80rem for a wide table
or a dashboard.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.Sizes} />

## Padded

`padded` adds side padding by breakpoint, for a page outside the App
Shell, such as a sign-in page or a public page: `--space-container`, and
`--space-section` from a 64rem viewport: App Content's tokens and step,
measured against the viewport instead of the shell, on the sides only.
The cap measures the content, so a padded and an unpadded Container of one
size give the same line length.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.Padded} />

## In an App Shell

No `padded`: App Content already pads the page, and the Container centres
the content in it. With an aside, it centres in the page column.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.InAppShell} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={ContainerStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **Full width up to the cap.** It fills its parent, block, grid or flex,
  until it reaches its size, then centres with equal space on each side.
- **Narrower than its size,** it takes the width it is given and never
  overflows.
- **Padding follows the viewport,** not a container query: outside the
  App Shell no ancestor is a size container to query.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

Tailwind UI's Containers, and where this departs from them:

- **Three steps, not every `max-w-*`.** `sm`, `md` and `lg` follow
  Tailwind's `max-w-3xl`, `5xl` and `7xl`.
- **Padding is opt-in and uses the kit's spacing tokens.** Tailwind pads
  every container (`px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8`); here App Content pads the page
  in the shell, so padding twice would be wrong. One step at 64rem, as in
  App Content, instead of Tailwind's two.
- **No "full width on mobile" variant.** Under its size a Container is
  already full width; a flush, unpadded page on a phone is App Content's
  job.

## Accessibility

- A plain `div`: no landmark, no role and no focus. The landmark is the
  `main` around it (App Content's, or your own outside the shell).
- It changes no order; content reads and tabs in DOM order.
- At 320px it takes the full width and its content reflows; it adds no
  horizontal scroll.

# Context Menu A menu that opens at the pointer when someone right-clicks, or long-presses...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as ContextMenuStories from './ContextMenu.stories'

<Meta of={ContextMenuStories} />

# Context Menu

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A menu that opens at the pointer when someone right-clicks, or long-presses
on touch, an area: a table row, a card, an object on a canvas. Its items
are an action menu's, so it is a faster way to the same actions.

<Status of={ContextMenuStories} />

<Canvas of={ContextMenuStories.Default} />

## Variants

Context Menu has one look: the popup is a
[Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) popup and takes the
same entries: actions with icons and shortcuts, links, submenus, checkbox
and radio items, groups and separators.

| Area | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Enabled (the default) | An area with actions on it. Right click and long press open the menu. |
| Disabled (`disabled`) | An area with nothing to act on right now. The browser's own menu shows instead. |

On a list or table, give each row its own Context Menu, with the same items
as the row's visible "more" button:

<Canvas of={ContextMenuStories.OnRows} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ContextMenu } from 'zweihander/context-menu'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/context-menu.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/ContextMenu.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/ContextMenu.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Context Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/context-menu)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ContextMenuStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ContextMenuStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The popup on this tab is a picture: it is drawn open below its area, not at
a pointer, and does not lock the page. Its parts are Menu's; see
[Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) for the item's own
anatomy.

## Measurements

The popup is Menu's, with the same items of the md control tier. It opens
with its top-left corner on the pointer, as the operating system's menus
do. Near the bottom of the window it flips above the pointer; near the
right edge it slides left to stay on screen. On
touch it opens at the finger after a 500ms press.

<SpecTable
  caption="Popup"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-field' },
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-md' },
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Layer', token: '--layer-overlay' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Area, open', property: 'Outline width', token: '--focus-width' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Area and popup"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Area, open', property: 'Outline', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Text', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Item, highlighted', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Destructive item', property: 'Text and icon', token: '--danger-text' },
  ]}
/>

The area keeps its own colours. While its menu is open it gets a primary
outline inside its edge, so the reader sees which row or object the menu
acts on. The rest of the popup's colours are Menu's.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Closed', content: <Story of={ContextMenuStories.Default} /> },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={ContextMenuStories.Open} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={ContextMenuStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Closed**: the area looks like itself; nothing hints at the menu, which
  is why its items must be reachable another way.
- **Open**: the area is outlined in `--primary`; items highlight as in Menu.
- **Disabled**: a right click shows the browser's menu.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ContextMenuStories} />
</div>

`items` is Menu's `items`. `children` is one element: the area itself, its
props and the open marker merged onto it, so a `<tr>` stays a row of the
table.

### Differences from the spec

- **No placement props.** Menu's `side` and `align` are left out: a context
  menu opens at the pointer, and flips on its own near the window edge.
- **Always modal.** There is no `isModal`: Base UI makes a context menu
  modal, as the operating system's menus are, so page scroll is locked
  until it closes.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Context Menu where people act on many things in place, rows of a
table, files, cards on a board, objects on a canvas, and expect the right
click they know from desktop apps. Put the same actions behind a visible
control too, a row's "more" button or a toolbar: the right click is a
shortcut, not the way in.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ContextMenuStories.DoShortcutToVisible} />}
  doCaption="The right click repeats the row's visible actions menu."
  dont={<Story of={ContextMenuStories.DontOnlyWay} />}
  dontCaption="Actions only a right click reaches. Nothing on screen says they exist, and keyboard and touch users may never find them."
/>

## When not to use

- **For the only way to an action.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) from a visible
  button, or Buttons; add a Context Menu with the same items on top.
- **On text people read or copy.** A right click there should keep the
  browser's menu: copy, look up, translate.
- **For a tool's commands by category.** Use a
  [Menubar](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menubar--docs).

## Accessibility

- A right click on the area opens the menu at the pointer and outlines the
  area while it is open.
- The popup is Menu's: `role="menu"` with `menuitem` entries, and the keys
  inside are Menu's: the arrows move, Enter runs the action and closes.
- Shift+F10 or the Menu key open it from the keyboard: the browser fires
  `contextmenu` on the focused element, so the area, or a control in it,
  must take focus.
- Escape closes it and returns focus to where it was.
- Nothing announces that a context menu exists, so each of its items must
  also sit behind a visible control, such as the row's "more" button,
  named after the row.
- `disabled` leaves the browser's own menu in place.
- It is modal: page scroll is locked while it is open, so the menu is the
  only thing to interact with.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

  {

    note: "Matches the browser's own convention: an interactive element that doesn't navigate keeps the regular arrow, not a hand.",
    demo: <Button>Button</Button>,
  },
  {
    token: '--cursor-link',
    value: 'pointer',
    usage: 'A Button rendered as a real link',

    demo: <Button href="#cursors">Link</Button>,

  {

    value: 'not-allowed',
    usage: 'A disabled control that stays hoverable',
    note: 'TextInput uses this. Button does not — its disabled state is pointer-events: none, so it is never hovered and a cursor there would be dead CSS.',
    demo: (

] as const

# Cursors Three tokens, and a convention that surprises most people: **buttons do not get ...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as CursorsStories from './Cursors.stories'

<Meta of={CursorsStories} />

# Cursors

Three tokens, and a convention that surprises most people: **buttons do
not get `cursor: pointer`. Links do.**

## The convention

`cursor: pointer` means "this navigates" — it is the hand that appears
over a link. Browsers have never applied it to `<button>`, `<select>` or a
checkbox, and neither does this kit. Interactive elements that act on the
current page keep the regular arrow; only a link gets the hand. This is a
deliberate departure from the very common `button { cursor: pointer }`
reset.

It is worth knowing the argument on the other side: a large body of
usability opinion holds that the hand cursor is now such a widespread
affordance for "clickable" that removing it costs more than the semantic
purity gains. If your product takes that view, this is a one-line change —
see **Customization** below. The point of making it a token is that it is
one line, in one place, rather than a decision re-litigated per component.

<Canvas of={CursorsStories.Tokens} />

## `--cursor-button`

`default` — the regular arrow. Applied by Button.

Note this changes nothing visually today: a native `<button>` already
shows the arrow. **The token's job is not its current value; it is that
the value is reachable.** Without it, switching the kit to `pointer` means
editing every component; with it, it is one declaration.

## `--cursor-link`

`pointer` — the hand.

This one exists because the convention above has a second half that is
easy to state and easy to get wrong. Button takes `href`, so it can
render as a real `<a href>` — and when it did, it inherited
`--cursor-button` and lost the hand that the browser gives every other
link on the page. A link styled as a button is still a link.

```css
a[href].button {
  cursor: var(--cursor-link);
}
```

The `a[href]` part is doing real work. An `<a>` without `href` is not a
link and browsers do not give it the hand either, so matching on the
attribute rather than the element keeps the rule honest.

The distinction the kit draws is navigation versus action, not
appearance: a `<button>` styled as a link would still act on the current
page, so it would keep the arrow.

| | Element | Cursor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<Button>` | `<button>` | arrow |
| `<Button href="/x">` | `<a href>` | hand |

The Button `Href` story asserts this, and compares against a bare
`<a href>` rather than the literal `pointer` — so overriding
`--cursor-link` moves the assertion with it instead of breaking it.

## `--cursor-disabled`

`not-allowed` — used by TextInput, and **not** by Button. That asymmetry
is not an oversight.

A disabled `<input>` stays hit-testable, so a cursor set on it renders and
the user gets feedback on hover. Button's disabled state is
`pointer-events: none`, which makes the element untargetable; an
untargetable element is never hovered, so a cursor there would be dead
CSS. The `pointer-events: none` is not incidental — because Button
can render as an `<a>`, which ignores the `disabled` attribute entirely. Blocking pointer events is what actually disables it
in that case.

So the token applies to the pattern where a control stays hoverable while
disabled — including a control deliberately wrapped so a tooltip can
explain *why*. That trade-off, between a disabled control you can
interrogate and one that is inert, is a real design choice, and the two
components here happen to sit on opposite sides of it.

## Adding tokens

A mature system ends up with a token per interactive component —
checkboxes, menu items, radios, switches, slider thumbs. This kit has
three, because it has two components and one of them can render as two
different things.

{/* docs:check allow --cursor-slider-thumb -- an example of a token not to add */}

**Add a token when the component that needs it is built, not before.** A
`--cursor-slider-thumb` with no Slider is a value nobody can verify and
that the eventual Slider may not want.

## Customization

All three are plain CSS keywords, not colors, so they override like any
other custom property:

```css
:root {
  --cursor-button: pointer;
}
```

Load any override after Zweihänder's own stylesheet so the cascade picks it
up. Setting `--cursor-button: pointer` is the one-line version of adopting
the mainstream convention; it leaves `--cursor-link` alone, which is
already `pointer`, so the two simply converge.

# Dark mode Dark mode is **a class, not a media query.** `tokens.css` declares the light v...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DarkModeStories from './DarkMode.stories'

<Meta of={DarkModeStories} />

# Dark mode

Dark mode is **a class, not a media query.** `tokens.css` declares the
light values on `:root, .light` and the dark values on `.dark`, and
Every rule in the kit reads those variables, so the class is the only
switch there is. The same scopes set `color-scheme`, so the UI the browser
draws itself (scrollbars, date and select popups, autofill) switches with
them.

Nothing is automatic about it. Adding `class="dark"` to `<html>` is what
switches the document; without that, a device set to dark mode gets the
light theme. That is the trade — see **Following the system** below.

<Canvas of={DarkModeStories.SideBySide} />

## Components don't know about it

No component stylesheet — `Button.module.css`, `InputField.module.css` or any other — mentions `.dark`.
They write `background: var(--primary)`, and it is the variable that
changes; the rule is identical in both modes.

This is the main reason to reach for a token rather than a literal. A
hard-coded `#0a0a0a` is near-black in both modes and needs a `.dark`
override beside it to survive a theme switch; `var(--primary)` needs
nothing. Every theme conditional in a codebase is a place a value was
hardcoded and then patched.

## Dark is not an inversion

Flipping lightness would produce the wrong result in three places, and the
palette deliberately doesn't:

- **`--background` is neutral-950, not black.** A pure-black page makes
  the halation around light text worse and leaves no room to sit a surface
  *below* the page level.
- **Surfaces go up, not down.** `--card` and `--popover` are a step
  *lighter* than the page in dark mode and identical to it in light mode.
  Elevation in dark mode is carried by lightness, because a drop shadow
  has almost nothing left to darken (see
  [Shadows](?path=/docs/foundations-shadows--docs)).
- **Strong fills become light, so their labels become dark.**
  `--primary` goes from near-black to near-white, and
  `--primary-foreground` inverts with it. `--destructive` does the same,
  red-600 to red-400 — which is exactly where the palette's one contrast
  bug lived: keeping the near-white label on the lightened red measured
  2.77:1. It is now neutral-900 at 6.19:1. Inverting a fill without
  inverting its foreground is the single easiest dark-mode mistake to
  make.

Full measurements for both modes are in
[Color → Contrast](?path=/docs/foundations-colors--docs).

## Alpha for edges

`--border` and `--input` are the one place the palette uses transparency:
opaque neutral-200 in light, `white / 10%` and `white / 15%` in dark. An
opaque dark border would have to be re-chosen for every surface it sits
on; a translucent white edge lightens whatever is underneath, so the same
token reads correctly on `--background` and on a lifted `--card`.

## Scoping

`Theme` switches an appearance for a subtree rather than the document —
a dark footer on a light page, a light popover inside a dark shell. See
[Overview → Nesting](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs) for how the
nesting resolves and the one caveat that comes with it.

```tsx
<Theme appearance="dark">
  <Footer />
</Theme>
```

## Following the system

The kit ships no `prefers-color-scheme` handling, because the choice
between "follow the OS" and "remember what the user picked" belongs to the
app, not the component library. The usual shape:

```ts
const media = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')
const stored = localStorage.getItem('theme') // 'light' | 'dark' | null
const dark = stored ? stored === 'dark' : media.matches
document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', dark)
```

Two things worth getting right. Run it **before first paint** — in a
blocking inline script in `<head>`, not in a `useEffect` — or the page
renders light and flips, which is the flash every themed site has had at
some point. And keep listening to `media` afterwards so a user changing
their OS setting mid-session is followed, unless they have made an
explicit choice.

In this Storybook, the **Theme** toolbar control does the class toggle for
you; there is no persistence and no system detection.

const iso = (d: Date) =>
  `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`

/** The locale's numeric date format, its field order and a placeholder pattern. */
function useDateFormat(locale?: string) {
  return useMemo(() => {
    // Gregorian and Western digits whatever the locale's defaults: the grid is
    // Gregorian, and the parser reads ASCII digits. Without this, th-TH shows
    // the Buddhist year (2569) and fa-IR Persian digits, and neither reads back.
    const format = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {
      day: '2-digit',
      month: '2-digit',
      year: 'numeric',
      calendar: 'gregory',
      numberingSystem: 'latn',
    })
    const parts = format.formatToParts(new Date(2026, 10, 22))
    const order = parts.filter((p) => p.type === 'day' || p.type === 'month' || p.type === 'year').map((p) => p.type)
    const pattern = parts
      .map((p) => (p.type === 'day' ? 'dd' : p.type === 'month' ? 'mm' : p.type === 'year' ? 'yyyy' : p.value))
      .join('')
    /** Reads the three numbers in the locale's order; any separator will do. */
    const parse = (text: string): Date | null | undefined => {
      const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
      if (!text.trim()) return null
      if (!nums || nums.length !== 3) return undefined
      const v: Record<string, number> = {}
      order.forEach((type, i) => (v[type] = Number(nums[i])))
      const year = v.year < 100 ? 2000 + v.year : v.year
      const d = new Date(year, v.month - 1, v.day)
      // Rejects 31/02 and the like, which Date would roll into March.
      return d.getFullYear() === year && d.getMonth() === v.month - 1 && d.getDate() === v.day ? d : undefined
    }
    return { format: (d: Date) => format.format(d), parse, pattern }
  }, [locale])
}

export function DatePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DatePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const date = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => (date ? format(date) : ''))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [month, setMonth] = useState(() => date ?? today)
  // Follow a controlled value that changes from outside.
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(date)
  if (!isSameDay(shown, date) && !(shown === null && date === null)) {
    setShown(date)
    setText(date ? format(date) : '')
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: Date | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(next ? format(next) : '')
    setInvalid(false)
    if (next) setMonth(next)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  const commitText = () => {
    const parsed = parse(text)
    if (parsed === undefined || (parsed && !allowed(parsed))) setInvalid(true)
    else if (parsed === null ? date !== null : !isSameDay(parsed, date)) commit(parsed)
    else setInvalid(false)
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => setMonth(date ?? today)}
      triggerLabel={date ? `Choose date, ${format(date)} selected` : 'Choose date'}
      popupLabel="Choose date"
      hidden={name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={date ? iso(date) : ''} />}
      label={label}
      helperText={invalid ? `Enter a date as ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText}
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      placeholder={placeholder ?? pattern}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => (
        <Calendar
          value={date}
          month={month}
          onMonthChange={setMonth}
          onValueChange={(d) => {
            commit(d)
            close()
          }}
          min={min}
          max={max}
          isDateDisabled={isDateDisabled}
          locale={locale}
          weekStartsOn={weekStartsOn}
          autoFocus={autoFocus}
          className={styles.body}
        />
      )}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ range */

export interface DateRangePreset {
  label: string
  start: Date
  end: Date
}

/** The built-in presets, whole periods around today: Today … Last year. */
export function rangePresets(weekStartsOn: number, today = startOfDay(new Date())): DateRangePreset[] {
  const week = addDays(today, -((today.getDay() - weekStartsOn + 7) % 7))
  const y = today.getFullYear()
  const m = today.getMonth()
  return [
    { label: 'Today', start: today, end: today },
    { label: 'Yesterday', start: addDays(today, -1), end: addDays(today, -1) },
    { label: 'This week', start: week, end: addDays(week, 6) },
    { label: 'Last week', start: addDays(week, -7), end: addDays(week, -1) },
    { label: 'This month', start: new Date(y, m, 1), end: new Date(y, m + 1, 0) },
    { label: 'Last month', start: new Date(y, m - 1, 1), end: new Date(y, m, 0) },
    { label: 'This year', start: new Date(y, 0, 1), end: new Date(y, 11, 31) },
    { label: 'Last year', start: new Date(y - 1, 0, 1), end: new Date(y - 1, 11, 31) },
  ]
}

export interface DateRangePickerProps extends Omit<DatePickerProps, 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onValueChange' | 'name'> {
  /** Both ends set, or `null`. */
  value?: DateRange | null
  defaultValue?: DateRange | null
  onValueChange?: (range: DateRange | null) => void
  /** A list beside the calendars: `true` for the built-in one (Today … Last year), or your own. */
  presets?: boolean | DateRangePreset[]
  /** Submitted as `yyyy-mm-dd/yyyy-mm-dd`, an ISO 8601 interval. */
  name?: string
}

const NO_RANGE: DateRange = { start: null, end: null }
const monthIndex = (d: Date) => d.getFullYear() * 12 + d.getMonth()
/** The range's first month on the left, its last on the right; the next month when it spans one. */
const monthsFor = (r: DateRange | null, today: Date): [Date, Date] => {
  const left = r?.start ?? today
  const right = r?.end && monthIndex(r.end) > monthIndex(left) ? r.end : addMonths(left, 1)
  return [left, right]
}
/** The two days as a range, earlier first. */
const ordered = (a: Date | null, b: Date | null): DateRange => (a && b && b < a ? { start: b, end: a } : { start: a, end: b })
const sameRange = (a: DateRange | null, b: DateRange | null) =>
  a === b || (!!a && !!b && isSameDay(a.start, b.start) && isSameDay(a.end, b.end))

export function DateRangePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  presets = false,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DateRangePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const range = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const show = (r: DateRange | null) => (r?.start && r.end ? `${format(r.start)} – ${format(r.end)}` : '')
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => show(range))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<DateRange>(range ?? NO_RANGE)
  // The two calendars page on their own; the left one always shows the
  // earlier month. Moving one past the other pushes the other along.
  const [months, setMonths] = useState(() => monthsFor(range, today))
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(range)
  if (!sameRange(shown, range)) {
    setShown(range)
    setText(show(range))
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const presetList = presets === true ? rangePresets(weekStartsOn ?? firstDayOfWeek(locale), today) : presets || []
  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: DateRange | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(show(next))
    setInvalid(false)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  /** Two dates, each in the locale's order: six numbers, any separators. */
  const commitText = () => {
    const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
    let parsed: DateRange | null | undefined = null
    if (text.trim()) {
      const a = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(0, 3).join(' ')) : undefined
      const b = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(3).join(' ')) : undefined
      parsed = a && b && allowed(a) && allowed(b) ? ordered(a, b) : undefined
    }
    if (parsed === undefined) setInvalid(true)
    else if (!sameRange(parsed, range)) commit(parsed)
    else setText(show(range))
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => {
        setDraft(range ?? NO_RANGE)
        setMonths(monthsFor(range, today))
      }}
      triggerLabel={range ? `Choose dates, ${show(range)} selected` : 'Choose dates'}
      popupLabel="Choose dates"
      popupClassName={styles.rangePopup}
      hidden={
        name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={range?.start && range.end ? `${iso(range.start)}/${iso(range.end)}` : ''} />
      }
      label={label}
      helperText={
        invalid ? `Enter two dates as ${pattern} – ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText
      }
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      placeholder={placeholder ?? `${pattern} – ${pattern}`}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => {
        // A range applies as soon as both ends are in.
        const choose = (r: DateRange) => {
          setDraft(r)
          if (!r.start || !r.end) return
          if (!sameRange(r, range)) commit(r)
          close()
        }
        // The first click starts a range, the second ends it, either way round.
        const pick = (d: Date) => choose(!draft.start || draft.end ? { start: d, end: null } : ordered(draft.start, d))
        const calendar = { range: draft, onValueChange: pick, min, max, isDateDisabled, locale, weekStartsOn }
        return (
          <>
            {presetList.length > 0 && (
              <div role="group" aria-label="Presets" className={styles.presets}>
                {presetList.map((p) => (
                  <button
                    key={p.label}
                    type="button"
                    aria-pressed={isSameDay(p.start, draft.start) && isSameDay(p.end, draft.end)}
                    className={styles.preset}
                    onClick={() => {
                      setMonths(monthsFor(p, today))
                      choose({ start: p.start, end: p.end })
                    }}
                  >
                    {p.label}
                  </button>
                ))}
              </div>
            )}
            <div className={styles.months}>
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[0]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([, right]) => [m, monthIndex(m) < monthIndex(right) ? right : addMonths(m, 1)])}
                autoFocus={autoFocus}
                className={styles.body}
              />
              {/* Hidden on a narrow screen, where one month fits. */}
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[1]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([left]) => [monthIndex(left) < monthIndex(m) ? left : addMonths(m, -1), m])}
                className={cn(styles.body, styles.second)}
              />
            </div>
          </>
        )
      }}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

# Date Picker

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A date field: type the date, or pick it from a calendar.

<Status of={DatePickerStories} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two sizes, `sm` and `md`, and the field's validation states, as on
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs). The typed
order follows `locale`: day first in `en-GB` and `vi-VN`, month first in
`en-US`. The form always gets `yyyy-mm-dd`.

| Locale | Typed as |
| --- | --- |
| `en-GB`, `vi-VN` | `dd/mm/yyyy` |
| `en-US` | `mm/dd/yyyy` |

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.UnitedStates} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Vietnamese} />

`min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled` limit what can be picked or typed:

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Range} />

For a span of days, see
[Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs).

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { DatePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/date-picker.json
```

- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover), and the kit's [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Empty', content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" /> },
    { label: 'Filled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    {
      label: 'Error',
      content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" validationState="error" helperText="Enter a date as dd/mm/yyyy." />,
    },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 8, 18)} readOnly /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 8, 18)} disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 8, 18)} />
</States>

- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the field, drawn while
  the input has focus, by pointer too. In the error state the ring is
  `--danger-text`. The calendar button draws its own ring when tabbed to.
- **Error** turns the edge and the helper `--danger-text`. It is also
  shown on its own while the typed text is not a date, or is outside
  `min` and `max`: the helper then gives the expected pattern.
- **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the calendar icon darkens from
  `--muted-foreground` to `--foreground`.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--surface-filled`, as every
  Zweihänder field does. The input stays focusable and copyable and its
  value is submitted; the calendar icon stays but is not a button, so the
  calendar never opens. Say why in `helperText`.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity; the calendar button is
  disabled with it.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DatePickerStories} />
</div>

### Design notes

- **Typing is first-class.** Many people type a known date faster than
  they can page to it. Any separator works (`3.10.26`, `3/10/2026`); the
  field reformats on blur or Enter.
- **An impossible date is kept, not guessed.** `31/02/2026` stays as
  typed, the field turns to its error state and the helper shows the
  expected pattern; nothing is reported until it is a real date.
- **A click in the input opens the calendar, and keeps focus there.**
  Typing carries on with the month in view; the calendar button and
  Alt+Down move focus into the calendar instead.
- **The form gets ISO.** Whatever the display order, `name` submits
  `yyyy-mm-dd`, so the server never has to guess the locale.
### Differences from the spec

- **`onValueChange`, not `onChange`**, with a `Date` or `null`, as the
  kit's other value fields.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Date Picker for one date: a start date, a due date, a booking. Let
people type it when they know it, and pick it when they want to see the
week around it. Set `min`, `max` or `isDateDisabled` so a date that cannot
be used cannot be chosen, rather than refusing it after submit.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DatePickerStories.DoPatternPlaceholder} />}
  doCaption="The empty field shows the pattern to type, in the locale's order."
  dont={<Story of={DatePickerStories.DontExamplePlaceholder} />}
  dontCaption="An example date as the placeholder reads as a value already filled in."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a span of days.** Use a
  [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs):
  one field, both ends, never back to front.
- **To show a month on the page.** Use a
  [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) inline.
- **For a time of day.** The picker holds a date only.

## Accessibility

- The input is a labelled text box with `inputmode="numeric"` for a
  number keypad; while the text is not a valid date it has
  `aria-invalid` and the helper explains the format.
- The calendar button is named "Choose date", with the current date when
  there is one. Alt+Down in the input opens it too.
- `readOnly` puts `readonly` on the input: screen readers announce it,
  it stays in the tab order, and there is no calendar button; a click or
  Alt+Down opens nothing.
- The calendar opens as a dialog named "Choose date" with focus on the
  selected day; Escape closes it without a change.
- **After a pick the field goes back to rest.** Picked with the pointer,
  focus leaves the field (no caret, no ring), as in Combobox. Picked with
  the keyboard, focus returns to where it came from (the button, or the
  input), so keyboard and screen reader users are not dropped to the page.
- The field and calendar's own labels ("Choose date", "Previous month")
  are in English, like the rest of the kit's built-in labels.
- On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) the calendar button gets a 44×44px
  hit area without the field growing.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

const iso = (d: Date) =>
  `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`

/** The locale's numeric date format, its field order and a placeholder pattern. */
function useDateFormat(locale?: string) {
  return useMemo(() => {
    // Gregorian and Western digits whatever the locale's defaults: the grid is
    // Gregorian, and the parser reads ASCII digits. Without this, th-TH shows
    // the Buddhist year (2569) and fa-IR Persian digits, and neither reads back.
    const format = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {
      day: '2-digit',
      month: '2-digit',
      year: 'numeric',
      calendar: 'gregory',
      numberingSystem: 'latn',
    })
    const parts = format.formatToParts(new Date(2026, 10, 22))
    const order = parts.filter((p) => p.type === 'day' || p.type === 'month' || p.type === 'year').map((p) => p.type)
    const pattern = parts
      .map((p) => (p.type === 'day' ? 'dd' : p.type === 'month' ? 'mm' : p.type === 'year' ? 'yyyy' : p.value))
      .join('')
    /** Reads the three numbers in the locale's order; any separator will do. */
    const parse = (text: string): Date | null | undefined => {
      const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
      if (!text.trim()) return null
      if (!nums || nums.length !== 3) return undefined
      const v: Record<string, number> = {}
      order.forEach((type, i) => (v[type] = Number(nums[i])))
      const year = v.year < 100 ? 2000 + v.year : v.year
      const d = new Date(year, v.month - 1, v.day)
      // Rejects 31/02 and the like, which Date would roll into March.
      return d.getFullYear() === year && d.getMonth() === v.month - 1 && d.getDate() === v.day ? d : undefined
    }
    return { format: (d: Date) => format.format(d), parse, pattern }
  }, [locale])
}

export function DatePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DatePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const date = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => (date ? format(date) : ''))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [month, setMonth] = useState(() => date ?? today)
  // Follow a controlled value that changes from outside.
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(date)
  if (!isSameDay(shown, date) && !(shown === null && date === null)) {
    setShown(date)
    setText(date ? format(date) : '')
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: Date | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(next ? format(next) : '')
    setInvalid(false)
    if (next) setMonth(next)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  const commitText = () => {
    const parsed = parse(text)
    if (parsed === undefined || (parsed && !allowed(parsed))) setInvalid(true)
    else if (parsed === null ? date !== null : !isSameDay(parsed, date)) commit(parsed)
    else setInvalid(false)
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => setMonth(date ?? today)}
      triggerLabel={date ? `Choose date, ${format(date)} selected` : 'Choose date'}
      popupLabel="Choose date"
      hidden={name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={date ? iso(date) : ''} />}
      label={label}
      helperText={invalid ? `Enter a date as ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText}
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      placeholder={placeholder ?? pattern}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => (
        <Calendar
          value={date}
          month={month}
          onMonthChange={setMonth}
          onValueChange={(d) => {
            commit(d)
            close()
          }}
          min={min}
          max={max}
          isDateDisabled={isDateDisabled}
          locale={locale}
          weekStartsOn={weekStartsOn}
          autoFocus={autoFocus}
          className={styles.body}
        />
      )}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ range */

export interface DateRangePreset {
  label: string
  start: Date
  end: Date
}

/** The built-in presets, whole periods around today: Today … Last year. */
export function rangePresets(weekStartsOn: number, today = startOfDay(new Date())): DateRangePreset[] {
  const week = addDays(today, -((today.getDay() - weekStartsOn + 7) % 7))
  const y = today.getFullYear()
  const m = today.getMonth()
  return [
    { label: 'Today', start: today, end: today },
    { label: 'Yesterday', start: addDays(today, -1), end: addDays(today, -1) },
    { label: 'This week', start: week, end: addDays(week, 6) },
    { label: 'Last week', start: addDays(week, -7), end: addDays(week, -1) },
    { label: 'This month', start: new Date(y, m, 1), end: new Date(y, m + 1, 0) },
    { label: 'Last month', start: new Date(y, m - 1, 1), end: new Date(y, m, 0) },
    { label: 'This year', start: new Date(y, 0, 1), end: new Date(y, 11, 31) },
    { label: 'Last year', start: new Date(y - 1, 0, 1), end: new Date(y - 1, 11, 31) },
  ]
}

export interface DateRangePickerProps extends Omit<DatePickerProps, 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onValueChange' | 'name'> {
  /** Both ends set, or `null`. */
  value?: DateRange | null
  defaultValue?: DateRange | null
  onValueChange?: (range: DateRange | null) => void
  /** A list beside the calendars: `true` for the built-in one (Today … Last year), or your own. */
  presets?: boolean | DateRangePreset[]
  /** Submitted as `yyyy-mm-dd/yyyy-mm-dd`, an ISO 8601 interval. */
  name?: string
}

const NO_RANGE: DateRange = { start: null, end: null }
const monthIndex = (d: Date) => d.getFullYear() * 12 + d.getMonth()
/** The range's first month on the left, its last on the right; the next month when it spans one. */
const monthsFor = (r: DateRange | null, today: Date): [Date, Date] => {
  const left = r?.start ?? today
  const right = r?.end && monthIndex(r.end) > monthIndex(left) ? r.end : addMonths(left, 1)
  return [left, right]
}
/** The two days as a range, earlier first. */
const ordered = (a: Date | null, b: Date | null): DateRange => (a && b && b < a ? { start: b, end: a } : { start: a, end: b })
const sameRange = (a: DateRange | null, b: DateRange | null) =>
  a === b || (!!a && !!b && isSameDay(a.start, b.start) && isSameDay(a.end, b.end))

export function DateRangePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  presets = false,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DateRangePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const range = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const show = (r: DateRange | null) => (r?.start && r.end ? `${format(r.start)} – ${format(r.end)}` : '')
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => show(range))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<DateRange>(range ?? NO_RANGE)
  // The two calendars page on their own; the left one always shows the
  // earlier month. Moving one past the other pushes the other along.
  const [months, setMonths] = useState(() => monthsFor(range, today))
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(range)
  if (!sameRange(shown, range)) {
    setShown(range)
    setText(show(range))
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const presetList = presets === true ? rangePresets(weekStartsOn ?? firstDayOfWeek(locale), today) : presets || []
  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: DateRange | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(show(next))
    setInvalid(false)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  /** Two dates, each in the locale's order: six numbers, any separators. */
  const commitText = () => {
    const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
    let parsed: DateRange | null | undefined = null
    if (text.trim()) {
      const a = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(0, 3).join(' ')) : undefined
      const b = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(3).join(' ')) : undefined
      parsed = a && b && allowed(a) && allowed(b) ? ordered(a, b) : undefined
    }
    if (parsed === undefined) setInvalid(true)
    else if (!sameRange(parsed, range)) commit(parsed)
    else setText(show(range))
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => {
        setDraft(range ?? NO_RANGE)
        setMonths(monthsFor(range, today))
      }}
      triggerLabel={range ? `Choose dates, ${show(range)} selected` : 'Choose dates'}
      popupLabel="Choose dates"
      popupClassName={styles.rangePopup}
      hidden={
        name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={range?.start && range.end ? `${iso(range.start)}/${iso(range.end)}` : ''} />
      }
      label={label}
      helperText={
        invalid ? `Enter two dates as ${pattern} – ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText
      }
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      placeholder={placeholder ?? `${pattern} – ${pattern}`}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => {
        // A range applies as soon as both ends are in.
        const choose = (r: DateRange) => {
          setDraft(r)
          if (!r.start || !r.end) return
          if (!sameRange(r, range)) commit(r)
          close()
        }
        // The first click starts a range, the second ends it, either way round.
        const pick = (d: Date) => choose(!draft.start || draft.end ? { start: d, end: null } : ordered(draft.start, d))
        const calendar = { range: draft, onValueChange: pick, min, max, isDateDisabled, locale, weekStartsOn }
        return (
          <>
            {presetList.length > 0 && (
              <div role="group" aria-label="Presets" className={styles.presets}>
                {presetList.map((p) => (
                  <button
                    key={p.label}
                    type="button"
                    aria-pressed={isSameDay(p.start, draft.start) && isSameDay(p.end, draft.end)}
                    className={styles.preset}
                    onClick={() => {
                      setMonths(monthsFor(p, today))
                      choose({ start: p.start, end: p.end })
                    }}
                  >
                    {p.label}
                  </button>
                ))}
              </div>
            )}
            <div className={styles.months}>
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[0]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([, right]) => [m, monthIndex(m) < monthIndex(right) ? right : addMonths(m, 1)])}
                autoFocus={autoFocus}
                className={styles.body}
              />
              {/* Hidden on a narrow screen, where one month fits. */}
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[1]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([left]) => [monthIndex(left) < monthIndex(m) ? left : addMonths(m, -1), m])}
                className={cn(styles.body, styles.second)}
              />
            </div>
          </>
        )
      }}
    </PickerField>
  )
}
