# Date Range Picker A field for a span of days: a report period, a booking. Typed like [Da...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { DateRangePicker } from './DatePicker'
import * as DateRangePickerStories from './DateRangePicker.stories'

<Meta of={DateRangePickerStories} />

# Date Range Picker

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A field for a span of days: a report period, a booking. Typed like
[Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs), or picked
from two months side by side.

<Status of={DateRangePickerStories} />

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two sizes, `sm` and `md`, and the field's validation states, as on Date
Picker. With `presets`, whole periods sit beside the calendars.

| Option | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| No presets | Ranges that rarely line up with a calendar period: a booking, a leave request. |
| `presets` | Reports and filters, where people mostly want "Last month" or "This year". |

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.Presets} />

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.Vietnamese} />

## Resources

Shipped in the same file as Date Picker, which it shares its field and
popover with. From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { DateRangePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/date-picker.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover), and the kit's [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={DateRangePickerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={DateRangePickerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The popover holds:

- **Presets**, with `presets`: whole periods, Today to Last year, in a
  column beside the calendars, or a row above them on a narrow screen.
- **Calendars**: two months that page on their own, opening on the
  range's first and last months (this month and the next when empty). The
  left one always stays before the right: paging one past the other
  pushes the other along. One month on a screen narrower than 40rem.

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.PagingApart} />

## Measurements

The field is Date Picker's: each size is a control tier, with the normal
inline padding and the field radius.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad' },

/>

<SpecTable

    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Popover, every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Popover', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Each month', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Presets', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Preset', property: 'Minimum height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Preset', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-control' },
    { part: 'Preset', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

Presets are 2px apart and at least 7rem wide in the column. The field is
20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`; a range is longer than one date, so give
it room or `isFullWidth`.

The days and the band between the range's ends are the

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Empty', content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" /> },
    { label: 'Filled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    {
      label: 'Error',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" validationState="error" helperText="Choose both ends." />,
    },
    {
      label: 'Read-only',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} readOnly />,
    },
    {
      label: 'Disabled',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} disabled />,
    },
  ]}
>
  <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} />
</States>

The field's states are Date Picker's: a `--ring` outline while the input
has focus, `--danger-text` in error (also while the typed text is not a
range), `--surface-filled` and no calendar button when read-only, 50%
opacity when disabled. A preset matching the picked range
stays in its pressed look.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DateRangePickerStories} />
</div>

### Design notes

- **Either way round.** The first click starts the range, the second
  ends it; a second click before the first swaps them. So does typing
  the later date first.
- **Presets are whole periods.** "This month" is the 1st to the last
  day, not the 1st to today, so a preset reads the same all month.
- **No Cancel or Apply.** A range applies, and the popover closes, once
  both ends are in; Escape before the second click leaves the value as
  it was.
- **No hover preview.** The band shows once both ends are in; add a
  preview if testing shows people lose track of the first click.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Date Range Picker when the two dates are one thing: a period to
report on, a stay, a sprint. Both ends are set together, start never after
end, and the value is complete or `null`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DateRangePickerStories.DoOneField} />}
  doCaption="One field for one period: it cannot be half filled or set back to front."
  dont={<Story of={DateRangePickerStories.DontTwoFields} />}
  dontCaption="Two Date Pickers for one period: here the end is before the start, and nothing stops it."
/>

## When not to use

- **For one date.** Use a
  [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).
- **When one end is optional**, such as a contract with no end date. The
  range needs both ends; use two Date Pickers and check their order
  yourself.

## Accessibility

- As Date Picker: a labelled text box, an error state with the expected
  pattern, and the calendars in a dialog named "Choose dates".
- The calendar button is named "Choose dates", with the current range
  when there is one.
- `readOnly` works as on Date Picker: `readonly` on the input, no
  calendar button, and a click or Alt+Down opens nothing.
- Every day in the range has `aria-selected`, so the span is announced,
  not only its ends.
- A day of the month either side is decoration: hidden from assistive
  tech and not pickable, so each day is one button.
- Presets are toggle buttons in a group named "Presets"; the one that
  matches the picked range is `aria-pressed`.
- After both ends are in the field goes back to rest, as Date Picker's
  does after a pick.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import styles from './DescriptionList.module.css'

export interface DescriptionItem {
  term: string
  details: ReactNode
  /** An action for this row, e.g. an "Update" link. Shown at the row's end. */
  action?: ReactNode
  /** In the grid layout, take the full width: for long text or attachments. */
  isWide?: boolean
}

export interface DescriptionListProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'section'>, 'title'> {
  items: DescriptionItem[]
  title?: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  /** Buttons at the end of the header. */
  actions?: ReactNode
  /**
   * `columns`: term and details side by side, a row each.
   * `grid`: two columns of term-over-details pairs.
   * `stacked`: term over details, one after another. Columns fall back to
   * this on narrow screens anyway.
   */
  layout?: 'columns' | 'grid' | 'stacked'
  /** Put the list on a card with the header in its top band. */
  isCard?: boolean
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3
}

/**
 * The fields of a record as terms and details: a profile, an order, an
 * application. Read-only; its editable twin is a settings form.
 */
export function DescriptionList({
  items,
  title,
  description,
  actions,
  layout = 'columns',
  isCard = false,
  headingLevel = 2,
  className,
  ...props
}: DescriptionListProps) {
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  const hasHeader = title !== undefined || description !== undefined || actions !== undefined
  return (
    <section className={cn(styles.descriptionList, styles[layout], isCard && styles.card, className)} {...props}>
      {hasHeader && (
        <div className={styles.header}>
          <div className={styles.headerText}>
            {title && <Heading className={styles.title}>{title}</Heading>}
            {description && <p className={styles.description}>{description}</p>}
          </div>
          {actions && <div className={styles.actions}>{actions}</div>}
        </div>
      )}
      <dl className={styles.list}>
        {items.map((item) => (
          <div key={item.term} className={cn(styles.row, item.isWide && styles.wide, item.action !== undefined && styles.withAction)}>
            <dt className={styles.term}>{item.term}</dt>
            <dd className={styles.details}>{item.details}</dd>
            {item.action && <dd className={styles.action}>{item.action}</dd>}
          </div>
        ))}
      </dl>
    </section>
  )
}

# Description List The fields of a record, as terms and their details: a profile, an order...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DescriptionListStories from './DescriptionList.stories'

<Meta of={DescriptionListStories} />

# Description List

The fields of a record, as terms and their details: a profile, an order,
an application. It is read-only; its editable twin is a settings form in
Form Layouts.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/description-list.json
```

## Columns

Term and details side by side, a line between rows, and an optional
action at the end of each row ("Update").

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.Columns} />

## In a card

`isCard` puts the header in a top band and the list below it, inside one
border. With `layout="grid"`, fields run two to a row; `isWide` gives
long text and attachments the full width.

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.InCard} />

## Stacked

Term over details, one field after another: for a sidebar or a narrow
panel.

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.Stacked} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `DescriptionItem[]` | – | Required. `{ term, details, action?, isWide? }` |
| `title` | node | – | |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `actions` | node | – | Buttons at the end of the header. |
| `layout` | `columns`, `grid`, `stacked` | `columns` | |
| `isCard` | boolean | `false` | |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

<Controls of={DescriptionListStories.Columns} />

## Layout

- **It responds to its own width, not the viewport's.** Columns and grid
  are container queries: under 36rem of list width they stack, so the
  same list works in a main column, a sidebar and a phone.

  <Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.ColumnsNarrow} />

- Details wrap anywhere, so a long email address or URL never pushes the
  layout wide.

## Accessibility

- A real `<dl>`: a screen reader announces a list of terms and reads each
  detail with its term.
- Row actions sit in their own `<dd>` after the details. Give each one the
  field it acts on ("Update Email address"), hidden if you like, so a
  list of links is not six identical "Update"s.

import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Divider.module.css'

export interface DividerProps extends ComponentProps<'hr'> {
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /** Indents both ends so the line stops short of its container's edges. */
  inset?: boolean
  /** Line thickness: 1px, 2px, 4px. */
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** uiguideline calls this `variant`; renamed because `variant` means color here. */
  appearance?: 'solid' | 'dashed'
}

export function Divider({
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  inset = false,
  size = 'sm',
  appearance = 'solid',
  className,
  ...props
}: DividerProps) {
  return (
    <hr
      // <hr> is already role="separator" (horizontal). Only the vertical
      // case needs saying, or a screen reader announces the wrong axis.
      aria-orientation={orientation === 'vertical' ? 'vertical' : undefined}
      className={cn(
        styles.divider,
        styles[orientation],
        styles[size],
        styles[appearance],
        inset && styles.inset,
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

<Meta of={DividerStories} />

# Divider

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A thin line that separates content into groups: sections of a card, items
in a toolbar, blocks of a page.

<Status of={DividerStories} />

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `solid` | Almost everywhere: the quiet default. |
| `dashed` | A boundary that is softer or provisional: a drop zone, a "more below" break, a draft section. |

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Dashed} />

A **vertical** divider separates items in a row: toolbar groups, links in
a footer. It has no fixed height and stretches to its flex row.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Vertical} />

**Inset** stops the line short of the container's edges, so it aligns with
the text in a padded list rather than running edge to edge.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Inset} />

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Sizes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Divider } from 'zweihander/divider'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/divider.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/divider](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/divider)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={DividerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={DividerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

One part. The line is a border, top for horizontal and start for
vertical, and the box shrinks to it: a vertical divider is exactly as
wide as its line.

## Measurements

Thickness is whole pixels, not a token: the token layer has no
border-width scale, and a rule should stay a crisp pixel at every
`--scaling`.

| Size | Thickness |
| --- | --- |
| `sm` | 1px |
| `md` | 2px |
| `lg` | 4px |

<SpecTable
  caption="inset, every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Horizontal line', property: 'Inline margin', token: '--space-4' },
    { part: 'Vertical line', property: 'Block margin', token: '--space-2' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

Every size and appearance uses the same colour.

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Line', property: 'Colour', token: '--border' }]} />

## States

A divider is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. It looks the same
whether it is announced or decorative; only a screen reader tells them
apart.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Solid', content: <Stack><Divider /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Dashed', content: <Stack><Divider appearance="dashed" size="md" /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Inset', content: <Stack><Divider inset /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Decorative', content: <Stack><Divider aria-hidden /></Stack> },
  ]}
/>

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DividerStories} />
</div>

Every other `<hr>` attribute passes through, including `ref` and
`aria-hidden`.

### Differences from the spec

- **`appearance`, not `variant`.** In this kit `variant` always means a
  colour by intent (primary, destructive…) and `appearance` means a style.
  Solid versus dashed is a style.
- **Thickness is raw px.** The token layer has no border-width scale, and
  a divider is the only component that needs three.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Divider between groups that spacing alone does not separate: the
sections of a menu, the blocks of a settings page, groups in a toolbar.
Divide groups, not every item: a line after each row turns a list into
stripes and makes the real breaks harder to see.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DividerStories.DoDivideGroups} />}
  doCaption="One line between two groups: the break carries meaning."
  dont={<Story of={DividerStories.DontDivideEveryItem} />}
  dontCaption="A line after every item: nothing stands out as a group."
/>

## When not to use

- **Where space already separates.** Cards, list items with padding and
  headed sections are grouped by their own whitespace; a line adds noise.
- **As the only thing that tells groups apart.** The line is faint on
  purpose (see Accessibility). Pair it with a heading or space.
- **For a border of a component.** Draw that with the component's own
  border, not a Divider beside it.

## Accessibility

- `<hr>` is announced as a separator. Vertical dividers add
  `aria-orientation="vertical"`; horizontal ones don't, because that is
  already the default.
- If the line is purely decorative, e.g. between two icons that are
  already grouped, pass `aria-hidden` so it isn't announced at all.
- The `--border` colour is below 3:1 against the background on purpose: a
  divider is decoration and is not required to meet the non-text contrast
  ratio. Never let a divider be the only thing that tells groups apart.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { STORY_RENDERED } from 'storybook/internal/core-events'
import { addons } from 'storybook/preview-api'
import { expect, userEvent, waitFor, within } from 'storybook/test'
import { Button } from '@/components/buttons/Button'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '.'

/* Stories for the docs blocks themselves, tagged !dev: they run as tests (and
   a11y) like any story, but stay out of the sidebar and the Playground. The
   Internal / Docs blocks page shows them in use. */
const meta = {
  title: 'Internal/Docs blocks',
  tags: ['!dev'],
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

const example = (
  <Button startIcon={<Icon name="plus" />} size="md">
    Add item
  </Button>
)

const tabs = (
  <DocTabs>
    <DocTab value="overview">
      <p>What it is.</p>
    </DocTab>
    <DocTab value="specs">
      <p>How it is built.</p>
    </DocTab>
    <DocTab value="guidelines">
      <p>How to use it.</p>
    </DocTab>
  </DocTabs>
)

export const Tabs: Story = {
  render: () => tabs,
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('tablist', { name: 'Documentation' })).toBeVisible()
    const [overview, specs, guidelines] = canvas.getAllByRole('tab')
    await expect([overview, specs, guidelines].map((t) => t.textContent)).toEqual(['Overview', 'Specs', 'Guidelines'])
    // Overview first, always.
    await expect(overview).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true')
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('tabpanel')).toHaveTextContent('What it is.')
    // Mouse.
    await userEvent.click(specs)
    await waitFor(() => expect(canvas.getByRole('tabpanel')).toHaveTextContent('How it is built.'))
    // Arrow keys select as they move: a docs page, not a toolbar.
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowRight}')
    await waitFor(() => expect(guidelines).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true'))
    await waitFor(() => expect(canvas.getByRole('tabpanel')).toHaveTextContent('How to use it.'))
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}{ArrowLeft}')
    await waitFor(() => expect(overview).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true'))
    await expect(overview).toHaveFocus()
  },
}

const anatomy = (
  <Anatomy
    parts={[
      { name: 'Container', selector: 'button', description: 'The box.' },
      { name: 'Start icon', selector: 'svg', description: 'Decorative: `aria-hidden`.' },
    ]}
  >
    {example}
  </Anatomy>
)

export const AnatomyMarkers: Story = {
  name: 'Anatomy',
  render: () => anatomy,
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    // One marker per part, each named by number and part.
    const markers = await canvas.findAllByRole('img', { name: /^\d: / })
    await expect(markers.map((m) => m.getAttribute('aria-label'))).toEqual(['1: Container', '2: Start icon'])
    await expect(markers.map((m) => m.textContent)).toEqual(['1', '2'])
    // Each sits above its part, centred on it, with a line down to the part.
    for (const [marker, part] of [
      [markers[0], canvas.getByRole('button')],
      [markers[1], canvas.getByRole('button').querySelector('svg')!],
    ] as const) {
      const m = marker.getBoundingClientRect()
      const p = part.getBoundingClientRect()
      await expect(Math.abs(m.left + m.width / 2 - (p.left + p.width / 2))).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1)
      await expect(m.bottom).toBeLessThan(p.top)
      const line = (marker.previousElementSibling as HTMLElement).getBoundingClientRect()
      await expect(Math.abs(line.bottom - p.top)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1)
    }
    // The key lists every part.
    const key = canvas.getByRole('table')
    await expect(within(key).getByRole('rowheader', { name: 'Start icon' })).toBeVisible()
    await expect(key).not.toHaveTextContent('Not found')
    // Backticks in a description become inline code.
    await expect(within(key).getByText('aria-hidden').tagName).toBe('CODE')
    await expect(key).not.toHaveTextContent('`')
  },
}

export const AnatomyCrowded: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Anatomy
      parts={[
        { name: 'Container', selector: 'button' },
        { name: 'Label', selector: 'button' },
        { name: 'Again', selector: 'button' },
      ]}
    >
      {example}
    </Anatomy>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    // Parts with the same centre still get three markers that do not overlap:
    // one above, one below, one slid aside.
    const boxes = (await canvas.findAllByRole('img', { name: /^\d: / })).map((m) => m.getBoundingClientRect())
    await expect(boxes).toHaveLength(3)
    for (const [i, a] of boxes.entries())
      for (const b of boxes.slice(i + 1))
        await expect(a.right <= b.left || b.right <= a.left || a.bottom <= b.top || b.bottom <= a.top).toBe(true)
  },
}

export const AnatomyMissingPart: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Anatomy
      parts={[
        { name: 'Container', selector: 'button' },
        { name: 'Badge', selector: '[data-badge]' },
      ]}
    >
      {example}
    </Anatomy>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    // A selector that matches nothing gets no marker, and says so in the key.
    await expect(await canvas.findAllByRole('img', { name: /^\d: / })).toHaveLength(1)
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('table')).toHaveTextContent('Not found: [data-badge] matches nothing in the example.')
  },
}

const spec = (
  <SpecTable
    caption="Measurements, md"
    rows={[
      { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
      { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
      { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    ]}
  />
)

export const Spec: Story = {
  render: () => spec,
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const rows = canvas.getAllByRole('row').slice(1) as HTMLTableRowElement[]
    const value = (row: HTMLTableRowElement) => row.cells[3]
    // A length resolves to px, calc() and all.
    await expect(value(rows[0])).toHaveTextContent(/^32px$/)
    await expect(value(rows[0])).toHaveAttribute('data-kind', 'length')
    // A colour shows a swatch and the computed colour.
    const background = value(rows[1])
    await expect(background).toHaveAttribute('data-kind', 'color')
    await expect(background.querySelector('[aria-hidden="true"]')).not.toBeNull()
    // Anything else shows its declared value.
    await expect(value(rows[2])).toHaveAttribute('data-kind', 'raw')
    // The value follows the theme.
    const html = document.documentElement
    const wasDark = html.classList.contains('dark')
    const before = background.textContent
    html.classList.toggle('dark')
    try {
      await waitFor(() => expect(background.textContent).not.toBe(before))
    } finally {
      html.classList.toggle('dark', wasDark)
    }
    await waitFor(() => expect(background.textContent).toBe(before))
  },
}

const states = (
  <States
    states={[
      { label: 'Enabled' },
      { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
      { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
      { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
      {
        label: 'Disabled',
        content: (
          <Button startIcon={<Icon name="plus" />} disabled>
            Add item
          </Button>
        ),
      },
    ]}
  >
    {example}
  </States>
)

export const StateRow: Story = {
  name: 'States',
  render: () => states,
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    // Storybook announces each render, and the addon rewrites the stylesheets
    // then (docs pages included). The test runner announces nothing, so play
    // Storybook's part.
    addons.getChannel().emit(STORY_RENDERED)
    const cells = within(canvasElement).getAllByRole('listitem')
    await expect(cells.map((c) => c.lastElementChild!.textContent)).toEqual(['Enabled', 'Hover', 'Focus', 'Pressed', 'Disabled'])
    const stage = (label: string) => canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-state="${label}"]`)!
    await expect(stage('Hover')).toHaveClass('pseudo-hover-all')
    await expect(stage('Focus')).toHaveClass('pseudo-focus-visible-all')
    await expect(stage('Pressed')).toHaveClass('pseudo-active-all')
    await expect(stage('Disabled').querySelector('button')).toBeDisabled()
    // The forced states actually paint: the addon rewrote :hover and friends.
    const look = (label: string) => {
      const s = getComputedStyle(stage(label).querySelector('button')!)
      return `${s.backgroundColor} ${s.outlineStyle}`
    }
    // What the addon did to the stylesheets, for the failure message.
    const rewritten = () => {
      const button = stage('Hover').querySelector('button')!
      const rules = [...document.styleSheets].flatMap((sheet) => {
        try {
          return [...sheet.cssRules]
        } catch {
          return []
        }
      })
      const hover = rules.filter((r): r is CSSStyleRule => r instanceof CSSStyleRule && r.selectorText.includes(':hover'))
      const forced = hover.filter((r) => r.selectorText.includes('pseudo-hover-all'))
      const engaged = forced.filter((r) => button.matches(r.selectorText))
      return `${document.styleSheets.length} sheets, ${hover.length} :hover rules, ${forced.length} rewritten, ${engaged.length} reach the button: ${engaged.map((r) => r.cssText).join(' | ').slice(0, 300) || hover.find((r) => r.selectorText.includes('button'))?.cssText.slice(0, 300)}`
    }
    await waitFor(() => {
      // Again on each try: a stylesheet Vite injects late is rewritten too.
      addons.getChannel().emit(STORY_RENDERED)
      expect(look('Hover'), rewritten()).not.toBe(look('Enabled'))
    })
    // No transition to wait out: each state shows its end value at once.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(stage('Hover').querySelector('button')!).transitionDuration).toBe('0s')
    await expect(look('Pressed')).not.toBe(look('Hover'))
    await expect(getComputedStyle(stage('Focus').querySelector('button')!).outlineStyle).toBe('solid')
  },
}

  /** The button that opens it. Omit when `open` is controlled from elsewhere. */
  trigger?: ReactElement
  /** Required: it names the dialog. */
  title: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  children?: ReactNode
  /** Actions, pinned under the body, right-aligned: the main one last. */
  footer?: ReactNode
  /** The edge it slides in from, and the way a swipe dismisses it. */
  side?: 'right' | 'left' | 'bottom'
  /** Width of a side drawer: 20rem, 28rem, 40rem. Ignored at the bottom, which is full width. */
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  hasCloseButton?: boolean
  closeLabel?: string
  /** Close on a press on the backdrop. Turn off for a form that would lose its input. */
  closeOnBackdropClick?: boolean
  /**
   * While open, trap focus, lock page scroll and make the rest of the page
   * inert. `false` drops those three; the backdrop still covers the page.
   */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where the drawer renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Where focus goes on open. By default, the drawer itself, so its title is read first. */
  initialFocus?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
  className?: string
}

const swipeDirections = { right: 'right', left: 'left', bottom: 'down' } as const
const widths = { sm: styles.sm, md: styles.md, lg: styles.lg }

export function Drawer({
  trigger,
  title,
  description,
  children,
  footer,
  side = 'right',
  size = 'md',
  hasCloseButton = true,
  closeLabel = 'Close',
  closeOnBackdropClick = true,
  isModal = true,
  container,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  initialFocus,
  className,
}: DrawerProps) {
  return (
    <BaseDrawer.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}
      disablePointerDismissal={!closeOnBackdropClick}
      modal={isModal}
      swipeDirection={swipeDirections[side]}
    >
      {trigger && <BaseDrawer.Trigger render={trigger} />}
      <BaseDrawer.Portal container={container}>
        <BaseDrawer.Backdrop className={styles.backdrop} />
        <BaseDrawer.Viewport className={styles.viewport}>
          <BaseDrawer.Popup
            initialFocus={initialFocus}
            className={cn(styles.popup, side !== 'bottom' && widths[size], className)}
          >
            <div className={styles.header}>
              <BaseDrawer.Title className={styles.title}>{title}</BaseDrawer.Title>
              {hasCloseButton && (
                <BaseDrawer.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close}>
                  <Icon name="close" />
                </BaseDrawer.Close>
              )}
              {description && (
                <BaseDrawer.Description className={styles.description}>{description}</BaseDrawer.Description>
              )}
            </div>
            {/* Content lets a mouse select text without starting a swipe. A tab
                stop, so a keyboard can scroll a body that holds only text. */}
            {children && (
              <BaseDrawer.Content tabIndex={0} className={styles.body}>
                {children}
              </BaseDrawer.Content>
            )}
            {footer && <div className={styles.footer}>{footer}</div>}
          </BaseDrawer.Popup>
        </BaseDrawer.Viewport>
      </BaseDrawer.Portal>
    </BaseDrawer.Root>
  )
}

/** A button inside the drawer that closes it, e.g. "Cancel": `<DrawerClose render={<Button />}>Cancel</DrawerClose>`. */
export const DrawerClose = BaseDrawer.Close

# Drawer A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen, over the page, for work that s...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as DrawerStories from './Drawer.stories'

<Meta of={DrawerStories} />

# Drawer

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen, over the page, for work
that sits beside what the reader was doing: filters, a quick look at a
record, a short form.

<Status of={DrawerStories} />

<Canvas of={DrawerStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Side | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Right (default) | Details and editing: a quick look at a record from its list, a create or edit form, notifications. |
| Left | Content tied to the left of the page, such as a panel for the list or tree beside it. |
| Bottom | A short sheet as tall as its content: share, a few actions, a picker. Works best on a phone. |

<Canvas of={DrawerStories.Sides} />

`size` sets the width of a side drawer: `sm` (20rem) for filters, `md`
(28rem) for a form, `lg` (40rem) for a record with a lot to show. A side
drawer always leaves a touch target's width of backdrop, so on a phone it
is nearly full width and can still be tapped away. For short content on
a phone, pick `bottom` yourself: the side does not change with the
screen. Taller than the
screen, the body scrolls and the header and footer stay in view.

<Canvas of={DrawerStories.Long} />

On a touch screen it can also be swiped back towards its edge.

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Drawer, DrawerClose } from 'zweihander/drawer'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/drawer.json
```

- Source: [src/components/overlays/Drawer.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Drawer.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/drawer](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/drawer)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Drawer](https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={DrawerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={DrawerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open drawers on this tab and the next are pictures: real drawers
rendered in a frame with `container`, not modal (`isModal={false}`) and
inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Container"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Header, body, footer', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-xl' },
    { part: 'Bottom sheet', property: 'Top corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Backdrop left beside it', property: 'Minimum', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-heading-sm' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-heading-sm' },
    { part: 'Title to close button', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Title to description', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Footer', property: 'Gap between actions', token: '--space-inline' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Close button"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Padding', token: '--control-xs-gap' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

A side drawer is full height and at most 20rem (`sm`), 28rem (`md`) or
40rem (`lg`) wide. A bottom sheet is full width and as tall as its content,
up to the screen less `--target-coarse`. Borders are 1px: on the edge that
faces the page, under the header and over the footer. Backdrop and drawer
sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and slide in over `--duration-base`.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Every drawer"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Backdrop', property: 'Background', token: '--scrim' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Container, header, footer', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Title, body', property: 'Colour', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Description', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

Buttons in the footer keep their own colours: see Button.

## States

The drawer is open or closed. Opening fades the backdrop in and slides the
container in from its edge; closing reverses it. During a swipe the
container follows the finger and the backdrop fades with it. The close
button is the only part with states of its own:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={DrawerStories.CloseButton} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills the button with `--accent`.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the button.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DrawerStories} />
</div>

`DrawerClose` closes the drawer it is in. Give it your own button with
`render`: `<DrawerClose render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Cancel</DrawerClose>`.

### Differences from the spec

- **No push mode.** A drawer always covers the page with a scrim. A panel
  that pushes the page aside is part of the page's layout, not an overlay:
  build it into the page.
- **No top side.** Nothing in a business app slides down from the top
  that a Menu or a Toast does not already cover.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a drawer when the reader needs the context behind it: a record looked
at from its list, filters for the table they are reading, a form that
fills in something on the page. The page stays visible, dimmed, at its
place.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DrawerStories.DoQuickView} />}
  doCaption="Show a record from its list in a drawer: the list stays in place behind it, where the reader left it."
  dont={<Story of={DrawerStories.DontConfirm} />}
  dontCaption="Do not ask a yes-or-no question at the edge of the screen. A decision belongs in a Modal with isAlert."
/>

Put the main action last in the footer, and dismiss actions (Cancel,
Clear) in the `secondary` variant. A form that would lose its input sets
`closeOnBackdropClick={false}`.

## When not to use

- **For a decision or a confirmation.** Use a
  [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`, or a
  [Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs)
  before a delete: it sits in the middle, where the reader is looking.
- **For a small form tied to one button.** Use a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs): it opens beside
  the button and leaves the page usable.
- **For site navigation.** Keep it in the sidebar; on a phone the sidebar
  folds to its icon rail.
- **For a long or many-step task.** Give it a page of its own.
- **Over another drawer or a modal.** Close the first, or move the second
  step into it.

## Accessibility

- `role="dialog"`, named by the title and described by the description.
- Opening moves focus to the drawer itself, so its title and description
  are read first and a phone does not pop up its keyboard; Tab then
  reaches the close button. Focus is trapped inside. The page behind is `aria-hidden` and its scroll is
  locked. Closing returns focus to the trigger.

  <Canvas of={DrawerStories.Default} />

- The body is a tab stop after the close button, so a keyboard can scroll
  a long body of text.

  <Canvas of={DrawerStories.Long} />

- `initialFocus` sends focus to another element on open, such as the
  first field of a form.

  <Canvas of={DrawerStories.InitialFocus} />

- Escape, a press outside the drawer and the close button each close it.
  The close button is named `Close` (`closeLabel`). Swiping is never the
  only way out.

  <Canvas of={DrawerStories.Dismissing} />

- With `closeOnBackdropClick={false}`, a press outside does nothing;
  Escape still closes it.

  <Canvas of={DrawerStories.KeepInput} />

- A Select opened inside a drawer lists its options above it: both sit at
  `--layer-overlay`, and the one opened last is on top.

  <Canvas of={DrawerStories.Left} />

- `side` is physical: on a right-to-left page a right drawer is still on
  the right, and swipes right to close.

  <Canvas of={DrawerStories.RightToLeft} />

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Empty State What a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet: why it...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as EmptyStateStories from './EmptyState.stories'

<Meta of={EmptyStateStories} />

# Empty State

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

What a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet: why
it is empty, and what to do about it.

<Status of={EmptyStateStories} />

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.FirstUse} />

## Variants

There are three kinds of empty, and they need three kinds of copy. The
component is the same; the words and the action are not.

| Kind | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| First use | Nothing has been made yet. Say what will live here, and offer the way in: "No projects yet", New project. |
| No results | A search or a filter matched nothing. Say what was searched, and offer to clear it: "No projects match", Clear search. |
| Cleared out | Everything is done. Often no action at all: "All caught up". |

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.TitleOnly} />

`size="sm"` fits a panel or a table body; `md` fills a page or a section.

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.Small} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { EmptyState } from 'zweihander/empty-state'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/empty-state.json

action does, and those are the action's own (here, an outlined Button).

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Empty State wherever a list, a table or a page can have nothing in
it: before the first item is made, after a search matches nothing, when
everything is done. Write the title for the reader's situation, and give
them the next step.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={EmptyStateStories.FirstUse} />}
  doCaption="Say what is empty and what will live here, and offer the way in."
  dont={<Story of={EmptyStateStories.DontNoData} />}
  dontCaption="“No data” says neither why nor what to do next."
/>

## When not to use

- **When loading failed.** Use an
  [Error State](?path=/docs/components-states-errorstate--docs): "No
  projects" when the request failed tells the reader their work is gone.
- **When a flow has finished.** Use a
  [Success State](?path=/docs/components-states-successstate--docs).
- **While content is loading.** Use a Skeleton or a Spinner: an empty
  state shown before the data arrives flashes the wrong message.

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading, so a screen reader user jumping by
  headings finds out the area is empty. Set `headingLevel` to fit the
  outline: `3` inside a section headed by an `h2`.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title has to say it all.
- It is not a live region, so it is not announced when it replaces
  results. If a search updates as you type, announce the count elsewhere,
  in a `role="status"` line such as "0 results".

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { EmptyState, type EmptyStateProps } from './EmptyState'
import styles from './ErrorState.module.css'

export interface ErrorStateProps extends Omit<EmptyStateProps, 'title'> {
  /** What failed, in the reader's words. */
  title?: ReactNode
  /** A reference for support, e.g. an error code or request id. Shown small, selectable. */
  details?: ReactNode
  /** Announce it when it replaces content that was loading (`role="alert"`). */
  isLive?: boolean
}

/**
 * What a list, panel or page shows when loading it failed: why, and a way
 * forward, usually a retry. Empty State's layout in the danger tone.
 */
export function ErrorState({
  title = 'Something went wrong',
  icon = <Icon name="danger" />,
  description,
  details,
  isLive = false,
  className,
  ...props
}: ErrorStateProps) {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      role={isLive ? 'alert' : undefined}
      title={title}
      icon={icon}
      description={
        (description || details) && (
          <>
            {description}
            {details && <span className={styles.details}>{details}</span>}
          </>
        )
      }
      className={cn(styles.error, className)}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Error State in place of content that failed to load: a list, a
panel, a whole page. Say what failed in the reader's words, say that
nothing is lost when that is true, and offer a way forward.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ErrorStateStories.Default} />}
  doCaption="Say what failed, that nothing is lost, and offer to try again."
  dont={<Story of={ErrorStateStories.DontRawError} />}
  dontCaption="A raw error is for developers, and with no action the reader is stuck."
/>

Details are for support, not for the reader: keep them small and
selectable so they can be pasted into a message.

## When not to use

- **When there is simply nothing there.** Use an
  [Empty State](?path=/docs/components-states-emptystate--docs).
- **When an action failed but the screen is fine**, such as a save. Use an
  Alert or a Toast and keep the reader's work on screen.
- **For a field's error.** Show it on the field, through its own error
  message.

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading, as on Empty State. Set `headingLevel` to
  fit the outline.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title says what failed.
- `isLive` makes it a `role="alert"`: use it when the error replaces
  content that was loading, so a screen reader hears that it failed.
  Without it, nothing is announced.

'use client'

import {
  useEffect,
  useId,
  useMemo,
  useRef,
  useState,
  type ComponentProps,
  type CSSProperties,
  type Key,
  type KeyboardEvent,
  type ReactNode,
} from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import type { TagVariant } from '../../atomic-elements/Tag'
import { Button } from '../../buttons/Button'
import { Calendar, addDays, addMonths, firstDayOfWeek, isSameDay, startOfDay } from '../../data-display/Calendar'
import { Select } from '../../inputs/Select'
import styles from './EventCalendar.module.css'

export type EventCalendarView = 'day' | 'week' | 'month' | 'year'

export interface CalendarEvent {
  id: Key
  title: string
  start: Date
  /** When it ends. Without it the event is a moment. For an all-day event, the last day it covers. */
  end?: Date
  /** Covers whole days: no time is shown, and the day and week views put it in the all-day row. */
  allDay?: boolean
  /** A Tag variant: a status or a hue, e.g. one per kind of event. */
  color?: TagVariant
  /** Makes the event a link. */
  href?: string
}

export interface EventCalendarProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children' | 'title'> {
  /** The events to show. The calendar picks those that fall in view; it never changes them. */
  events: CalendarEvent[]
  /** The view shown, when you control it. */
  view?: EventCalendarView
  defaultView?: EventCalendarView
  onViewChange?: (view: EventCalendarView) => void
  /** The views offered in the switch, in its order. One view hides the switch. */
  views?: EventCalendarView[]
  /** The selected day; the view shows the day, week, month or year around it. */
  date?: Date
  defaultDate?: Date
  onDateChange?: (date: Date) => void
  /** Makes events without `href` buttons, e.g. to open them in a Drawer. */
  onEventClick?: (event: CalendarEvent) => void
  /** At the end of the header, e.g. an "Add event" Button. */
  actions?: ReactNode
  /** Lists the selected day's events under the month view. A narrow month shows dots, so this is where its events are read. */
  hasEventList?: boolean
  /** The level of the title (the month, week, day or year shown). */
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4
  /** BCP 47 tag, e.g. `vi-VN`. Defaults to the browser's. */
  locale?: string
  /** 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Defaults to the locale's. */
  weekStartsOn?: number
}

const VIEWS: EventCalendarView[] = ['day', 'week', 'month', 'year']
const VIEW_LABEL: Record<EventCalendarView, string> = { day: 'Day', week: 'Week', month: 'Month', year: 'Year' }
// A month cell lists this many, then "n more" leads to the day or the list.
const PER_CELL = 3
// A moment or a short event still gets a readable block in the day and week views.
const MIN_BLOCK_MS = 30 * 60_000

/** The last instant an event covers: its end day when all-day, else just before its end. */
const lastOf = (e: CalendarEvent) => {
  const end = e.end ?? e.start
  // An end before the start is read as a moment, so the event still shows.
  if (end <= e.start) return e.start
  return e.allDay ? end : new Date(end.getTime() - 1)
}
/** Whether an event covers any part of a day (a local midnight). */
const occursOn = (e: CalendarEvent, day: Date) => startOfDay(e.start) <= day && day <= startOfDay(lastOf(e))
/** All-day, or crossing midnight: these sit in the all-day row rather than on the hour grid. */
const isAllDayRow = (e: CalendarEvent) => !!e.allDay || !isSameDay(e.start, lastOf(e))
const blockEnd = (e: CalendarEvent) => Math.max((e.end ?? e.start).getTime(), e.start.getTime() + MIN_BLOCK_MS)
const byStart = (a: CalendarEvent, b: CalendarEvent) =>
  Number(isAllDayRow(b)) - Number(isAllDayRow(a)) || a.start.getTime() - b.start.getTime()

interface PlacedEvent {
  event: CalendarEvent
  /** The column it takes among the events it overlaps, and how many columns they need. */
  col: number
  cols: number
}

/** Side by side where timed events overlap: each cluster of overlapping events shares the width evenly. */
function layoutDay(events: CalendarEvent[]): PlacedEvent[] {
  const sorted = [...events].sort((a, b) => a.start.getTime() - b.start.getTime() || blockEnd(b) - blockEnd(a))
  const placed: PlacedEvent[] = []
  let cluster: PlacedEvent[] = []
  let columns: number[] = []
  let clusterEnd = -Infinity
  const close = () => {
    for (const p of cluster) p.cols = columns.length
    cluster = []
    columns = []
  }
  for (const event of sorted) {
    const start = event.start.getTime()
    if (start >= clusterEnd) close()
    let col = columns.findIndex((busyUntil) => busyUntil <= start)
    if (col < 0) col = columns.push(0) - 1
    columns[col] = blockEnd(event)
    clusterEnd = Math.max(clusterEnd, blockEnd(event))
    const p = { event, col, cols: 0 }
    cluster.push(p)
    placed.push(p)
  }
  close()
  return placed
}

/** The Tag palette as custom properties the CSS reads. Neutral has no ramp, as in Tag. */
const colorVars = (c: TagVariant = 'info') =>
  (c === 'neutral'
    ? { '--event-subtle': 'var(--secondary)', '--event-text': 'var(--secondary-foreground)', '--event-solid': 'var(--foreground)' }
    : { '--event-subtle': `var(--${c}-subtle)`, '--event-text': `var(--${c}-text)`, '--event-solid': `var(--${c})` }) as CSSProperties

/**
 * Events on a day, week, month or year grid, with a header to move
 * through time and switch views. Owns no events: it shows what it is given.
 */
export function EventCalendar({
  events,
  view: viewProp,
  defaultView = 'month',
  onViewChange,
  views = VIEWS,
  date: dateProp,
  defaultDate,
  onDateChange,
  onEventClick,
  actions,
  hasEventList = false,
  headingLevel = 2,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  className,
  ...props
}: EventCalendarProps) {
  const [viewState, setViewState] = useState(defaultView)
  const view = viewProp ?? viewState
  const [dateState, setDateState] = useState(() => startOfDay(defaultDate ?? new Date()))
  const date = dateProp ? startOfDay(dateProp) : dateState
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const first = weekStartsOn ?? firstDayOfWeek(locale)
  const titleId = useId()
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const scrollerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const moveFocus = useRef(false)

  const fmt = useMemo(() => {
    const f = (o: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions) => new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { calendar: 'gregory', ...o })
    return {
      month: f({ month: 'long', year: 'numeric' }),
      range: f({ month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' }),
      full: f({ dateStyle: 'full' }),
      year: f({ year: 'numeric' }),
      weekday: f({ weekday: 'short' }),
      weekdayLong: f({ weekday: 'long' }),
      day: f({ day: 'numeric' }),
      time: f({ timeStyle: 'short' }),
      hour: f({ hour: 'numeric' }),
    }
  }, [locale])

  const setView = (v: EventCalendarView) => {
    setViewState(v)
    onViewChange?.(v)
  }
  const setDate = (d: Date) => {
    setDateState(startOfDay(d))
    onDateChange?.(startOfDay(d))
  }
  /** From a summary (a year's day, a month's "n more") to the day itself. */
  const openDay = (d: Date) => {
    setDate(d)
    if (views.includes('day')) setView('day')
    else if (views.includes('month')) setView('month')
  }

  const weekStart = addDays(date, -((date.getDay() - first + 7) % 7))
  const days = view === 'week' ? Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, i) => addDays(weekStart, i)) : [date]
  const on = (day: Date) => events.filter((e) => occursOn(e, day)).sort(byStart)

  const step = (n: number) =>
    setDate(
      view === 'month'
        ? addMonths(date, n)
        : view === 'year'
          ? addMonths(date, 12 * n)
          : addDays(date, view === 'week' ? 7 * n : n),
    )
  const title =
    view === 'month'
      ? fmt.month.format(date)
      : view === 'year'
        ? fmt.year.format(date)
        : view === 'week'
          ? fmt.range.formatRange(days[0], days[6])
          : fmt.full.format(date)

  // The day and week views open an hour before the first timed event on
  // show, or at 8:00, so the hour's label is in view too.
  const shownKey = days.map((d) => d.getTime()).join()
  useEffect(() => {
    const el = scrollerRef.current
    if (!el) return
    const hours = days.flatMap((d) =>
      on(d)
        .filter((e) => !isAllDayRow(e))
        .map((e) => e.start.getHours()),
    )
    el.scrollTop = ((hours.length ? Math.max(Math.min(...hours) - 1, 0) : 8) / 24) * el.scrollHeight
    // Not on `events`: events loading later must not yank the viewer's scroll.
  }, [view, shownKey]) // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps

  // Arrow keys moved the selected day: focus follows it to its button.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!moveFocus.current) return
    moveFocus.current = false
    rootRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-day][tabindex="0"]')?.focus()
  })

  const onMonthKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLElement>) => {
    if (!(e.target as HTMLElement).hasAttribute('data-day')) return
    // Right to left mirrors the grid, so the arrows follow what is on screen.
    const ahead = getComputedStyle(e.currentTarget).direction === 'rtl' ? -1 : 1
    const by = ({ ArrowLeft: -ahead, ArrowRight: ahead, ArrowUp: -7, ArrowDown: 7 } as Record<string, number>)[e.key]
    if (!by) return
    e.preventDefault()
    moveFocus.current = true
    setDate(addDays(date, by))
  }

  const eventItem = (event: CalendarEvent, withTime = true, position?: CSSProperties) => {
    const content = (
      <>
        <span className={styles.eventTitle}>{event.title}</span>{' '}
        {withTime && !isAllDayRow(event) && (
          <time dateTime={event.start.toISOString()} className={styles.time}>
            {fmt.time.format(event.start)}
          </time>
        )}
      </>
    )
    const shared = { className: styles.event, style: colorVars(event.color) }
    return (
      <li key={event.id} className={styles.eventSlot} style={position}>
        {event.href ? (
          <a {...shared} href={event.href}>
            {content}
          </a>
        ) : onEventClick ? (
          <button {...shared} type="button" onClick={() => onEventClick(event)}>
            {content}
          </button>
        ) : (
          <span {...shared}>{content}</span>
        )}
      </li>
    )
  }

  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  const SubHeading = `h${headingLevel + 1}` as 'h3' | 'h4' | 'h5'

  const month = () => {
    const start = new Date(date.getFullYear(), date.getMonth(), 1)
    const lead = (start.getDay() - first + 7) % 7
    const length = new Date(date.getFullYear(), date.getMonth() + 1, 0).getDate()
    const gridStart = addDays(start, -lead)
    const weeks = Array.from({ length: Math.ceil((lead + length) / 7) }, (_, w) =>
      Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, d) => addDays(gridStart, w * 7 + d)),
    )
    // Cut the list short only where "n more" leads to a place that lists them all.
    const limit = views.includes('day') || hasEventList ? PER_CELL : Infinity
    return (
      <table className={styles.month} aria-labelledby={titleId} onKeyDown={onMonthKeyDown}>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            {weeks[0].map((d) => (
              <th key={d.getDay()} scope="col" abbr={fmt.weekdayLong.format(d)} className={styles.weekday}>
                {fmt.weekday.format(d)}
              </th>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {weeks.map((week, w) => (
            <tr key={w}>
              {week.map((d) => {
                const list = on(d)
                // "n more" takes the last line, so it never says "1 more".
                const shown = list.length > limit ? list.slice(0, limit - 1) : list
                const more = list.length - shown.length
                return (
                  <td key={d.getTime()} className={styles.cell} data-outside={d.getMonth() !== date.getMonth() || undefined}>
                    <button
                      type="button"
                      data-day=""
                      tabIndex={isSameDay(d, date) ? 0 : -1}
                      aria-label={
                        fmt.full.format(d) + (list.length ? `, ${list.length} ${list.length === 1 ? 'event' : 'events'}` : '')
                      }
                      aria-pressed={isSameDay(d, date)}
                      aria-current={isSameDay(d, today) ? 'date' : undefined}
                      className={styles.dayNumber}
                      onClick={() => setDate(d)}
                    >
                      {fmt.day.format(d)}
                    </button>
                    {list.length > 0 && (
                      <>
                        {/* A narrow month has no room for titles: dots say there is
                            something, the day's label says how many. */}
                        <span className={styles.dots} aria-hidden="true">
                          {list.slice(0, PER_CELL).map((e) => (
                            <span key={e.id} className={styles.dot} style={colorVars(e.color)} />
                          ))}
                        </span>
                        <ul className={styles.cellEvents}>
                          {shown.map((e) => eventItem(e))}
                          {more > 0 && (
                            <li>
                              <button
                                type="button"
                                className={styles.more}
                                aria-label={`${more} more on ${fmt.full.format(d)}`}
                                onClick={() => openDay(d)}
                              >
                                {more} more
                              </button>
                            </li>
                          )}
                        </ul>
                      </>
                    )}
                  </td>
                )
              })}
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    )
  }

  const timeGrid = () => {
    const allDay = days.map((d) => on(d).filter(isAllDayRow))
    return (
      <div className={styles.timeGrid} style={{ '--days': days.length } as CSSProperties}>
        {days.length > 1 && (
          // The columns carry their dates as labels; this row is for the eye.
          <div className={styles.dayHeads} aria-hidden="true">
            {days.map((d) => (
              <div key={d.getTime()} className={styles.dayHead}>
                {fmt.weekday.format(d)}{' '}
                <span className={cn(styles.headNumber, isSameDay(d, today) && styles.today)}>{fmt.day.format(d)}</span>
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
        )}
        {allDay.some((l) => l.length > 0) && (
          <div className={styles.allDay}>
            <span className={styles.allDayLabel}>All day</span>
            {days.map((d, i) => (
              <ul key={d.getTime()} className={styles.allDayEvents} aria-label={`All day, ${fmt.full.format(d)}`}>
                {allDay[i].map((e) => eventItem(e, false))}
              </ul>
            ))}
          </div>
        )}
        {/* It scrolls, so it takes focus: the hours can be read without a pointer. */}
        <div ref={scrollerRef} className={styles.scroller} tabIndex={0} role="group" aria-label="Schedule">
          <div className={styles.hours} aria-hidden="true">
            {Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, h) => (
              <span key={h} className={styles.hour}>
                {h > 0 && fmt.hour.format(new Date(2000, 0, 1, h))}
              </span>
            ))}
          </div>
          {days.map((d) => {
            // By the clock, not elapsed time, so an event lines up with its
            // hour's label on a daylight-saving day too.
            const next = addDays(d, 1).getTime()
            const at = (t: number) => {
              if (t <= d.getTime()) return 0
              if (t >= next) return 100
              const c = new Date(t)
              return ((c.getHours() + c.getMinutes() / 60) / 24) * 100
            }
            return (
              <ul key={d.getTime()} className={styles.column} aria-label={fmt.full.format(d)}>
                {layoutDay(on(d).filter((e) => !isAllDayRow(e))).map(({ event, col, cols }) => {
                  const top = at(event.start.getTime())
                  return eventItem(event, true, {
                    insetBlockStart: `${top}%`,
                    blockSize: `${at(blockEnd(event)) - top}%`,
                    insetInlineStart: `${(col / cols) * 100}%`,
                    inlineSize: `${100 / cols}%`,
                  })
                })}
              </ul>
            )
          })}
        </div>
      </div>
    )
  }

  const year = () => (
    <div className={styles.year}>
      {Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, m) => {
        const start = new Date(date.getFullYear(), m, 1)
        // Bounded to its own month, so its arrows are off (and hidden): the
        // year moves with the header's.
        return (
          <Calendar
            key={m}
            month={start}
            min={start}
            max={new Date(date.getFullYear(), m + 1, 0)}
            value={date.getMonth() === m ? date : null}
            onValueChange={openDay}
            locale={locale}
            weekStartsOn={first}
          />
        )
      })}
    </div>
  )

  const selected = on(date)

  return (
    <div ref={rootRef} className={cn(styles.root, className)} data-view={view} {...props}>
      <div className={styles.header}>
        <Heading id={titleId} className={styles.title} aria-live="polite">
          {title}
        </Heading>
        <div className={styles.nav}>
          <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" isIconOnly aria-label={`Previous ${view}`} onClick={() => step(-1)}>
            <Icon name="chevron-left" className={styles.dirIcon} />
          </Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" appearance="outlined" onClick={() => setDate(today)}>
            Today
          </Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" isIconOnly aria-label={`Next ${view}`} onClick={() => step(1)}>
            <Icon name="chevron-right" className={styles.dirIcon} />
          </Button>
        </div>
        {views.length > 1 && (
          <Select
            aria-label="View"
            className={styles.viewSelect}
            options={views.map((v) => ({ value: v, label: VIEW_LABEL[v] }))}
            value={view}
            onValueChange={(v) => v && setView(v as EventCalendarView)}
          />
        )}
        {actions != null && <div className={styles.actions}>{actions}</div>}
      </div>
      {view === 'month' ? month() : view === 'year' ? year() : timeGrid()}
      {hasEventList && view === 'month' && (
        <div className={styles.eventList}>
          <SubHeading className={styles.listTitle}>{fmt.full.format(date)}</SubHeading>
          {selected.length ? (
            <ul className={styles.listEvents}>{selected.map((e) => eventItem(e))}</ul>
          ) : (
            <p className={styles.empty}>No events</p>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

# Event Calendar Events on a month, week, day or year view, with a header to move through ...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as EventCalendarStories from './EventCalendar.stories'

<Meta of={EventCalendarStories} />

# Event Calendar

Events on a month, week, day or year view, with a header to move through
time and switch views: a team's schedule, bookings, deadlines. After
Tailwind UI Application UI, Data Display: Calendars.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/calendar-events.json
```

It owns no events: pass the ones you have, and it shows those that fall in
view. Picking a date is the [Calendar](?path=/docs/data-display-calendar--docs)
component; this pattern reuses its date helpers, and draws the year view
with it.

## Month

The default view. Each day lists its events, all-day ones first, then by
start time with the time after the title. A day with more than three
lists two and "n more", which opens the day view (or picks the day for the
list below). An all-day or multi-day event shows on every day it covers.
`actions` takes the header's last slot, e.g. an "Add event" button.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Month} />

## Week

An hour grid, a column per day. Timed events sit by their start and end;
events that overlap share the width side by side. All-day events, and
timed events that cross midnight, go to a row above the hours. The grid
opens at the week's first timed event, or at 8:00.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Week} />

## Day

The week's hour grid, one column wide.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Day} />

## Year

Twelve small Calendars. Picking a day opens it in the day view (or the
month, when `views` leaves the day out).

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Year} />

## The selected day's events

`hasEventList` lists the selected day's events under the month, in full.
With `views={['month']}` the view switch is gone.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.WithEventList} />

## Clickable events

`onEventClick` makes events buttons, to open one in a
[Drawer](?path=/docs/overlays-drawer--docs) for example; an event with
`href` is a link.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Clickable} />

## Empty

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={EventCalendarStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through. Each event takes `id`,
`title`, `start`, and optionally `end` (exclusive for a timed event, the
last day for an all-day one), `allDay`, `color` (a Tag variant) and
`href`.

## Layout

- **The header wraps.** Title first; the arrows and Today, the view
  switch and `actions` follow on the same row while it has room, then
  drop under the title.
- **A month under 40rem wide shows dots, not titles**: one per event, up
  to three, in the event's colour. The day's button still says how many.
  Turn on `hasEventList` wherever the calendar can be that narrow, so the
  titles are one tap away. It follows the calendar's own width, not the
  viewport's.
- **The week keeps each day at least 6rem** and scrolls sideways under
  that; the day view takes the full width. Both show ten hours and scroll
  for the rest.
- **Long titles are cut with an ellipsis** in the month; in the hour grid
  they clip at the event's edge. The full title is in the event's
  accessible name either way.

<Canvas of={EventCalendarStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

Tailwind UI's Calendars, and where this departs from them:

- **The view switch is a Select**, as Tailwind's menu is, but it changes
  only the view: "Add event" is yours to put in `actions`.
- **Multi-day events repeat on each day** in the month, rather than one
  bar across the week. Simpler, and it reads the same on a phone.
- **The narrow week does not swap to a strip of days.** It scrolls
  sideways; pick the day view for a phone.
- **No "current time" line** in the week and day views.
- **The year view marks no events.** It is twelve Calendars, and Calendar
  has no way to mark a day; its API stays as it is. Pick a day to see it.

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading (`headingLevel`, 2 by default) and a polite live
  region, so moving through time is announced. The event list's heading
  is one level below.
- The month is a table named by the title, with a column header per
  weekday. Each day is a button named by its full date and its number of
  events, `aria-pressed` when selected and `aria-current="date"` on today.
- One day is a tab stop. The arrow keys move the selected day (across the
  month's edge too, which turns the month) and focus follows; Tab goes
  on to that day's events. Right to left, left and right follow the
  screen.
- Events are links with `href`, buttons with `onEventClick`, and text
  otherwise. Their name is the title then the start time.
- In the week and day views each day is a list named by its full date,
  and the all-day row's lists say "All day". The hour labels and the day
  headings above the columns are hidden from assistive tech: the lists
  carry the dates and the events their times. The scrolling hours are a
  focusable group, so a keyboard can scroll them.
- Previous and Next are named for the view's unit ("Next week"); their
  arrows mirror right to left.

import type { ComponentProps, Key, MouseEventHandler, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Badge } from '../../atomic-elements/Badge'
import styles from './Feed.module.css'

export interface FeedItem {
  /** A stable key. Without it the index is the key, which is fine for a list re-rendered whole. */
  id?: Key
  /** An Avatar of who did it, or an Icon for the kind of event. Decorative: the sentence says it all. */
  media?: ReactNode
  /** Who did it, in bold. */
  actor: ReactNode
  /** The rest of the sentence: what they did, and to what ("changed the status of Harbor Lights"). */
  action: ReactNode
  /** When it happened. */
  at: Date
  /** What they wrote, in a box under the sentence. */
  comment?: ReactNode
  /** Makes the sentence a link, and the whole row clickable. Keep links out of `actor` and `action` then: links cannot nest. */
  href?: string
  /** Runs when the link is followed, e.g. to mark the item read. */
  onClick?: MouseEventHandler<HTMLAnchorElement>
  /** Not seen yet: a dot at the end of the row, read out as "Unread". */
  isUnread?: boolean
}

export interface FeedProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  /** The events, in the order to show them; newest first is the norm. */
  items: FeedItem[]
  /** The vertical line joining one event to the next. */
  hasConnector?: boolean
  /** A form to add a comment, after the last event. The form is yours: the feed lines it up with the text. */
  composer?: ReactNode
  /** Shown instead of the list when there are no items. */
  empty?: ReactNode
  /** How the time reads. The `<time>` element carries the full ISO moment either way. */
  formatTime?: (at: Date) => string
}

const moment = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en', { dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'short' })

/**
 * What happened, as a list of sentences: who did what to what, and when,
 * with an optional comment under each and an optional form to add one. It
 * owns no data and no landmark: the page names the region around it.
 */
export function Feed({
  items,
  hasConnector = true,
  composer,
  empty = 'No activity yet.',
  formatTime = (at) => moment.format(at),
  className,
  ...props
}: FeedProps) {
  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.feed, hasConnector && styles.connected, className)} {...props}>
      {items.length === 0 ? (
        <p className={styles.empty}>{empty}</p>
      ) : (
        <ol className={styles.items}>
          {items.map((item, i) => (
            <li key={item.id ?? i} className={styles.item} data-unread={item.isUnread || undefined}>
              <span className={styles.media} aria-hidden="true">
                {item.media}
              </span>
              <div className={styles.body}>
                <p className={styles.sentence}>
                  {item.href ? (
                    <a href={item.href} onClick={item.onClick} className={styles.link}>
                      <strong>{item.actor}</strong> {item.action}
                    </a>
                  ) : (
                    <>
                      <strong>{item.actor}</strong> {item.action}
                    </>
                  )}{' '}
                  <time className={styles.time} dateTime={item.at.toISOString()}>
                    {formatTime(item.at)}
                  </time>
                </p>
                {item.comment && <div className={styles.comment}>{item.comment}</div>}
              </div>
              {item.isUnread && <Badge isDot aria-label="Unread" className={styles.unread} />}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ol>
      )}
      {composer && <div className={styles.composer}>{composer}</div>}
    </div>
  )
}

# Feed What happened to a record, or across many, as a list of sentences: who did what to ...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FeedStories from './Feed.stories'

<Meta of={FeedStories} />

# Feed

What happened to a record, or across many, as a list of sentences: who
did what to what, and when, with what they wrote under it. For a
record's history, a comment thread, or recent activity on a home page.
After Tailwind UI Application UI, Lists: Feeds.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/feed.json
```

## Simple

An Icon per kind of event, joined by a line. Each event is one
sentence: `actor` in bold, then `action`, the rest of it, then the time.
Build the sentence so it reads whole: "changed the status of Harbor
Lights from Active to On hold", not "Status: Active → On hold".

<Canvas of={FeedStories.Simple} />

## With comments

An Avatar for an event a person made, an Icon for one the system made,
and what they wrote in a box under the sentence. The [Project
Detail](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-project-detail--docs)
template puts a status change's note there.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.WithComments} />

## Without the line

`hasConnector={false}` drops the line, for a short list where each event
stands alone.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.WithoutConnector} />

## With a comment box

`composer` takes a form and puts it after the last event, lined up with
the sentences. The form is yours: a labelled
[Textarea](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs) and a Button,
adding to the items you pass. A thread with a box lists oldest first,
so the newest sits by the box.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.WithComposer} />

## Linked and unread

`href` makes the sentence a link whose target is the whole row, and
`isUnread` ends the row with a dot; `onClick` runs when the link is
followed, to mark the item read. The [Notification
Center](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-notification-center--docs)
lists its notifications this way. With `href`, keep links out of
`actor` and `action`: links cannot nest.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.LinkedAndUnread} />

## Empty

No items shows `empty`, "No activity yet." by default, in place of the
list. The composer still shows, so the first comment can be written.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={FeedStories} />

Every `<div>` attribute passes through to the root, so a page names the
feed with `role="region"` and `aria-label` when it has no heading of its
own.

## Layout

- The media column is as wide as a small Avatar; an Icon sits in a
  filled circle of that size, and an Avatar covers it.
- The line runs down the centre of that column, from one media to the
  next, and stops at the last.
- The time follows the sentence instead of taking a column at the end,
  so the feed fits a narrow aside: it wraps whole, never mid-date.
- Long names, links and comments break anywhere rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={FeedStories.LongContent} />

## Differences from the spec

- **Time** follows the sentence instead of sitting at the end of the
  row: the feed lives in asides and expanded rows as often as on a page.
- **Comment** is a slot of the event, not a separate event type, so any
  event can carry text: a status change keeps its reason.
- **Composer**: Tailwind draws the box with the user's avatar beside it.
  Here it lines up with the sentences and the form is yours.

## Accessibility

- The events are an ordered list, so a screen reader announces how many
  there are and where each one sits.
- The media is hidden from assistive tech: the sentence names the
  person and the event, so the avatar or icon adds nothing to hear.
- Each time is a `<time>` element with the full ISO moment, whatever
  `formatTime` shows.
- The feed has no landmark or heading of its own. Put it under a
  heading, or pass `role="region"` and an `aria-label` when it stands
  alone, as the Projects row does ("Harbor Lights activity").
- A row with `href` is one link, named by its sentence; the time and
  comment sit outside it.
- The unread dot is an image named "Unread", so the state is heard as
  well as seen.
- The composer's field needs a visible label, such as "Add a comment".
