# Field The label, required mark, info note and helper text for a control that has none of...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Field, FieldControl } from './Field'
import { boxClass, inputStyles } from './InputField'
import * as FieldStories from './Field.stories'

<Meta of={FieldStories} />

# Field

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

The label, required mark, info note and helper text for a control
that has none of its own.

<Status of={FieldStories} />

Every Zweihänder control (Text Input, Select, Checkbox and the rest)
already carries this anatomy. Field is for the control that does not: a
native element the kit has no component for, a Base UI primitive, or one
of your own. It wires the label, description and invalid state to it
through Base UI Field.

<Canvas of={FieldStories.Default} />

## Variants

There is one appearance. What changes is which optional parts are there.

<Canvas of={FieldStories.Validation} />

| Part | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `helperText` | The format, limits or purpose, in a line; the error message when invalid. |
| `labelInfo` | A longer rule or explanation most people do not need every time: behind an info button, so the form stays short. |
| `validationState` | `error` when the value cannot be accepted: the helper text says what to change, and it and the edge turn red. `success` for a value checked and accepted. |
| `required` | An asterisk after the label. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Field } from 'zweihander/field'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/field.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/Field.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Field.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/text-input](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/text-input) (the label and helper parts)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={FieldStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={FieldStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The control is whatever you put inside; in these stories it is a native
time input in the same box as Text Input.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Every field"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label and helper text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label and helper text', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Label, control, helper', property: 'Gap between', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Label and info button', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Info button', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-sm' },

    { part: 'Info note', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-3' },
    { part: 'Info note', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-field' },
  ]}
/>

The field is 20rem wide, capped at its container; with `isFullWidth` it
fills the container. The info note is at most 22rem wide and opens above
the button.

## Color

/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    {
      label: 'Error',
      content: (
        <Field label="Start time" validationState="error" helperText="Enter a time between 06:00 and 22:00.">
          <span className={boxClass('md')}>
            <FieldControl type="time" className={inputStyles.control} />
          </span>
        </Field>
      ),
    },
    {
      label: 'Read-only',
      content: (
        <Field label="Start time" helperText="Set by the rota.">
          <span className={boxClass('md')}>
            <FieldControl defaultValue="09:00" readOnly className={inputStyles.control} />
          </span>
        </Field>
      ),
    },
    {
      label: 'Disabled',
      content: (
        <Field label="Start time" helperText="Pick a shift first." disabled>
          <span className={boxClass('md')}>
            <FieldControl type="time" className={inputStyles.control} />
          </span>
        </Field>
      ),
    },
  ]}
>
  <Field label="Start time" labelInfo="When the shift starts." helperText="HH:MM">
    <span className={boxClass('md')}>
      <FieldControl type="time" className={inputStyles.control} />
    </span>
  </Field>
</States>

- **Hover** and **focus** belong to the control. The info button turns
  `--foreground` on hover and draws the `--ring` outline on keyboard focus.
- **Error** colours the helper text, which then says what to change, and
  the edge of a field box inside.
- **Read-only** is set on the control (`readOnly`), not on the Field.
  A field box with a read-only control inside is filled with
  `--surface-filled`; the edge, label and helper stay as they are.
- **Disabled** disables the control; how it dims is the control's own. The
  info button stays active: the note may say why the field is disabled.

## API

<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={FieldStories} />
</div>

`FieldControl` is Base UI's `Field.Control`: an `<input>` by default, any
element through `render`, with the label, description and invalid state
wired to it. A Base UI control (Slider, Number Field, Checkbox) inside a
Field wires itself.

### Differences from the spec

- **No separate error part.** As in every Zweihänder control, the error
  is the helper text in the error state (the kit's API convention), so a
  field never shows a hint and an error at once.
- **The info note is a toggletip**, opened by press or Enter, not a
  hover tooltip: tooltips do not open on touch.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Field round a control that has no label of its own. Keep the helper
text to a line; put a longer rule behind `labelInfo`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FieldStories.DoLongNoteInInfo} />}
  doCaption="The format in a line under the control; the full rule behind the info button."
  dont={<Story of={FieldStories.DontLongHelper} />}
  dontCaption="A paragraph of helper text pushes every field below it down, on every visit."
/>

An **error** says what to change, not only that something is wrong.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FieldStories.DoSayWhatToFix} />}
  doCaption="The error names the allowed range."
  dont={<Story of={FieldStories.DontVagueError} />}
  dontCaption="'Invalid value' leaves people guessing what to change."
/>

### Read-only

A value people need to see but cannot change here (set by a rule,
another team or their role) stays a field: put `readOnly` on the control
and say in `helperText` why, and who can change it. Every Zweihänder
control takes `readOnly`. The boxed fields (Text Input, Textarea,
Search, Number Input, Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Date Range Picker)
all look the same: a filled box, still focusable, the value selectable
and submitted with the form. Checkbox, Radio, Switch and Rating keep
their look, since their mark is the value, and only stop changing.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FieldStories.DoReadOnlyWithReason} />}
  doCaption="Read-only: readable, focusable, copyable, and it says who can change it."
  dont={<Story of={FieldStories.DontDisableToLock} />}
  dontCaption="Disabled: dimmed below readable contrast, skipped by Tab, not submitted."
/>

- **Not disabled.** A locked value is still read and copied; a disabled
  one is not (Disabled, below, is for "not yet").
- **No lock icon by default.** The fill already marks the state, and an
  icon would need its own name for screen readers; the helper text says
  more than a lock.
- **A whole record that cannot be edited** is not a form of read-only
  fields: show it as a [Description List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-description-list--docs),
  label and value with no box.

### Disabled

Disable a control only while it does not apply yet, and people can change
that on the same screen: a choice earlier in the form, a step not done.
Say what turns it on, in `helperText` or in the control that does it.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FieldStories.DoDisableWithReason} />}
  doCaption="Disabled for now, and the helper text says what turns it on."
  dont={<Story of={FieldStories.DontDisableWithoutReason} />}
  dontCaption="Nothing says why it is off or how to turn it on."
/>

- **Disable for "not yet", hide for "not you", read-only for "not
  changeable here".** An action or a field people's role never lets them
  use, and that they do not need to read, is left out, not shown disabled:
  a control they can never turn on is noise and a support ticket. A value
  they need to see but may not change is read-only.
- **No tooltip for the reason.** A disabled control leaves the tab order,
  so a tooltip on it never opens by keyboard or on touch. Put the reason
  in text people can see; `labelInfo` stays active on a disabled Field.
- **Dimmed on purpose.** Disabled controls are exempt from contrast
  rules and drop below readable contrast, one more reason not to disable
  a value people need to read.
- **Fields that turn off together** go in a disabled
  [`FormFieldGroup`](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs#field-groups):
  every control inside is disabled and dimmed, Checkbox, Switch and Radio
  included, and none is submitted. Slider and File Uploader do not read
  the group: give them `disabled` too.

## When not to use

- **Round a Zweihänder control.** Text Input, Textarea, Number Input,
  Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Checkbox, Switch and Radio have their own
  label, helper text and validation; a Field round one gives it two labels.
- **For a group of controls** under one name, use a
  [`FormFieldGroup`](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs#field-groups)
  (a `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`), or Radio's own group.

## Accessibility

- The label is a real `<label>` for the control: it is the control's
  accessible name, and clicking it focuses the control.
- `helperText` is the control's description (`aria-describedby`), read
  after its name.
- A read-only control keeps its place in the tab order and has the
  `readonly` attribute, so screen readers announce it as read-only;
  typing does not change the value, and the reason in `helperText` is read
  as its description.
- A disabled control is left out of the tab order; its helper text is still its description, so a screen reader browsing to it
  hears why.
- `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the control.
  Colour is never the only signal: the helper text says what is wrong.
- The required asterisk is `aria-hidden`; put `required` on the control so
  screen readers announce it.
- The info button is named by `infoLabel` ("More information") and
  described by the label, so a list of buttons tells which field each is
  for. It sits outside the `<label>`: pressing it opens the note without
  focusing the control. Enter or a press opens the note, a dialog named by
  the label; Escape closes it and returns focus to the button.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useEffect, useId, useRef, useState, type DragEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Button } from '../buttons/Button'
import { Spinner } from '../loaders/Spinner'
import styles from './FileUploader.module.css'

export interface FileRejection {
  file: File
  reason: 'type' | 'size' | 'count'
  /** Ready to show, e.g. "photo.gif is not an accepted type." */
  message: string
}

export interface FileStatus {
  /** 0–100 while uploading: a ring beside the remove button, hidden at 100. */
  progress?: number
  /** Short, beside the remove button in the danger colour, e.g. "Upload failed". */
  error?: string
}

export interface FileUploaderProps {
  files?: File[]
  defaultFiles?: File[]
  /** The list after an add or a remove. Rejected files are never in it. */
  onFilesChange?: (files: File[]) => void
  /** Files that were dropped or chosen but did not pass `accept`, `maxSize` or `maxFiles`. */
  onReject?: (rejections: FileRejection[]) => void
  /** As the native attribute: extensions and MIME types, e.g. `".pdf,image/*"`. Also checked on drop. */
  accept?: string
  multiple?: boolean
  /** In bytes. */
  maxSize?: number
  maxFiles?: number
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Inside the drop zone, under the button, e.g. "PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB." */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  /** Upload progress or a server error per file. The uploader does not upload: you do. */
  getFileStatus?: (file: File) => FileStatus | undefined
  /** Submitted with the form, as a native file input. */
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  className?: string
}

const sizeFormat = (bytes: number) => {
  const [value, unit] =
    bytes >= 1e6 ? [bytes / 1e6, 'megabyte'] : bytes >= 1e3 ? [bytes / 1e3, 'kilobyte'] : [bytes, 'byte']
  return new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'unit', unit, unitDisplay: 'short', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }).format(value)
}

/** Does the file match the `accept` list? Extensions, exact MIME types and `type/*`. */
function accepts(file: File, accept?: string) {
  if (!accept) return true
  const name = file.name.toLowerCase()
  const type = file.type.toLowerCase()
  return accept
    .split(',')
    .map((t) => t.trim().toLowerCase())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .some((t) => (t.startsWith('.') ? name.endsWith(t) : t.endsWith('/*') ? type.startsWith(t.slice(0, -1)) : type === t))
}

function syncInput(input: HTMLInputElement | null, files: File[]) {
  if (!input || typeof DataTransfer === 'undefined') return
  const transfer = new DataTransfer()
  files.forEach((f) => transfer.items.add(f))
  input.files = transfer.files
}

type FileKind = 'word' | 'excel' | 'powerpoint' | 'pdf' | 'image' | 'audio'

function fileKind(file: File): FileKind | undefined {
  const ext = file.name.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase() ?? ''
  const type = file.type.toLowerCase()
  if (ext === 'pdf' || type === 'application/pdf') return 'pdf'
  if (['doc', 'docx', 'odt', 'rtf'].includes(ext)) return 'word'
  if (['xls', 'xlsx', 'csv', 'ods'].includes(ext)) return 'excel'
  if (['ppt', 'pptx', 'odp'].includes(ext)) return 'powerpoint'
  if (type.startsWith('image/')) return 'image'
  if (type.startsWith('audio/') || ['mp3', 'wav', 'm4a', 'ogg', 'flac'].includes(ext)) return 'audio'
}

const badgeText: Partial<Record<FileKind, string>> = { word: 'W', excel: 'X', powerpoint: 'P', pdf: 'PDF' }

/** A page with a coloured type badge, after Microsoft 365's file icons. Unknown types get the bare page. */
function FileTypeIcon({ file }: { file: File }) {
  const kind = fileKind(file)
  return (
    <svg className={styles.fileIcon} data-kind={kind} viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true">
      <path className={styles.page} d="M9.5 2.5h11l7 7v18a2 2 0 0 1-2 2h-16a2 2 0 0 1-2-2v-23a2 2 0 0 1 2-2Z" />
      <path className={styles.fold} d="M20.5 2.5v5a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h5Z" />
      {kind && (
        <g>
          <rect className={styles.badge} x="2" y="13" width={kind === 'pdf' ? 20 : 15} height="14" rx="2" />
          {badgeText[kind] ? (
            <text className={styles.badgeText} x={kind === 'pdf' ? 12 : 9.5} y="23.5" textAnchor="middle">
              {badgeText[kind]}
            </text>
          ) : kind === 'image' ? (
            <g className={styles.glyph}>
              <circle cx="12.5" cy="17.5" r="1.25" />
              <path d="M5 24.5l3.5-4.5 2.5 3 1.5-1.5 2.5 3Z" />
            </g>
          ) : (
            <g className={styles.glyph}>
              <circle cx="7.5" cy="23" r="1.75" />
              <path d="M9.25 23v-6.5l4 1.25v2" fill="none" strokeWidth="1.5" strokeLinejoin="round" />
            </g>
          )}
        </g>
      )}
    </svg>
  )
}

const sameFile = (a: File, b: File) => a.name === b.name && a.size === b.size && a.lastModified === b.lastModified

export function FileUploader({
  files: filesProp,
  defaultFiles = [],
  onFilesChange,
  onReject,
  accept,
  multiple = false,
  maxSize,
  maxFiles,
  label,
  helperText,
  getFileStatus,
  name,
  disabled = false,
  required,
  isFullWidth,
  className,
}: FileUploaderProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  const chooseRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null)
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLUListElement>(null)
  const [filesState, setFilesState] = useState(defaultFiles)
  const files = filesProp ?? filesState
  const [rejections, setRejections] = useState<FileRejection[]>([])
  const [dragging, setDragging] = useState(false)
  const [announcement, setAnnouncement] = useState('')
  const limit = multiple ? (maxFiles ?? Infinity) : 1

  const [missing, setMissing] = useState(false)

  // The native input carries the list, so a plain form post sends it. Also
  // after a controlled `files` changes from outside, e.g. cleared after upload.
  useEffect(() => syncInput(inputRef.current, files), [files])

  const update = (next: File[]) => {
    setFilesState(next)
    syncInput(inputRef.current, next)
    onFilesChange?.(next)
  }

  const add = (incoming: File[]) => {
    const rejected: FileRejection[] = []
    const accepted: File[] = []
    for (const file of incoming) {
      if (!accepts(file, accept)) rejected.push({ file, reason: 'type', message: `${file.name} is not an accepted type.` })
      else if (maxSize !== undefined && file.size > maxSize)
        rejected.push({ file, reason: 'size', message: `${file.name} is larger than ${sizeFormat(maxSize)}.` })
      else accepted.push(file)
    }
    // A single-file uploader replaces its file, but only with one that passed:
    // a rejected drop leaves the chosen file where it is. A multiple one appends.
    let next = multiple ? [...files] : []
    for (const file of accepted) {
      if (next.some((f) => sameFile(f, file))) continue
      if (next.length >= limit)
        rejected.push({
          file,
          reason: 'count',
          message: multiple ? `${file.name} was not added: the limit is ${limit} files.` : `${file.name} was not added: only one file can be added.`,
        })
      else next.push(file)
    }
    if (!multiple && next.length === 0) next = files
    const added = next.filter((f) => !files.some((g) => sameFile(f, g))).length
    setRejections(rejected)
    if (rejected.length) onReject?.(rejected)
    if (next.length) setMissing(false)
    if (added || next.length !== files.length) update(next)
    else syncInput(inputRef.current, files)
    setAnnouncement(
      [added ? `${added} ${added === 1 ? 'file' : 'files'} added.` : '', rejected.length ? `${rejected.length} not added.` : '']
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(' '),
    )
  }

  const remove = (index: number) => {
    const removed = files[index]
    const next = files.filter((_, i) => i !== index)
    update(next)
    setAnnouncement(`${removed.name} removed.`)
    // Focus goes to the next remove button, else the previous, else Choose.
    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      const buttons = listRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>('button[data-remove]')
      const target = buttons?.[Math.min(index, buttons.length - 1)] ?? chooseRef.current
      target?.focus()
    })
  }

  const onDrop = (e: DragEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setDragging(false)
    if (!disabled) add([...e.dataTransfer.files])
  }

  const helperId = `${id}-helper`
  const errorId = `${id}-errors`

  return (
    // A group named by the label: the control inside is a button with its own
    // name ("Choose files"), so a <label> would have nothing to label.
    <div
      role="group"
      aria-labelledby={label ? `${id}-label` : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.uploader, isFullWidth && styles.fullWidth, disabled && styles.disabled, className)}
    >
      {label && (
        <div id={`${id}-label`} className={styles.label}>
          {label}
          {required && (
            <>
              <span className={styles.required} aria-hidden="true">
                *
              </span>
              {/* A group cannot be aria-required; the name says it instead. */}
              <span className={styles.srOnly}> (required)</span>
            </>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
      <div
        className={cn(styles.dropzone, dragging && styles.dragging, (rejections.length > 0 || missing) && styles.invalid)}
        data-disabled={disabled || undefined}
        onDragEnter={(e) => {
          e.preventDefault()
          if (!disabled) setDragging(true)
        }}
        onDragOver={(e) => {
          e.preventDefault()
          e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = disabled ? 'none' : 'copy'
        }}
        onDragLeave={(e) => {
          if (!e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget as Node)) setDragging(false)
        }}
        onDrop={onDrop}
      >
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          <Icon name="upload" />
        </span>
        <p className={styles.prompt}>
          {/* Dragging is a shortcut; the button is the way in for everyone. */}
          Drag {multiple ? 'files' : 'a file'} here or
        </p>
        <Button
          ref={chooseRef}
          variant="accent"
          size="sm"
          disabled={disabled}
          aria-describedby={[helperText ? helperId : '', rejections.length || missing ? errorId : ''].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || undefined}
          onClick={() => inputRef.current?.click()}
        >
          {multiple ? 'Choose files' : 'Choose a file'}
        </Button>
        {helperText && (
          <p id={helperId} className={styles.helper}>
            {helperText}
          </p>
        )}
        <input
          ref={inputRef}
          type="file"
          className={styles.srOnly}
          tabIndex={-1}
          name={name}
          accept={accept}
          multiple={multiple}
          disabled={disabled}
          required={required && files.length === 0}
          aria-hidden="true"
          onChange={(e) => add([...(e.target.files ?? [])])}
          // The browser would focus this hidden input and pin its bubble to
          // it. Show the message ourselves and send focus to Choose instead.
          onInvalid={(e) => {
            e.preventDefault()
            setMissing(true)
            chooseRef.current?.focus()
          }}
        />
      </div>
      {(rejections.length > 0 || missing) && (
        <ul id={errorId} className={styles.errors}>
          {missing && <li>{multiple ? 'Choose at least one file.' : 'Choose a file.'}</li>}
          {rejections.map((r, i) => (
            <li key={i}>{r.message}</li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
      {files.length > 0 && (
        <ul ref={listRef} className={styles.list} aria-label={multiple ? 'Chosen files' : 'Chosen file'}>
          {files.map((file, i) => {
            const status = getFileStatus?.(file)
            const uploading = status?.progress !== undefined && status.progress < 100 && !status.error
            return (
              <li key={`${file.name}-${file.size}-${file.lastModified}`} className={styles.item}>
                <FileTypeIcon file={file} />
                {/* The name truncates; the size always shows in full. */}
                <span className={styles.nameRow}>
                  <span className={styles.name}>{file.name}</span>
                  <span className={styles.size}>{sizeFormat(file.size)}</span>
                </span>
                {uploading && (
                  <Spinner value={status?.progress} variant="primary" size="sm" aria-label={`Uploading ${file.name}`} />
                )}
                {status?.error && (
                  <span className={styles.fileError} title={status.error}>
                    {status.error}
                  </span>
                )}
                <Button
                  isIconOnly
                  data-remove=""
                  className={styles.remove}
                  aria-label={`Remove ${file.name}`}
                  variant="secondary"
                  appearance="ghost"
                  size="sm"
                  disabled={disabled}
                  onClick={() => remove(i)}
                >
                  <Icon name="close" />
                </Button>
              </li>
            )
          })}
        </ul>
      )}
      <p role="status" className={styles.srOnly}>
        {announcement}
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

# File Uploader

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Choose files to send: drag them onto the drop zone or pick them with the
button. It checks type, size and count, lists what was chosen, and shows
progress or an error per file. It does not upload: your code does, and
tells it how that is going.

<Status of={FileUploaderStories} />

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.WithStatus} />

## Variants

| Mode | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `multiple` | Attachments, a batch of photos: files are appended, up to `maxFiles`. |
| Single | One document: an invoice, a CV. A new file replaces the chosen one, if it passes the checks. |

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.Single} />

Each file gets a type icon: a page with a coloured badge for Word, Excel,
PowerPoint, PDF, image and audio, after Microsoft 365, from the extension
or MIME type. Anything else is the bare page.

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.FileTypes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { FileUploader } from 'zweihander/file-uploader'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/file-uploader.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/FileUploader.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/FileUploader.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader)
- Behaviour: a native `<input type="file">` behind a kit [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={FileUploaderStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={FileUploaderStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Two more parts show only when needed:

- **Errors**: one line per file that was not added, under the drop zone,
  e.g. "raw-scan.png is larger than 5 MB."
- **File error**: in place of the progress ring, a short message from
  `getFileStatus`, e.g. "Upload failed". A long one truncates.

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.Rejected} />

The type badges keep fixed colours in both modes: they are each file
type's identity, not the theme's, and white on each is above 4.5:1. The
Choose button is an `accent contained` Button and the remove buttons
`secondary ghost`; their states are Button's.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Uploading', content: <Fit><Story of={FileUploaderStories.Anatomy} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Fit><Story of={FileUploaderStories.Disabled} /></Fit> },
  ]}
>
  <Fit><Story of={FileUploaderStories.DoStateTheRules} /></Fit>
</States>

- **Dragging**: while a file is over the drop zone its edge turns solid
  `--ring` and it fills with `--accent`, so the change is not colour
  alone.
- **Rejected or required and empty**: the drop zone's edge turns
  `--danger-text` and the errors list why, one line per file.
- **Focus** is the Choose button's and the remove buttons' own ring.
- **Uploading**: a progress ring beside the remove button while
  `progress` is under 100; it goes at 100. An `error` takes its place.
- **Disabled** fades the icon and the buttons, not the text: none of it
  is a native label, so faded text would fail contrast rather than be
  exempt.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={FileUploaderStories} />
</div>

### Design notes

- **Checks on every path in.** The system picker filters by `accept`, but
  a drop, or "All files" in the picker, does not. The uploader checks the
  type, size and count of everything and says why a file was left out.
- **A rejected file never replaces a good one.** In single-file mode a
  new file replaces the chosen one only if it passes the checks.
- **The same file twice is one file.** Name, size and modified time
  match, so it is skipped rather than listed again.
- **Uploading is yours.** Start it in `onFilesChange` and report through
  `getFileStatus`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a File Uploader to attach files to a form: receipts to a claim,
documents to an application. Say what is allowed in `helperText`, and set
`accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles` to match, so the rules are read before
a file is turned away.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FileUploaderStories.DoStateTheRules} />}
  doCaption="The rules up front: types and size in the helper text, checked by accept and maxSize."
  dont={<Story of={FileUploaderStories.DontHideTheRules} />}
  dontCaption="No rules shown: people learn them one rejection at a time."
/>

Report upload progress per file with `getFileStatus`, and keep errors
short ("Upload failed"): the row has room for a few words.

## When not to use

- **For text people could paste.** Use a
  [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs).
- **For a link to a file.** Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with
  `type="url"`.

## Accessibility

- Dragging is a shortcut, never the only way: the Choose button is a
  real button, reached by Tab, and opens the system picker. The file
  input itself is hidden from assistive tech so there is one control, not
  two.
- The uploader is a `group` named by its label; `required` adds
  "(required)" to that name, since a group cannot be `aria-required`.
  Submitting it empty shows "Choose at least one file." (or "Choose a
  file.") in the errors and moves focus to the Choose button, instead of
  the browser's bubble on the hidden input.
- The helper text and any errors describe the Choose button, so they
  are read when focus lands on it.
- A polite status line announces "2 files added. 1 not added." and
  "report.pdf removed."
- Remove buttons are named "Remove report.pdf". After a remove, focus
  moves to the next file's button, or back to Choose when the list is
  empty, so it is never lost.
- The progress ring is a `progressbar` named "Uploading report.pdf",
  with its value.
- While dragging, the drop zone's edge turns solid as well as changing
  colour.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useLayoutEffect, useRef, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Tag } from '../../atomic-elements/Tag'
import { Button } from '../../buttons/Button'
import styles from './FilterBar.module.css'

const focusable =
  'input:not([disabled]):not([type="hidden"]), button:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), a[href], [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'

export interface AppliedFilter {
  id: string
  /** What the chip says, field and value: "Status: Active". */
  label: string
}

export interface FilterBarProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  /** Usually a Search. */
  search?: ReactNode
  /** A button per field that opens its choices (a Menu or a Popover), then Add filter or More filters. */
  filters?: ReactNode
  /** The filters in force, one removable chip each. The row hides when empty. */
  applied?: AppliedFilter[]
  onRemove?: (id: string) => void
  /** Shows Clear all after the chips. */
  onClearAll?: () => void
  /** Defaults to "Clear all". */
  clearAllLabel?: string
  /** Names the chip list. Defaults to "Applied filters". */
  appliedLabel?: string
}

/**
 * Search and filters above a list or table, with what is applied as chips
 * that each remove on their own, and Clear all.
 */
export function FilterBar({
  search,
  filters,
  applied = [],
  onRemove,
  onClearAll,
  clearAllLabel = 'Clear all',
  appliedLabel = 'Applied filters',
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Filters',
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: FilterBarProps) {
  const barRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLUListElement>(null)
  // The chip whose remove button had focus. Removing it unmounts the button,
  // which would drop focus on the body, so take it to the chip that slid into
  // its place, or the one before; with no chips left, back to the controls.
  // Wait for that chip to leave `applied`: the removal may be async, or refused.
  const pendingFocus = useRef<{ index: number; id: string } | null>(null)
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const pending = pendingFocus.current
    if (!pending || applied.some((f) => f.id === pending.id)) return
    pendingFocus.current = null
    const removes = listRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('li button') ?? []
    const bar = barRef.current
    const next = removes[Math.min(pending.index, removes.length - 1)] ?? bar?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(focusable)
    if (next) next.focus()
    else if (bar) {
      bar.tabIndex = -1
      bar.focus()
    }
  }, [applied])

  return (
    <div role="search" aria-label={ariaLabel} ref={(node) => {
        barRef.current = node
        if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(node)
        else if (ref) ref.current = node
      }}
      className={cn(styles.bar, className)} {...props}>
      <div className={styles.controls}>
        {search}
        {filters}
      </div>
      {applied.length > 0 && (
        <div className={styles.applied}>
          <ul ref={listRef} aria-label={appliedLabel} className={styles.chips}>
            {applied.map((filter, i) => (
              <li key={filter.id}>
                <Tag
                  text={filter.label}
                  variant="neutral"
                  hasRemoveButton={!!onRemove}
                  onRemove={() => {
                    pendingFocus.current = { index: i, id: filter.id }
                    onRemove?.(filter.id)
                  }}
                />
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
          {onClearAll && (
            <Button
              variant="secondary"
              appearance="ghost"
              size="sm"
              onClick={() => {
                pendingFocus.current = { index: 0, id: applied[0].id }
                onClearAll()
              }}
            >
              {clearAllLabel}
            </Button>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

# Filter Bar Search and filters above a list or table, with the filters in force shown as ...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FilterBarStories from './FilterBar.stories'

<Meta of={FilterBarStories} />

# Filter Bar

Search and filters above a list or table, with the filters in force shown
as chips that each remove on their own, and Clear all. After SAP Fiori List
Report (filter bar), Carbon Filtering and Polaris Index table.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/filter-bar.json
```

The pattern owns no data: it lays out the controls you pass and renders the
`applied` list you keep. Choose how each filter applies with the component
you put in `filters`.

## Applied at once

A button per field opens a [Menu](?path=/docs/navigation-menu--docs) of
checkbox items; each tick applies straight away and adds a chip. Use it for
the few fields people filter by most, with short lists of values.

<Canvas of={FilterBarStories.Default} />

## Applied in a batch

More filters opens a [Drawer](?path=/docs/overlays-drawer--docs) holding a
draft: nothing changes until Apply, and Cancel drops the draft. Use it for
the long tail of fields, or when each change is slow to run (a server query
over a large ledger).

<Canvas of={FilterBarStories.AppliedInABatch} />

## Empty

With nothing applied there is no chip row and no Clear all.

<Canvas of={FilterBarStories.Empty} />

## In a table toolbar

Put it first inside a [TableToolbar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-data-table-page--docs):
it takes the free space, the page's main action stays at the end, and the
toolbar swaps it for the selection's actions while rows are selected.

<Canvas of={FilterBarStories.InTableToolbar} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={FilterBarStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **Two rows.** The controls on top; the chips and Clear all under them,
  only while something is applied.
- **Everything wraps, nothing squeezes.** On a phone the search takes its
  own line and the field buttons flow under it; chips wrap onto more lines.
- **A long value truncates inside its chip** with an ellipsis, rather than
  widen the page. The remove button keeps the full name.

<Canvas of={FilterBarStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- The bar is a `search` landmark named "Filters"; pass `aria-label` to
  name it after what it filters, e.g. "Invoice filters", when a page has
  more than one.
- The chips are a list named "Applied filters", so a screen reader says how
  many are in force. Each remove button is named after its chip, e.g.
  "Remove Status: Overdue".
- Removing a chip moves focus to the chip that takes its place, or the one
  before; removing the last one, or Clear all, moves it to the first
  control, usually the search. Focus never drops to the page.
- Field buttons say only the field ("Status"); what is chosen is read from
  the chips and from the checked items in the menu.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { TokenTable } from './TokenTable'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

const TOKENS = [
  { name: '--focus-width', use: 'Ring thickness, on every focusable element' },
  { name: '--focus-offset', use: 'Ring outside the element: buttons, fields, links, free-standing controls' },
  { name: '--focus-offset-inset', use: 'Ring inside the element: tabs, rows, accordion headers, close buttons in a panel' },
]

const SAMPLE: React.CSSProperties = {
  inlineSize: 'var(--control-md)',
  blockSize: 'var(--control-md)',
  borderRadius: 'var(--radius-control)',
  background: 'var(--muted)',
  outline: 'var(--focus-width) solid var(--ring)',
}

// Both rings drawn at rest, so the page shows the difference without a
// keyboard.
function RingDemo() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.stackWide}>
      <TokenTable tokens={TOKENS} />
      <div className={docs.row}>
        <div data-ring="offset" style={{ ...SAMPLE, outlineOffset: 'var(--focus-offset)' }} />
        <span className={docs.caption}>offset</span>
        <div data-ring="inset" style={{ ...SAMPLE, outlineOffset: 'var(--focus-offset-inset)' }} />
        <span className={docs.caption}>offset-inset</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Focus.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Focus',
  render: () => <RingDemo />,
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Rings: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const ring = (kind: string) => getComputedStyle(canvasElement.querySelector(`[data-ring="${kind}"]`)!)
    await expect(ring('offset').outlineWidth).toBe('2px')
    await expect(ring('offset').outlineOffset).toBe('2px')
    await expect(ring('inset').outlineOffset).toBe('-2px')
  },
}

./src/foundations/Focus.mdx
# Focus One ring for the whole kit: `outline: var(--focus-width) solid var(--ring)`, shown...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FocusStories from './Focus.stories'

<Meta of={FocusStories} />

# Focus

One ring for the whole kit: `outline: var(--focus-width) solid var(--ring)`,
shown on `:focus-visible` only. Its colour is `--ring`, measured at 3:1
against the page (see [Colors](?path=/docs/foundations-colors--docs)).

<Canvas of={FocusStories.Rings} />

## Outside or inside

There are two offsets and the choice is mechanical.

**`--focus-offset`** draws the ring outside the element. It is the default
for anything that stands on its own: buttons, fields, links, checkboxes.

**`--focus-offset-inset`** draws it inside. Use it when the element sits
flush against the edge of a container that clips its overflow, or when an
outside ring would run into a neighbour: tabs, table rows and sortable
headers, accordion triggers, the close button in a modal, popover, alert
or toast, the remove button in a tag, the steppers in a number input.

A third value is a smell. The one exception is a selected colour swatch,
which already carries a selection ring at `--focus-offset`, so its focus
ring sits one pixel further out to stay visible.

## Why the ring is not scaled

`--focus-width` and both offsets are plain pixels, not multiplied by
`--scaling`. A ring is a stroke: at 90% scaling it should not thin to
1.8px, and WCAG 2.4.13 measures it in CSS pixels.

# Forgot Password Two pages for a forgotten password. **Forgot Password** asks for the ema...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ForgotPasswordStories from './ForgotPassword.stories'
import * as ResetPasswordStories from './ResetPassword.stories'

<Meta of={ForgotPasswordStories} />

# Forgot Password

Two pages for a forgotten password. **Forgot Password** asks for the
email, then says to check it. **Reset Password** is the page the emailed
link opens: a new password with its rules, then "Password changed". After
Carbon's login pattern. Built on the **Auth Layout** (see
[Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#auth-layout)), the
`PasswordInput` Sign Up uses, and the kit's TextInput, Link, Alert and
Button.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/forgot-password-template.json
```

<Canvas of={ForgotPasswordStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Step 1, the email**: one field and Send reset link. An empty or
  malformed email is marked with a message and keeps focus. The email,
  trimmed, goes to `onRequest`.
- **Step 2, check your email**: "If an account exists for …, we sent it a
  link". It never says whether one does, so the page cannot be used to
  find out who has an account. Focus moves to the new title.
- **Resend link**: disabled for `resendCooldown` seconds (30 by default),
  showing the time left, then sends to the same email and says so. A
  failed resend shows why and starts no cooldown. It is the same button
  as OTP Input's Resend code.
- **No single sign-on buttons**: an account that signs in with a provider
  has no password here to reset.
- **Use a different email** goes back to step 1 with the email filled in.
- **Step 3, a new password** (Reset Password): the rules are listed under
  the field and ticked off as the reader types, at least 12 characters by
  default, as on Sign Up; pass your own `passwordRules`. There is no
  "confirm password" field: Show lets the reader check what they typed.
  Pass `email` to name the account and to let a password manager save the
  new password under it.
- **Password changed**: the form gives way to the title, a line and a Sign
  in button; focus moves to the title.
- **When it fails**: `onRequest` and `onChangePassword` return (or resolve
  to) a message, such as too many requests or an expired link. It shows
  above the form and is announced. If they throw or reject, the page says
  "Something went wrong. Try again."

<Canvas of={ForgotPasswordStories.Sent} />

<Canvas of={ResetPasswordStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={ResetPasswordStories.LinkExpired} />

## Variants

**Card** (default) and **plain**, and **with a panel** through `aside`,
exactly as on Sign In: they are the Auth Layout's.

<Canvas of={ResetPasswordStories.WithoutEmail} />

## Make it yours

`onRequest` calls your API, which emails a link with a single-use token
when the account exists and does nothing when it does not; return a
message only for what the reader can act on (too many requests). Mount
`ResetPassword` on the page the link opens, read the token from the URL,
and send it with the password in `onChangePassword`; return a message
when the token is expired or used. A code instead of a link? Build step 2
with OTP Input, which has the same resend button.

## Props

### ForgotPassword

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onRequest` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ email }`, from the form and from Resend link. A returned message shows above the form and keeps the step; the button is busy while a promise is pending. |
| `resendCooldown` | seconds | `30` | Before Resend link is allowed, after each send. |
| `signInHref` | `string` | `"#sign-in"` | Where "Back to sign in" goes. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the Back to sign in link, outside the card. |

### ResetPassword

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | `string` | | The account the link is for: named under the title and given to password managers. |
| `passwordRules` | `{ label, test(password) }[]` | at least 12 characters | Listed under the password and ticked off; all must pass to send. |
| `onChangePassword` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ password }` once the rules pass. A returned message shows above the form; otherwise the page says the password changed. |
| `signInHref` | `string` | `"#sign-in"` | Where "Back to sign in" and Sign in go. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the form, outside the card. |

The title and the line under it change with the step, so neither takes
`title` or `description`. Every other Auth Layout prop passes through.

## Layout

The Auth Layout's, as on [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#layout).
A long email wraps; nothing scrolls sideways.

<Canvas of={ForgotPasswordStories.Phone} />

## Accessibility

- The form is in a `main` landmark, and its one heading is the `h1`.
- When a step replaces the form (Check your email, Password changed), focus
  moves to the new `h1`, so a screen reader reads the page from there and
  focus is not left on a button that is gone. Use a different email puts
  focus back in the email field.
- An invalid field has `aria-invalid="true"` and its message as its
  description, and gets focus.
- Resend link is disabled during the cooldown and its name carries the time
  left. After a resend, "We sent another link" is a `status`, announced
  politely, and focus moves to the `h1` because the button is disabled
  again.
- The password rules are the field's description, each followed by "(met)"
  or "(not met)". The message from `onRequest` or `onChangePassword` is an
  `alert`, and the button is `aria-busy` while it waits.
- The email for password managers is a `hidden` input: out of the tab order
  and the accessibility tree.

"use client";

import { useId, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Fieldset } from "@base-ui/react/fieldset";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
import styles from "./FormLayouts.module.css";

export interface FormSectionProps extends Omit<
  ComponentProps<"section">,
  "title"
> {
  title: ReactNode;
  /** What these fields are for, or who sees them. */
  description?: ReactNode;
  /** The fields. Give each input `isFullWidth`; wrap one in FormFullWidth to span both columns. */
  children: ReactNode;
  /**
   * `split`: title and description in a column beside the fields, as on a
   * settings page. `stacked`: title above the fields. Split stacks by itself
   * when the section is narrower than 48rem.
   */
  layout?: "split" | "stacked";
  /** Lay the fields out two to a row (one on narrow screens). */
  columns?: 1 | 2;
  /** Put the fields on a card. With `footer`, the footer is the card's bottom band. */
  isCard?: boolean;
  /** Usually FormActions. */
  footer?: ReactNode;
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3;
}

/**
 * A group of related fields with a heading: one block of a settings page or
 * a form. Stack several, with FormActions after them.
 */
export function FormSection({
  title,
  description,
  children,
  layout = "split",
  columns = 1,
  isCard = false,
  footer,
  headingLevel = 2,
  className,
  ...props
}: FormSectionProps) {
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const;
  return (
    // The section is the container and .layout inside it the grid: an
    // element cannot query its own size.
    <section
      className={cn(styles.section, styles[layout], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      <div className={styles.layout}>
        <div className={styles.intro}>
          <Heading className={styles.title}>{title}</Heading>
          {description && <p className={styles.description}>{description}</p>}
        </div>
        <div className={cn(styles.body, isCard && styles.card)}>
          <div
            className={cn(styles.fields, columns === 2 && styles.twoColumns)}
          >
            {children}
          </div>
          {footer && <div className={styles.footer}>{footer}</div>}
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

/** In a two-column FormSection, a field that takes the whole row. */
export function FormFullWidth({ className, ...props }: ComponentProps<"div">) {
  return <div className={cn(styles.fullWidth, className)} {...props} />;
}

export interface FormFieldGroupProps extends ComponentProps<"fieldset"> {
  /** Names the group: "Billing address", "By email". */
  legend: ReactNode;
  /** A line under the legend. Screen readers hear it with the group's name. */
  description?: ReactNode;
  /** The fields. Give each input `isFullWidth`. */
  children: ReactNode;
  /** Lay the group's fields out two to a row (one on narrow screens). */
  columns?: 1 | 2;
}

/**
 * Related fields inside a FormSection, under a legend: an address, a set of
 * checkboxes. It takes a whole row of a two-column section and lays out its
 * own columns. `disabled` turns off every field in it: it is Base UI's
 * Fieldset, whose context disables every Base UI Field inside, because a bare
 * disabled `<fieldset>` only reaches native controls and would leave
 * Checkbox, Switch and Radio (`<span>`s) clickable and undimmed.
 */
export function FormFieldGroup({
  legend,
  description,
  children,
  columns = 1,
  className,
  "aria-describedby": describedBy,
  ...props
}: FormFieldGroupProps) {
  const descriptionId = useId();
  return (
    <Fieldset.Root
      {...props}
      className={cn(styles.group, className)}
      aria-describedby={
        cn(description && descriptionId, describedBy) || undefined
      }
    >
      <legend className={styles.legend}>{legend}</legend>
      {description && (
        <p id={descriptionId} className={styles.description}>
          {description}
        </p>
      )}
      <div className={cn(styles.fields, columns === 2 && styles.twoColumns)}>
        {children}
      </div>
    </Fieldset.Root>
  );
}

export interface FormActionsProps extends ComponentProps<"div"> {
  /** Buttons, the primary one last. */
  children: ReactNode;
}

/** The row of buttons at the end of a form: secondary actions first, the primary one last, at the end. */
export function FormActions({ className, ...props }: FormActionsProps) {
  return <div className={cn(styles.actions, className)} {...props} />;
}

# Form Layouts How the kit's fields are arranged into a form: sections with a heading and ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FormLayoutsStories from './FormLayouts.stories'

<Meta of={FormLayoutsStories} />

# Form Layouts

How the kit's fields are arranged into a form: sections with a heading
and a line of context, fields one or two to a row, and a row of actions
at the end. Four pieces: `FormSection`, `FormFieldGroup`,
`FormFullWidth` and `FormActions`. The `<form>` element is yours.
After Tailwind UI's Form Layouts.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/form-layouts.json
```

## Settings sections

A settings page. Each section's title and description sit in a column
beside its fields, sections are separated by a line, and one row of
actions saves the lot.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.SettingsSections} />

## Stacked in a card

One section on a card: the title above, fields two to a row, and the
actions in the card's bottom band.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.StackedInCard} />

## Field groups

Related fields inside one section, under a legend: an address, a set of
checkboxes. `FormFieldGroup` is a `<fieldset>`: it takes the section's
whole row, lays out its own columns, and `disabled` turns off every field
in it, Checkbox, Switch and Radio included (they are left out of the
submitted data, as the browser does for any disabled field). Slider and
File Uploader do not read the group: give them `disabled` too. Disable a
group while it does not apply, with the reason on screen, as the "Ship to
the billing address" checkbox does here; see
[Field › Disabled](?path=/docs/components-inputs-field--docs) for when to
disable, hide or make read-only.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.FieldGroups} />

## In a modal

A short form in a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs).
The submit button sits in the modal's footer, outside the `<form>`, and
points at it with the `form` attribute, so Enter in a field and a click on
the button both submit.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.InModal} />

## FormSection props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | – | Required. An `h2` by default. |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `children` | node | – | The fields. Give each input `isFullWidth`. |
| `layout` | `split`, `stacked` | `split` | Split puts the intro in a column beside the fields. |
| `columns` | `1`, `2` | `1` | Two fields to a row. Wrap one in `FormFullWidth` to span the row. |
| `isCard` | boolean | `false` | |
| `footer` | node | – | Usually `FormActions`; the card's bottom band when `isCard`. |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

`FormFieldGroup` takes `legend` (required), `description`, `columns`
(`1`, `2`) and everything a `<fieldset>` takes, `disabled` among them.

`FormActions` is a row of buttons aligned to the end: secondary actions
first, the primary one last.

<Controls of={FormLayoutsStories.Narrow} />

## Layout

- **Sections respond to their own width.** Split turns into stacked under
  48rem of section width, and two columns into one when the fields' side
  of the section (its whole width once stacked) is under 32rem. A form in
  a sidebar or a phone needs no extra props.
- **Sections are size containers**, so they take their width from where
  they sit. As a flex or grid item that would shrink to fit, give the
  section a width (`inline-size: 100%`), or it collapses.

  <Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.Narrow} />

- **A field group takes a whole row** of a two-column section, and its
  own `columns` follow the same 32rem rule.
- Labels sit above their fields, never beside them: the label width does
  not depend on the longest translation, and a form reflows to a phone
  with no change.
- Actions end-aligned, primary last: the same place in every form, where
  the eye and the Tab key end up.

## Accessibility

- Each section is a `<section>` with a heading, so the form's parts are in
  the page outline and a screen reader can jump between them.
- Group related fields in a `FormFieldGroup`, as the Notifications and
  Billing sections do: a `group` named by its legend and described by its
  description, so a screen reader announces both on entering it.
  RadioGroup is a group of its own; do not wrap it.
- Mark required fields with `required`. The field shows the asterisk and
  the browser enforces it; say in the description if most fields are
  optional instead.
- Never disable the submit button to show that a form is incomplete. Let
  it submit, and show what is missing next to each field.

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { ListContainer, ListContainerItem, type ListContainerProps } from './ListContainer'
import { ListItemActions, ListItemContextMenu, ListItemHeading, ListItemMedia } from './ListItemParts'
import parts from './ListItemParts.module.css'
import type { StackedListItem } from './StackedList'
import styles from './GridList.module.css'

/** A Stacked List item, plus an optional picture across the top of the card. */
export interface GridListItem extends StackedListItem {
  /** A picture across the top of the card: a photo, a file preview, a logo. Decorative, so give an `<img>` `alt=""`: the title names the item. */
  cover?: ReactNode
}

export interface GridListProps extends Omit<ListContainerProps, 'children' | 'appearance'> {
  /** The cards, in reading order: left to right, then down. */
  items: GridListItem[]
}

/**
 * Records as cards in a grid: people, projects, files. Each card takes the
 * same item as a Stacked List row, plus an optional cover picture. The grid
 * fits as many columns as its container allows. The card panels, footer and
 * empty state are List Container's `separate` appearance.
 */
export function GridList({ items, className, ...props }: GridListProps) {
  return (
    <ListContainer {...props} appearance="separate" className={cn(styles.grid, className)}>
      {items.map((item, i) => (
        <ListItemContextMenu key={item.id ?? i} item={item}>
          <ListContainerItem className={cn(parts.target, styles.card)}>
            {item.cover && (
              <div className={styles.cover} aria-hidden="true">
                {item.cover}
              </div>
            )}
            <div className={styles.body}>
              <ListItemMedia item={item} />
              <div className={styles.text}>
                <ListItemHeading item={item} />
                {item.description && <p className={parts.description}>{item.description}</p>}
                {item.meta && <div className={parts.meta}>{item.meta}</div>}
              </div>
              <ListItemActions item={item} index={i} />
            </div>
          </ListContainerItem>
        </ListItemContextMenu>
      ))}
    </ListContainer>
  )
}

# Grid List Records as cards in a grid: people on a team, projects, files and photos. Each...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as GridListStories from './GridList.stories'

<Meta of={GridListStories} />

# Grid List

Records as cards in a grid: people on a team, projects, files and photos.
Each card names the record, says a little about it, and either opens it
or offers its actions. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Lists: Grid
Lists.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/grid-list.json
```

A card takes the same item as a [Stacked
List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stacked-list--docs) row, plus an
optional `cover`, so a list can switch between rows and cards without
reshaping its data. Use cards when the picture or the record's identity
matters more than comparing facts down a column; use Stacked List when
people scan and compare.

## Simple

An Avatar or an Icon, the `title` with a `description` under it, and
`meta` under that: an email, an owner, a date.

<Canvas of={GridListStories.Simple} />

## Linked

`href` makes the title a link whose target is the whole card. `status`
takes a Tag (or a Badge) and puts it after the title.

<Canvas of={GridListStories.Linked} />

## With actions

`actions` takes [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs)
entries, as in Stacked List and Table's `rowActions`: a ⋯ button in the
card's corner, named "Actions for" the title, and a [Context
Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-context-menu--docs) on the card
with the same entries. A card with `href` keeps the browser's own link
menu instead, so there the ⋯ button is the only way in.

<Canvas of={GridListStories.WithActions} />

A card can link and have actions: the menu sits above the card's link, so
a click on it opens the menu, not the record. Keep `status`,
`description` and `meta` free of controls on a linked card: the link
covers them.

<Canvas of={GridListStories.LinkedWithActions} />

## With a cover

`cover` puts a picture across the top of the card, edge to edge, at
16:9: a file preview, a photo, a logo. It is decorative, so give the
`<img>` `alt=""`; the title names the card.

<Canvas of={GridListStories.WithCover} />

## Footer and empty

The card panels, the footer and the empty state come from [List
Container](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-list-container--docs),
always in its `separate` appearance: a card is its own panel, so there is
no `flat` or `card` grid. `footer` goes after the grid; `empty` shows in
place of it, "Nothing here yet." by default.

<Canvas of={GridListStories.WithFooter} />

<Canvas of={GridListStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={GridListStories} />

Every `<div>` attribute passes through to the root, so a page names the
grid with `role="region"` and `aria-label` when it has no heading of its
own.

## Layout

- As many columns at least 16rem wide as the container fits, measured
  on the container rather than the viewport: three in 840px, one in a
  narrow aside or on a phone. There is no breakpoint of its own.
- A lone card stays one column wide instead of stretching across the
  row.
- Cards in a row are as tall as the tallest; text starts at the top.
- Long titles, emails and paths break anywhere rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={GridListStories.LongContent} />

## Differences from the spec

- **Column count** follows the container, not fixed counts per viewport
  breakpoint as in Tailwind, so the grid works in a side panel too.
- **Actions** are a ⋯ Menu, not a row of buttons along the bottom of the
  card (Tailwind's contact cards with Email and Call): two or more
  actions fit one menu at every width, and the card stays one shape.
- **Centred contact cards** (avatar above the name) are left out: one
  layout, media beside the title, reads the same as a Stacked List row.

## Accessibility

- The cards are an unordered list, so a screen reader announces how many
  there are. Reading and tab order go left to right, then down.
- The media and the cover are hidden from assistive tech: the title
  names the record.
- A card with `href` is one link, named by its title; the status,
  description and meta sit outside it.
- Each card is one tab stop, two with actions: the link, then the ⋯
  button.
- The ⋯ button is named "Actions for" the title; keep `title` a string
  when there are actions. The context menu is a shortcut to the same
  entries, never the only way to reach one.
- The grid has no landmark or heading of its own. Put it under a
  heading, or pass `role="region"` and an `aria-label`.

# Home The page an app opens on: a greeting and the period to look at, a setup guide while...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as HomeStories from './Home.stories'

<Meta of={HomeStories} />

# Home

The page an app opens on: a greeting and the period to look at, a setup
guide while the workspace is new, the key figures, a chart and the user's
tasks in a grid of cards, and recent activity in the aside. After Tailwind
UI's home screens, shadcn's dashboard-01, Polaris' homepage and Fiori's
overview page. Built from
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs),
[Stats](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stats--docs),
[Card Heading](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-card-heading--docs),
[Action Panel](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-action-panel--docs),
the charts and the kit's Select, Checkbox, Progress Bar and Card. The data
is made up.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/home-template.json
```

<Canvas of={HomeStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Period**: Last 7, 30 or 90 days. It changes the figures that add up
  over time (hours logged, invoiced: each against the period before) and
  the chart. Active projects is a count as it stands now, so the period
  does not touch it; it links to the list instead.
- **Setup guide**: an Action Panel with the steps, how many are done and
  one button, for the next step. It shows until every step is done, then
  goes, and focus moves to the page's heading. It sits first, above the
  figures: while a workspace is new, setting it up is the job, and the
  figures are mostly empty anyway.
- **Your tasks**: what is assigned to you, soonest first, each with its
  project and when it is due; overdue says so in words as well as red.
  Ticking one keeps it in the list, struck through, so a slip can be undone.
  No tasks shows "Nothing due".
- **Recent activity**: the newest events across every project, each
  naming its project, in the aside: it is context, not the job, so it
  takes the side column on a desktop and goes under the page on a phone.

<Canvas of={HomeStories.SetupGuide} />

## Make it yours

`Home` reads the samples in `home-data.ts` and the Projects template's
`projects-data.ts`. Load your figures, tasks and setup steps in their
place, and pass `today={new Date()}`: the sample pins today so the page
and its tests hold still. `onTaskChange(id, isDone)` and
`onSetupStep(id)` are where your API calls go.

Keep the figures few, three or four, and only ones the reader acts on.
A card per figure the business tracks turns home into a report nobody
reads; put those in a report page and link to it. A card on home answers
"what needs me today?" or "is anything off?".

The recent activity list is the [Feed](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-feed--docs) pattern, fed the same events
as the Project Detail template's.

<Canvas of={HomeStories.NothingDue} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={HomeStories} />

Any other prop goes to the App Shell's root, e.g. `style` to set its
`block-size` when the page is not the whole viewport.

## Layout

- The greeting and the period share a row while there is room; the period
  drops under the greeting when there is not.
- The figures take as many columns as fit, one on a phone.
- From 40rem of page width the chart and the tasks sit side by side, the
  chart the wider; below, the tasks go under the chart. 40rem is less than
  a desktop page keeps with the sidebar and the aside both open.
- The aside is beside the page from 80rem of the shell's width, under it
  below that.

<Canvas of={HomeStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- One `h1`, the greeting; the cards' and the aside's titles are `h2`.
- The figures are a region named after the period ("Key figures, last
  30 days"), so the name changes with it.
- Each task is a checkbox named by its title and described by its project
  and when it is due ("Overdue", "Due today"), so the colour is never the
  only cue.
- The setup guide is a group named "Finish setting up"; its progress bar
  says how many steps are done, and a done step reads "(done)". When the
  last step is done the guide goes and focus moves to the `h1`, not to the
  page's body.
- The aside is a complementary landmark named "Recent activity".

# Icons One module, `src/lib/icon.tsx`, and one component: ``. Every component in the kit ...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as IconStories from './Icon.stories'

<Meta of={IconStories} />

# Icons

One module, `src/lib/icon.tsx`, and one component: `<Icon name="close" />`.
Every component in the kit imports its icons from here and nowhere else.

<Canvas of={IconStories.Catalog} />

## Why names say what an icon is for

`close`, `danger`, `success` — not `x`, `alert-circle`, `check-circle`.
The set is temporary: it is Google Material Symbols for now, and may be
replaced by the kit's own set. Named by purpose, that swap is an edit to this one file.
Named by shape, it would be a search through every component for which
shape meant what. Navigation shapes (`chevron-down`, `search`, `plus`)
keep their plain names because the shape *is* the purpose.

## Sizing and colour

The icon is a `1em` square filled with `currentColor`, so it takes both
from the text around it. Set `font-size` on a wrapper, or on the icon
itself, to size it; never pass a colour.

```tsx
<span style={{ fontSize: 20 }}><Icon name="warning" /></span>
```

## Accessibility

- Without `label` an icon is decorative: `aria-hidden`, and not focusable
  in old Edge. This is almost always right, because the icon sits next to
  words that already say the same thing.
- With `label` it is exposed as an image with that name. Use it only when
  the icon stands alone and carries meaning, e.g. a status with no text.
- An icon-only *button* is named on the button (`aria-label`), not on
  the icon.

## Source and licence

Path data is copied from Google Material Symbols (`@material-symbols/svg-600`
0.47.6): Rounded, weight 600 (400 drew too thin a stroke at 16px), grade 0, optical size 24, fill 0 unless the
table says Fill 1. Apache 2.0. The licence notice is in the file header, so
it travels with the file when the registry copies it into another project.
There is no npm dependency on Material Symbols, and no icon font.

The paths use Material's own `0 -960 960 960` viewBox; keep it when adding
icons.

## Names in Material Symbols

Each purpose name in code is one Material Symbol, so designers can find the
same glyph at [fonts.google.com/icons](https://fonts.google.com/icons) or
in the Material Symbols Figma community file:

| Code (`name`) | Material Symbol |
| --- | --- |
| `calendar` | `calendar_today` |
| `check` | `check` |
| `chevron-down` | `keyboard_arrow_down` |
| `chevron-left` | `keyboard_arrow_left` |
| `chevron-right` | `keyboard_arrow_right` |
| `chevron-up` | `keyboard_arrow_up` |
| `chevrons-up-down` | `unfold_more` |
| `clear` | `cancel` (filled) |
| `close` | `close` |
| `danger` | `error` |
| `danger-filled` | `error (Fill 1)` |
| `edit` | `edit` |
| `external` | `open_in_new` |
| `file` | `draft` |
| `help` | `help` |
| `info` | `info` |
| `info-filled` | `info (Fill 1)` |
| `menu` | `menu` |
| `minus` | `remove` |
| `more` | `more_horiz` |
| `notifications` | `notifications` |
| `pause` | `pause` |
| `play` | `play_arrow` |
| `plus` | `add` |
| `search` | `search` |
| `sidebar-collapse` | `left_panel_close` |
| `sidebar-expand` | `left_panel_open` |
| `star` | `star` |
| `star-filled` | `star (Fill 1)` |
| `success` | `check_circle` |
| `success-filled` | `check_circle (Fill 1)` |
| `upload` | `upload` |
| `user` | `person` |
| `warning` | `warning` |
| `warning-filled` | `warning (Fill 1)` |

To add an icon: find it at fonts.google.com/icons, copy the `d`
attribute(s) from `rounded/<name>.svg` (or `<name>-fill.svg`) in
`@material-symbols/svg-600` into the `paths` map under a purpose name,
add a row to this table, and add the name to the catalog story.

# Import Export Getting rows into a list from a file, and out of it into one: the spreadsh...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ImportExportStories from './ImportExport.stories'

<Meta of={ImportExportStories} />

# Import Export

Getting rows into a list from a file, and out of it into one: the
spreadsheet round trip every ERP and back-office list needs. No outside
block covers it (Catalyst Blocks has none); the anatomy is the
Application UI catalogue's own. Two dialogs,
`ImportDialog` and `ExportDialog`, built from the [File
Uploader](?path=/docs/components-inputs-file-uploader--docs),
[Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs),
[Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs) and [Column
Chooser](?path=/docs/components-data-display-column-chooser--docs) in a
[Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs). The
[Projects](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-projects--docs) index
page uses both.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/import-export.json
```

## Import

Three steps, then the result.

1. **Upload**: one file, CSV by default. `templateHref` links a blank
   file with the right headings.
2. **Map columns**: each column of the file goes into one of your
   `fields`, or is not imported. A heading that matches a field's key,
   label or one of its `aliases` is mapped already, so a file made from
   the template needs no work here. A field takes one column; Next waits
   until every required field has one.
3. **Review**: every row with its problems beside it, from `validate`
   and from required fields left empty. A row with a problem is skipped,
   not fixed here: the file is the place to fix it. The button says how
   many rows it imports.

The result says how many were imported and how many skipped, and offers
the skipped rows as a CSV, with their problems in a last column, to fix
and upload again.

<Canvas of={ImportExportStories.Default} />

## Mapping

No heading matches a required field: the step names it and Next waits.
Choosing a field already taken moves it to this column.

<Canvas of={ImportExportStories.MapColumns} />

## Errors

A file that cannot be read, or has no rows, says so on the upload step.
An `onImport` that throws keeps you on the review step with its message:
nothing is lost, and Import can be tried again.

<Canvas of={ImportExportStories.Errors} />

## Export

Which rows (`scopes`: all, the current view, the selection, each with its
count), which format when there is more than one, and which columns,
ticked from the ones on screen. Each opening starts from those defaults,
since the view or the selection may have changed. Export calls
`onExport` and closes. A long export returns at once and says when the
file is ready with a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs)
and a Download action, as the story does.

<Canvas of={ImportExportStories.Export} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={ImportExportStories} />

`ExportDialog` takes `scopes` (radio options), `defaultScope`, `formats`
(radio options; one format hides the choice, CSV by default), `columns`
and `defaultColumnKeys` (as the Column Chooser's), `onExport`, which gets
`{ format, scope, columns }` and may return a promise, and the same
`trigger`, `title`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` and `container`.

The pattern owns no data. Reading the file is `readFile` (CSV text by
default; for Excel, read it with your spreadsheet library into `{ columns,
rows }` and widen `accept`), checking a row is `validate`, saving is
`onImport`, and writing the export is `onExport`. Three helpers come
with it: `parseCsv`, `toCsv` and `downloadCsv`. `toCsv` puts a `'` before
a cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` and is not a number, so a
spreadsheet shows it instead of running it as a formula.

## Layout

- The import is a large Modal (48rem), never wider than the window; the
  export a medium one.
- The review scrolls inside the dialog under its sticky heading row,
  so the summary above it and the buttons under it stay in view. It
  lists the first 100 rows and says how many more there are; the import
  still takes them all.
- Long values with no spaces break rather than widen the table.

<Canvas of={ImportExportStories.LongFile} />

## Differences from the spec

The catalogue lists Confirm as a step of its own. Here the review is the
confirmation: its button says how many rows it imports and the summary
above it how many it skips, so a fourth step would only repeat them.
Formats beyond CSV, and reading Excel, are the app's: the pattern adds no
spreadsheet library. The notice when an export is done is the app's
too, a Toast, since only the app knows when its file is ready. Both
dialogs are Modals rather than Drawers: each is a task that blocks the
list until it is done, not a side panel to keep open beside it.

## Accessibility

- Each dialog is named by its title. The import closes on Escape or its
  close button, not on a click outside, so a stray click does not throw
  away a mapped file.
- The steps are a navigation landmark, "Import steps", with the current
  step marked and each step's state said.
- Rows are numbered as a spreadsheet numbers them, the heading row
  being 1, so a problem can be found in the file. Blank rows keep their
  number and are not imported.
- Each mapping Select is named after its column: "Field for Budget".
- The review is a scrollable region the keyboard can reach and scroll.
  Each row's problems are text in its row, under a Problems heading, not
  colour alone.
- A failed read or import is announced as an alert; the result is
  announced as a status.
- The skipped rows and the template are real downloads, a button and a
  link.

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon, type IconName } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './InlineAlert.module.css'

export interface InlineAlertProps extends ComponentProps<'div'> {
  variant?: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** Replaces the variant's icon; `false` shows none. */
  icon?: ReactNode | false
  /** A short link or button after the message, e.g. "Retry". */
  action?: ReactNode
  /**
   * Announce it when it appears: `danger` and `warning` interrupt
   * (`role="alert"`), the others wait (`role="status"`).
   */
  isLive?: boolean
}

const icons: Record<NonNullable<InlineAlertProps['variant']>, IconName> = {
  info: 'info-filled',
  success: 'success-filled',
  warning: 'warning-filled',
  danger: 'danger-filled',
}

/**
 * A one-line message in the flow of a form or a section: no box, no title,
 * no close button. For a message about a whole page or region, use Alert.
 */
export function InlineAlert({
  variant = 'info',
  size = 'md',
  icon,
  action,
  isLive = false,
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: InlineAlertProps) {
  const urgent = variant === 'danger' || variant === 'warning'
  return (
    <div
      role={isLive ? (urgent ? 'alert' : 'status') : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.inlineAlert, styles[variant], styles[size], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {icon !== false && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {icon ?? <Icon name={icons[variant]} />}
        </span>
      )}
      <span className={styles.message}>{children}</span>
      {action && <span className={styles.action}>{action}</span>}
    </div>
  )
}
