# Inline Alert A one-line message in the flow of a form or a section, with no box, no titl...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as InlineAlertStories from './InlineAlert.stories'

<Meta of={InlineAlertStories} />

# Inline Alert

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A one-line message in the flow of a form or a section, with no box, no
title and no close button: "Changes are saved automatically", "Couldn't
reach the server".

<Status of={InlineAlertStories} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.Variants} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour, by meaning, and the whole line takes it.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `info` | A fact about what is above it: "Changes are saved automatically." |
| `success` | A check that passed: "Domain verified." |
| `warning` | A consequence to know before going on: "This link expires in 24 hours." |
| `danger` | Something that failed: "Couldn't reach the server." |

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.WithAction} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.LongMessage} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { InlineAlert } from 'zweihander/inline-alert'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/inline-alert.json
```

- Source: [src/components/notifications/InlineAlert.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/InlineAlert.tsx)
- Spec: our own; uiguideline.com has no page for it
- Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={InlineAlertStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={InlineAlertStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The icon box is one line tall, so on a message that wraps it stays on the
first line.

No padding, border or background: it lines up with the text and fields
around it.

## Color

The whole line, icon and message, takes the variant's text colour. An Alert
can keep its message in `--foreground` because its box carries the colour;
an inline alert has no box, so the text does. Every `--*-text` token is
4.5:1 on the page in both modes, so a message of any length stays readable.

<SpecTable
  caption="Icon and message, by variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'info', property: 'Colour', token: '--info-text' },
    { part: 'success', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'warning', property: 'Colour', token: '--warning-text' },
    { part: 'danger', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
  ]}
/>

The action keeps its own colours: a Link or a Button, as passed.

## States

The message has no states. An action in it has its own.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Action hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Action focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={InlineAlertStories.WithAction} />
</States>

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={InlineAlertStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Inline Alert for a short message about the thing right above it: a
group of fields, a whole form, a section. A failed submit is the common
case.

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.InAForm} />

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={InlineAlertStories.DoFieldError} />}
  doCaption="An error about one field goes on the field, as its helper text: it is read when the field is focused."
  dont={<Story of={InlineAlertStories.DontForOneField} />}
  dontCaption="An inline alert under a field is not tied to it: a screen reader in the field never hears it."
/>

## When not to use

- **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and
  `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`.
- **For a message about a whole page or region**, or one that needs a
  title, an action row or a close button. Use an
  [Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs).
- **For news about something that just happened.** Use a
  [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs).

## Accessibility

- A plain `<div>` by default, read in order with the page.
- `isLive` for a message that appears in response to something (a failed
  submit): `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at
  once, `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning.
- The action is whatever you pass (a Link, a Button) and keeps its own
  keyboard behaviour and focus ring.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState, type ComponentProps, type FocusEvent, type KeyboardEvent, type MouseEvent } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Button } from '../../buttons/Button'
import { TextInput } from '../../inputs/TextInput'
import styles from './InlineEdit.module.css'

export interface InlineEditProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children' | 'onChange'> {
  value: string
  /** What the value is, e.g. "Email". Names the input and the value's button ("Edit Email"). */
  label: string
  /**
   * Called with the new value on Enter, Save or leaving the field, only when
   * it changed. Return (or resolve) a message to show it under the field and
   * stay in edit; a throw or rejection shows its message the same way.
   */
  onSave: (value: string) => void | string | undefined | Promise<void | string | undefined>
  /** Shown, muted, when the value is empty. */
  placeholder?: string
  /**
   * The on-screen keyboard to offer. The input stays `type="text"`, so the
   * whole value can be selected on edit (browsers cannot select an email or
   * number input); check the format in `onSave`.
   */
  inputMode?: 'text' | 'email' | 'numeric' | 'decimal' | 'tel' | 'url'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
}

/**
 * A value that edits where it stands: in a table cell or a description list
 * row. Click it (or Enter on it) for a text input; Enter or Save keeps the
 * change, Escape or Cancel drops it. The pattern owns no data: it reports the
 * new value and shows the error you return.
 */
export function InlineEdit({
  value,
  label,
  onSave,
  placeholder = 'Empty',
  inputMode,
  size = 'md',
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: InlineEditProps) {
  const [isEditing, setIsEditing] = useState(false)
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState(value)
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const [isSaving, setIsSaving] = useState(false)
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const valueRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  // Enter, Save, Escape and Cancel hand focus back to the value; leaving the
  // field by Tab or click does not pull it back.
  const shouldRefocusValue = useRef(false)
  // A ref, not state: a blur and a click can both commit within one render.
  const isPending = useRef(false)

  // Layout, not passive: a save that resolves later must hand focus over
  // before anything else can read where it is.
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    if (isEditing) {
      inputRef.current?.focus()
      inputRef.current?.select()
    } else if (shouldRefocusValue.current) {
      shouldRefocusValue.current = false
      valueRef.current?.focus()
    }
  }, [isEditing])

  // A slow save must not pull focus back once the viewer has moved on.
  const focusIsHere = () => {
    const active = document.activeElement
    return !active || active === document.body || !!rootRef.current?.contains(active)
  }

  const start = () => {
    setDraft(value)
    setError(null)
    setIsEditing(true)
  }
  const close = (focusValue: boolean) => {
    shouldRefocusValue.current = focusValue
    setIsEditing(false)
  }
  const commit = async (focusValue: boolean) => {
    if (isPending.current) return
    if (draft === value) return close(focusValue)
    isPending.current = true
    setIsSaving(true)
    setError(null)
    let message: string | null = null
    try {
      message = (await onSave(draft)) || null
    } catch (e) {
      message = (e instanceof Error && e.message) || 'Could not save.'
    }
    isPending.current = false
    setIsSaving(false)
    const refocus = focusValue && focusIsHere()
    if (message) {
      setError(message)
      if (refocus) inputRef.current?.focus()
    } else close(refocus)
  }

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.nativeEvent.isComposing) {
      e.preventDefault()
      commit(true)
    } else if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      // Inside a Drawer or Modal, Escape cancels the edit, not the overlay,
      // and during a save it does nothing: the save cannot be called back.
      e.preventDefault()
      e.stopPropagation()
      if (!isSaving) close(true)
    }
  }
  // Pressing Save or Cancel keeps focus in the input, so no blur commits
  // first (Safari does not focus a clicked button, so relatedTarget is null).
  const preventBlurCommit = (e: MouseEvent) => e.preventDefault()
  const onBlur = (e: FocusEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    // Moving to Save or Cancel stays inside the editor.
    if (e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget)) return
    commit(false)
  }

  return (
    <div
      ref={(node) => {
        rootRef.current = node
        if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(node)
        else if (ref) ref.current = node
      }}
      className={cn(styles.inlineEdit, styles[size], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {isEditing ? (
        <div className={styles.editor} onBlur={onBlur}>
          <TextInput
            ref={inputRef}
            aria-label={label}
            inputMode={inputMode}
            autoComplete="off"
            size={size}
            isFullWidth
            className={styles.field}
            value={draft}
            readOnly={isSaving}
            onChange={(e) => {
              setDraft(e.target.value)
              setError(null)
            }}
            onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
            validationState={error ? 'error' : 'default'}
            helperText={error ?? undefined}
          />
          <Button
            size={size}
            variant="secondary"
            appearance="ghost"
            isIconOnly
            aria-label="Save"
            isLoading={isSaving}
            onMouseDown={preventBlurCommit}
            onClick={() => commit(true)}
          >
            <Icon name="check" />
          </Button>
          <Button
            size={size}
            variant="secondary"
            appearance="ghost"
            isIconOnly
            aria-label="Cancel"
            disabled={isSaving}
            onMouseDown={preventBlurCommit}
            onClick={() => close(true)}
          >
            <Icon name="close" />
          </Button>
        </div>
      ) : (
        <button ref={valueRef} type="button" className={styles.value} onClick={start}>
          <span className={styles.srOnly}>Edit {label}: </span>
          <span className={value ? styles.text : styles.placeholder}>{value || placeholder}</span>
          <Icon name="edit" className={styles.pencil} />
        </button>
      )}
      {/* Always rendered, so "Saving" and an error are announced when they
          appear, even after a blur save, when focus has left the field. */}
      <span role="status" className={styles.srOnly}>
        {isSaving ? 'Saving' : (error ?? '')}
      </span>
    </div>
  )
}

# Inline Edit A value that edits where it stands, in a table cell or a description list ro...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as InlineEditStories from './InlineEdit.stories'

<Meta of={InlineEditStories} />

# Inline Edit

A value that edits where it stands, in a table cell or a description list
row, so changing one field does not take a trip to a form. After the inline
edit of enterprise SaaS and ERP tools (Salesforce, Airtable, SAP Fiori's
editable tables).

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/inline-edit.json
```

The pattern owns no data. It shows `value`, calls `onSave` with the new
one, and shows the message you return when the save fails.

## Description list

Each detail of a record edits in its row. Hover or focus a value and a
pencil shows that it can change; click it, or press Enter on it, and it
becomes a text input with the whole value selected. Enter or Save keeps the
change, Escape or Cancel drops it.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.Default} />

## Table cell

Put it in a column's `cell`. Use `size="sm"` in a table row, and name each
one by its row in `label` ("PO reference for INV-1041"), since every cell in
the column says the same thing otherwise.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.InTable} />

## Error

Return a message from `onSave` (or throw one) and it shows under the field,
which stays open with what was typed. Typing again clears it. Check the
format here: the input is always `type="text"`, so `inputMode` only picks
the on-screen keyboard.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.Invalid} />

## Saving

Return a promise and the field is saving until it settles: the input is
read-only, Save spins, and Cancel and Escape wait. A rejection shows its
message as an error.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.Saving} />

## Leaving the field

Tab or click away and the change is saved, not lost. Focus goes where the
viewer sent it, and a slow save does not pull it back. A save that fails
leaves the field open with its error. An unchanged value closes without calling `onSave`.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.SaveOnBlur} />

## Empty and long values

An empty value shows `placeholder`, muted, so there is still something to
click. A long value wraps, even with no spaces, instead of widening the
cell.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.EmptyAndLong} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={InlineEditStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through to the root.

## Layout

- **The value lines up with the text around it.** The root pulls back by
  the field's inline padding, so the value's text starts where a plain
  cell's text does, and the input's text starts in the same place: entering
  edit mode does not shift it. It pulls back by the extra height too, so the
  value sits on the same line as the term or the cells beside it.
- **Save and Cancel sit at the end of the input**, aligned to its box; an
  error goes under the box and pushes the row taller, not the buttons down.
- **The pencil does not take space away from the value** on hover: it has
  its place from the start, hidden until hover or focus. On a touch screen,
  where nothing hovers, it always shows.
- **On a touch screen** the value's hit area grows to 44px without the value
  growing.

## Accessibility

- The value is a button named "Edit {label}: {value}", so a screen reader
  says what it edits and what it holds. Enter or Space on it opens the
  input, focused, with the value selected.
- The input is named by `label`. Enter saves; Escape cancels and does not
  close a Drawer or Modal around it.
- After Enter, Save, Escape or Cancel, focus returns to the value.
- An error marks the input invalid and becomes its description, so it is
  read with the field; a status announces it too, since after a blur save
  focus has already left.
- While saving, a status says "Saving" and Save is busy. Escape waits,
  and still does not reach the overlay.

<Canvas of={InlineEditStories.Keyboard} />

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect, waitFor } from 'storybook/test'
import { Button } from '@/components/buttons/Button'
import { anatomyPartFor, startInspector, type TokenValue } from './inspect'

/**
 * What the Specs tab draws inside the preview frame: the parts numbered, the
 * hovered row's redline, and the tokens resolved as the frame sees them.
 */
const meta = {
  title: 'Site/Inspect',
  render: () => <Button>Subscribe</Button>,
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

const layer = () => document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-playground-inspector]')

/** Which anatomy part a Specs row is about. */
export const RowToPart: Story = {
  play: async () => {
    const names = ['Container', 'Start icon', 'Label', 'Title', 'Previous month']
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Container, outlined', names)).toBe('Container')
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Title and description', names)).toBe('Title')
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Icon', names)).toBe('Start icon')
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Previous and next', names)).toBe('Previous month')
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Focus ring', names)).toBe('Focus ring')
    // A whole word only: "Lab" is not Label.
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Lab', names)).toBeNull()
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Option', names)).toBeNull()
  },
}

export const Default: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    let values: Record<string, TokenValue> = {}
    const inspector = startInspector(
      () => canvasElement,
      (v) => (values = v),
    )
    const parts = [
      { name: 'Container', selector: 'button' },
      { name: 'Missing', selector: 'nav' },
    ]
    try {
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: ['--control-md', '--primary', '--nope'] })
      // One number, on the part that is there; decoration only.
      await waitFor(() => expect(layer()?.textContent).toBe('①'))
      await expect(layer()).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true')
      await expect(getComputedStyle(layer()!).pointerEvents).toBe('none')
      await waitFor(() => expect(values['--control-md']).toEqual({ kind: 'length', text: '32px' }))
      await expect(values['--primary'].kind).toBe('color')
      await expect(values['--nope']).toEqual({ kind: 'missing', text: 'Not defined here' })

      // A row's redline: the part's height, with its value.
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: ['--control-md'], highlight: { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' } })
      await waitFor(() => expect(layer()?.textContent).toContain('Height 32px'))
      const button = canvasElement.querySelector('button')!.getBoundingClientRect()
      const line = [...layer()!.children].find((el) => (el as HTMLElement).style.width === '1px') as HTMLElement
      await expect(parseFloat(line.style.height)).toBeCloseTo(button.height, 0)

      // Inline padding shades the two sides.
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: [], highlight: { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--x' } })
      await waitFor(() => expect([...layer()!.children].filter((el) => (el as HTMLElement).style.background.includes('0.25'))).toHaveLength(2))

      // The focus ring at its width and offset around the focusable element, though no anatomy part names it.
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: ['--focus-width'], highlight: { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' } })
      await waitFor(() => expect(layer()?.textContent).toContain('Width 2px'))
      const ring = [...layer()!.children].find((el) => (el as HTMLElement).style.borderWidth === '2px') as HTMLElement
      await expect(parseFloat(ring.style.width)).toBeCloseTo(button.width + 2 * (2 + 2), 0)

      // Radius marks the corner; font size shades the first line of text.
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: [], highlight: { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--x' } })
      await waitFor(() => expect([...layer()!.children].some((el) => (el as HTMLElement).style.borderTopLeftRadius !== '')).toBe(true))
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: [], highlight: { part: 'Container', property: 'Font size', token: '--x' } })
      await waitFor(() => expect([...layer()!.children].filter((el) => (el as HTMLElement).style.background.includes('0.25'))).toHaveLength(1))

      // A forced state goes on the item's root as the pseudo-states addon's class, and comes off.
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: [], pseudo: 'hover' })
      await expect(canvasElement).toHaveClass('pseudo-hover-all')
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: [], pseudo: 'active' })
      await expect(canvasElement).not.toHaveClass('pseudo-hover-all')
      await expect(canvasElement).toHaveClass('pseudo-active-all')
    } finally {
      inspector.set(null)
    }
    await expect(layer()).toBeNull()
    await expect(canvasElement).not.toHaveClass('pseudo-active-all')
  },
}

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Kbd.module.css'

/** One key as `children`, or a combination as `keys`: never both. */
export type KbdProps = Omit<ComponentProps<'kbd'>, 'children'> & { size?: 'sm' | 'md' } & (
    | { children: ReactNode; keys?: never }
    | { /** A key combination, one key cap per entry: `['⌘', 'K']`. */ keys: string[]; children?: never }
  )

export function Kbd({ keys, size = 'md', className, children, ...props }: KbdProps) {
  const cap = cn(styles.key, styles[size])
  if (!keys) {
    return (
      <kbd className={cn(cap, className)} {...props}>
        {children}
      </kbd>
    )
  }
  // HTML's own markup for a combination: a <kbd> of <kbd>s, one per key.
  return (
    <kbd className={cn(styles.group, className)} {...props}>
      {keys.map((key, i) => (
        <kbd key={i} className={cap}>
          {key}
        </kbd>
      ))}
    </kbd>
  )
}

# Kbd

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A key cap that shows which key to press: a glyph like ⌘ or ⇧, a letter,
or a short word like Esc.

<Status of={KbdStories} />

Kbd is outside the 1.0 component list, so it starts as experimental.

<Canvas of={KbdStories.Sizes} />

## Variants

| Form | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> one key | A single key: `children`. |
| <Kbd keys={['⌘', 'K']} /> combination | Keys pressed together: `keys`, one cap per key. |

<Canvas of={KbdStories.Combination} />

`size="sm"` (16px) fits inside a small control or a dense row; `md`
(20px) is the default, for running text, tooltips and menus.

<Canvas of={KbdStories.InText} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Kbd } from 'zweihander/kbd'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/kbd.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Kbd.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Kbd.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; after [shadcn/ui Kbd](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/kbd)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={KbdStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={KbdStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

A combination is HTML's own markup for one: an outer `<kbd>` holding a
`<kbd>` per key. A single key is just the cap.

## States

A key cap is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are
what it shows.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Glyph', content: <Kbd>⌘</Kbd> },
    { label: 'Word', content: <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> },
    { label: 'Combination', content: <Kbd keys={['⌘', '⇧', 'P']} /> },
    { label: 'sm', content: <Kbd size="sm" keys={['⌘', 'K']} /> },
  ]}
/>

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={KbdStories} />
</div>

Every other `<kbd>` attribute passes through to the outer element.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Kbd wherever the page tells someone which key to press: a hint in a
tooltip, a command palette row, a line of help text, a shortcuts sheet.
These are places where people come to learn a shortcut, so the key gets a
cap. A Menu is not: see below.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={KbdStories.DoHideInControl} />}
  doCaption="Inside a control the caps are hidden and the button says Meta+K through aria-keyshortcuts: its name stays “Search”."
  dont={<Story of={KbdStories.DontLeaveInName} />}
  dontCaption="Left in, the glyphs join the name: a screen reader hears “Search ⌘ K”, and ⌘ is read as “place of interest”."
/>

Match the platform: ⌘ and ⌥ on a Mac, Ctrl and Alt elsewhere. Kbd shows
what it is given and does not detect the platform.

## When not to use

- **For a Menu item's shortcut.** Use Menu's `shortcut` string: menus
  show shortcuts as quiet text at the end of the row, the way desktop
  menus do. The menu is for acting, and a cap on every row would pull the
  eye from the labels. A command palette is the exception: it is where
  shortcuts are discovered, so its rows use Kbd.
- **For code or a value someone types.** Use `<code>`: Kbd is a key, not
  text to copy.
- **To bind the key.** Kbd is display only; the page binds the shortcut.

## Accessibility

- Kbd is a native `<kbd>`; a combination is a `<kbd>` of `<kbd>`s, one
  per key.
- It is not focusable and has no role: it is never in the tab order.
- In running text it is read where it sits, as text: "Press Esc to close".
  A combination's keys are read one after the other with no "plus" (⌘S);
  write the combination out in the sentence when that matters.
- Inside a control, hide it with `aria-hidden` and put the shortcut on the
  control with `aria-keyshortcuts` (for example `Meta+K`), so the
  control's name stays its label.
- Contrast is checked by addon-a11y in error mode for every story.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Layering Four layers for everything that leaves the page flow. A component picks the lay...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as LayeringStories from './Layering.stories'

<Meta of={LayeringStories} />

# Layering

Four layers for everything that leaves the page flow. A component picks
the layer by what it is, never by trying a bigger number.

<Canvas of={LayeringStories.Layers} />

## One layer for every overlay

Popovers, menus, listboxes, date pickers, modals and drawers all share
`--layer-overlay`. They are portalled to the end of `<body>`, so at an equal
z-index the one opened last paints on top: a Select opened inside a Modal
lands above the Modal without either knowing about the other. Giving the
Modal a higher layer would break exactly that case.

Tooltips sit one layer up because they can belong to anything, including a
trigger inside an open overlay. Toasts sit above everything: a toast raised
while a modal is open still has to be read.

## Local z-index

A value used only to order parts inside one component (a table's sticky
header at `1`, the tab indicator at `-1`) is local and stays a plain number.
Keep these at single digits so they stay well below `--layer-sticky`.

# Link Text that takes you somewhere: another page, a section of this one, an outside site...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Link } from './Link'
import * as LinkStories from './Link.stories'

<Meta of={LinkStories} />

# Link

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Text that takes you somewhere: another page, a section of this one, an
outside site. It navigates; it does not act.

<Status of={LinkStories} />

<Canvas of={LinkStories.InText} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour; `underline` says whether the line shows at rest.
Any variant takes either underline.

<Canvas of={LinkStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Link href="#link">Primary</Link> | Links in running text and on their own. The default. |
| <Link href="#link" variant="accent">Accent</Link> | Links in the foreground colour, where the brand colour would compete: dense lists, navigation. |
| <Link href="#link" variant="secondary">Secondary</Link> | Footers, captions and meta text, where the link is not the point. |

| Underline | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Link href="#link">Always</Link> | Inside running text, where only the line tells a link from the words around it. The default. |
| <Link href="#link" underline="hover">Hover</Link> | Places that are obviously lists of links: a nav list, a footer column. |

Without a `size`, a link takes the size of the sentence around it, which
is what a link in text wants. `sm`, `md` and `lg` are for links that stand
alone.

<Canvas of={LinkStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={LinkStories.External} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Link } from 'zweihander/link'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/link.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Link.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Link.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/link](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/link)
- Behaviour: a native `<a>`; `render` from [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={LinkStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={LinkStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The underline is a text decoration on the link itself, 1px thick and
offset 0.2em below the text.

## Measurements

Each size sets only the text; without one, the link inherits it.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="lg"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-lg' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-lg' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius (the focus ring follows it)', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

The text is medium weight. The external icon is 0.9em, so it scales with
the text, with 0.2em before it.

## Color

The text and its underline share one colour. Switch the theme and the
accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable caption="primary" rows={[{ part: 'Text and underline', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-text' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="accent" rows={[{ part: 'Text and underline', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="secondary" rows={[{ part: 'Text and underline', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="Every variant" rows={[{ part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' }]} />

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={LinkStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={LinkStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** thickens the underline from 1px to 2px and keeps the colour,
  so the link keeps the contrast it was measured at. With
  `underline="hover"`, hover is when the line appears.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the text.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity, with no `href`.
- There is no visited style: most links in an app lead to screens, not
  documents, and a "seen it" colour there is noise.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={LinkStories} />
</div>

Every other `<a>` attribute passes through, including `ref`, `target` and
`rel`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Link to go somewhere: another page, a section of this one, a file,
an outside site. Inside a sentence, keep the underline; let the link
text say where it goes, so it still makes sense read on its own.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={LinkStories.DoSayWhere} />}
  doCaption="The link text names the destination: it reads on its own, in a screen reader's list of links too."
  dont={<Story of={LinkStories.DontClickHere} />}
  dontCaption={'"Click here" says nothing out of context, and hides where the link goes.'}
/>

Mark links that leave for another site with `isExternal` only when they
open a new tab, and keep that rare: a new tab breaks the Back button.

With a router, pass its link as `render`. Link merges its class and props
onto it, and the router keeps control of navigation:

```tsx
<Link render={<RouterLink to="/settings" />}>Settings</Link>
```

## When not to use

- **For an action.** Saving, deleting or opening a dialog is a
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). A link-styled
  action looks like it will take you away, and does not respond to Space.
- **For a prominent call to action that navigates.** Use a Button with
  `href`: it renders an `<a>` with the weight of a button.
- **For a trail of parent pages.** Use Breadcrumbs.
- **For moving through pages of a list.** Use Pagination.

## Accessibility

- A real `<a href>`, so it is in the tab order, opens with Enter, and
  shows up in a screen reader's list of links.
- Underlined by default: colour alone does not mark a link for someone who
  cannot tell the colours apart (WCAG 1.4.1).
- `isExternal` adds "(opens in a new tab)" to the accessible name, and
  sets `rel="noopener noreferrer"`: a new tab that opens without warning
  strands people who cannot see it happen.
- `isDisabled` removes `href`, the only thing that stops an `<a>`
  navigating, drops the click handlers and sets `aria-disabled`. Without
  an `href` it leaves the tab order. Prefer hiding a link that cannot be
  followed, or saying in text why it is unavailable.
- Every variant is a text colour measured at 4.5:1 on the page, and hover
  does not change it.
- Focus ring: 2px `--ring`, 2px offset.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

 * The frame around a list: a line between rows, optionally a panel around
 * them, a footer and an empty state. It owns the rows' padding and dividers;
 * what sits in a row is up to the caller (Stacked List puts its records here).
 */
export function ListContainer({ children, appearance = 'flat', footer, empty = 'Nothing here yet.', className, ...props }: ListContainerProps) {
  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.root, styles[appearance], className)} {...props}>
      {Children.toArray(children).length === 0 ? <p className={styles.empty}>{empty}</p> : <ul className={styles.list}>{children}</ul>}
      {footer && <div className={styles.footer}>{footer}</div>}
    </div>
  )
}

/** One row of a ListContainer: an `<li>` with the row's padding and divider. Every `<li>` prop passes through. */
export function ListContainerItem({ className, ...props }: ComponentProps<'li'>) {
  return <li className={cn(styles.item, className)} {...props} />
}

# List Container The frame around a list: a line between rows, optionally a panel around t...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ListContainerStories from './ListContainer.stories'

<Meta of={ListContainerStories} />

# List Container

The frame around a list: a line between rows, optionally a panel around
them, a footer and an empty state. It owns the rows' padding and dividers
and nothing inside them. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Lists: List
containers.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/list-container.json
```

`ListContainer` is the `<ul>` and its frame; `ListContainerItem` is one
`<li>`, padded as a Table row. For records (an avatar, a title, a status, a
link or actions), use [Stacked
List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stacked-list--docs): it renders
through List Container and takes the same `appearance`, `footer` and
`empty`, so there is one way to frame a list, add a footer or say it is
empty.

## Flat

Rows divided by a line, no frame. The default: a list in a page section,
or in a panel that already has an edge.

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.Flat} />

## Card

The same rows in a bordered panel, as an outline Card, for a list that
stands on its own on the page.

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.Card} />

## Separate

Each row its own panel, a gap instead of lines: rows that read as separate
objects rather than one list.

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.Separate} />

## With Stacked List

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.WithStackedList} />

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.SeparateStackedList} />

## Empty

No rows shows `empty`, "Nothing here yet." by default, in place of the
list, inside the frame. The footer still shows.

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={ListContainerStories} />

Every `<div>` attribute passes through to the root, and every `<li>`
attribute to `ListContainerItem`.

## Layout

- Rows pad by `--space-inline` above and below and `--space-4` at the
  sides, and are at least `--row-height` tall, so a list lines up with a
  Table of the same density.
- `footer` sits past a divider in `flat` and `card`, and after the gap in
  `separate`.
- No breakpoints: the container is as wide as its column. Long words in a
  row break anywhere rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={ListContainerStories.LongContent} />

## Differences from the spec

- **Full width on mobile** (Tailwind's card and separate variants that
  drop their side edges on small screens) is left out: whether a panel
  bleeds to the screen edge is the page layout's call, not the list's.
- **Flat card** (a tinted panel without a border) is the `card`
  appearance: one panel look, the outline Card's.

## Accessibility

- The rows are an unordered list, so a screen reader announces how many
  there are. Keep `ListContainerItem` the only child of the container, so
  the list has only `<li>` children.
- The empty state is a paragraph in place of the list, so an empty list
  is not announced as a list of zero items.
- The container has no landmark or heading of its own. Put it under a
  heading, or pass `role="region"` and an `aria-label`.

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './MediaObject.module.css'

export interface MediaObjectProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'title'> {
  /** An Avatar, an Icon or an image beside the text. Decorative: the title names what it shows. */
  media: ReactNode
  /** What the object is: a person, a product, a comment's author. */
  title: ReactNode
  /** A line or a paragraph under the title. */
  description?: ReactNode
  /** Anything after the description: actions, or nested Media Objects for replies. */
  children?: ReactNode
  /** Where the media sits against the text: top, middle, bottom, or stretched to the text's full height. */
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'stretch'
  /** Which side the media is on. */
  mediaPosition?: 'start' | 'end'
  /** Makes the title a heading of this level. Without it the title is bold text, right for a list of comments. */
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4
}

/**
 * Media beside a block of text: an avatar by a comment, an icon by a
 * setting, a thumbnail by a product. It owns no data and no landmark.
 */
export function MediaObject({
  media,
  title,
  description,
  children,
  align = 'start',
  mediaPosition = 'start',
  headingLevel,
  className,
  ...props
}: MediaObjectProps) {
  const Title = headingLevel ? (`h${headingLevel}` as const) : 'p'
  return (
    <div
      className={cn(styles.mediaObject, className)}
      data-align={align}
      data-media-position={mediaPosition}
      {...props}
    >
      <div className={styles.media} aria-hidden="true">
        {media}
      </div>
      <div className={styles.body}>
        <Title className={styles.title}>{title}</Title>
        {description && <div className={styles.description}>{description}</div>}
        {children}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

# Media Object Media beside a block of text: an avatar by a comment, an icon by a setting,...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as MediaObjectStories from './MediaObject.stories'

<Meta of={MediaObjectStories} />

# Media Object

Media beside a block of text: an avatar by a comment, an icon by a
setting, a thumbnail by a product. After Tailwind UI Application UI,
Layout: Media Objects.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/media-object.json
```

Use it for one thing on its own. A list of records is a [Stacked
List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stacked-list--docs) or a [Grid
List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-grid-list--docs); a history of
events is a [Feed](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-feed--docs); the top
row of a card is a [Card
Heading](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-card-heading--docs). Those
lay out their own media because each treats it differently (a filled
circle, a timeline, a heading-sized row). A framed block with a picture on
the side is a [Card](?path=/docs/data-display-card--docs) with
`orientation="horizontal"`.

## Basic

`media`, then `title` and `description`. The title is bold text, so a
column of comments does not fill the page outline with headings.

<Canvas of={MediaObjectStories.Basic} />

## As a heading

`headingLevel` makes the title a heading, for a media object that starts a
section.

<Canvas of={MediaObjectStories.AsHeading} />

## Alignment

`align` places the media at the top (the default), the middle or the
bottom of the text, or stretches it to the text's height.

<Canvas of={MediaObjectStories.AlignCenter} />
<Canvas of={MediaObjectStories.AlignEnd} />
<Canvas of={MediaObjectStories.Stretch} />

## Media at the end

`mediaPosition="end"` draws the media after the text. The DOM order does
not change.

<Canvas of={MediaObjectStories.MediaAtEnd} />

## Nested

`children` comes after the description: actions, or a reply as another
Media Object, which lines up with the parent's text.

<Canvas of={MediaObjectStories.Nested} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={MediaObjectStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **No breakpoint.** Media and text share a row while the text keeps
  12rem; in a narrower container the text wraps under the media. It
  follows the container, so it works in an aside as on a full page.
- **Long words break anywhere** rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={MediaObjectStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

Tailwind UI's Media Objects, and where this departs from them:

- **Responsive stacking follows the container, not the viewport.** The
  text wraps under the media only when it would get less than 12rem, so
  an avatar stays beside its text on a phone. Tailwind's "basic
  responsive" and "wide responsive" stack below the `sm` breakpoint, and
  the wide one swaps a large image's size; neither is a separate variant
  here.
- **Stretch suits a thumbnail or a placeholder** with no fixed height. An
  Avatar or an `<img>` with a height keeps it.
- **The media is always decorative**, and `headingLevel` is opt-in;
  Tailwind uses an `h4` every time.

## Accessibility

- The media is decorative and hidden from assistive tech: the title says
  who or what it is. Do not put a link or a button in `media`.
- The title is a paragraph unless `headingLevel` is set. Set it only when
  the object starts a section, and pick the level that follows the
  heading above, so the outline has no gaps.
- `mediaPosition="end"` moves the media visually only (CSS `order`); reading and focus
  order stay media, title, description, then `children`.

'use client'

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Menu as BaseMenu } from '@base-ui/react/menu'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Menu.module.css'

interface ItemBase {
  label: ReactNode
  /** Used for typeahead when `label` is not plain text. */
  textValue?: string
  icon?: ReactNode
  disabled?: boolean
}

/** An action, a link (`href`), or a submenu (`items`). */
export interface MenuActionItem extends ItemBase {
  type?: 'item'
  onSelect?: () => void
  href?: string
  /** Shown right-aligned, e.g. "⌘ D". Display only: it does not bind the key. */
  shortcut?: string
  /** Deletes or removes something: drawn in the danger colour. */
  isDestructive?: boolean
  /** Opens a submenu instead of acting. */
  items?: MenuEntry[]
}
export interface MenuCheckboxItem extends ItemBase {
  type: 'checkbox'
  checked?: boolean
  defaultChecked?: boolean
  onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean) => void
}
export interface MenuRadioGroupItem {
  type: 'radio'
  label?: ReactNode
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  options: { value: string; label: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }[]
}
export interface MenuGroupItem {
  type: 'group'
  label: ReactNode
  items: MenuEntry[]
}
export interface MenuSeparator {
  type: 'separator'
}
export type MenuEntry = MenuActionItem | MenuCheckboxItem | MenuRadioGroupItem | MenuGroupItem | MenuSeparator

export interface MenuProps {
  /** The button that opens it. Its props are merged, not wrapped. */
  trigger: ReactElement
  items: MenuEntry[]
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /**
   * While open, lock page scroll and make the rest of the page inert, so the
   * menu is the only thing to interact with. `false` leaves the page as is.
   */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where the popup renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
}

const text = (label: ReactNode, textValue?: string) => textValue ?? (typeof label === 'string' ? label : undefined)

/** Renders `MenuEntry[]` as Base UI menu parts, inside a `MenuSurface`. A building block for menus that share Menu's look. */
export function MenuEntries({ items }: { items: MenuEntry[] }) {
  return items.map((entry, i) => {
    switch (entry.type) {
      case 'separator':
        return <BaseMenu.Separator key={i} className={styles.separator} />
      case 'group':
        return (
          <BaseMenu.Group key={i} className={styles.group}>
            <BaseMenu.GroupLabel className={styles.groupLabel}>{entry.label}</BaseMenu.GroupLabel>
            <MenuEntries items={entry.items} />
          </BaseMenu.Group>
        )
      case 'checkbox':
        return (
          <BaseMenu.CheckboxItem
            key={i}
            label={text(entry.label, entry.textValue)}
            checked={entry.checked}
            defaultChecked={entry.defaultChecked}
            onCheckedChange={entry.onCheckedChange && ((c) => entry.onCheckedChange!(c))}
            disabled={entry.disabled}
            closeOnClick={false}
            className={styles.item}
          >
            <span className={styles.indicator}>
              <BaseMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator>
                <Icon name="check" />
              </BaseMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator>
            </span>
            <span className={styles.label}>{entry.label}</span>
          </BaseMenu.CheckboxItem>
        )
      case 'radio':
        return (
          <BaseMenu.Group key={i} className={styles.group}>
            {entry.label && <BaseMenu.GroupLabel className={styles.groupLabel}>{entry.label}</BaseMenu.GroupLabel>}
            <BaseMenu.RadioGroup
              value={entry.value}
              defaultValue={entry.defaultValue}
              onValueChange={entry.onValueChange && ((v) => entry.onValueChange!(v as string))}
            >
              {entry.options.map((o) => (
                <BaseMenu.RadioItem
                  key={o.value}
                  value={o.value}
                  label={text(o.label)}
                  disabled={o.disabled}
                  closeOnClick={false}
                  className={styles.item}
                >
                  <span className={styles.indicator}>
                    <BaseMenu.RadioItemIndicator>
                      <Icon name="check" />
                    </BaseMenu.RadioItemIndicator>
                  </span>
                  <span className={styles.label}>{o.label}</span>
                </BaseMenu.RadioItem>
              ))}
            </BaseMenu.RadioGroup>
          </BaseMenu.Group>
        )
      default: {
        const content = (
          <>
            {entry.icon && (
              <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
                {entry.icon}
              </span>
            )}
            <span className={styles.label}>{entry.label}</span>
            {entry.shortcut && (
              <kbd className={styles.shortcut} aria-hidden="true">
                {entry.shortcut}
              </kbd>
            )}
          </>
        )
        const className = cn(styles.item, entry.isDestructive && styles.destructive)
        if (entry.items) {
          return (
            <BaseMenu.SubmenuRoot key={i}>
              <BaseMenu.SubmenuTrigger label={text(entry.label, entry.textValue)} disabled={entry.disabled} className={className}>
                {content}
                <span className={styles.chevron} aria-hidden="true">
                  <Icon name="chevron-right" />
                </span>
              </BaseMenu.SubmenuTrigger>
              <MenuSurface side="right" align="start">
                <MenuEntries items={entry.items} />
              </MenuSurface>
            </BaseMenu.SubmenuRoot>
          )
        }
        // A disabled link is an inert item: Base UI's LinkItem has no disabled state.
        if (entry.href !== undefined && !entry.disabled) {
          return (
            <BaseMenu.LinkItem key={i} href={entry.href} label={text(entry.label, entry.textValue)} className={className}>
              {content}
            </BaseMenu.LinkItem>
          )
        }
        return (
          <BaseMenu.Item
            key={i}
            label={text(entry.label, entry.textValue)}
            disabled={entry.disabled}
            onClick={entry.onSelect && (() => entry.onSelect!())}
            className={className}
          >
            {content}
          </BaseMenu.Item>
        )
      }
    }
  })
}

/** Menu's popup surface, rendered through a portal, 4px from its trigger by default. */
export function MenuSurface({
  side,
  align,
  sideOffset = 4,
  container,
  className,
  children,
}: {
  side: MenuProps['side']
  align: MenuProps['align']
  sideOffset?: number
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
  children: ReactNode
}) {
  return (
    <BaseMenu.Portal container={container}>
      <BaseMenu.Positioner className={styles.positioner} side={side} align={align} sideOffset={sideOffset}>
        <BaseMenu.Popup className={cn(styles.popup, className)}>{children}</BaseMenu.Popup>
      </BaseMenu.Positioner>
    </BaseMenu.Portal>
  )
}

export function Menu({
  trigger,
  items,
  side = 'bottom',
  align = 'start',
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  isModal = true,
  container,
  className,
}: MenuProps) {
  return (
    <BaseMenu.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}
      modal={isModal}
    >
      <BaseMenu.Trigger render={trigger} />
      <MenuSurface side={side} align={align} container={container} className={className}>
        <MenuEntries items={items} />
      </MenuSurface>
    </BaseMenu.Root>
  )
}

# Menu A list of actions that opens from a button: the "…" on a row, an "Actions" dropdown...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as MenuStories from './Menu.stories'

<Meta of={MenuStories} />

# Menu

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A list of actions that opens from a button: the "…" on a row, an
"Actions" dropdown, a "View" menu of toggles. It acts or toggles; to pick a
value for a form, use a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs).

<Status of={MenuStories} />

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Default} />

## Variants

Menu has one look. What changes is the kind of entry in `items`, and a
menu can mix them:

| Entry | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Action (the default) | Something to do now: Edit, Duplicate, Delete. Closes the menu. `isDestructive` draws it in the danger colour. |
| Link (`href`) | Going somewhere: Documentation, Settings. A real `<a>`. |
| Submenu (`items`) | A set of choices that belongs under one item: Move to, Share with. |
| Checkbox (`type: 'checkbox'`) | Settings that are on or off, several at a time: Show hidden files. Keeps the menu open. |
| Radio (`type: 'radio'`) | One of a few settings: Sort by name, date or size. Keeps the menu open. |
| Group (`type: 'group'`) and separator | Structure for a longer menu: a label over related items, a rule between sets. |

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Groups} />

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Submenu} />

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Links} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Menu } from 'zweihander/menu'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/menu.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Menu.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Menu.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={MenuStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={MenuStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

A link item has the same parts as an action. Checkbox and radio items show
a check where an action shows its icon, so their labels line up.

## Measurements

The popup is the Select list's surface. Each item is a row of the md
control tier, with the normal pad: its text is left-aligned. The item's
corner nests inside the popup's: the popup radius minus the popup padding,
so the highlight runs parallel to the popup edge.

<SpecTable
  caption="Popup"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-field' },
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-md' },
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Layer', token: '--layer-overlay' },
    { part: 'Separator', property: 'Margin', token: '--space-1' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Item"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-md-gap' },
    { part: 'Icon, check, chevron', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Shortcut, group label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Shortcut', property: 'Space before', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The popup is at least 12rem wide, or the trigger's width if that is wider,
and no taller than the space on screen: past that it scrolls. It opens
4px from the trigger.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Popup"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Text', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Separator', property: 'Colour', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Group label, shortcut, chevron', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Item"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Item, highlighted', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Item, highlighted', property: 'Text and icon', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Item, disabled', property: 'Text', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Destructive item"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Text and icon', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Item, highlighted', property: 'Background', token: '--danger-subtle' },
  ]}
/>

The destructive item uses the danger text colour, not the solid: it reads
at 4.5:1 on the popup and on its highlight.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Closed', content: <Story of={MenuStories.Default} /> },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={MenuStories.Open} /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Highlighted** is where the arrow keys or the pointer are: a `--accent`
  fill, the icon taking the text colour. A submenu's item stays highlighted
  while its submenu is open. Focus moves with the highlight, so there is no
  separate focus ring inside the popup.
- **Disabled** items are muted at 60% opacity and skipped by the arrow
  keys (Archive, above).
- **Checked** checkbox and radio items show the check; unchecked ones keep
  the empty column.
- The trigger's own hover, focus and pressed states are the
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs)'s.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={MenuStories} />
</div>

`items` is data, like Select's `options`, not child components.
`shortcut` is display only: binding the key is left to the page, which
knows what else is bound.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Menu for actions that belong to one thing but would crowd the
screen as buttons: the actions on a table row, a card's overflow, a
toolbar's "More". Keep it short, put the most used item first, and give
destructive actions the last place, after a separator.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={MenuStories.DoDestructiveLast} />}
  doCaption="Delete last, after a separator, in the danger colour."
  dont={<Story of={MenuStories.DontDestructiveAmongOthers} />}
  dontCaption="Delete between two everyday actions: one arrow key too far and it is chosen."
/>

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={MenuStories.DoActions} />}
  doCaption="A menu of actions. Each item does something now."
  dont={<Story of={MenuStories.DontMenuAsField} />}
  dontCaption="A menu standing in for a form field. Use a Select: it has a label, a value and a form name."
/>

## When not to use

- **To pick a value for a form.** Use a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs) when the list
  is long enough to search.
- **For one or two actions.** Show them as
  [Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs): a hidden action
  is one fewer person finds.
- **For the app's main navigation.** Use a
  [Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs) or
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs), which show where
  the reader is.
- **For content: a form, a preview.** Use a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). A menu holds
  only menu items.

## Accessibility

- The trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; the popup
  is a `role="menu"` of `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and
  `menuitemradio`, with `aria-checked` on the toggles and
  `aria-disabled` on disabled items.
- Keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow Down on the trigger opens it; arrows
  move (disabled items are skipped), typing a few letters jumps to the
  matching item, Enter selects, Arrow Right opens a submenu and Arrow
  Left closes it, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- Toggles keep the menu open, so several can be changed in one go;
  actions close it and focus returns to the trigger.
- The icon and shortcut are hidden from assistive tech; the label names
  the item. Give `textValue` when a label is not plain text, or typeahead
  cannot find it.
- A disabled link has no `href`, so it cannot be followed.
- Items are 32px tall, 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`).
- `isModal` (the default) makes the rest of the page inert while the menu
  is open, so a screen reader stays in the menu.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { Menu as BaseMenu } from '@base-ui/react/menu'
import { Menubar as BaseMenubar } from '@base-ui/react/menubar'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { MenuEntries, MenuSurface, type MenuEntry } from './Menu'
import styles from './Menubar.module.css'

export interface MenubarMenu {
  /** The top-level item: File, Edit, View. */
  label: string
  /** The flyout's entries, the same data as Menu's `items`. */
  items: MenuEntry[]
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Open this menu on first render, uncontrolled. */
  defaultOpen?: boolean
}

export interface MenubarProps {
  menus: MenubarMenu[]
  /** Names the bar. Needed when a page has more than one menubar. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  /**
   * While a flyout is open, lock page scroll and make the rest of the page
   * inert. `false` leaves the page as is.
   */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where the flyouts render instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
}

/** A row of menus, as in a desktop app: File, Edit, View, each opening a flyout. */
export function Menubar({ menus, 'aria-label': ariaLabel, isModal = true, container, className }: MenubarProps) {
  return (
    <BaseMenubar aria-label={ariaLabel} modal={isModal} className={cn(styles.bar, className)}>
      {menus.map((menu, i) => (
        <BaseMenu.Root key={i} disabled={menu.disabled} defaultOpen={menu.defaultOpen}>
          <BaseMenu.Trigger className={styles.trigger}>{menu.label}</BaseMenu.Trigger>
          <MenuSurface side="bottom" align="start" container={container}>
            <MenuEntries items={menu.items} />
          </MenuSurface>
        </BaseMenu.Root>
      ))}
    </BaseMenubar>
  )
}

# Menubar A row of menus across the top of a tool, as in a desktop app: File, Edit, View, ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as MenubarStories from './Menubar.stories'

<Meta of={MenubarStories} />

# Menubar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A row of menus across the top of a tool, as in a desktop app: File, Edit,
View, each opening a flyout of commands. Use it in an editor-like screen
with more commands than a toolbar can show.

<Status of={MenubarStories} />

<Canvas of={MenubarStories.Default} />

## Variants

Menubar has one look. Each flyout is a
[Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) popup and takes the
same entries: actions with shortcuts, links, submenus, checkbox and radio
items, groups and separators.

| Menu | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Enabled (the default) | Commands that apply now. |
| Disabled (`disabled`) | A menu that does not apply in the current state. It stays in place, muted, so the bar does not shift. |

<Canvas of={MenubarStories.DisabledMenu} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Menubar } from 'zweihander/menubar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/menubar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Menubar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Menubar.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Menubar](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menubar)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={MenubarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={MenubarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The flyout on this tab is a picture: it is drawn open in place, not
positioned over the page. Its parts are Menu's; see
[Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) for the item's own
anatomy.

## Measurements

The bar is a strip: its triggers are rows of the sm control tier, one step
shorter than the md items in the flyout. Triggers sit inset from the bar
edge by the same amount as items inside a Menu popup, and their corner
nests inside the bar's the same way.

<SpecTable
  caption="Bar"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Bar', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Bar', property: 'Gap between triggers', token: '--space-0-5' },
    { part: 'Bar', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-field' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Focus ring width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

A flyout opens 4px below its trigger, lined up with the trigger's start
edge. When the bar is wider than its container, it scrolls sideways.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Bar"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Bar', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Bar', property: 'Text', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Bar', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Trigger, hover, highlighted or open', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Trigger, hover, highlighted or open', property: 'Text', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Trigger, disabled', property: 'Text', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Trigger, focus', property: 'Ring', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

The flyout's colours are Menu's.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Closed', content: <Story of={MenubarStories.Default} /> },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={MenubarStories.Open} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled menu', content: <Story of={MenubarStories.DisabledMenu} /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Hover and highlighted**: the trigger takes the same `--accent` fill as
  a highlighted item in the flyout.
- **Open**: the trigger keeps that fill while its flyout is open, so the
  reader sees which menu they are in.
- **Focus**: a keyboard focus ring inside the trigger, so it does not
  collide with its neighbours.
- **Disabled**: muted at 60% opacity, no fill on hover, skipped by the
  arrow keys.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={MenubarStories} />
</div>

`menus` is data, and each menu's `items` is Menu's `items`. Shortcuts are
plain trailing text, as in Menu: display only, binding the key is left to
the page.

### Differences from the spec

- **No navigation menu.** The source pairs a menubar with a navigation
  menu: links in flyouts, each with a description. Zweihänder leaves that
  out: app navigation is the Nav Sidebar and the Top Bar's links, which
  show the current page; a flyout of described links is a marketing-site
  pattern.
- **No item description.** Flyout items are Menu's entries, one line
  each. A second line of text is what a navigation menu needs, and it is
  not built.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Menubar in a screen that works like a desktop tool, an invoice or
report editor, a spreadsheet, where people look for commands by category
and learn their shortcuts. Name each menu for what it holds and keep the
order people know from desktop apps: File, Edit, View, then your own,
then Help.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={MenubarStories.DoConventionalOrder} />}
  doCaption="Commands, grouped by the familiar File, Edit, View, with their shortcuts."
  dont={<Story of={MenubarStories.DontNavigation} />}
  dontCaption="Pages behind flyouts. Navigation belongs in the Nav Sidebar or the Top Bar, where the current page shows."
/>

## When not to use

- **For the app's navigation.** Use a
  [Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs) or
  the [Top Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-top-bar--docs)'s
  links: they show where the reader is, a menubar does not.
- **For a few actions on one thing.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) from a button, or
  Buttons.
- **To find any command by name.** Add a
  [Command Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-command-palette--docs);
  it can sit alongside the menubar.

## Accessibility

- The bar is a `role="menubar"`, named by `aria-label`. Each trigger is a
  `menuitem` with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; a disabled
  menu's trigger has `aria-disabled`.
- The bar is one tab stop. Arrow Left and Right move along the triggers,
  skipping disabled menus.
- Arrow Down, Enter or Space on a trigger opens its flyout on the first
  item. Inside a flyout the keys are Menu's.
- With a flyout open, Arrow Right and Left move to the next and previous
  menu and open it, and moving the pointer onto another trigger opens that
  menu instead.
- Escape closes the flyout and returns focus to its trigger; choosing an
  action closes it too.
- Shortcuts and icons are hidden from assistive tech; the label names the
  item.
- Triggers are 24px tall; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) their hit
  area grows to 44px.
- `isModal` (the default) makes the rest of the page inert while a flyout
  is open, so a screen reader stays in the menu.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# MFA Challenge The second step of signing in: the reader enters a one-time code from thei...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as MFAChallengeStories from './MFAChallenge.stories'

<Meta of={MFAChallengeStories} />

# MFA Challenge

The second step of signing in: the reader enters a one-time code from
their authenticator app, or the one sent to their phone or email. **Try
another way** switches method, and a **backup code** gets them in when
none is at hand. After Carbon's login pattern and shadcn's Input OTP.
Built on the **Auth Layout** (see
[Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#auth-layout)), **OTP
Input** with its Resend code, and the kit's TextInput, Checkbox, Link,
Alert and Button.

Show it after the password, from **Sign In** or **Progressive Sign In**,
when the account has a second factor. Setting one up (the QR code, the
first backup codes) is a separate screen.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/mfa-challenge-template.json
```

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.Default} />

## What works

- **The code**: six cells by default (`codeLength`). Typing or pasting the
  last digit sends the form; **Verify** does too, and with cells empty it
  marks the field and says what is missing. `onVerify` gets the method's
  `id`, the code and **Remember this device**.
- **Where the code went**: the line under the title follows the method.
  An authenticator app: "Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator
  app." A text message or an email: "We sent a 6-digit code to •••• 4821",
  with the destination as you pass it (mask it yourself), and **Resend
  code** under the cells, counting down from `resendCooldown` seconds,
  calling `onResend` and saying the new code went out.
- **Try another way**, when the account has more than one method: the
  other methods ("Authenticator app", "Text message to •••• 4821", "Email
  to a•••@example.com") and **Back**. Picking one calls `onMethodSelect`,
  where you send its code, then shows its code step. A resend still on its
  way when the reader moves on is ignored.
- **Use a backup code**: a plain text field, since backup codes are longer
  and often have letters and a dash. `onVerify` gets it as method
  `'backup'`, trimmed. **Use a verification code instead** goes back.
- **Remember this device for 30 days**: the template stores nothing. When
  `rememberDevice` is true, set your trusted-device cookie for
  `rememberDeviceDays`, and skip this page next time.
- **When it fails**: every handler returns (or resolves to) a message. It
  shows above the form and is announced; a wrong code is cleared and the
  first cell focused. If a handler throws or rejects, the page says
  "Something went wrong. Try again."

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.TextMessage} />

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.TryAnotherWay} />

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.BackupCode} />

## Variants

**Card** (default) and **plain**, and **with a panel** through `aside`,
exactly as on Sign In: they are the Auth Layout's. With one method and
`hasBackupCode={false}`, there are no other ways in to offer.

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.OnlyOneWay} />

## Make it yours

Pass the account's methods in the order you want, the default (the one
the reader set up first, or used last) first. Rate-limit `onVerify`,
`onResend` and `onMethodSelect` on the server and return the message
("Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes."): the page shows it as it
is. After `onVerify` succeeds, navigate on.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `methods` | `{ id, kind: 'app' }` or `{ id, kind: 'sms' \| 'email', destination }`, in an array | | The account's second factors; the first shows first. |
| `onVerify` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ method, code, rememberDevice }`; `method` is an `id` or `'backup'`. A returned message shows above the form. |
| `onResend` | `(method) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Resend code, for `sms` and `email`. |
| `onMethodSelect` | `(method) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | A method picked under Try another way. A returned message keeps the list. |
| `codeLength` | `number` | `6` | Digits in a code. |
| `resendCooldown` | `number` | `30` | Seconds before Resend code is allowed. |
| `hasRememberDevice` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows Remember this device. |
| `rememberDeviceDays` | `number` | `30` | The days in its label. |
| `hasBackupCode` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows Use a backup code. |
| `signInHref` | `string` | `"#sign-in"` | Back to sign in, under the form. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under Back to sign in, outside the card. |

Every other Auth Layout prop passes through.

## Layout

The Auth Layout's, as on [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#layout).
On a phone the six cells fit the column, and Try another way and Use a
backup code wrap onto two lines when they must.

<Canvas of={MFAChallengeStories.Phone} />

## Accessibility

- The form is in a `main` landmark, and its one heading is the `h1`.
- The cells are a group named "Verification code"; the first cell has
  `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so the phone offers a code from a text
  message.
- An incomplete code marks the cells `aria-invalid="true"`, describes the
  group with the message and focuses the first cell; an empty backup code
  does the same on its field.
- Each step replaces the last, so focus moves on: to the first cell, to
  the backup code field, or to the new `h1` on the list of methods.
- A message from a handler is an `alert`, the "new code sent" note a
  `status`, and Verify is `aria-busy` while it waits.

  /**
   * A decision that must be made: `role="alertdialog"`, and a click on the
   * backdrop does not close it. Pair it with explicit buttons in `footer`.
   */
  isAlert?: boolean
  /** Close on a click on the backdrop. Ignored when `isAlert`. */
  closeOnBackdropClick?: boolean
  /**
   * While open, trap focus, lock page scroll and make the rest of the page
   * inert. `false` drops those three; the backdrop still covers the page.
   * Ignored when `isAlert`: an alert
   * is always modal.
   */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where the modal renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Where focus goes on open. By default, the first focusable element. */
  initialFocus?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
  className?: string
}

const widths = { sm: styles.sm, md: styles.md, lg: styles.lg }

export function Modal({
  trigger,
  title,
  description,
  children,
  footer,
  size = 'md',
  hasCloseButton,
  closeLabel = 'Close',
  isAlert = false,
  closeOnBackdropClick = true,
  isModal = true,
  container,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  initialFocus,
  className,
}: ModalProps) {
  const showClose = hasCloseButton ?? !isAlert
  const content = (
    <>
      {trigger && (isAlert ? <AlertDialog.Trigger render={trigger} /> : <Dialog.Trigger render={trigger} />)}
      <Dialog.Portal container={container}>
        <Dialog.Backdrop className={styles.backdrop} />
        <Dialog.Viewport className={styles.viewport}>
          <Dialog.Popup initialFocus={initialFocus} className={cn(styles.popup, widths[size], className)}>
            <div className={styles.header}>
              <Dialog.Title className={styles.title}>{title}</Dialog.Title>
              {showClose && (
                <Dialog.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close}>
                  <Icon name="close" />
                </Dialog.Close>
              )}
            </div>
            {description && <Dialog.Description className={styles.description}>{description}</Dialog.Description>}
            {children && <div className={styles.body}>{children}</div>}
            {footer && <div className={styles.footer}>{footer}</div>}
          </Dialog.Popup>
        </Dialog.Viewport>
      </Dialog.Portal>
    </>
  )
  const change = onOpenChange && ((next: boolean) => onOpenChange(next))
  return isAlert ? (
    <AlertDialog.Root open={open} defaultOpen={defaultOpen} onOpenChange={change}>
      {content}
    </AlertDialog.Root>
  ) : (
    <Dialog.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={change}
      disablePointerDismissal={!closeOnBackdropClick}
      modal={isModal}
    >
      {content}
    </Dialog.Root>
  )
}

/** A button inside the modal that closes it, e.g. "Cancel": `<ModalClose render={<Button />}>Cancel</ModalClose>`. */
export const ModalClose = Dialog.Close
