# Modal A dialog over the page that has to be dealt with before going back: a short form, ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as ModalStories from './Modal.stories'

<Meta of={ModalStories} />

# Modal

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A dialog over the page that has to be dealt with before going back: a
short form, a confirmation, a decision. Everything behind it is dimmed and
out of reach until it closes.

<Status of={ModalStories} />

<Canvas of={ModalStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Dialog (default) | A short task on its own: edit a profile, invite people. A close button, Escape and a press on the backdrop all close it. |
| Alert (`isAlert`) | A decision with consequences: delete, discard, leave. No close button and a press on the backdrop does nothing, so it ends only through its own buttons or Escape. |

<Canvas of={ModalStories.Alert} />

`size` sets the maximum width: `sm` (24rem) for an alert, `md` (32rem) for
a short form, `lg` (48rem) for long content. Taller than the screen, the
body scrolls and the title and footer stay in view.

<Canvas of={ModalStories.Long} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Modal, ModalClose } from 'zweihander/modal'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/modal.json
```

- Source: [src/components/overlays/Modal.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Modal.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog) and [Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ModalStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ModalStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open modals on this tab and the next are pictures: real modals
rendered in a frame with `container`, not modal (`isModal={false}`) and
inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Container"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },

    { part: 'Title', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-heading-sm' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-heading-sm' },
    { part: 'Title to close button', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-group' },

    { part: 'Body, footer', property: 'Gap above', token: '--space-group' },

/>

<SpecTable

  rows={[
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Padding', token: '--control-xs-gap' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },

    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },

Width is `size`: at most 24rem (`sm`), 32rem (`md`) or 48rem (`lg`), and
never wider than the screen less its margin. The border is 1px. Backdrop
and modal sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade in over
`--duration-base`.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Every modal"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Backdrop', property: 'Background', token: '--scrim' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Title, body', property: 'Colour', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Description', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

Buttons in the footer keep their own colours: see Button.

## States

The modal is open or closed. Opening fades the backdrop in and scales the
container up from 97%; closing reverses it. The close button is the only
part with states of its own:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ModalStories.CloseButton} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills the button with `--accent`.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the button, so it is not
  clipped at the container's corner.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ModalStories} />
</div>

`ModalClose` closes the modal it is in. Give it your own button with
`render`: `<ModalClose render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Cancel</ModalClose>`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Reach for a modal last: it stops everything else. Use one when the task
must be finished or abandoned before going on, or for a decision with
consequences. For a decision, use `isAlert`, say exactly what will happen in
the description, and name the buttons after what they do. Before a delete
or anything else that cannot be undone, use a
[Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs): it
is this alert with the warning, the focus on Cancel and type to confirm
built in.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ModalStories.DoNameTheActions} />}
  doCaption="Name the buttons after what they do: Delete, Keep project. The choice reads without the question."
  dont={<Story of={ModalStories.DontOkCancel} />}
  dontCaption="OK and Cancel make the reader go back to the question to know which one deletes."
/>

Put the main action last in the footer, and dismiss actions (Cancel, Keep)
in the `secondary` variant.

## When not to use

- **For a small form tied to one button**, such as Share or a filter. Use a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs): it opens beside
  the button and leaves the page usable.
- **For information**: a success, a warning, a tip. Use an
  [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs) or a
  [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs); neither stops
  the reader.
- **For a long or many-step task.** Give it a page of its own.
- **Over another modal.** Close the first, or move the second step into it.

## Accessibility

- `role="dialog"` (or `alertdialog`), named by the title and described by
  the description.
- Opening moves focus to the first focusable element, or `initialFocus`,
  and traps it inside. The page behind is `aria-hidden`, its pointer
  events are blocked by the backdrop, and its scroll is locked. Closing
  returns focus to the trigger.
- `isModal={false}` drops the focus trap, the scroll lock and the hidden
  page, but the backdrop still covers the page. It is for pictures of a
  modal, such as the ones on these tabs: a real modal stays modal.
- Escape closes it, as does a press outside unless `isAlert` or
  `closeOnBackdropClick={false}`. An alert dialog closes only through its
  own buttons (and Escape).

  <Canvas of={ModalStories.Dismissing} />

- **One layer with the popups.** Modal, Popover, Select and Combobox all
  sit at `--layer-overlay`. Each portals to the end of `<body>` when it
  opens, so the most recent is on top: a Select opened inside a modal
  lists its options above the modal, which a higher modal layer would
  hide.

  <Canvas of={ModalStories.WithSelect} />

- The close button is named `Close` (`closeLabel`), has the 2px focus ring
  and a 44px hit area on touch screens.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

const TOKENS = [
  { name: '--duration-fast', use: 'Popups appearing: menu, tooltip, popover, date picker, listbox' },
  { name: '--duration-base', use: 'State changes: hover and press colours, switch, accordion, modal' },
  { name: '--duration-slow', use: 'Things that travel: the tab indicator, a toast sliding in, a drawer' },
  { name: '--duration-spin', use: 'One turn of every spinner' },
  { name: '--duration-spin-reduced', use: 'One turn under prefers-reduced-motion' },

export const Durations: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const value = (name: string) => canvasElement.querySelector(`[data-token="${name}"]`)!.textContent
    // Under reduced motion the three transition steps resolve to 0ms, which
    // is the point of the token; the test runner does not emulate it.
    await expect(value('--duration-fast')).toBe('100ms')
    await expect(value('--duration-base')).toBe('150ms')
    await expect(value('--duration-slow')).toBe('200ms')
    await expect(value('--duration-spin')).toBe('800ms')
    await expect(value('--duration-spin-reduced')).toBe('2.5s')
  },
}

# Motion Three transition durations and one spinner speed. Every `transition` in the kit r...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as MotionStories from './Motion.stories'

<Meta of={MotionStories} />

# Motion

Three transition durations and one spinner speed. Every `transition` in the
kit reads one of them; nothing types a number of milliseconds.

<Canvas of={MotionStories.Durations} />

## Choosing a step

The step follows what moves, not how important it is. A popup appearing
is `fast`: it answers a click, and anything slower reads as lag. A colour
or state change is `base`. Something that travels across the screen (the
tab indicator, a toast, a drawer) is `slow`, because the eye has to follow
it. If a new transition does not fit one of the three, that is a reason to
question the transition before adding a fourth step.

Easing is the browser default (`ease`) except where something grows or
shrinks: Accordion and Collapse open with `ease-out`, so the panel arrives
fast and settles. There is no easing token: two curves, each with an
obvious owner, do not need a name yet.

## Reduced motion

Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the three transition steps resolve to
`0ms` in `tokens.css`, so every transition in the kit stops in one place
without each component repeating a media query.

Two things are exempt. Toast swaps its slide for a 200ms fade, written as
a number on purpose, since the tokens would turn the fade into a jump.
And spinners: a stopped spinner says nothing is happening, so instead of
stopping they slow from `--duration-spin` to `--duration-spin-reduced`.
Each spinner opts into that itself.

Loop animations with their own rhythm (the skeleton pulse, the
indeterminate progress bar) keep their own timing: they are a single
animation each, not a step anyone else should reuse.

import { Tooltip } from '../../overlays/Tooltip'

export interface NavSidebarItem {
  type?: 'item'
  label: string
  href?: string
  /** Needed to show in the rail: an item without one is left out of it. */
  icon?: ReactNode
  /** A count or short tag after the label, e.g. unread items. */
  badge?: ReactNode
  /** Replaces the `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link to="…" />`. */

  label: string
  items: NavSidebarItem[]
  /** At the end of the label row, e.g. an icon Button that adds an item. Shows on hover and focus. */
  action?: ReactNode
  /** The label becomes a button that shows and hides the items. */
  isCollapsible?: boolean
  isCollapsed?: boolean
  defaultCollapsed?: boolean
  onCollapsedChange?: (collapsed: boolean) => void
  /** Show this many items and a "Show more" button for the rest. */
  limit?: number
}
export type NavSidebarEntry = NavSidebarItem | NavSidebarGroup

export interface NavSidebarProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  items: NavSidebarEntry[]
  /** The href of the page the reader is on: that item gets aria-current="page". */
  currentHref?: string
  /**
   * The logo, in the top row with the collapse button. Inside an AppShell's
   * sidebar layout the shell passes its own `brand` here.
   */
  brand?: ReactNode
  /** Under the logo, e.g. a tenant switcher and search, built from NavSidebarButton. Stays in the rail. */
  header?: ReactNode
  /** Pinned to the bottom, e.g. the account, notifications and help. Stays in the rail, stacked. */
  footer?: ReactNode
  /** An icon rail: labels move into tooltips; items without an icon are left out. */
  isCollapsed?: boolean
  defaultCollapsed?: boolean
  onCollapsedChange?: (collapsed: boolean) => void
  /** Show a button that collapses and expands the sidebar. */
  isCollapsible?: boolean
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/** Whether the sidebar is the rail, for the parts in its header and footer. */
const RailContext = createContext(false)

/** `null`, `false` and `undefined` render nothing. */
const given = (node: ReactNode) => node != null && node !== false

function ItemLink({ item, current, collapsed }: { item: NavSidebarItem; current: boolean; collapsed: boolean }) {
  // Collapsed hides the badge too, so a count or short tag joins the name.
  const name =
    typeof item.badge === 'string' || typeof item.badge === 'number' ? `${item.label}, ${item.badge}` : item.label
  const link = useRender({
    render: item.render,
    defaultTagName: 'a',
    props: {
      href: item.href,
      className: cn(styles.item, current && styles.current),
      'aria-current': current ? ('page' as const) : undefined,
      // Collapsed, the label is gone from view but must still name the link;
      // with a badge, the name puts a comma between them ("Inbox, 12").
      'aria-label': collapsed || name !== item.label ? name : undefined,
      children: (
        <>
          {item.icon && (
            <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
              {item.icon}
            </span>
          )}
          <span className={styles.label}>{item.label}</span>
          {item.badge !== undefined && <span className={styles.badge}>{item.badge}</span>}
        </>
      ),
    },
  })
  return collapsed ? (
    <Tooltip content={name} side="right">
      {link}
    </Tooltip>
  ) : (
    link
  )
}

export interface NavSidebarButtonProps extends ComponentProps<'button'> {
  icon: ReactNode
  /** The visible text, and the button's name in the rail. */
  label: string
  /** A second, quieter line, e.g. the account's role. */
  description?: ReactNode
  /** A count after the label, e.g. unread notifications. Joins the name in the rail. */
  badge?: ReactNode
  /** A chevron or a shortcut hint: right after the label for `switcher`, at the far end otherwise. */
  end?: ReactNode
  /**
   * `ghost`: a row like an item (notifications, help, the account).
   * `switcher`: the label in medium weight with its chevron right after it,
   * for a tenant or workspace switcher. `field`: drawn as an input, for a
   * search button that opens a command palette.
   */
  appearance?: 'ghost' | 'switcher' | 'field'
}

/**
 * A row for the header and footer: a tenant switcher, a search button, the
 * account. A button, so it can be a Menu's or Popover's trigger; in the rail
 * it is its icon, named by its label.
 */
export function NavSidebarButton({
  icon,
  label,
  description,
  badge,
  end,
  appearance = 'ghost',
  className,
  ...props
}: NavSidebarButtonProps) {
  const collapsed = useContext(RailContext)
  // Collapsed hides the badge, so a count joins the name, as on an item.
  const name = typeof badge === 'string' || typeof badge === 'number' ? `${label}, ${badge}` : label
  const button = (
    <button
      type="button"
      className={cn(styles.item, styles.button, styles[appearance], className)}
      aria-label={collapsed || name !== label ? name : undefined}
      {...props}
    >
      <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
        {icon}
      </span>
      <span className={styles.text}>
        <span className={styles.label}>{label}</span>
        {description && <span className={styles.description}>{description}</span>}
      </span>
      {badge !== undefined && <span className={styles.badge}>{badge}</span>}
      {/* A chevron or a shortcut hint: shown, not part of the name ("Search", not "Search⌘K"). */}
      {end && (
        <span className={styles.end} aria-hidden="true">
          {end}
        </span>
      )}
    </button>
  )
  return collapsed ? (
    <Tooltip content={name} side="right">
      {button}
    </Tooltip>
  ) : (
    button
  )
}

/** Runs of ungrouped items become one list; groups stay as they are. */
function sections(items: NavSidebarEntry[]) {
  const out: (NavSidebarItem[] | NavSidebarGroup)[] = []
  for (const entry of items) {
    if (entry.type === 'group') out.push(entry)
    else if (Array.isArray(out.at(-1))) (out.at(-1) as NavSidebarItem[]).push(entry)
    else out.push([entry])
  }
  return out
}

function Group({
  group,
  id,
  collapsed,
  list,
  currentHref,
}: {
  group: NavSidebarGroup
  id: string
  collapsed: boolean
  list: (entries: NavSidebarItem[], labelledBy?: string) => ReactNode
  currentHref?: string
}) {
  const [closedState, setClosedState] = useState(group.defaultCollapsed ?? false)
  const closed = group.isCollapsed ?? closedState
  const toggle = () => {
    setClosedState(!closed)
    group.onCollapsedChange?.(!closed)
  }
  // Open from the start when the current page is past the limit, so it is never hidden.
  const [showAll, setShowAll] = useState(
    () => group.limit !== undefined && group.items.findIndex((it) => it.href === currentHref) >= group.limit,
  )
  // The rail has no label to reopen a category or a "Show more" to press, so it shows every item it can.
  const items = collapsed
    ? group.items
    : group.limit !== undefined && !showAll
      ? group.items.slice(0, group.limit)
      : group.items
  const hasMore = !collapsed && group.limit !== undefined && group.items.length > group.limit
  const hidden = closed && !collapsed

  return (
    // The label names the list ("Pinned, list, 3 items") rather than being a
    // heading, so it cannot break the page's outline.
    <div className={styles.group}>
      <div className={styles.groupHead}>
        {group.isCollapsible ? (
          <button
            type="button"
            id={`${id}-label`}
            className={cn(styles.groupLabel, styles.groupToggle)}
            aria-expanded={!closed}
            aria-controls={`${id}-list`}
            onClick={toggle}
          >
            {group.label}
            <Icon name={closed ? 'chevron-right' : 'chevron-down'} className={styles.groupChevron} />
          </button>
        ) : (
          <div id={`${id}-label`} className={styles.groupLabel}>
            {group.label}
          </div>
        )}
        {given(group.action) && <div className={styles.groupAction}>{group.action}</div>}
      </div>
      <div id={`${id}-list`} hidden={hidden}>
        {list(items, `${id}-label`)}
        {hasMore && (
          <button type="button" className={cn(styles.item, styles.button, styles.more)} onClick={() => setShowAll(!showAll)}>
            <span className={styles.label}>{showAll ? 'Show less' : 'Show more'}</span>
          </button>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

export function NavSidebar({
  items,
  currentHref,
  brand: brandProp,
  header,
  footer,
  isCollapsed,
  defaultCollapsed = false,
  onCollapsedChange,
  isCollapsible = false,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Main',
  className,
  ...props
}: NavSidebarProps) {
  const [collapsedState, setCollapsedState] = useState(defaultCollapsed)
  const shell = useContext(ShellContext)
  // In an App Shell under 64rem it is always the rail: expanded, it would
  // cover most of a phone. The hover preview still floats over the page, but
  // there is no expanding or docking it there.
  const isRail = shell.isNarrow || (isCollapsed ?? collapsedState)
  const canToggle = isCollapsible && !shell.isNarrow
  const setRail = (next: boolean) => {
    setCollapsedState(next)
    onCollapsedChange?.(next)
  }
  const brand = given(brandProp) ? brandProp : shell.sidebarBrand
  const id = useId()
  const slotRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const peek = usePeek(isRail, slotRef)
  // While the pointer rests on the rail, the full sidebar floats over the
  // page (as in the Claude apps); its button docks it.
  const collapsed = isRail && !peek.isOpen
  const list = (entries: NavSidebarItem[], labelledBy?: string) => (
    <ul className={styles.list} aria-labelledby={labelledBy}>
      {entries.map((item) => (
        <li key={item.href ?? item.label}>
          <ItemLink item={item} current={item.href !== undefined && item.href === currentHref} collapsed={collapsed} />
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
  // The rail shows icons only, so an item without one has nothing to show there.
  const shown = collapsed
    ? sections(items)
        .map((s) => (Array.isArray(s) ? s.filter((it) => it.icon) : { ...s, items: s.items.filter((it) => it.icon) }))
        .filter((s) => (Array.isArray(s) ? s : s.items).length > 0)
    : sections(items)

  return (
    <RailContext.Provider value={collapsed}>
      {/* The slot keeps the rail's width in the layout while the preview
          floats; expanded it is display: contents and lays out nothing. */}
      <div
        ref={slotRef}
        className={cn(styles.slot, isRail && styles.railSlot)}
        onPointerEnter={peek.onPointerEnter}
        onPointerLeave={peek.onPointerLeave}
      >
        <nav
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          className={cn(styles.sidebar, collapsed && styles.collapsed, peek.isOpen && styles.peek, className)}
          {...props}
        >
          {(given(brand) || canToggle) && (
            <div className={cn(styles.brandRow, given(brand) && styles.withBrand)}>
              {given(brand) && <div className={styles.brand}>{brand}</div>}
              {canToggle && (
                <button
                  type="button"
                  className={styles.toggle}
                  aria-expanded={!isRail}
                  aria-label={peek.isOpen ? 'Keep sidebar open' : isRail ? 'Expand sidebar' : 'Collapse sidebar'}
                  onClick={() => {
                    peek.close()
                    setRail(!isRail)
                  }}
                >
                  <Icon name={isRail ? 'sidebar-expand' : 'sidebar-collapse'} />
                </button>
              )}
            </div>
          )}
          {given(header) && <div className={styles.header}>{header}</div>}
          <div className={styles.body}>
            {shown.map((section, i) =>
              Array.isArray(section) ? (
                <div key={i}>{list(section)}</div>
              ) : (
                <Group
                  key={section.label}
                  group={section}
                  id={`${id}-group-${i}`}
                  collapsed={collapsed}
                  list={list}
                  currentHref={currentHref}
                />
              ),
            )}
          </div>
          {given(footer) && <div className={styles.footer}>{footer}</div>}
        </nav>
      </div>
    </RailContext.Provider>
  )
}

/** Hover delay before the rail previews the full sidebar, so passing the pointer across does not flash it. */
const PEEK_DELAY = 120

/**
 * The rail's hover preview. Mouse only: touch has no hover, and keyboard
 * focus reaches the same links in the rail (the expand button docks it). It
 * stays open while one of its menus is, and closes once the pointer is
 * elsewhere and no menu is open.
 */
/** Whether a menu or popover opened from inside the element is still open. */
const hasOpenMenu = (el: HTMLElement | null) => el?.querySelector('[aria-haspopup][aria-expanded="true"]') != null

function usePeek(isRail: boolean, ref: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>) {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false)
  const timer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(undefined)
  const close = () => {
    clearTimeout(timer.current)
    setIsOpen(false)
  }
  useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(timer.current), [])
  // A menu opened from the preview keeps it; once that menu closes, the next
  // pointer move outside closes the preview.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isOpen) return
    const onMove = (e: PointerEvent) => {
      if (!ref.current?.contains(e.target as Node) && !hasOpenMenu(ref.current)) setIsOpen(false)
    }
    document.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove)
    return () => document.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove)
  }, [isOpen, ref])
  return {
    // Only the rail previews; a stale open state from before docking is ignored.
    isOpen: isRail && isOpen,
    close,
    onPointerEnter: (e: ReactPointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
      if (!isRail || e.pointerType !== 'mouse') return
      clearTimeout(timer.current)
      timer.current = setTimeout(() => setIsOpen(true), PEEK_DELAY)
    },
    onPointerLeave: () => {
      clearTimeout(timer.current)
      if (!hasOpenMenu(ref.current)) setIsOpen(false)
    },
  }
}

# Nav Sidebar The app's main navigation, down the side of the screen, laid out as in the C...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as NavSidebarStories from './NavSidebar.stories'

<Meta of={NavSidebarStories} />

# Nav Sidebar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

The app's main navigation, down the side of the screen, laid out as in the
Claude apps: the logo and the collapse button on top, a header for the
tenant switcher and search, links in categories, and a footer for the
account, notifications and help. It can collapse to an icon rail. A pattern,
one of the three pieces the [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs)
template places (with the Top Bar and App Content); it was the
Navigation/Sidebar component.

<Status of={NavSidebarStories} />

<Canvas of={NavSidebarStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Expanded | The default: icon, label and badge on every row. |
| Collapsible (`isCollapsible`) | Apps where the content needs the width at times: a button in the top row folds the sidebar to the rail. |
| Rail (`isCollapsed` or `defaultCollapsed`) | Icons only, labels in tooltips. For tools the reader knows well. The header and footer stay, as icons; items without an icon are left out. |
| Plain | No logo, header or footer: a section's own navigation inside a larger layout. |

<Canvas of={NavSidebarStories.Collapsible} />

### Rail preview

Collapsed, resting the mouse on the rail for a moment floats the full
sidebar over the page, as in the Claude apps; the rail keeps its place in
the layout, so the page does not move. The preview's top button, "Keep
sidebar open", docks it. It stays while a menu opened from it is open.
Touch and keyboard do not open it: keyboard focus reaches the same links in
the rail, and the expand button docks the sidebar.

<Canvas of={NavSidebarStories.RailPreview} />

### Categories

A group is a category. `isCollapsible` makes its label a button that opens
and closes it; `limit` shows its first items with a small "Show more" for
the rest, and the current page is never hidden behind the limit. `action`
is opt-in: a button at the end of the label row (an icon Button that adds an
item, say), shown on hover and focus. Leave it off where nothing is added
from the sidebar.

<Canvas of={NavSidebarStories.Categories} />

### Header and footer rows

`NavSidebarButton` is a row that looks like an item: an icon, a label, an
optional `badge`, `description` line and `end` (a chevron, a shortcut). It
is a button, so it can be a Menu's or Popover's trigger. Its appearances:

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `ghost` | A row like an item: notifications (with its count as `badge`), help, the account. |
| `switcher` | A tenant or workspace switcher: the name in medium weight, its chevron right after it, the avatar a rounded square. |
| `field` | A search button drawn as an input, its shortcut hint at the far end, that opens a command palette. |

An Avatar in the leading slot is 20px in every density, and every leading
visual (logo mark, avatar, icon) is centred on the nav icons' line. In the
rail a row shows its icon only and takes its label (and badge) as its name
and tooltip.

### Backgrounds

Gray is the sidebar's own `--surface-filled`, and what a transparent
sidebar shows on the neutral canvas. In an App Shell it can also be white
(`sidebarSurface="solid"`, the current item in the brand tint) or
transparent on a deep canvas of your own; see Sidebar surfaces on the
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) page.

<Canvas of={NavSidebarStories.Plain} />

## Resources

Copied into your project through the registry, like every pattern (not in
the npm package):

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/nav-sidebar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/patterns/application-ui/NavSidebar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/patterns/application-ui/NavSidebar.tsx)
- Spec: our own; uiguideline.com has no page for it
- Behaviour: a plain `<nav>`; the rail's labels use [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={NavSidebarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={NavSidebarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

In the rail the logo keeps its place, cut to the rail's width, and the
expand button shows over it on hover or focus. The header and footer stay
as icons; labels, badges, category heads and "Show more" are hidden, and
each category starts with a rule instead of its label.

## Measurements

Items are rows of the md control tier, 2px apart in every density, so
hover and current fills never touch.

  rows={[

    { part: 'Header', property: 'Gap between rows', token: '--space-inline' },

Expanded, the sidebar is 16rem wide. The rail is one square row plus the
padding either side: `--control-md` plus twice `--space-2`. A long label is
cut with an ellipsis. Give the sidebar the height to fill; its body
scrolls when the items do not fit.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Sidebar"
  rows={[
    { part: 'NavSidebar', property: 'Background', token: '--surface-filled' },
    { part: 'NavSidebar', property: 'Edge', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Category label', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Search field', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Search field', property: 'Edge', token: '--input' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Item"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--subtle-foreground' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Item, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--hover-overlay' },
    { part: 'Item, hover', property: 'Label and icon', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Item, current', property: 'Background', token: '--selected' },
    { part: 'Item, current', property: 'Label and icon', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Badge', property: 'Background', token: '--destructive' },
    { part: 'Badge', property: 'Colour', token: '--destructive-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

Hover is an overlay, not a solid: in dark mode the sidebar's own surface
is the same grey as `--accent`, so an opaque hover fill would vanish. A
badge is a count that needs attention, so it is red and sits right after
its label. An App Shell overrides the current fill, the hover, the search
field and the badge for its white and transparent surfaces.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Current', content: <Story of={NavSidebarStories.CurrentItem} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={NavSidebarStories.Item} />
</States>

- **Current** is a `--selected` fill, a step past the hover fill so the
  two never read alike, plus medium weight for anyone who cannot tell the
  fills apart. It stays off the accent: where you are is not a call to
  action.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the row, so rows that
  sit flush do not cover each other's ring.
- **Collapsed** is the rail; see Variants.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={NavSidebarStories} />
</div>

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a NavSidebar for an app's main navigation when it has more than five or
so destinations, or will grow: the list runs down and does not wrap. Name
groups by what is in them, keep labels to a word or two, and give every
item an icon if the sidebar can collapse.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={NavSidebarStories.DoGroupWithIcons} />}
  doCaption="Short labels, an icon on each, grouped under a few names."
  dont={<Story of={NavSidebarStories.DontLongLabelsNoIcons} />}
  dontCaption="Long labels get cut, and with no icons there is nothing to show in the rail."
/>

## When not to use

- **For three to five sections of one page or object.** Use
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs) across the top.
- **For actions.** A sidebar goes places. Put actions in
  [Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) or a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs).
- **On a phone, as is.** 16rem is most of a phone's width. In an
  [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) under
  64rem it is always the icon rail, with no collapse button; elsewhere,
  pass `isCollapsed`.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Main"; rename it with `aria-label` when the
  page has another navigation. The current item has
  `aria-current="page"`.
- Each group's label names its list through `aria-labelledby` ("Projects,
  list, 3 items"), and keeps doing so in the rail, where it is only
  visually hidden. Labels are not headings, so they do not compete with
  the page's outline.
- In the rail each link keeps its name through `aria-label`, badge
  included ("Inbox, 12"), and a tooltip shows the same text on hover and
  on keyboard focus.
- The collapse button is named "Collapse sidebar" / "Expand sidebar" and
  carries `aria-expanded`; in the rail preview it is "Keep sidebar open".
- A badge joins its row's name after a comma ("Inbox, 12",
  "Notifications, 3"), expanded and in the rail alike.
- The rail preview opens on mouse hover only. Keyboard focus never covers
  the rail with it: the rail's links are reachable as they are, and the
  expand button docks the sidebar.
- A collapsible category's label is a button with `aria-expanded` and
  `aria-controls` pointing at its list; Enter and Space open and close it.
  A category's `action` needs its own name ("Add to Pinned").
- A `NavSidebarButton` is named by its text; in the rail, by its `label`
  through `aria-label`, with the same text as a tooltip.
- Rows are 32px tall, 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`).

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Badge } from '../../atomic-elements/Badge'
import { Button } from '../../buttons/Button'
import { Tabs } from '../../navigation/Tabs'
import { Popover } from '../../overlays/Popover'
import { Feed, type FeedItem } from './Feed'
import styles from './NotificationCenter.module.css'

export interface NotificationPanelProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children' | 'title'> {
  /** The notifications, newest first: Feed items, usually with `href` and `isUnread`. */
  items: FeedItem[]
  /** Shows "Mark all as read" in the header; disabled while nothing is unread. */
  onMarkAllRead?: () => void
  /** More header actions after "Mark all as read", such as a link to notification settings. */
  actions?: ReactNode
  /** All and Unread tabs above the list. */
  hasTabs?: boolean
  /** Shown instead of the list when there are no notifications. */
  empty?: ReactNode
  /** Shown on the Unread tab when everything is read. */
  emptyUnread?: ReactNode
  /** How the time reads, passed to the Feed. */
  formatTime?: (at: Date) => string
  /** The heading's text. */
  title?: ReactNode
  /** The heading's level, so it fits the outline it lands in. */
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4
}

/**
 * The inside of the notification center: a heading with "Mark all as read"
 * and your actions, optional All and Unread tabs, and the notifications as a
 * Feed without the connecting line. It owns no data: marking read is yours.
 */
export function NotificationPanel({
  items,
  onMarkAllRead,
  actions,
  hasTabs = false,
  empty = 'No notifications yet.',
  emptyUnread = 'You are all caught up.',
  formatTime,
  title = 'Notifications',
  headingLevel = 2,
  className,
  ...props
}: NotificationPanelProps) {
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  const unread = items.filter((item) => item.isUnread)
  const feed = (list: FeedItem[], none: ReactNode) => (
    <Feed items={list} hasConnector={false} empty={none} formatTime={formatTime} />
  )

  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.panel, className)} {...props}>
      <div className={styles.header}>
        <Heading className={styles.title}>{title}</Heading>
        {(onMarkAllRead || actions) && (
          <div className={styles.actions}>
            {onMarkAllRead && (
              <Button size="sm" variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" disabled={unread.length === 0} onClick={onMarkAllRead}>
                Mark all as read
              </Button>
            )}
            {actions}
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
      {hasTabs ? (
        <Tabs
          size="sm"
          aria-label="Show"
          items={[
            { value: 'all', label: 'All', content: feed(items, empty) },
            {
              value: 'unread',
              label: (
                <>
                  Unread
                  {unread.length > 0 && <Badge size="sm" variant="secondary" count={unread.length} maxCount={99} />}
                </>
              ),
              content: feed(unread, emptyUnread),
            },
          ]}
        />
      ) : (
        feed(items, empty)
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

export interface NotificationCenterProps extends NotificationPanelProps {
  /** The bell's name; the unread count is added to it ("Notifications, 3 unread"). */
  label?: string
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Where the panel renders instead of `<body>`. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
}

/**
 * A bell for the Top Bar, with the unread count on it, that opens the
 * NotificationPanel in a Popover. The list scrolls under a pinned header.
 */
export function NotificationCenter({
  label = 'Notifications',
  side = 'bottom',
  align = 'end',
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  container,
  ...panel
}: NotificationCenterProps) {
  const count = panel.items.filter((item) => item.isUnread).length
  return (
    <Popover
      aria-label={label}
      side={side}
      align={align}
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      container={container}
      className={styles.popup}
      trigger={
        <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" isIconOnly aria-label={count ? `${label}, ${count} unread` : label}>
          {/* The count is in the button's name; the floating badge is hidden and only shows it. */}
          <Badge isFloating count={count || undefined} maxCount={99} size="sm">
            <Icon name="notifications" />
          </Badge>
        </Button>
      }
    >
      <NotificationPanel {...panel} />
    </Popover>
  )
}

# Notification Center What needs your attention across the app: a bell in the [Top Bar](?p...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as NotificationCenterStories from './NotificationCenter.stories'

<Meta of={NotificationCenterStories} />

# Notification Center

What needs your attention across the app: a bell in the [Top
Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-top-bar--docs) with the unread
count on it, and a panel under it listing the notifications, newest
first, unread ones marked with a dot. After Catalyst Blocks,
Notifications.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/notification-center.json
```

## In the Top Bar

`NotificationCenter` is the bell and the panel. The bell is a ghost icon
Button with a floating [Badge](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-badge--docs)
for the unread count, and opens the panel in a
[Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). The rows are a
[Feed](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-feed--docs) without the
connecting line: each is a sentence, `href` makes the whole row a link,
and `isUnread` puts a dot at its end and counts it.

<Canvas of={NotificationCenterStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={NotificationCenterStories.Open} />

## With tabs

`hasTabs` adds All and Unread tabs; Unread carries the count, and shows
`emptyUnread` once everything is read. `NotificationPanel` is the inside
on its own, for a [Drawer](?path=/docs/components-overlays-drawer--docs)
or a column of a page.

<Canvas of={NotificationCenterStories.WithTabs} />

## Empty

No items shows `empty` in place of the list; the bell has no count and
Mark all as read is disabled.

<Canvas of={NotificationCenterStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={NotificationCenterStories} />

`NotificationPanel` takes the same props except `label`, `side`, `align`,
`open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` and `container`, which belong to
the bell and its Popover. The pattern owns no data: `onMarkAllRead` is
where you set every `isUnread` to false, and an item's `onClick` runs
when its link is followed, to mark that one read.

A notification that arrives while the panel is closed only changes the
count. When it needs attention now, also raise a
[Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): the count is
not announced, and the bell is easy to miss.

## Layout

- The panel is as wide as a Popover goes (22rem), and narrower when the
  window is.
- It is no taller than the room under the bell. The list scrolls; the
  header stays pinned at the top.
- The header wraps: the actions drop under the heading when they do
  not fit beside it.
- The unread dot has a column of its own at the end of the row, so the
  sentence never runs under it. Long names and file names break anywhere
  rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={NotificationCenterStories.LongContent} />

## Differences from the spec

- **Settings** is not a built-in button: `actions` takes what the app
  has, such as a More menu with View all and Notification settings.
- **Tabs** are optional; a short list reads fine without them.
- **Time** is the Feed's: pass a relative `formatTime` ("5 minutes ago")
  as the stories do.

## Accessibility

- The bell's name carries the count ("Notifications, 3 unread"); the
  floating badge is hidden, so the count is said once.
- The panel is a dialog named "Notifications". Opening it moves focus
  inside; Escape closes it and returns focus to the bell.
- A heading (level 2 by default, `headingLevel` to change it) names the
  panel for heading navigation.
- The notifications are a list. A row with `href` is one link: the
  sentence is its text, and the whole row is its target.
- An unread row ends with a dot named "Unread", so the state is heard
  as well as seen.
- Mark all as read is disabled when nothing is unread.

} from './InputField'
import styles from './NumberInput.module.css'

export interface NumberInputProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLInputElement>
  value?: number | null
  defaultValue?: number
  /** The spec's `onChange`. `null` when the field is emptied. */
  onValueChange?: (value: number | null) => void
  min?: number
  max?: number
  step?: number
  /** Decimal places shown and accepted. */
  precision?: number
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  name?: string
  placeholder?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

export function NumberInput({
  ref,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  precision,
  name,
  placeholder,
  disabled,
  required,
  className,
  onValueChange,
  id,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  ...props
}: NumberInputProps) {
  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <NumberField.Root
        {...props}
        id={id}
        required={required}
        format={
          precision === undefined
            ? undefined
            : { minimumFractionDigits: precision, maximumFractionDigits: precision }
        }
        onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next))}
      >
        <NumberField.Group className={cn(boxClass(size), styles.group, styles[size])}>
          <NumberField.Input
            ref={ref}
            placeholder={placeholder}
            aria-label={ariaLabel}
            className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.input)}

          {/* Base UI names these "Decrease" and "Increase" for assistive tech. */}
          <NumberField.Decrement className={styles.step}>
            <Icon name="minus" />
          </NumberField.Decrement>
          <NumberField.Increment className={styles.step}>
            <Icon name="plus" />
          </NumberField.Increment>
        </NumberField.Group>
      </NumberField.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Number Input A number, typed or stepped: a quantity, a price, a count. The field is [Tex...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { NumberInput } from './NumberInput'
import * as NumberInputStories from './NumberInput.stories'

<Meta of={NumberInputStories} />

# Number Input

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A number, typed or stepped: a quantity, a price, a count. The field is
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s, with a
decrease and an increase button inside it.

<Status of={NumberInputStories} />

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Default} />

## Variants

One appearance, the white outlined box. What changes is the size and how
the number steps and is shown.

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and dialogs: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a quantity in a cart row or a table cell. |

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Precision} />

| Setting | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `min`, `max` | A range the value must stay in. The button at a limit is disabled. |
| `step` | Values that move in fixed amounts: 5 minutes, 0.25 of a unit. |
| `precision` | A fixed number of decimals, such as 2 for a price: `9.5` shows as `9.50`. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { NumberInput } from 'zweihander/number-input'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/number-input.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/NumberInput.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/NumberInput.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/number-input](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/number-input)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Number Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={NumberInputStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={NumberInputStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The steppers float inside the box: no divider, a small inset from its end,
and a fill only on hover.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier, as on Text Input. A stepper is square and
inset 4px (`--space-1`) from the box's top and bottom, so it is the field's
height minus 8px: 16px in `sm`, 24px in `md`.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding, start', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Stepper', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-xs' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding, start', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Stepper', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding, end', token: '--control-xs-gap' },
    { part: 'Stepper', property: 'Inset from top and bottom', token: '--control-xs-gap' },
    { part: 'Stepper', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Stepper', property: 'Width on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Label and helper text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
  ]}
/>

The two steppers are 2px apart. The `sm` stepper's icon is one step below
its tier: a 14px icon would fill a 16px button edge to edge. The input
uses tabular figures, so digits do not shift as the value changes.

## Color

The field's colours are Text Input's; the steppers add their own.

<SpecTable
  caption="default"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--field-border' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Stepper icon', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Stepper, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Stepper icon, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="error"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="success"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Read-only" rows={[{ part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--surface-filled' }]} />

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Stepper hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'At max', content: <NumberInput label="Guests" defaultValue={12} min={1} max={12} /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <NumberInput label="Guests" defaultValue={0} validationState="error" helperText="At least 1." /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <NumberInput label="Guests" defaultValue={4} disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <NumberInput label="Guests" defaultValue={4} min={1} max={12} />
</States>

- **Hover** on a stepper fills it with `--accent` and darkens its icon; the
  field itself does not change.
- **Focus** is the field's 2px ring around the whole box, in
  `--danger-text` when invalid.
- **At a limit** the stepper that would go past it is disabled, at 50%
  opacity, and ignores hover, so it looks as unavailable as it is.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--surface-filled`; the steppers do
  nothing.
- **Disabled** dims the whole field to 50%.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={NumberInputStories} />
</div>

`ref` goes to the input. `id` and `className` are passed through too; no
other attributes are.

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`onValueChange` with a number**, not `onChange`: built on Base UI, it
  takes Base UI's name, and the value arrives parsed rather than as text.
- **`max` is optional with no default.** The spec marks it required with a
  default of 100, which contradicts itself; a quantity with no upper
  bound is common.
- **`label`, `helperText`, `validationState`** are added
  from the shared field.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Number Input for a quantity people adjust by a little, or type
outright: guests, items in a cart, minutes, a price. Set `min` and `max`
whenever the range is known, so the steppers stop at its ends.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={NumberInputStories.DoQuantity} />}
  doCaption="A quantity, nudged up and down within a known range."
  dont={<Story of={NumberInputStories.DontIdentifier} />}
  dontCaption="A postcode is not a quantity: stepping it is meaningless, and formatting may change it."
/>

## When not to use

- **For numbers that are identifiers**: postcodes, card numbers, phone
  numbers, IDs. Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with
  `inputMode="numeric"`, which brings up the number keyboard without
  steppers or formatting.
- **For a value picked on a scale**, such as volume or a percentage
  people judge by eye. Use a Slider.
- **For a small fixed set of numbers** (1, 2 or 4 seats). Use radios or a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs).

## Accessibility

- The input is a text field with `inputmode="numeric"` and the role
  description "Number field", named by the label.
- **Keyboard:** Up and Down step the value by `step` from the input; with
  Shift they step by 10, with Alt by 0.1. The steppers are out of the tab order
  (`tabindex="-1"`): the arrow keys do the same from the field.
- The steppers are named "Increase" and "Decrease" and are disabled at
  the limits, so a screen reader hears why nothing happened.
- The value is parsed and formatted in the user's locale; the form
  receives the plain number.
- `helperText` is the input's description and
  `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid`, as on Text Input.
- Steppers widen to 44px on touch screens, the one direction they can
  grow without covering the input or each other.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { Fragment, useRef, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react'
import { OTPField } from '@base-ui/react/otp-field'
import { ResendButton } from '../buttons/ResendButton'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { InputField, assignRef, type InputSize, type ValidationState } from './InputField'
import styles from './OTPInput.module.css'

export interface OTPInputProps {
  /** Points at the first cell. */
  ref?: Ref<HTMLInputElement>
  /** Number of characters. */
  length?: number
  /** Splits the cells into groups of this many, with a dash between groups. */
  groupSize?: number
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  /** Called once every cell is filled, typed or pasted. */
  onValueComplete?: (value: string) => void
  /** Which characters a cell accepts; others are dropped. */
  validationType?: 'numeric' | 'alpha' | 'alphanumeric'
  /** Shows dots instead of the characters. */
  mask?: boolean
  /** Submits the surrounding form once every cell is filled. */
  autoSubmit?: boolean
  /**
   * Shows a resend button under the cells, disabled while the cooldown counts
   * down. Return a promise to show the button busy until it settles: the
   * cooldown restarts only if it resolves, so a failed send can be retried.
   */
  onResend?: () => void | Promise<unknown>
  /** Seconds before resend is allowed, from mount and after each resend. */
  resendCooldown?: number
  resendLabel?: string
  /** The accessible name of each cell after the first, which the label names. */
  slotLabel?: (position: number, length: number) => string
  /** Names the group and the first cell. Required: Base UI names the first cell only through a label. */
  label: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  id?: string
  className?: string
}

const defaultSlotLabel = (position: number, length: number) => `Character ${position} of ${length}`

export function OTPInput({
  ref,
  length = 6,
  groupSize,
  onValueChange,
  onValueComplete,
  onResend,
  resendCooldown = 30,
  resendLabel = 'Resend code',
  slotLabel = defaultSlotLabel,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  name,
  disabled,
  required,
  className,
  ...props
}: OTPInputProps) {
  const firstCell = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)

  async function resend() {
    await onResend?.()
    // The button is about to be disabled: move focus to where the new code goes.
    firstCell.current?.focus()
  }

  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      className={className}
      footer={
        onResend && (
          <ResendButton
            className={styles.resend}
            cooldown={resendCooldown}
            label={resendLabel}
            disabled={disabled}
            onResend={resend}
          />
        )
      }
    >
      <OTPField.Root
        {...props}
        length={length}
        required={required}
        // Only the value: Base UI's event details are not part of this API.
        onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next))}
        onValueComplete={onValueComplete && ((next) => onValueComplete(next))}
        className={cn(styles.root, styles[size])}
      >
        {Array.from({ length }, (_, i) => (
          <Fragment key={i}>
            {groupSize && i > 0 && i % groupSize === 0 && (
              <OTPField.Separator className={styles.separator}>–</OTPField.Separator>
            )}
            <OTPField.Input
              ref={
                i === 0
                  ? (node: HTMLInputElement | null) => {
                      firstCell.current = node
                      assignRef(ref, node)
                    }
                  : undefined
              }
              aria-label={i === 0 ? undefined : slotLabel(i + 1, length)}
              className={styles.cell}
            />
          </Fragment>
        ))}
      </OTPField.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# OTP Input A short one-time code, typed or pasted into a row of single-character cells: t...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { OTPInput } from './OTPInput'
import * as OTPInputStories from './OTPInput.stories'

<Meta of={OTPInputStories} />

# OTP Input

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A short one-time code, typed or pasted into a row of single-character
cells: the code from a text message, an email or an authenticator app.

<Status of={OTPInputStories} />

<Canvas of={OTPInputStories.Default} />

## Variants

One appearance, a row of small outlined boxes. What changes is the size,
whether the cells are grouped, and whether there is a resend button.

<Canvas of={OTPInputStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Sign-in, verification and confirmation screens: the default. |
| `sm` | A code asked for inside a dense panel or a table row. |

<Canvas of={OTPInputStories.Resend} />

| Setting | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `groupSize` | A code people read in chunks: `3` shows six digits as 3 – 3, `4` an eight-character backup code as 4 – 4. |
| `onResend` | A code that was sent and may not arrive. The button waits `resendCooldown` seconds, showing the time left. Return a promise: a failed send starts no cooldown. |
| `validationType` | `numeric` for codes from texts and apps; `alphanumeric` for backup and recovery codes. |
| `mask` | A code that should not be read over someone's shoulder. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { OTPInput } from 'zweihander/otp-input'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/otp-input.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/OTPInput.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/OTPInput.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; the reference is [shadcn/ui Input OTP](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/input-otp)
- Behaviour: [Base UI OTP Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/otp-field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={OTPInputStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={OTPInputStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Each cell is its own box with the field's edge, fill and radius, so the
row reads as several small fields that belong together. The label and
helper text are Text Input's.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier, as on Text Input, and a cell is a square of
that tier.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Width and height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Width and height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Cells and separator', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Resend button', property: 'Pulled back to line up with the cells', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Height on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The characters use tabular figures, centred in the cell. The resend
button is a small ghost [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="default"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Border', token: '--field-edge' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-2xs' },
    { part: 'Character', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Caret', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
    { part: 'Group separator', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="error"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Read-only" rows={[{ part: 'Cell', property: 'Background', token: '--surface-filled' }]} />

`--field-edge` is the shared field's edge colour: `--field-border` by
default, `--danger-text` on error and `--success-text` on success, so every
cell and the helper text change together.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Filled', content: <OTPInput label="Code" length={4} defaultValue="4821" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <OTPInput label="Code" length={4} defaultValue="4821" validationState="error" helperText="That code is wrong." /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <OTPInput label="Code" length={4} defaultValue="48" disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <OTPInput label="Code" length={4} />
</States>

- **Hover** changes nothing: a cell is a text field, and the caret shows
  where typing goes.
- **Focus** rings only the cell being typed into, in `--danger-text` when
  invalid.
- **Error** turns every cell's edge and the helper text `--danger-text`.
- **Read-only** fills the cells with `--surface-filled`; typing does
  nothing.
- **Disabled** dims the cells to 50% and disables the resend button.
- **Cooling down**, the resend button is disabled and shows the time left
  as `m:ss`.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={OTPInputStories} />
</div>

`ref` goes to the first cell. `id` and `className` are passed through too;
no other attributes are.

### Differences from the spec

There is no uiguideline.com spec for this component; the reference is shadcn/ui Input OTP.

- **One component, flat props.** shadcn composes `InputOTP`, `InputOTPGroup`,
  `InputOTPSlot` and `InputOTPSeparator`; Zweihänder takes `length` and
  `groupSize`, as the API conventions ask for flat props before 1.0.
- **Resend is built in.** shadcn leaves it to the page. Every screen that
  sends a code needs the same button and countdown, so it lives here.
- **Real inputs, one per cell**, from Base UI, not one hidden input under
  drawn slots: each cell is focusable and named.
- **`label`, `helperText`, `validationState`** are added from the shared field.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an OTP Input for a short code someone copies from another place: a
text message, an email, an authenticator app. Say where the code was sent
in `helperText`, and give a way to send another.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={OTPInputStories.DoOneField} />}
  doCaption="Six digits, labelled, with where the code went and a way to resend it."
  dont={<Story of={OTPInputStories.DontLongCode} />}
  dontCaption="Sixteen cells are too many to scan or correct. A long key is one Text Input."
/>

## When not to use

- **For codes longer than about 8 characters**, licence keys or recovery
  phrases. Use a [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs).
- **For a PIN or password people make up themselves.** Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with
  `type="password"`: cells suggest a code that was sent.
- **For a number people adjust.** Use a
  [Number Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-numberinput--docs).

## Accessibility

- The cells sit in a `group` named by the label; the label also names the
  first cell, and each later cell is named by `slotLabel`, "Character 2 of 6"
  by default.
- **Keyboard:** the group is one tab stop: only the cell to type into is in
  the tab order. Typing a character fills the cell and moves to the next;
  Backspace clears the cell before and moves back; Left and Right move
  between cells.
- Characters `validationType` does not allow are dropped, so letters cannot
  enter a numeric code.
- Pasting the whole code into any cell fills every cell; spaces are ignored.
- The first cell has `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so phones offer the code
  from a text message.
- `helperText` is the group's description and `validationState="error"` sets
  `aria-invalid` on every cell.
- The resend button is disabled during the cooldown and its name carries the
  time left. After a send, focus moves to the first cell, so it is not lost
  with the disabled button; while a send is pending the button stays
  focusable and is marked `aria-busy`. The countdown is not a live region, so it does not interrupt
  every second.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useState, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Select } from '../inputs/Select'
import styles from './Pagination.module.css'

export interface PaginationProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children' | 'onChange'> {
  /** Ignored when `totalItems` is set: the count is then worked out from `pageSize`, so the two cannot disagree. */
  totalPages?: number
  /** Rows in all. Shows the "21–40 of 340" summary. */
  totalItems?: number
  pageSize?: number
  defaultPageSize?: number
  onPageSizeChange?: (pageSize: number) => void
  /** Choices for the "Rows per page" select; without them there is no select. */
  pageSizeOptions?: number[]
  /** 1-based. */
  page?: number
  defaultPage?: number
  onPageChange?: (page: number) => void
  /** Pages shown either side of the current one. */
  siblingCount?: number
  /** Pages always shown at each end. */
  boundaryCount?: number
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** Render links instead of buttons, for pages with their own URL. */
  getHref?: (page: number) => string
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

const range = (from: number, to: number) => Array.from({ length: Math.max(0, to - from + 1) }, (_, i) => from + i)

/** The page numbers to show, with 'start-ellipsis' / 'end-ellipsis' where a run is skipped. */
export function paginationItems(page: number, total: number, siblings = 1, boundary = 1) {
  const start = range(1, Math.min(boundary, total))
  const end = range(Math.max(total - boundary + 1, boundary + 1), total)
  const siblingsStart = Math.max(Math.min(page - siblings, total - boundary - siblings * 2 - 1), boundary + 2)
  const siblingsEnd = Math.min(Math.max(page + siblings, boundary + siblings * 2 + 2), end.length > 0 ? end[0] - 2 : total - 1)
  return [
    ...start,
    ...(siblingsStart > boundary + 2 ? ['start-ellipsis' as const] : boundary + 1 < total - boundary ? [boundary + 1] : []),
    ...range(siblingsStart, siblingsEnd),
    ...(siblingsEnd < total - boundary - 1 ? ['end-ellipsis' as const] : total - boundary > boundary ? [total - boundary] : []),
    ...end,
  ]
}

export function Pagination({
  totalPages,
  totalItems,
  pageSize: pageSizeProp,
  defaultPageSize = 20,
  onPageSizeChange,
  pageSizeOptions,
  page: pageProp,
  defaultPage = 1,
  onPageChange,
  siblingCount = 1,
  boundaryCount = 1,
  size = 'md',
  getHref,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Pagination',
  className,
  ...props
}: PaginationProps) {
  const [pageState, setPageState] = useState(defaultPage)
  const [pageSizeState, setPageSizeState] = useState(defaultPageSize)
  const pageSize = Math.max(1, pageSizeProp ?? pageSizeState)
  const pagesFor = (size: number) => Math.max(1, totalItems === undefined ? (totalPages ?? 1) : Math.ceil(totalItems / size))
  const total = pagesFor(pageSize)
  const page = Math.min(Math.max(1, pageProp ?? pageState), total)
  const go = (p: number) => {
    setPageState(p)
    onPageChange?.(p)
  }
  const first = (page - 1) * pageSize + 1
  const changePageSize = (size: number) => {
    setPageSizeState(size)
    onPageSizeChange?.(size)
    // Keep the first row the reader was looking at on screen.
    const next = Math.min(Math.floor((first - 1) / size) + 1, pagesFor(size))
    if (next !== page) go(next)
  }
  // Grouped in the reader's locale; the words around it are English, like the rest of the labels.
  const formatCount = (n: number) => n.toLocaleString()

  const control = (target: number, label: string, content: ReactNode, extra?: string, current?: boolean) => {
    const disabled = target < 1 || target > total
    const common = {
      className: cn(styles.control, extra, current && styles.current),
      'aria-label': label,
      'aria-current': current ? ('page' as const) : undefined,
    }
    if (getHref) {
      // A link at the ends has nowhere to go: no href, aria-disabled. Without
      // href an <a> has no role, and aria-label is not allowed on it, so the
      // role is set back explicitly.
      return disabled ? (
        <a {...common} role="link" aria-disabled="true">
          {content}
        </a>
      ) : (
        <a {...common} href={getHref(target)} onClick={() => !current && go(target)}>
          {content}
        </a>
      )
    }
    return (
      <button type="button" {...common} disabled={disabled} onClick={() => !current && go(target)}>
        {content}
      </button>
    )
  }

  return (
    <nav aria-label={ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.pagination, styles[size], className)} {...props}>
      {totalItems !== undefined && (
        <p role="status" className={styles.summary}>
          {totalItems > 0
            ? `${formatCount(first)}–${formatCount(Math.min(page * pageSize, totalItems))} of ${formatCount(totalItems)}`
            : '0 of 0'}
        </p>
      )}
      <ul className={styles.list}>
        <li>{control(page - 1, 'Previous page', <Icon name="chevron-left" />, styles.step)}</li>
        {paginationItems(page, total, siblingCount, boundaryCount).map((item) => (
          <li key={item}>
            {typeof item === 'string' ? (
              <span className={styles.ellipsis} aria-hidden="true">
                …
              </span>
            ) : (
              control(item, `Page ${item}`, item, undefined, item === page)
            )}
          </li>
        ))}
        <li>{control(page + 1, 'Next page', <Icon name="chevron-right" />, styles.step)}</li>
      </ul>
      {pageSizeOptions && (
        <div className={styles.pageSize}>
          {/* The select carries the same name; this text is only what sighted readers see. */}
          <span aria-hidden="true">Rows per page</span>
          <Select
            aria-label="Rows per page"
            size={size}
            className={styles.pageSizeSelect}
            options={pageSizeOptions.map(String)}
            value={String(pageSize)}
            onValueChange={(v) => v && changePageSize(Number(v))}
          />
        </div>
      )}
    </nav>
  )
}

# Pagination Moves through a long list one page at a time: previous, next, and the page nu...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as PaginationStories from './Pagination.stories'

<Meta of={PaginationStories} />

# Pagination

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Moves through a long list one page at a time: previous, next, and the page
numbers around the current one. Under a table it can also say which rows
are shown ("21–40 of 340") and let the reader pick how many rows a page
holds.

<Status of={PaginationStories} />

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.Middle} />

## Variants

Pagination has one look. What changes is the size, how many numbers show,
whether the pages are buttons or links, and the two optional ends.

| Form | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Under a table or a list of results. The default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a card, a side panel, a compact table footer. |
| `getHref` | Pages with their own URL: each page is a link that can be opened in a new tab and shared. |
| Buttons | Pages that only exist in this view's state, such as a filtered list in a dialog. The default. |
| `totalItems` | A table footer, where the reader needs to know how many rows there are: adds the summary at the start. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | Long tables where readers scan in bulk: adds a "Rows per page" select at the end. |

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.WithSummary} />

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.FewPages} />

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.Links} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Pagination } from 'zweihander/pagination'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/pagination.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Pagination.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Pagination.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/pagination](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/pagination)
- Behaviour: a plain `<nav>` around a list of buttons or links
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={PaginationStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={PaginationStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The first and last page always show, the current page keeps a sibling
each side, and "…" appears only where it hides two or more pages. A single
hidden page is shown instead, since "…" would take the same room. So the
number of controls stays the same as you move through the middle, and
Next does not jump.

The summary and the select only appear when `totalItems` and
`pageSizeOptions` are passed. The summary sits at the start and pushes the
pages and the select to the end; on a narrow screen the row wraps.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). A control is square
at its minimum; the inline padding only shows on a page number of three
digits or more. Previous and next have no padding, so they stay square.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Height and minimum width', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius' },
    { part: 'Previous, Next', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-sm' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
