    { part: 'Control', property: 'Height and minimum width', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius' },
    { part: 'Previous, Next', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'List', property: 'Gap between controls', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Summary, List, Rows per page', property: 'Gap between them', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis', property: 'Minimum width', token: '--space-6' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Height and minimum width on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

One colour set: the current page is the only fill. Switch the theme and
the accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Page, Previous, Next', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Page, Previous, Next, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Page, Previous, Next, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Current page', property: 'Background', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Current page', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-foreground' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis, Summary, Rows per page label', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

At rest a control has no fill.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={PaginationStories.StatesExample} />
</States>

- **Selected**: the current page is filled with `--primary`, medium
  weight. It does not change on hover, and pressing it does nothing.
- **Hover** fills a page, Previous or Next with an `--accent` chip.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the control.
- **Disabled**: Previous on the first page (above) and Next on the last, at 50%
  opacity. As buttons they are `disabled`; as links they lose their
  `href`.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={PaginationStories} />
</div>

The rows-per-page select is a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs)
at the same `size`. Changing it moves to the page that holds the first row
shown before, so the reader does not lose their place; it calls
`onPageSizeChange`, then `onPageChange` if the page moved.

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through. `paginationItems(page,
total, siblings, boundary)` is exported too, for building your own.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Pagination under a long list or table when the reader needs to know
where they are in it and jump to a page: search results, an audit log, an
order history. Put it below the content it pages, and keep the list's
position stable as pages change.

Leave `siblingCount` and `boundaryCount` at 1. The control stays short and
keeps the same width as the reader moves, so Next stays under the pointer.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={PaginationStories.DoKeepItShort} />}
  doCaption="The default range: first, last, and the current page with a neighbour each side, on one line."
  dont={<Story of={PaginationStories.DontShowEveryPage} />}
  dontCaption="Every page number at once wraps over several lines and buries the current page."
/>

Under a table, pass `totalItems` so the reader knows how much there is.
Offer `pageSizeOptions` only when readers really scan in bulk; three or
four choices (10, 20, 50, 100) are enough.

When the pages have URLs, pass `getHref`, so a page can be opened in a new
tab, bookmarked and shared.

## When not to use

- **For a feed read top to bottom.** Load more as the reader scrolls, or
  with a "Load more" [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs):
  page numbers mean nothing in a stream.
- **For a few items.** If everything fits on one page, show it all.
- **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper.
- **For switching between views of one thing.** Use Tabs.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Pagination", around a list.
- Each page control is named "Page 3"; the current one has
  `aria-current="page"`. Previous and next are named "Previous page" and
  "Next page".
- At either end, Previous or Next is disabled. As links they lose their
  `href` (the only thing that stops an `<a>` navigating) and keep
  `role="link"` with `aria-disabled`, so they are still announced as a
  disabled link.
- With `getHref`, each control is a real `<a href>`; without it, a native
  `<button>`. Both are in the tab order and activate with Enter (buttons
  with Space too).
- The summary has `role="status"`, a polite live region, so "21–40 of 340"
  is read out after a page or size change.
- The rows-per-page select is a combobox named "Rows per page"; its
  visible label is `aria-hidden` so the name is not read twice.
- The ellipsis is `aria-hidden`: the page names already say which numbers
  are there.
- Controls are 24px (`sm`) or 32px (`md`) and grow to 44px on touch
  screens (`pointer: coarse`).
- Focus ring: 2px `--ring`, 2px offset.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Password Input A password field with a Show / Hide button and, where a password is being...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { PasswordInput, defaultPasswordRules } from './PasswordInput'
import * as PasswordInputStories from './PasswordInput.stories'

<Meta of={PasswordInputStories} />

# Password Input

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A password field with a Show / Hide button and, where a password is being
chosen, the rules it must meet, ticked off as the reader types.

<Status of={PasswordInputStories} />

<Canvas of={PasswordInputStories.Default} />

## Variants

One appearance, Text Input's. What changes is whether the password is
being typed or chosen.

| Use | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Signing in, or confirming who you are before a change | The default: `autoComplete="current-password"`, no rules. |
| Choosing a password: sign up, reset, change | `autoComplete="new-password"` and `rules`, so password managers suggest one and the reader sees what it needs. |

<Canvas of={PasswordInputStories.WithRules} />

<Canvas of={PasswordInputStories.Sizes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { PasswordInput, defaultPasswordRules } from 'zweihander/password-input'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/password-input.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/PasswordInput.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/PasswordInput.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; the rules follow [NIST SP 800-63B](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html) (length over character kinds)
- Built on: [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) and its `TextInputButton`
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={PasswordInputStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={PasswordInputStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The field, label, helper text and button are Text Input's; this
component adds the rules and the button's behaviour.

## Measurements

Field sizes are Text Input's. The rules sit in its helper text, one per
line.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Rule', property: 'Gap between tick and text', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Tick', property: 'Width and height', token: '--icon-sm' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="default"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Met rule', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
  ]}
/>

A rule not yet met takes the helper text's colour. A met rule stays
green when the field is in error: it is done.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Rules met', content: <PasswordInput label="New password" rules={defaultPasswordRules} defaultValue="correct horse battery" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <PasswordInput validationState="error" helperText="That password is wrong." defaultValue="hunter2" /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <PasswordInput disabled defaultValue="hunter2" /> },
  ]}
>
  <PasswordInput />
</States>

- **Hover and focus** are Text Input's; the Show button has the add-on
  button's hover and focus.
- **Shown**, the field is `type="text"` and the button reads Hide. It goes
  back to dots when the form is sent.
- **Error** colours the edge and the helper text `--danger-text`; met
  rules stay green.
- **Disabled** dims the field and disables the button.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={PasswordInputStories} />
</div>

Every other Text Input prop and input attribute passes through, except
`type` and `endAddon`, which the component owns. `ref` points at the
input. `defaultPasswordRules` and the `PasswordRule` type are exported
with it.

### Differences from the spec

There is no uiguideline.com spec for this component. It moved here from
the auth templates, where it was a template file, when Settings became its
first use outside sign-in.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use it for every password field: sign in, sign up, reset, and change
password in Settings. Give a new password `rules` so the reader knows what
it needs before sending, not after.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={PasswordInputStories.DoWithRules} />}
  doCaption="A new password, hidden, with its rule and a Show button."
  dont={<Story of={PasswordInputStories.DontPlainText} />}
  dontCaption="A plain Text Input shows the password to anyone nearby and tells the reader nothing about what it needs."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a code that was sent**, such as a sign-in code. Use an
  [OTP Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-otpinput--docs).
- **For an API key or token** the reader copies. Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) that is
  read-only, with a copy button.

## Accessibility

- The field is named by its label. The Show / Hide button's name says
  what it does next and to which field ("Show password", "Hide new
  password"), and its visible text is the start of that name.
- The rules are part of the field's description, each ending "(met)" or
  "(not met)", so they are read when the field gets focus; ticking one off
  is not announced on every keystroke.
- When the form is sent the field goes back to dots, so the browser does
  not keep the password as plain text in its form history.
- `autoComplete` is `current-password` by default and should be
  `new-password` where a password is chosen, so password managers fill or
  suggest the right one.
- A disabled field disables its button too.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, useState } from 'react'
import { arc, pie } from 'd3-shape'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Table } from '../data-display/Table'
import { Skeleton } from '../loaders/Skeleton'
import { ChartFrame, useEnterOnce } from './ChartFrame'
import { ChartLegend } from './ChartLegend'
import { colorVar, formatCompact, formatShare, groupSlices, type Slice } from './chart-utils'
import styles from './Chart.module.css'

export interface PieChartProps {
  /** Shown above the chart, and its accessible name. */
  title: string
  data: Slice[]
  /** `donut` leaves a hole with the total in it. */
  appearance?: 'pie' | 'donut'
  /** Under the total in a donut, e.g. "requests". */
  centerLabel?: string
  /** Diameter in pixels. */
  size?: number
  format?: (value: number) => string
  isLoading?: boolean
  className?: string
}

/**
 * Parts of one whole. No labels on the slices: the legend beside it carries
 * value and share. Past six slices, or under 3%, slices merge into "Other".
 */
export function PieChart({
  title,
  data,
  appearance = 'pie',
  centerLabel = 'Total',
  size = 200,
  format = formatCompact,
  isLoading = false,
  className,
}: PieChartProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [focusKey, setFocusKey] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const total = data.reduce((sum, d) => sum + d.value, 0)
  // All zeros is no data: a pie of nothing has no parts to show.
  const hasData = total > 0
  const isEntering = useEnterOnce(!isLoading && hasData)
  const shareOf = (value: number) => formatShare(value / total)

  const slices = groupSlices(data)
  const isDonut = appearance === 'donut'
  const radius = size / 2 - 2
  const arcs = pie<(typeof slices)[number]>()
    .sort(null)
    .value((d) => d.value)(slices)
  const path = arc<(typeof arcs)[number]>()
    .innerRadius(isDonut ? radius * 0.64 : 0)
    .outerRadius(radius)
    .padAngle(isDonut ? 0.015 : 0)
    .cornerRadius(isDonut ? 2 : 0)

  return (
    <ChartFrame
      title={title}
      isLoading={isLoading}
      loading={<Skeleton appearance="circle" width={size} height={size} />}
      hasData={hasData}
      emptyHeight={size}
      className={className}
      table={() => (
        <Table
          caption={title}
          density="sm"
          rows={data}
          getRowId={(_, i) => String(i)}
          columns={[
            { key: 'label', header: 'Label', isRowHeader: true },
            { key: 'value', header: 'Value', align: 'end', cell: (d) => format(d.value) },
            { key: 'share', header: 'Share', align: 'end', cell: (d) => shareOf(d.value) },
          ]}
        />
      )}
    >
      {(titleId) => (
        <div className={styles.pieBody}>
          <svg
            role="img"
            aria-labelledby={`${titleId} ${id}-desc`}
            className={cn(isEntering && styles.entering)}
            width={size}
            height={size}
            viewBox={`${-size / 2} ${-size / 2} ${size} ${size}`}
          >
            {/* The sweep-in: a ring stroke drawn round the mask, once. */}
            <mask id={`${id}-sweep`}>
              <circle className={styles.sweep} r={radius / 2} fill="none" stroke="white" strokeWidth={radius + 4} pathLength={1} transform="rotate(-90)" />
            </mask>
            <g mask={isEntering ? `url(#${id}-sweep)` : undefined}>
              {arcs.map((a, i) => (
                <path
                  key={i}
                  className={cn(styles.slice, focusKey && focusKey !== String(i) && styles.dim)}
                  d={path(a) ?? ''}
                  fill={colorVar(a.data.color)}
                  onPointerEnter={() => setFocusKey(String(i))}
                  onPointerLeave={() => setFocusKey(null)}
                />
              ))}
            </g>
            {isDonut && (
              <>
                <text className={styles.centerTotal} textAnchor="middle" dy="-0.05em">
                  {format(total)}
                </text>
                <text className={styles.centerLabel} textAnchor="middle" dy="1.5em">
                  {centerLabel}
                </text>
              </>
            )}
          </svg>
          <span id={`${id}-desc`} className={styles.srOnly}>
            {slices.map((s) => `${s.label} ${shareOf(s.value)}`).join(', ')}
          </span>
          <ChartLegend
            orientation="vertical"
            items={slices.map((s, i) => ({ key: String(i), label: s.label, color: colorVar(s.color), value: `${format(s.value)} · ${shareOf(s.value)}` }))}
            onFocusChange={setFocusKey}
          />
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartFrame>
  )
}

'use client'

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Popover as BasePopover } from '@base-ui/react/popover'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Popover.module.css'

export interface PopoverProps {
  /** The element that opens it: one button. Its props are merged, not wrapped. */
  trigger: ReactElement
  /** Names the popover (it is a dialog). Without one, pass `aria-label`. */
  title?: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  children?: ReactNode
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  /** A close button in the corner. Escape and a click outside close it either way. */
  hasCloseButton?: boolean
  closeLabel?: string
  /** Open on hover as well as click, for previews. Content must still be reachable by click and keyboard. */
  openOnHover?: boolean
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Trap focus inside while open, lock page scroll and block clicks outside (Base UI's modal mode). */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where the popup renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function Popover({
  trigger,
  title,
  description,
  children,
  side = 'bottom',
  align = 'center',
  hasCloseButton = false,
  closeLabel = 'Close',
  openOnHover = false,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  isModal = false,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  className,
}: PopoverProps) {
  return (
    <BasePopover.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}
      modal={isModal}
    >
      <BasePopover.Trigger render={trigger} openOnHover={openOnHover} />
      <BasePopover.Portal container={container}>
        <BasePopover.Positioner className={styles.positioner} side={side} align={align} sideOffset={6}>
          <BasePopover.Popup aria-label={title ? undefined : ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.popup, className)}>
            {(title || hasCloseButton) && (
              <div className={styles.header}>
                {title && <BasePopover.Title className={styles.title}>{title}</BasePopover.Title>}
                {hasCloseButton && (
                  <BasePopover.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close}>
                    <Icon name="close" />
                  </BasePopover.Close>
                )}
              </div>
            )}
            {/* Base UI only traps focus in a modal popover that contains a
                Close, and a touch screen reader needs one to get out. */}
            {isModal && !hasCloseButton && (
              <BasePopover.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={cn(styles.close, styles.hiddenClose)}>
                <Icon name="close" />
              </BasePopover.Close>
            )}
            {description && <BasePopover.Description className={styles.description}>{description}</BasePopover.Description>}
            {children && <div className={styles.body}>{children}</div>}
          </BasePopover.Popup>
        </BasePopover.Positioner>
      </BasePopover.Portal>
    </BasePopover.Root>
  )
}

./src/components/overlays/Popover.mdx
# Popover A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a share form,...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as PopoverStories from './Popover.stories'

<Meta of={PopoverStories} />

# Popover

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a share
form, a filter, a set of options. It opens on click and stays until you
close it.

<Status of={PopoverStories} />

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.Open} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Non-modal (default) | Most popovers. Tab can leave it and the page stays usable while it is open. |
| Modal (`isModal`) | A popover that must be finished or closed first: focus stays inside, the page does not scroll and presses outside are blocked. |
| `openOnHover` | A preview that also opens on hover, when what it holds must be reachable by click, keyboard and touch. For a person or record preview on a link, use [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs). |

A title is optional. Without one, name the popover with `aria-label`:

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.ContentOnly} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Popover } from 'zweihander/popover'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/popover.json
```

- Source: [src/components/overlays/Popover.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Popover.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/popover](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/popover)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={PopoverStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={PopoverStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open popovers on this tab and the next are pictures: real popovers
rendered in place with `container` and inert, the popup laid out under the
trigger where it opens.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Container"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-md' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Title to close button', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Title to description', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Body', property: 'Gap above', token: '--space-3' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Close button"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The container is as wide as its content, at most 22rem and never wider
than the room beside the trigger. It has no arrow: it opens 6px from the
trigger and lines up with it, which already ties the two. It has a 1px
border and a semibold title. The close button is 20px: 2px around its icon,
one line of text tall. Popovers sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade
in over `--duration-fast`.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Every popover"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Title, body', property: 'Colour', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Description', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

Select and Combobox lists use the same surface: `--popover`, its border
and shadow.

## States

The popover is open or closed. Opening fades it in and scales it up from
97%, from the trigger's side. The trigger keeps the states of its own
component (see Button); the close button is the only part with states of
its own:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={PopoverStories.CloseButton} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills the close button with `--accent`.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the button.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={PopoverStories} />
</div>

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Popover for a short task that belongs to the button that opens it:
share a file, set a filter, pick from a few options. It holds links,
inputs and buttons, which a Tooltip must not.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={PopoverStories.DoShortTask} />}
  doCaption="A short task tied to its button: one field and one action."
  dont={<Story of={PopoverStories.DontLongForm} />}
  dontCaption="A whole form in a popover. It closes on a stray press outside and loses the work: use a Modal."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a label or a hint** on hover or focus. Use a
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs).
- **For a list of actions or commands.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs): it has the
  arrow-key navigation a list of commands needs.
- **For a long form or a decision with consequences.** Use a
  [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs).

## Accessibility

- The popup is a `role="dialog"` named by `title` (or `aria-label`) and
  described by `description`. The trigger carries `aria-expanded` and
  `aria-haspopup`.
- Opening moves focus into the popup; Escape or a press outside closes it
  and returns focus to the trigger.
- **Non-modal by default:** Tab can leave the popup, and the page stays
  usable. `isModal` switches to Base UI's modal mode: focus is trapped,
  page scroll is locked and presses outside are blocked.
- Base UI only traps focus when the popup contains a close button, and a
  touch screen reader needs one to get out. So a modal popover without
  `hasCloseButton` still renders one: hidden until it has keyboard focus,
  then shown in the corner, so focus is never invisible.

  <Canvas of={PopoverStories.Modal} />

- `openOnHover` adds hover to click, it does not replace it: the content
  stays reachable by keyboard and touch.
- The close button has the 2px focus ring and a 44px hit area on touch
  screens.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { withPrefersDark } from '@/test/story-helpers'

/**
 * The preview decorator's side of the Preview theme: the globals the
 * Playground sends become a `<Theme>` around the story.
 */
const meta = {
  title: 'Site/Preview theme',
  render: () => <p>Themed content</p>,
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

const wrapper = (canvasElement: HTMLElement) => canvasElement.querySelector('[data-preview-theme]')

export const Dark: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'dark' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(wrapper(canvasElement)).toHaveClass('dark')
    // Popups portal to <body>: the frame's <html> goes dark with it.
    await expect(document.documentElement).toHaveClass('dark')
  },
}

export const Light: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'light' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(wrapper(canvasElement)).toHaveClass('light')
    await expect(document.documentElement).not.toHaveClass('dark')
  },
}

export const SystemOnDarkOs: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'system' },
  beforeEach: withPrefersDark(true),
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(wrapper(canvasElement)).toHaveClass('dark')
  },
}

export const SystemOnLightOs: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'system' },
  beforeEach: withPrefersDark(false),
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(wrapper(canvasElement)).toHaveClass('light')
  },
}

export const ColorAndRadius: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'light', accent: 'rose', gray: 'slate', radius: 'full-rounded' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const scope = wrapper(canvasElement) as HTMLElement
    await expect(scope).toHaveAttribute('data-accent', 'rose')
    await expect(scope).toHaveAttribute('data-gray', 'slate')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--radius-factor')).toBe('1.5')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--radius-full')).toBe('9999px')
    // Popups portal to <body>: the frame's <html> wears the same.
    await expect(document.documentElement).toHaveAttribute('data-accent', 'rose')
    await expect(document.documentElement.style.getPropertyValue('--radius-factor')).toBe('1.5')
  },
}

export const Typography: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'light', font: 'inter', scaling: '110%' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const scope = wrapper(canvasElement) as HTMLElement
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--font-sans')).toContain('Inter')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--scaling')).toBe('1.1')
    // Headings follow: --font-heading derives from --font-sans on every element.
    const text = canvasElement.querySelector('p')!
    await expect(getComputedStyle(text).getPropertyValue('--font-heading')).toContain('Inter')
    await expect(getComputedStyle(text).fontFamily).toContain('Inter')
    // Popups portal to <body>: the frame's <html> wears the same.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(document.body).getPropertyValue('--font-heading')).toContain('Inter')
    await expect(document.documentElement.style.getPropertyValue('--scaling')).toBe('1.1')
    // The face is there: bundled with the preview (the build has no font CDN request).
    await document.fonts.load('16px "Inter Variable"')
    await expect(document.fonts.check('16px "Inter Variable"')).toBe(true)
  },
}

/** System is the token's own stack: nothing set, so the default stays. */
export const SystemFont: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'light', font: 'system', scaling: '100%' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const scope = wrapper(canvasElement) as HTMLElement
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--font-sans')).toBe('')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--scaling')).toBe('1')
  },
}

/** A value the kit does not have is dropped: the default stays. */
export const UnknownValues: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'light', accent: 'foo', radius: 'huge', font: 'comic', scaling: '200%' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const scope = wrapper(canvasElement) as HTMLElement
    await expect(scope).not.toHaveAttribute('data-accent')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--radius-factor')).toBe('')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--font-sans')).toBe('')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--scaling')).toBe('')
  },
}

/** Outside the Playground no appearance is set: no wrapper, the toolbar's theme as before. */
export const ToolbarTheme: Story = {
  globals: { theme: 'dark' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(wrapper(canvasElement)).toBeNull()
    await expect(document.documentElement).toHaveClass('dark')
  },
}

'use client'

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Progress } from '@base-ui/react/progress'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './ProgressBar.module.css'

export interface ProgressBarProps extends Omit<Progress.Root.Props, 'value' | 'children' | 'className' | 'render'> {
  value?: number
  /** The spec's `maxValue`. */
  max?: number
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  isRounded?: boolean
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary' | 'destructive'
  /** Progress is happening but how much is unknown: a sliding bar. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  /** Show the value ("70%") after the bar. */
  showValueLabel?: boolean
  /** A visible label above the bar; also its accessible name. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** The accessible name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function ProgressBar({
  value = 0,
  max = 100,
  size = 'md',
  isRounded = false,
  variant = 'primary',
  isIndeterminate = false,
  showValueLabel = false,
  label,
  className,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  ...props
}: ProgressBarProps) {
  return (
    <Progress.Root
      {...props}
      value={isIndeterminate ? null : value}
      max={max}
      aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}
      className={cn(styles.root, styles[size], styles[variant], isRounded && styles.rounded, className)}
    >
      {label && <Progress.Label className={styles.label}>{label}</Progress.Label>}
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <Progress.Track className={styles.track}>
          <Progress.Indicator className={styles.indicator} />
        </Progress.Track>
        {showValueLabel && !isIndeterminate && <Progress.Value className={styles.value} />}
      </div>
    </Progress.Root>
  )
}

# Progress Bar Shows how far a task with a known size has got: an upload, an install, the ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { ProgressBar } from './ProgressBar'
import * as ProgressBarStories from './ProgressBar.stories'

<Meta of={ProgressBarStories} />

# Progress Bar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Shows how far a task with a known size has got: an upload, an install,
the steps of a setup.

<Status of={ProgressBarStories} />

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.ValueLabel} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the fill, by meaning. The track is the same in
all four.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `primary` | The default: a task the user started and is waiting on. |
| `accent` | A strong fill in neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. |
| `secondary` | Low emphasis: progress in the background, or one of many bars in a list. |
| `destructive` | A task that is failing, or a quota about to run out. |

`size` is the track's thickness, and `isRounded` gives it pill ends.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Sizes} />

When a task has started but its size is not known yet, go indeterminate,
and switch to a value as soon as there is one.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Indeterminate} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ProgressBar } from 'zweihander/progress-bar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/progress-bar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/loaders/ProgressBar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/ProgressBar.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Progress](https://base-ui.com/react/components/progress)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ProgressBarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ProgressBarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

## Measurements

The bar fills the width of its container. Each size sets only the track's
height.

<SpecTable caption="sm" rows={[{ part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--progress-sm' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="md" rows={[{ part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--progress-md' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="lg" rows={[{ part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--progress-lg' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label to track', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Track to value label', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Track and indicator, rounded', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
    { part: 'Label and value label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label and value label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Transition between values', token: '--duration-slow' },
  ]}
/>

The value label is at least 4 characters wide, so the bar does not jump as
the number grows from 9% to 100%.

## Color

The fill is what carries the value, so it must clear 3:1 against the
track. Not every accent's solid does (amber's is about 2.9:1 on white), so
each variant fills with a colour meant to be read as text on the page,
which keeps it at 3:1 or better on the track. Switch the theme and the
accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable caption="primary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--primary-text' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="accent" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--foreground' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="secondary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--muted-foreground' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="destructive" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--danger-text' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--secondary' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Value label', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

## States

A progress bar is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed
state.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Progress' },
    { label: 'Indeterminate', content: <ProgressBar isIndeterminate label="Connecting" /> },
    { label: 'Complete', content: <ProgressBar value={100} label="Uploaded" showValueLabel /> },
  ]}
>
  <ProgressBar value={70} label="Uploading" showValueLabel />
</States>

- **Progress** fills from the start edge, easing between values over
  `--duration-slow`.
- **Indeterminate** slides a third of the track across, once every 1.4s.
  The value label is hidden: there is no value to show.
- **Complete** is a full bar. It does not change on its own; replace or
  remove it when the task ends.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ProgressBarStories} />
</div>

Every other prop goes to Base UI's `Progress.Root`: `id`,
`aria-labelledby`, `min`, `format`, `locale`, `getAriaValueText`.

### Differences from the spec

- **`max`, not `maxValue`**, the name Base UI and the native `<progress>`
  use.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Progress Bar for a task that takes long enough to wait on and whose
size is known, or will be: an upload, an import, the steps of a setup.
Name the task in the `label`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ProgressBarStories.DoNameTheTask} />}
  doCaption="The label names the task, so the reader knows what they are waiting for."
  dont={<Story of={ProgressBarStories.DontBareBar} />}
  dontCaption="A bare bar leaves sighted readers guessing what it measures, even with an aria-label."
/>

`value` is out of `max`, and the value label shows the percentage:

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Max} />

Without a visible label, `aria-label` names the bar for screen readers.
Use it only where the context already says what the bar measures.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.WithoutVisibleLabel} />

## When not to use

- **For a short wait with no known size.** Use a
  [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs).
- **For content whose shape you know.** A
  [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the
  layout.
- **For steps the user moves through themselves.** Use a
  [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs): it names the
  steps, and the user can go back.

## Accessibility

- `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and
  `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext` from Base UI. Indeterminate drops
  `aria-valuenow` rather than reporting 0.
- Every bar needs a name: a visible `label` (linked by Base UI) or
  `aria-label`.
- The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every variant and accent, in both
  modes. The value label is `--muted-foreground`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the fill stops easing between values and
  the indeterminate slide slows from 1.4s to 4s a pass.
- A progressbar is not a live region. If completion matters, announce it
  (a Toast, or a status message) when the task ends.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Progressive Sign In A sign-in page that asks for the email first and only then decides h...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ProgressiveSignInStories from './ProgressiveSignIn.stories'

<Meta of={ProgressiveSignInStories} />

# Progressive Sign In

A sign-in page that asks for the email first and only then decides how
the account signs in: accounts whose organization uses single sign-on go
to their identity provider, the rest are asked for a password. After
Carbon's login pattern. Built on the **Auth Layout** (see
[Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#auth-layout)), its
`PasswordInput` and `AuthProviders`, and the kit's TextInput, Checkbox,
Spinner, Link, Alert and Button.

Use it when some of your customers sign in through their company's
identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace): they never see a
password field they cannot use. Where everyone signs in with a password,
use **Sign In**, which asks for both at once.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/progressive-sign-in-template.json
```

<Canvas of={ProgressiveSignInStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Step 1, the email**: one field, **Remember my email** and Continue. An
  empty or malformed email is marked with a message and keeps focus. The
  email, trimmed, goes to `onContinue`, which returns the route.
- **The route is yours**: `onContinue` looks the account up (by the
  domain, say) and returns nothing for a password, `{ sso: 'Okta' }` for
  single sign-on, or a message such as "This account is locked".
- **Step 2, a password**: "Signing in as …" with **Change**, the password
  with Show / Hide, Forgot password? and Sign in. Focus moves to the
  password. The email is also in a hidden field, so a password manager
  fills and saves the right account. `onSignIn` gets the email, Remember
  my email and the password.
- **Step 2, single sign-on**: the title says where the reader is going,
  with a spinner and the email, while your redirect loads. **Use a
  different email** goes back; it cannot stop a redirect that is already
  loading, so it is for when the provider does not answer.
- **Change** and **Use a different email** go back to step 1 with the email
  filled in and focused.
- **Remember my email**: the template does not store anything. Store the
  email when `rememberEmail` is true and pass it back as `defaultEmail`;
  the field then starts filled in and the box ticked.
- **Social buttons**: `providers` puts them above the email on step 1, as
  on Sign In. They are for consumer identities (Google, Microsoft), not a
  company's single sign-on, which the email routes to.
- **When it fails**: `onContinue` and `onSignIn` return (or resolve to) a
  message. It shows above the form and is announced; a wrong password is
  cleared and focused. If they throw or reject, the page says "Something
  went wrong. Try again."

<Canvas of={ProgressiveSignInStories.Password} />

<Canvas of={ProgressiveSignInStories.SingleSignOn} />

## Variants

**Card** (default) and **plain**, and **with a panel** through `aside`,
exactly as on Sign In: they are the Auth Layout's.

<Canvas of={ProgressiveSignInStories.WithProviders} />

## Make it yours

`onContinue` calls your API with the email, which answers with the
account's sign-in method; for single sign-on, start the redirect (to
your identity provider's authorize URL) and return `{ sso }` with its
name for the page to show. Answer the same for an email with no account
as for one with a password, so the page cannot be used to find out who
has an account: the wrong password message then covers both. After
`onSignIn` succeeds, navigate on, or show a second factor.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onContinue` | `(values) => string \| void \| { sso } \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ email, rememberEmail }`. Nothing: the password step. `{ sso: name }`: the single sign-on step. A string: a message above the form. |
| `onSignIn` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ email, rememberEmail, password }`. A returned message shows above the form. |
| `defaultEmail` | `string` | | A remembered email: fills the field and ticks Remember my email. |
| `hasRememberEmail` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows Remember my email. |
| `providers` | `{ id, label, icon? }[]` | `[]` | Social buttons above the email, with an "or" line. |
| `onProviderSelect` | `(id) => void` | | Called with the button's `id`. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | `"Sign in to your account"` | The `h1` of the email and password steps. |
| `forgotPasswordHref` | `string` | `"#forgot-password"` | On the password step. |
| `signUpHref` | `string` | | Shows "No account? Sign up". Leave it out where accounts are by invitation. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the form, outside the card. |

Every other Auth Layout prop passes through.

## Layout

The Auth Layout's, as on [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#layout).
A long email wraps, and Change drops under it; nothing scrolls sideways.

<Canvas of={ProgressiveSignInStories.Phone} />

## Accessibility

- The form is in a `main` landmark, and its one heading is the `h1`.
- Continue replaces the email with the next step, so focus moves on: to
  the password, or to the new `h1` on the single sign-on step, where the
  spinner's "Taking you to …" is a `status`. Change and Use a different
  email put focus back in the email field.
- Change is named "Change email".
- An invalid field has `aria-invalid="true"` and its message as its
  description, and gets focus.
- The message from `onContinue` or `onSignIn` is an `alert`, and the button
  is `aria-busy` while it waits.
- The email for password managers is a `hidden` input: out of the tab order
  and the accessibility tree.

# Project Detail An object page: one project, with a breadcrumb back to the list, a header...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ProjectDetailStories from './ProjectDetail.stories'

<Meta of={ProjectDetailStories} />

# Project Detail

An object page: one project, with a breadcrumb back to the list, a header
with its name, status, key facts and actions, tabs for its sections, and
an aside with its summary and activity. After Tailwind UI's detail
screens, Polaris' details page and Fiori's object page. Built from
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) (its
`aside` column), [Description List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-description-list--docs)
and the kit's Breadcrumbs, Tabs, Table, Menu, Drawer, Tag and Button. It
is the record behind a row of [Projects](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-projects--docs).
The data is made up.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/project-detail-template.json
```

<Canvas of={ProjectDetailStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Breadcrumb**: Projects, then this project as the current page.
- **Header**: the name as the `h1`, the status tag beside it, and the key
  facts under it: PM, timeline, and the team's head count. Edit and a "More actions" menu
  (Archive or Restore) sit at its end.
- **Tabs**: Overview (PM, timeline, estimation) and Team (who works on it, in
  a table).
- **Aside**: the summary (status, health, last update) and
  the activity, newest first, on the [Feed](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-feed--docs) pattern: the same list a
  Projects row expands to.
- **Edit** opens a Drawer with the name, status and estimation. Save
  updates the page, and a status or estimation change joins the top of
  the activity. Cancel, Escape or the close button drops the edit; a
  press on the backdrop does nothing, so a stray click loses nothing. An
  empty name is refused.

<Canvas of={ProjectDetailStories.Edit} />

## Make it yours

`ProjectDetail` takes `project` (a `Project`, see `projects-data.ts`) and
`team` (`TeamMember[]`), and keeps the project in state. Replace the
samples with your data, and the `setProject` calls (Save, Archive) with
calls to your API. Add a tab per section of your record; a long record that reads top
to bottom can drop the tabs and stack its sections instead.

There is no save bar: the page is for reading, and editing happens in the
drawer, which owns its Save and Cancel. A record edited in place, field
by field, is the job of inline edit, not this page.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | `Project` | the first sample project | The record. Read once; later changes are local. |
| `team` | `TeamMember[]` | `sampleTeam` | The Team tab's rows. Empty shows an empty state. |

Any other prop goes to the App Shell's root, e.g. `style` to set its
`block-size` when the page is not the whole viewport.

## Layout

- From 80rem of shell width the aside sits right of the page and each
  scrolls on its own, so the summary stays in view; under 80rem it
  follows the page and the two scroll as one (App Shell). Keep what the
  reader needs first in the page, not the aside.

<Canvas of={ProjectDetailStories.Stacked} />

- The header's actions share the name's row while there is room and drop
  under it when there is not. The status tag wraps under a long name, and
  the key facts wrap one by one.
- A long name with no spaces wraps, in the header and the breadcrumb;
  the page never scrolls sideways. The Team table scrolls inside its own
  frame.

<Canvas of={ProjectDetailStories.Sparse} />

## Accessibility

- One `h1`, the project's name; the Details, Summary and Activity
  headings are `h2`. The breadcrumb is the "Breadcrumb" navigation, its
  last item the current page (`aria-current="page"`).
- The key facts are a list named "Key facts"; a missing PM reads
  "Unassigned" and missing dates "Not scheduled", not an empty slot.
- The aside is a `complementary` landmark named "Project summary", after
  the page in reading and focus order. The activity is a region named
  after the project ("Harbor Lights activity").
- The tab list is named "Project sections"; the Team table's caption is
  "Team", and each member's name is the row header.
- The icon-only menu button is named "More actions". The edit drawer is
  a dialog named "Edit project"; on close, focus returns to Edit. An
  empty name marks the field invalid with the message "Enter a name."

import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ProjectsStories from './Projects.stories'

<Meta of={ProjectsStories} />

# Projects

An index page, or list report: every project in saved views, narrowed by
search and filters, as a table with pages or as a chart. The table sorts,
hides columns, selects rows for a bulk archive and expands to each
project's activity. Built from
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs),
[Saved Views](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-saved-views--docs),
[Filter Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-filter-bar--docs),
[Table Chart Switch](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-table-chart-switch--docs),
[Data Table Page](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-data-table-page--docs)'s
toolbar and footer, and the kit's Table, Column Chooser, Pagination,
BarChart, Search, Menu, Tag, Badge, Avatar and Button. The data is made up.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/projects-template.json
```

<Canvas of={ProjectsStories.Default} />

## Anatomy

From the top: the heading (title, the open count, Import, Export and the
primary action, Add project), the views, the toolbar (search, the Status and Health
filters with their chips, compact rows and Columns), the summary with the
Table / Chart switch, the table, and the footer with the pages.

## What works

- **Views** are predefined (All, Risk, On hold, Potential risk, On track,
  Archived) or saved. A view holds the filters, the columns and the sort;
  the search is not part of it. Each count is the rows the view shows
  with the current search; the view in force counts its unsaved changes
  too, so its count always matches the table.
- **Modified**: a filter, a column or a sort that differs from the view
  marks it modified. Discard puts it back; Save writes it into a saved
  view; on a predefined view, Save as new view keeps it under a new name.
  Manage views deletes saved views.
- **Search** matches the project name and the PM.
- **Filters** are checkbox menus, Status and Health; each choice shows as
  a chip that removes on its own, and Clear all removes them all.
- **Sort** by name, PM, last update, resources, timeline or estimation.
  The sort covers every page, not only the one shown.
- **Pages** of 10, 25 or 50. Any change to what is listed goes back to
  the first page.
- **Chart** shows the estimation of the same projects by status, under
  the same view, search and filters.
- **Selection** turns the toolbar into an Archive action; archived
  projects move to the Archived view. Changing the page, the view, the
  search or a filter clears it, so you never act on rows you cannot see.
- **Clear filters**, in the empty state, clears the search and puts the
  view's own filters back; it does not leave the view.
- **Expand** a row to see its activity: status changes with their note,
  estimation changes, and when it was created.
- **Import** reads a CSV of projects through the [Import
  Export](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-import-export--docs) dialog:
  the headings map to Project name, PM, Status and Estimation, an unknown
  status or an estimation that is not a number skips its row, and the
  rest join the list on track and unscheduled.
- **Export** downloads a CSV of the current view, the selected projects
  or all of them, with the columns on screen ticked; dates are ISO and
  money a bare number, for a spreadsheet to read.
- **Compact rows** switches the table to its small density, and
  **Columns** hides the ones you do not need.

<Canvas of={ProjectsStories.FilterAndSaveView} />

## Make it yours

`Projects` takes `projects` (an array of `Project`, see
`projects-data.ts`) and keeps a copy in state. Replace `sampleProjects`
with your data, the `setProjects` calls (Archive) with calls to your API,
and the `views` state with the views you store per user. With many rows,
filter, sort and page on the server: the page slices locally only because
the sample is small. The activity list is the
[Feed](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-feed--docs) pattern; `ProjectActivity.tsx` turns a project's events into its
sentences, and
[Project Detail](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-project-detail--docs)
shares it.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projects` | `Project[]` | `sampleProjects` | The rows. Read once; later changes are local. |

Any other prop goes to the App Shell's root, e.g. `style` to set its
`block-size` when the page is not the whole viewport.

## Layout

<Canvas of={ProjectsStories.Tablet} />

- The sidebar sits beside the page; below 64rem it is the icon rail, and
  the header comes back with the account (App Shell).
- The heading wraps: Add project drops under the title when there is no
  room beside it.
- The toolbar wraps: on a phone the search takes its own line, and the
  filters and the table settings flow under it.
- The views scroll sideways when they do not fit, instead of wrapping
  onto a second line.
- The table keeps its columns and scrolls inside its own frame; the page
  never scrolls sideways.

<Canvas of={ProjectsStories.Mobile} />

## Accessibility

- One `h1` ("Projects" and the count), a `main` landmark with a skip link,
  and the sidebar as the "Main" navigation (App Shell).
- The views are a tab list named "Project views"; each tab's name
  includes its count ("Risk 3"). "Modified" is a status, announced when
  it appears (Saved Views).
- The filters are a search landmark, "Project filters"; the chips are a
  list, "Applied filters", and removing one moves focus to the next
  (Filter Bar).
- The Table / Chart switch is a second tab list, "Show projects as"; the
  count beside it ("16 projects") is a status, announced as it changes
  (Table Chart Switch).
- The table's caption names the current view ("Risk projects"); the
  project name is each row's header, so the checkbox and the expand button
  are named after it ("Select Harbor Lights", "Expand Harbor Lights").
- The pages are a navigation, "Project pages".
- An expanded row's activity is a region named after the project
  ("Harbor Lights activity"), holding an ordered list, newest first. The
  arrow between a timeline's dates is hidden and read as "to".
- A PM without a name says "Unassigned", and a project without dates says
  "Not scheduled", instead of an empty cell.
- The selection count is announced as it changes (Data Table Page).

'use client'

import { useId, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { Fieldset } from '@base-ui/react/fieldset'
import { Radio } from '@base-ui/react/radio'
import { RadioGroup as BaseRadioGroup } from '@base-ui/react/radio-group'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { choiceStyles, type ValidationState } from './ChoiceField'
import styles from './Radio.module.css'

export interface RadioOption {
  value: string
  label: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  disabled?: boolean
}

export interface RadioGroupProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>
  options: RadioOption[]
  /** The group's legend. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Under the whole group; the error message when `validationState` is error. */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  /** The spec's `onChange`. Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  name?: string
  /** Colour of the selected radio. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'neutral'
  orientation?: 'vertical' | 'horizontal'
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  validationState?: ValidationState
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/**
 * A set of radios, one of which is selected. A radio is meaningless alone —
 * arrow keys move within its group — so the component is the group, with
 * the radios as flat `options`.
 */
export function RadioGroup({
  ref,
  options,
  label,
  helperText,
  name,
  variant = 'neutral',
  orientation = 'vertical',
  disabled,
  required,
  validationState = 'default',
  className,
  onValueChange,
  ...props
}: RadioGroupProps) {
  // Plain help describes the group once. An error message goes through Field,
  // which puts it on every radio: whichever one has focus, the reader hears
  // what is wrong.
  const helperId = useId()
  const isError = validationState === 'error'
  return (
    <Field.Root
      name={name}
      disabled={disabled}
      invalid={isError}
      className={cn(choiceStyles.field, choiceStyles[validationState], styles.field, className)}
    >
      <Fieldset.Root
        render={
          <BaseRadioGroup
            {...props}
            ref={ref}
            aria-describedby={helperText && !isError ? helperId : undefined}
            required={required}
            onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next as string))}
          />
        }
        className={cn(styles.group, styles[orientation])}
      >
        {label && (
          <Fieldset.Legend className={styles.legend}>
            {label}
            {required && (
              <span aria-hidden="true" className={choiceStyles.required}>
                *
              </span>
            )}
          </Fieldset.Legend>
        )}
        {options.map((option) => (
          <Field.Item key={option.value} disabled={option.disabled} className={styles.item}>
            <Field.Label className={choiceStyles.label}>
              <Radio.Root
                value={option.value}
                className={cn(choiceStyles.control, styles.radio, styles[variant])}
              >
                <Radio.Indicator className={styles.dot} />
              </Radio.Root>
              {option.label}
            </Field.Label>
            {option.helperText && (
              <Field.Description className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.optionHelper)}>
                {option.helperText}
              </Field.Description>
            )}
          </Field.Item>
        ))}
      </Fieldset.Root>
      {helperText &&
        (isError ? (
          <Field.Description className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.groupHelper)}>
            {helperText}
          </Field.Description>
        ) : (
          <p id={helperId} className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.groupHelper)}>
            {helperText}
          </p>
        ))}
    </Field.Root>
  )
}

# Radio

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Chooses exactly one option from a short list, all visible at once. The
component is `RadioGroup`.

<Status of={RadioStories} />

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the selected radio; `orientation` lays the
options out in a column or a row.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `neutral` | The default: forms and settings. The selected radio is the foreground colour. |
| `primary` | A choice that carries the brand: a plan picker beside a primary button. |

| Orientation | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `vertical` | The default. Options with helper text, or labels longer than a word or two. |
| `horizontal` | Two to four short labels: sizes, yes or no. The row wraps when narrow. |

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Horizontal} />

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Validation} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { RadioGroup } from 'zweihander/radio'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/radio.json
```

- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/radio](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/radio)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Radio Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/radio), [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) and [Fieldset](https://base-ui.com/react/components/fieldset)
- Figma: not in the library yet

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={RadioStories.Disabled} /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <RadioGroup label="Plan" options={[{ value: 'free', label: 'Free' }, { value: 'pro', label: 'Pro' }]} validationState="error" helperText="Choose a plan." /> },
  ]}
>
  <RadioGroup label="Plan" options={[{ value: 'free', label: 'Free' }, { value: 'pro', label: 'Pro' }]} defaultValue="pro" />
</States>

- **Hover** anywhere on an option's label darkens an unselected ring to
  `--foreground`. The selected radio mixes 12% of the dot's colour into
  its fill, as Button does. An error ring stays red.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the circle.
- **Disabled** dims the radio and its label to 50%, for the whole group
  or one option.
- **Read-only** looks enabled but has no hover and an arrow cursor.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={RadioStories} />
</div>

`className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the group.

### Differences from the spec

- **The component is the group.** The spec describes a single radio, but
  a radio means nothing alone: selection, arrow keys and the single tab
  stop all belong to the group. Following the kit's "flat props"
  convention, the radios are `options` rather than child components.
- **`checked` and `autoFocus` per radio are not props.** The group's
  `value` says which is checked.
- Base UI's `onValueChange` and native `disabled`, `required`,
  `readOnly` names, as on Checkbox.
- **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as selected, so only
  `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship, as on Checkbox.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use radios to choose one option from a short list, when seeing every
option at once helps the choice: a plan, a delivery method, a size. Up to
about six options. Select the usual choice by default when there is one.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={RadioStories.DoFewOptions} />}
  doCaption="A few options, all in view, the usual one already selected."
  dont={<Story of={RadioStories.DontTooMany} />}
  dontCaption="Ten radios are a wall to scan. A long list belongs in a Select or a Combobox."
/>

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Controlled} />

## When not to use

- **For more than about six options, or options that do not fit on
  screen.** Use a Select, or a Combobox when the reader knows what to type.
- **For several choices at once.** Use
  [Checkboxes](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs).
- **For a single on or off.** Use a
  [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs) in a form, or a
  [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs) for a setting
  that applies at once.

## Accessibility

- A `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, exposed as a `radiogroup` named by
  the legend.
- **One tab stop for the group.** Tab enters at the selected radio (or
  the first), arrow keys move and select, Tab leaves. Disabled options
  are skipped.
- Each option's helper text is its own description. Plain group help
  describes the group once; an error message reaches every radio, so
  whichever has focus says what is wrong.
- The unselected outline is `--control-border`, 3:1 on the page.
- A hidden native input carries `name` and `required` into form
  submission and validation.
- 44×44px touch target on each radio on coarse pointers.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

  { token: 'radius-field', label: 'field', note: 'Input, textarea' },
  { token: 'radius-panel', label: 'panel', note: 'Card, dialog' },
] as const

function Intents() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.rowWrap}>
      {INTENTS.map(({ token, label, note }) => (
        <div key={token} style={COL}>
          <div
            style={{
              display: 'flex',
              height: '4rem',
              width: '7rem',
              alignItems: 'center',
              justifyContent: 'center',
              background: 'var(--secondary)',
              color: 'var(--secondary-foreground)',
              fontSize: 'var(--text-body)',
              borderRadius: `var(--${token})`,
            }}
          >
            {label}
          </div>
          <span className={docs.caption}>--{token}</span>
          <span className={docs.caption}>{note}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

const PRESETS: RadiusPreset[] = ['sharp', 'rounded', 'full-rounded']

function PresetRow({ preset }: { preset: RadiusPreset }) {
  return (
    <Theme radius={preset} className={docs.stack}>
      <span className={docs.caption}>radius="{preset}"</span>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', alignItems: 'center', gap: 'var(--space-3)' }}>
        <Button>Button</Button>
        <div style={{ width: '10rem' }}>
          <TextInput aria-label="Input" placeholder="Input" isFullWidth />
        </div>
        <div
          data-panel
          style={{
            border: '1px solid var(--border)',
            background: 'var(--card)',
            color: 'var(--card-foreground)',
            padding: 'var(--space-2) var(--space-4)',
            fontSize: 'var(--text-body)',
            borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)',
          }}
        >
          Panel
        </div>
      </div>
    </Theme>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Radius.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Radius',
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Presets: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.stackWide}>
      {PRESETS.map((preset) => (
        <PresetRow key={preset} preset={preset} />
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const px = (el: Element) => Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).borderRadius)
    const scopeFor = (preset: string) =>
      canvas.getByText(`radius="${preset}"`).parentElement as HTMLElement
    const parts = (preset: string) => {
      const scope = scopeFor(preset)
      return {
        control: px(scope.querySelector('button')!),
        // The field's corner is on the box that draws it, not the bare <input>.
        field: px(scope.querySelector('input')!.parentElement!),
        panel: px(scope.querySelector('[data-panel]')!),
      }
    }

    // sharp flattens everything.
    const sharp = parts('sharp')
    await expect(sharp.control).toBe(0)
    await expect(sharp.field).toBe(0)
    await expect(sharp.panel).toBe(0)

    const rounded = parts('rounded')
    const full = parts('full-rounded')

    // full pills the control...
    await expect(full.control).toBeGreaterThan(1000)
    // ...but a field must never reach a pill. The input is 32px tall, so
    // anything at or above 16px is one.
    await expect(full.field).toBeLessThan(16)
    await expect(full.panel).toBeLessThan(1000)
    // ...and it still has to be a step up from rounded, or "full-rounded"
    // would just be "rounded with a pill button".
    await expect(full.field).toBeGreaterThan(rounded.field)
    await expect(full.panel).toBeGreaterThan(rounded.panel)
  },
}

export const Steps: Story = {
  render: () => <StepScale />,
}

export const Intent: Story = {
  render: () => <Intents />,
}

const SCALES = ['90%', '100%', '110%'] as const

/* A corner that stayed put while the padding shrank would break the nesting
   rule at every scaling but 100%, so the two have to move together. */
export const Scaling: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.row}>
      {SCALES.map((scaling) => (
        <Theme key={scaling} scaling={scaling} className={docs.stack}>
          <Button>{scaling}</Button>
        </Theme>
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const measure = (scaling: string) => {
      const style = getComputedStyle(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: scaling }))
      return { radius: Number.parseFloat(style.borderTopLeftRadius), pad: Number.parseFloat(style.paddingLeft) }
    }
    const base = measure('100%')
    for (const scaling of ['90%', '110%']) {
      const { radius, pad } = measure(scaling)
      await expect(radius / base.radius).toBeCloseTo(pad / base.pad, 2)
      await expect(radius).not.toBe(base.radius)
    }
  },
}

# Radius Rounding is a **single setting**, not a value picked per component. A `radius` pr...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as RadiusStories from './Radius.stories'

<Meta of={RadiusStories} />

# Radius

Rounding is a **single setting**, not a value picked per component. A
`radius` preset on `Theme` rescales everything inside it at once, and
components follow because they reference an *intent* — control, field,
panel — rather than a fixed number.

```tsx
<Theme radius="full-rounded">
  <Button>Pill</Button>
</Theme>
```

## Presets

Three: `sharp`, **`rounded` (the default)**, `full-rounded`. The
default is set by `--radius-factor: 1` and `--radius-full: 0px` on
`:root`, which is exactly what the `rounded` preset writes — so a scope
with no `radius` prop and a scope with `radius="rounded"` are identical.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Presets} />

Look at the `full-rounded` row. **The button becomes a pill; the input and the
panel get rounder but stop short of one.** That is the whole reason this
is a system rather than a number: a fully rounded text field reads as a
search pill in a form that isn't one, and a fully rounded card stops
looking like a container. Only controls opt all the way in.

`sharp` flattens every corner in the scope to `0`, including panels.

## How it works

Two variables do the work, both on `:root`:

| Variable | Default | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--radius` | `0.625rem` | you, for the base step |
| `--radius-factor` | `1` | the `radius` preset |
| `--radius-full` | `0px` | the `radius` preset, only at `full-rounded` |

Every step is the base multiplied by the factor, so the preset scales the
whole scale rather than replacing it:

| Preset | Factor | `--radius-full` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sharp` | `0` | `0px` |
| `rounded` | `1` | `0px` |
| `full-rounded` | `1.5` | `9999px` |

The pill is a `max()`. `--radius-control` resolves to
`max(step, var(--radius-full))` — normally the step wins because
`--radius-full` is `0px`, and at the `full-rounded` preset the `9999px` wins
instead.

Fields and panels use the same shape with a ceiling wrapped around it:

```css
max(step, min(cap, var(--radius-full)))
```

`min(cap, --radius-full)` is `0px` normally and the cap at `full-rounded`, so they
step up with the preset and stop there. Concretely, at the default base:

| Preset | `control` | `field` | `panel` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sharp` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `rounded` | 8px | 8px | 14px |
| `full-rounded` | pill | 15px | 27px |

The default input is 32px tall, so a pill would be 16px. `field` at
`full-rounded` lands under that on purpose, and a test asserts it.

## Three rules

### 1. Radius is tier × intent

A control's corner is not picked per component. Its **size tier** picks
the step, and its **intent** picks what happens at `full-rounded`:

| Tier | Step | Control (pill at `full-rounded`) | Field (stops one step up) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `xs` (20px) | `--radius-sm` | `--control-xs-radius` | `--control-xs-radius-field` |
| `sm` (24px) | `--radius-sm` | `--control-sm-radius` | `--control-sm-radius-field` |
| `md` (32px) | `--radius-md` | `--control-md-radius` = `--radius-control` | `--control-md-radius-field` = `--radius-field` |

{/* docs:check allow --radius-xs -- the paragraph explains why it does not exist */}

The small tiers take the smaller step because the same corner on a box
two thirds the height reads as a pill. There is no `--radius-xs`: `xs`
parts are small enough that `--radius-sm` already reads as soft. See
[Sizing](?path=/docs/foundations-sizing--docs) for which component reads
which tier.

### 2. Nested corners are the outer corner minus the inset

When a rounded thing sits inside another, with an even inset, its corner
is the container's minus that inset, never its own token:

```css
.menu {
  --menu-inset: var(--space-1);
  padding: var(--menu-inset);
  border-radius: var(--radius-field);
}
.menu-item {
  border-radius: calc(var(--radius-field) - var(--menu-inset));
}
```

At the default that is 8 − 4 = 4px for a menu item, and the pills Tabs
chips are their track's corner minus the 2px track inset. A negative
result clamps to 0, so a square container gets square children. Both
corners then stay concentric at every preset; two independent tokens only
line up at one.

The rule is for concentric shapes. A close button 12px inside a popover's
corner is a free-standing control, not a nested shape, and keeps its own
step.

### 3. Radius scales with `--scaling`

Every step is multiplied by `--scaling`, as padding is. At 110% a 32px
button is 35.2px tall with 13.2px padding, and its 8px corner becomes
8.8px. Without this, the nesting rule above would hold at 100% only:
padding would shrink at 90% while the corners stayed put.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Scaling} />

## Always round: `--radius-pill`

`--radius-pill` is `9999px` at every preset. It is for things that are
round by nature, not by preset: a badge count, an avatar, a switch track,
a slider thumb, a spinner. `--radius-full` is the preset's pill switch:
read directly it is `0` everywhere except `radius="full-rounded"`.

## Intent tokens

What components actually use.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Intent} />

| Token | Used by | Pills at `full-rounded` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--radius-control` | the md tier of Button, ToggleButton, Tabs, Pagination | yes |
| `--radius-field` | the md tier of every field, Select and Combobox lists, menus | no |
| `--radius-panel` | Card, Modal, Popover, the date picker | no |

A new component should pick the intent that matches its shape, not a step.
Getting this wrong is invisible at the default preset and only shows up
when someone sets `radius="full-rounded"` — which is exactly the kind of bug a
token system exists to prevent.

## Steps

The raw scale — `--radius-sm` through `--radius-xl` — for anything that is
genuinely decorative rather than a control, field or panel.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Steps} />

These follow the preset like everything else, so a decorative corner in
application code stays in step with the controls beside it.

A genuinely circular element uses `--radius-pill` (see above), not
`--radius-full`.

## Scoping and overriding

Presets nest, and `Theme` takes a `render` prop, so a single component can
opt out without a wrapper element:

```tsx
<Theme radius="full-rounded" render={<Button />}>
  Just this one is a pill
</Theme>
```

For a value the presets don't cover, set the variables directly — `tokens`
is applied after the preset, so it wins:

```tsx
<Theme radius="rounded" tokens={{ 'radius-factor': '2.4' }}>
```

Globally, change the base in CSS and leave the factor to the presets:

```css
:root {
  --radius: 1rem;
}
```

## One caveat about the base

The steps are offsets from the base — `sm` is `base − 4px`, not
`base × 0.6` — so a base far below the default degenerates. At
`--radius: 0.25rem` (4px) the steps are `0 / 2 / 4 / 8px` and `sm`
collapses to a square corner.

The factor does not have this problem, because it multiplies the finished
step. Prefer moving the preset over moving the base, and if the base does
need to change substantially, switch the four `calc()`s in `tokens.css`
from offsets to ratios.
