'use client'

import { useId, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Rating.module.css'

export interface RatingProps {
  /** 0 is unrated. Read-only ratings take fractions, e.g. 4.5. */
  value?: number
  defaultValue?: number
  onValueChange?: (value: number) => void
  max?: number
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Shows a rating rather than asking for one. */
  readOnly?: boolean
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Visible label; the group's name. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** The name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  /** Submitted with a form. */
  name?: string
  /** How each value is spoken, e.g. `(n) => `${n} stars``. */
  getValueText?: (value: number, max: number) => string
  className?: string
}

const defaultText = (value: number, max: number) => `${value} out of ${max} stars`

export function Rating({
  value,
  defaultValue = 0,
  onValueChange,
  max = 5,
  size = 'md',
  readOnly = false,
  disabled = false,
  label,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  name,
  getValueText = defaultText,
  className,
}: RatingProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [state, setState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const current = Math.min(max, Math.max(0, value ?? state))
  const stars = Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => i + 1)
  const classes = cn(styles.rating, styles[size], className)

  // Read-only: one image with the value as its name; stars can be partly filled.
  if (readOnly) {
    return (
      <span className={classes}>
        {label && <span className={styles.label}>{label}</span>}
        <span role="img" aria-label={getValueText(current, max)} className={styles.stars}>
          {stars.map((n) => {
            const fill = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, current - (n - 1)))
            return (
              <span key={n} className={styles.star} aria-hidden="true">
                <Icon name="star" className={styles.empty} />
                <span className={styles.fill} style={{ inlineSize: `${fill * 100}%` }}>
                  <Icon name="star-filled" />
                </span>
              </span>
            )
          })}
        </span>
      </span>
    )
  }

  // Interactive: native radios, so arrows, Tab and form submission are the
  // browser's own. Each radio is visually hidden behind its star.
  return (
    <fieldset className={classes} disabled={disabled} aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}>
      {label && <legend className={styles.label}>{label}</legend>}
      <span className={styles.stars}>
        {stars.map((n) => (
          <label key={n} className={cn(styles.star, n <= current && styles.on)}>
            <input
              type="radio"
              className={styles.input}
              name={name ?? id}
              value={n}
              checked={n === Math.round(current)}
              aria-label={getValueText(n, max)}
              onChange={() => {
                setState(n)
                onValueChange?.(n)
              }}
            />
            <Icon name={n <= current ? 'star-filled' : 'star'} />
          </label>
        ))}
      </span>
    </fieldset>
  )
}

# Rating Asks for, or shows, a score out of a few stars: a review, a template's rating, a ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Rating } from './Rating'
import * as RatingStories from './Rating.stories'

<Meta of={RatingStories} />

# Rating

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Asks for, or shows, a score out of a few stars: a review, a template's
rating, a difficulty.

<Status of={RatingStories} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Default} />

## Variants

A rating either asks for a score or shows one.

| Mode | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Rating label="Interactive" defaultValue={3} /> | Asking: a review form, rating a template. Whole stars only. |
| <Rating readOnly value={4.5} aria-label="Read-only" /> | Showing: an average beside a product. Fractions draw as a star filled part-way. |

<Canvas of={RatingStories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Sizes} />

`getValueText` changes what each score is called, for a scale that is not
stars:

<Canvas of={RatingStories.CustomText} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Rating } from 'zweihander/rating'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/rating.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/Rating.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Rating.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/rating](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/rating)
- Behaviour: native radio buttons; no Base UI part covers it
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={RatingStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={RatingStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Each star is a label over an invisible native radio, so arrows, Tab and
form submission are the browser's own. Read-only drops the radios: the
stars are one image.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[{ part: 'Star', property: 'Size', token: '--space-4' }]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[{ part: 'Star', property: 'Size', token: '--space-6' }]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="lg"
  rows={[{ part: 'Star', property: 'Size', token: '--space-8' }]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Gap above the stars', token: '--space-1-5' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

Stars sit 2px apart, below the spacing scale on purpose, as on Tag. The
label is medium weight.

## Color

<SpecTable
  rows={[
    { part: 'Filled star', property: 'Colour', token: '--warning' },
    { part: 'Empty star', property: 'Colour', token: '--control-border' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

The fill is the bright `--warning` amber, not the darker warning text
colour: a rating reads as a rating when it looks like one. It is 2.1:1 on
white, below the 3:1 a meaningful graphic needs, so colour is not what
carries the score. A filled star differs from the outlined empty one by
shape, and the group or image is named "3 out of 5 stars".

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={RatingStories.Disabled} /> },
    { label: 'Unrated', content: <Story of={RatingStories.Unrated} /> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <Rating readOnly value={3.5} aria-label="Rating" /> },
  ]}
>
  <Rating aria-label="Rating" defaultValue={3} />
</States>

- **Hover** previews the score up to the star under the pointer, and only
  while the rating can be changed.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline round the focused star.
- **Disabled** dims the stars to 50%.
- **Read-only** is one image; fractions fill a star part-way, cut rather
  than shrunk.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={RatingStories} />
</div>

`className` passes through to the group.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a rating to ask for, or show, a quick score on a short scale: a
review, a difficulty, how useful something was. Keep the scale short:
five stars is the convention readers already know.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={RatingStories.DoFiveStars} />}
  doCaption="Five stars: few enough to hit and to tell apart at a glance."
  dont={<Story of={RatingStories.DontTenStars} />}
  dontCaption="Ten stars are small targets, and 7 looks much like 8. Use a Slider or a Number Input for a fine scale."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a precise number.** Use a
  [Slider](?path=/docs/components-controls-slider--docs) or a Number Input.
- **For a choice between named options.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group, so the
  options say what they mean.
- **To show progress.** Use a Progress Bar.

## Accessibility

- Interactive: a `<fieldset>` named by its legend (or `aria-label`), with
  one radio per star named "1 out of 5 stars" and so on (change the words
  with `getValueText`). Arrows move the choice; Tab moves into and out of
  the group.
- Read-only: `role="img"` named with the value, "4.5 out of 5 stars".
- Hover previews the score; focus shows the 2px ring round the star.
- A filled star differs from an empty one by shape as well as colour.
- Stars grow a 44px target on coarse pointers.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useEffect, useId, useRef, useState, type CSSProperties, type KeyboardEvent, type PointerEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Resizable.module.css'

export interface ResizableProps {
  /** The first pane: on the inline start side by side, on top when stacked. The handle sets its size. */
  start: ReactNode
  /** The second pane: it takes the space the first leaves. */
  end: ReactNode
  /** `horizontal` puts the panes side by side, `vertical` stacks them. */
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /** The first pane's size in percent of the whole, for controlled use. Pair with `onSizeChange`. */
  size?: number
  /** The first pane's starting size in percent, when uncontrolled. */
  defaultSize?: number
  /** Called with the first pane's new size in percent while the handle moves. */
  onSizeChange?: (size: number) => void
  /** The first pane's smallest size, in percent. */
  minSize?: number
  /** The first pane's largest size, in percent. */
  maxSize?: number
  /** The handle's accessible name. Name it after the first pane: "Resize filters". */
  handleLabel?: string
  className?: string
  style?: CSSProperties
}

// Table's column resize handle moves 16px a key press too, so both feel alike.
const KEY_STEP = 16

/**
 * Two panes and a handle between them that moves the split, by dragging or
 * with the arrow keys, after the APG window splitter. Nest one in a pane for three.
 */
export function Resizable({
  start,
  end,
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  size,
  defaultSize = 50,
  onSizeChange,
  minSize = 10,
  maxSize = 90,
  handleLabel = 'Resize',
  className,
  style,
}: ResizableProps) {
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const startId = useId()
  const [uncontrolledSize, setUncontrolledSize] = useState(defaultSize)
  const stopDrag = useRef<(() => void) | null>(null)
  useEffect(() => () => stopDrag.current?.(), [])
  const clamp = (v: number) => Math.min(maxSize, Math.max(minSize, v))
  const now = clamp(size ?? uncontrolledSize)
  const isHorizontal = orientation === 'horizontal'

  const setSize = (v: number) => {
    const next = clamp(v)
    // Pressing on against a limit is not a change.
    if (next === now) return
    if (size === undefined) setUncontrolledSize(next)
    onSizeChange?.(next)
  }
  const rootLength = () => {
    const r = rootRef.current!.getBoundingClientRect()
    return (isHorizontal ? r.width : r.height) || 1
  }
  // Side by side in RTL the first pane is on the right, so moving left grows it.
  const sign = () => (isHorizontal && getComputedStyle(rootRef.current!).direction === 'rtl' ? -1 : 1)
  const toPercent = (px: number) => (px * 100) / rootLength()

  // Window listeners, not pointer capture: the move keeps tracking past
  // the handle, and synthetic test pointers need no active pointer id.
  const onPointerDown = (e: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (e.button !== 0) return
    e.preventDefault()
    const from = now
    const at = isHorizontal ? e.clientX : e.clientY
    const s = sign()
    const move = (m: globalThis.PointerEvent) => setSize(from + s * toPercent((isHorizontal ? m.clientX : m.clientY) - at))
    const stop = () => {
      window.removeEventListener('pointermove', move)
      window.removeEventListener('pointerup', stop)
      window.removeEventListener('pointercancel', stop)
      stopDrag.current = null
    }
    stopDrag.current = stop
    window.addEventListener('pointermove', move)
    window.addEventListener('pointerup', stop)
    window.addEventListener('pointercancel', stop)
  }

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const keys: Record<string, number> = isHorizontal ? { ArrowRight: 1, ArrowLeft: -1 } : { ArrowDown: 1, ArrowUp: -1 }
    const dir = keys[e.key]
    const next = dir !== undefined ? now + sign() * dir * toPercent(KEY_STEP) : e.key === 'Home' ? minSize : e.key === 'End' ? maxSize : undefined
    if (next === undefined) return
    e.preventDefault()
    setSize(next)
  }

  return (
    <div
      ref={rootRef}
      className={cn(styles.root, !isHorizontal && styles.vertical, className)}
      style={{ ...style, '--resizable-size': `${now}%` } as CSSProperties}
    >
      <div id={startId} className={styles.pane}>
        {start}
      </div>
      <div
        role="separator"
        aria-orientation={isHorizontal ? 'vertical' : 'horizontal'}
        aria-label={handleLabel}
        aria-controls={startId}
        aria-valuenow={Math.round(now)}
        aria-valuemin={minSize}
        aria-valuemax={maxSize}
        tabIndex={0}
        className={styles.handle}
        onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
        onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
      />
      <div className={cn(styles.pane, styles.end)}>{end}</div>
    </div>
  )
}

./src/components/data-display/Resizable.mdx
# Resizable Two panes split by a handle that people drag, or move with the arrow keys, to ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Resizable } from './Resizable'
import * as ResizableStories from './Resizable.stories'

<Meta of={ResizableStories} />

# Resizable

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Two panes split by a handle that people drag, or move with the arrow keys,
to give one pane more room: a list beside its detail, a query above its
results.

<Status of={ResizableStories} />

Resizable is outside the 1.0 component list, so it starts as experimental.

<Canvas of={ResizableStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Orientation | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `horizontal` (default) | Panes side by side: a list and the record picked from it, a file tree and the file. |
| `vertical` | Panes stacked: an editor over its output, a chart over its table. |

<Canvas of={ResizableStories.Vertical} />

`minSize` and `maxSize` keep the first pane between two sizes, in percent
of the whole, so neither pane can be dragged out of sight.

<Canvas of={ResizableStories.Limits} />

For three panes, put a Resizable in a pane of another.

<Canvas of={ResizableStories.DoNameEachHandle} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Resizable } from 'zweihander/resizable'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/resizable.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Resizable.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Resizable.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; after [shadcn/ui Resizable](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/resizable) and the [APG window splitter](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/)
- Base UI: none; Base UI has no splitter
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ResizableStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ResizableStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The limits, `minSize` and `maxSize`, have no element of their own: they
are where the handle stops.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Every orientation"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Hit area across the line', token: '--box-sm' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Line on hover and drag', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Focus outline offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

The line is 1px; its hit area reaches past it on both sides, and grows
to 44px on touch screens without the line getting wider. The panes have no padding of their own: what goes in
them sets it. Sizes are percentages of the whole, so the split holds
when the window changes size.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Handle"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Line', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Line on hover and drag', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Focus outline', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Dragging', pseudo: 'active' },
  ]}
>
  <div style={{ blockSize: 80, inlineSize: 160, border: '1px solid var(--border)' }}>
    <Resizable start={null} end={null} />
  </div>
</States>

- **Hover** and **Dragging** thicken the line to 2px `--primary`, as on
  Table's column resize handle. The cursor turns to a resize arrow.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the line.
- There is no disabled state: a split that should not move is two plain
  boxes.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ResizableStories} />
</div>

Resizable fills its parent: give the parent a height for side-by-side
panes, and both a height for stacked ones.

### Differences from the spec

shadcn's Resizable is a group of any number of panels and handles
(`ResizablePanelGroup`, `ResizablePanel`, `ResizableHandle`). Zweihänder
takes flat props and two panes, `start` and `end`, as its API conventions
ask; nest one for three panes. There is no collapse on Enter and no saved
layout: store `onSizeChange` to keep the split.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Resizable where people need to trade room between two things they
look at together, and the right split depends on the content: a long name
in a list, a wide table in the detail.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ResizableStories.DoNameEachHandle} />}
  doCaption="Each handle is named after the pane it sizes: “Resize folders”, “Resize inbox”."
  dont={<Story of={ResizableStories.DontKeepDefaultName} />}
  dontCaption="Both handles keep the default name, so a screen reader hears “Resize” twice and cannot tell them apart."
/>

Keep `minSize` above zero (the default is 10%), so a pane cannot be
dragged out of sight with its content still in the tab order.

## When not to use

- **For a fixed sidebar beside the page.** Use the App Shell template:
  its Nav Sidebar has a set width and collapses.
- **For a panel that slides over the page.** Use Drawer.
- **For a column of a table.** Use Table's `isResizable`.
- **For layouts that only change with the window.** Use the
  Multi-column layout template: Resizable is for people, not
  breakpoints.

## Accessibility

- The handle is a focusable `role="separator"`, after the APG window
  splitter. Side by side it is `aria-orientation="vertical"`; stacked it
  is `"horizontal"`.
- Its name is `handleLabel` and `aria-controls` points at the first pane.
- `aria-valuenow` is the first pane's size in percent, between
  `aria-valuemin` (`minSize`) and `aria-valuemax` (`maxSize`).
- Side by side, Arrow Right moves the handle 16px right and Arrow Left
  16px left; in right-to-left text the first pane is on the right, so
  Arrow Left grows it. Stacked, Arrow Down and Arrow Up do the same.
  Home moves it to `minSize`, End to `maxSize`. These are the keys and
  the step of Table's column resize handle.
- Dragging the handle moves it by the distance dragged, never past the
  limits.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useEffect, useId, useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState, type ComponentProps, type FormEvent } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Badge } from '../../atomic-elements/Badge'
import { Tag } from '../../atomic-elements/Tag'
import { Button } from '../../buttons/Button'
import { Checkbox } from '../../controls/Checkbox'
import { TextInput } from '../../inputs/TextInput'
import { Menu, type MenuEntry } from '../../navigation/Menu'
import { Tabs } from '../../navigation/Tabs'
import { Modal, ModalClose } from '../../overlays/Modal'
import styles from './SavedViews.module.css'

export interface SavedView {
  id: string
  label: string
  /** Rows the view holds, shown next to its name. */
  count?: number
  /** Shipped with the product: it can be picked and copied, not saved over or deleted. */
  isPredefined?: boolean
  /** Shared with others; Manage views says so. */
  isShared?: boolean
}

export interface NewView {
  label: string
  isShared: boolean
}

export interface SavedViewsProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  views: SavedView[]
  /** The id of the view in force. */
  value: string
  onValueChange: (id: string) => void
  /** `tabs` for a handful of views; `menu` for more than fit on one line. */
  display?: 'tabs' | 'menu'
  /** The filters, sort or columns now differ from the view as saved. */
  isModified?: boolean
  /** Saves the changes into the view in force. Not offered on a predefined view. */
  onSave?: () => void
  /** Drops the changes and goes back to the view as saved. */
  onDiscard?: () => void
  /** Saves the current state as a new view. Shows Save as new view. */
  onSaveAs?: (view: NewView) => void
  /** Offers "Share with everyone" when saving a new view. */
  isShareable?: boolean
  /** Deletes a view that is not predefined. Shows Manage views. */
  onDelete?: (id: string) => void
}

/**
 * The views of a list or table, predefined and saved, with a mark when the
 * view in force has changed, Save, Save as new view and Manage views. The
 * pattern owns no views: it renders the list you keep and reports changes.
 */
export function SavedViews({
  views,
  value,
  onValueChange,
  display = 'tabs',
  isModified = false,
  onSave,
  onDiscard,
  onSaveAs,
  isShareable = false,
  onDelete,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Views',
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: SavedViewsProps) {
  const [dialog, setDialog] = useState<'save-as' | 'manage' | null>(null)
  // Menu radio items keep the menu open; picking a view should close it.
  const [isMenuOpen, setIsMenuOpen] = useState(false)
  const active = views.find((v) => v.id === value)
  const canSave = !!onSave && !!active && !active.isPredefined

  // Save, Discard and Save as new view unmount the button that was pressed
  // (or that the dialog would hand focus back to): send focus to the view in
  // force once the change has landed, instead of dropping it on the page.
  const barRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const refocus = useRef(false)
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!refocus.current || isModified || dialog) return
    refocus.current = false
    barRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"], [aria-haspopup="menu"]')?.focus()
  }, [isModified, dialog, value])
  const thenRefocus = (action: () => void) => () => {
    refocus.current = true
    action()
  }

  const countBadge = (view: SavedView) =>
    view.count !== undefined && <Badge count={view.count} size="sm" variant="secondary" />

  const viewActions: MenuEntry[] = [
    ...(onSaveAs ? [{ label: 'Save as new view…', onSelect: () => setDialog('save-as') }] : []),
    ...(onDelete ? [{ label: 'Manage views…', onSelect: () => setDialog('manage') }] : []),
  ]

  return (
    <div
      ref={(node) => {
        barRef.current = node
        if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(node)
        else if (ref) ref.current = node
      }}
      className={cn(styles.bar, className)} {...props}>
      {display === 'tabs' ? (
        <Tabs
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          className={styles.views}
          value={value}
          onValueChange={onValueChange}
          items={views.map((view) => ({
            value: view.id,
            label: (
              <>
                {view.label} {countBadge(view)}
              </>
            ),
          }))}
        />
      ) : (
        <Menu
          align="start"
          open={isMenuOpen}
          onOpenChange={setIsMenuOpen}
          trigger={
            <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" endIcon={<Icon name="chevron-down" />} className={styles.trigger}>
              <span className={styles.srOnly}>{ariaLabel}: </span>
              <span className={styles.name}>{active?.label ?? ariaLabel}</span>
            </Button>
          }
          items={[
            {
              type: 'radio',
              label: ariaLabel,
              value,
              onValueChange: (id) => {
                onValueChange(id)
                setIsMenuOpen(false)
              },
              options: views.map((view) => ({
                value: view.id,
                label: (
                  <span className={styles.option}>
                    {view.label} {countBadge(view)}
                  </span>
                ),
              })),
            },
          ]}
        />
      )}
      <div className={styles.actions}>
        {/* Always rendered, so the mark is announced when it appears. */}
        <span role="status" className={styles.modified}>
          {isModified && 'Modified'}
        </span>
        {isModified && onDiscard && (
          <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" onClick={thenRefocus(onDiscard)}>
            Discard
          </Button>
        )}
        {isModified && canSave && (
          <Button variant="secondary" appearance="outlined" onClick={thenRefocus(onSave!)}>
            Save
          </Button>
        )}
        {isModified && !canSave && onSaveAs && (
          <Button variant="secondary" appearance="outlined" onClick={() => setDialog('save-as')}>
            Save as new view
          </Button>
        )}
        {viewActions.length > 0 && (
          <Menu
            align="end"
            trigger={
              <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" isIconOnly aria-label="View actions">
                <Icon name="more" />
              </Button>
            }
            items={viewActions}
          />
        )}
      </div>
      {onSaveAs && (
        <SaveAsDialog
          open={dialog === 'save-as'}
          onOpenChange={(open) => setDialog(open ? 'save-as' : null)}
          taken={views.map((v) => v.label)}
          isShareable={isShareable}
          onSave={(view) => {
            refocus.current = true
            onSaveAs(view)
            setDialog(null)
          }}
        />
      )}
      {onDelete && (
        <ManageDialog
          open={dialog === 'manage'}
          onOpenChange={(open) => setDialog(open ? 'manage' : null)}
          views={views}
          label={ariaLabel}
          onDelete={onDelete}
        />
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

interface DialogProps {
  open: boolean
  onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void
}

function SaveAsDialog({
  open,
  onOpenChange,
  taken,
  isShareable,
  onSave,
}: DialogProps & { taken: string[]; isShareable: boolean; onSave: (view: NewView) => void }) {
  const formId = useId()
  const nameRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  const [label, setLabel] = useState('')
  const [isShared, setIsShared] = useState(false)
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)

  // A fresh form each time it opens.
  const [wasOpen, setWasOpen] = useState(open)
  if (open !== wasOpen) {
    setWasOpen(open)
    if (open) {
      setLabel('')
      setIsShared(false)
      setError(null)
    }
  }

  const submit = (event: FormEvent) => {
    event.preventDefault()
    const name = label.trim()
    if (!name) return setError('Enter a name for the view.')
    if (taken.some((t) => t.trim().toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase())) return setError('A view with this name already exists.')
    onSave({ label: name, isShared })
  }

  return (
    <Modal
      size="sm"
      title="Save as new view"
      description="Saves the current filters, sort and columns under a new name."
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      initialFocus={nameRef}
      footer={
        <>
          <ModalClose render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Cancel</ModalClose>
          <Button type="submit" form={formId}>
            Save view
          </Button>
        </>
      }
    >
      <form id={formId} noValidate onSubmit={submit} className={styles.form}>
        <TextInput
          ref={nameRef}
          label="View name"
          required
          isFullWidth
          value={label}
          onChange={(e) => {
            setLabel(e.target.value)
            setError(null)
          }}
          validationState={error ? 'error' : 'default'}
          helperText={error ?? undefined}
        />
        {isShareable && <Checkbox label="Share with everyone" checked={isShared} onCheckedChange={setIsShared} />}
      </form>
    </Modal>
  )
}

function ManageDialog({
  open,
  onOpenChange,
  views,
  label,
  onDelete,
}: DialogProps & { views: SavedView[]; label: string; onDelete: (id: string) => void }) {
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLUListElement>(null)
  const closeRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)
  // Deleting unmounts the focused button: hand focus to the next delete
  // button, or the one before, once the view has left `views`; with none
  // left, to Done.
  const pending = useRef<{ index: number; id: string } | null>(null)
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const p = pending.current
    if (!p || views.some((v) => v.id === p.id)) return
    pending.current = null
    const buttons = listRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('button') ?? []
    ;(buttons[Math.min(p.index, buttons.length - 1)] ?? closeRef.current)?.focus()
  }, [views])

  const own = views.filter((v) => !v.isPredefined)
  return (
    <Modal
      size="sm"
      title="Manage views"
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={(next) => {
        // A delete the app declined must not move focus later on.
        pending.current = null
        onOpenChange(next)
      }}
      footer={
        <ModalClose ref={closeRef} render={<Button />}>
          Done
        </ModalClose>
      }
    >
      <ul ref={listRef} aria-label={label} className={styles.manage}>
        {views.map((view) => (
          <li key={view.id}>
            <span className={styles.name}>{view.label}</span>
            {view.isPredefined && <Tag text="Predefined" variant="neutral" size="sm" />}
            {view.isShared && <Tag text="Shared" variant="neutral" size="sm" />}
            {!view.isPredefined && (
              <Button
                variant="destructive"
                appearance="ghost"
                aria-label={`Delete ${view.label}`}
                className={styles.delete}
                onClick={() => {
                  pending.current = { index: own.indexOf(view), id: view.id }
                  onDelete(view.id)
                }}
              >
                Delete
              </Button>
            )}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </Modal>
  )
}

# Saved Views The views of a list or table, the ones that ship with the product and the on...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SavedViewsStories from './SavedViews.stories'

<Meta of={SavedViewsStories} />

# Saved Views

The views of a list or table, the ones that ship with the product and the
ones people save, with a mark when the view in force has changed, Save,
Save as new view and Manage views. After SAP Fiori variant management
(List Report, Worklist) and Polaris Index filters.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/saved-views.json
```

The pattern owns no views: it renders the `views` you keep and calls you
back. What a view holds (filters, sort, columns) is yours to store; compare
it with what is on screen and pass `isModified`. Picking another view puts
that view's saved state in force and drops unsaved changes, as in Fiori:
Modified, beside the views, is the warning.

## Tabs

For a handful of views. Each tab can carry a count. Put it above a
[Filter Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-filter-bar--docs): picking
a view puts its filters in force there.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.Default} />

## Modified

Change a filter and the view says Modified, with Discard and Save. Save
writes the change into the view in force.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.Modified} />

## Save as new view

A predefined view cannot be saved over, so a change offers Save as new view
in place of Save; it is also always in View actions. The dialog asks for a
name, refuses an empty or taken one, and with `isShareable` offers to share
the view.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.SaveAsNewView} />

## Manage views

In View actions when you pass `onDelete`. It lists every view, marks the
predefined and shared ones, and deletes saved ones at once: pair it with an
Undo toast if a view is costly to rebuild. Deleting the view in force is
yours to handle: put another view in force, usually the first. There is no
rename or unshare yet: save a copy under the new name, then delete the old
one.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.ManageViews} />

## Menu

For more views than fit on one line: a button names the view in force and
opens the views as a menu.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.AsMenu} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={SavedViewsStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **One row** while there is room: the views take the free space, the
  actions sit at the end.
- **The actions drop under the views** when the row is too narrow, rather
  than squeeze the tabs.
- **More tabs than fit scroll sideways** inside the bar; nothing widens the
  page. Past five or six views, use `display="menu"`.
- In menu display a long view name truncates with an ellipsis.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- In tabs display the views are a tab list named "Views" (Manage views'
  list takes the same name); pass
  `aria-label` to say what they list, e.g. "Invoice views". Each tab's name
  includes its count.
- In menu display the button's name says the list and the view in force,
  e.g. "Invoice views: All"; the views are radio items in the menu.
- Modified sits in a `status` region, so a screen reader announces it when
  a change makes the view differ from what is saved.
- Save as new view moves focus to the name field. A missing or taken name
  marks the field invalid and names the problem in its description.
- Manage views: each delete button is named after its view, e.g. "Delete
  To chase". Deleting one moves focus to the next delete button, or the one
  before, or to Done when none is left.
- Save, Discard and Save as new view take away the button that was
  pressed; focus moves to the view in force.

'use client'

import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type ChangeEvent, type ComponentProps, type KeyboardEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { Kbd } from '../atomic-elements/Kbd'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  assignRef,
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
} from './InputField'
import styles from './Search.module.css'

export interface SearchProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'input'>, 'size' | 'type' | 'value' | 'defaultValue'> {
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  /** A visible label. Without one the field is named by `aria-label` ("Search" by default). */
  label?: ReactNode
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /**
   * One key, e.g. `/`, that focuses the field from anywhere on the page.
   * No modifiers: ⌘K belongs to the Command Palette. One per page.
   */
  shortcut?: string
}

// Focus is in a form field: the key belongs to it, not to us.
const isInField = (el: EventTarget | null) =>
  el instanceof HTMLElement && (el.isContentEditable || el.matches('input, textarea, select'))

export function Search({
  value,
  defaultValue = '',
  label,
  placeholder = 'Search',
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  shortcut,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  onChange,
  onKeyDown,
  className,
  ref,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  ...props
}: SearchProps) {
  const input = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null)
  // Only to know whether to show the clear button; the input stays the
  // source of truth for an uncontrolled field.
  const [uncontrolled, setUncontrolled] = useState(defaultValue)
  const current = value ?? uncontrolled
  const canClear = current !== '' && !disabled && !readOnly

  // Disabled or read-only, the field has nothing to type into.
  const key = disabled || readOnly ? undefined : shortcut

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!key) return
    const onKey = (e: globalThis.KeyboardEvent) => {
      // Case-blind, as Command Palette's hotkey, so Caps Lock does not matter.
      if (e.key.toLowerCase() !== key.toLowerCase() || e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.altKey || e.repeat || e.isComposing) return
      if (e.defaultPrevented || isInField(e.target)) return
      // Or the key would be typed into the field, and Firefox's quick find takes `/`.
      e.preventDefault()
      input.current?.focus()
    }
    document.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
    return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
  }, [key])

  const clear = () => {
    const el = input.current
    if (!el) return
    // Set the value the way typing would, so onChange receives a real event
    // whether the field is controlled or not.
    Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value')!.set!.call(el, '')
    el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }))
    // The button unmounts once the field is empty; hand keyboard focus back
    // to the input rather than losing it. A pointer press never focuses the
    // button (see onMouseDown), so an idle field stays idle.
    if (document.activeElement?.tagName === 'BUTTON') el.focus()
  }

  return (
    <InputField label={label} disabled={disabled} isFullWidth={isFullWidth} className={className}>
      <span className={boxClass(size)} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
        <span className={inputStyles.affix}>
          <Icon name="search" />
        </span>
        <Field.Control
          {...props}
          ref={(node: HTMLInputElement | null) => {
            input.current = node
            assignRef(ref, node)
          }}
          type="search"
          value={value}
          defaultValue={value === undefined ? defaultValue : undefined}
          placeholder={placeholder}
          disabled={disabled}
          readOnly={readOnly}
          aria-label={label ? ariaLabel : (ariaLabel ?? 'Search')}
          aria-keyshortcuts={key}
          onChange={(event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
            setUncontrolled(event.target.value)
            onChange?.(event)
          }}
          onKeyDown={(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
            onKeyDown?.(event)
            // Firefox does not clear a search field on Escape; Chrome and
            // Safari do. Doing it here makes them all agree.
            if (event.key === 'Escape' && canClear && !event.defaultPrevented) {
              event.preventDefault()
              clear()
            }
          }}
          className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.input)}
        />
        {/* Where the clear button goes: the two never show at once. */}
        {key && current === '' && (
          <Kbd size={size} aria-hidden="true" className={styles.shortcut}>
            {key}
          </Kbd>
        )}
        {canClear && (
          <button
            type="button"
            aria-label="Clear search"
            className={inputStyles.iconButton}
            // Keep focus where it is: a focused field stays focused, an idle one stays idle.
            onMouseDown={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
            onClick={clear}
          >
            <Icon name="clear" />
          </button>
        )}
      </span>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Search A field for a search query, with a button to clear it and, optionally, a key that...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Search } from './Search'
import * as SearchStories from './Search.stories'

<Meta of={SearchStories} />

# Search

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A field for a search query, with a button to clear it and, optionally, a
key that focuses it. The field is
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s. It searches
one place: a list, a table, a results page. Finding anything from anywhere
is the [Command Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-commandpalette--docs).

<Status of={SearchStories} />

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Clear} />

## Variants

One appearance, the white outlined box, in two sizes, with or without a
visible label.

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Above a list or a page of results: the default. |
| `sm` | Toolbars and table headers, beside `sm` buttons. |

<Canvas of={SearchStories.WithLabel} />

| Label | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| None (default) | A search box whose place makes its purpose plain: a page header, above a list. It is named "Search", or by `aria-label`. |
| `label` | A search inside a form, among other labelled fields. |

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Shortcut} />

| Shortcut | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| None (default) | Most fields. |
| `shortcut="/"` | The one search a page is about, such as a list page's [Filter Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-filterbar--docs). The key cap shows while the field is empty and idle. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Search } from 'zweihander/search'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/search.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/Search.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Search.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/search](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/search)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SearchStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SearchStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The placeholder is the input's, "Search" unless given. The browser's own
clear control is hidden, so there are not two. Not numbered above: with `shortcut`, a
[Kbd](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-kbd--docs) key cap of the
field's size sits where the clear button goes, while the field is empty and
not focused; the two never show at once.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier, as on Text Input. The search icon and the
clear button both take the tier's icon size.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Search icon and clear button', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-sm' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-md-gap' },
    { part: 'Search icon and clear button', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Clear button', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Clear button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

20rem wide, capped at its container, or the container's width with
`isFullWidth`.

## Color

Search has no validation state; its field colours are Text Input's
default ones.

<SpecTable
  caption="default"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--field-border' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-2xs' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Placeholder and search icon', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Clear button', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Clear button, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Read-only" rows={[{ part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--surface-filled' }]} />

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Empty' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'With a query', content: <Search defaultValue="tooltip" /> },
    { label: 'Clear hover', pseudo: 'hover', content: <Search defaultValue="tooltip" /> },
    { label: 'With a shortcut', content: <Search shortcut="/" /> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <Search defaultValue="tooltip" readOnly /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Search defaultValue="tooltip" disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <Search />
</States>

- **The clear button** appears once there is a query, and not while the
  field is disabled or read-only. On hover its icon darkens to
  `--foreground`.
- **Focus** is the field's 2px `--ring` outline around the box, on click
  as well as keyboard. The clear button, when tabbed to, draws its own
  ring instead, so the two never double.
- **The shortcut's key cap** shows while the field is empty and hides on
  focus, when the key would type instead. Disabled or read-only, there is
  no key cap and the key is not bound.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--surface-filled`.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SearchStories} />
</div>

Every other `<input>` attribute passes through, including `ref`, `name`,
`autoFocus` and `onKeyDown`. `type` is always `search`.

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`label` and `size` are added**, from the shared field,
  so a search box can match the form or toolbar it sits in.
- **`value` is added** for a controlled query.
- **`shortcut` is added**, a single key that focuses the field.
- **No suggestion panel.** Recent searches and results grouped by type, as the
  spec's global search shows them, are the
  [Command Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-commandpalette--docs)'s
  job; picking one value from matches is the
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs)'s. Search stays a
  field, so there are not three lists that behave alike.
- Native `disabled`, `readOnly` names.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Search to find or filter: a list of components, a table, the whole
site. Say in the placeholder what is searched.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SearchStories.DoSaySearchWhat} />}
  doCaption="A Search field: a searchbox to assistive tech, with a clear button and Escape to clear."
  dont={<Story of={SearchStories.DontTextInputWithIcon} />}
  dontCaption="A Text Input with a search icon looks the same but is a plain textbox, with no way to clear it."
/>

When it searches the site, put it inside a `<form role="search">` (or
`<search>`) so it becomes a landmark people can jump to. The component is
only the field: filtering a list in place does not need a landmark.

Above a list page, Search goes in the
[Filter Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-filterbar--docs)'s `search`
slot, which is already the `role="search"` landmark. Give the page's main
search `shortcut="/"`, and only that one.

## When not to use

- **To find anything from anywhere in the app**, with recent items and
  results grouped by type. Use the
  [Command Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-commandpalette--docs),
  opened with ⌘K or from a search button. Do not bind ⌘K to a Search.

- **To choose one value from a list.** Use a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs): it shows the
  matches and keeps the choice.
- **For other free text.** Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs).

## Accessibility

- `type="search"`, exposed as a `searchbox`, named by the visible label
  or "Search". A placeholder is not a name.
- **Clearing works the same everywhere:** the button, and Escape in the
  field (Chrome and Safari do this natively; Firefox did not). Either way
  `onChange` fires with a real event.
- The clear button is a real `<button>` named "Clear search", reached
  with Tab after the input. Pressed from the keyboard, it hands focus
  back to the field instead of losing it; a mouse press leaves focus
  where it was.
- The clear button's hit area grows to 44px on touch screens.
- The search icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers.
- **`shortcut`** focuses the field from anywhere on the page, without typing
  the key. It does nothing while focus is in a form field, or with ⌘,
  Ctrl or Alt held, or while the field is disabled or read-only. The input carries `aria-keyshortcuts`; the key cap is
  hidden from screen readers so the key is not read twice.
- The edge is the light `--field-border`, the approved exception to WCAG
  1.4.11 described on Text Input.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Select as BaseSelect } from '@base-ui/react/select'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  popupInset,
  inputStyles as s,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'

export type SelectOption = string | { value: string; label: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }

/** Strings are their own label; objects carry one. */
export function normalizeOptions(options: SelectOption[]) {
  return options.map((o) => (typeof o === 'string' ? { value: o, label: o as ReactNode } : o))
}

export interface SelectProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>
  options: SelectOption[]
  value?: string | null
  defaultValue?: string | null
  /** The spec's `onChange`. `null` when nothing is selected. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string | null) => void
  placeholder?: string
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Options are still arriving: a spinner replaces the chevron. */
  isLoading?: boolean
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  autoFocus?: boolean
  id?: string
  /** Where the popup renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen or a scope with its own density. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

export function Select({
  ref,
  options,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  placeholder,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  isLoading,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  autoFocus,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: SelectProps) {
  const items = normalizeOptions(options)
  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      hasButtonControl
      className={className}
    >
      <BaseSelect.Root
        items={items}
        value={value}
        defaultValue={defaultValue}
        onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next as string | null))}
        readOnly={readOnly}
        required={required}
      >
        <BaseSelect.Trigger
          ref={ref}
          id={id}
          autoFocus={autoFocus}
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          aria-busy={isLoading || undefined}
          className={cn(boxClass(size), s.trigger)}
        >
          <BaseSelect.Value className={s.value} placeholder={placeholder} />
          {isLoading ? (
            <span className={cn(s.icon, s.spinner)} aria-hidden="true" />
          ) : (
            <BaseSelect.Icon className={s.icon}>
              <Icon name="chevron-down" />
            </BaseSelect.Icon>
          )}
        </BaseSelect.Trigger>
        <BaseSelect.Portal container={container}>
          {/* Opens below the field like a list, rather than laid over it
              with the selected option aligned to the trigger. */}
          <BaseSelect.Positioner className={s.positioner} sideOffset={4} alignItemWithTrigger={false}>
            <BaseSelect.Popup className={s.popup} style={popupInset(size)}>
              <BaseSelect.List>
                {items.map((item) => (
                  <BaseSelect.Item key={item.value} value={item.value} disabled={item.disabled} className={s.option}>
                    <BaseSelect.ItemText>{item.label}</BaseSelect.ItemText>
                    <BaseSelect.ItemIndicator className={s.check}>
                      <Icon name="check" />
                    </BaseSelect.ItemIndicator>
                  </BaseSelect.Item>
                ))}
              </BaseSelect.List>
            </BaseSelect.Popup>
          </BaseSelect.Positioner>
        </BaseSelect.Portal>
      </BaseSelect.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Select Chooses one option from a list that opens below the field. The field is [Text Inp...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

# Select

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Chooses one option from a list that opens below the field. The field is
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s.

<Status of={SelectStories} />

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Default} />

## Variants

One appearance, the white outlined box. What changes is the size and the
validation state.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and dialogs: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: toolbars, table filters. The list keeps 32px options. |

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Validation} />

| Validation state | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Before anything is checked. |
| `error` | Nothing chosen where a choice is required, or a choice that cannot be accepted. `helperText` says which. |
| `success` | Rare: a choice checked and accepted elsewhere. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Select } from 'zweihander/select'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/select.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/Select.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Select.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/select](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/select)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Select](https://base-ui.com/react/components/select)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SelectStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SelectStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The **options list** opens below the field, 4px away, at least as wide as
the field. It renders in a portal at the end of `<body>`, so it is not
marked above. Each **option** is inset by the field's own padding, so its
text starts where the field's text does; the chosen one has a check
before its label, in the brand colour. Open the list in the example at
the top of Overview to see it.

Each size is a control tier, as on Text Input.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Chosen', content: <Select label="Priority" options={['Low', 'High']} defaultValue="High" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Select label="Priority" options={['Low', 'High']} placeholder="Choose" validationState="error" helperText="Choose one." required /> },
    { label: 'Loading', content: <Select label="Priority" options={[]} placeholder="Choose" isLoading /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Select label="Priority" options={['Low', 'High']} defaultValue="Low" disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <Select label="Priority" options={['Low', 'High']} placeholder="Choose" />
</States>

- **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the cursor turns to the button cursor.
- **Focus** is the field's 2px `--ring` outline, shown from the keyboard,
  and kept while the list is open: focus moves into the list, but the
  field is still the one being chosen for.
- **Highlighted option** is where the arrow keys or the pointer are:
  `--accent` behind it. Disabled options are dimmed to 60% and skipped.
- **Loading** swaps the chevron for a spinner in the same place.
- **Read-only** fills the field with `--surface-filled`.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SelectStories} />
</div>

`ref` goes to the field's button. `id` and `className` are passed through
too; no other attributes are.

### Differences from the spec

- **Outlined only.** The spec's filled, underlined and unstyled appearances were dropped to match the Claude apps, where every select is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`onValueChange` with the value**, Base UI's name, instead of
  `onChange`.
- **Native names** for `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`.
- **Options are strings or `{ value, label }` objects.** A bare component
  is not an option: an option needs a value to submit and compare, so a
  component goes in `label`.
- **The list opens below the field** instead of Base UI's default of
  laying it over the trigger with the selected option aligned: the
  spec's anatomy shows a list below.
- **The field keeps its focus ring while the list is open.** Focus moves
  into the list, but the field is still the one being filled.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Select to choose one option from five to about fifteen, when the
choices do not need to be compared side by side: a priority, a country
among a short list, a team member.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SelectStories.DoAHandful} />}
  doCaption="A handful of options, chosen once and then out of the way."
  dont={<Story of={SelectStories.DontTwoOptions} />}
  dontCaption="Two options hidden behind a click. A Switch or two radios show both at once."
/>

Give it a placeholder that says what to choose, and order the options in
a way people expect: by size or frequency, or alphabetically for names.

## When not to use

- **Two to four options.** Use radios, which show every choice at once,
  or a Switch for on and off.
- **More than about fifteen, or when people know what they want.** Use a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs), which lets
  them type to filter.
- **Several choices.** A Select picks one. Use checkboxes or a
  multi-select Combobox.
- **To run an action** such as Export or Delete. Use a Menu: a Select
  keeps a value, a Menu does something.

## Accessibility

- The field is a `<button>` with `role="combobox"`,
  `aria-haspopup="listbox"` and `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox`
  of `option`s, with `aria-selected` on the chosen one.
- **Keyboard:** Space, Enter or Up/Down open it; the arrows move, typing
  jumps to a matching option, Enter selects, Escape closes, and focus
  returns to the field.
- The label is associated with the field (`aria-labelledby`). It is a
  `<div>`, because a `<label>` would also click the button and open the
  list.
- `helperText` is the field's description; `validationState="error"`
  sets `aria-invalid`, and `required` sets `aria-required`.
- **Read-only** locks the value, not the list: it still opens so the
  options can be read, but choosing one changes nothing. The field has
  `aria-readonly`. Use `disabled` when the list should not open at all.
- `isLoading` sets `aria-busy` on the field.
- The list renders in a portal at the end of `<body>`: it reads the
  root's tokens, so a `Theme` scope around the field does not restyle it.
- Options are 32px, 44px on touch screens.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Settings The signed-in user's settings: a heading, a [Vertical Nav](?path=/docs/patterns...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SettingsStories from './Settings.stories'

<Meta of={SettingsStories} />

# Settings

The signed-in user's settings: a heading, a
[Vertical Nav](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-vertical-nav--docs) of
sections beside the one shown, each section a form of
[Form Sections](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs)
with a save bar at its end, and a danger zone last. After Tailwind UI's
settings screens and Polaris' settings page. Built from
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) and the
kit's Text Input, Textarea,
[Password Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-passwordinput--docs),
Checkbox, Radio, Modal and Button. The data is made up.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/settings-template.json
```

<Canvas of={SettingsStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Nav**: Profile, Account and Notifications. A link swaps the section in
  place and becomes the current page. Every section stays mounted while
  hidden, so a half-done edit survives a look at another section.
- **Save bar**: at the end of each section's form, Discard and Save, with
  a status line. It sticks to the bottom of the view while a long form
  runs past the fold. Save stores what the form sends and says "Saved.";
  Discard puts the fields back to what was last saved. Both are always
  there: a disabled Save cannot say why it is disabled.
- **Account**: change password asks for the current password, to prove
  it is you, and a new one with its rules. Both are checked on send, focus
  goes to the first one to fix, and the fields empty once it changes.
- **Read-only**: the email is managed by the organisation's sign-in, so
  it is a read-only field that says who can change it, not a disabled one:
  it stays readable, focusable and sent with the form.
- **Danger zone**: Delete account, last on the Account section and set
  off by a rule, opens a [Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs)
  that waits until the username is typed. Cancel or Escape keeps everything.

<Canvas of={SettingsStories.Account} />

## Make it yours

`Settings` keeps the saved values in state and hands each save to
`onSave(section, values)`, the form's fields by name. Call your API there,
and load your values in place of the samples. Add a section by adding it
to `SECTIONS` and a `SectionForm` for it; past seven or so sections, group
them in the nav.

Settings are edited as forms with one Save per section, not field by
field with [Inline Edit](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-inline-edit--docs):
a reader changes several related values at once and expects to review them
before they apply. Inline edit suits a record read more than edited.
[Form Layouts' Settings Sections](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs)
shows the sections alone; this template is the whole page around them.

The sample swaps sections in place. In an app with a router, give each nav
item its own URL (a `render` link), and render the section the URL names.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={SettingsStories} />

Any other prop goes to the App Shell's root, e.g. `style` to set its
`block-size` when the page is not the whole viewport.

## Layout

- From 48rem of page width the nav is a column as wide as the app's
  sidebar and stays in view while the section scrolls. Below that it
  stacks above the section, every link still showing: a settings nav is a
  handful of links, and folding it into a menu would hide where else to go.
- Form Sections split (title and description beside the fields) from
  48rem of their own width, and stack below.

<Canvas of={SettingsStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- One `h1`, "Settings"; each Form Section's title is an `h2`.
- The nav is a navigation landmark named "Settings", the shown section's
  link `aria-current="page"`. Focus stays on the link; the section follows
  it in reading order.
- Each section is a form named after it ("Profile", "Change password").
  The save bar's status line is a `status` live region, so "Saved." is
  announced without moving focus.
- A field that fails is marked `aria-invalid`, its message part of its
  description, and gets focus.
- Delete account opens an `alertdialog` named "Delete your account?",
  with focus in the field to type the username; the delete button stays
  disabled until it matches. On close focus returns to the button.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { Theme } from '@/theme/Theme'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

const STEPS = ['2xs', 'xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl', '2xl'] as const

function Swatch({ step }: { step: string }) {
  return (
    // The caption clears the largest step's reach rather than sitting inside
    // it: 2xl extends about 3rem below the box, so a tighter gap puts the
    // label in the shadow and both read as mud.
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', alignItems: 'center', gap: 'var(--space-12)' }}>
      <div
        style={{
          height: '4.5rem',
          width: '4.5rem',
          borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)',
          background: 'var(--card)',
          boxShadow: `var(--shadow-${step})`,
        }}
      />
      <span className={docs.caption}>--shadow-{step}</span>
    </div>
  )
}

function ShadowScale() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.rowWrap} style={{ padding: 'var(--space-6)', gap: 'var(--space-12)' }}>
      {STEPS.map((step) => (
        <Swatch key={step} step={step} />
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Shadows.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Shadows',
  render: () => <ShadowScale />,
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Scale: Story = {}

/** Both appearances at once — the toolbar can only show one at a time. */
export const Modes: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div
      style={{
        display: 'grid',
        gap: 'var(--space-4)',
        gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(auto-fit, minmax(18rem, 1fr))',
      }}
    >
      {(['light', 'dark'] as const).map((appearance) => (
        <Theme
          key={appearance}
          appearance={appearance}
          style={{
            background: 'var(--background)',
            // The light panel is the near-white page, so without this its
            // edge barely shows and the comparison looks one-sided.
            border: '1px solid var(--border)',
            borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)',
            padding: 'var(--space-6)',
          }}
        >
          <div className={docs.caption} style={{ marginBottom: 'var(--space-6)' }}>
            {appearance}
          </div>
          <div className={docs.rowWrap} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-8)' }}>
            {(['xs', 'md', '2xl'] as const).map((step) => (
              <Swatch key={step} step={step} />
            ))}
          </div>
        </Theme>
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    // The point of the alpha scale: the same token is not the same value in
    // both modes. If someone copies the light values into .dark, this fails.
    const shadows = (['light', 'dark'] as const).map((mode) =>
      getComputedStyle(canvas.getByText(mode).parentElement!).getPropertyValue('--shadow-md').trim(),
    )
    await expect(shadows[0]).not.toBe(shadows[1])
    await expect(shadows.every(Boolean)).toBe(true)
  },
}

# Shadows Seven elevation steps and an off switch. They read as `var(--shadow-2xs)` throug...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ShadowsStories from './Shadows.stories'

<Meta of={ShadowsStories} />

# Shadows

Seven elevation steps and an off switch. They read as `var(--shadow-2xs)`
through `var(--shadow-2xl)`, and each resolves per appearance rather than
being a fixed value.

<Canvas of={ShadowsStories.Scale} />

## The scale is one shape at seven heights

A step is not a blur radius someone liked. Each one is a **height `h`**,
and both of its layers fall out of that number:

```
ambient  0  h     2h    -h/2     the spread of light around a raised object
contact  0  h/2   h     -h/2     the tighter dark where it meets the surface
```

Two layers because one cannot do both jobs. A single soft shadow floats
without touching down; a single tight one reads as a border. The negative
spread pulls both layers in as they rise, which is what keeps a tall step
from bleeding sideways into whatever sits next to it.

| Token | h | Light |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--shadow-none` | — | `0 0 #0000` |
| `--shadow-2xs` | 1 | 1px drop, 3.3% |
| `--shadow-xs` | 2 | 2px + 1px, 3.9% / 2.6% |
| `--shadow-sm` | 4 | 4px + 2px, 5.2% / 3.3% |
| `--shadow-md` | 8 | 8px + 4px, 5.8% / 3.9% |
| `--shadow-lg` | 12 | 12px + 6px, 6.5% / 4.6% |
| `--shadow-xl` | 20 | 20px + 10px, 7.8% / 5.2% |
| `--shadow-2xl` | 32 | 32px + 16px, 10.4% / 6.5% |

The alphas are deliberately faint: a panel separates from the page by
being lighter (white on the gray-50 page) and by its border, so a shadow
is reserved for things that genuinely float — menus, popovers, dialogs.

`h` doubles through the lower steps and eases off at the top, because the
difference between 1px and 2px of lift is legible and the difference
between 40px and 48px is not.

`--shadow-none` exists so that turning elevation off is a token rather
than a literal. `box-shadow: none` also works, but it cannot be swapped by
a `Theme` and it breaks a transition between two shadow states — `0 0
#0000` interpolates, `none` does not.

## Dark mode is derived, not retyped

Only the light values are written down. The dark ones are **computed from
them**: every alpha is multiplied by 4 and clamped at 0.6.

<Canvas of={ShadowsStories.Modes} />

Look at the dark half. The shadows are nearly invisible, and multiplying
the alpha by four is not what fixes it — nothing fixes it. Here is the
measurement, sampling the darkest pixel each shadow can produce:

| | Page | Darkest shadow pixel | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Light, `--shadow-md` | 255 | 232 | **23 levels** |
| Light, `--shadow-2xl` | 255 | 214 | **41 levels** |
| Dark, `--shadow-md` | 10 | 6 | **4 levels** |
| Dark, `--shadow-2xl` | 10 | 4 | **6 levels** |

A drop shadow works by darkening what is under it. The dark page is
already at 10 of 255, so **the entire budget is 10 levels** — even a
pure-black shadow at full opacity could not do better. Light mode has 255
to spend. That is a 25× difference in available range, and no choice of
alpha closes it.

So the multiplier is not rescuing dark mode; it is spending a small budget
well rather than leaving it unspent. What actually carries elevation in
dark mode is the surface: `--card` sits at **23** against a background of
**10**, a 13-level lift — two to three times stronger than any shadow on
this page.

**In dark mode, surface lightness is the primary elevation signal and the
shadow is a secondary cue.** In light mode it is the other way around. If
you are building a floating surface and it does not read as raised in dark
mode, reach for a lighter surface token, not a heavier shadow.

The **clamp** at 0.6 is therefore housekeeping rather than tuning — it
stops a large light alpha from generating a nonsensical dark one, and
between `--shadow-2xl` uncapped and capped there is about one level in it.

Deriving rather than retyping closes a different gap. When both modes were
written by hand there were fourteen numbers and nothing checking that they
told the same story; editing a step meant remembering to edit its twin.
Now editing a step edits both, and the `Modes` story asserts the two did
not collapse into the same value — set the multiplier to 1 and that test
fails.

## Who uses them

Controls are flat: Button, Text Input and the rest carry borders, not
shadows. **Card** is the first surface on the scale — `elevated` rests on
`--shadow-sm` and lifts to `--shadow-md` on hover when clickable. The
remaining steps are for the surfaces still to come (popover, dropdown,
modal, toast), documented now so they adopt a shared scale instead of each
inventing a `box-shadow`.

That also means the steps are **untested against real components.** The
geometry is consistent, but consistent is not the same as tuned. Treat
them as a starting point to adjust when the first floating surface lands.

## A note on rings and shadows

`box-shadow` is a single property, so a shadow and a focus ring drawn the
same way would overwrite each other — which is why systems that draw rings
with `box-shadow` need machinery to compose the two.

The kit sidesteps it: focus is drawn with `outline`, which has its own
property and its own `outline-offset`, and current browsers follow
`border-radius` with it. An elevated surface can carry a shadow and a
focus ring at once, and neither needs to know about the other.

## What is not here

**Inset shadows.** For recessed wells and pressed states. They are a real
gap, but the kit has no recessed surface and no pressed treatment yet, so
they would be a step nothing reads — and this page already carries seven
of those. Add them as `elevation-inset-*` in `tokens/semantic.json` when
the first one lands; the alpha derivation applies unchanged.

**Coloured shadows.** A shadow tinted toward the accent instead of black.
Worth having, but it needs a real decision about which token it reads and
how it behaves in dark mode, not a mechanical port.

## Customization

The raw values are `--elevation-none` through `--elevation-2xl` in `:root`
and `.dark`; the `*` block maps them onto `--shadow-*` and does not need to
change.

Change a step by editing `tokens/semantic.json` and running `npm run
tokens` — light and dark regenerate together. Overriding `--shadow-md`
directly on a `Theme` scope also works and skips the derivation, which is
the right tool for a one-off surface and the wrong one for changing the
scale.

# Session The two ends of a session: **Session Timeout**, the warning a minute before an i...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SessionStories from './Session.stories'
import { SessionTimeout } from './Session'

<Meta of={SessionStories} />

# Session

The two ends of a session: **Session Timeout**, the warning a minute
before an idle session ends, and **Signed Out**, the page the reader lands
on after it ends, with the account they were signed in to and **Sign in
again**. After Carbon's login pattern. Built on
[Modal](?path=/docs/overlays-modal--docs) (as an alert dialog), the **Auth
Layout** (see [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#auth-layout)),
Button and Link.

Neither part knows about sessions. The app tracks inactivity, opens the
warning, extends or ends the session from its buttons, and picks the
reason the signed-out page gives.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/session.json
```

## Session timeout warning

Open it `countdown` seconds (60 by default) before an idle session ends.
The time left counts down in the sentence. **Stay signed in** has focus,
since that is what most readers want; it and Escape call `onContinue`,
where you extend the session and close the warning. **Sign out** calls
`onSignOut`. At zero, `onExpire` (or `onSignOut` when you leave it out):
sign out and show Signed Out with reason `inactive`.

<Canvas of={SessionStories.Warning} />

Keep `countdown` at 20 seconds or more: WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable)
asks for a warning and at least 20 seconds to extend with a simple action.
The countdown runs to a fixed end, so a background tab, whose timers the
browser slows down, still ends on time. Closing and reopening it starts
the count again.

## Signed out

The page after a session ends, with a title and a line for the `reason`:

- `signed-out` (default): the reader pressed Sign out.
- `inactive`: the warning ran out.
- `expired`: the server ended the session, for example a token reached
  its lifetime.

<Canvas of={SessionStories.SignedOutPage} />

### Remembered account

Pass `account` (an email or a username, masked if you need to) to say which
account **Sign in again** is for, and carry it in `signInHref` so the reader
only types a password: [Progressive Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-progressive-sign-in--docs)
takes it as `defaultEmail`, which is also where its **Remember my email**
comes back. `otherAccountHref` adds **Use another account**. Leave
`account` out after a deliberate sign out on a shared computer.

<Canvas of={SessionStories.Inactive} />

## Props

### Signed Out

<ArgTypes of={SessionStories} />

Every other Auth Layout prop (`brand`, `appearance`, `aside`, `footer`) and
`<div>` attribute passes through.

### Session Timeout

<ArgTypes of={SessionTimeout} />

## Layout

- **Session Timeout** is a small (24rem) modal, never wider than the
  screen. The buttons sit at the end of the footer, Stay signed in last.
- **Signed Out** follows the Auth Layout: one 25rem column centred on the
  canvas, in a card by default. A long account breaks anywhere instead of
  pushing the page sideways at 320px.

<Canvas of={SessionStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- The warning is an `alertdialog` named by its title and described by its
  sentence, so a screen reader reads the time left once, when it opens.
  The time is a `timer`, which is not a live region: it does not announce
  every second.
- Focus moves to **Stay signed in** when the warning opens, and back to
  where it was when it closes. Enter keeps the session; Escape does too.
- Signed Out has one `h1`, the reason, inside `main`. **Sign in again** is
  the first control in the page, before Use another account.
