# Sign In A sign-in page: the logo and the title, single sign-on buttons if you have them,...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SignInStories from './SignIn.stories'

<Meta of={SignInStories} />

# Sign In

A sign-in page: the logo and the title, single sign-on buttons if you have
them, then email and password. After Tailwind UI's sign-in screens,
shadcn/ui's login blocks and Carbon's login pattern. Built on the **Auth
Layout**, the frame the other auth screens (sign up, reset password,
multi-factor) share, and the kit's TextInput, Checkbox, Link, Alert and
Button.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/sign-in-template.json
```

<Canvas of={SignInStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Single sign-on**: a full-width button per provider, then an "or" line,
  then the form. `onProviderSelect` gets the provider's `id`; send the
  reader to your identity provider from there.
- **Email and password**: Show reveals the password and turns into Hide;
  sending the form hides it again, so the browser does not keep it as
  plain text. The fields carry `autocomplete="username"` and
  `"current-password"`, so password managers fill them.
- **Checks before sending**: an empty field, or an email with no `@`, is
  marked with a message saying what to do, and the first one gets focus.
  Typing in a field clears its message. Valid values go to `onSignIn`.
- **Wrong credentials**: `onSignIn` returns (or resolves to) a message. It
  shows above the form and is announced, the password is cleared and
  focused, the email kept. Say "The email or password is incorrect", not
  which one: naming it tells an attacker which emails have accounts. If
  `onSignIn` throws or rejects, the page says "Something went wrong. Try
  again." instead.
- **Keep me signed in**, **Forgot password?** and **Sign up** are links and a
  checkbox; drop the checkbox with `hasRememberMe={false}` and the link
  with no `signUpHref`.

<Canvas of={SignInStories.WrongPassword} />

## Variants

**Card** (default): the form in a card on the Theme's canvas. The most
common in business software; it reads as a step apart from the app.

**Plain**: the form straight on the canvas, for a quieter page or a canvas
that is already a colour or an image. Here also without single sign-on,
Keep me signed in or sign-up, as where accounts come by invitation.

<Canvas of={SignInStories.Plain} />

**With a panel**: `aside` puts a panel beside the form from 64rem of the
page's width: a picture, a customer quote, what is new. The form keeps the
left half and lines up at its start.

<Canvas of={SignInStories.WithAside} />

## Make it yours

Replace `onSignIn` with a call to your API and return its error message;
on success, navigate away. `providers` takes `{ id, label, icon }`: the
label is the whole button text ("Continue with Google", "Sign in with
SSO"), the icon the provider's mark. The kit ships no brand marks.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | "Sign in to your account" | The page's `h1`. |
| `providers` | `{ id, label, icon? }[]` | none | Single sign-on and social buttons above the form. |
| `onProviderSelect` | `(id) => void` | | A provider's button was pressed. |
| `onSignIn` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ email, password, remember }` once the fields pass. A returned message shows above the form; the button is busy while a promise is pending. |
| `hasRememberMe` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows "Keep me signed in". |
| `forgotPasswordHref` | `string` | `"#forgot-password"` | Where "Forgot password?" goes. |
| `signUpHref` | `string` | none | Shows "No account? Sign up". |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the sign-up line, outside the card: legal links, "Ask your administrator". |

Every other Auth Layout prop below passes through; `children` is the
page's form.

## Auth Layout

`AuthLayout` (in `AuthLayout.tsx`) is the frame: the logo, an `h1`, an
optional line under it, the form and a footer, in one column about 25rem
wide, centred on the canvas. Every auth screen uses it, so they line up
with each other. It owns no state. The same file exports `AuthDivider`,
the "or" line. The password field with Show / Hide is the kit's
[Password Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-passwordinput--docs) (pass `autoComplete="new-password"` where the password is being chosen;
its button is named after a text `label`, "Show confirm password", so two
on one page differ).

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/auth-layout.json
```

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` | `ReactNode` | | The logo, above the title. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | required | The page's `h1`. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | | A line under the title. |
| `appearance` | `card`, `plain` | `card` | The form in a card, or straight on the canvas. Ignored with `aside`. |
| `aside` | `ReactNode` | | A panel beside the form from 64rem; hidden below. |
| `asideLabel` | `string` | | The panel's accessible name, when it says something. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the form, outside the card. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | required | The form. |

Any other prop goes to the root, e.g. `style` to set its `min-block-size`
when the page is not the whole viewport.

## Layout

- The page fills the viewport and the column sits in its middle, both
  ways. It is about 25rem wide; on a phone it takes the full width less
  the page's padding. A long title with no spaces wraps; nothing scrolls
  sideways.
- With `aside`, from 64rem of the page's width the form and the panel
  take half each and the heading lines up at the start. Below 64rem the
  panel is hidden and the page is the centred column again, so put nothing
  in the panel the reader needs. An `<img>` in it fills the panel.
- "Keep me signed in" and "Forgot password?" share a row while they fit;
  the link drops under the checkbox when they do not.

<Canvas of={SignInStories.Phone} />

## Accessibility

- The form is in a `main` landmark, and its one heading is the `h1`. The
  panel is a `complementary` landmark after `main`, named by `asideLabel`;
  a panel that is only a picture should hold an `<img alt="">`.
- The single sign-on buttons come before the form in reading and focus
  order, as they do on screen.
- Every field has a visible label. An invalid field has
  `aria-invalid="true"` and its message as its description, and the first
  invalid field gets focus.
- The message from `onSignIn` is an `alert`, so it is announced; focus
  moves to the cleared password. The Sign in button is `aria-busy` while
  it waits, and a second press sends nothing.
- The Show button is named "Show password", then "Hide password" (after
  the field's label): its visible text is part of its name, as voice
  control needs.
- The single sign-on buttons are disabled while a sign-in is pending.

# Sign Up A sign-up page: the logo and the title, single sign-on buttons if you have them,...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SignUpStories from './SignUp.stories'

<Meta of={SignUpStories} />

# Sign Up

A sign-up page: the logo and the title, single sign-on buttons if you have
them, then full name, email and a new password with its rules, the terms
and a link back to sign in. After shadcn/ui's sign-up blocks and Carbon's
login pattern. Built on the **Auth Layout** (see
[Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#auth-layout)) and the
kit's TextInput, Checkbox, Link, Alert and Button.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/sign-up-template.json
```

<Canvas of={SignUpStories.Default} />

## What works

- **Single sign-on**: as on Sign In, a full-width button per provider,
  then an "or" line, then the form. `onProviderSelect` gets the `id`.
- **One name field**, "Full name", not first and last: names do not split
  the same way everywhere. `autocomplete="name"` and `"email"` let the
  browser fill them.
- **A new password with its rules**: the rules are listed under the field
  from the start and ticked off as the reader types. The default is one
  rule, at least 12 characters, with no rules about kinds of characters
  (after NIST SP 800-63B); pass your own `passwordRules`. There is no
  "confirm password" field: Show lets the reader check what they typed.
  `autocomplete="new-password"` lets a password manager suggest one.
- **Terms**: pass `terms`, the label with its links, and a checkbox the
  reader must tick appears above the button. Leave it out and there is
  none; put a line in `footer` instead if your terms need no consent.
- **Checks before sending**: an empty field, an email with no `@`, an unmet
  rule or unticked terms is marked with a message saying what to do, and
  the first one gets focus. Typing clears a field's message. Valid values
  go to `onSignUp`.
- **The account cannot be made**: `onSignUp` returns (or resolves to) a
  message. It shows above the form and is announced; what was typed stays.
  If `onSignUp` throws or rejects, the page says "Something went wrong. Try
  again."

<Canvas of={SignUpStories.EmailTaken} />

## Variants

**Card** (default) and **plain**, and **with a panel** through `aside`,
exactly as on Sign In: they are the Auth Layout's. Plain here is also
without single sign-on or terms, the fewest parts.

<Canvas of={SignUpStories.Plain} />

## Make it yours

Replace `onSignUp` with a call to your API and return its error message;
on success, send the reader on (to verify their email, or into the app).
Whether to say "An account with this email already exists" is your call:
it tells anyone which emails have accounts. Where that matters, accept
the sign-up and email the address instead.

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | "Create your account" | The page's `h1`. |
| `providers` | `{ id, label, icon? }[]` | none | Single sign-on and social buttons above the form. |
| `onProviderSelect` | `(id) => void` | | A provider's button was pressed. |
| `passwordRules` | `{ label, test(password) }[]` | at least 12 characters | Listed under the password and ticked off; all must pass to send. |
| `terms` | `ReactNode` | none | The label of a checkbox the reader must tick. |
| `onSignUp` | `(values) => string \| void \| Promise<…>` | | Gets `{ name, email, password, acceptedTerms }` once the fields pass. A returned message shows above the form; the button is busy while a promise is pending. |
| `signInHref` | `string` | `"#sign-in"` | Where "Already have an account? Sign in" goes. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | | Under the sign-in line, outside the card. |

Every other Auth Layout prop passes through. The rules come from
`PasswordInput`'s `rules` prop, so a reset-password page can list the same
ones.

## Layout

The Auth Layout's, as on [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs#layout):
a column about 25rem wide in the middle of the page, the full width less
the padding on a phone, and a panel beside it from 64rem with `aside`. A
long title, rule or terms label wraps; nothing scrolls sideways.

<Canvas of={SignUpStories.Phone} />

## Accessibility

- The form is in a `main` landmark, and its one heading is the `h1`.
- Every field has a visible label. An invalid field has
  `aria-invalid="true"` and its message as its description, and the first
  invalid field gets focus.
- The password rules are the field's description, each followed by
  "(met)" or "(not met)" for a screen reader, so they are read with the
  field. Ticking one off is not announced as you type; the tick and the
  colour show it on screen.
- The message from `onSignUp` is an `alert`, so it is announced. The
  Create account button is `aria-busy` while it waits, a second press
  sends nothing, and the single sign-on buttons are disabled.
- The terms checkbox's links are inside its label; pressing a link opens
  it, pressing the rest of the label ticks the box.

'use client'
import { useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { Button } from '@/components/buttons/Button'
import { Select } from '@/components/inputs/Select'
import { TextInput } from '@/components/inputs/TextInput'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

const TIERS = ['xs', 'sm', 'md'] as const

/* Each cell is a token, read back in pixels: a probe element takes the token
   as a length and the table shows what it resolves to here, so the numbers
   follow the Theme's scaling and radius preset and are never retyped. */
const ROWS = [
  { label: 'Height', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}`, prop: 'inlineSize' },
  { label: 'Padding, pad', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}-pad`, prop: 'inlineSize' },
  { label: 'Padding, pad-spacious', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}-pad-spacious`, prop: 'inlineSize' },
  { label: 'Gap, icon to label', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}-gap`, prop: 'inlineSize' },
  { label: 'Icon', token: (t: string) => `--icon-${t}`, prop: 'inlineSize' },
  { label: 'Radius, control', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}-radius`, prop: 'borderTopLeftRadius' },
  { label: 'Radius, field', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}-radius-field`, prop: 'borderTopLeftRadius' },
] as const

/* Reads every [data-probe] in the table once it is laid out, keyed by its
   probe name. data-prop names the CSS property to read (inlineSize if unset). */
function useProbes() {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null)
  const [values, setValues] = useState<Record<string, string>>({})

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const read: Record<string, string> = {}
    for (const probe of ref.current!.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-probe]')) {
      const value = getComputedStyle(probe)[(probe.dataset.prop ?? 'inlineSize') as 'inlineSize']
      // A pill radius computes to 9999px; say what it means.
      read[probe.dataset.probe!] = Number.parseFloat(value) > 1000 ? 'pill' : value
    }
    setValues(read)
  }, [])

  return { ref, values }
}

function TierTable() {
  const { ref, values } = useProbes()

  return (
    <table ref={ref} className={docs.tokenTable}>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>Property</th>
          {TIERS.map((t) => (
            <th key={t}>
              <code>{t}</code>
            </th>
          ))}
          <th>Token</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {ROWS.map((row) => (
          <tr key={row.label}>
            <td>{row.label}</td>
            {TIERS.map((t) => (
              <td key={t} data-token={row.token(t)}>
                <span
                  data-probe={row.token(t)}
                  data-prop={row.prop}
                  aria-hidden="true"
                  style={{
                    position: 'absolute',
                    visibility: 'hidden',
                    [row.prop]: `var(${row.token(t)})`,
                  }}
                />
                <code>{values[row.token(t)]}</code>
              </td>
            ))}
            <td>
              <code>{row.token('{tier}')}</code>
            </td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  )
}

const STEPS = ['2xs', 'xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'] as const
const DENSITIES = ['default', 'compact'] as const

/* The ramp in both densities at once: each column's probes sit inside their
   own [data-density], so the table never depends on the toolbar. */
function BoxRampTable() {
  const { ref, values } = useProbes()

  return (
    <table ref={ref} className={docs.tokenTable}>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>Step</th>
          {DENSITIES.map((d) => (
            <th key={d}>{d === 'default' ? 'Default' : 'Compact'}</th>
          ))}
          <th>Token</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {STEPS.map((step) => (
          <tr key={step}>
            <td>
              <code>{step}</code>
            </td>
            {DENSITIES.map((d) => (
              <td key={d} data-density={d} data-token={`--box-${step}@${d}`}>
                <span
                  data-probe={`--box-${step}@${d}`}
                  aria-hidden="true"
                  style={{ position: 'absolute', visibility: 'hidden', inlineSize: `var(--box-${step})` }}
                />
                <code>{values[`--box-${step}@${d}`]}</code>
              </td>
            ))}
            <td>
              <code>--box-{step}</code>
            </td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  )
}

function SmallControls() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.row} style={{ flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
      <Button size="sm" startIcon={<Icon name="plus" />}>
        Button
      </Button>
      <TextInput size="sm" aria-label="Text input" placeholder="Text input" prefix={<Icon name="search" />} />
      <Select size="sm" aria-label="Select" placeholder="Select" options={['One', 'Two']} />
    </div>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Sizing.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Sizing',
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Tiers: Story = {
  render: () => <TierTable />,
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const value = (name: string) => canvasElement.querySelector(`[data-token="${name}"] code`)!.textContent
    await expect(value('--control-xs')).toBe('20px')
    await expect(value('--control-sm')).toBe('24px')
    await expect(value('--control-md')).toBe('32px')
    await expect(value('--icon-xs')).toBe('12px')
    await expect(value('--icon-sm')).toBe('14px')
    await expect(value('--icon-md')).toBe('16px')
    await expect(value('--control-md-pad')).toBe('10px')
    await expect(value('--control-md-pad-spacious')).toBe('12px')
  },
}

export const BoxRamp: Story = {
  render: () => <BoxRampTable />,
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const column = (d: string) =>
      STEPS.map((step) => canvasElement.querySelector(`[data-token="--box-${step}@${d}"] code`)!.textContent)
    await expect(column('default')).toEqual(['16px', '20px', '24px', '32px', '40px', '48px'])
    await expect(column('compact')).toEqual(['16px', '20px', '22px', '28px', '36px', '44px'])
  },
}

/* The point of a tier: a Button, a text field and a select of the same size
   carry the same icon, corner and type, whoever built them. */
export const SameTier: Story = {
  render: () => <SmallControls />,
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const button = canvasElement.querySelector('button:not([role="combobox"])')!
    const field = canvasElement.querySelector('input')!.parentElement!
    const select = canvasElement.querySelector('[role="combobox"]')!
    const parts = [button, field, select]
    const iconOf = (el: Element) => el.querySelector('svg')!.getBoundingClientRect().width
    const style = (el: Element) => getComputedStyle(el)

    for (const el of parts) {
      await expect(el.getBoundingClientRect().height).toBe(24)
      await expect(iconOf(el)).toBe(14)
      await expect(style(el).fontSize).toBe(style(button).fontSize)
      await expect(style(el).borderTopLeftRadius).toBe(style(button).borderTopLeftRadius)
    }
  },
}

# Sizing Every control's geometry comes from two facts: its **size tier** and its **intent...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SizingStories from './Sizing.stories'

<Meta of={SizingStories} />

# Sizing

Every control's geometry comes from two facts: its **size tier** and its
**intent**. The tier binds height, inline padding, the gap between icon and
label, the icon and the corner. The intent (control or field) decides two
things only: which padding it takes, and whether it becomes a pill at
`radius="full-rounded"`.

<Canvas of={SizingStories.Tiers} />

The table reads each token back from the page, so it shows what the
current scaling and radius preset resolve to. Every length here, the
radius included, is multiplied by `--scaling`.

## The box ramp

Every element is a box, and every box with a fixed height or a fixed
square stands on a step of one ramp. The same role always takes the same
step, so a close button is 24px in a Modal and in a Toast, and a nav
item is as tall as the button beside it.

<Canvas of={SizingStories.BoxRamp} />

`md` (32px) is the default. Density maps the whole ramp with one rule:
16 and 20 stay, every larger step drops one notch (24 to 22, 32 to 28,
40 to 36, 48 to 44). The control tiers below are the ramp's `xs`, `sm`
and `md` under another name.

### Which step a role takes

| Role | Step | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The default control: field, button, tab, pagination and menu item, calendar day, an icon button in the app frame (sidebar toggle, carousel arrows), a nav item | `md` | 32px |
| A small inline control; a close button inside a surface (Modal, Popover, Toast, Alert); the small Stepper marker; the medium spinner | `sm` | 24px |
| Small parts: Tag `size="sm"`, the slider thumb, the checkbox and radio box, Badge `md`, Kbd `md`, a file icon | `xs` | 20px |
| A mark that sits with a glyph: Badge `sm`, Kbd `sm`, the small slider thumb, the small spinner, a skeleton line | `2xs` | 16px |
| A leading visual: Avatar `md`, the small EmptyState icon | `lg` | 40px |
| A large visual: Avatar `lg`, the Stats icon, the EmptyState icon | `xl` | 48px |
| A glyph inside a control | `--icon-{tier}` | 12 / 14 / 16px |
| A line of text, and an icon beside it | `--leading-*` × `--text-*` | one line |
| A table or list row | `box-md` + 2 × `--space-inline` | 48px |

The rules that go with the table:

- **A component picks the step by role.** Whoever uses the component
  picks only its `size`, and `size` points at a step.
- **Composite boxes take no free number.** A row, a Tag or a top bar is
  the box inside it plus a spacing role on each side: `--row-height` is
  `box-md` plus `--space-inline` above and below (48 / 36px). Text boxes
  are a line tall (`--leading-*` × `--text-*`); an icon beside text sits
  in a box one line tall.
- **A box that grows with its content** uses `min-block-size` at a step,
  never `block-size`.
- **A box with a fixed size and padding or a border declares
  `box-sizing: border-box` itself.** The kit ships no global reset, so
  the app's own CSS decides the default.

Off the ramp, each for a reason: 1–2px strokes, dots and bars under
12px (radio dot, Badge dot, progress bar), switch track widths, region
sizes (ColorPicker, a vertical Slider, overlay widths), the 44px touch
target and icons sized in `em` inside text. `npm run tokens` stops when a
control, size or row token leaves the ramp of its density without a
listed reason, and when `--row-height` stops being the sum above.

## Who reads which tier

| Tier | Height (Default / Compact) | Components |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `md` | 32 / 28px | the default: Button, ToggleButton, every field (TextInput, Search, Select, Combobox, NumberInput, DatePicker, Textarea), Tabs, Pagination, Menu item |
| `sm` | 24 / 22px | the small inline size of the same components, Tag `size="md"`, and the Menubar trigger |
| `xs` | 20 / 20px | compact parts only: Tag `size="sm"`, the slider thumb |

Density keeps every tier and tightens each; see
[Spacing](?path=/docs/foundations-spacing--docs#density). The checkbox and
radio box, the switch tracks, Badge and Avatar have their own size tokens
(`--choice-box`, `--switch-md-w`, `--badge-md`, `--avatar-md`), which follow
density too.

A component's `size` prop points at a tier; the names need not match.
Tag `size="md"` reads tier `sm`, because a tag sits in a line of text and
a 32px tag would push it apart.

**Buttons and fields have no `xs`.** A 20px button reads as a part,
not a control.

**The 24px floor is for the hit area, not the drawn box.** WCAG 2.5.8
asks for a 24×24px target. A box drawn smaller (Compact `sm` is 22px, the
checkbox 20px) keeps its look and widens its hit area to 24px with a
`::before`. On touch screens every tier grows its hit area to
`--target-coarse` (44px) the same way, without growing the visible box.

## Intent

**Padding.** Fields and rows take `pad`, because their text is left
aligned and has to line up with the label above it. Buttons take
`pad-spacious`: a centred label reads as cramped with less. The two only
differ at `md` (10 against 12px); at `sm` and `xs` there is no room to
spend.

**Radius.** The tier picks the step (`--radius-sm` for `xs` and `sm`,
`--radius-md` for `md`, so a short box does not read as a pill by
accident). The intent picks what happens at `radius="full-rounded"`:
`--control-{tier}-radius` becomes a pill, `--control-{tier}-radius-field`
stops one step up. At `md` these are exactly `--radius-control` and
`--radius-field`. See [Radius](?path=/docs/foundations-radius--docs).

<Canvas of={SizingStories.SameTier} />

A Button, a text field and a select at `size="sm"`: one height, one icon,
one corner, one type size. The story asserts all four.

## Why these gaps

The gap grows with the tier: 4, 6, 8px. Before tiers each component chose
its own, and they disagreed at the small size: Button and the field put
8px between icon and label, Tag put 4px. `md` keeps the 8px every default
control already had, so the size most of an interface uses does not move.
`sm` takes the step between, 6px, which is the one change: small buttons
and fields tighten by 2px, and a medium Tag loosens by 2px.

## The one exception

NumberInput's stepper at `sm` is a 16px button inside the field, so its
chevron stays at `--icon-xs` (12px). A 14px chevron would fill it edge to
edge.

import type { ComponentProps, CSSProperties } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Skeleton.module.css'

export interface SkeletonProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  /** A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length. */
  width?: string | number
  height?: string | number
  appearance?: 'circle' | 'square' | 'rounded'
  /** Several lines of text: stacked bars, the last one shorter. A circle's rows are rounded bars. */
  rows?: number
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** A gentle pulse. Off by default: many pulsing shapes are noise. */
  hasAnimation?: boolean
}

const length = (v: string | number | undefined) => (typeof v === 'number' ? `${v}px` : v)

/**
 * A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading. Decorative:
 * put `aria-busy` on the region it stands in for, and announce the load
 * elsewhere if it matters.
 */
export function Skeleton({
  width,
  height,
  appearance = 'square',
  rows,
  isFullWidth = false,
  hasAnimation = false,
  className,
  style,
  ...props
}: SkeletonProps) {
  const inlineSize = isFullWidth ? '100%' : length(width)

  if (rows && rows > 1) {
    // Lines of text are bars: a circle would stack into a column of dots.
    const line = cn(styles.bone, styles[appearance === 'circle' ? 'rounded' : appearance], styles.line, hasAnimation && styles.animated)
    return (
      <div aria-hidden="true" className={cn(styles.rows, className)} style={{ inlineSize, ...style } as CSSProperties} {...props}>
        {Array.from({ length: rows }, (_, i) => (
          <div key={i} className={line} style={{ blockSize: length(height) }} />
        ))}
      </div>
    )
  }
  // A circle takes its height from its width, so `height` is ignored.
  const blockSize = appearance === 'circle' ? undefined : length(height)
  return (
    <div
      aria-hidden="true"
      className={cn(styles.bone, styles[appearance], hasAnimation && styles.animated, className)}
      style={{ inlineSize, blockSize, ...style } as CSSProperties}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Skeleton } from './Skeleton'
import * as SkeletonStories from './Skeleton.stories'

<Meta of={SkeletonStories} />

# Skeleton

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading, so the page
keeps its layout and the reader sees what is coming.

<Status of={SkeletonStories} />

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.CardPlaceholder} />

## Variants

`appearance` sets the corners, to match what the shape stands in for. Any
appearance takes any size.

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Appearances} />

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `circle` | An avatar or a round icon. Its height is its width. |
| `square` | The default: an image, a media block, anything with square corners. |
| `rounded` | Text, buttons and cards: anything with the kit's rounded corners. |

`rows` stacks lines of text, the last one shorter so it reads as a
paragraph rather than a block.

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Rows} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Skeleton } from 'zweihander/skeleton'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/skeleton.json
```

- Source: [src/components/loaders/Skeleton.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/Skeleton.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/skeleton](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/skeleton)
- Behaviour: a plain element; there is no behaviour here worth Base UI
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SkeletonStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SkeletonStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

A skeleton is built from shapes like these, placed by the page in the
layout of the content that will replace them.

## Measurements

A skeleton has no sizes: `width` and `height` copy the content it stands
in for. These are the defaults, and the parts it sizes itself.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every appearance"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Shape', property: 'Default height', token: '--space-4' },
    { part: 'Circle', property: 'Default width and height', token: '--space-10' },
    { part: 'Lines', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Rounded', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-md' },
    { part: 'Circle', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
  ]}
/>

The default width is the container's. The last of several `rows` is 60%
of the width.

## Color

Every shape is one colour, the same subtle surface as a hover. It is below
any contrast floor on purpose: a placeholder should read as "something
goes here", not compete with content that has arrived. Switch the theme in
the toolbar: the value follows.

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Shape', property: 'Background', token: '--muted' }]} />

## States

A skeleton is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Static' },
    { label: 'Pulsing', content: <div style={card}><Skeleton appearance="rounded" rows={3} height={12} width={200} hasAnimation /></div> },
  ]}
>
  <div style={card}>
    <Skeleton appearance="rounded" rows={3} height={12} width={200} />
  </div>
</States>

- **Static** is the default.
- **Pulsing**, with `hasAnimation`, fades to 50% and back every 1.6s. It
  stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SkeletonStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through to the outer element.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Skeleton when you know the shape of what is loading: a list, a card,
a profile. Match the shapes to the content that will replace them, with
the same sizes and the same gaps.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SkeletonStories.CardPlaceholder} />}
  doCaption="Shapes of the content that is coming: the layout holds when it arrives."
  dont={<Story of={SkeletonStories.DontOneBlock} />}
  dontCaption="One block for a whole card jumps to a different layout on load, which is worse than a spinner."
/>

Animate the few shapes that matter, or none: `hasAnimation` is off by
default because a screen of pulsing shapes is noise.

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Animated} />

## When not to use

- **When you do not know the shape of what is coming.** Use a
  [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs).
- **For a long task with a known size.** Use a
  [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs).
- **For a load that is usually instant.** A skeleton that flashes for
  200ms is noise; show nothing, or a Spinner with a `delay`.

## Accessibility

- **A skeleton is decoration** and is `aria-hidden`, with its `rows`
  hidden as one. It says nothing to a screen reader.
- The region it stands in for has to say it is loading: put
  `aria-busy="true"` on it, as the CardPlaceholder story does, and remove
  it when the content arrives.
- If the wait matters, announce it: a visually hidden status, or a Spinner
  with a label.
- `--muted` is below 3:1 on the page in both modes, on purpose. It is not
  content, and should not compete with content that has arrived.
- The pulse stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

  max?: number
  step?: number
  /** Page Up / Page Down and Shift+arrow step. */
  largeStep?: number
  /** Visible label; also the accessible name of a single thumb. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Show the current value (or range) after the label. */
  showValue?: boolean
  /** How the value is written, e.g. `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }`. */
  format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions
  /** One name per thumb for a range, e.g. `['Minimum price', 'Maximum price']`. */
  thumbLabels?: string[]
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  disabled?: boolean
  name?: string
  /** The accessible name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function Slider<V extends Value = number>({
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  onValueCommitted,
  min = 0,
  max = 100,
  step = 1,
  largeStep,
  label,
  showValue = false,
  format,
  thumbLabels,
  size = 'md',
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  disabled = false,
  name,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  className,
}: SliderProps<V>) {
  const current = value ?? defaultValue ?? (min as V)
  const thumbs = Array.isArray(current) ? current.length : 1
  return (
    <BaseSlider.Root
      value={value as number | number[] | undefined}
      defaultValue={defaultValue as number | number[] | undefined}
      onValueChange={onValueChange && ((v) => onValueChange(v as V))}
      onValueCommitted={onValueCommitted && ((v) => onValueCommitted(v as V))}
      min={min}
      max={max}
      step={step}
      largeStep={largeStep}
      format={format}
      orientation={orientation}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      thumbAlignment="edge"
      className={cn(styles.slider, styles[size], styles[orientation], className)}
    >
      {(label || showValue) && (
        <div className={styles.header}>
          {label && <BaseSlider.Label className={styles.label}>{label}</BaseSlider.Label>}
          {showValue && (
            <BaseSlider.Value className={styles.value}>
              {(formatted) => formatted.join(' – ')}
            </BaseSlider.Value>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
      <BaseSlider.Control className={styles.control}>
        <BaseSlider.Track className={styles.track}>
          <BaseSlider.Indicator className={styles.indicator} />
          {Array.from({ length: thumbs }, (_, i) => (
            <BaseSlider.Thumb
              key={i}
              index={i}
              className={styles.thumb}
              // A range needs a name per thumb; a single thumb takes the
              // label, or aria-label when there is none.
              getAriaLabel={thumbLabels ? (index) => thumbLabels[index] ?? '' : label ? undefined : () => ariaLabel ?? ''}
            />
          ))}
        </BaseSlider.Track>
      </BaseSlider.Control>
    </BaseSlider.Root>
  )
}

# Slider Picks a number, or a range, by dragging along a track: volume, a price range, a b...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Slider } from './Slider'
import * as SliderStories from './Slider.stories'

<Meta of={SliderStories} />

# Slider

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Picks a number, or a range, by dragging along a track: volume, a price
range, a brush size.

<Status of={SliderStories} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Default} />

## Variants

One value or two: a `defaultValue` (or `value`) that is an array of two
makes a range, with a thumb at each end.

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Range} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | The default: a 20px thumb on a 6px track. |
| `sm` | Dense panels and toolbars: a 16px thumb on a 4px track, 12px label. |

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Steps} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Vertical} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Slider } from 'zweihander/slider'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/slider.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/Slider.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Slider.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/slider](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/slider)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Slider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/slider)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SliderStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SliderStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The control strip is as tall as the thumb, so the whole strip is the
target, not just the track: a press anywhere along it moves the nearest
thumb there.

The thumb has a 2px ring. A vertical slider is 12rem tall.

## Color

<SpecTable
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--secondary' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--primary-text' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Ring', token: '--primary-text' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Value', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Label, disabled', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

The fill is a text colour, as on Progress Bar: `--primary-text` clears
3:1 on the `--secondary` track for every accent, where the solid
`--primary` does not.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={SliderStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Slider label="Volume" defaultValue={40} showValue />
</States>

- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the thumb.
- **Dragging** changes the cursor to a closed hand.
- **Disabled** dims the track and thumbs to 50%. The label turns
  `--muted-foreground` and the value stays as it was, so both still read
  at 4.5:1: they are not a native `<label>`, so faded text would fail
  contrast rather than be exempt as part of a disabled control.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SliderStories} />
</div>

`className` passes through to the root.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a slider when an approximate value is fine and seeing it change helps:
volume, brightness, a price range to filter by. Show the value with
`showValue` so the reader knows where they landed.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SliderStories.DoApproximate} />}
  doCaption="An approximate value, with the number shown as it moves."
  dont={<Story of={SliderStories.DontExactNumber} />}
  dontCaption="An exact figure on a long scale: 137 out of 500 is fiddly to hit by dragging. Use a Number Input."
/>

## When not to use

- **For an exact number** (a price, a quantity). Use a Number Input, or
  pair one with the slider.
- **For a few named options.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group, so each
  option says what it means.
- **For a score out of five.** Use a
  [Rating](?path=/docs/components-controls-rating--docs).

## Accessibility

- Each thumb is a `role="slider"` (a real range input) with
  `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and a formatted
  `aria-valuetext`.
- A single thumb is named by `label`, or `aria-label`; a range needs
  `thumbLabels` so each thumb says which end it is.
- Keyboard: arrows move by `step`, Page Up / Page Down and Shift+arrows
  by `largeStep`, Home and End jump to `min` and `max`.
- The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every accent.
- Thumbs keep their size and grow a 44px hit area on coarse pointers.

<Canvas of={SliderStories.WithoutVisibleLabel} />

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { DENSITIES } from '@/theme/Theme'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

const ROLES = ['stack', 'inline', 'cluster', 'group', 'container', 'section']

/* Each role as a bar, once per density. The bars read the tokens inside a
   [data-density] scope, so they show what the stylesheet resolves. */
function RoleBars() {
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(auto-fit, minmax(14rem, 1fr))', gap: 'var(--space-container)' }}>
      {DENSITIES.map((density) => (
        <div key={density} data-density={density} className={docs.stack}>
          <strong className={docs.caption}>{density === 'default' ? 'Default' : 'Compact'}</strong>
          {ROLES.map((role) => (
            <div key={role} className={docs.row}>
              <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '5rem', flexShrink: 0 }}>
                {role}
              </span>
              <div
                style={{
                  height: '1rem',
                  borderRadius: 'var(--radius-sm)',
                  background: 'var(--primary)',
                  width: `var(--space-${role})`,
                }}
              />
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Spacing.mdx.

  title: 'Foundations/Spacing',
  render: () => <RoleBars />,
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

# Spacing Pick a spacing token by **what the gap does**, not by its size. Six roles cover ...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SpacingStories from './Spacing.stories'

<Meta of={SpacingStories} />

# Spacing

Pick a spacing token by **what the gap does**, not by its size. Six roles
cover every gap and pad in the kit; a **density**, Default or Compact,
decides the number behind each one. A designer never chooses between 12
and 16 pixels: they choose `--space-cluster` or `--space-group`, and the
product's density does the rest.

<Canvas of={SpacingStories.Roles} />

## The six roles

| Token | Use for | Default | Compact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--space-stack` | Lines of text under each other: title to description, label to value | 4 | 2 |
| `--space-inline` | Small things side by side: icon to text, label to value on one line, sidebar items | 8 | 4 |
| `--space-cluster` | Controls or parts that sit together: filters in a toolbar, an avatar to its content, the parts of a page heading, inside a small card | 12 | 8 |
| `--space-group` | Items and blocks that belong together: cards in a row, toolbar to table, table cell sides | 16 | 12 |
| `--space-container` | Inside the edge of a card, panel or page heading | 24 | 16 |
| `--space-section` | Page edge and between page sections | 24 | 20 |

The scale is short on purpose: 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. In Compact each
role takes the Default value of the role below it; only section steps
24 to 20. Section and container share 24px in Default, so separate
sections with a card edge or a rule, not with extra white space. AppShell
applies `--space-section` to the page edge from 64rem up; below that the
edge stays at its narrow value.

The numeric steps (`--space-1` to `--space-12`) still exist for the few
places no role fits, such as the size of an icon disc. They do not follow
density.

## Density

Density changes four things together, and keeps every size:

- **The six roles**, as in the table above.
- **The control tier.** Every tier exists in both densities. Compact
  gives each tier the padding and gap of the tier below it; md drops from
  32 to 28px, sm from 24 to 22px, xs stays at 20px (the floor of its text).
- **Type.** Body text is 14px in Default and 13px in Compact. Text of 12px
  and below never shrinks; 13 to 16px drops 1px; headings from 20px up
  drop one step. Compact body leading is 13/18, off the 4px grid on
  purpose. See [Typography](?path=/docs/foundations-typography--docs).
- **Component sizes**: the checkbox and radio box (`--choice-box`, 20 to
  16), the radio dot, the three switch tracks, the progress bar heights,
  avatars xs to lg (`--avatar-md`, 40 to 32), badge heights and dots, and
  table rows (`--row-height`, 48 to 36). In Compact each size takes the
  size below it; the smallest switch, avatar and badge step down further
  so sizes stay apart.

| Control token | md (D / C) | sm (D / C) | xs (D / C) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--control-{tier}` height | 32 / 28 | 24 / 22 | 20 / 20 |
| `--control-{tier}-pad` (fields, rows) | 10 / 8 | 8 / 6 | 6 / 4 |
| `--control-{tier}-pad-spacious` (buttons) | 12 / 8 | 8 / 6 | 6 / 4 |
| `--control-{tier}-gap` (icon to label) | 8 / 6 | 6 / 4 | 4 / 2 |

A small control inside a component (a table's sort button, a modal's
close button, a badge, the number input's steppers) reads the control tier
of its own size, like any other control, not a spacing role.

## Setting it

Density is set like appearance: on the root of the app, through `Theme`.

```tsx
<Theme density="compact">
  <App />
</Theme>
```

`Theme` writes `data-density` on its element, and every token picks its
number from the nearest one. A nested `Theme density="default"` inside a
compact app gets Default back. Popups portal to `<body>`, so set density
at the root; for a compact panel inside a default page, pass the panel
element as `container` to Popover, Menu, Tooltip, Modal, Select, Combobox
and DatePicker so their popups render inside it.

Density and `scaling` are independent. Scaling multiplies every size by
one factor (12px becomes 11.2px at 93%); density picks each number,
keeps whole pixels and holds the 12px floor. Both can be set at once.

In Storybook, the **Density** toolbar switches every story between the two.

## Touch and rem

Controls are below the 44px touch minimum in both densities on purpose:
on coarse pointers every control widens its hit area to 44px without
growing the box, so Compact does not cost touch users. Every value is in
`rem`, so it follows the user's root font size; "32px" is 32px at the
default 16px root.

import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { colorVar, type ChartColor } from './chart-utils'
import styles from './Chart.module.css'

export interface SparklineProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  /** Values in order, oldest first. Empty or null shows "No data". */
  data: number[] | null | undefined
  color?: ChartColor
  /** `area` fills under the line. */
  appearance?: 'line' | 'area'
  /**
   * Off by default: next to a figure and its change the trend is decoration.
   * Give it a name when the spark is the only place the trend is shown.
   */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/**
 * A trend with no axes, sized by its container. The viewBox stretches to any
 * width without measuring, and non-scaling-stroke keeps the line 1.25px.
 */
export function Sparkline({ data, color = 'chart-1', appearance = 'area', className, 'aria-label': ariaLabel, ...props }: SparklineProps) {
  const isEmpty = !data?.length
  let line = ''
  if (!isEmpty) {
    // A zero baseline: a spark that starts at its minimum exaggerates small swings.
    const max = Math.max(...data, 0) || 1
    const step = data.length > 1 ? 100 / (data.length - 1) : 0
    line = 'M' + data.map((v, i) => `${(i * step).toFixed(2)},${(29 - (v / max) * 27).toFixed(2)}`).join('L')
    if (data.length === 1) line += 'L100,' + line.split(',')[1]
  }
  return (
    <div {...props} className={cn(styles.spark, className)}>
      <svg viewBox="0 0 100 30" preserveAspectRatio="none" {...(ariaLabel ? { role: 'img', 'aria-label': ariaLabel } : { 'aria-hidden': true })}>
        {isEmpty ? (
          <path className={styles.sparkEmpty} d="M0,20 C25,14 40,24 60,18 S90,12 100,16" />
        ) : (
          <>
            {appearance === 'area' && <path className={styles.sparkArea} d={`${line}L100,30L0,30Z`} fill={colorVar(color)} />}
            <path className={styles.sparkLine} d={line} stroke={colorVar(color)} />
          </>
        )}
      </svg>
      {isEmpty && <span className={styles.badge}>No data</span>}
    </div>
  )
}

'use client'

import { useEffect, useState, type ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Spinner.module.css'

export interface SpinnerProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'span'>, 'children'> {
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Colour of the indicator. `accent` is the foreground, as on Button. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary'
  /** Wait this many milliseconds before showing, so a fast load never flashes a spinner. */
  delay?: number
  /** 0–100. Omit for an indeterminate, spinning indicator. */
  value?: number
  /** Spin even when `value` is given. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  /** Shown under the indicator and used as its accessible name ("Loading" when omitted). */
  label?: string
}

// Circle of radius 10 in a 24-unit viewBox: the stroke scales with the size.
const R = 10
const C = 2 * Math.PI * R

export function Spinner({
  size = 'md',
  variant = 'accent',
  delay = 0,
  value,
  isIndeterminate = false,
  label,
  className,
  ...props
}: SpinnerProps) {
  const [elapsed, setElapsed] = useState(false)
  // Always after mount, even with no delay: the live region below has to be
  // in the page before its text arrives for the text to be announced.
  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => setElapsed(true), Math.max(0, delay))
    return () => clearTimeout(timer)
  }, [delay])

  const determinate = value !== undefined && !isIndeterminate
  const clamped = determinate ? Math.min(100, Math.max(0, value)) : 0
  const name = label || 'Loading'

  const indicator = (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" className={cn(styles.svg, !determinate && styles.spinning)} aria-hidden="true">
      <circle className={styles.track} cx="12" cy="12" r={R} />
      <circle
        className={styles.indicator}
        cx="12"
        cy="12"
        r={R}
        strokeDasharray={C}
        // Indeterminate shows a quarter arc; determinate shows the value.
        strokeDashoffset={determinate ? C * (1 - clamped / 100) : C * 0.75}
      />
    </svg>
  )

  // Determinate: a progressbar that says how far along it is.
  if (determinate) {
    if (delay > 0 && !elapsed) return null
    return (
      <span
        role="progressbar"
        aria-valuenow={clamped}
        aria-valuemin={0}
        aria-valuemax={100}
        aria-label={name}
        className={cn(styles.spinner, styles[size], styles[variant], className)}
        {...props}
      >
        {indicator}
        {label && <span className={styles.label}>{label}</span>}
      </span>
    )
  }

  // Indeterminate: a polite live region that is in the page from the first
  // render, empty through the delay. Screen readers announce text inserted
  // into a live region that already exists, not a region that mounts full.
  return (
    <span
      role="status"
      aria-label={name}
      className={cn(styles.spinner, styles[size], styles[variant], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {elapsed && (
        <>
          {indicator}
          <span className={label ? styles.label : styles.hiddenLabel}>{name}</span>
        </>
      )}
    </span>
  )
}

# Spinner Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will take, o...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Spinner } from './Spinner'
import * as SpinnerStories from './Spinner.stories'

<Meta of={SpinnerStories} />

# Spinner

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will
take, or, given a value, how far along it is.

<Status of={SpinnerStories} />

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.WithLabel} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the indicator. The track and the label are the
same in all three.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Spinner variant="accent" /> `accent` | The default: a quiet placeholder in `--foreground`, inside content that has its own colour. |
| <Spinner variant="primary" /> `primary` | A load the page is about, where the brand colour helps it be found: the first load of a view. |
| <Spinner variant="secondary" /> `secondary` | Low emphasis: a spinner beside other muted text, or in a dense list. |

With a `value` it stops spinning and becomes a progress ring, which reads
better than a bar in a small space such as a thumbnail.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Determinate} />

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Sizes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Spinner } from 'zweihander/spinner'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/spinner.json
```

- Source: [src/components/loaders/Spinner.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/Spinner.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/spinner](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/spinner)
- Behaviour: a plain element; there is no behaviour here worth Base UI
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SpinnerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SpinnerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

While spinning, the indicator is a quarter of the ring turning once every
`--duration-spin`. With no `label`, a visually hidden "Loading" stands in
for it.

## Measurements

The ring is an SVG drawn in a 24-unit box and scaled to the size, so the
stroke (2.5 units) scales with it: 1.7px at `sm`, 3.3px at `lg`.

<SpecTable caption="sm" rows={[{ part: 'Ring', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-4' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="md" rows={[{ part: 'Ring', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-6' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="lg" rows={[{ part: 'Ring', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-8' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Ring to label', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'One turn', token: '--duration-spin' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'One turn, reduced motion', token: '--duration-spin-reduced' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

The indicator is the part that has to be seen, so each variant takes a
colour that clears 3:1 on the page. Switch the theme and the accent in the
toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable caption="primary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Stroke', token: '--primary-text' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="accent" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Stroke', token: '--foreground' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="secondary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Stroke', token: '--muted-foreground' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Stroke', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

## States

A spinner is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Spinning' },
    { label: 'Progress', content: <Spinner value={40} label="Uploading" variant="primary" /> },
    { label: 'Complete', content: <Spinner value={100} label="Uploaded" variant="primary" /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={SpinnerStories.WithLabel} />
</States>

- **Spinning** is the default, and what it shows with `isIndeterminate`
  even when given a `value`.
- **Progress** fills the ring clockwise from twelve o'clock, easing
  between values over `--duration-slow`.
- **Delayed**: with `delay`, nothing shows until it has passed. The live
  region is in the page, empty, from the start.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SpinnerStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the outer element.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Spinner when something is loading and you cannot say what its result
will look like or how long it will take. Use one per region that is
loading, labelled with what is coming.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SpinnerStories.DoOneForTheRegion} />}
  doCaption="One spinner for the region, named for what is coming."
  dont={<Story of={SpinnerStories.DontOnePerItem} />}
  dontCaption="A spinner per card says the same thing three times, and three screen-reader announcements."
/>

Give a load you expect to be fast a `delay` of 300–500ms. The spinner only
appears if the wait turns out to be long enough to notice.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Delay} />

## When not to use

- **When you know the shape of what is coming.** A
  [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the
  layout and says more.
- **For a long task with a known size**: an upload, an install. Use a
  [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs), or a
  `value` here when space is tight.
- **Inside a button.** Use the Button's `isLoading`: it keeps the button's
  width and focus and stops a second click.

## Accessibility

- **Spinning, it is `role="status"`**, a polite live region, named by
  `label` or "Loading". The region renders empty and its text (the label,
  or a visually hidden "Loading") is inserted just after, or once `delay`
  has passed: screen readers announce text added to a live region that is
  already in the page, not a region that mounts full.
- **With a value, it is `role="progressbar"`** with `aria-valuenow`,
  `aria-valuemin="0"` and `aria-valuemax="100"`. Values outside 0–100 are
  clamped.
- The SVG is hidden.
- The indicator clears 3:1 on the page in every variant: `--primary-text`
  (measured at 4.5:1 per accent), `--muted-foreground`, `--foreground`.
  The track is decoration and may be faint.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it slows to one turn in 2.5s rather than
  stopping, since a frozen arc reads as "stuck", and the progress ring
  stops easing between values.
- Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading, and remove the
  spinner when the load ends, so the change is announced.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Stacked List Records as rows, one under the other: people on a team, projects, files, in...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as StackedListStories from './StackedList.stories'

<Meta of={StackedListStories} />

# Stacked List

Records as rows, one under the other: people on a team, projects, files,
invoices. Each row names the record, says a little about it, and either
opens it or offers its actions. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Lists:
Stacked Lists; Polaris Resource list; Salesforce Item.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stacked-list.json
```

## Simple

An Avatar or an Icon, the `title` with a `description` under it, and
`meta` at the end: facts that help pick the row out, such as a role, an
owner or a date. A line divides the rows.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.Simple} />

## Linked

`href` makes the title a link whose target is the whole row, with a
chevron at the end to say it opens. `status` takes a Tag (or a Badge)
and puts it after the title.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.Linked} />

## With actions

`actions` takes [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs)
entries, the same as Table's `rowActions`: a ⋯ button at the end of the
row, named "Actions for" the title, and a [Context
Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-context-menu--docs) on the row
with the same entries, for right click or long press. A row with `href`
keeps the browser's own link menu instead (open in a new tab, copy the
link), so there the ⋯ button is the only way in.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.WithActions} />

A row can link and have actions: the menu takes the chevron's place and
sits above the row's link, so a click on it opens the menu, not the
record. Keep `status`, `description` and `meta` free of controls on a
linked row: the row's link covers them.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.LinkedWithActions} />

## Frame, footer and empty

The frame, the lines between rows, the footer and the empty state come
from [List Container](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-list-container--docs):
`appearance` puts the list in a card (`card`) or makes each row its own
panel (`separate`).

`footer` goes after the last row, past a divider. A list on its own page
takes a [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs);
a short list in a card or on a dashboard takes a "View all" link.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.WithPagination} />

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.WithViewAll} />

### Empty

No items shows `empty`, "Nothing here yet." by default, in place of the
list. The footer still shows.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.Empty} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={StackedListStories} />

Every `<div>` attribute passes through to the root, so a page names the
list with `role="region"` and `aria-label` when it has no heading of its
own.

## Layout

- The media column is as wide as a medium Avatar; an Icon sits in a
  filled circle of that size, and an Avatar covers it.
- `meta` sits at the end of the row while the title fits beside it, and
  wraps under the text when it does not. The list has no breakpoint of
  its own, so it works in a narrow aside as on a full page.
- Long titles, emails and paths break anywhere rather than overflow.
- Rows pad by `--space-inline` above and below, as Table rows do, and
  are at least `--row-height` tall: a one-line row without media lines up
  with a Table row of the same density.

<Canvas of={StackedListStories.LongContent} />

## Differences from the spec

- **Selection and bulk actions** (Polaris) are left out: a list you
  select from and act on in bulk is a
  [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs).
- **Actions** are a ⋯ Menu, not buttons written out in the row:
  Tailwind's "View" button is the row link, and two or more actions fit
  one menu at every width.
- **Meta** wraps under the text instead of hiding on small screens, so
  nothing is lost on a phone.

## Accessibility

- The rows are an unordered list, so a screen reader announces how many
  there are.
- The media is hidden from assistive tech: the title names the record.
- A row with `href` is one link, named by its title; the status,
  description and meta sit outside it. The chevron is decorative.
- Each row is one tab stop, two with actions: the link, then the ⋯
  button.
- The ⋯ button is named "Actions for" the title; keep `title` a string
  when there are actions, or it falls back to "Actions for item 2". The
  context menu is a shortcut to the same entries, never the only way to
  reach one.
- The list has no landmark or heading of its own. Put it under a
  heading, or pass `role="region"` and an `aria-label`.

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Card } from '../../data-display/Card'
import { Link } from '../../navigation/Link'
import styles from './Stats.module.css'

export interface StatChange {
  /** As shown, e.g. "12%" or "3.2k". */
  value: string
  direction: 'up' | 'down'
  /** Whether the change is good news. Defaults to up is good; pass it for figures where down is good, like churn. */
  isPositive?: boolean
}

export interface Stat {
  label: string
  value: ReactNode
  /** Context under or beside the value, e.g. "from 71,897". */
  previous?: ReactNode
  change?: StatChange
  /** Shown in a disc before the label. */
  icon?: ReactNode
  /** A link at the foot of the card, to where the figure comes from. */
  href?: string
  linkLabel?: string
  /** A trend under the figures, edge to edge at the foot of the card: usually a `Sparkline`. */
  chart?: ReactNode
}

export interface StatsProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'section'>, 'title'> {
  stats: Stat[]
  /** A heading above the cards, e.g. "Last 30 days". */
  title?: ReactNode
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3
}

/**
 * Key figures in a row of cards: a label, a value, and optionally the
 * change since last period, an icon and a link to the details.
 */
export function Stats({ stats, title, headingLevel = 2, className, ...props }: StatsProps) {
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  return (
    <section className={cn(styles.stats, className)} {...props}>
      {title && <Heading className={styles.title}>{title}</Heading>}
      <dl className={styles.grid}>
        {stats.map((stat) => {
          const positive = stat.change ? (stat.change.isPositive ?? stat.change.direction === 'up') : undefined
          return (
            <Card key={stat.label} appearance="outline" className={cn(styles.card, stat.icon !== undefined && styles.withIcon)}>
              <dt className={styles.label}>
                {/* Inside the dt: a dl's groups may hold only dt and dd. */}
                {stat.icon && (
                  <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
                    {stat.icon}
                  </span>
                )}
                {stat.label}
              </dt>
              <dd className={styles.figures}>
                <span className={styles.value}>{stat.value}</span>
                {stat.previous && <span className={styles.previous}>{stat.previous}</span>}
                {stat.change && (
                  <span className={cn(styles.change, positive ? styles.positive : styles.negative)}>
                    <Icon name={stat.change.direction === 'up' ? 'chevron-up' : 'chevron-down'} />
                    {/* The arrow and the colour say it at a glance; the words say it to everyone. */}
                    <span className={styles.srOnly}>{stat.change.direction === 'up' ? 'Increased by' : 'Decreased by'} </span>
                    {stat.change.value}
                  </span>
                )}
              </dd>
              {stat.href && (
                <dd className={styles.footer}>
                  <Link href={stat.href} size="sm" underline="hover">
                    {stat.linkLabel ?? 'View all'}
                    <span className={styles.srOnly}> {stat.label}</span>
                  </Link>
                </dd>
              )}
              {stat.chart && <dd className={styles.chart}>{stat.chart}</dd>}
            </Card>
          )
        })}
      </dl>
    </section>
  )
}

# Stats Key figures in a row of cards: what is measured, the figure, and optionally how it...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as StatsStories from './Stats.stories'

<Meta of={StatsStories} />

# Stats

Key figures in a row of cards: what is measured, the figure, and
optionally how it moved since the last period, an icon, and a link to
the details. The top of a dashboard or a report.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stats.json
```

## Simple

<Canvas of={StatsStories.Simple} />

## With trend

`previous` gives the figure to compare against; `change` says by how
much and which way. The colour follows whether the change is good news,
not its direction: pass `isPositive: true` for figures where down is
good, like churn or response time.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithTrend} />

## With icon and link

An icon on a rounded square of the primary colour, and a link at the foot of each
card to where the figure comes from.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithIconAndLink} />

## With sparkline

A trend at the foot of each card, edge to edge: pass a `Sparkline` as the
stat's `chart`. Leave out the spark where the period has no data and the
card would only say "No data" twice.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithSparkline} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stats` | `Stat[]` | – | Required. See below. |
| `title` | node | – | A heading above the cards. |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

Each `Stat` has `label`, `value`, and optionally `previous`, `change`
(`{ value, direction: 'up' \| 'down', isPositive? }`), `icon`, `href`,
`linkLabel` (default "View all") and `chart` (a node at the foot of the card,
usually a `Sparkline`).

<Controls of={StatsStories.Simple} />

## Layout

- As many 14rem columns as fit: three or four on a desktop, one on a
  phone. Cards in a row share a height.

  <Canvas of={StatsStories.Narrow} />

- Figures use tabular numbers, so a row of values lines up digit by digit
  and does not jitter when it updates.

## Accessibility

- A definition list: each figure is the definition of its label, so a
  screen reader reads "Total subscribers, 71,897".
- The change is read as words ("Increased by 12%"), not only shown as an
  arrow and a colour. The colours are `--success-text` and `--danger-text`
  on their subtle surfaces, 4.5:1 in both appearances.
- Each "View all" link carries its figure's label for screen readers
  ("View all Avg. open rate"), so a list of links is not three identical
  entries.
- The icon is decorative.
- The sparkline is decorative too (`aria-hidden`): the change already says
  the trend in words.

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Stepper.module.css'

export interface StepperStep {
  label: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  /** Override the status worked out from `current`, e.g. to flag a step with an error. */
  status?: 'complete' | 'current' | 'upcoming' | 'error'
}

export interface StepperProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  steps: StepperStep[]
  /** 0-based index of the step the reader is on. Steps before it are complete. */
  current: number
  /** Ignored with `appearance="bullets"`, which is always one row. */
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /**
   * `circles` shows every step's marker and label. `bullets` shows only
   * the current step's label ("Step 2 of 4: Workspace") over a row of
   * dots, for a narrow space or a longer flow.
   */
  appearance?: 'circles' | 'bullets'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /**
   * Makes finished steps (and the current one) buttons that go back to
   * them. Upcoming steps stay plain: they cannot be skipped to.
   */
  onStepClick?: (index: number) => void
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

const statusText = { complete: 'completed', current: 'current', upcoming: 'not started', error: 'has an error' }

export function Stepper({
  steps,
  current,
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  appearance = 'circles',
  size = 'md',
  onStepClick,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Progress',
  className,
  ...props
}: StepperProps) {
  const bullets = appearance === 'bullets'
  const currentStep = steps[current]
  return (
    <nav
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      className={cn(styles.stepper, bullets ? styles.bullets : styles[orientation], styles[size], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {/* Hidden from screen readers: the list already says each step's position and status. */}
      {bullets && currentStep && (
        <p className={styles.summary} aria-hidden="true">
          <span className={styles.count}>
            Step {current + 1} of {steps.length}:
          </span>{' '}
          <span className={styles.label}>{currentStep.label}</span>
        </p>
      )}
      <ol className={styles.list}>
        {steps.map((step, i) => {
          const status = step.status ?? (i < current ? 'complete' : i === current ? 'current' : 'upcoming')
          const clickable = onStepClick !== undefined && status !== 'upcoming'
          const marker = (
            <span className={styles.marker} aria-hidden="true">
              {bullets ? null : status === 'complete' ? <Icon name="check" /> : status === 'error' ? <Icon name="danger" /> : i + 1}
            </span>
          )
          // Bullets show only the dot: the label and status are said, not shown.
          const text = (
            <span className={cn(styles.text, bullets && styles.srOnly)}>
              <span className={styles.label}>
                {step.label}
                {/* Said, not shown: the marker carries it visually. */}
                <span className={styles.srOnly}>, {statusText[status]}</span>
              </span>
              {step.description && <span className={styles.description}>{step.description}</span>}
            </span>
          )
          return (
            <li
              key={i}
              className={cn(styles.step, styles[status])}
              // An error on the current step does not stop it being where the reader is.
              aria-current={status === 'current' || i === current ? 'step' : undefined}
            >
              {clickable ? (
                <button type="button" className={styles.target} onClick={() => onStepClick(i)}>
                  {marker}
                  {text}
                </button>
              ) : (
                <span className={styles.target}>
                  {marker}
                  {text}
                </span>
              )}
              {!bullets && i < steps.length - 1 && <span className={styles.connector} aria-hidden="true" />}
            </li>
          )
        })}
      </ol>
    </nav>
  )
}

# Stepper Shows where the reader is in a flow of a few ordered steps: sign-up, checkout, a...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as StepperStories from './Stepper.stories'

<Meta of={StepperStories} />

# Stepper

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Shows where the reader is in a flow of a few ordered steps: sign-up,
checkout, a setup wizard.

<Status of={StepperStories} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Horizontal (default) | Three to five steps above a form. The label sits under its marker, so every step gets the same width whatever its label. |
| Vertical | Steps with long descriptions, or a narrow column beside the form. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a dialog, a side panel. |
| Bullets (`appearance="bullets"`) | A phone, a narrow dialog, or more steps than fit with labels: only the current step's label shows, "Step 3 of 4: Invite", over a row of dots. |
| Navigable (`onStepClick`) | Flows where going back to fix an earlier step is normal. Finished steps become buttons. |

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Navigable} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Bullets} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Stepper } from 'zweihander/stepper'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stepper.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/stepper](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/stepper)
- Behaviour: a plain `<nav>` around an ordered list
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={StepperStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={StepperStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The last step has no connector. Vertical, the connector runs down from
each marker, beside the text.
