'use client'

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Toggle } from '@base-ui/react/toggle'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Button, type ButtonProps } from './Button'
import styles from './ToggleButton.module.css'

interface ToggleButtonBaseProps
  extends Omit<ComponentProps<'button'>, 'ref' | 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onChange'> {
  // Always a <button> (Button itself may be an <a>, hence its wider type).
  ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>
  /** Colour of the pressed state. Unpressed is always neutral. */
  variant?: ButtonProps['variant']
  /** Style of the pressed state. */
  appearance?: ButtonProps['appearance']
  size?: ButtonProps['size']
  startIcon?: ReactNode
  endIcon?: ReactNode
  isLoading?: boolean
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Controlled pressed state (the spec's `isSelected`). */
  pressed?: boolean
  defaultPressed?: boolean
  /** Base UI's second argument (event details) is dropped: nothing here needs it. */
  onPressedChange?: (pressed: boolean) => void
  /** Identifies the toggle inside a group. */
  value?: string
}

/** An icon-only toggle has no text to name it, so `aria-label` is required. */
export type ToggleButtonProps =
  | (ToggleButtonBaseProps & { isIconOnly?: false })
  | (ToggleButtonBaseProps & { isIconOnly: true; 'aria-label': string })

export function ToggleButton({
  variant = 'primary',
  appearance = 'contained',
  size,
  startIcon,
  endIcon,
  isLoading,
  isFullWidth,
  isIconOnly,
  pressed,
  defaultPressed,
  onPressedChange,
  disabled,
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: ToggleButtonProps) {
  return (
    <Toggle
      {...props}
      pressed={pressed}
      defaultPressed={defaultPressed}
      onPressedChange={onPressedChange && ((next) => onPressedChange(next))}
      disabled={disabled}
      render={(toggleProps, state) => {
        const buttonProps = {
          ...toggleProps,
          // Off is the same neutral button whatever the pressed style is, so
          // "on" is always the one that stands out.
          variant: state.pressed ? variant : 'secondary',
          appearance: state.pressed ? appearance : appearance === 'ghost' ? 'ghost' : 'outlined',
          size,
          startIcon,
          endIcon,
          isLoading,
          isFullWidth,
          // Its aria-label reached Toggle with the other props and comes back
          // in toggleProps, which is what Button's icon-only type asks for.
          isIconOnly,
          // A disabled ToggleGroup disables its toggles through state.
          disabled: state.disabled,
          className: cn(state.pressed && appearance !== 'contained' && styles.tinted, className),
          children,
        } as ButtonProps
        return <Button {...buttonProps} />
      }}
    />
  )
}

# Toggle Button A button that stays pressed: bold on or off, following or not, a filter ap...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { ToggleButton } from './ToggleButton'
import * as ToggleButtonStories from './ToggleButton.stories'

<Meta of={ToggleButtonStories} />

# Toggle Button

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A button that stays pressed: bold on or off, following or not, a filter
applied or not. It looks like a [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).

<Status of={ToggleButtonStories} />

<Canvas of={ToggleButtonStories.Default} />

## Variants

Unpressed is always the same neutral button, so the pressed one is the one
that stands out. `variant` and `appearance` choose how it looks when
pressed. Each pair below: unpressed, then pressed.

<Canvas of={ToggleButtonStories.Matrix} />

| Appearance when pressed | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `contained` | A toggle that should read as clearly on from across the screen: a filter, Follow. |
| `outlined` | A toggle among other outlined controls. Pressed, it fills neutral and keeps the variant's border. |
| `ghost` | Toolbars and dense rows: Bold, Italic, a star. Usually `isIconOnly`. |

<Canvas of={ToggleButtonStories.IconOnly} />

<Canvas of={ToggleButtonStories.WithIcon} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ToggleButton } from 'zweihander/toggle-button'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/toggle-button.json
```

- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/toggle-button](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/toggle-button)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Toggle](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>

## Color

Unpressed is the same in every variant. Pressed and `contained` takes the
variant's solid, as on Button. Pressed `outlined` and `ghost` fill with the
neutral secondary instead of a tint of the variant: a toggle stays pressed
indefinitely, so its label has to pass 4.5:1 on the fill, and red text on a
red tint measures 3.7:1.

## States

Hover, focus, disabled and loading behave as on Button, in both the
pressed and the unpressed look.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ToggleButtonStories} />
</div>

Every other `<button>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **Two sizes, not four.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`pressed`, `defaultPressed`, `onPressedChange`** instead of
  `isSelected`: Base UI's names, per the kit's convention for components
  built on it. "Pressed" is also the ARIA word (`aria-pressed`).
- **`disabled`**, not `isDisabled`.
- **`variant` and `appearance` describe the pressed state.** The spec
  applies them to the button without saying what changes when it is
  selected. If unpressed also took them, a contained toggle would look
  pressed whether it was or not.
- **A pressed outlined or ghost toggle is filled neutral, not tinted with
  its variant.** It stays in that state indefinitely, so its label has to
  pass 4.5:1 on the fill.
- **`isIconOnly`**, as on Button.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a toggle for a setting that is on or off and applies immediately:
Bold, Follow, a filter. The label names the setting, and stays the same in
both states.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ToggleButtonStories.DoSameLabel} />}
  doCaption="The label names the setting; pressed says it is on. A screen reader hears “Follow, toggle button, pressed”."
  dont={<Story of={ToggleButtonStories.DontSwitchLabel} />}
  dontCaption="A label that flips to the action reads as “Unfollow, pressed”, which contradicts itself."
/>

<Canvas of={ToggleButtonStories.Controlled} />

## When not to use

- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a Checkbox or a Switch: a
  toggle applies at once, a form field waits for Submit.
- **For one of many.** Put the toggles in a
  [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttons-buttongroup--docs), or use
  radios or Tabs. A lone toggle is independent: pressing one does not
  release another.
- **For an action.** Something that happens once (Save, Send) is a
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).

## Accessibility

- A native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader announces
  "Subscribe, toggle button, pressed".
- **Keep the label the same in both states.** `aria-pressed` carries the
  state; a label that switches from "Follow" to "Unfollow" as well reads
  as "Unfollow, pressed", which contradicts itself.
- Enter and Space both toggle it.
- `isIconOnly` needs `aria-label`, as on Button.
- `isLoading` keeps it focusable but inert, as on Button.
- 44×44px touch target at `sm` and `md`, from Button.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { ToggleGroup as BaseToggleGroup } from '@base-ui/react/toggle-group'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './ButtonGroup.module.css'

export type ButtonGroupProps = ComponentProps<'div'>

/** Buttons joined into one bar: related actions that read as a set. */
export function ButtonGroup({ className, ...props }: ButtonGroupProps) {
  return <div role="group" {...props} className={cn(styles.group, className)} />
}

export interface ToggleGroupProps
  extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'defaultValue' | 'onChange' | 'dir'> {
  /** Controlled: the `value` of each pressed ToggleButton. */
  value?: string[]
  /** Uncontrolled: the values pressed at first. */
  defaultValue?: string[]
  /** Base UI's second argument (event details) is dropped: nothing here needs it. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string[]) => void
  /** Any number pressed at once. Without it, one at a time: a segmented control. */
  multiple?: boolean
  /** Disables every toggle in the group. */
  disabled?: boolean
}

/** ToggleButtons joined into one bar, sharing one selection. */
export function ToggleGroup({ onValueChange, multiple = false, className, ...props }: ToggleGroupProps) {
  return (
    <BaseToggleGroup
      {...props}
      multiple={multiple}
      onValueChange={(next, details) => {
        // Single choice is a segmented control: once a segment is chosen,
        // pressing it again does not leave none chosen.
        if (!multiple && next.length === 0) return details.cancel()
        onValueChange?.(next)
      }}
      className={cn(styles.group, className)}
    />
  )
}

# Button Group

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Buttons joined into one bar. `ToggleGroup` joins
[Toggle Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) that
share one selection; `ButtonGroup` joins plain
[Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) that act.

<Status of={ButtonGroupStories} />

Button Group is outside the 1.0 component list, so it starts as experimental.

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Form | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `ToggleGroup`, single | A segmented control: one view, one mode, one period at a time. |
| `ToggleGroup multiple` | Settings that combine: status filters, Bold and Italic. |
| `ButtonGroup` | Related actions that read as a set: previous and next, zoom in and out. |

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.Multiple} />

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.Actions} />

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.IconOnly} />

- Behaviour: [Base UI Toggle Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle-group)

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ButtonGroupStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ButtonGroupStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The buttons keep their own anatomy; the container only joins them.

## Measurements

The group adds no size of its own. Each button keeps its tier, so a group
of `sm` buttons is `--control-sm` tall. Inner corners are square and each
button after the first overlaps the one before by its 1px border, so two
outlined buttons share one line. The outer corners keep the buttons'
radius.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Outer corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Outer corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

The group paints nothing: unpressed and pressed colours are the Toggle
Button's, and a ButtonGroup's are each Button's. The pressed toggle is
raised over its neighbours so its own border wins where they overlap.

<SpecTable
  caption="Default toggles"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Button, unpressed', property: 'Border', token: '--input' },
    { part: 'Selected', property: 'Background', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Selected', property: 'Label', token: '--primary-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={ButtonGroupStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ButtonGroupStories.Default} />
</States>

Hover, focus and pressed are each button's own. The focused button is
raised over its neighbours so the ring is never cut.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ButtonGroupStories} />
</div>

The table is `ToggleGroup`'s. `ButtonGroup` takes only `<div>` attributes:
`aria-label` names it. Both pass every other `<div>` attribute through.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use `ToggleGroup` when the toggles answer one question (which view, which
filters) and `ButtonGroup` when a few actions belong together. Give every
button in a group the same variant and appearance, so the pressed one is
the only one that stands out.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ButtonGroupStories.DoSameLook} />}
  doCaption="One look across the group: only the pressed segment stands out."
  dont={<Story of={ButtonGroupStories.DontMixLooks} />}
  dontCaption="A different variant per button reads as several states at once."
/>

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.Controlled} />

## When not to use

- **To switch between panels of content.** Use Tabs: they own the panel
  and its `tabpanel` role.
- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a Radio group or Checkboxes:
  a toggle applies at once, a form field waits for Submit.
- **For unrelated actions.** Lay out separate Buttons with a gap; joining
  them says they belong together.
- **For more than a handful of options.** Use a Select.

## Accessibility

- Both containers have `role="group"`; name them with `aria-label`.
- Each toggle is a native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader
  announces "Board, toggle button, pressed".
- A `ToggleGroup` is one tab stop. Arrow keys move between its toggles
  and wrap, Home and End jump to the first and last; Space or Enter
  presses.
- Single choice keeps one pressed: pressing the pressed toggle again does
  not release it.
- A `ButtonGroup`'s buttons are each a tab stop, with no `aria-pressed`.
- A disabled `ToggleGroup` disables every toggle in it.
- An icon-only button needs its own `aria-label`, as on Button. A
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) can show that
  label to sighted users: it merges onto the button instead of wrapping
  it, so the buttons still join.

  <Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.WithTooltips} />

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, useState, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { PreviewCard } from '@base-ui/react/preview-card'
import { Tooltip as BaseTooltip } from '@base-ui/react/tooltip'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Tooltip.module.css'

export interface TooltipProps {
  /** What the tooltip says. Short: a label or a hint, never the only way to learn something essential. */
  content: ReactNode
  /** The trigger: one focusable element, such as a Button. Its props are merged, not wrapped. */
  children: ReactElement
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  /** Milliseconds of hover before it opens. Focus opens it at once. */
  delay?: number
  closeDelay?: number
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Never open, e.g. while the trigger's label is already visible. */
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Where the tooltip renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
}

export function Tooltip({
  content,
  children,
  side = 'top',
  align = 'center',
  delay = 300,
  closeDelay = 0,
  open: openProp,
  defaultOpen = false,
  onOpenChange,
  disabled = false,
  container,
  className,
}: TooltipProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [openState, setOpenState] = useState(defaultOpen)
  const open = openProp ?? openState
  return (
    <BaseTooltip.Root
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={(next) => {
        setOpenState(next)
        onOpenChange?.(next)
      }}
      disabled={disabled}
    >
      <BaseTooltip.Trigger
        delay={delay}
        closeDelay={closeDelay}
        render={children}
        // Base UI leaves tooltips out of the accessibility tree; while one is
        // open, point the trigger at it so it is read as a description.
        aria-describedby={open ? id : undefined}
      />
      <BaseTooltip.Portal container={container}>
        <BaseTooltip.Positioner className={styles.positioner} side={side} align={align} sideOffset={6}>
          <BaseTooltip.Popup id={id} role="tooltip" className={cn(styles.popup, className)}>
            {content}
          </BaseTooltip.Popup>
        </BaseTooltip.Positioner>
      </BaseTooltip.Portal>
    </BaseTooltip.Root>
  )
}

/** Tooltips inside share one delay: once one has opened, moving to the next opens it at once. */
export const TooltipGroup = BaseTooltip.Provider

export interface HoverCardProps {
  /** The trigger: a link to what the card previews. Its props are merged, not wrapped. */
  trigger: ReactElement
  /** Usually an Avatar, at the card's start. */
  avatar?: ReactNode
  /** The name of what is previewed: a person, a record, a document. */
  title: ReactNode
  /** One or two lines of meta under the title: role, team, last active. */
  description?: ReactNode
  /** A shortcut, such as a Button. Keyboard focus cannot reach it, so the page the trigger links to must offer it too. */
  action?: ReactNode
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  /** Milliseconds of hover or focus before it opens. */
  delay?: number
  /** Milliseconds before it closes once the pointer leaves, so the pointer can cross to the card. */
  closeDelay?: number
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Where the card renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
}

/** A preview of a person or record on hover or focus of a link to it, on Base UI PreviewCard. */
export function HoverCard({
  trigger,
  avatar,
  title,
  description,
  action,
  side = 'bottom',
  align = 'start',
  delay = 600,
  closeDelay = 300,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  container,
  className,
}: HoverCardProps) {
  return (
    // Base UI's second argument (event details) is dropped, as in Popover.
    <PreviewCard.Root open={open} defaultOpen={defaultOpen} onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}>
      <PreviewCard.Trigger render={trigger} delay={delay} closeDelay={closeDelay} />
      <PreviewCard.Portal container={container}>
        <PreviewCard.Positioner className={styles.cardPositioner} side={side} align={align} sideOffset={6}>
          <PreviewCard.Popup className={cn(styles.card, className)}>
            {avatar && <div className={styles.cardAvatar}>{avatar}</div>}
            <div className={styles.cardTitle}>{title}</div>
            {description && <div className={styles.cardDescription}>{description}</div>}
            {action && <div className={styles.cardAction}>{action}</div>}
          </PreviewCard.Popup>
        </PreviewCard.Positioner>
      </PreviewCard.Portal>
    </PreviewCard.Root>
  )
}

# Tooltip A short label that appears when you hover over or focus a control: the name of a...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as TooltipStories from './Tooltip.stories'
import { HoverCard } from './Tooltip'

<Meta of={TooltipStories} />

# Tooltip

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A short label that appears when you hover over or focus a control: the
name of an icon-only button, a keyboard shortcut, a one-line hint. Its
sibling `HoverCard` previews a person or record behind a link.

<Status of={TooltipStories} />

<Canvas of={TooltipStories.LongContent} />

## Variants

| Variant | When to use |
|---|---|
| Tooltip | A label or a one-line hint on a control. |
| Hover card | A preview of a person or record on a link to it: avatar, name, meta and an optional action. |

The tooltip opens on hover after a short delay and on keyboard focus at
once. Wrap a row of tooltips in `TooltipGroup` so that
once one has opened, moving to the next opens it without the delay:

<Canvas of={TooltipStories.Group} />

Only one tooltip is open at a time: opening one closes any other. Hover or
focus the triggers above to see them.

### Hover card

`HoverCard` opens after 600ms of hover or focus on a link and stays open
for 300ms after the pointer leaves, so the pointer can cross to it. It is
drawn like a Popover, a raised surface, not an inverted label:

<Canvas of={TooltipStories.HoverCardPicture} />

Hover the name to open the real one:

<Canvas of={TooltipStories.HoverCardPerson} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { HoverCard, Tooltip, TooltipGroup } from 'zweihander/tooltip'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tooltip.json
```

- Source: [src/components/overlays/Tooltip.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Tooltip.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tooltip](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tooltip)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Tooltip](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip), [Base UI Preview Card](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TooltipStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TooltipStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open tooltips on this tab and the next are pictures: real tooltips
held open and rendered in place with `container`, laid out above the
trigger where they open.

The hover card, open under its link:

<Anatomy parts={TooltipStories.hoverCardParts}>
  <Story of={TooltipStories.HoverCardAnatomy} />
</Anatomy>

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Container"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

The container is as wide as its text, at most 20rem and never wider than
the room beside the trigger; longer text wraps. It opens 6px from the
trigger, on the `--layer-tooltip` layer, above popovers and modals, so a
tooltip on a control inside one still shows. It fades in over
`--duration-fast`.

<SpecTable
  caption="Hover card"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-md' },
    { part: 'Avatar to text', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Text to action', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-3' },
    { part: 'Name', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Meta', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

The hover card is as wide as its content, at most 20rem. It opens 6px
under the link, start-aligned, on the `--layer-overlay` layer with
Popover, below tooltips.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Every tooltip"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Colour', token: '--background' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Hover card"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Name', property: 'Colour', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Meta', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

The tooltip is inverted in both modes: a tooltip is not part of the page, and the
dark-on-light (light-on-dark in dark mode) box says so, at the same
contrast as body text.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Closed', content: <Story of={TooltipStories.Closed} /> },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={TooltipStories.OpenPicture} /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Closed** until the pointer rests on the trigger for `delay` (300ms), or
  the trigger takes keyboard focus, which opens it at once.
- **Open** until Escape, blur or the pointer leaves, after `closeDelay`.
  Opening fades it in and scales it up from 96%.
- The trigger keeps the states of its own component; the tooltip has none
  of its own.
- The hover card has the same two states, after `delay` (600ms) of hover
  or focus and `closeDelay` (300ms) after the pointer leaves both the link
  and the card.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TooltipStories} />
</div>

`TooltipGroup` is Base UI's `Tooltip.Provider`: tooltips inside it share
one delay.

### HoverCard

<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={HoverCard} />
</div>

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Tooltip for a label or a hint: the name of an icon-only button, a
keyboard shortcut, one line on what a control does. 300ms before it opens
is quick enough to feel responsive and long enough that tooltips do not
flash as the pointer crosses a toolbar.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TooltipStories.DoShortLabel} />}
  doCaption="A short label that repeats the icon-only button's name for sighted users."
  dont={<Story of={TooltipStories.DontEssentialInfo} />}
  dontCaption="Rules the reader needs to fill the field. Touch cannot open a tooltip, and it hides as soon as focus moves on: put the rules under the field."
/>

## When not to use

- **For anything a reader needs to finish a task.** Put it on the page: a
  tooltip cannot be reached by touch, and it disappears the moment you
  look away.
- **For links, buttons or other interactive content.** Hover and touch
  cannot reach the tooltip. Use a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs).
- **For a rich preview.** A tooltip holds text only. To preview a person
  or record behind a link, use `HoverCard`. Its action is a shortcut, so
  the linked page must offer the same action.
- **On a disabled button.** It is not focusable, so its tooltip never opens
  by keyboard. Put the reason it is disabled in text next to it.

## Accessibility

- It opens on hover after `delay` and on keyboard focus at once, and
  closes on Escape, blur or pointer leave.

  <Canvas of={TooltipStories.Default} />

- Base UI keeps tooltips out of the accessibility tree. This component
  gives the popup `role="tooltip"` and, while it is open, points the
  trigger's `aria-describedby` at it, so it is read as a description.
- It is a **description, not a name.** An icon-only button still needs its
  own `aria-label`; the tooltip then shows that label to sighted users too.
- The trigger must be focusable: a Button, a link, a field.
- `--background` on `--foreground` reads at 16:1 or more in both modes.

### Hover card

- The trigger is a link to what the card previews. Hover or keyboard focus
  on it opens the card; Escape closes it.

  <Canvas of={TooltipStories.HoverCardFocus} />

- The card is a visual preview, not a dialog: focus stays on the link and
  Tab moves past the card, its action included. Touch has no hover, so
  everything on it must be on the page the link opens.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { createContext, useContext, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './TopBar.module.css'

/**
 * What the shell's pieces need from the App Shell around them: the brand,
 * whether it takes a sidebar-wide cell, where a NavSidebar's top row puts
 * it, and whether the shell is narrower than 64rem, where a NavSidebar is
 * the icon rail. Outside a shell, none of it applies.
 */
export const ShellContext = createContext<{
  brand: ReactNode
  brandCell: boolean
  isNarrow: boolean
  /** The logo for a NavSidebar's top row: the sidebar layout, while the sidebar is expanded. */
  sidebarBrand: ReactNode
}>({
  brand: null,
  brandCell: false,
  isNarrow: false,
  sidebarBrand: null,
})

/** `null`, `false` and `undefined` render nothing. */
const given = (node: ReactNode) => node != null && node !== false

export interface TopBarProps extends ComponentProps<'header'> {
  /** Breadcrumbs, or TopBarNav links. */
  start?: ReactNode
  /** Search, notifications, the account menu. */
  end?: ReactNode
  children?: ReactNode
}

/** The bar above the page. Inside an App Shell it shows the shell's brand. */
export function TopBar({ start, end, children, className, ...props }: TopBarProps) {
  const shell = useContext(ShellContext)
  return (
    <header className={cn(styles.header, className)} data-brand-cell={shell.brandCell || undefined} {...props}>
      {given(shell.brand) && <div className={styles.brand}>{shell.brand}</div>}
      {start && <div className={styles.start}>{start}</div>}
      {children && <div className={styles.center}>{children}</div>}
      {end && <div className={styles.end}>{end}</div>}
    </header>
  )
}

export interface TopBarNavItem {
  label: string
  href: string
}

export interface TopBarNavProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  items: TopBarNavItem[]
  /** The href of the page you are on. */
  currentHref?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/** Navigation links across the Top Bar. When they do not fit, they scroll sideways. */
export function TopBarNav({ items, currentHref, className, 'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Main', ...props }: TopBarNavProps) {
  return (
    <nav aria-label={ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.nav, className)} {...props}>
      <ul>
        {items.map((item) => (
          <li key={item.href}>
            <a href={item.href} className={styles.navLink} aria-current={item.href === currentHref ? 'page' : undefined}>
              {item.label}
            </a>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </nav>
  )
}

# Top Bar The bar above the page: `start`, a middle and `end` slots, and `TopBarNav` for n...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TopBarStories from './TopBar.stories'

<Meta of={TopBarStories} />

# Top Bar

The bar above the page: `start`, a middle and `end` slots, and `TopBarNav`
for navigation links across it. One of the three pieces the
[App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) template places; inside
one it also shows the shell's `brand`. It was `AppHeader` (and
`TopBarNav` was `AppNav`).

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/top-bar.json
```

## Search and actions

<Canvas of={TopBarStories.Default} />

## Top navigation

`TopBarNav` takes `items` (`{ label, href }[]`) and `currentHref`. Links
that do not fit scroll sideways, so on a phone they stay in the bar.

<Canvas of={TopBarStories.WithNavigation} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | node | – | Breadcrumbs, or TopBarNav links. |
| `children` | node | – | The middle, e.g. a wide search field. |
| `end` | node | – | Search, notifications, the account menu. |

## Layout

- The bar is one row, `--control-md` plus two `--space-cluster` tall, so
  it follows density. Its fill and edge come from the App Shell's top cell
  (solid or transparent), not from the bar.
- In the shell's top-bar layout with a sidebar, the brand takes a cell as
  wide as the sidebar (`--sidebar-width`), so the logo sits where it sits
  in the sidebar layout.
- Breakpoints read the container, which in an app is the shell.

## Accessibility

- The bar is a `header`; inside an App Shell it is the page's banner.
- `TopBarNav` is a `nav` named "Main"; the current page has
  `aria-current="page"` and is shown by more than colour.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import type { CSSProperties } from 'react'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

/** A type role is a size, a line height and a weight together. */
const role = (name: string, weight: number): CSSProperties => ({
  fontSize: `var(--text-${name})`,
  lineHeight: `var(--leading-${name})`,
  fontWeight: weight,
})

const HEADINGS = [
  { token: 'heading-2xl', px: '32 / 36' },
  { token: 'heading-xl', px: '28 / 32' },
  { token: 'heading-lg', px: '24 / 28' },
  { token: 'heading-md', px: '20 / 24' },
  { token: 'heading-sm', px: '16 / 20' },
  { token: 'heading-xs', px: '14 / 20' },
  { token: 'heading-2xs', px: '12 / 16' },
] as const

const BODY = [
  { token: 'body-lg', px: '16 / 24' },
  { token: 'body', px: '14 / 20' },
  { token: 'body-sm', px: '12 / 16' },
  { token: 'body-xs', px: '11 / 16' },
] as const

function Row({ token, px, weight }: { token: string; px: string; weight: number }) {
  return (
    <div
      className={docs.rowBaseline}
      style={{ borderBottom: '1px solid var(--border)', padding: 'var(--space-2) 0' }}
    >
      <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '10rem', flexShrink: 0 }}>
        --text-{token}
      </span>
      <span style={{ flex: 1, ...role(token, weight) }}>Zweihänder</span>
      <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '7rem', textAlign: 'right' }}>
        {px}
      </span>
    </div>
  )
}

const WEIGHTS = [
  { value: 400, name: 'regular' },
  { value: 500, name: 'medium' },
  { value: 600, name: 'semibold' },
  { value: 700, name: 'bold' },
] as const

// Narrative and prose live in Typography.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Typography',
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Headings: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column' }}>
      {HEADINGS.map((h) => (
        <Row key={h.token} {...h} weight={700} />
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const el = canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder')[0]
    // A heading role carries its weight, not just its size.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(el).fontWeight).toBe('700')
    await expect(Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize)).toBe(32)
  },
}

export const Body: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column' }}>
      {BODY.map((b) => (
        <Row key={b.token} {...b} weight={400} />
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const el = canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder')[1]
    // body is 14px, one step down from the 16px many interfaces start at.
    await expect(Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize)).toBe(14)
    // Every body line sits on the 4px grid at 100% scaling.
    for (const sample of canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder')) {
      await expect(Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(sample).lineHeight) % 4).toBeCloseTo(0, 5)
    }
  },
}

export const Weights: Story = {

          <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '8rem', flexShrink: 0 }}>

          </span>

  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const bold = canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder').at(-1)!

}

export const Families: Story = {

      <div className={docs.stack}>
        <span className={docs.caption}>--font-sans</span>
        <span style={{ ...role('heading-md', 700), fontFamily: 'var(--font-sans)' }}>
          Zweihänder — system-ui 0123
        </span>
      </div>
      <div className={docs.stack}>
        <span className={docs.caption}>--font-mono</span>
        <span style={{ ...role('heading-md', 700), fontFamily: 'var(--font-mono)' }}>

# Typography Type is **role-based**: you reach for `--text-heading-lg` or `--text-body`, n...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TypographyStories from './Typography.stories'

<Meta of={TypographyStories} />

# Typography

Type is **role-based**: you reach for `--text-heading-lg` or `--text-body`,
not a size. Each role carries its size, line height and weight together, so a
heading cannot end up at body weight or a body line height by omission.

The alternative — a purely dimensional scale, where a name says how big and
never what it is for — is what this replaces. Each role is three variables
that belong together:

```css
.heading {
  font-size: var(--text-heading-lg);
  line-height: var(--leading-heading-lg);
  font-weight: 700;
}
```

## The typeface

One face: the platform UI font. Nothing is downloaded, and text looks the
way the rest of the operating system does — San Francisco on Apple, Segoe UI
on Windows, Roboto on Android.

```css
--font-sans: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …
--font-mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, …
```

Components read two role tokens rather than the face directly, so a
product can give headings or prose their own face without touching a
component:

| Role | Default | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--font-heading` | `var(--font-sans)` | Page titles, `Modal` and `EmptyState` titles |
| `--font-prose` | `var(--font-sans)` | long-form reading text; no component reads it yet |

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Families} />

**There is nothing to load.** To use a brand face instead, load it yourself
and point the tokens at it (see **Customization**).

## Headings

Seven steps, all bold. The line height tightens as the size grows, which
is the thing a single ratio applied across a whole scale gets wrong.

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Headings} />

| Role | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--text-heading-2xl` | 2rem / 32px | 36px |
| `--text-heading-xl` | 1.75rem / 28px | 32px |
| `--text-heading-lg` | 1.5rem / 24px | 28px |
| `--text-heading-md` | 1.25rem / 20px | 24px |
| `--text-heading-sm` | 1rem / 16px | 20px |
| `--text-heading-xs` | 0.875rem / 14px | 20px |
| `--text-heading-2xs` | 0.75rem / 12px | 16px |

Note that headings go *below* body size: `--text-heading-2xs` is 12px. Those
bottom steps are for labels and section eyebrows — a heading role is about
the semantic weight of the text, not about being large.

## Body

Four steps. `--text-body` is the default at 14px — one step down from the
16px a lot of interfaces start at, which is deliberate for dense product
UI and worth knowing before you reach for it in long-form content.

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Body} />

| Role | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--text-body-lg` | 1rem / 16px | 24px |
| `--text-body` | 0.875rem / 14px | 20px |
| `--text-body-sm` | 0.75rem / 12px | 16px |
| `--text-body-xs` | 0.6875rem / 11px | 16px |

**Every component uses these.** Button, the field label, the input itself,
and the helper and error text are all `--text-body`; only the large Button
steps up to `--text-body-lg`.

`--text-body-sm` is the label of every small control (the `sm` and `xs`
size tiers, see [Sizing](?path=/docs/foundations-sizing--docs)), and
secondary text: helper text in a menu, shortcuts, captions.

`--text-body-xs` is for dense metadata only: badge counts, timestamps,
table footnotes. Badge is the one component that reads it. Nothing a user
has to read in full or act on belongs at 11px.

Every body line height is a multiple of 4px (24, 20, 16, 16), so body text
of any size sits on the same 4px grid as the spacing and control heights.

## Weights

Four. Anything outside this set is not part of the system.

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Weights} />

| Weight | Value |
| --- | --- |
| regular | 400 |
| medium | 500 |
| semibold | 600 |
| bold | 700 |

{/* docs:check allow --font-weight-medium -- the paragraph explains why weights are not tokens */}

Weight is written directly rather than tokenised — there are four of them
and they are the same four everywhere, so a `--font-weight-medium`
indirection would buy nothing. Button is `--text-body` at `font-weight:
500`; the role supplies the size and line height, the rule supplies the
weight.

With a system stack, the weight you ask for is not guaranteed to be a
drawn face: where one is missing the browser synthesises it, and
synthesised weights look noticeably worse. 400 and 500 are safe
everywhere; verify 600 on the platforms you support.

## Scaling

Every size above is `calc(<base> * var(--scaling))`, so the
[`scaling`](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs) setting moves type and
spacing together. Line heights are stored as *ratios* — `calc(20 / 14)`
rather than `1.25rem` — so they follow the font size instead of having to
be rescaled themselves.

The 4px grid above holds at 100% only. At 110% a 16px line is 17.6px: the
ratio keeps type in proportion to the controls around it, which matters
more than whole pixels, and it is the trade-off Radix Themes makes too.

## What is not here

**A metric role for large figures.** Its sizes would be identical to three
of the heading steps; the real difference is tabular figures, which
`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` already covers. There is no stat
component yet, so it would be a role nothing reads.

**A code role.** Same size as `--text-body-sm`, differing only by family.
`var(--font-mono)` covers it until a Code component exists.

## Customization

The family is a token like any other:

```css
:root {
  --font-sans: 'Geist Variable', system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-heading: 'Newsreader Variable', Georgia, serif; /* serif headings */
}
```

Every rule that reads `var(--font-sans)` picks it up with no component
change — which is all of them, because components set the family
explicitly rather than inheriting it from the page. Re-check the weights when you do — a real typeface
usually ships fewer weights than the four above, or different ones.

To move the scale itself rather than the face, override the role tokens
directly — each is a `--text-<role>` and its `--leading-<role>` partner.

'use client'

import { useId, type ComponentProps, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { useRender } from '@base-ui/react/use-render'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Badge } from '../../atomic-elements/Badge'
import styles from './VerticalNav.module.css'

export interface VerticalNavItem {
  type?: 'item'
  label: string
  href?: string
  icon?: ReactNode
  /** A count after the label, e.g. the number of members. Joins the link's name: "Members, 12". */
  badge?: number
  /** Replaces the `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link to="…" />`. */
  render?: ReactElement
}
/** A named list of items. */
export interface VerticalNavGroup {
  type: 'group'
  label: string
  items: VerticalNavItem[]
}
export type VerticalNavEntry = VerticalNavItem | VerticalNavGroup

export interface VerticalNavProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  items: VerticalNavEntry[]
  /** The href of the page the reader is on: that item gets aria-current="page". */
  currentHref?: string
  /** The nav landmark's name, e.g. "Settings". Required: the app's own nav is already a navigation landmark. */
  'aria-label': string
}

function Item({ item, current }: { item: VerticalNavItem; current: boolean }) {
  // The count joins the name with a comma ("Members, 12"), not run on ("Members12").
  const name = item.badge === undefined ? item.label : `${item.label}, ${item.badge}`
  return useRender({
    render: item.render,
    defaultTagName: 'a',
    props: {
      href: item.href,
      className: cn(styles.item, current && styles.current),
      'aria-current': current ? ('page' as const) : undefined,
      'aria-label': name !== item.label ? name : undefined,
      children: (
        <>
          {item.icon && (
            <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
              {item.icon}
            </span>
          )}
          <span className={styles.label}>{item.label}</span>
          {item.badge !== undefined && <Badge count={item.badge} size="sm" variant="secondary" />}
        </>
      ),
    },
  })
}

/**
 * Secondary navigation inside a page, e.g. the sections of Settings. The
 * app's own navigation is NavSidebar; this one has no rail, no collapse and
 * no fill of its own, and takes the width its container gives it.
 */
export function VerticalNav({ items, currentHref, className, ...props }: VerticalNavProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const list = (entries: VerticalNavItem[], labelledBy?: string) => (
    <ul className={styles.list} aria-labelledby={labelledBy}>
      {entries.map((item) => (
        <li key={item.href ?? item.label}>
          <Item item={item} current={item.href !== undefined && item.href === currentHref} />
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
  // Runs of ungrouped items become one list; groups stay as they are.
  const sections: (VerticalNavItem[] | VerticalNavGroup)[] = []
  for (const entry of items) {
    const last = sections.at(-1)
    if (entry.type === 'group') sections.push(entry)
    else if (Array.isArray(last)) last.push(entry)
    else sections.push([entry])
  }

  return (
    <nav className={cn(styles.nav, className)} {...props}>
      {sections.map((section, i) =>
        Array.isArray(section) ? (
          <div key={i}>{list(section)}</div>
        ) : (
          // The label names the list rather than being a heading, so it
          // cannot break the page's outline.
          <div key={i} className={styles.group}>
            <div id={`${id}-${i}`} className={styles.groupLabel}>
              {section.label}
            </div>
            {list(section.items, `${id}-${i}`)}
          </div>
        ),
      )}
    </nav>
  )
}

./src/components/patterns/application-ui/VerticalNav.mdx
# Vertical Nav Secondary navigation inside a page: the sections of Settings, or the parts ...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as VerticalNavStories from './VerticalNav.stories'

<Meta of={VerticalNavStories} />

# Vertical Nav

Secondary navigation inside a page: the sections of Settings, or the
parts of a long record, as a column of links beside the content. The
app's own navigation is the [Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs);
this one has no rail, no collapse and no fill, and sits on the page.
After Tailwind UI Application UI, Navigation: Vertical navigation.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/vertical-nav.json
```

## With icons

An icon before each label helps when the reader comes back often and
scans by shape. Use icons on every item or on none. A count after the
label is information (how many members), so it is a secondary
[Badge](?path=/docs/atomic-elements-badge--docs), not the Nav Sidebar's
red one for unread items.

<Canvas of={VerticalNavStories.WithIcons} />

## Grouped

Past seven or so sections, name groups of them. Ungrouped items before
the first group form a list of their own.

<Canvas of={VerticalNavStories.Grouped} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={VerticalNavStories} />

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **No width of its own.** It fills the column the page gives it; the
  page decides the column's width and what happens on a narrow screen
  (the Settings template stacks it above the content).
- **Long labels wrap** rather than truncate: a cut-off section name hides
  which section it is. A word with no spaces breaks anywhere.
- Rows are `--control-md` tall at least, as in the Nav Sidebar, and
  `--target-coarse` under a coarse pointer.

<Canvas of={VerticalNavStories.LongLabels} />

## Accessibility

- It is a `nav` landmark and needs an `aria-label` ("Settings"): the
  app's own navigation is already a navigation landmark, so the two need
  different names.
- The current section has `aria-current="page"` as well as the selected
  fill and medium weight, so it is not shown by color alone.
- A group label names its list ("Workspace, list, 4 items") and is not a
  heading, so it cannot break the page's heading outline.
- A count joins the link's name after a comma ("Members, 12").
  Icons are decorative and hidden from assistive tech.
- Tab moves down the links in order; there are no other stops.

'use client'

import type { ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Accordion as BaseAccordion } from '@base-ui/react/accordion'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Accordion.module.css'

export interface AccordionItem {
  value: string
  title: ReactNode
  content: ReactNode
  disabled?: boolean
}

export interface AccordionProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>
  items: AccordionItem[]
  /** Controlled: the values of the open items. */
  value?: string[]
  defaultValue?: string[]
  /** Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string[]) => void
  /** Allow more than one item open at once. */
  multiple?: boolean
  appearance?: 'outlined' | 'flush'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** The heading element each trigger sits in. Match it to the page's outline. */
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6
  disabled?: boolean
  className?: string
}

export function Accordion({
  items,
  onValueChange,
  appearance = 'outlined',
  size = 'md',
  headingLevel = 3,
  className,
  ...props
}: AccordionProps) {
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  return (
    <BaseAccordion.Root
      {...props}
      onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next as string[]))}
      // Collapsed panels stay in the DOM as hidden="until-found", so the
      // browser's find-in-page can reach text inside them and open them.
      hiddenUntilFound
      className={cn(styles.accordion, styles[appearance], styles[size], className)}
    >
      {items.map((item) => (
        <BaseAccordion.Item key={item.value} value={item.value} disabled={item.disabled} className={styles.item}>
          <BaseAccordion.Header render={<Heading />} className={styles.header}>
            <BaseAccordion.Trigger className={styles.trigger}>
              <span className={styles.title}>{item.title}</span>
              <Icon name="chevron-down" className={styles.chevron} />
            </BaseAccordion.Trigger>
          </BaseAccordion.Header>
          <BaseAccordion.Panel className={styles.panel}>
            <div className={styles.content}>{item.content}</div>
          </BaseAccordion.Panel>
        </BaseAccordion.Item>
      ))}
    </BaseAccordion.Root>
  )
}

# Accordion A stack of headings that each show or hide a section of content: FAQs, setting...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as AccordionStories from './Accordion.stories'

<Meta of={AccordionStories} />

# Accordion

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A stack of headings that each show or hide a section of content: FAQs,
settings groups, long forms split into parts.

<Status of={AccordionStories} />

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Default} />

## Variants

`appearance` chooses the frame, `size` the scale. By default one item is
open at a time; `multiple` lets several stay open.

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `outlined` | A self-contained block on the page: an FAQ, a settings group. The items sit in a bordered panel. |
| `flush` | Sections inside something that already has a frame, such as a card or a sidebar. Edge to edge, no side padding. |

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Open} />

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Flush} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | The default: 32px triggers, 14px text. |
| `sm` | Dense panels and side columns: 24px triggers, 12px text. |

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Small} />

| Mode | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Single (default) | Sections a reader compares one at a time. Opening one closes the other. |
| `multiple` | Sections a reader may want side by side, such as settings groups. |

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Multiple} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Accordion } from 'zweihander/accordion'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/accordion.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Accordion.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Accordion.tsx)
- Spec: the kit's own. uiguideline.com has no page for it yet.
- Behaviour: [Base UI Accordion](https://base-ui.com/react/components/accordion)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={AccordionStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={AccordionStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

## Measurements

Each size takes its trigger height from a control tier (Foundations /
Sizing). `flush` drops the inline padding to 0 at both sizes, so the
title lines up with the text around it.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Minimum height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Inline padding (outlined)', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-3' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Chevron', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Inline padding (outlined)', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Bottom padding', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Minimum height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Inline padding (outlined)', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-3' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Chevron', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Inline padding (outlined)', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Bottom padding', token: '--space-cluster' },

  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring, outlined', property: 'Offset (inset)', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
    { part: 'Focus ring, flush', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Minimum height on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Panel and chevron', property: 'Open and close duration', token: '--duration-base' },
  ]}
/>

Dividers and the outlined frame are 1px. The title is medium weight (500)
and wraps; the chevron keeps its size.

## Color

The two appearances share their colours; they differ only in where the
lines go. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="outlined"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Divider', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Chevron', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Text colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Trigger, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="flush"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Divider, and a line under the last item', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Chevron', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Text colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Trigger, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' }]} />

The lines are `--border`, the lighter border for things that are not
controls. The trigger has no fill at rest.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={AccordionStories.Open} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={AccordionStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={AccordionStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills the trigger with `--accent`. A disabled trigger does not
  change on hover.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline. In `outlined` it sits 2px inside
  the trigger, because the frame clips anything outside; in `flush` there
  is no clipping and no side padding, so it sits 2px outside instead.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own: the trigger keeps its hover fill
  while the pointer is down.
- **Open** turns the chevron to point up, and the panel's height animates
  from 0 to its content's height over `--duration-base`.
- **Disabled** dims the trigger to 50% opacity, on one item
  (`disabled` in `items`) or on all of them (`disabled` on the accordion).

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AccordionStories} />
</div>

`ref` reaches the container.

The props are the kit's own, since there is no spec to follow. `items` is
flat, per the kit's "flat props" convention. `value` is an array in single
mode too, because that is Base UI's model and it keeps the type the same
when `multiple` is switched on. `headingLevel` exists because a heading
level must follow the page's outline, which the component cannot know.

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Controlled} />

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Accordion for several related sections that most readers only
need some of: an FAQ, groups of settings, the parts of a long form. Each
title should say what is inside, so a reader can pick without opening
every item.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={AccordionStories.DoRelatedSections} />}
  doCaption="Several related sections, each title naming what is inside."
  dont={<Story of={AccordionStories.DontSingleItem} />}
  dontCaption="One item is not a list of sections. Use a Collapse."
/>

Set `headingLevel` to fit the page: under an `h2`, the items are `h3`, the
default.

<Canvas of={AccordionStories.Headings} />

## When not to use

- **For one section.** Use a
  [Collapse](?path=/docs/components-data-display-collapse--docs): a text
  button that belongs to the content around it.
- **For views of the same thing, one at a time.** Use
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs).
- **For content most readers need.** An accordion trades a shorter page for
  an extra click on everything inside it. Show that content.

## Accessibility

- Each trigger is a `<button>` inside a real heading, with
  `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; each panel is a region labelled by
  its trigger.
- `headingLevel` sets the heading element, `h3` by default.
- **Every trigger is a tab stop.** Enter and Space toggle. There is no
  arrow-key movement between triggers, following the current APG
  guidance (Base UI dropped it too).
- A disabled item's trigger has `aria-disabled` and does not open.
- Collapsed panels are `hidden="until-found"`: the browser's find-in-page
  reaches their text and opens the item.
- Triggers are 32px (`sm` 24px), the compact control scale. On touch
  (`pointer: coarse`) they grow to 44px rather than overlapping each
  other with invisible hit areas.
- The open/close animation stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Card, type CardProps } from '../../data-display/Card'
import styles from './ActionPanel.module.css'

export interface ActionPanelProps extends Omit<CardProps, 'title' | 'onClick' | 'render' | 'orientation'> {
  title: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  action: ReactNode
  actionPlacement?: 'below' | 'end'
  variant?: 'default' | 'danger'
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4
}

/**
 * A card that offers one action: what it is, what it does, and the control
 * that does it. The panel is a group named by its title and described by
 * its description, so the control is announced with that context.
 */
export function ActionPanel({
  title,
  description,
  action,
  actionPlacement = 'below',
  variant = 'default',
  headingLevel = 2,
  className,
  ...props
}: ActionPanelProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  return (
    <Card
      role="group"
      aria-labelledby={`${id}title`}
      aria-describedby={description ? `${id}description` : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.actionPanel, styles[actionPlacement], variant === 'danger' && styles.danger, className)}
      {...props}
    >
      <div className={styles.text}>
        <Heading id={`${id}title`} className={styles.title}>
          {title}
        </Heading>
        {description && (
          <div id={`${id}description`} className={styles.description}>
            {description}
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
      <div className={styles.action}>{action}</div>
    </Card>
  )
}

# Action Panel A [Card](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) that offers one ac...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ActionPanelStories from './ActionPanel.stories'

<Meta of={ActionPanelStories} />

# Action Panel

A [Card](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) that offers one action:
a title saying what it does, a description of what happens when you take
it, and the control that does it. For actions that stand on their own on a
settings or detail page, such as exporting data, renewing a plan or
deleting a workspace. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Forms: Action
panels.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/action-panel.json
```

## Simple

A button under the description. The default, and the right one when the
description runs to two lines or more.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.Simple} />

## Button at the end

`actionPlacement="end"` puts the action beside the text, for a short
description. It drops under the text when the card gets narrow.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.ButtonAtEnd} />

## With a switch

A setting that takes effect the moment it changes, so there is no Save
button. Give the Switch an `aria-label` that matches the title: the
panel's title is not its label.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.WithSwitch} />

## With an input

A small form, one field and its button, for an action that needs one
value. The form is yours: the panel lays out what you pass.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.WithInput} />

## Danger

`variant="danger"` edges the panel in the destructive colour, in every
appearance, flat surface included. Use it only for what cannot be undone,
with a destructive Button, and confirm in a
[Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs) before acting. Put it
last on the page.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.Danger} />

## Without a description

The description is optional; several actions wrap onto more rows rather
than overflow.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.TitleOnly} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={ActionPanelStories} />

Every other Card prop and `<div>` attribute passes through, except
`onClick`, `render` and `orientation`: the panel is not itself a control,
and its placement prop sets the direction.

## Layout

- **Below** stacks the text and the action, in the Card's gap.
- **End** keeps the text at least 16rem wide, then wraps the action under
  it, keeping its order.
- The description stops at 65 characters a line; long titles and words
  break anywhere rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={ActionPanelStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

- **With link**: no slot of its own. Pass a [Link](?path=/docs/components-navigation-link--docs)
  as the `action`.
- **Simple well, with well**: not a variant. The tinted inset is the
  Card's look; pick it with `appearance` so the panel matches the other
  blocks on the page.
- **Danger** is added: Tailwind leaves a danger zone to a red button.

## Accessibility

- The panel is a `group` named by its title, so a screen reader names
  it when focus enters the control. The description is linked with
  `aria-describedby`; screen readers differ on reading a group's
  description, so the control's own name must make sense alone. The title
  is heard twice in reading order, as the heading and the group's name.
- The title is an `h2` by default. Use `headingLevel={3}` or `4` under a
  section heading, so the outline has no gaps.
- The danger edge is not the only warning: the title and the destructive
  button say it too, so it does not rest on colour.
- The control keeps its own name: a Switch needs an `aria-label`, a
  button names its action ("Delete workspace", not "Delete"), a field
  has its label.

import type { ComponentProps, MouseEvent, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon, type IconName } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Alert.module.css'

export interface AlertProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'title'> {
  variant?: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'
  appearance?: 'subtle' | 'outlined' | 'solid'
  title?: ReactNode
  /** Replaces the variant's icon; `false` shows none. */
  icon?: ReactNode | false
  /** Buttons or links under the message, e.g. "Retry". */
  action?: ReactNode
  /** Shows a close button that calls this. The alert does not hide itself: remove it when this fires. */
  onClose?: (event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void
  /** Accessible name of the close button. */
  closeLabel?: string
  /**
   * Announce the alert when it appears. `danger` and `warning` interrupt
   * (`role="alert"`), the others wait their turn (`role="status"`). Leave it
   * off for an alert that is on the page from the start.
   */
  isLive?: boolean
}

const icons: Record<NonNullable<AlertProps['variant']>, IconName> = {
  info: 'info-filled',
  success: 'success-filled',
  warning: 'warning-filled',
  danger: 'danger-filled',
}

export function Alert({
  variant = 'info',
  appearance = 'subtle',
  title,
  icon,
  action,
  onClose,
  closeLabel = 'Dismiss',
  isLive = false,
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: AlertProps) {
  const urgent = variant === 'danger' || variant === 'warning'
  return (
    <div
      role={isLive ? (urgent ? 'alert' : 'status') : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.alert, styles[variant], styles[appearance], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {icon !== false && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {icon ?? <Icon name={icons[variant]} />}
        </span>
      )}
      <div className={styles.body}>
        {title && <div className={styles.title}>{title}</div>}
        {children && <div className={styles.description}>{children}</div>}
        {action && <div className={styles.action}>{action}</div>}
      </div>
      {onClose && (
        <button type="button" aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close} onClick={onClose}>
          <Icon name="close" />
        </button>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

const Dismissible = function Render(args) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(true)
  return open ? (
    <Alert
      {...args}
      onClose={(e) => {
        args.onClose?.(e)
        setOpen(false)
      }}
    />
  ) : (

};

# Alert A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes or the ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as AlertStories from './Alert.stories'

<Meta of={AlertStories} />

# Alert

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes
or the reader dismisses it: something went wrong, needs attention, or worked.

<Status of={AlertStories} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithAction} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour, by meaning; `appearance` is the emphasis. Any
variant takes any appearance.

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `info` | Something worth knowing that changes nothing: a plan change, scheduled maintenance. |
| `success` | Something finished and stays true: a domain verified, an import done. |
| `warning` | Something that will go wrong if nobody acts: a card expiring, a quota nearly used. |
| `danger` | Something that went wrong and needs a next step: a failed upload, a lost connection. |

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Appearances} />

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `subtle` | The default. Sits on the page without shouting. |
| `outlined` | On a tinted or busy background, where a tint would disappear. |
| `solid` | The one message nobody should miss, such as an outage banner. Rarely more than one per page. |

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Dismissible} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithoutIcon} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Alert } from 'zweihander/alert'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/alert.json
```

- Source: [src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/alert](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/alert)
- Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={AlertStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={AlertStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Only the description is required. The icon is one line of body text tall,
so it sits on the title's line.

## Measurements

One size. The text is body text, so an alert sits in running content
without a jump in size.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every alert"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-md' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap, icon to text', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Action', property: 'Space above, and between actions', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Minimum hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset (inside)', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
  ]}
/>

The border is always there, 1px and transparent unless `outlined`, so
switching appearance never moves the content.

## Color

Each variant reads four tokens, the same four as a Tag of that variant, so
the two always agree. Subtle and outlined keep the description in
`--foreground`: a paragraph in the variant's colour is tiring to read, so
the colour goes on the icon and the title.

<SpecTable
  caption="info"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--info-subtle' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--info-text' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--info-text' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--info' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--info-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="success"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--success-subtle' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--success' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="warning"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--warning-subtle' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--warning-text' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--warning-text' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--warning' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--warning-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="danger"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--danger-subtle' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--danger' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Description, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

## States

The alert itself has no states. Its close button does.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Close hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Close focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={AlertStories.Dismissible} />
</States>

- **Hover** tints the close button with 15% of the alert's own text
  colour, so it reads on every variant and appearance.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, inside the button's edge.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AlertStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **Placed in the content, not at the top of the screen.** The spec
  describes a prominent message at the top; here an alert goes where the
  thing it is about is. An outage banner is a `solid` alert placed at the
  top by the page.
- **Closing is the parent's job.** `onClose` reports the click and the
  alert stays until whoever rendered it removes it, so "dismissed" lives in
  your state and can be remembered across visits.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Alert for a message about a page or a section that should stay put
until it is dealt with: a failed save, a card about to expire, an import
that finished. The title says what happened; the description says what it
means and what to do.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={AlertStories.DoSayWhatHappened} />}
  doCaption="Say what happened and offer the next step."
  dont={<Story of={AlertStories.DontVague} />}
  dontCaption="“Something went wrong” leaves the red box to do the talking, and the reader with nothing to do."
/>

The icon is decorative, so the variant has to be clear from the words too:
"Upload failed", not just a red box.

## When not to use

- **For news about something that just happened and needs nothing more.**
  Use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): it goes
  away by itself.
- **For a one-line message under a form or a group of fields.** Use an
  [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs).
- **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and
  `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`.
- **For a decision the reader must make before going on.** Use a Modal.

## Accessibility

- A plain `<div>` by default: an alert on the page when it loads is read in
  order, like the text around it, and does not interrupt.
- An alert that **appears** in response to something (a failed save) needs
  `isLive`. `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at
  once; `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait for the screen
  reader to finish.

  <Canvas of={AlertStories.Live} />

- The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning.
- The close button is a native `<button>` named `Dismiss` (change it with
  `closeLabel`). Tab reaches it, Enter and Space press it.
- Focus ring: 2px `--ring` on the close button. On touch screens its hit
  area grows to 44×44px without the button growing.
- Every variant and appearance passes the story tests' contrast check
  (light mode).

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './AppContent.module.css'

export interface AppContentProps extends ComponentProps<'main'> {
  /**
   * A column beside the page for a summary, a status or activity, in an
   * `aside` landmark. From 80rem of shell width it sits to the right and
   * scrolls on its own; below that it follows the page.
   */
  aside?: ReactNode
  /** The aside's accessible name. Give one when the page has more than one `aside`. */
  asideLabel?: string
}

/**
 * The page region of an App Shell: the `main` landmark, as one flat card
 * surface or as blocks on the canvas, whichever the Theme's `contentStyle`
 * picks, with an optional aside column. The shell renders it around its
 * children; it reads the shell's grid and canvas values, so it is not used
 * on its own.
 */
export function AppContent({ aside, asideLabel, className, children, ...props }: AppContentProps) {
  // `null`, `false` and `undefined` render nothing, so they are no aside either.
  const hasAside = aside != null && aside !== false
  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.content, hasAside && styles.withAside)}>
      <main tabIndex={-1} className={cn(styles.main, className)} {...props}>
        {children}
      </main>
      {hasAside && (
        // Focusable: side by side it scrolls on its own, and an aside of
        // plain text has nothing else a keyboard could scroll it with.
        <aside tabIndex={0} aria-label={asideLabel} className={styles.aside}>
          {aside}
        </aside>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
