# Calendar A month grid to pick one day from, or to show one: a booking page, the inside o...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Calendar } from './Calendar'
import * as CalendarStories from './Calendar.stories'

<Meta of={CalendarStories} />

# Calendar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A month grid to pick one day from, or to show one: a booking page, the
inside of a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).

<Status of={CalendarStories} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Default} />

## Variants

Calendar has one look and one size. What changes is what it shows.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| One day (`value`) | Picking or showing a single day: a delivery date, a booking. |
| A span (`range`) | Showing a stay or a report period. Clicks still report one day; Date Range Picker decides the span. |
| Limits (`min`, `max`) | Booking windows: nothing before tomorrow, nothing after the season ends. |
| Ruled-out days (`isDateDisabled`) | Weekends, holidays, days already booked. |
| Locale (`locale`, `weekStartsOn`) | Month and weekday names in the reader's language, and their first day of the week. |

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Range} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.MinMax} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.NoWeekends} />

The locale decides the week: `vi-VN` and `en-GB` start on Monday, `en-US`
on Sunday, read from `Intl.Locale` where the browser knows it (Monday
otherwise). The grid is always Gregorian, so a locale whose own calendar is
not (Persian) still gets Gregorian days, in its own digits.

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Vietnamese} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Calendar } from 'zweihander/calendar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/calendar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/calendar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/calendar)
- Behaviour: a plain element, using `Intl` for names and the week's first day: no date library
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CalendarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CalendarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The grid always has six rows. Months span four to six weeks; a fixed height
keeps a popover or a page from jumping as you page through them.

Two more looks sit on the days: **today**, an orange disc, round where a
selected day takes the control's corners; and with `range`, the **band**, as tall as a day,
behind the days between the two ends. The band rounds off where a week or
the month starts or ends. Days of the months either side are never banded,
so two months side by side never draw the same day twice.

## Measurements

Calendar has one size. Days are 32px, 4px apart: each cell pads by half
of `--space-1` on every side, so a range's band runs unbroken under the
gap.

Figures are tabular, so the columns of dates line up. On touch screens
(`pointer: coarse`) days grow to 44px, the touch target; the previous and
next buttons stay 32px.

## Color

One table per kind of day. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar:
the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="Header and weekdays"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Month', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Previous and next', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Weekdays', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

  ]}
/>

/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Outside the month and unavailable"
  rows={[

/>

- **Day** has no fill at rest.
- **Today's figure is dark**, not white: white on `--orange` is 3.4:1,
  under the 4.5:1 a 14px figure needs, while `--orange-contrast` clears
  4.9:1 in both modes. A selected today shows as selected.
- **Outside days** are `--muted-foreground` mixed 50% with transparent,
  about 2:1. No token is lighter, and WCAG allows it for decoration: they
  are hidden from assistive tech and cannot be picked.
- **Unavailable days** are struck through as well as faded, so they do not
  rely on colour.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CalendarStories.Default} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CalendarStories.Default} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={CalendarStories.MinMax} /> },
    { label: 'Today', content: <Calendar locale="en-GB" weekStartsOn={1} /> },
  ]}
/>

<States states={[{ label: 'Selected range', content: <Story of={CalendarStories.Range} /> }]} />

Each example forces the state on every day at once; on screen it is the
one under the pointer or the keyboard.

- **Hover** fills a day, or the previous and next buttons, with `--accent`
  behind `--accent-foreground`. The selected day and today keep their own
  colours; unavailable and outside days do not react.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the day.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click selects the day, and the
  selected look follows.
- **Disabled** is per day: before `min`, after `max`, or ruled out by
  `isDateDisabled`. The previous and next buttons disable at the limits,
  at 50% opacity.
- **Selected** is the brand fill, with the control's corners; **today** is the orange disc,
  round. With `range`, both ends are selected and the days between are
  banded.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CalendarStories} />
</div>

Also exported, for working with the same plain dates: `isSameDay`,
`addDays`, `addMonths`, `startOfDay`, `firstDayOfWeek` and the `DateRange`
type. Every date is local midnight; times are ignored.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Calendar where the day is picked by looking at the month: a booking
page, a delivery slot, a few weeks either side of today. Rule out the days
that cannot be picked with `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled`, rather than
refusing the choice after it is made.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CalendarStories.DoNearDate} />}
  doCaption="A date close to now, where seeing the week matters: unavailable days are struck through before anyone picks them."
  dont={<Story of={CalendarStories.DontFarDate} />}
  dontCaption="A date of birth is decades away: paging back a month, or even a year, at a time is slow. Type it in a Date Picker."
/>

Month steps keep the day where they can: 31 January plus a month is 28
February, not 3 March.

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.MonthEnds} />

## When not to use

- **For a date far from today**, or one people know by heart, like a date
  of birth. Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs):
  it takes the date typed, and opens this calendar when wanted.
- **For a span inside a form.** Use a
  [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs):
  it owns the two clicks that make a span and shows it here.
- **For a schedule of events.** A day here holds a number, not content.
  Use the [Event Calendar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-event-calendar--docs)
  pattern, or list the events in a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs).

## Accessibility

- A `role="grid"` named by the month and year ("September 2026"), with
  column headers that carry the full weekday name in `abbr`.
- Each day is a button named by its full date ("Friday 18 September
  2026"). The selected cell has `aria-selected`, and with `range` every
  cell from one end to the other does. Today has `aria-current="date"`.
- One tab stop: the selected day, or today when nothing is selected.
- Arrow keys move a day or a week, Home and End go to the week's ends,
  Page Up and Page Down move a month, and Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page
  Down a year. Enter or Space selects. Moving past the month shows the
  next one.
- Right to left, the arrows follow the screen (ArrowLeft is the next day)
  and the previous and next chevrons are mirrored.

  <Canvas of={CalendarStories.Keyboard} />

- The month and year are a polite live region, so paging is announced.
- The previous and next buttons are named "Previous month" and "Next
  month", and are disabled at `min` and `max`.
- Unavailable days stay focusable with `aria-disabled`, so they are found
  and announced as unavailable rather than skipped. Enter on one does
  nothing.
- Days of the months either side are not buttons and are hidden from
  assistive tech.
- Today's figure measures at least 4.5:1 on its disc, in both modes, on
  its own and inside a range.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

export function CardHeading({

  description,
  media,

# Card Heading The top row of a card: what the card is, a line of context, and what you ca...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as CardHeadingStories from './CardHeading.stories'

<Meta of={CardHeadingStories} />

# Card Heading

The top row of a card: what the card is, a line of context, and what you
can do with it. Put it first inside a [Card](?path=/docs/data-display-card--docs);
the card's padding and gap space it from the content. After Tailwind UI
Application UI, Headings: Card headings.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/card-heading.json
```

## Simple

A title and, optionally, one line of description.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.Simple} />

## With action

The card's main action at the end of the title row. One primary button at
most; a card is part of a page that has its own primary action.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.WithAction} />

## With avatar and menu

Who or what the card is about, as an Avatar or an Icon before the title.
Rarely used actions go in a Menu behind "More actions" so the row stays
short.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.WithAvatarAndMenu} />

## With a rule

The heading draws no line of its own. When the content needs setting off,
put a [Divider](?path=/docs/atomic-elements-divider--docs) after the heading,
inside the card.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.WithIconAndRule} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={CardHeadingStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **Actions wrap, the title does not squeeze.** The title and description
  keep the row down to 16rem, then the actions drop underneath them,
  keeping their order.
- **Long titles break anywhere** rather than overflow.

<Canvas of={CardHeadingStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- The title is an `h2` by default: a card on a page sits under the
  page's `h1`. Use `headingLevel={3}` or `4` when the card sits under a
  section heading, so the outline has no gaps.
- The media is decorative and hidden from assistive tech: the title
  already says who or what the card is about.
- An icon-only action needs an `aria-label`, as on any Button. When a card
  repeats on a page, make action names unique, e.g. "Edit Chelsea Hagon".

'use client'

import { Children, useCallback, useEffect, useId, useRef, useState, useSyncExternalStore, type CSSProperties, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Carousel.module.css'

export interface CarouselProps {
  /** One child per slide. */
  children: ReactNode
  /** Names the carousel, e.g. "Featured templates". Required: there may be several on a page. */
  label: string
  /** Slides in view at once. */
  slidesPerView?: number
  /** Show a dot per slide under the track. */
  showDots?: boolean
  /** Advance every this many milliseconds. Paused on hover and focus, and never under reduced motion. */
  autoPlay?: number
  /** Previous/next wrap around at the ends. */
  loop?: boolean
  index?: number
  defaultIndex?: number
  onIndexChange?: (index: number) => void
  className?: string
}

// Measured from the first slide, not the track: offsetLeft counts from the
// offset parent, and in right-to-left the distances (and scrollLeft) are negative.
const offsetOf = (track: HTMLElement, slide: HTMLElement) => slide.offsetLeft - (track.children[0] as HTMLElement).offsetLeft

const motionQuery = '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'
const prefersReducedMotion = () => window.matchMedia(motionQuery).matches
const subscribeMotion = (onChange: () => void) => {
  const query = window.matchMedia(motionQuery)
  query.addEventListener('change', onChange)
  return () => query.removeEventListener('change', onChange)
}

export function Carousel({
  children,
  label,
  slidesPerView = 1,
  showDots = true,
  autoPlay,
  loop = false,
  index: indexProp,
  defaultIndex = 0,
  onIndexChange,
  className,
}: CarouselProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const slides = Children.toArray(children)
  const count = slides.length
  const last = Math.max(0, count - slidesPerView)
  const trackRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const [indexState, setIndexState] = useState(defaultIndex)
  const index = Math.min(indexProp ?? indexState, last)
  const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(autoPlay !== undefined)
  const [paused, setPaused] = useState(false)
  const reducedMotion = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeMotion, prefersReducedMotion, () => false)

  const report = useCallback(
    (next: number) => {
      setIndexState(next)
      onIndexChange?.(next)
    },
    [onIndexChange],
  )

  // Where a scroll this component started is headed. A press mid-scroll
  // interrupts the old smooth scroll, and Firefox fires scrollend for it where
  // it stopped; reading that would report a slide nobody asked for.
  const heading = useRef<number | null>(null)
  const scrollTrack = useCallback(
    (track: HTMLElement, to: number) => {
      const slide = track.children[to] as HTMLElement | undefined
      if (!slide) return
      heading.current = to
      track.scrollTo({ left: offsetOf(track, slide), behavior: reducedMotion ? 'auto' : 'smooth' })
    },
    [reducedMotion],
  )
  // The reader taking over (swipe, wheel, arrow keys) ends the wait.
  const letGo = () => {
    heading.current = null
  }

  const goTo = useCallback(
    (next: number) => {
      const target = loop ? (next + last + 1) % (last + 1) : Math.min(Math.max(next, 0), last)
      if (trackRef.current) scrollTrack(trackRef.current, target)
      report(target)
    },
    [last, loop, report, scrollTrack],
  )

  // Swipes and trackpad scrolls move the track directly; read the index back
  // once it comes to rest. Reading it mid-scroll would report every slide a
  // smooth scroll passes, including the one it started from.
  const settle = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(undefined)
  useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(settle.current), [])
  // scrollend where the browser has it: Firefox pauses longer than 100ms
  // between the events of one smooth scroll, so the timer read a slide mid-way.
  // Safari has no scrollend and keeps the timer.
  const hasScrollEnd = typeof window !== 'undefined' && 'onscrollend' in window
  const onScroll = () => {
    if (hasScrollEnd) return
    clearTimeout(settle.current)
    settle.current = setTimeout(readIndex, 100)
  }
  const readIndex = () => {
    const track = trackRef.current
    if (!track) return
    const first = track.children[0] as HTMLElement | undefined
    if (!first) return
    const step = first.getBoundingClientRect().width + parseFloat(getComputedStyle(track).columnGap || '0')
    const next = Math.min(last, Math.max(0, Math.round(Math.abs(track.scrollLeft) / step)))
    if (heading.current !== null) {
      if (next !== heading.current) return
      heading.current = null
    }
    if (next !== index) report(next)
  }

  // Start at defaultIndex (or a controlled index) without animating there.
  const placed = useRef(false)
  useEffect(() => {
    if (placed.current) return
    placed.current = true
    const track = trackRef.current
    const slide = track?.children[index] as HTMLElement | undefined
    if (track && slide && index > 0) track.scrollTo({ left: offsetOf(track, slide), behavior: 'auto' })
  }, [index])

  // A controlled index that changes from outside scrolls the track.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (indexProp === undefined) return
    const track = trackRef.current
    const slide = track?.children[index] as HTMLElement | undefined
    if (track && slide && Math.abs(track.scrollLeft - offsetOf(track, slide)) > 1) scrollTrack(track, index)
  }, [indexProp, index, scrollTrack])

  const rotating = autoPlay !== undefined && playing && !paused && !reducedMotion
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!rotating) return
    const timer = setInterval(() => goTo(index >= last ? 0 : index + 1), autoPlay)
    return () => clearInterval(timer)
  }, [rotating, autoPlay, index, last, goTo])

  return (
    <section
      aria-roledescription="carousel"
      aria-label={label}
      className={cn(styles.carousel, className)}
      style={{ '--carousel-per-view': slidesPerView } as CSSProperties}
      onMouseEnter={() => setPaused(true)}
      onMouseLeave={() => setPaused(false)}
      onFocus={() => setPaused(true)}
      onBlur={(e) => {
        if (!e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget as Node)) setPaused(false)
      }}
    >
      <div className={styles.controls}>
        {autoPlay !== undefined && (
          <button
            type="button"
            className={styles.button}
            aria-label={playing ? 'Stop automatic slide show' : 'Start automatic slide show'}
            onClick={() => setPlaying(!playing)}
          >
            <Icon name={playing ? 'pause' : 'play'} />
          </button>
        )}
        <button
          type="button"
          className={styles.button}
          aria-label="Previous slide"
          aria-controls={`${id}-track`}
          disabled={!loop && index === 0}
          onClick={() => goTo(index - 1)}
        >
          <Icon name="chevron-left" className={styles.dirIcon} />
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          className={styles.button}
          aria-label="Next slide"
          aria-controls={`${id}-track`}
          disabled={!loop && index >= last}
          onClick={() => goTo(index + 1)}
        >
          <Icon name="chevron-right" className={styles.dirIcon} />
        </button>
      </div>
      <div
        id={`${id}-track`}
        ref={trackRef}
        className={styles.track}
        // Focusable so arrow keys scroll it, like any scrolling region.
        tabIndex={0}
        onScroll={onScroll}
        onPointerDown={letGo}
        onWheel={letGo}
        onKeyDown={letGo}
        onScrollEnd={hasScrollEnd ? readIndex : undefined}
      >
        {slides.map((slide, i) => (
          <div
            key={i}
            role="group"
            aria-roledescription="slide"
            aria-label={`${i + 1} of ${count}`}
            className={styles.slide}
          >
            {slide}
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
      {/* Every slide is always in the DOM, so a live region round the track
          would never change. This line does: polite while the reader drives
          it, silent while it rotates on its own. */}
      <p className={styles.srOnly} aria-live={rotating ? 'off' : 'polite'} aria-atomic="true">
        {slidesPerView > 1
          ? `Slides ${index + 1} to ${Math.min(index + slidesPerView, count)} of ${count}`
          : `Slide ${index + 1} of ${count}`}
      </p>
      {showDots && last > 0 && (
        <div className={styles.dots}>
          {Array.from({ length: last + 1 }, (_, i) => (
            <button
              key={i}
              type="button"
              className={cn(styles.dot, i === index && styles.dotActive)}
              aria-label={`Slide ${i + 1}`}
              aria-current={i === index ? 'true' : undefined}
              aria-controls={`${id}-track`}
              onClick={() => goTo(i)}
            />
          ))}
        </div>
      )}
    </section>
  )
}

# Carousel A row of slides seen one (or a few) at a time: featured items, a gallery, onboa...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as CarouselStories from './Carousel.stories'

<Meta of={CarouselStories} />

# Carousel

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A row of slides seen one (or a few) at a time: featured items, a gallery,
onboarding cards.

<Status of={CarouselStories} />

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Default} />

## Variants

The carousel has no `variant` prop. These are its configurations:

| Configuration | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| One in view (default) | Large slides that each need the full width: a feature, a photo. |
| `slidesPerView={3}` | Smaller items browsed in a row: templates, products. |
| `loop` | A short set with no natural first or last, where next from the end should wrap. |
| `autoPlay` | Rarely. A showcase where motion is the point; it adds a stop/start button. |

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.ThreeInView} />

With three in view, five slides have three stops (1-3, 2-4, 3-5), and the
dots count stops, not slides.

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.Loop} />

<Canvas of={CarouselStories.AutoPlay} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Carousel } from 'zweihander/carousel'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/carousel.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Carousel.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Carousel.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/carousel](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/carousel)
- Behaviour: [WAI-ARIA carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CarouselStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CarouselStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The controls sit above the track, at its end, so they never cover a slide.
A visually hidden line after the track says where the reader is (see
Accessibility).

- **Native scrolling.** No transform maths and no gesture library: the
  track is `overflow-x: auto` with `scroll-snap-type`, so touch, trackpad
  and momentum behave as the platform does. The index is read back once
  the track comes to rest.
- **Right to left works.** Offsets are measured from the first slide, so
  the negative `scrollLeft` of a right-to-left track reads correctly, and
  the previous and next chevrons are mirrored.
- **`defaultIndex` starts there.** The track jumps to it on mount, without
  a scroll animation.

## Measurements

There is one size. Slide width follows from the carousel's width,
`slidesPerView` and the gap between slides.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every carousel"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Carousel', property: 'Gap between controls, track and dots', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Gap between slides', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Controls', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-8' },
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Dots', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Current dot', property: 'Width', token: '--space-6' },
    { part: 'Dot', property: 'Hit area', token: '--space-6' },
    { part: 'Button and dot', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

A dot is 6px round (1.5 × `--space-1`); the current one stretches to a
24px pill. Buttons have a 1px border.

## Color

The carousel has no variants: one table. Slides bring their own colours.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every carousel"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Icon colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Button', property: 'Border', token: '--control-border' },
    { part: 'Button, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Button, hover', property: 'Icon colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Dot', property: 'Background', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Current dot', property: 'Background', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled, first stop' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Current slide 3', content: <Story of={CarouselStories.StartAtThird} /> },
    { label: 'Last stop', content: <Story of={CarouselStories.AtEnd} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CarouselStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills an enabled button with `--accent` and its icon with
  `--accent-foreground`. Dots have no hover look.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the track, a button or a
  dot.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own.
- **Disabled**: previous at the first stop and next at the last, unless
  `loop`. A disabled button is the enabled look at 50% opacity, with the
  disabled cursor and no hover.
- **Current slide**: the current stop's dot is the longer `--foreground`
  pill.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CarouselStories} />
</div>

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Everything in a carousel past the first slide is hidden until the reader
goes looking. Use one for content that is fine to miss: featured items,
examples, a gallery. Give it a `label` that names what is in it.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CarouselStories.Default} />}
  doCaption="Featured templates: browsing is optional, and missing one costs nothing."
  dont={<Story of={CarouselStories.DontHideImportant} />}
  dontCaption="Account notices the reader must act on, four of them hidden in slides most readers never reach."
/>

Prefer no `autoPlay`. Motion pulls the eye away from the rest of the page,
and a slide can move on before it has been read.

## When not to use

- **For content everyone must see.** Show it at once: a list, or
  [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) in a grid, show
  more and hide nothing.
- **For items to compare.** Use a
  [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs): side by side
  beats one at a time.
- **For steps in a flow.** Use a
  [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs): it shows how
  many steps there are and where you are.

## Accessibility

Follows the [WAI-ARIA carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/).

- A `<section>` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and your `label`;
  each slide is a group with `aria-roledescription="slide"` and a name
  like "2 of 5".
- Previous, next, stop/start and the dots are native buttons: Tab reaches
  them, Enter and Space press them.
- Previous and next are disabled at the ends unless `loop`. Dots are
  buttons named "Slide 3", with `aria-current` on the current stop.
- **Autoplay** (WCAG 2.2.2) pauses while the pointer is over the carousel
  or focus is inside it, has a stop/start button as its first control, and
  never runs under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- A visually hidden line says where you are ("Slide 3 of 5", or "Slides
  3 to 5 of 5"). It is `aria-live="polite"` when the reader moves the
  carousel, so a screen reader hears the change, and `off` while it
  rotates on its own. Every slide is in the DOM from the start, so a live
  region round the track would stay silent.
- The track is in the tab order (`tabindex="0"`), like any scrolling
  region.
- In right to left, the previous and next chevrons are mirrored.
- Buttons and dots have 44px touch targets on coarse pointers.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

Code:
import type { CSSProperties } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Chart.module.css'

export interface ChartLegendItem {
  key: string
  label: string
  /** A CSS colour, usually from `colorVar`. */
  color: string
  /** Shown after the label, e.g. the series total "2.56K". */
  value?: string
}

export interface ChartLegendProps {
  items: ChartLegendItem[]
  /** Keys of series that are switched off. */
  hiddenKeys?: string[]
  /** Makes each item a toggle button. Without it the legend is a plain list. */
  onToggle?: (key: string) => void
  /** Called with the key under the pointer or focus, null when it leaves. Charts use it to fade the other series. */
  onFocusChange?: (key: string | null) => void
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  className?: string
}

/** Swatch, label and value per series. As toggles, it shows and hides series in the chart above it. */
export function ChartLegend({ items, hiddenKeys = [], onToggle, onFocusChange, orientation = 'horizontal', className }: ChartLegendProps) {
  const visibleCount = items.length - hiddenKeys.length
  return (
    <ul
      className={cn(styles.legend, orientation === 'vertical' && styles.legendVertical, className)}
      aria-label="Legend"
      onPointerLeave={() => onFocusChange?.(null)}
    >
      {items.map((item) => {
        const isHidden = hiddenKeys.includes(item.key)
        const content = (
          <>
            <span className={styles.swatch} style={{ '--swatch': item.color } as CSSProperties} aria-hidden="true" />
            <span className={styles.legendLabel}>{item.label}</span>
            {item.value !== undefined && <span className={styles.legendValue}>{item.value}</span>}
          </>
        )
        const focus = () => onFocusChange?.(isHidden ? null : item.key)
        const blur = () => onFocusChange?.(null)
        return (
          <li key={item.key} onPointerEnter={focus}>
            {onToggle ? (
              <button
                type="button"
                className={styles.legendItem}
                aria-pressed={!isHidden}
                // The last visible series cannot be hidden: an empty chart reads as "no data".
                aria-disabled={!isHidden && visibleCount === 1 ? true : undefined}
                onClick={() => (!isHidden && visibleCount === 1 ? undefined : onToggle(item.key))}
                onFocus={focus}
                onBlur={blur}
              >
                {content}
              </button>
            ) : (
              <span className={styles.legendItem}>{content}</span>
            )}
          </li>
        )
      })}
    </ul>
  )
}

'use client'

import { useCallback, useRef, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react'
import { Checkbox as BaseCheckbox } from '@base-ui/react/checkbox'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { ChoiceField, choiceStyles, type ValidationState } from './ChoiceField'
import styles from './Checkbox.module.css'

export interface CheckboxProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>
  checked?: boolean
  defaultChecked?: boolean
  /** The spec's `onChange`. Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean) => void
  /** Neither checked nor unchecked: a "select all" with some selected. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  name?: string
  /** Submitted when checked; "on" by default. */
  value?: string
  /** Colour of the checked box. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'neutral'
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  autoFocus?: boolean
  validationState?: ValidationState
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

export function Checkbox({
  ref,
  autoFocus,
  label,
  helperText,
  name,
  variant = 'neutral',
  isIndeterminate,
  disabled,
  required,
  validationState,
  className,
  onCheckedChange,
  ...props
}: CheckboxProps) {
  // The root is a focusable <span>, and React only honours autoFocus on form
  // elements, so it is done by hand — once, on mount, not on every render.
  const focused = useRef(false)
  const setRef = useCallback(
    (node: HTMLElement | null) => {
      if (node && autoFocus && !focused.current) {
        focused.current = true
        node.focus()
      }
      if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(node)
      else if (ref) ref.current = node
    },
    [autoFocus, ref],
  )
  return (
    <ChoiceField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      className={cn(styles.field, className)}
    >
      <BaseCheckbox.Root
        {...props}
        ref={setRef}
        indeterminate={isIndeterminate}
        required={required}
        onCheckedChange={onCheckedChange && ((next) => onCheckedChange(next))}
        className={cn(choiceStyles.control, styles.box, styles[variant])}
      >
        <BaseCheckbox.Indicator
          className={styles.indicator}
          render={(indicatorProps, state) => (
            <span {...indicatorProps}>
              <Icon name={state.indeterminate ? 'minus' : 'check'} />
            </span>
          )}
        />
      </BaseCheckbox.Root>
    </ChoiceField>
  )
}

# Checkbox Selects an option, or several from a list, to apply when a form is submitted. #...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Checkbox } from './Checkbox'
import * as CheckboxStories from './Checkbox.stories'

<Meta of={CheckboxStories} />

# Checkbox

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Selects an option, or several from a list, to apply when a form is
submitted.

<Status of={CheckboxStories} />

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the checked box. Each row: unchecked, checked,
indeterminate.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Checkbox defaultChecked label="Neutral" /> | The default: lists, forms, tables. The checked box is the foreground colour, so a column of them stays calm. |
| <Checkbox variant="primary" defaultChecked label="Primary" /> | One checkbox that carries the brand: an opt-in, a terms box beside a primary button. |

**Indeterminate** is for a parent whose children are partly selected. It
is a display state: clicking the parent chooses all or none, never
"mixed".

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.SelectAll} />

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Validation} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Checkbox } from 'zweihander/checkbox'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/checkbox.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/checkbox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/checkbox)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Checkbox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/checkbox) and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CheckboxStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CheckboxStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The label wraps the box, so the whole label is part of the click target.

## Measurements

One size. The box is control tier xs (Foundations / Sizing) and sits
centred on the first line of its label, however many lines the label
wraps to.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every checkbox"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--choice-box' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Check mark', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Gap from the box', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Gap from the label', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The box's corner is the radius step, not the control tier's radius: a box
that turned round under `radius="full-rounded"` would read as a radio.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Unchecked' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Checked', content: <Checkbox defaultChecked label="Remember me" /> },
    { label: 'Indeterminate', content: <Story of={CheckboxStories.Indeterminate} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Checkbox disabled defaultChecked label="Remember me" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Checkbox validationState="error" label="Remember me" /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CheckboxStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** anywhere on the label darkens an unchecked outline to
  `--foreground`. A checked box mixes 12% of the mark's colour into its
  fill, as Button does. An error outline stays red.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the box.
- **Disabled** dims the box and the label to 50%.
- **Read-only** looks enabled but has no hover and an arrow cursor.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CheckboxStories} />
</div>

`id`, `className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the box.

### Differences from the spec

- **Base UI's and HTML's names:** `defaultChecked` and `onCheckedChange`
  for the spec's `defaultValue` (a string there, which reads as the
  submitted value: that is `value`) and `onChange`; native `disabled`,
  `required`, `readOnly` for the `is…` forms.
- **`isIndeterminate` keeps its prefix.** Indeterminate is a DOM property,
  not an HTML attribute, so by the kit's naming rule it takes `is`; Base UI
  calls it `indeterminate`.
- **`autoFocus` is applied on mount by the component.** The box is a
  focusable `<span>`, which React's own `autoFocus` ignores.
- **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as checked, so only
  `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a checkbox for a choice that is submitted with a form: accepting
terms, opting in, picking several items from a list. Nothing happens
until the form is sent.

Write the label so that checked means yes.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CheckboxStories.DoPositiveLabel} />}
  doCaption="The label says what checking does: checked means yes."
  dont={<Story of={CheckboxStories.DontNegativeLabel} />}
  dontCaption="A negative label makes unchecked a double negative, and readers stop to work it out."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a setting that applies at once.** Use a
  [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs): it acts like a
  light switch, a checkbox waits for Submit.
- **For one choice out of several.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group; checkboxes
  are independent.
- **For a toggle in a toolbar.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs).

## Accessibility

- `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`, `mixed` when indeterminate.
  Space toggles it.
- The label wraps the box, so it names it and clicking it toggles the box.
- `helperText` is the box's description; the error state sets
  `aria-invalid`.
- The unchecked outline is `--control-border`, 3:1 on the page on every
  gray ramp.
- A hidden native input carries `name`, `value` and `required` into form
  submission and validation.
- 44×44px touch target on coarse pointers, without the box growing.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Collapsible } from '@base-ui/react/collapsible'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Collapse.module.css'

export interface CollapseProps {
  /** The trigger's text, e.g. "Show details". */
  label: ReactNode
  /** The trigger's text while open, e.g. "Hide details". Defaults to `label`. */
  openLabel?: ReactNode
  children: ReactNode
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  disabled?: boolean
  /**
   * Keep the closed content in the page as `hidden="until-found"`, so the
   * browser's find-in-page reaches it and opens it. On by default.
   */
  hiddenUntilFound?: boolean
  className?: string
}

/**
 * One show/hide section: a text button with a chevron and the content it
 * reveals. For a list of sections, use Accordion.
 */
export function Collapse({
  label,
  openLabel,
  children,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  size = 'md',
  disabled = false,
  hiddenUntilFound = true,
  className,
}: CollapseProps) {
  return (
    <Collapsible.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}
      disabled={disabled}
      className={cn(styles.collapse, styles[size], className)}
    >
      <Collapsible.Trigger className={styles.trigger}>
        <span className={styles.chevron} aria-hidden="true">
          <Icon name="chevron-right" />
        </span>
        {openLabel === undefined ? (
          label
        ) : (
          <>
            <span className={styles.closedLabel}>{label}</span>
            <span className={styles.openLabel}>{openLabel}</span>
          </>
        )}
      </Collapsible.Trigger>
      <Collapsible.Panel className={styles.panel} hiddenUntilFound={hiddenUntilFound}>
        <div className={styles.content}>{children}</div>
      </Collapsible.Panel>
    </Collapsible.Root>
  )
}

# Collapse One show/hide section, such as "Show details" or "Advanced settings": a text bu...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as CollapseStories from './Collapse.stories'

<Meta of={CollapseStories} />

# Collapse

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

One show/hide section, such as "Show details" or "Advanced settings": a
text button with a chevron, and the content it reveals under it.

<Status of={CollapseStories} />

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Open} />

## Variants

Collapse has one look. `size` matches it to the text around it, and
`openLabel` decides whether the label changes when it opens.

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Body text, 14px. The default. |
| `sm` | Small text, 12px: captions, dense panels, notes under a field. |

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Small} />

| Label | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| With `openLabel` | A label that names the action: "Show details" becomes "Hide details". |
| Without `openLabel` | A label that names the section: "Advanced settings" stays the same, and the chevron shows the state. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Collapse } from 'zweihander/collapse'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/collapse.json
```

- Spec: the kit's own. uiguideline.com has no page for it.
- Behaviour: [Base UI Collapsible](https://base-ui.com/react/components/collapsible)
- Figma: not in the library yet

## Color

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={CollapseStories.Open} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={CollapseStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CollapseStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** underlines the label, like a link.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the trigger.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own: the label stays underlined while the
  pointer is down.
- **Open** turns the chevron from right to down, shows `openLabel` if
  there is one, and animates the panel's height over `--duration-base`.
- **Disabled** dims the trigger to 50% opacity, with no underline on hover.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CollapseStories} />
</div>

The props are the kit's own, since there is no spec to follow. Closed
content is kept as `hidden="until-found"` by default: the browser's
find-in-page still matches it and opens the section.

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Searchable} />

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Collapse for one aside in running content: billing details under a
plan, advanced settings under a form. It is a text button, not a bar,
because it belongs to the content around it, and its trigger reads like a
link in a sentence.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CollapseStories.DoAsideInText} />}
  doCaption="One aside, under the text it belongs to. The label says what opening it does."
  dont={<Story of={CollapseStories.DontStackAsList} />}
  dontCaption="A stack of Collapses is a list of sections. Use an Accordion: its items are real headings, framed and divided."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a list of sections.** Use an
  [Accordion](?path=/docs/components-data-display-accordion--docs). Its
  items are full-width bars with dividers because they are the page's
  structure.
- **For a short hint about a control.** Use a
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) or a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs), which do not
  push the page down.
- **For content most readers need.** Hiding it costs everyone a click.
  Show it.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`
  pointing at the panel.
- Enter or Space toggles it. With `openLabel`, the button's name changes
  with its state ("Show details" / "Hide details"), and `aria-expanded`
  says it either way. Without it, the name stays the same.
- The chevron is decorative (`aria-hidden`), so it adds nothing to the
  name.
- Closed content is `hidden="until-found"` by default, so find-in-page
  reaches it.
- The trigger grows to a 44px target on coarse pointers.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the panel and chevron change without
  animating.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

 */
export function normalizeHex(text: string): string | null {
  let m = text.trim().replace(/^#/, '').toLowerCase()
  if (!/^([0-9a-f]{3,4}|[0-9a-f]{6}|[0-9a-f]{8})$/.test(m)) return null
  if (m.length < 5) m = [...m].map((c) => c + c).join('')
  return `#${m.endsWith('ff') && m.length === 8 ? m.slice(0, 6) : m}`
}

let ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D | null | undefined

 * normalizeHex gives; anything else to `null`. The browser does the parsing:
 * outside one (SSR), only hex is read.

export function parseColor(text: string): string | null {
  const hex = normalizeHex(text)
  if (hex || typeof document === 'undefined' || !CSS.supports('color', text.trim())) return hex
  ctx ??= document.createElement('canvas').getContext('2d', { willReadFrequently: true })
  if (!ctx) return null
  ctx.fillStyle = '#000'
  ctx.fillStyle = text.trim()
  // Usually comes back as #rrggbb or rgba(r, g, b, a).
  const style = ctx.fillStyle
  const m = style.match(/^rgba?\(([\d.]+), ([\d.]+), ([\d.]+)(?:, ([\d.]+))?\)$/)
  if (m) return normalizeHex([m[1], m[2], m[3]].map(Number).map(byteHex).join('') + byteHex(Number(m[4] ?? 1) * 255))
  if (style.startsWith('#')) return normalizeHex(style)
  // Wide-gamut spaces keep their own syntax: paint a pixel and read it back in sRGB.
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, 1, 1)
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 1, 1)
  return normalizeHex([...ctx.getImageData(0, 0, 1, 1).data].map(byteHex).join(''))
}

/** parseColor, dropping the alpha when the picker has none. */
const readHex = (text: string, alpha: boolean) => {

const toRgb = (hex: string) => {

const byteHex = (n: number) => Math.round(n).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')

function hexToHsv(hex: string): Hsv {
  const [r, g, b] = toRgb(hex).map((c) => c / 255)

/**

 */
function ChannelInput({

  value,

  onStep,
  disabled,
  className,
}: {

  value: string

  onCommit: (text: string) => void
  onStep?: (delta: number) => void
  disabled?: boolean
  className?: string
}) {
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const commit = () => {
    if (draft !== null && draft.trim() !== '') onCommit(draft)
    setDraft(null)

  return (
    <input
      type="text"
      inputMode={onStep ? 'numeric' : undefined}
      spellCheck={false}
      autoComplete="off"
      aria-label={label}
      className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.channel, className)}
      value={draft ?? value}
      disabled={disabled}
      onChange={(e) => setDraft(e.target.value)}
      onFocus={(e) => e.currentTarget.select()}
      onBlur={commit}
      onKeyDown={(e) => {
        if (e.key === 'Enter') commit()
        else if (onStep && (e.key === 'ArrowUp' || e.key === 'ArrowDown')) {
          e.preventDefault()
          setDraft(null)
          onStep((e.key === 'ArrowUp' ? 1 : -1) * (e.shiftKey ? 10 : 1))

  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  onValueChange?: (hex: string) => void
  /** Show the opacity slider and field. Off, the value is always `#rrggbb`. */
  alpha?: boolean
  /** The format of the channel fields when the panel opens. */
  defaultFormat?: ColorFormat
  /** Preset colours under the pickers. A plain string is named by its hex. */
  swatches?: Swatch[]
  disabled?: boolean
  className?: string
}

/**
 * The picker on its own, laid out like Figma's: a saturation/brightness area,
 * hue and opacity strips, channel fields in a chosen
 * format, and optional swatches. Use it inline, or through ColorPicker, which
 * puts it in a popover under a hex field.
 */
export function ColorPanel({
  value,
  defaultValue = '#3b82f6',
  onValueChange,
  alpha = true,
  defaultFormat = 'hex',
  swatches,
  disabled = false,
  className,
}: ColorPanelProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(() => readHex(defaultValue, alpha) ?? '#000000')
  const hex = (value !== undefined ? readHex(value, alpha) : null) ?? valueState
  const rgbHex = hex.slice(0, 7)
  const a = hex.length > 7 ? parseInt(hex.slice(7), 16) / 255 : 1
  // Kept as HSV, not read back from hex: at zero saturation or brightness the
  // hex forgets the hue, and the strip would jump to red.
  const [hsv, setHsv] = useState(() => hexToHsv(hex))
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(hex)
  if (hex !== shown) {
    setShown(hex)
    if (hsvToHex(hsv) !== rgbHex) setHsv(hexToHsv(hex))
  }
  const [format, setFormat] = useState(defaultFormat)

  const change = (next: Hsv, nextA = a) => {
    setHsv(next)
    const byte = Math.round(clamp(nextA) * 255)
    const nextHex = hsvToHex(next) + (byte < 255 ? byteHex(byte) : '')
    setShown(nextHex)
    setValueState(nextHex)
    if (nextHex !== hex) onValueChange?.(nextHex)
  }
  // From an RGB colour, keeping the hue where the colour has none.
  const pickRgb = (rgb: string, nextA = a) => {
    const next = hexToHsv(rgb)
    change(next.s && next.v ? next : { ...next, h: hsv.h }, nextA)
  }

  const fromPointer = (e: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const box = e.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect()
    change({ ...hsv, s: clamp((e.clientX - box.left) / box.width), v: clamp(1 - (e.clientY - box.top) / box.height) })
  }

  // One tab stop for the area, and the keys move it the way the thumb looks:
  // left/right saturation, up/down brightness, Shift for steps of 10%.
  const onAreaKey = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    const step = e.shiftKey ? 0.1 : 0.01
    const keys: Record<string, Partial<Hsv>> = {
      ArrowRight: { s: hsv.s + step },
      ArrowLeft: { s: hsv.s - step },
      ArrowUp: { v: hsv.v + step },
      ArrowDown: { v: hsv.v - step },
      PageUp: { v: hsv.v + 0.1 },
      PageDown: { v: hsv.v - 0.1 },
      Home: { s: 0 },
      End: { s: 1 },
    }
    const move = keys[e.key]
    if (!move) return
    e.preventDefault()
    change({ ...hsv, s: clamp(move.s ?? hsv.s), v: clamp(move.v ?? hsv.v) })
  }

  // Each format as [label, shown value, max, apply]: apply takes a new number
  // for that channel and returns the colour, so typing and stepping share it.
  const rgb = toRgb(rgbHex)
  const hsl = hsvToHsl(hsv)
  const channels: [string, number, number, (n: number) => void][] =
    format === 'rgb'
      ? (['Red', 'Green', 'Blue'] as const).map((name, i) => [
          name,
          rgb[i],
          255,
          (n) => pickRgb(`#${rgb.map((c, j) => byteHex(j === i ? n : c)).join('')}`),
        ])
      : format === 'hsl'
        ? [
            ['Hue degrees', Math.round(hsl.h), 360, (n) => change({ ...hsv, h: n % 360 })],
            ['Saturation percent', pct(hsl.s), 100, (n) => change(hslToHsv({ ...hsl, s: n / 100 }))],
            ['Lightness percent', pct(hsl.l), 100, (n) => change(hslToHsv({ ...hsl, l: n / 100 }))],
          ]
        : format === 'hsb'
          ? [
              ['Hue degrees', Math.round(hsv.h), 360, (n) => change({ ...hsv, h: n % 360 })],
              ['Saturation percent', pct(hsv.s), 100, (n) => change({ ...hsv, s: n / 100 })],
              ['Brightness percent', pct(hsv.v), 100, (n) => change({ ...hsv, v: n / 100 })],
            ]
          : []
  const numeric = (label: string, shownValue: number, max: number, apply: (n: number) => void, className?: string) => (
    <ChannelInput
      key={label}
      label={label}
      value={String(shownValue)}
      className={className}
      disabled={disabled}
      onCommit={(text) => {
        const n = Number(text.replace('%', ''))
        if (Number.isFinite(n)) apply(clamp(Math.round(n), max))
      }}
      onStep={(d) => apply(clamp(shownValue + d, max))}
    />
  )

  const presets = swatches?.map((s) => (typeof s === 'string' ? { value: s, label: s } : s))

  return (
    <div
      className={cn(styles.panel, disabled && styles.disabled, className)}
      style={{ '--picker-hue': hsv.h, '--picker-color': hex, '--picker-rgb': rgbHex } as CSSProperties}
    >
      <div
        className={styles.area}
        data-disabled={disabled || undefined}
        onPointerDown={(e) => {
          if (disabled || e.button !== 0) return
          // Firefox throws on a pointer id it does not know (synthetic events);
          // the click still sets the colour, only the drag needs the capture.
          try {
            e.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)
          } catch {}
          e.preventDefault()
          e.currentTarget.querySelector('input')?.focus({ preventScroll: true })
          fromPointer(e)
        }}
        onPointerMove={(e) => e.currentTarget.hasPointerCapture(e.pointerId) && fromPointer(e)}
      >
        <div className={styles.areaThumb} style={{ left: `${hsv.s * 100}%`, top: `${(1 - hsv.v) * 100}%` }}>
          <input
            type="range"
            className={styles.srOnly}
            aria-label="Saturation"
            aria-valuetext={`Saturation ${pct(hsv.s)}%, brightness ${pct(hsv.v)}%`}
            min={0}
            max={100}
            value={pct(hsv.s)}
            disabled={disabled}
            onChange={(e) => change({ ...hsv, s: Number(e.target.value) / 100 })}
            onKeyDown={onAreaKey}
          />
          {/* Reachable by a screen reader's virtual cursor; the keyboard gets it through the arrows above. */}
          <input
            type="range"
            className={styles.srOnly}
            tabIndex={-1}
            aria-label="Brightness"
            aria-valuetext={`Brightness ${pct(hsv.v)}%`}
            min={0}
            max={100}
            value={pct(hsv.v)}
            disabled={disabled}
            onChange={(e) => change({ ...hsv, v: Number(e.target.value) / 100 })}
          />
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className={styles.strips}>
        <Slider.Root
          className={styles.strip}
          min={0}
          max={359}
          value={Math.round(hsv.h) % 360}
          disabled={disabled}
          onValueChange={(h) => change({ ...hsv, h: h as number })}
          thumbAlignment="edge"
        >
          <Slider.Control className={styles.stripControl}>
            <Slider.Track className={cn(styles.stripTrack, styles.hueTrack)}>
              <Slider.Thumb
                className={cn(styles.stripThumb, styles.hueThumb)}
                getAriaLabel={() => 'Hue'}
                getAriaValueText={(_, v) => `${v} degrees`}
              />
            </Slider.Track>
          </Slider.Control>
        </Slider.Root>
        {alpha && (
          <Slider.Root
            className={styles.strip}
            min={0}
            max={100}
            value={pct(a)}
            disabled={disabled}
            onValueChange={(n) => change(hsv, (n as number) / 100)}
            thumbAlignment="edge"
          >
            <Slider.Control className={styles.stripControl}>
              <Slider.Track className={cn(styles.stripTrack, styles.alphaTrack)}>
                <Slider.Thumb
                  className={cn(styles.stripThumb, styles.alphaThumb)}
                  getAriaLabel={() => 'Opacity'}
                  getAriaValueText={(_, v) => `${v}%`}
                />
              </Slider.Track>
            </Slider.Control>
          </Slider.Root>
        )}
      </div>

      <div className={styles.fields}>
        <Select
          aria-label="Colour format"
          className={styles.format}
          options={formats}
          value={format}
          disabled={disabled}
          onValueChange={(v) => v && setFormat(v as ColorFormat)}
        />
        <span className={cn(boxClass('md'), styles.channels)} data-disabled={disabled || undefined}>
          {format === 'hex' ? (
            <ChannelInput
              label="Hex"
              value={rgbHex.slice(1)}
              className={styles.hexChannel}
              disabled={disabled}
              onCommit={(text) => {
                // Any CSS colour; its alpha too, when it has one.
                const n = readHex(text, alpha)
                if (n) pickRgb(n.slice(0, 7), n.length > 7 ? parseInt(n.slice(7), 16) / 255 : a)
              }}
            />
          ) : (
            channels.map(([label, v, max, apply]) => numeric(label, v, max, apply))
          )}
          {alpha && numeric('Opacity percent', pct(a), 100, (n) => change(hsv, n / 100), styles.alphaChannel)}
          {alpha && (
            <span className={cn(inputStyles.affix, styles.unit)} aria-hidden>
              %
            </span>
          )}
        </span>
      </div>

      {presets && presets.length > 0 && (
        // Native radios: one choice at a time, one tab stop, arrows to move.
        // None is checked while the colour is not one of the swatches.
        <div role="radiogroup" aria-label="Swatches" className={styles.swatches}>
          {presets.map((s) => {
            const sv = readHex(s.value, alpha) ?? s.value
            return (
              <input
                key={s.value}
                type="radio"
                name={`${id}-swatch`}
                className={styles.swatch}
                style={{ '--swatch': sv } as CSSProperties}
                aria-label={s.label}
                checked={sv === hex}
                disabled={disabled}
                onChange={() => pickRgb(sv.slice(0, 7), sv.length > 7 ? parseInt(sv.slice(7), 16) / 255 : 1)}
              />
            )
          })}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

export interface ColorPickerProps extends Omit<ColorPanelProps, 'className'> {
  label?: ReactNode
  /**
   * Under the field. Replaced by a format hint while the typed text is not a
   * colour. The field reads any CSS colour and shows it back as hex.
   */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Submitted as the hex value. */
  name?: string
  required?: boolean
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/** A hex field with a swatch button that opens the ColorPanel. */
export function ColorPicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = '#3b82f6',
  onValueChange,
  alpha = true,
  defaultFormat,
  swatches,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: ColorPickerProps) {
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(() => readHex(defaultValue, alpha) ?? '#000000')
  const hex = (value !== undefined ? readHex(value, alpha) : null) ?? valueState
  const [text, setText] = useState(hex)
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  // Follow a controlled value that changes from outside.
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(hex)
  if (hex !== shown) {
    setShown(hex)
    setText(hex)
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const commit = (next: string) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(next)
    setInvalid(false)
    if (next !== hex) onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  const commitText = () => {
    const parsed = readHex(text, alpha)
    if (parsed) commit(parsed)
    else setInvalid(true)
  }

  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={invalid ? 'Enter a colour, e.g. #3b82f6, rgb(59 130 246) or hsl(217 91% 60%).' : helperText}
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <span className={boxClass(size)} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
        <Popover.Root>
          <Popover.Trigger
            className={cn(inputStyles.iconButton, styles.trigger)}
            style={{ '--swatch': hex } as CSSProperties}
            disabled={disabled}
            aria-label={`Choose colour, ${hex} selected`}
          />
          <Popover.Portal>
            <Popover.Positioner className={styles.positioner} side="bottom" align="start" sideOffset={6}>
              <Popover.Popup aria-label="Choose colour" className={styles.popup}>
                <ColorPanel value={hex} onValueChange={commit} alpha={alpha} defaultFormat={defaultFormat} swatches={swatches} />
              </Popover.Popup>
            </Popover.Positioner>
          </Popover.Portal>
        </Popover.Root>
        <Field.Control
          id={id}
          value={text}
          spellCheck={false}
          autoComplete="off"
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          required={required}
          className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.hexInput)}
          onChange={(e) => {
            setText(e.target.value)
            setInvalid(false)
          }}
          onBlur={commitText}
          onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === 'Enter' && commitText()}
        />
        {name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={hex} />}
      </span>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Color Picker Chooses a colour: type it in any CSS format, pick a swatch, find it on a sa...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { ColorPicker } from './ColorPicker'
import * as ColorPickerStories from './ColorPicker.stories'

<Meta of={ColorPickerStories} />

# Color Picker

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Chooses a colour: type it in any CSS format, pick a swatch, find it on a
saturation and brightness area and a hue strip, or type its channels in
Hex, RGB, HSL or HSB. The panel is laid out like Figma's colour picker.

<Status of={ColorPickerStories} />

<Canvas of={ColorPickerStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two exports.

| Export | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `ColorPicker` | A form field: the hex in a text field, with a swatch button that opens the panel in a popover. |
| `ColorPanel` | The panel on its own, always open: a sidebar, an inspector, a settings page about colour. |

<Canvas of={ColorPickerStories.Panel} />

`alpha` adds opacity; `defaultFormat` picks which channels the fields show
first.

<Canvas of={ColorPickerStories.FormatsAndOpacity} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ColorPicker, ColorPanel } from 'zweihander/color-picker'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/color-picker.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/ColorPicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/ColorPicker.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/color-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/color-picker)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover) and [Slider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/slider)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ColorPickerStories.anatomyParts}>

The panel here is shown open under its field; in a `ColorPicker` it opens
in a popover from the swatch button.

## Measurements

The field is a Text Input: the same tiers, padding and label. The panel is
the same at both field sizes.

    { part: 'Hue and opacity strips', property: 'Thickness', token: '--space-3' },
    { part: 'Hue and opacity strips', property: 'Gap between them', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Thumbs', property: 'Size', token: '--space-4' },
    { part: 'Format menu and channel fields', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Swatches', property: 'Minimum size', token: '--space-6' },
    { part: 'Swatches', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Hit area, strip thumbs', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The panel is 16rem wide, so eight swatches fit in a row, and the area is
10rem tall. The format menu and the channels are the kit's md (32px)
Select and field box.

## Color

The area, the hue strip and the checkerboard are the colour model itself,
so they are fixed colours, not theme tokens. The thumbs are white rings
with a dark edge: one of the two is at least 3:1 against whatever colour
is under them.

<SpecTable
  rows={[
    { part: 'Popover', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Popover', property: 'Text', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Popover and swatch divider', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Popover', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-md' },
    { part: 'Swatch button', property: 'Inner edge', token: '--control-border' },
    { part: 'Chosen swatch', property: 'Ring', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Channel fields', property: 'Divider', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

Swatches have a faint inner edge, black 10% in light mode and white 10%
in dark, as in Figma. That is below the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11 round a white
swatch on white, accepted because the hex in the field, not the edge,
tells the colour.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <ColorPicker label="Brand colour" disabled /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <ColorPicker label="Brand colour" validationState="error" helperText="Pick a darker colour." /> },
  ]}
>
  <ColorPicker label="Brand colour" />
</States>

- **Focus** follows Text Input on the field. In the panel every thumb,
  swatch and field draws a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside.
- **Disabled** dims the field and disables the swatch button.
- **Error** is Text Input's. Typed text that is not a colour turns the
  field to error on its own, with a hint, and keeps the last good value.
- **Chosen swatch** has a 2px `--primary` ring; focused as well, the ring
  turns `--ring` and moves 1px further out.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ColorPickerStories} />
</div>

`ColorPanel` takes `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `alpha`,
`defaultFormat`, `swatches`, `disabled` and `className`.

`parseColor(text)` reads any CSS colour (`rgb(59 130 246)`,
`hsl(217 91% 60% / 50%)`, `oklch(...)`, `rebeccapurple`) to the same hex,
or `null`; the browser parses it, so outside one only hex is read.
`normalizeHex(text)` turns `#abc`, `ABC` or `#AABBCC` into `#aabbcc`,
keeps an alpha byte (`#3b82f680`, or `#abc8` as `#aabbcc88`) unless it is
`ff`, and turns anything else into `null`.

### Design notes

- **Hex in, hex out.** The value is lowercase `#rrggbb`, with an alpha
  byte only while opacity is under 100%. Typed text is read on Enter or
  blur: hex of 3, 4, 6 or 8 digits with or without `#`, or any CSS colour.
  It is shown back as hex.
- **Formats are a view, not a value.** RGB, HSL and HSB only change the
  fields; the value stays hex. Channel fields commit on Enter or blur, and
  up and down step by 1 (Shift by 10), as in a design tool.
- **The hue is remembered.** The picker keeps hue, saturation and
  brightness, so dragging to black and back leaves the hue strip where it
  was instead of jumping to red.
- **Not in this version:** Figma's library picker ("On this page"),
  gradients and an eyedropper.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a colour picker when any colour is a valid answer: a brand colour, a
chart series, a label someone defines. When there is a palette to follow,
offer it as named swatches.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ColorPickerStories.DoBrandSwatches} />}
  doCaption="The colours people should use, as named swatches: one click, and a screen reader says “Blue”, not a hex."
  dont={<Story of={ColorPickerStories.DontNoSwatches} />}
  dontCaption="A palette to follow but no swatches: people match it by eye and land a few steps off."
/>

<Canvas of={ColorPickerStories.Swatches} />

## When not to use

- **For a few fixed colours.** When only a set of colours is allowed (tag
  colours, a theme accent), use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group of swatches or
  a Select: the picker lets anyone type any colour.
- **To show a colour.** Use a swatch and its hex as text.

## Accessibility

- The field is a text input named by its label. The swatch button is
  named "Choose colour, #3b82f6 selected", and the popover is a dialog
  named "Choose colour" that returns focus to the button on Escape.
- The area is one tab stop: a slider named "Saturation" whose value text
  reads both numbers ("Saturation 76%, brightness 96%"). Left and right
  change saturation, up and down brightness, Shift moves 10%, Page Up and
  Page Down change brightness by 10%, Home and End set saturation to 0 or
  100%. A second "Brightness" slider is there for a screen reader's
  browse mode.
- The hue strip is a slider named "Hue", read as "217 degrees"; the
  opacity strip, "Opacity", read as "50%".
- The format menu is the kit's Select, named "Colour format". Channel
  fields are text inputs named for what they hold ("Red", "Hue degrees",
  "Lightness percent", "Opacity percent", "Hex"), so they do not share a
  name with the sliders.
- Swatches are native radios in a radio group named "Swatches": one tab
  stop, arrows move and choose, and the chosen one is checked. None is
  checked while the colour is not one of them. They are 24px with 8px
  between them, which meets WCAG 2.5.8 without a larger invisible target.
- A colour is never the only way to know the value: the hex is always in
  the field.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, useRef, useState, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react'
import { Combobox as BaseCombobox } from '@base-ui/react/combobox'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  popupInset,
  inputStyles as s,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'
import styles from './Combobox.module.css'

/** Labels are strings here: they are what is typed, matched and shown in the input. */
export type ComboboxOption = string | { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }
type Item = { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }

export interface ComboboxProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLInputElement>
  options: ComboboxOption[]
  value?: string | null
  defaultValue?: string | null
  /** The spec's `onChange`. `null` when cleared. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string | null) => void
  placeholder?: string
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Options are still arriving: a spinner, and "Loading…" in the list. */
  isLoading?: boolean
  /** Show a button that clears the selection. */
  isClearable?: boolean
  /** Shown in the list when nothing matches. */
  emptyText?: string
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  autoFocus?: boolean
  id?: string
  /** Where the popup renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen or a scope with its own density. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/** The first case-insensitive match of the query, marked. */
function Highlight({ text, query }: { text: string; query: string }) {
  const at = query ? text.toLowerCase().indexOf(query.toLowerCase()) : -1
  if (at < 0) return <>{text}</>
  return (
    <>
      {text.slice(0, at)}
      <mark className={styles.match}>{text.slice(at, at + query.length)}</mark>
      {text.slice(at + query.length)}
    </>
  )
}

export function Combobox({
  ref,
  options,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  placeholder,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  isLoading,
  isClearable = true,
  emptyText = 'No matches',
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  autoFocus,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: ComboboxProps) {
  const items: Item[] = options.map((o) => (typeof o === 'string' ? { value: o, label: o } : o))
  const find = (v: string | null | undefined) => (v == null ? v : (items.find((i) => i.value === v) ?? null))
  // Only for highlighting the typed text in each option; Base UI owns the
  // input's value and the filtering.
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('')
  // A pointer pick sends the field back to rest: no caret, no ring, as a
  // native select after a click. A keyboard pick keeps focus where the user is.
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null)
  const labelId = useId()

  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      labelId={labelId}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <BaseCombobox.Root
        items={items}
        value={find(value)}
        defaultValue={find(defaultValue)}
        onValueChange={(next, details) => {
          // After Base UI's own refocus of the input, hence the timeout.
          if (details.event instanceof MouseEvent) setTimeout(() => inputRef.current?.blur())
          onValueChange?.((next as Item | null)?.value ?? null)
        }}
        // Highlight only what was typed. When an option is chosen the input
        // takes its label, which is not a query to mark in other options.
        onInputValueChange={(next, details) => setQuery(details.reason === 'input-change' ? next : '')}
        // items are rebuilt each render, so compare by value, not identity,
        // or the selection loses its check on the next keystroke.
        isItemEqualToValue={(a: Item, b: Item) => a.value === b.value}
        readOnly={readOnly}
        required={required}
        autoHighlight
      >
        <BaseCombobox.InputGroup
          className={cn(boxClass(size), styles.group)}
        >
          <BaseCombobox.Input
            ref={(el) => {
              inputRef.current = el
              if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(el)
              else if (ref) ref.current = el
            }}
            id={id}
            placeholder={placeholder}
            autoFocus={autoFocus}
            aria-label={ariaLabel}
            aria-busy={isLoading || undefined}
            className={s.control}
          />
          {isLoading && <span className={cn(s.icon, s.spinner)} aria-hidden="true" />}
          {isClearable && !readOnly && (
            <BaseCombobox.Clear className={s.iconButton} aria-label="Clear selection">
              <Icon name="clear" />
            </BaseCombobox.Clear>
          )}
          <BaseCombobox.Trigger
            className={s.iconButton}
            // Field labels every control in it with the field's label; this
            // button is not the field, so it keeps its own name rather than
            // being a second "Team member".
            render={(props) => <button {...props} aria-labelledby={undefined} aria-label="Show options" />}
          >
            <Icon name="chevron-down" />
          </BaseCombobox.Trigger>
        </BaseCombobox.InputGroup>
        <BaseCombobox.Portal container={container}>
          <BaseCombobox.Positioner className={s.positioner} sideOffset={4}>
            <BaseCombobox.Popup
              className={s.popup}
              style={popupInset(size)}
            >
              {isLoading ? (
                <BaseCombobox.Status className={s.status}>Loading…</BaseCombobox.Status>
              ) : (
                <BaseCombobox.Empty className={s.empty}>{emptyText}</BaseCombobox.Empty>
              )}
              {/* A listbox needs a name of its own: the field's. */}
              <BaseCombobox.List aria-labelledby={label ? labelId : undefined} aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}>
                {(item: Item) => (
                  <BaseCombobox.Item key={item.value} value={item} disabled={item.disabled} className={s.option}>
                    <BaseCombobox.ItemIndicator className={s.check}>
                      <Icon name="check" />
                    </BaseCombobox.ItemIndicator>
                    <span>
                      <Highlight text={item.label} query={query} />
                    </span>
                  </BaseCombobox.Item>
                )}
              </BaseCombobox.List>
            </BaseCombobox.Popup>
          </BaseCombobox.Positioner>
        </BaseCombobox.Portal>
      </BaseCombobox.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}
