# Combobox

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A field you type into to filter a list of options, then choose one.

<Status of={ComboboxStories} />

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two sizes, and the field's validation states. Typing filters the list and
marks the match; the chosen option carries a check.

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and settings: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a toolbar filter, a table row, beside `sm` buttons. |

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Validation} />

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Clear} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Combobox } from 'zweihander/combobox'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/combobox.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/combobox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/combobox)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Combobox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ComboboxStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ComboboxStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The options list opens under the field, at least as wide as it:

- **Option**: the label, with the typed text marked by weight and
  underline. Options are inset by the field's padding, so their text
  starts where the input's does.
- **Check**: before the chosen option's label, in a column kept for every
  option so labels never shift.
- **Message**: "No matches" (`emptyText`) when nothing matches,
  "Loading…" while `isLoading`.

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.OpenButton} />

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). Fields take the normal
inline padding, so the value lines up with the label above it, and the
field radius, which never becomes a pill.

The field is 20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`; the list is at least as
wide as the field, 4px under it, and scrolls after 20rem (about ten
options).

## Color

  caption="Field"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Border', token: '--field-border' },

    { part: 'Placeholder, helper, icons', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Required asterisk', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable

  rows={[
    { part: 'Border, helper, focus ring, error', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Border, helper, success', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Field, read-only', property: 'Background', token: '--surface-filled' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Options list"
  rows={[
    { part: 'List', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'List', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'List', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-md' },
    { part: 'Option', property: 'Colour', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Option, highlighted', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Option, highlighted', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Check', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-text' },
    { part: 'No matches, Loading…', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

The field's edge is a light hairline, about 1.5:1, as in the Claude apps:
an approved exception to WCAG 1.4.11. The label, placeholder and focus
ring still mark the field. The matched text keeps the option's own colour,
so it holds full contrast on the highlighted row.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Filled', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Clear} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Validation} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <Fit><Combobox label="Team member" options={['Miya Burns']} defaultValue="Miya Burns" readOnly /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Disabled} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Loading', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Loading} /></Fit> },
  ]}
>
  <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Default} /></Fit>
</States>

- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the field, drawn while
  the input has focus, by pointer too: that is where typing goes. In the
  error state the ring is `--danger-text`. The clear and open buttons draw
  their own ring when tabbed to, so the field never shows two.
- **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the clear and open buttons
  darken from `--muted-foreground` to `--foreground`.
- **Error** turns the edge and the helper `--danger-text` together; the
  words are the message, the colour only points at it.
- **Read-only** fills the field with `--surface-filled`; there is no clear
  button.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.
- **Loading** adds a spinner before the buttons and says "Loading…" in the
  list.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ComboboxStories} />
</div>

### Differences from the spec

- **Labels must be strings**, not components: they are what is typed,
  matched and shown in the input.
- **`emptyText`** is added: an empty list needs to say why.
- **`onValueChange`, not `onChange`**, and native names (`disabled`,
  `readOnly`, `required`), as on Select.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Combobox to choose one option from a long list, when people already
know what they are looking for: a person, a country, a project. Typing a
few letters is faster than scrolling. It chooses from the list only; free
text that is not an option is not a value.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ComboboxStories.DoLongList} />}
  doCaption="A long list people know an entry of: type a few letters, pick it."
  dont={<Story of={ComboboxStories.DontFewOptions} />}
  dontCaption="Three options hidden behind typing. A Select or a radio group shows them all."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a handful of options.** Under about seven, use a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group when they
  should all be visible.
- **For free text.** If any answer is valid, use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs); to filter
  a page, use [Search](?path=/docs/components-inputs-search--docs).
- **For several values.** It holds one; a multi-select is not built yet.

## Accessibility

- The input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and
  `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox` named by the field's label (or
  `aria-label` when there is no visible label), as the input is.
- **Keyboard:** typing opens and filters; the first match is highlighted
  so Enter picks it; Up and Down move; Escape closes, then clears.
- The match is marked by weight and underline, not colour, so it keeps
  the option's full contrast on the highlighted row.
- The open button is named "Show options" and is out of the tab order
  (the input already opens the list); the clear button is "Clear
  selection".
- `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid`, and the helper text is
  the input's description.
- Loading and empty states are announced from the list.
- After an option is picked with the pointer, the input loses focus and the
  field returns to rest (no caret, no ring). A keyboard pick keeps focus in
  the input, so keyboard and screen reader users are not dropped to the page.
- Options are 32px tall; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) they grow to
  44px, and the clear and open buttons get a 44×44px hit area.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useEffect, useId, useRef, useState, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Autocomplete } from '@base-ui/react/autocomplete'
import { Dialog } from '@base-ui/react/dialog'
import { Kbd } from '../atomic-elements/Kbd'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './CommandPalette.module.css'

/** A command or an object: what is typed is matched against `label` and `keywords`. */
export interface CommandPaletteItem {
  value: string
  label: string
  icon?: ReactNode
  /** More words that find it: "bill" for "New invoice". Not shown. */
  keywords?: string[]
  /** Shown right-aligned, one key cap per key: `['⌘', 'N']`. Display only: it does not bind the key. */
  shortcut?: string[]
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Runs when the item is chosen, once the palette has closed and given focus back. */
  onSelect?: () => void
}

/** A titled run of items: Recent, Commands, Customers. A group with no match is left out. */
export interface CommandPaletteGroup {
  label: string
  items: CommandPaletteItem[]
}

export interface CommandPaletteProps {
  groups: CommandPaletteGroup[]
  /** The button that opens it, e.g. a search field in the sidebar. */
  trigger?: ReactElement
  /**
   * The letter that toggles it with ⌘ or Ctrl, anywhere on the page.
   * `false` binds nothing: only one palette on a page should own the key.
   */
  hotkey?: string | false
  /** Called with the chosen item, after its own `onSelect`. */
  onSelect?: (item: CommandPaletteItem) => void
  placeholder?: string
  /** Names the search input. */
  inputLabel?: string
  /** Shown when nothing matches. */
  emptyText?: string
  /** Names the dialog. */
  label?: string
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Trap focus, lock page scroll and make the page inert while open. `false` is for pictures of it. */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where it renders instead of `<body>`. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
}

export function CommandPalette({
  groups,
  trigger,
  hotkey = 'k',
  onSelect,
  placeholder = 'Search commands…',
  inputLabel = 'Search commands',
  emptyText = 'No results',
  label = 'Command palette',
  open,
  defaultOpen = false,
  onOpenChange,
  isModal = true,
  container,
  className,
}: CommandPaletteProps) {
  const [ownOpen, setOwnOpen] = useState(defaultOpen)
  const isOpen = open ?? ownOpen
  const setOpen = (next: boolean) => {
    if (open === undefined) setOwnOpen(next)
    onOpenChange?.(next)
  }
  const hintsId = useId()
  // Accent-insensitive, so "hoa don" finds "Hóa đơn".
  const { contains } = Autocomplete.useFilter({ sensitivity: 'base' })

  // Re-bound every render: the handler reads the current open state.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!hotkey) return
    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (e.repeat || e.isComposing) return
      if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && !e.altKey && !e.shiftKey && e.key.toLowerCase() === hotkey.toLowerCase()) {
        e.preventDefault()
        setOpen(!isOpen)
      }
    }
    document.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
    return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
  })

  // The choice runs after the close has finished and focus is back on the
  // trigger, so an action that opens a dialog or moves focus keeps it.
  const chosen = useRef<CommandPaletteItem | null>(null)
  const choose = (item: CommandPaletteItem) => {
    chosen.current = item
    setOpen(false)
  }
  const onClosed = (isOpenNow: boolean) => {
    const item = chosen.current
    if (isOpenNow || !item) return
    chosen.current = null
    item.onSelect?.()
    onSelect?.(item)
  }

  return (
    <Dialog.Root open={isOpen} onOpenChange={setOpen} onOpenChangeComplete={onClosed} modal={isModal}>
      {trigger && <Dialog.Trigger render={trigger} />}
      <Dialog.Portal container={container}>
        <Dialog.Backdrop className={styles.backdrop} />
        <Dialog.Viewport className={styles.viewport}>
          <Dialog.Popup className={cn(styles.popup, className)} aria-label={label}>
            {/* inline + open: the list is part of the dialog, not a popup of its own. */}
            <Autocomplete.Root
              items={groups}
              itemToStringValue={(item: CommandPaletteItem) => item.label}
              filter={(item: CommandPaletteItem, query) =>
                [item.label, ...(item.keywords ?? [])].some((text) => contains(text, query))
              }
              open
              inline
              autoHighlight="always"
              keepHighlight
            >
              <Autocomplete.InputGroup className={styles.search}>
                <Icon name="search" className={styles.searchIcon} />
                <Autocomplete.Input
                  className={styles.input}
                  placeholder={placeholder}
                  aria-label={inputLabel}
                  aria-describedby={hintsId}
                />
              </Autocomplete.InputGroup>
              <div className={styles.results}>
                <Autocomplete.Empty className={styles.empty}>{emptyText}</Autocomplete.Empty>
                <Autocomplete.List className={styles.list}>
                  {(group: CommandPaletteGroup) => (
                    <Autocomplete.Group key={group.label} items={group.items} className={styles.group}>
                      <Autocomplete.GroupLabel className={styles.groupLabel}>{group.label}</Autocomplete.GroupLabel>
                      <Autocomplete.Collection>
                        {(item: CommandPaletteItem) => (
                          <Autocomplete.Item
                            key={item.value}
                            value={item}
                            disabled={item.disabled}
                            className={styles.item}
                            onClick={() => choose(item)}
                          >
                            {item.icon && (
                              <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
                                {item.icon}
                              </span>
                            )}
                            <span className={styles.label}>{item.label}</span>
                            {/* Shown, not part of the name, as on a Menu item. */}
                            {item.shortcut && <Kbd size="sm" keys={item.shortcut} aria-hidden="true" />}
                          </Autocomplete.Item>
                        )}
                      </Autocomplete.Collection>
                    </Autocomplete.Group>
                  )}
                </Autocomplete.List>
              </div>
              {/* The keys, drawn for sight and said once to a screen reader as the input's description. */}
              <div className={styles.footer}>
                <span id={hintsId} className={styles.visuallyHidden}>
                  Arrow keys to move, Enter to choose, Escape to close.
                </span>
                <span className={styles.hint} aria-hidden="true">
                  <Kbd size="sm" keys={['↑', '↓']} /> Move
                </span>
                <span className={styles.hint} aria-hidden="true">
                  <Kbd size="sm">↵</Kbd> Choose
                </span>
                <span className={styles.hint} aria-hidden="true">
                  <Kbd size="sm">Esc</Kbd> Close
                </span>
              </div>
            </Autocomplete.Root>
          </Dialog.Popup>
        </Dialog.Viewport>
      </Dialog.Portal>
    </Dialog.Root>
  )
}

# Command Palette A search box over the page that finds a command or a record by typing an...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as CommandPaletteStories from './CommandPalette.stories'

<Meta of={CommandPaletteStories} />

# Command Palette

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A search box over the page that finds a command or a record by typing and
runs it with Enter, without a mouse. Opened by its trigger or by ⌘K
(Ctrl+K).

<Status of={CommandPaletteStories} />

<Canvas of={CommandPaletteStories.Default} />

## Variants

There is one palette; what changes is what you put in its groups.

| Content | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Commands | Actions a power user repeats: New invoice, Export ledger. Give each its `shortcut` when it has one, so the palette teaches the key. |
| Records | Objects to jump to, grouped by type: Customers, Invoices. Load them from your search as the user types, or pass the few that matter. |
| Recent | What the user opened last, as the first group. The palette does not remember it for you: pass it from your app's history. |

Typing matches the label and `keywords`, ignoring case and accents, so
"bill" finds New invoice and "hoa binh" finds Hòa Bình Trading.

<Canvas of={CommandPaletteStories.Matching} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { CommandPalette } from 'zweihander/command-palette'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/command-palette.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/CommandPalette.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/CommandPalette.tsx)
- Spec: uiguideline.com has no command palette; anatomy from Tailwind UI Command Palettes and shadcn/ui Command
- Behaviour: [Base UI Autocomplete](https://base-ui.com/react/components/autocomplete) (inline, inside a [Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog))
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CommandPaletteStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CommandPaletteStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open palettes on this tab and the next are pictures: real palettes
rendered in a frame with `container`, not modal (`isModal={false}`) and
inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Container"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-xl' },

    { part: 'Search row', property: 'Gap, icon to input', token: '--control-md-gap' },
    { part: 'Search icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Search input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-lg' },

/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Item and group label"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-md-gap' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Group label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Group label', property: 'Padding above', token: '--control-xs-pad' },

  ]}
/>

The container is at most 40rem wide and never wider than the screen. It
sits near the top, at 12% of the screen height, not centred: the list
grows and shrinks as you type, and the input stays where the eye is. The
list shows about ten rows (24rem) and then scrolls; the search row and the
key hints stay. The search icon lines up with the item icons. Items are
the [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs)'s rows; shortcuts
are [Kbd](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-kbd--docs) `sm`.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Every palette"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Backdrop', property: 'Background', token: '--scrim' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Container, rules', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Input, items', property: 'Colour', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Placeholder, icons, group labels, hints', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Highlighted item', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Highlighted item', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Results', content: <Story of={CommandPaletteStories.Results} /> },
    { label: 'No results', content: <Story of={CommandPaletteStories.NoResults} /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Highlighted** is where the arrow keys or the pointer are: an `--accent`
  fill, the icon taking the text colour. The first match is always
  highlighted, so Enter always does something. Focus stays in the input;
  the highlight is the list's `aria-activedescendant`.
- **Disabled** items are muted at 60% opacity. The arrow keys still reach
  them, so a screen reader hears that they exist, but Enter and a click do
  nothing.
- **No results** shows `emptyText` and no group labels.
- The input has no focus ring of its own: it is the palette's only field,
  and the caret shows where typing goes.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CommandPaletteStories} />
</div>

### Differences from the spec

The queue's anatomy lists the open shortcut, an empty state and recent
results as parts. Here the shortcut is behaviour (`hotkey`, and a Kbd on the
trigger), the empty state is a state (under States), and Recent is a group
you pass: the palette does not store history.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

In an app with many pages and actions, as a fast way around for people who
use it every day: jump to a record, run a command, without going through
the navigation. Open it from a search button in the sidebar
(`NavSidebarButton appearance="field"`) and from ⌘K.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CommandPaletteStories.DoGroup} />}
  doCaption="Group the results, start each command with a verb, and put records under their type. Recent first."
  dont={<Story of={CommandPaletteStories.DontMix} />}
  dontCaption="One list of bare nouns: Invoice could mean open one, create one or list them all."
/>

Keep the palette a shortcut, not the only way: everything in it must also
be reachable from the navigation or a button on the page.

## When not to use

- **To search inside one list or table.** Use a search field above it,
  which filters what is on the page.
- **To pick a value in a form.** Use a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs): it fills a
  field, the palette runs something.
- **For a handful of actions on one object.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) on that object.

## Accessibility

- The container is a `role="dialog"` named "Command palette" (`label`).
  Opening moves focus to the search input and traps it inside; closing
  returns focus to the trigger.
- The input is a `role="combobox"` named "Search commands" (`inputLabel`), its
  description the key hints: "Arrow keys to move, Enter to choose, Escape to
  close". The drawn hints are hidden, so they are read once.
- Each group is a `role="group"` named by its label; each item is a
  `role="option"`. A shortcut is drawn, not read: the item's name is its
  label.
- Up and Down move the highlight and the first match is highlighted; Enter
  chooses it, as does a click. A disabled item is reachable but Enter does
  nothing on it. The choice runs once the palette has closed and focus is
  back on the trigger.

  <Canvas of={CommandPaletteStories.Keyboard} />

- Escape closes it, as does a press outside.

  <Canvas of={CommandPaletteStories.Empty} />

- ⌘K or Ctrl+K toggles it from anywhere on the page; one palette per page
  should own that key, and the others set `hotkey={false}`.

  <Canvas of={CommandPaletteStories.Hotkey} />

Give the trigger `aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K"` when the palette
owns the key, as the trigger in these examples does.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Container Caps a page's content at a maximum width and centres it in the space it is giv...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ContainerStories from './Container.stories'

<Meta of={ContainerStories} />

# Container

Caps a page's content at a maximum width and centres it in the space it
is given. After Tailwind UI Application UI, Layout: Containers.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/container.json
```

Container only sets a width. Inside an [App
Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs), [App
Content](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-app-content--docs) owns the
page: its padding, its scroll and the aside column. Put a Container inside
it when a page should not stretch across a wide screen, a settings page or
a form; leave it out for a table that uses every column.

## Sizes

`size` is the widest the content gets: `sm` 48rem for a form or a settings
page, `md` (the default) 64rem for most pages, `lg` 80rem for a wide table
or a dashboard.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.Sizes} />

## Padded

`padded` adds side padding by breakpoint, for a page outside the App
Shell, such as a sign-in page or a public page: `--space-container`, and
`--space-section` from a 64rem viewport: App Content's tokens and step,
measured against the viewport instead of the shell, on the sides only.
The cap measures the content, so a padded and an unpadded Container of one
size give the same line length.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.Padded} />

## In an App Shell

No `padded`: App Content already pads the page, and the Container centres
the content in it. With an aside, it centres in the page column.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.InAppShell} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={ContainerStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **Full width up to the cap.** It fills its parent, block, grid or flex,
  until it reaches its size, then centres with equal space on each side.
- **Narrower than its size,** it takes the width it is given and never
  overflows.
- **Padding follows the viewport,** not a container query: outside the
  App Shell no ancestor is a size container to query.

<Canvas of={ContainerStories.Narrow} />

## Differences from the spec

Tailwind UI's Containers, and where this departs from them:

- **Three steps, not every `max-w-*`.** `sm`, `md` and `lg` follow
  Tailwind's `max-w-3xl`, `5xl` and `7xl`.
- **Padding is opt-in and uses the kit's spacing tokens.** Tailwind pads
  every container (`px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8`); here App Content pads the page
  in the shell, so padding twice would be wrong. One step at 64rem, as in
  App Content, instead of Tailwind's two.
- **No "full width on mobile" variant.** Under its size a Container is
  already full width; a flush, unpadded page on a phone is App Content's
  job.

## Accessibility

- A plain `div`: no landmark, no role and no focus. The landmark is the
  `main` around it (App Content's, or your own outside the shell).
- It changes no order; content reads and tabs in DOM order.
- At 320px it takes the full width and its content reflows; it adds no
  horizontal scroll.

const iso = (d: Date) =>
  `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`

/** The locale's numeric date format, its field order and a placeholder pattern. */
function useDateFormat(locale?: string) {
  return useMemo(() => {
    // Gregorian and Western digits whatever the locale's defaults: the grid is
    // Gregorian, and the parser reads ASCII digits. Without this, th-TH shows
    // the Buddhist year (2569) and fa-IR Persian digits, and neither reads back.
    const format = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {
      day: '2-digit',
      month: '2-digit',
      year: 'numeric',
      calendar: 'gregory',
      numberingSystem: 'latn',
    })
    const parts = format.formatToParts(new Date(2026, 10, 22))
    const order = parts.filter((p) => p.type === 'day' || p.type === 'month' || p.type === 'year').map((p) => p.type)
    const pattern = parts
      .map((p) => (p.type === 'day' ? 'dd' : p.type === 'month' ? 'mm' : p.type === 'year' ? 'yyyy' : p.value))
      .join('')
    /** Reads the three numbers in the locale's order; any separator will do. */
    const parse = (text: string): Date | null | undefined => {
      const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
      if (!text.trim()) return null
      if (!nums || nums.length !== 3) return undefined
      const v: Record<string, number> = {}
      order.forEach((type, i) => (v[type] = Number(nums[i])))
      const year = v.year < 100 ? 2000 + v.year : v.year
      const d = new Date(year, v.month - 1, v.day)
      // Rejects 31/02 and the like, which Date would roll into March.
      return d.getFullYear() === year && d.getMonth() === v.month - 1 && d.getDate() === v.day ? d : undefined
    }
    return { format: (d: Date) => format.format(d), parse, pattern }
  }, [locale])
}

    setInvalid(false)
    if (next) setMonth(next)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  const commitText = () => {
    const parsed = parse(text)
    if (parsed === undefined || (parsed && !allowed(parsed))) setInvalid(true)
    else if (parsed === null ? date !== null : !isSameDay(parsed, date)) commit(parsed)
    else setInvalid(false)
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => setMonth(date ?? today)}
      triggerLabel={date ? `Choose date, ${format(date)} selected` : 'Choose date'}
      popupLabel="Choose date"
      hidden={name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={date ? iso(date) : ''} />}
      label={label}
      helperText={invalid ? `Enter a date as ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText}
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      placeholder={placeholder ?? pattern}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => (
        <Calendar
          value={date}
          month={month}
          onMonthChange={setMonth}
          onValueChange={(d) => {
            commit(d)
            close()
          }}
          min={min}
          max={max}
          isDateDisabled={isDateDisabled}
          locale={locale}
          weekStartsOn={weekStartsOn}
          autoFocus={autoFocus}
          className={styles.body}
        />
      )}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ range */

export interface DateRangePreset {
  label: string
  start: Date
  end: Date
}

/** The built-in presets, whole periods around today: Today … Last year. */
export function rangePresets(weekStartsOn: number, today = startOfDay(new Date())): DateRangePreset[] {
  const week = addDays(today, -((today.getDay() - weekStartsOn + 7) % 7))
  const y = today.getFullYear()
  const m = today.getMonth()
  return [
    { label: 'Today', start: today, end: today },
    { label: 'Yesterday', start: addDays(today, -1), end: addDays(today, -1) },
    { label: 'This week', start: week, end: addDays(week, 6) },
    { label: 'Last week', start: addDays(week, -7), end: addDays(week, -1) },
    { label: 'This month', start: new Date(y, m, 1), end: new Date(y, m + 1, 0) },
    { label: 'Last month', start: new Date(y, m - 1, 1), end: new Date(y, m, 0) },
    { label: 'This year', start: new Date(y, 0, 1), end: new Date(y, 11, 31) },
    { label: 'Last year', start: new Date(y - 1, 0, 1), end: new Date(y - 1, 11, 31) },
  ]
}

export interface DateRangePickerProps extends Omit<DatePickerProps, 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onValueChange' | 'name'> {
  /** Both ends set, or `null`. */
  value?: DateRange | null
  defaultValue?: DateRange | null
  onValueChange?: (range: DateRange | null) => void
  /** A list beside the calendars: `true` for the built-in one (Today … Last year), or your own. */
  presets?: boolean | DateRangePreset[]
  /** Submitted as `yyyy-mm-dd/yyyy-mm-dd`, an ISO 8601 interval. */
  name?: string
}

const NO_RANGE: DateRange = { start: null, end: null }
const monthIndex = (d: Date) => d.getFullYear() * 12 + d.getMonth()
/** The range's first month on the left, its last on the right; the next month when it spans one. */
const monthsFor = (r: DateRange | null, today: Date): [Date, Date] => {
  const left = r?.start ?? today
  const right = r?.end && monthIndex(r.end) > monthIndex(left) ? r.end : addMonths(left, 1)
  return [left, right]
}
/** The two days as a range, earlier first. */
const ordered = (a: Date | null, b: Date | null): DateRange => (a && b && b < a ? { start: b, end: a } : { start: a, end: b })
const sameRange = (a: DateRange | null, b: DateRange | null) =>
  a === b || (!!a && !!b && isSameDay(a.start, b.start) && isSameDay(a.end, b.end))

export function DateRangePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  presets = false,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DateRangePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const range = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const show = (r: DateRange | null) => (r?.start && r.end ? `${format(r.start)} – ${format(r.end)}` : '')
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => show(range))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<DateRange>(range ?? NO_RANGE)
  // The two calendars page on their own; the left one always shows the
  // earlier month. Moving one past the other pushes the other along.
  const [months, setMonths] = useState(() => monthsFor(range, today))
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(range)
  if (!sameRange(shown, range)) {
    setShown(range)
    setText(show(range))
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const presetList = presets === true ? rangePresets(weekStartsOn ?? firstDayOfWeek(locale), today) : presets || []
  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: DateRange | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(show(next))
    setInvalid(false)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  /** Two dates, each in the locale's order: six numbers, any separators. */
  const commitText = () => {
    const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
    let parsed: DateRange | null | undefined = null
    if (text.trim()) {
      const a = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(0, 3).join(' ')) : undefined
      const b = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(3).join(' ')) : undefined
      parsed = a && b && allowed(a) && allowed(b) ? ordered(a, b) : undefined
    }
    if (parsed === undefined) setInvalid(true)
    else if (!sameRange(parsed, range)) commit(parsed)
    else setText(show(range))
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => {
        setDraft(range ?? NO_RANGE)
        setMonths(monthsFor(range, today))
      }}
      triggerLabel={range ? `Choose dates, ${show(range)} selected` : 'Choose dates'}
      popupLabel="Choose dates"
      popupClassName={styles.rangePopup}
      hidden={
        name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={range?.start && range.end ? `${iso(range.start)}/${iso(range.end)}` : ''} />
      }
      label={label}
      helperText={
        invalid ? `Enter two dates as ${pattern} – ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText
      }
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      placeholder={placeholder ?? `${pattern} – ${pattern}`}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => {
        // A range applies as soon as both ends are in.
        const choose = (r: DateRange) => {
          setDraft(r)
          if (!r.start || !r.end) return
          if (!sameRange(r, range)) commit(r)
          close()
        }
        // The first click starts a range, the second ends it, either way round.
        const pick = (d: Date) => choose(!draft.start || draft.end ? { start: d, end: null } : ordered(draft.start, d))
        const calendar = { range: draft, onValueChange: pick, min, max, isDateDisabled, locale, weekStartsOn }
        return (
          <>
            {presetList.length > 0 && (
              <div role="group" aria-label="Presets" className={styles.presets}>
                {presetList.map((p) => (
                  <button
                    key={p.label}
                    type="button"
                    aria-pressed={isSameDay(p.start, draft.start) && isSameDay(p.end, draft.end)}
                    className={styles.preset}
                    onClick={() => {
                      setMonths(monthsFor(p, today))
                      choose({ start: p.start, end: p.end })
                    }}
                  >
                    {p.label}
                  </button>
                ))}
              </div>
            )}
            <div className={styles.months}>
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[0]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([, right]) => [m, monthIndex(m) < monthIndex(right) ? right : addMonths(m, 1)])}
                autoFocus={autoFocus}
                className={styles.body}
              />
              {/* Hidden on a narrow screen, where one month fits. */}
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[1]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([left]) => [monthIndex(left) < monthIndex(m) ? left : addMonths(m, -1), m])}
                className={cn(styles.body, styles.second)}
              />
            </div>
          </>
        )
      }}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

# Date Picker A date field: type the date, or pick it from a calendar. ## Variants Two siz...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { DatePicker } from './DatePicker'

# Date Picker

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A date field: type the date, or pick it from a calendar.

<Status of={DatePickerStories} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two sizes, `sm` and `md`, and the field's validation states, as on
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs). The typed
order follows `locale`: day first in `en-GB` and `vi-VN`, month first in
`en-US`. The form always gets `yyyy-mm-dd`.

| Locale | Typed as |
| --- | --- |
| `en-GB`, `vi-VN` | `dd/mm/yyyy` |
| `en-US` | `mm/dd/yyyy` |

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.UnitedStates} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Vietnamese} />

`min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled` limit what can be picked or typed:

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Range} />

For a span of days, see
[Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs).

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { DatePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/date-picker.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover), and the kit's [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={DatePickerStories.anatomyParts}>

The calendar opens in a popover 4px under the field, aligned to its
start: a [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs)
in a panel. Its days, header and paging buttons are specified there.

normal inline padding and the field radius.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Empty', content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" /> },
    { label: 'Filled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    {
      label: 'Error',
      content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" validationState="error" helperText="Enter a date as dd/mm/yyyy." />,
    },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 8, 18)} readOnly /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 8, 18)} disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 8, 18)} />
</States>

- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the field, drawn while
  the input has focus, by pointer too. In the error state the ring is
  `--danger-text`. The calendar button draws its own ring when tabbed to.
- **Error** turns the edge and the helper `--danger-text`. It is also
  shown on its own while the typed text is not a date, or is outside
  `min` and `max`: the helper then gives the expected pattern.
- **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the calendar icon darkens from
  `--muted-foreground` to `--foreground`.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--surface-filled`, as every
  Zweihänder field does. The input stays focusable and copyable and its
  value is submitted; the calendar icon stays but is not a button, so the
  calendar never opens. Say why in `helperText`.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity; the calendar button is
  disabled with it.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DatePickerStories} />
</div>

### Design notes

- **Typing is first-class.** Many people type a known date faster than
  they can page to it. Any separator works (`3.10.26`, `3/10/2026`); the
  field reformats on blur or Enter.
- **An impossible date is kept, not guessed.** `31/02/2026` stays as
  typed, the field turns to its error state and the helper shows the
  expected pattern; nothing is reported until it is a real date.
- **A click in the input opens the calendar, and keeps focus there.**
  Typing carries on with the month in view; the calendar button and
  Alt+Down move focus into the calendar instead.
- **The form gets ISO.** Whatever the display order, `name` submits
  `yyyy-mm-dd`, so the server never has to guess the locale.
### Differences from the spec

- **`onValueChange`, not `onChange`**, with a `Date` or `null`, as the
  kit's other value fields.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Date Picker for one date: a start date, a due date, a booking. Let
people type it when they know it, and pick it when they want to see the
week around it. Set `min`, `max` or `isDateDisabled` so a date that cannot
be used cannot be chosen, rather than refusing it after submit.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DatePickerStories.DoPatternPlaceholder} />}
  doCaption="The empty field shows the pattern to type, in the locale's order."
  dont={<Story of={DatePickerStories.DontExamplePlaceholder} />}
  dontCaption="An example date as the placeholder reads as a value already filled in."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a span of days.** Use a
  [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs):
  one field, both ends, never back to front.
- **To show a month on the page.** Use a
  [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) inline.
- **For a time of day.** The picker holds a date only.

## Accessibility

- The input is a labelled text box with `inputmode="numeric"` for a
  number keypad; while the text is not a valid date it has
  `aria-invalid` and the helper explains the format.
- The calendar button is named "Choose date", with the current date when
  there is one. Alt+Down in the input opens it too.
- `readOnly` puts `readonly` on the input: screen readers announce it,
  it stays in the tab order, and there is no calendar button; a click or
  Alt+Down opens nothing.
- The calendar opens as a dialog named "Choose date" with focus on the
  selected day; Escape closes it without a change.
- **After a pick the field goes back to rest.** Picked with the pointer,
  focus leaves the field (no caret, no ring), as in Combobox. Picked with
  the keyboard, focus returns to where it came from (the button, or the
  input), so keyboard and screen reader users are not dropped to the page.
- The field and calendar's own labels ("Choose date", "Previous month")
  are in English, like the rest of the kit's built-in labels.
- On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) the calendar button gets a 44×44px
  hit area without the field growing.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

} from '../data-display/Calendar'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'
import styles from './DatePicker.module.css'

export interface DatePickerProps {
  value?: Date | null
  defaultValue?: Date | null
  /** `null` when the field is cleared. Not called while the typed text is not a date yet. */
  onValueChange?: (date: Date | null) => void
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Under the field. Replaced by a format hint while the typed text is not a valid date. */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  min?: Date | null
  max?: Date | null
  isDateDisabled?: (date: Date) => boolean
  /** BCP 47 tag; decides the typed order (day/month/year) and the calendar's. */
  locale?: string
  weekStartsOn?: number
  /** Defaults to the locale's pattern, e.g. "dd/mm/yyyy". */
  placeholder?: string
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Submitted as `yyyy-mm-dd`, whatever the display format. */
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Shown and submitted but locked: still focusable and copyable; the calendar does not open. */
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  id?: string
  /** Where the popup renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen or a scope with its own density. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

const iso = (d: Date) =>
  `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`

/** The locale's numeric date format, its field order and a placeholder pattern. */
function useDateFormat(locale?: string) {
  return useMemo(() => {
    // Gregorian and Western digits whatever the locale's defaults: the grid is
    // Gregorian, and the parser reads ASCII digits. Without this, th-TH shows
    // the Buddhist year (2569) and fa-IR Persian digits, and neither reads back.
    const format = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {
      day: '2-digit',
      month: '2-digit',
      year: 'numeric',
      calendar: 'gregory',
      numberingSystem: 'latn',
    })
    const parts = format.formatToParts(new Date(2026, 10, 22))
    const order = parts.filter((p) => p.type === 'day' || p.type === 'month' || p.type === 'year').map((p) => p.type)
    const pattern = parts
      .map((p) => (p.type === 'day' ? 'dd' : p.type === 'month' ? 'mm' : p.type === 'year' ? 'yyyy' : p.value))
      .join('')
    /** Reads the three numbers in the locale's order; any separator will do. */
    const parse = (text: string): Date | null | undefined => {
      const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
      if (!text.trim()) return null
      if (!nums || nums.length !== 3) return undefined
      const v: Record<string, number> = {}
      order.forEach((type, i) => (v[type] = Number(nums[i])))
      const year = v.year < 100 ? 2000 + v.year : v.year
      const d = new Date(year, v.month - 1, v.day)
      // Rejects 31/02 and the like, which Date would roll into March.
      return d.getFullYear() === year && d.getMonth() === v.month - 1 && d.getDate() === v.day ? d : undefined
    }
    return { format: (d: Date) => format.format(d), parse, pattern }
  }, [locale])
}

interface PickerFieldProps {
  text: string
  onTextChange: (text: string) => void
  /** Reads the typed text, on blur and Enter. */
  onCommit: () => void
  /** Before the popover opens: show the value's month, reset a half-picked range. */
  onShow: () => void
  triggerLabel: string
  popupLabel: string
  popupClassName?: string
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  /** The hidden input that submits the value. */
  hidden?: ReactNode
  children: (popup: { autoFocus: boolean; close: () => void }) => ReactNode
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size: InputSize
  placeholder: string
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/**
 * The typed field and its calendar popover, shared by both pickers. The
 * calendar button and Alt+Down open it with focus on the calendar; a click
 * in the input opens it too, but leaves focus there so typing carries on.
 */
function PickerField({
  text,
  onTextChange,
  onCommit,
  onShow,
  triggerLabel,
  popupLabel,
  popupClassName,
  container,
  hidden,
  children,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size,
  placeholder,
  isFullWidth,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: PickerFieldProps) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [fromInput, setFromInput] = useState(false)
  const boxRef = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null)
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  // Whether the last press in the popup was the pointer's. A pointer pick
  // sends the field back to rest (no caret, no ring); a keyboard pick or
  // Escape returns focus to where it came from, so keyboard users stay put.
  const byPointer = useRef(false)
  const show = (byInput: boolean) => {
    if (readOnly) return
    onShow()
    byPointer.current = false
    setFromInput(byInput)
    setOpen(true)
  }
  /** Where focus goes when the popover closes. */
  const finalFocus = () => {
    if (!byPointer.current) return fromInput ? inputRef.current : true
    // Opened from the input, focus never left it. After the render, so the
    // input's blur commit reads the picked text.
    setTimeout(() => document.activeElement === inputRef.current && inputRef.current?.blur())
    return false
  }

  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <span ref={boxRef} className={boxClass(size)} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
        <Field.Control
          ref={inputRef}
          id={id}
          value={text}
          placeholder={placeholder}
          inputMode="numeric"
          autoComplete="off"
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          required={required}
          readOnly={readOnly}
          className={inputStyles.control}
          onChange={(e) => onTextChange(e.target.value)}
          onBlur={onCommit}
          onClick={() => !open && show(true)}
          onKeyDown={(e) => {
            if (e.key === 'Enter') onCommit()
            if (e.key === 'ArrowDown' && e.altKey) show(false)
          }}
        />
        {hidden}
        <Popover.Root
          open={open}
          onOpenChange={(next, details) => {
            if (next) return show(false)
            // A press in the field is not outside: the calendar stays open while typing.
            if (details.reason === 'outside-press' && boxRef.current?.contains(details.event.target as Node)) return
            setOpen(false)
          }}
        >
          {/* Read-only keeps the icon, so the field still reads as a date, but
              not the button: a calendar that cannot pick is a dead end. */}
          {readOnly ? (
            <span className={inputStyles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
              <Icon name="calendar" />
            </span>
          ) : (
            <Popover.Trigger className={inputStyles.iconButton} disabled={disabled} aria-label={triggerLabel}>
              <Icon name="calendar" />
            </Popover.Trigger>
          )}
          <Popover.Portal container={container}>
            {/* Under the whole field, start-aligned and 4px clear of it; not the
                calendar button, which sits inside the box. */}
            <Popover.Positioner
              className={styles.positioner}
              anchor={boxRef}
              side="bottom"
              align="start"
              sideOffset={4}
            >
              <Popover.Popup
                aria-label={popupLabel}
                className={cn(styles.popup, popupClassName)}
                initialFocus={!fromInput}
                finalFocus={finalFocus}
                onPointerDownCapture={() => (byPointer.current = true)}
                onKeyDownCapture={() => (byPointer.current = false)}
              >
                {children({ autoFocus: !fromInput, close: () => setOpen(false) })}
              </Popover.Popup>
            </Popover.Positioner>
          </Popover.Portal>
        </Popover.Root>
      </span>
    </InputField>
  )
}

export function DatePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DatePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const date = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => (date ? format(date) : ''))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [month, setMonth] = useState(() => date ?? today)
  // Follow a controlled value that changes from outside.
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(date)
  if (!isSameDay(shown, date) && !(shown === null && date === null)) {
    setShown(date)
    setText(date ? format(date) : '')
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: Date | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(next ? format(next) : '')
    setInvalid(false)
    if (next) setMonth(next)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  const commitText = () => {
    const parsed = parse(text)
    if (parsed === undefined || (parsed && !allowed(parsed))) setInvalid(true)
    else if (parsed === null ? date !== null : !isSameDay(parsed, date)) commit(parsed)
    else setInvalid(false)
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => setMonth(date ?? today)}
      triggerLabel={date ? `Choose date, ${format(date)} selected` : 'Choose date'}
      popupLabel="Choose date"
      hidden={name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={date ? iso(date) : ''} />}
      label={label}
      helperText={invalid ? `Enter a date as ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText}
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      placeholder={placeholder ?? pattern}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => (
        <Calendar
          value={date}
          month={month}
          onMonthChange={setMonth}
          onValueChange={(d) => {
            commit(d)
            close()
          }}
          min={min}
          max={max}
          isDateDisabled={isDateDisabled}
          locale={locale}
          weekStartsOn={weekStartsOn}
          autoFocus={autoFocus}
          className={styles.body}
        />
      )}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ range */

export interface DateRangePreset {
  label: string
  start: Date
  end: Date
}

/** The built-in presets, whole periods around today: Today … Last year. */
export function rangePresets(weekStartsOn: number, today = startOfDay(new Date())): DateRangePreset[] {
  const week = addDays(today, -((today.getDay() - weekStartsOn + 7) % 7))
  const y = today.getFullYear()
  const m = today.getMonth()
  return [
    { label: 'Today', start: today, end: today },
    { label: 'Yesterday', start: addDays(today, -1), end: addDays(today, -1) },
    { label: 'This week', start: week, end: addDays(week, 6) },
    { label: 'Last week', start: addDays(week, -7), end: addDays(week, -1) },
    { label: 'This month', start: new Date(y, m, 1), end: new Date(y, m + 1, 0) },
    { label: 'Last month', start: new Date(y, m - 1, 1), end: new Date(y, m, 0) },
    { label: 'This year', start: new Date(y, 0, 1), end: new Date(y, 11, 31) },
    { label: 'Last year', start: new Date(y - 1, 0, 1), end: new Date(y - 1, 11, 31) },
  ]
}

export interface DateRangePickerProps extends Omit<DatePickerProps, 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onValueChange' | 'name'> {
  /** Both ends set, or `null`. */
  value?: DateRange | null
  defaultValue?: DateRange | null
  onValueChange?: (range: DateRange | null) => void
  /** A list beside the calendars: `true` for the built-in one (Today … Last year), or your own. */
  presets?: boolean | DateRangePreset[]
  /** Submitted as `yyyy-mm-dd/yyyy-mm-dd`, an ISO 8601 interval. */
  name?: string
}

const NO_RANGE: DateRange = { start: null, end: null }
const monthIndex = (d: Date) => d.getFullYear() * 12 + d.getMonth()
/** The range's first month on the left, its last on the right; the next month when it spans one. */
const monthsFor = (r: DateRange | null, today: Date): [Date, Date] => {
  const left = r?.start ?? today
  const right = r?.end && monthIndex(r.end) > monthIndex(left) ? r.end : addMonths(left, 1)
  return [left, right]
}
/** The two days as a range, earlier first. */
const ordered = (a: Date | null, b: Date | null): DateRange => (a && b && b < a ? { start: b, end: a } : { start: a, end: b })
const sameRange = (a: DateRange | null, b: DateRange | null) =>
  a === b || (!!a && !!b && isSameDay(a.start, b.start) && isSameDay(a.end, b.end))

export function DateRangePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  presets = false,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DateRangePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const range = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const show = (r: DateRange | null) => (r?.start && r.end ? `${format(r.start)} – ${format(r.end)}` : '')
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => show(range))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<DateRange>(range ?? NO_RANGE)
  // The two calendars page on their own; the left one always shows the
  // earlier month. Moving one past the other pushes the other along.
  const [months, setMonths] = useState(() => monthsFor(range, today))
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(range)
  if (!sameRange(shown, range)) {
    setShown(range)
    setText(show(range))
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const presetList = presets === true ? rangePresets(weekStartsOn ?? firstDayOfWeek(locale), today) : presets || []
  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: DateRange | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(show(next))
    setInvalid(false)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  /** Two dates, each in the locale's order: six numbers, any separators. */
  const commitText = () => {
    const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
    let parsed: DateRange | null | undefined = null
    if (text.trim()) {
      const a = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(0, 3).join(' ')) : undefined
      const b = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(3).join(' ')) : undefined
      parsed = a && b && allowed(a) && allowed(b) ? ordered(a, b) : undefined
    }
    if (parsed === undefined) setInvalid(true)
    else if (!sameRange(parsed, range)) commit(parsed)
    else setText(show(range))
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => {
        setDraft(range ?? NO_RANGE)
        setMonths(monthsFor(range, today))
      }}
      triggerLabel={range ? `Choose dates, ${show(range)} selected` : 'Choose dates'}
      popupLabel="Choose dates"
      popupClassName={styles.rangePopup}
      hidden={
        name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={range?.start && range.end ? `${iso(range.start)}/${iso(range.end)}` : ''} />
      }
      label={label}
      helperText={
        invalid ? `Enter two dates as ${pattern} – ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText
      }
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      placeholder={placeholder ?? `${pattern} – ${pattern}`}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => {
        // A range applies as soon as both ends are in.
        const choose = (r: DateRange) => {
          setDraft(r)
          if (!r.start || !r.end) return
          if (!sameRange(r, range)) commit(r)
          close()
        }
        // The first click starts a range, the second ends it, either way round.
        const pick = (d: Date) => choose(!draft.start || draft.end ? { start: d, end: null } : ordered(draft.start, d))
        const calendar = { range: draft, onValueChange: pick, min, max, isDateDisabled, locale, weekStartsOn }
        return (
          <>
            {presetList.length > 0 && (
              <div role="group" aria-label="Presets" className={styles.presets}>
                {presetList.map((p) => (
                  <button
                    key={p.label}
                    type="button"
                    aria-pressed={isSameDay(p.start, draft.start) && isSameDay(p.end, draft.end)}
                    className={styles.preset}
                    onClick={() => {
                      setMonths(monthsFor(p, today))
                      choose({ start: p.start, end: p.end })
                    }}
                  >
                    {p.label}
                  </button>
                ))}
              </div>
            )}
            <div className={styles.months}>
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[0]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([, right]) => [m, monthIndex(m) < monthIndex(right) ? right : addMonths(m, 1)])}
                autoFocus={autoFocus}
                className={styles.body}
              />
              {/* Hidden on a narrow screen, where one month fits. */}
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[1]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([left]) => [monthIndex(left) < monthIndex(m) ? left : addMonths(m, -1), m])}
                className={cn(styles.body, styles.second)}
              />
            </div>
          </>
        )
      }}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

# Date Range Picker A field for a span of days: a report period, a booking. Typed like [Da...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { DateRangePicker } from './DatePicker'
import * as DateRangePickerStories from './DateRangePicker.stories'

<Meta of={DateRangePickerStories} />

# Date Range Picker

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A field for a span of days: a report period, a booking. Typed like
[Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs), or picked
from two months side by side.

<Status of={DateRangePickerStories} />

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two sizes, `sm` and `md`, and the field's validation states, as on Date
Picker. With `presets`, whole periods sit beside the calendars.

| Option | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| No presets | Ranges that rarely line up with a calendar period: a booking, a leave request. |
| `presets` | Reports and filters, where people mostly want "Last month" or "This year". |

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.Presets} />

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.Vietnamese} />

## Resources

Shipped in the same file as Date Picker, which it shares its field and
popover with. From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { DateRangePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/date-picker.json
```

- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover), and the kit's [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={DateRangePickerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={DateRangePickerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The popover holds:

- **Presets**, with `presets`: whole periods, Today to Last year, in a
  column beside the calendars, or a row above them on a narrow screen.
- **Calendars**: two months that page on their own, opening on the
  range's first and last months (this month and the next when empty). The
  left one always stays before the right: paging one past the other
  pushes the other along. One month on a screen narrower than 40rem.

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.PagingApart} />

## Measurements

The field is Date Picker's: each size is a control tier, with the normal
inline padding and the field radius.

The days and the band between the range's ends are the

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Empty', content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" /> },
    { label: 'Filled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    {
      label: 'Error',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" validationState="error" helperText="Choose both ends." />,
    },
    {
      label: 'Read-only',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} readOnly />,
    },
    {
      label: 'Disabled',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} disabled />,
    },
  ]}
>
  <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} />
</States>

The field's states are Date Picker's: a `--ring` outline while the input
has focus, `--danger-text` in error (also while the typed text is not a
range), `--surface-filled` and no calendar button when read-only, 50%
opacity when disabled. A preset matching the picked range
stays in its pressed look.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DateRangePickerStories} />
</div>

### Design notes

- **Either way round.** The first click starts the range, the second
  ends it; a second click before the first swaps them. So does typing
  the later date first.
- **Presets are whole periods.** "This month" is the 1st to the last
  day, not the 1st to today, so a preset reads the same all month.
- **No Cancel or Apply.** A range applies, and the popover closes, once
  both ends are in; Escape before the second click leaves the value as
  it was.
- **No hover preview.** The band shows once both ends are in; add a
  preview if testing shows people lose track of the first click.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Date Range Picker when the two dates are one thing: a period to
report on, a stay, a sprint. Both ends are set together, start never after
end, and the value is complete or `null`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DateRangePickerStories.DoOneField} />}
  doCaption="One field for one period: it cannot be half filled or set back to front."
  dont={<Story of={DateRangePickerStories.DontTwoFields} />}
  dontCaption="Two Date Pickers for one period: here the end is before the start, and nothing stops it."
/>

## When not to use

- **For one date.** Use a
  [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).
- **When one end is optional**, such as a contract with no end date. The
  range needs both ends; use two Date Pickers and check their order
  yourself.

## Accessibility

- As Date Picker: a labelled text box, an error state with the expected
  pattern, and the calendars in a dialog named "Choose dates".
- The calendar button is named "Choose dates", with the current range
  when there is one.
- `readOnly` works as on Date Picker: `readonly` on the input, no
  calendar button, and a click or Alt+Down opens nothing.
- Every day in the range has `aria-selected`, so the span is announced,
  not only its ends.
- A day of the month either side is decoration: hidden from assistive
  tech and not pickable, so each day is one button.
- Presets are toggle buttons in a group named "Presets"; the one that
  matches the picked range is `aria-pressed`.
- After both ends are in the field goes back to rest, as Date Picker's
  does after a pick.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Description List The fields of a record, as terms and their details: a profile, an order...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DescriptionListStories from './DescriptionList.stories'

<Meta of={DescriptionListStories} />

# Description List

The fields of a record, as terms and their details: a profile, an order,
an application. It is read-only; its editable twin is a settings form in
Form Layouts.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/description-list.json
```

## Columns

Term and details side by side, a line between rows, and an optional
action at the end of each row ("Update").

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.Columns} />

## In a card

`isCard` puts the header in a top band and the list below it, inside one
border. With `layout="grid"`, fields run two to a row; `isWide` gives
long text and attachments the full width.

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.InCard} />

## Stacked

Term over details, one field after another: for a sidebar or a narrow
panel.

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.Stacked} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `DescriptionItem[]` | – | Required. `{ term, details, action?, isWide? }` |
| `title` | node | – | |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `actions` | node | – | Buttons at the end of the header. |
| `layout` | `columns`, `grid`, `stacked` | `columns` | |
| `isCard` | boolean | `false` | |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

<Controls of={DescriptionListStories.Columns} />

## Layout

- **It responds to its own width, not the viewport's.** Columns and grid
  are container queries: under 36rem of list width they stack, so the
  same list works in a main column, a sidebar and a phone.

  <Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.ColumnsNarrow} />

- Details wrap anywhere, so a long email address or URL never pushes the
  layout wide.

## Accessibility

- A real `<dl>`: a screen reader announces a list of terms and reads each
  detail with its term.
- Row actions sit in their own `<dd>` after the details. Give each one the
  field it acts on ("Update Email address"), hidden if you like, so a
  list of links is not six identical "Update"s.

  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /** Indents both ends so the line stops short of its container's edges. */
  inset?: boolean

  /** uiguideline calls this `variant`; renamed because `variant` means color here. */

        styles[size],

        className,

  )

<Meta of={DividerStories} />

# Divider

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A thin line that separates content into groups: sections of a card, items
in a toolbar, blocks of a page.

<Status of={DividerStories} />

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `solid` | Almost everywhere: the quiet default. |
| `dashed` | A boundary that is softer or provisional: a drop zone, a "more below" break, a draft section. |

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Dashed} />

A **vertical** divider separates items in a row: toolbar groups, links in
a footer. It has no fixed height and stretches to its flex row.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Vertical} />

**Inset** stops the line short of the container's edges, so it aligns with
the text in a padded list rather than running edge to edge.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Inset} />

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Sizes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Divider } from 'zweihander/divider'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/divider.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/divider](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/divider)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={DividerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={DividerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

One part. The line is a border, top for horizontal and start for
vertical, and the box shrinks to it: a vertical divider is exactly as
wide as its line.

## Measurements

Thickness is whole pixels, not a token: the token layer has no
border-width scale, and a rule should stay a crisp pixel at every
`--scaling`.

| Size | Thickness |
| --- | --- |
| `sm` | 1px |
| `md` | 2px |
| `lg` | 4px |

<SpecTable
  caption="inset, every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Horizontal line', property: 'Inline margin', token: '--space-4' },
    { part: 'Vertical line', property: 'Block margin', token: '--space-2' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

Every size and appearance uses the same colour.

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Line', property: 'Colour', token: '--border' }]} />

## States

A divider is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. It looks the same
whether it is announced or decorative; only a screen reader tells them
apart.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Solid', content: <Stack><Divider /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Dashed', content: <Stack><Divider appearance="dashed" size="md" /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Inset', content: <Stack><Divider inset /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Decorative', content: <Stack><Divider aria-hidden /></Stack> },
  ]}
/>

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DividerStories} />
</div>

Every other `<hr>` attribute passes through, including `ref` and
`aria-hidden`.

### Differences from the spec

- **`appearance`, not `variant`.** In this kit `variant` always means a
  colour by intent (primary, destructive…) and `appearance` means a style.
  Solid versus dashed is a style.
- **Thickness is raw px.** The token layer has no border-width scale, and
  a divider is the only component that needs three.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Divider between groups that spacing alone does not separate: the
sections of a menu, the blocks of a settings page, groups in a toolbar.
Divide groups, not every item: a line after each row turns a list into
stripes and makes the real breaks harder to see.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DividerStories.DoDivideGroups} />}
  doCaption="One line between two groups: the break carries meaning."
  dont={<Story of={DividerStories.DontDivideEveryItem} />}
  dontCaption="A line after every item: nothing stands out as a group."
/>

## When not to use

- **Where space already separates.** Cards, list items with padding and
  headed sections are grouped by their own whitespace; a line adds noise.
- **As the only thing that tells groups apart.** The line is faint on
  purpose (see Accessibility). Pair it with a heading or space.
- **For a border of a component.** Draw that with the component's own
  border, not a Divider beside it.

## Accessibility

- `<hr>` is announced as a separator. Vertical dividers add
  `aria-orientation="vertical"`; horizontal ones don't, because that is
  already the default.
- If the line is purely decorative, e.g. between two icons that are
  already grouped, pass `aria-hidden` so it isn't announced at all.
- The `--border` colour is below 3:1 against the background on purpose: a
  divider is decoration and is not required to meet the non-text contrast
  ratio. Never let a divider be the only thing that tells groups apart.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>
