## Color

One colour set: the current page is the only fill. Switch the theme and
the accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Page, Previous, Next', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Page, Previous, Next, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Page, Previous, Next, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Current page', property: 'Background', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Current page', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-foreground' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis, Summary, Rows per page label', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

At rest a control has no fill.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={PaginationStories.StatesExample} />
</States>

- **Selected**: the current page is filled with `--primary`, medium
  weight. It does not change on hover, and pressing it does nothing.
- **Hover** fills a page, Previous or Next with an `--accent` chip.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the control.
- **Disabled**: Previous on the first page (above) and Next on the last, at 50%
  opacity. As buttons they are `disabled`; as links they lose their
  `href`.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={PaginationStories} />
</div>

The rows-per-page select is a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs)
at the same `size`. Changing it moves to the page that holds the first row
shown before, so the reader does not lose their place; it calls
`onPageSizeChange`, then `onPageChange` if the page moved.

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through. `paginationItems(page,
total, siblings, boundary)` is exported too, for building your own.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Pagination under a long list or table when the reader needs to know
where they are in it and jump to a page: search results, an audit log, an
order history. Put it below the content it pages, and keep the list's
position stable as pages change.

Leave `siblingCount` and `boundaryCount` at 1. The control stays short and
keeps the same width as the reader moves, so Next stays under the pointer.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={PaginationStories.DoKeepItShort} />}
  doCaption="The default range: first, last, and the current page with a neighbour each side, on one line."
  dont={<Story of={PaginationStories.DontShowEveryPage} />}
  dontCaption="Every page number at once wraps over several lines and buries the current page."
/>

Under a table, pass `totalItems` so the reader knows how much there is.
Offer `pageSizeOptions` only when readers really scan in bulk; three or
four choices (10, 20, 50, 100) are enough.

When the pages have URLs, pass `getHref`, so a page can be opened in a new
tab, bookmarked and shared.

## When not to use

- **For a feed read top to bottom.** Load more as the reader scrolls, or
  with a "Load more" [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs):
  page numbers mean nothing in a stream.
- **For a few items.** If everything fits on one page, show it all.
- **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper.
- **For switching between views of one thing.** Use Tabs.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Pagination", around a list.
- Each page control is named "Page 3"; the current one has
  `aria-current="page"`. Previous and next are named "Previous page" and
  "Next page".
- At either end, Previous or Next is disabled. As links they lose their
  `href` (the only thing that stops an `<a>` navigating) and keep
  `role="link"` with `aria-disabled`, so they are still announced as a
  disabled link.
- With `getHref`, each control is a real `<a href>`; without it, a native
  `<button>`. Both are in the tab order and activate with Enter (buttons
  with Space too).
- The summary has `role="status"`, a polite live region, so "21–40 of 340"
  is read out after a page or size change.
- The rows-per-page select is a combobox named "Rows per page"; its
  visible label is `aria-hidden` so the name is not read twice.
- The ellipsis is `aria-hidden`: the page names already say which numbers
  are there.
- Controls are 24px (`sm`) or 32px (`md`) and grow to 44px on touch
  screens (`pointer: coarse`).
- Focus ring: 2px `--ring`, 2px offset.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, useState } from 'react'
import { arc, pie } from 'd3-shape'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Table } from '../data-display/Table'
import { Skeleton } from '../loaders/Skeleton'
import { ChartFrame, useEnterOnce } from './ChartFrame'
import { ChartLegend } from './ChartLegend'
import { colorVar, formatCompact, formatShare, groupSlices, type Slice } from './chart-utils'
import styles from './Chart.module.css'

export interface PieChartProps {
  /** Shown above the chart, and its accessible name. */
  title: string
  data: Slice[]
  /** `donut` leaves a hole with the total in it. */
  appearance?: 'pie' | 'donut'
  /** Under the total in a donut, e.g. "requests". */
  centerLabel?: string
  /** Diameter in pixels. */
  size?: number
  format?: (value: number) => string
  isLoading?: boolean
  className?: string
}

/**
 * Parts of one whole. No labels on the slices: the legend beside it carries
 * value and share. Past six slices, or under 3%, slices merge into "Other".
 */
export function PieChart({
  title,
  data,
  appearance = 'pie',
  centerLabel = 'Total',
  size = 200,
  format = formatCompact,
  isLoading = false,
  className,
}: PieChartProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [focusKey, setFocusKey] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const total = data.reduce((sum, d) => sum + d.value, 0)
  // All zeros is no data: a pie of nothing has no parts to show.
  const hasData = total > 0
  const isEntering = useEnterOnce(!isLoading && hasData)
  const shareOf = (value: number) => formatShare(value / total)

  const slices = groupSlices(data)
  const isDonut = appearance === 'donut'
  const radius = size / 2 - 2
  const arcs = pie<(typeof slices)[number]>()
    .sort(null)
    .value((d) => d.value)(slices)
  const path = arc<(typeof arcs)[number]>()
    .innerRadius(isDonut ? radius * 0.64 : 0)
    .outerRadius(radius)
    .padAngle(isDonut ? 0.015 : 0)
    .cornerRadius(isDonut ? 2 : 0)

  return (
    <ChartFrame
      title={title}
      isLoading={isLoading}
      loading={<Skeleton appearance="circle" width={size} height={size} />}
      hasData={hasData}
      emptyHeight={size}
      className={className}
      table={() => (
        <Table
          caption={title}
          density="sm"
          rows={data}
          getRowId={(_, i) => String(i)}
          columns={[
            { key: 'label', header: 'Label', isRowHeader: true },
            { key: 'value', header: 'Value', align: 'end', cell: (d) => format(d.value) },
            { key: 'share', header: 'Share', align: 'end', cell: (d) => shareOf(d.value) },
          ]}
        />
      )}
    >
      {(titleId) => (
        <div className={styles.pieBody}>
          <svg
            role="img"
            aria-labelledby={`${titleId} ${id}-desc`}
            className={cn(isEntering && styles.entering)}
            width={size}
            height={size}
            viewBox={`${-size / 2} ${-size / 2} ${size} ${size}`}
          >
            {/* The sweep-in: a ring stroke drawn round the mask, once. */}
            <mask id={`${id}-sweep`}>
              <circle className={styles.sweep} r={radius / 2} fill="none" stroke="white" strokeWidth={radius + 4} pathLength={1} transform="rotate(-90)" />
            </mask>
            <g mask={isEntering ? `url(#${id}-sweep)` : undefined}>
              {arcs.map((a, i) => (
                <path
                  key={i}
                  className={cn(styles.slice, focusKey && focusKey !== String(i) && styles.dim)}
                  d={path(a) ?? ''}
                  fill={colorVar(a.data.color)}
                  onPointerEnter={() => setFocusKey(String(i))}
                  onPointerLeave={() => setFocusKey(null)}
                />
              ))}
            </g>
            {isDonut && (
              <>
                <text className={styles.centerTotal} textAnchor="middle" dy="-0.05em">
                  {format(total)}
                </text>
                <text className={styles.centerLabel} textAnchor="middle" dy="1.5em">
                  {centerLabel}
                </text>
              </>
            )}
          </svg>
          <span id={`${id}-desc`} className={styles.srOnly}>
            {slices.map((s) => `${s.label} ${shareOf(s.value)}`).join(', ')}
          </span>
          <ChartLegend
            orientation="vertical"
            items={slices.map((s, i) => ({ key: String(i), label: s.label, color: colorVar(s.color), value: `${format(s.value)} · ${shareOf(s.value)}` }))}
            onFocusChange={setFocusKey}
          />
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartFrame>
  )
}

'use client'

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Popover as BasePopover } from '@base-ui/react/popover'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Popover.module.css'

export interface PopoverProps {
  /** The element that opens it: one button. Its props are merged, not wrapped. */
  trigger: ReactElement
  /** Names the popover (it is a dialog). Without one, pass `aria-label`. */
  title?: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  children?: ReactNode
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  /** A close button in the corner. Escape and a click outside close it either way. */
  hasCloseButton?: boolean
  closeLabel?: string
  /** Open on hover as well as click, for previews. Content must still be reachable by click and keyboard. */
  openOnHover?: boolean
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Trap focus inside while open, lock page scroll and block clicks outside (Base UI's modal mode). */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where the popup renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function Popover({
  trigger,
  title,
  description,
  children,
  side = 'bottom',
  align = 'center',
  hasCloseButton = false,
  closeLabel = 'Close',
  openOnHover = false,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  isModal = false,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  className,
}: PopoverProps) {
  return (
    <BasePopover.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}
      modal={isModal}
    >
      <BasePopover.Trigger render={trigger} openOnHover={openOnHover} />
      <BasePopover.Portal container={container}>
        <BasePopover.Positioner className={styles.positioner} side={side} align={align} sideOffset={6}>
          <BasePopover.Popup aria-label={title ? undefined : ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.popup, className)}>
            {(title || hasCloseButton) && (
              <div className={styles.header}>
                {title && <BasePopover.Title className={styles.title}>{title}</BasePopover.Title>}
                {hasCloseButton && (
                  <BasePopover.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close}>
                    <Icon name="close" />
                  </BasePopover.Close>
                )}
              </div>
            )}
            {/* Base UI only traps focus in a modal popover that contains a
                Close, and a touch screen reader needs one to get out. */}
            {isModal && !hasCloseButton && (
              <BasePopover.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={cn(styles.close, styles.hiddenClose)}>
                <Icon name="close" />
              </BasePopover.Close>
            )}
            {description && <BasePopover.Description className={styles.description}>{description}</BasePopover.Description>}
            {children && <div className={styles.body}>{children}</div>}
          </BasePopover.Popup>
        </BasePopover.Positioner>
      </BasePopover.Portal>
    </BasePopover.Root>
  )
}

./src/components/overlays/Popover.mdx
# Popover A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a share form,...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as PopoverStories from './Popover.stories'

<Meta of={PopoverStories} />

# Popover

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a share
form, a filter, a set of options. It opens on click and stays until you
close it.

<Status of={PopoverStories} />

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.Open} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Non-modal (default) | Most popovers. Tab can leave it and the page stays usable while it is open. |
| Modal (`isModal`) | A popover that must be finished or closed first: focus stays inside, the page does not scroll and presses outside are blocked. |
| `openOnHover` | A preview that also opens on hover, when what it holds must be reachable by click, keyboard and touch. For a person or record preview on a link, use [HoverCard](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs). |

A title is optional. Without one, name the popover with `aria-label`:

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.ContentOnly} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Popover } from 'zweihander/popover'
```

```sh

<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={PopoverStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={PopoverStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open popovers on this tab and the next are pictures: real popovers
rendered in place with `container` and inert, the popup laid out under the
trigger where it opens.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Container"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-md' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Title to close button', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Title to description', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Body', property: 'Gap above', token: '--space-3' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Close button"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The container is as wide as its content, at most 22rem and never wider
than the room beside the trigger. It has no arrow: it opens 6px from the
trigger and lines up with it, which already ties the two. It has a 1px
border and a semibold title. The close button is 20px: 2px around its icon,
one line of text tall. Popovers sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade
in over `--duration-fast`.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Every popover"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--popover' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Title, body', property: 'Colour', token: '--popover-foreground' },
    { part: 'Description', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--accent-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

Select and Combobox lists use the same surface: `--popover`, its border
and shadow.

## States

The popover is open or closed. Opening fades it in and scales it up from
97%, from the trigger's side. The trigger keeps the states of its own
component (see Button); the close button is the only part with states of
its own:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={PopoverStories.CloseButton} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills the close button with `--accent`.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the button.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={PopoverStories} />
</div>

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Popover for a short task that belongs to the button that opens it:
share a file, set a filter, pick from a few options. It holds links,
inputs and buttons, which a Tooltip must not.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={PopoverStories.DoShortTask} />}
  doCaption="A short task tied to its button: one field and one action."
  dont={<Story of={PopoverStories.DontLongForm} />}
  dontCaption="A whole form in a popover. It closes on a stray press outside and loses the work: use a Modal."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a label or a hint** on hover or focus. Use a
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs).
- **For a list of actions or commands.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs): it has the
  arrow-key navigation a list of commands needs.
- **For a long form or a decision with consequences.** Use a
  [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs).

## Accessibility

- The popup is a `role="dialog"` named by `title` (or `aria-label`) and
  described by `description`. The trigger carries `aria-expanded` and
  `aria-haspopup`.
- Opening moves focus into the popup; Escape or a press outside closes it
  and returns focus to the trigger.
- **Non-modal by default:** Tab can leave the popup, and the page stays
  usable. `isModal` switches to Base UI's modal mode: focus is trapped,
  page scroll is locked and presses outside are blocked.
- Base UI only traps focus when the popup contains a close button, and a
  touch screen reader needs one to get out. So a modal popover without
  `hasCloseButton` still renders one: hidden until it has keyboard focus,
  then shown in the corner, so focus is never invisible.

  <Canvas of={PopoverStories.Modal} />

- `openOnHover` adds hover to click, it does not replace it: the content
  stays reachable by keyboard and touch.
- The close button has the 2px focus ring and a 44px hit area on touch
  screens.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import styles from './ProgressBar.module.css'

export interface ProgressBarProps extends Omit<Progress.Root.Props, 'value' | 'children' | 'className' | 'render'> {
  value?: number
  /** The spec's `maxValue`. */
  max?: number
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  isRounded?: boolean
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary' | 'destructive'
  /** Progress is happening but how much is unknown: a sliding bar. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  /** Show the value ("70%") after the bar. */
  showValueLabel?: boolean
  /** A visible label above the bar; also its accessible name. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** The accessible name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function ProgressBar({
  value = 0,
  max = 100,
  size = 'md',
  isRounded = false,
  variant = 'primary',
  isIndeterminate = false,
  showValueLabel = false,
  label,
  className,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  ...props
}: ProgressBarProps) {
  return (
    <Progress.Root
      {...props}
      value={isIndeterminate ? null : value}
      max={max}
      aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}
      className={cn(styles.root, styles[size], styles[variant], isRounded && styles.rounded, className)}
    >
      {label && <Progress.Label className={styles.label}>{label}</Progress.Label>}
      <div className={styles.row}>
        <Progress.Track className={styles.track}>
          <Progress.Indicator className={styles.indicator} />
        </Progress.Track>
        {showValueLabel && !isIndeterminate && <Progress.Value className={styles.value} />}
      </div>
    </Progress.Root>
  )
}

# Progress Bar Shows how far a task with a known size has got: an upload, an install, the ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { ProgressBar } from './ProgressBar'
import * as ProgressBarStories from './ProgressBar.stories'

<Meta of={ProgressBarStories} />

# Progress Bar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Shows how far a task with a known size has got: an upload, an install,
the steps of a setup.

<Status of={ProgressBarStories} />

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.ValueLabel} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the fill, by meaning. The track is the same in
all four.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `primary` | The default: a task the user started and is waiting on. |
| `accent` | A strong fill in neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. |
| `secondary` | Low emphasis: progress in the background, or one of many bars in a list. |
| `destructive` | A task that is failing, or a quota about to run out. |

`size` is the track's thickness, and `isRounded` gives it pill ends.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Sizes} />

When a task has started but its size is not known yet, go indeterminate,
and switch to a value as soon as there is one.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Indeterminate} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ProgressBar } from 'zweihander/progress-bar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/progress-bar.json
```

- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Progress](https://base-ui.com/react/components/progress)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ProgressBarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ProgressBarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

## Measurements

The bar fills the width of its container. Each size sets only the track's
height.

<SpecTable caption="sm" rows={[{ part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--progress-sm' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="md" rows={[{ part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--progress-md' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="lg" rows={[{ part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--progress-lg' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label to track', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Track to value label', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Track and indicator, rounded', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
    { part: 'Label and value label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label and value label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Transition between values', token: '--duration-slow' },
  ]}
/>

The value label is at least 4 characters wide, so the bar does not jump as
the number grows from 9% to 100%.

## Color

The fill is what carries the value, so it must clear 3:1 against the
track. Not every accent's solid does (amber's is about 2.9:1 on white), so
each variant fills with a colour meant to be read as text on the page,
which keeps it at 3:1 or better on the track. Switch the theme and the
accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable caption="primary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--primary-text' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="accent" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--foreground' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="secondary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--muted-foreground' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="destructive" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--danger-text' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--secondary' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Value label', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

## States

A progress bar is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed
state.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Progress' },
    { label: 'Indeterminate', content: <ProgressBar isIndeterminate label="Connecting" /> },
    { label: 'Complete', content: <ProgressBar value={100} label="Uploaded" showValueLabel /> },
  ]}
>
  <ProgressBar value={70} label="Uploading" showValueLabel />
</States>

- **Progress** fills from the start edge, easing between values over
  `--duration-slow`.
- **Indeterminate** slides a third of the track across, once every 1.4s.
  The value label is hidden: there is no value to show.
- **Complete** is a full bar. It does not change on its own; replace or
  remove it when the task ends.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ProgressBarStories} />
</div>

Every other prop goes to Base UI's `Progress.Root`: `id`,
`aria-labelledby`, `min`, `format`, `locale`, `getAriaValueText`.

### Differences from the spec

- **`max`, not `maxValue`**, the name Base UI and the native `<progress>`
  use.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Progress Bar for a task that takes long enough to wait on and whose
size is known, or will be: an upload, an import, the steps of a setup.
Name the task in the `label`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ProgressBarStories.DoNameTheTask} />}
  doCaption="The label names the task, so the reader knows what they are waiting for."
  dont={<Story of={ProgressBarStories.DontBareBar} />}
  dontCaption="A bare bar leaves sighted readers guessing what it measures, even with an aria-label."
/>

`value` is out of `max`, and the value label shows the percentage:

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Max} />

Without a visible label, `aria-label` names the bar for screen readers.
Use it only where the context already says what the bar measures.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.WithoutVisibleLabel} />

## When not to use

- **For a short wait with no known size.** Use a
  [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs).
- **For content whose shape you know.** A
  [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the
  layout.
- **For steps the user moves through themselves.** Use a
  [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs): it names the
  steps, and the user can go back.

## Accessibility

- `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and
  `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext` from Base UI. Indeterminate drops
  `aria-valuenow` rather than reporting 0.
- Every bar needs a name: a visible `label` (linked by Base UI) or
  `aria-label`.
- The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every variant and accent, in both
  modes. The value label is `--muted-foreground`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the fill stops easing between values and
  the indeterminate slide slows from 1.4s to 4s a pass.
- A progressbar is not a live region. If completion matters, announce it
  (a Toast, or a status message) when the task ends.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { Fieldset } from '@base-ui/react/fieldset'
import { Radio } from '@base-ui/react/radio'
import { RadioGroup as BaseRadioGroup } from '@base-ui/react/radio-group'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { choiceStyles, type ValidationState } from './ChoiceField'
import styles from './Radio.module.css'

export interface RadioOption {
  value: string
  label: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  disabled?: boolean
}

export interface RadioGroupProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLDivElement>
  options: RadioOption[]
  /** The group's legend. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Under the whole group; the error message when `validationState` is error. */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  /** The spec's `onChange`. Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  name?: string
  /** Colour of the selected radio. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'neutral'
  orientation?: 'vertical' | 'horizontal'
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  validationState?: ValidationState
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/**
 * A set of radios, one of which is selected. A radio is meaningless alone —
 * arrow keys move within its group — so the component is the group, with
 * the radios as flat `options`.
 */
export function RadioGroup({
  ref,
  options,
  label,
  helperText,
  name,
  variant = 'neutral',
  orientation = 'vertical',
  disabled,
  required,
  validationState = 'default',
  className,
  onValueChange,
  ...props
}: RadioGroupProps) {
  // Plain help describes the group once. An error message goes through Field,
  // which puts it on every radio: whichever one has focus, the reader hears
  // what is wrong.
  const helperId = useId()
  const isError = validationState === 'error'
  return (
    <Field.Root
      name={name}
      disabled={disabled}
      invalid={isError}
      className={cn(choiceStyles.field, choiceStyles[validationState], styles.field, className)}
    >
      <Fieldset.Root
        render={
          <BaseRadioGroup
            {...props}
            ref={ref}
            aria-describedby={helperText && !isError ? helperId : undefined}
            required={required}
            onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next as string))}
          />
        }
        className={cn(styles.group, styles[orientation])}
      >
        {label && (
          <Fieldset.Legend className={styles.legend}>
            {label}
            {required && (
              <span aria-hidden="true" className={choiceStyles.required}>
                *
              </span>
            )}
          </Fieldset.Legend>
        )}
        {options.map((option) => (
          <Field.Item key={option.value} disabled={option.disabled} className={styles.item}>
            <Field.Label className={choiceStyles.label}>
              <Radio.Root
                value={option.value}
                className={cn(choiceStyles.control, styles.radio, styles[variant])}
              >
                <Radio.Indicator className={styles.dot} />
              </Radio.Root>
              {option.label}
            </Field.Label>
            {option.helperText && (
              <Field.Description className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.optionHelper)}>
                {option.helperText}
              </Field.Description>
            )}
          </Field.Item>
        ))}
      </Fieldset.Root>
      {helperText &&
        (isError ? (
          <Field.Description className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.groupHelper)}>
            {helperText}
          </Field.Description>
        ) : (
          <p id={helperId} className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.groupHelper)}>
            {helperText}
          </p>
        ))}
    </Field.Root>
  )
}

# Radio Chooses exactly one option from a short list, all visible at once. The component i...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { RadioGroup } from './Radio'
import * as RadioStories from './Radio.stories'

<Meta of={RadioStories} />

# Radio

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Chooses exactly one option from a short list, all visible at once. The
component is `RadioGroup`.

<Status of={RadioStories} />

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the selected radio; `orientation` lays the
options out in a column or a row.

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `neutral` | The default: forms and settings. The selected radio is the foreground colour. |
| `primary` | A choice that carries the brand: a plan picker beside a primary button. |

| Orientation | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `vertical` | The default. Options with helper text, or labels longer than a word or two. |
| `horizontal` | Two to four short labels: sizes, yes or no. The row wraps when narrow. |

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Horizontal} />

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Validation} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { RadioGroup } from 'zweihander/radio'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/radio.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/Radio.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Radio.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/radio](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/radio)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Radio Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/radio), [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) and [Fieldset](https://base-ui.com/react/components/fieldset)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={RadioStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={RadioStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Each option's label wraps its radio, so the whole label is part of the
click target.

## Measurements

One size. The circle is control tier xs (Foundations / Sizing) and sits
centred on the first line of its label.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every radio group"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Radio', property: 'Size', token: '--choice-box' },
    { part: 'Radio', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
    { part: 'Dot', property: 'Size', token: '--radio-dot-size' },
    { part: 'Option label', property: 'Gap from the radio', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Option label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Option label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Options', property: 'Gap, vertical', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Options', property: 'Gap, horizontal', token: '--space-6' },
    { part: 'Option helper', property: 'Gap from the label', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The legend is the body size at medium weight.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Unselected, every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Radio', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Radio', property: 'Border', token: '--control-border' },
    { part: 'Radio, hover', property: 'Border', token: '--foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="neutral, selected"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Radio', property: 'Background', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Dot', property: 'Colour', token: '--background' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="primary, selected"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Radio', property: 'Background', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Dot', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Legend and option label', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Option and group helper', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Radio, error', property: 'Border', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Group helper, error', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Group helper, success', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Required asterisk', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

An option's own helper describes the option, so it stays muted when the
group is in error or success; only the group message takes that colour.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={RadioStories.Disabled} /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <RadioGroup label="Plan" options={[{ value: 'free', label: 'Free' }, { value: 'pro', label: 'Pro' }]} validationState="error" helperText="Choose a plan." /> },
  ]}
>
  <RadioGroup label="Plan" options={[{ value: 'free', label: 'Free' }, { value: 'pro', label: 'Pro' }]} defaultValue="pro" />
</States>

- **Hover** anywhere on an option's label darkens an unselected ring to
  `--foreground`. The selected radio mixes 12% of the dot's colour into
  its fill, as Button does. An error ring stays red.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the circle.
- **Disabled** dims the radio and its label to 50%, for the whole group
  or one option.
- **Read-only** looks enabled but has no hover and an arrow cursor.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={RadioStories} />
</div>

`className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the group.

### Differences from the spec

- **The component is the group.** The spec describes a single radio, but
  a radio means nothing alone: selection, arrow keys and the single tab
  stop all belong to the group. Following the kit's "flat props"
  convention, the radios are `options` rather than child components.
- **`checked` and `autoFocus` per radio are not props.** The group's
  `value` says which is checked.
- Base UI's `onValueChange` and native `disabled`, `required`,
  `readOnly` names, as on Checkbox.
- **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as selected, so only
  `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship, as on Checkbox.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use radios to choose one option from a short list, when seeing every
option at once helps the choice: a plan, a delivery method, a size. Up to
about six options. Select the usual choice by default when there is one.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={RadioStories.DoFewOptions} />}
  doCaption="A few options, all in view, the usual one already selected."
  dont={<Story of={RadioStories.DontTooMany} />}
  dontCaption="Ten radios are a wall to scan. A long list belongs in a Select or a Combobox."
/>

<Canvas of={RadioStories.Controlled} />

## When not to use

- **For more than about six options, or options that do not fit on
  screen.** Use a Select, or a Combobox when the reader knows what to type.
- **For several choices at once.** Use
  [Checkboxes](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs).
- **For a single on or off.** Use a
  [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs) in a form, or a
  [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs) for a setting
  that applies at once.

## Accessibility

- A `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, exposed as a `radiogroup` named by
  the legend.
- **One tab stop for the group.** Tab enters at the selected radio (or
  the first), arrow keys move and select, Tab leaves. Disabled options
  are skipped.
- Each option's helper text is its own description. Plain group help
  describes the group once; an error message reaches every radio, so
  whichever has focus says what is wrong.
- The unselected outline is `--control-border`, 3:1 on the page.
- A hidden native input carries `name` and `required` into form
  submission and validation.
- 44×44px touch target on each radio on coarse pointers.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Rating.module.css'

export interface RatingProps {
  /** 0 is unrated. Read-only ratings take fractions, e.g. 4.5. */
  value?: number
  defaultValue?: number
  onValueChange?: (value: number) => void
  max?: number
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Shows a rating rather than asking for one. */
  readOnly?: boolean
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Visible label; the group's name. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** The name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  /** Submitted with a form. */
  name?: string
  /** How each value is spoken, e.g. `(n) => `${n} stars``. */
  getValueText?: (value: number, max: number) => string
  className?: string
}

const defaultText = (value: number, max: number) => `${value} out of ${max} stars`

export function Rating({
  value,
  defaultValue = 0,
  onValueChange,
  max = 5,
  size = 'md',
  readOnly = false,
  disabled = false,
  label,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  name,
  getValueText = defaultText,
  className,
}: RatingProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [state, setState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const current = Math.min(max, Math.max(0, value ?? state))
  const stars = Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => i + 1)
  const classes = cn(styles.rating, styles[size], className)

  // Read-only: one image with the value as its name; stars can be partly filled.
  if (readOnly) {
    return (
      <span className={classes}>
        {label && <span className={styles.label}>{label}</span>}
        <span role="img" aria-label={getValueText(current, max)} className={styles.stars}>
          {stars.map((n) => {
            const fill = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, current - (n - 1)))
            return (
              <span key={n} className={styles.star} aria-hidden="true">
                <Icon name="star" className={styles.empty} />
                <span className={styles.fill} style={{ inlineSize: `${fill * 100}%` }}>
                  <Icon name="star-filled" />
                </span>
              </span>
            )
          })}
        </span>
      </span>
    )
  }

  // Interactive: native radios, so arrows, Tab and form submission are the
  // browser's own. Each radio is visually hidden behind its star.
  return (
    <fieldset className={classes} disabled={disabled} aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}>
      {label && <legend className={styles.label}>{label}</legend>}
      <span className={styles.stars}>
        {stars.map((n) => (
          <label key={n} className={cn(styles.star, n <= current && styles.on)}>
            <input
              type="radio"
              className={styles.input}
              name={name ?? id}
              value={n}
              checked={n === Math.round(current)}
              aria-label={getValueText(n, max)}
              onChange={() => {
                setState(n)
                onValueChange?.(n)
              }}
            />
            <Icon name={n <= current ? 'star-filled' : 'star'} />
          </label>
        ))}
      </span>
    </fieldset>
  )
}

# Rating Asks for, or shows, a score out of a few stars: a review, a template's rating, a ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Rating } from './Rating'
import * as RatingStories from './Rating.stories'

<Meta of={RatingStories} />

# Rating

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Asks for, or shows, a score out of a few stars: a review, a template's
rating, a difficulty.

<Status of={RatingStories} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Default} />

## Variants

A rating either asks for a score or shows one.

| Mode | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Rating label="Interactive" defaultValue={3} /> | Asking: a review form, rating a template. Whole stars only. |
| <Rating readOnly value={4.5} aria-label="Read-only" /> | Showing: an average beside a product. Fractions draw as a star filled part-way. |

<Canvas of={RatingStories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={RatingStories.Sizes} />

`getValueText` changes what each score is called, for a scale that is not
stars:

<Canvas of={RatingStories.CustomText} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Rating } from 'zweihander/rating'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/rating.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/Rating.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Rating.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/rating](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/rating)
- Behaviour: native radio buttons; no Base UI part covers it
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={RatingStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={RatingStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Each star is a label over an invisible native radio, so arrows, Tab and
form submission are the browser's own. Read-only drops the radios: the
stars are one image.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[{ part: 'Star', property: 'Size', token: '--space-4' }]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[{ part: 'Star', property: 'Size', token: '--space-6' }]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="lg"
  rows={[{ part: 'Star', property: 'Size', token: '--space-8' }]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Gap above the stars', token: '--space-1-5' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

Stars sit 2px apart, below the spacing scale on purpose, as on Tag. The
label is medium weight.

## Color

<SpecTable
  rows={[
    { part: 'Filled star', property: 'Colour', token: '--warning' },
    { part: 'Empty star', property: 'Colour', token: '--control-border' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

The fill is the bright `--warning` amber, not the darker warning text
colour: a rating reads as a rating when it looks like one. It is 2.1:1 on
white, below the 3:1 a meaningful graphic needs, so colour is not what
carries the score. A filled star differs from the outlined empty one by
shape, and the group or image is named "3 out of 5 stars".

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={RatingStories.Disabled} /> },
    { label: 'Unrated', content: <Story of={RatingStories.Unrated} /> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <Rating readOnly value={3.5} aria-label="Rating" /> },
  ]}
>
  <Rating aria-label="Rating" defaultValue={3} />
</States>

- **Hover** previews the score up to the star under the pointer, and only
  while the rating can be changed.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline round the focused star.
- **Disabled** dims the stars to 50%.
- **Read-only** is one image; fractions fill a star part-way, cut rather
  than shrunk.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={RatingStories} />
</div>

`className` passes through to the group.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a rating to ask for, or show, a quick score on a short scale: a
review, a difficulty, how useful something was. Keep the scale short:
five stars is the convention readers already know.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={RatingStories.DoFiveStars} />}
  doCaption="Five stars: few enough to hit and to tell apart at a glance."
  dont={<Story of={RatingStories.DontTenStars} />}
  dontCaption="Ten stars are small targets, and 7 looks much like 8. Use a Slider or a Number Input for a fine scale."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a precise number.** Use a
  [Slider](?path=/docs/components-controls-slider--docs) or a Number Input.
- **For a choice between named options.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group, so the
  options say what they mean.
- **To show progress.** Use a Progress Bar.

## Accessibility

- Interactive: a `<fieldset>` named by its legend (or `aria-label`), with
  one radio per star named "1 out of 5 stars" and so on (change the words
  with `getValueText`). Arrows move the choice; Tab moves into and out of
  the group.
- Read-only: `role="img"` named with the value, "4.5 out of 5 stars".
- Hover previews the score; focus shows the 2px ring round the star.
- A filled star differs from an empty one by shape as well as colour.
- Stars grow a 44px target on coarse pointers.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useEffect, useId, useRef, useState, type CSSProperties, type KeyboardEvent, type PointerEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Resizable.module.css'

export interface ResizableProps {
  /** The first pane: on the inline start side by side, on top when stacked. The handle sets its size. */
  start: ReactNode
  /** The second pane: it takes the space the first leaves. */
  end: ReactNode
  /** `horizontal` puts the panes side by side, `vertical` stacks them. */
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /** The first pane's size in percent of the whole, for controlled use. Pair with `onSizeChange`. */
  size?: number
  /** The first pane's starting size in percent, when uncontrolled. */
  defaultSize?: number
  /** Called with the first pane's new size in percent while the handle moves. */
  onSizeChange?: (size: number) => void
  /** The first pane's smallest size, in percent. */
  minSize?: number
  /** The first pane's largest size, in percent. */
  maxSize?: number
  /** The handle's accessible name. Name it after the first pane: "Resize filters". */
  handleLabel?: string
  className?: string
  style?: CSSProperties
}

// Table's column resize handle moves 16px a key press too, so both feel alike.
const KEY_STEP = 16

/**
 * Two panes and a handle between them that moves the split, by dragging or
 * with the arrow keys, after the APG window splitter. Nest one in a pane for three.
 */
export function Resizable({
  start,
  end,
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  size,
  defaultSize = 50,
  onSizeChange,
  minSize = 10,
  maxSize = 90,
  handleLabel = 'Resize',
  className,
  style,
}: ResizableProps) {
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const startId = useId()
  const [uncontrolledSize, setUncontrolledSize] = useState(defaultSize)
  const stopDrag = useRef<(() => void) | null>(null)
  useEffect(() => () => stopDrag.current?.(), [])
  const clamp = (v: number) => Math.min(maxSize, Math.max(minSize, v))
  const now = clamp(size ?? uncontrolledSize)
  const isHorizontal = orientation === 'horizontal'

  const setSize = (v: number) => {
    const next = clamp(v)
    // Pressing on against a limit is not a change.
    if (next === now) return
    if (size === undefined) setUncontrolledSize(next)
    onSizeChange?.(next)
  }
  const rootLength = () => {
    const r = rootRef.current!.getBoundingClientRect()
    return (isHorizontal ? r.width : r.height) || 1
  }
  // Side by side in RTL the first pane is on the right, so moving left grows it.
  const sign = () => (isHorizontal && getComputedStyle(rootRef.current!).direction === 'rtl' ? -1 : 1)
  const toPercent = (px: number) => (px * 100) / rootLength()

  // Window listeners, not pointer capture: the move keeps tracking past
  // the handle, and synthetic test pointers need no active pointer id.
  const onPointerDown = (e: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (e.button !== 0) return
    e.preventDefault()
    const from = now
    const at = isHorizontal ? e.clientX : e.clientY
    const s = sign()
    const move = (m: globalThis.PointerEvent) => setSize(from + s * toPercent((isHorizontal ? m.clientX : m.clientY) - at))
    const stop = () => {
      window.removeEventListener('pointermove', move)
      window.removeEventListener('pointerup', stop)
      window.removeEventListener('pointercancel', stop)
      stopDrag.current = null
    }
    stopDrag.current = stop
    window.addEventListener('pointermove', move)
    window.addEventListener('pointerup', stop)
    window.addEventListener('pointercancel', stop)
  }

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const keys: Record<string, number> = isHorizontal ? { ArrowRight: 1, ArrowLeft: -1 } : { ArrowDown: 1, ArrowUp: -1 }
    const dir = keys[e.key]
    const next = dir !== undefined ? now + sign() * dir * toPercent(KEY_STEP) : e.key === 'Home' ? minSize : e.key === 'End' ? maxSize : undefined
    if (next === undefined) return
    e.preventDefault()
    setSize(next)
  }

  return (
    <div
      ref={rootRef}
      className={cn(styles.root, !isHorizontal && styles.vertical, className)}
      style={{ ...style, '--resizable-size': `${now}%` } as CSSProperties}
    >
      <div id={startId} className={styles.pane}>
        {start}
      </div>
      <div
        role="separator"
        aria-orientation={isHorizontal ? 'vertical' : 'horizontal'}
        aria-label={handleLabel}
        aria-controls={startId}
        aria-valuenow={Math.round(now)}
        aria-valuemin={minSize}
        aria-valuemax={maxSize}
        tabIndex={0}
        className={styles.handle}
        onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
        onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
      />
      <div className={cn(styles.pane, styles.end)}>{end}</div>
    </div>
  )
}

# Resizable Two panes split by a handle that people drag, or move with the arrow keys, to ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Resizable } from './Resizable'
import * as ResizableStories from './Resizable.stories'

<Meta of={ResizableStories} />

# Resizable

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Two panes split by a handle that people drag, or move with the arrow keys,
to give one pane more room: a list beside its detail, a query above its
results.

<Status of={ResizableStories} />

Resizable is outside the 1.0 component list, so it starts as experimental.

<Canvas of={ResizableStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Orientation | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `horizontal` (default) | Panes side by side: a list and the record picked from it, a file tree and the file. |
| `vertical` | Panes stacked: an editor over its output, a chart over its table. |

<Canvas of={ResizableStories.Vertical} />

`minSize` and `maxSize` keep the first pane between two sizes, in percent
of the whole, so neither pane can be dragged out of sight.

<Canvas of={ResizableStories.Limits} />

For three panes, put a Resizable in a pane of another.

<Canvas of={ResizableStories.DoNameEachHandle} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Resizable } from 'zweihander/resizable'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/resizable.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Resizable.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Resizable.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; after [shadcn/ui Resizable](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/resizable) and the [APG window splitter](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/)
- Base UI: none; Base UI has no splitter
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ResizableStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ResizableStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The limits, `minSize` and `maxSize`, have no element of their own: they
are where the handle stops.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Every orientation"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Hit area across the line', token: '--box-sm' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Line on hover and drag', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Focus outline offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

The line is 1px; its hit area reaches past it on both sides, and grows
to 44px on touch screens without the line getting wider. The panes have no padding of their own: what goes in
them sets it. Sizes are percentages of the whole, so the split holds
when the window changes size.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Handle"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Line', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Line on hover and drag', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Focus outline', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Dragging', pseudo: 'active' },
  ]}
>
  <div style={{ blockSize: 80, inlineSize: 160, border: '1px solid var(--border)' }}>
    <Resizable start={null} end={null} />
  </div>
</States>

- **Hover** and **Dragging** thicken the line to 2px `--primary`, as on
  Table's column resize handle. The cursor turns to a resize arrow.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the line.
- There is no disabled state: a split that should not move is two plain
  boxes.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ResizableStories} />
</div>

Resizable fills its parent: give the parent a height for side-by-side
panes, and both a height for stacked ones.

### Differences from the spec

shadcn's Resizable is a group of any number of panels and handles
(`ResizablePanelGroup`, `ResizablePanel`, `ResizableHandle`). Zweihänder
takes flat props and two panes, `start` and `end`, as its API conventions
ask; nest one for three panes. There is no collapse on Enter and no saved
layout: store `onSizeChange` to keep the split.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Resizable where people need to trade room between two things they
look at together, and the right split depends on the content: a long name
in a list, a wide table in the detail.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ResizableStories.DoNameEachHandle} />}
  doCaption="Each handle is named after the pane it sizes: “Resize folders”, “Resize inbox”."
  dont={<Story of={ResizableStories.DontKeepDefaultName} />}
  dontCaption="Both handles keep the default name, so a screen reader hears “Resize” twice and cannot tell them apart."
/>

Keep `minSize` above zero (the default is 10%), so a pane cannot be
dragged out of sight with its content still in the tab order.

## When not to use

- **For a fixed sidebar beside the page.** Use the App Shell template:
  its Nav Sidebar has a set width and collapses.
- **For a panel that slides over the page.** Use Drawer.
- **For a column of a table.** Use Table's `isResizable`.
- **For layouts that only change with the window.** Use the
  Multi-column layout template: Resizable is for people, not
  breakpoints.

## Accessibility

- The handle is a focusable `role="separator"`, after the APG window
  splitter. Side by side it is `aria-orientation="vertical"`; stacked it
  is `"horizontal"`.
- Its name is `handleLabel` and `aria-controls` points at the first pane.
- `aria-valuenow` is the first pane's size in percent, between
  `aria-valuemin` (`minSize`) and `aria-valuemax` (`maxSize`).
- Side by side, Arrow Right moves the handle 16px right and Arrow Left
  16px left; in right-to-left text the first pane is on the right, so
  Arrow Left grows it. Stacked, Arrow Down and Arrow Up do the same.
  Home moves it to `minSize`, End to `maxSize`. These are the keys and
  the step of Table's column resize handle.
- Dragging the handle moves it by the distance dragged, never past the
  limits.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useEffect, useId, useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState, type ComponentProps, type FormEvent } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Badge } from '../../atomic-elements/Badge'
import { Tag } from '../../atomic-elements/Tag'
import { Button } from '../../buttons/Button'
import { Checkbox } from '../../controls/Checkbox'
import { TextInput } from '../../inputs/TextInput'
import { Menu, type MenuEntry } from '../../navigation/Menu'
import { Tabs } from '../../navigation/Tabs'
import { Modal, ModalClose } from '../../overlays/Modal'
import styles from './SavedViews.module.css'

export interface SavedView {
  id: string
  label: string
  /** Rows the view holds, shown next to its name. */
  count?: number
  /** Shipped with the product: it can be picked and copied, not saved over or deleted. */
  isPredefined?: boolean
  /** Shared with others; Manage views says so. */
  isShared?: boolean
}

export interface NewView {
  label: string
  isShared: boolean
}

export interface SavedViewsProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  views: SavedView[]
  /** The id of the view in force. */
  value: string
  onValueChange: (id: string) => void
  /** `tabs` for a handful of views; `menu` for more than fit on one line. */
  display?: 'tabs' | 'menu'
  /** The filters, sort or columns now differ from the view as saved. */
  isModified?: boolean
  /** Saves the changes into the view in force. Not offered on a predefined view. */
  onSave?: () => void
  /** Drops the changes and goes back to the view as saved. */
  onDiscard?: () => void
  /** Saves the current state as a new view. Shows Save as new view. */
  onSaveAs?: (view: NewView) => void
  /** Offers "Share with everyone" when saving a new view. */
  isShareable?: boolean
  /** Deletes a view that is not predefined. Shows Manage views. */
  onDelete?: (id: string) => void
}

/**
 * The views of a list or table, predefined and saved, with a mark when the
 * view in force has changed, Save, Save as new view and Manage views. The
 * pattern owns no views: it renders the list you keep and reports changes.
 */
export function SavedViews({
  views,
  value,
  onValueChange,
  display = 'tabs',
  isModified = false,
  onSave,
  onDiscard,
  onSaveAs,
  isShareable = false,
  onDelete,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Views',
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: SavedViewsProps) {
  const [dialog, setDialog] = useState<'save-as' | 'manage' | null>(null)
  // Menu radio items keep the menu open; picking a view should close it.
  const [isMenuOpen, setIsMenuOpen] = useState(false)
  const active = views.find((v) => v.id === value)
  const canSave = !!onSave && !!active && !active.isPredefined

  // Save, Discard and Save as new view unmount the button that was pressed
  // (or that the dialog would hand focus back to): send focus to the view in
  // force once the change has landed, instead of dropping it on the page.
  const barRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const refocus = useRef(false)
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!refocus.current || isModified || dialog) return
    refocus.current = false
    barRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"], [aria-haspopup="menu"]')?.focus()
  }, [isModified, dialog, value])
  const thenRefocus = (action: () => void) => () => {
    refocus.current = true
    action()
  }

  const countBadge = (view: SavedView) =>
    view.count !== undefined && <Badge count={view.count} size="sm" variant="secondary" />

  const viewActions: MenuEntry[] = [
    ...(onSaveAs ? [{ label: 'Save as new view…', onSelect: () => setDialog('save-as') }] : []),
    ...(onDelete ? [{ label: 'Manage views…', onSelect: () => setDialog('manage') }] : []),
  ]

  return (
    <div
      ref={(node) => {
        barRef.current = node
        if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(node)
        else if (ref) ref.current = node
      }}
      className={cn(styles.bar, className)} {...props}>
      {display === 'tabs' ? (
        <Tabs
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          className={styles.views}
          value={value}
          onValueChange={onValueChange}
          items={views.map((view) => ({
            value: view.id,
            label: (
              <>
                {view.label} {countBadge(view)}
              </>
            ),
          }))}
        />
      ) : (
        <Menu
          align="start"
          open={isMenuOpen}
          onOpenChange={setIsMenuOpen}
          trigger={
            <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" endIcon={<Icon name="chevron-down" />} className={styles.trigger}>
              <span className={styles.srOnly}>{ariaLabel}: </span>
              <span className={styles.name}>{active?.label ?? ariaLabel}</span>
            </Button>
          }
          items={[
            {
              type: 'radio',
              label: ariaLabel,
              value,
              onValueChange: (id) => {
                onValueChange(id)
                setIsMenuOpen(false)
              },
              options: views.map((view) => ({
                value: view.id,
                label: (
                  <span className={styles.option}>
                    {view.label} {countBadge(view)}
                  </span>
                ),
              })),
            },
          ]}
        />
      )}
      <div className={styles.actions}>
        {/* Always rendered, so the mark is announced when it appears. */}
        <span role="status" className={styles.modified}>
          {isModified && 'Modified'}
        </span>
        {isModified && onDiscard && (
          <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" onClick={thenRefocus(onDiscard)}>
            Discard
          </Button>
        )}
        {isModified && canSave && (
          <Button variant="secondary" appearance="outlined" onClick={thenRefocus(onSave!)}>
            Save
          </Button>
        )}
        {isModified && !canSave && onSaveAs && (
          <Button variant="secondary" appearance="outlined" onClick={() => setDialog('save-as')}>
            Save as new view
          </Button>
        )}
        {viewActions.length > 0 && (
          <Menu
            align="end"
            trigger={
              <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" isIconOnly aria-label="View actions">
                <Icon name="more" />
              </Button>
            }
            items={viewActions}
          />
        )}
      </div>
      {onSaveAs && (
        <SaveAsDialog
          open={dialog === 'save-as'}
          onOpenChange={(open) => setDialog(open ? 'save-as' : null)}
          taken={views.map((v) => v.label)}
          isShareable={isShareable}
          onSave={(view) => {
            refocus.current = true
            onSaveAs(view)
            setDialog(null)
          }}
        />
      )}
      {onDelete && (
        <ManageDialog
          open={dialog === 'manage'}
          onOpenChange={(open) => setDialog(open ? 'manage' : null)}
          views={views}
          label={ariaLabel}
          onDelete={onDelete}
        />
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

interface DialogProps {
  open: boolean
  onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void
}

function SaveAsDialog({
  open,
  onOpenChange,
  taken,
  isShareable,
  onSave,
}: DialogProps & { taken: string[]; isShareable: boolean; onSave: (view: NewView) => void }) {
  const formId = useId()
  const nameRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  const [label, setLabel] = useState('')
  const [isShared, setIsShared] = useState(false)
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)

  // A fresh form each time it opens.
  const [wasOpen, setWasOpen] = useState(open)
  if (open !== wasOpen) {
    setWasOpen(open)
    if (open) {
      setLabel('')
      setIsShared(false)
      setError(null)
    }
  }

  const submit = (event: FormEvent) => {
    event.preventDefault()
    const name = label.trim()
    if (!name) return setError('Enter a name for the view.')
    if (taken.some((t) => t.trim().toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase())) return setError('A view with this name already exists.')
    onSave({ label: name, isShared })
  }

  return (
    <Modal
      size="sm"
      title="Save as new view"
      description="Saves the current filters, sort and columns under a new name."
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}
      initialFocus={nameRef}
      footer={
        <>
          <ModalClose render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Cancel</ModalClose>
          <Button type="submit" form={formId}>
            Save view
          </Button>
        </>
      }
    >
      <form id={formId} noValidate onSubmit={submit} className={styles.form}>
        <TextInput
          ref={nameRef}
          label="View name"
          required
          isFullWidth
          value={label}
          onChange={(e) => {
            setLabel(e.target.value)
            setError(null)
          }}
          validationState={error ? 'error' : 'default'}
          helperText={error ?? undefined}
        />
        {isShareable && <Checkbox label="Share with everyone" checked={isShared} onCheckedChange={setIsShared} />}
      </form>
    </Modal>
  )
}

function ManageDialog({
  open,
  onOpenChange,
  views,
  label,
  onDelete,
}: DialogProps & { views: SavedView[]; label: string; onDelete: (id: string) => void }) {
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLUListElement>(null)
  const closeRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)
  // Deleting unmounts the focused button: hand focus to the next delete
  // button, or the one before, once the view has left `views`; with none
  // left, to Done.
  const pending = useRef<{ index: number; id: string } | null>(null)
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const p = pending.current
    if (!p || views.some((v) => v.id === p.id)) return
    pending.current = null
    const buttons = listRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('button') ?? []
    ;(buttons[Math.min(p.index, buttons.length - 1)] ?? closeRef.current)?.focus()
  }, [views])

  const own = views.filter((v) => !v.isPredefined)
  return (
    <Modal
      size="sm"
      title="Manage views"
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={(next) => {
        // A delete the app declined must not move focus later on.
        pending.current = null
        onOpenChange(next)
      }}
      footer={
        <ModalClose ref={closeRef} render={<Button />}>
          Done
        </ModalClose>
      }
    >
      <ul ref={listRef} aria-label={label} className={styles.manage}>
        {views.map((view) => (
          <li key={view.id}>
            <span className={styles.name}>{view.label}</span>
            {view.isPredefined && <Tag text="Predefined" variant="neutral" size="sm" />}
            {view.isShared && <Tag text="Shared" variant="neutral" size="sm" />}
            {!view.isPredefined && (
              <Button
                variant="destructive"
                appearance="ghost"
                aria-label={`Delete ${view.label}`}
                className={styles.delete}
                onClick={() => {
                  pending.current = { index: own.indexOf(view), id: view.id }
                  onDelete(view.id)
                }}
              >
                Delete
              </Button>
            )}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </Modal>
  )
}

# Saved Views The views of a list or table, the ones that ship with the product and the on...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SavedViewsStories from './SavedViews.stories'

<Meta of={SavedViewsStories} />

# Saved Views

The views of a list or table, the ones that ship with the product and the
ones people save, with a mark when the view in force has changed, Save,
Save as new view and Manage views. After SAP Fiori variant management
(List Report, Worklist) and Polaris Index filters.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/saved-views.json
```

The pattern owns no views: it renders the `views` you keep and calls you
back. What a view holds (filters, sort, columns) is yours to store; compare
it with what is on screen and pass `isModified`. Picking another view puts
that view's saved state in force and drops unsaved changes, as in Fiori:
Modified, beside the views, is the warning.

## Tabs

For a handful of views. Each tab can carry a count. Put it above a
[Filter Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-filter-bar--docs): picking
a view puts its filters in force there.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.Default} />

## Modified

Change a filter and the view says Modified, with Discard and Save. Save
writes the change into the view in force.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.Modified} />

## Save as new view

A predefined view cannot be saved over, so a change offers Save as new view
in place of Save; it is also always in View actions. The dialog asks for a
name, refuses an empty or taken one, and with `isShareable` offers to share
the view.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.SaveAsNewView} />

## Manage views

In View actions when you pass `onDelete`. It lists every view, marks the
predefined and shared ones, and deletes saved ones at once: pair it with an
Undo toast if a view is costly to rebuild. Deleting the view in force is
yours to handle: put another view in force, usually the first. There is no
rename or unshare yet: save a copy under the new name, then delete the old
one.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.ManageViews} />

## Menu

For more views than fit on one line: a button names the view in force and
opens the views as a menu.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.AsMenu} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={SavedViewsStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **One row** while there is room: the views take the free space, the
  actions sit at the end.
- **The actions drop under the views** when the row is too narrow, rather
  than squeeze the tabs.
- **More tabs than fit scroll sideways** inside the bar; nothing widens the
  page. Past five or six views, use `display="menu"`.
- In menu display a long view name truncates with an ellipsis.

<Canvas of={SavedViewsStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- In tabs display the views are a tab list named "Views" (Manage views'
  list takes the same name); pass
  `aria-label` to say what they list, e.g. "Invoice views". Each tab's name
  includes its count.
- In menu display the button's name says the list and the view in force,
  e.g. "Invoice views: All"; the views are radio items in the menu.
- Modified sits in a `status` region, so a screen reader announces it when
  a change makes the view differ from what is saved.
- Save as new view moves focus to the name field. A missing or taken name
  marks the field invalid and names the problem in its description.
- Manage views: each delete button is named after its view, e.g. "Delete
  To chase". Deleting one moves focus to the next delete button, or the one
  before, or to Done when none is left.
- Save, Discard and Save as new view take away the button that was
  pressed; focus moves to the view in force.
