'use client'

import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type ChangeEvent, type ComponentProps, type KeyboardEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { Kbd } from '../atomic-elements/Kbd'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  assignRef,
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
} from './InputField'
import styles from './Search.module.css'

export interface SearchProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'input'>, 'size' | 'type' | 'value' | 'defaultValue'> {
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  /** A visible label. Without one the field is named by `aria-label` ("Search" by default). */
  label?: ReactNode
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /**
   * One key, e.g. `/`, that focuses the field from anywhere on the page.
   * No modifiers: ⌘K belongs to the Command Palette. One per page.
   */
  shortcut?: string
}

// Focus is in a form field: the key belongs to it, not to us.
const isInField = (el: EventTarget | null) =>
  el instanceof HTMLElement && (el.isContentEditable || el.matches('input, textarea, select'))

export function Search({
  value,
  defaultValue = '',
  label,
  placeholder = 'Search',
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  shortcut,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  onChange,
  onKeyDown,
  className,
  ref,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  ...props
}: SearchProps) {
  const input = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null)
  // Only to know whether to show the clear button; the input stays the
  // source of truth for an uncontrolled field.
  const [uncontrolled, setUncontrolled] = useState(defaultValue)
  const current = value ?? uncontrolled
  const canClear = current !== '' && !disabled && !readOnly

  // Disabled or read-only, the field has nothing to type into.
  const key = disabled || readOnly ? undefined : shortcut

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!key) return
    const onKey = (e: globalThis.KeyboardEvent) => {
      // Case-blind, as Command Palette's hotkey, so Caps Lock does not matter.
      if (e.key.toLowerCase() !== key.toLowerCase() || e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.altKey || e.repeat || e.isComposing) return
      if (e.defaultPrevented || isInField(e.target)) return
      // Or the key would be typed into the field, and Firefox's quick find takes `/`.
      e.preventDefault()
      input.current?.focus()
    }
    document.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)
    return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey)
  }, [key])

  const clear = () => {
    const el = input.current
    if (!el) return
    // Set the value the way typing would, so onChange receives a real event
    // whether the field is controlled or not.
    Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value')!.set!.call(el, '')
    el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }))
    // The button unmounts once the field is empty; hand keyboard focus back
    // to the input rather than losing it. A pointer press never focuses the
    // button (see onMouseDown), so an idle field stays idle.
    if (document.activeElement?.tagName === 'BUTTON') el.focus()
  }

  return (
    <InputField label={label} disabled={disabled} isFullWidth={isFullWidth} className={className}>
      <span className={boxClass(size)} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
        <span className={inputStyles.affix}>
          <Icon name="search" />
        </span>
        <Field.Control
          {...props}
          ref={(node: HTMLInputElement | null) => {
            input.current = node
            assignRef(ref, node)
          }}
          type="search"
          value={value}
          defaultValue={value === undefined ? defaultValue : undefined}
          placeholder={placeholder}
          disabled={disabled}
          readOnly={readOnly}
          aria-label={label ? ariaLabel : (ariaLabel ?? 'Search')}
          aria-keyshortcuts={key}
          onChange={(event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
            setUncontrolled(event.target.value)
            onChange?.(event)
          }}
          onKeyDown={(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
            onKeyDown?.(event)
            // Firefox does not clear a search field on Escape; Chrome and
            // Safari do. Doing it here makes them all agree.
            if (event.key === 'Escape' && canClear && !event.defaultPrevented) {
              event.preventDefault()
              clear()
            }
          }}
          className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.input)}
        />
        {/* Where the clear button goes: the two never show at once. */}
        {key && current === '' && (
          <Kbd size={size} aria-hidden="true" className={styles.shortcut}>
            {key}
          </Kbd>
        )}
        {canClear && (
          <button
            type="button"
            aria-label="Clear search"
            className={inputStyles.iconButton}
            // Keep focus where it is: a focused field stays focused, an idle one stays idle.
            onMouseDown={(event) => event.preventDefault()}
            onClick={clear}
          >
            <Icon name="clear" />
          </button>
        )}
      </span>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Search A field for a search query, with a button to clear it and, optionally, a key that...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Search } from './Search'
import * as SearchStories from './Search.stories'

<Meta of={SearchStories} />

# Search

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A field for a search query, with a button to clear it and, optionally, a
key that focuses it. The field is
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s. It searches
one place: a list, a table, a results page. Finding anything from anywhere
is the [Command Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-commandpalette--docs).

<Status of={SearchStories} />

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Clear} />

## Variants

One appearance, the white outlined box, in two sizes, with or without a
visible label.

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Above a list or a page of results: the default. |
| `sm` | Toolbars and table headers, beside `sm` buttons. |

<Canvas of={SearchStories.WithLabel} />

| Label | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| None (default) | A search box whose place makes its purpose plain: a page header, above a list. It is named "Search", or by `aria-label`. |
| `label` | A search inside a form, among other labelled fields. |

<Canvas of={SearchStories.Shortcut} />

| Shortcut | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| None (default) | Most fields. |
| `shortcut="/"` | The one search a page is about, such as a list page's [Filter Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-filterbar--docs). The key cap shows while the field is empty and idle. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Search } from 'zweihander/search'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/search.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/Search.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Search.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/search](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/search)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SearchStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SearchStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The placeholder is the input's, "Search" unless given. The browser's own
clear control is hidden, so there are not two. Not numbered above: with `shortcut`, a
[Kbd](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-kbd--docs) key cap of the
field's size sits where the clear button goes, while the field is empty and
not focused; the two never show at once.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier, as on Text Input. The search icon and the
clear button both take the tier's icon size.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Search icon and clear button', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-sm' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-md-gap' },
    { part: 'Search icon and clear button', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Clear button', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Clear button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

20rem wide, capped at its container, or the container's width with
`isFullWidth`.

## Color

Search has no validation state; its field colours are Text Input's
default ones.

<SpecTable
  caption="default"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--field-border' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-2xs' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Placeholder and search icon', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Clear button', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Clear button, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Read-only" rows={[{ part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--surface-filled' }]} />

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Empty' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'With a query', content: <Search defaultValue="tooltip" /> },
    { label: 'Clear hover', pseudo: 'hover', content: <Search defaultValue="tooltip" /> },
    { label: 'With a shortcut', content: <Search shortcut="/" /> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <Search defaultValue="tooltip" readOnly /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Search defaultValue="tooltip" disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <Search />
</States>

- **The clear button** appears once there is a query, and not while the
  field is disabled or read-only. On hover its icon darkens to
  `--foreground`.
- **Focus** is the field's 2px `--ring` outline around the box, on click
  as well as keyboard. The clear button, when tabbed to, draws its own
  ring instead, so the two never double.
- **The shortcut's key cap** shows while the field is empty and hides on
  focus, when the key would type instead. Disabled or read-only, there is
  no key cap and the key is not bound.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--surface-filled`.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SearchStories} />
</div>

Every other `<input>` attribute passes through, including `ref`, `name`,
`autoFocus` and `onKeyDown`. `type` is always `search`.

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`label` and `size` are added**, from the shared field,
  so a search box can match the form or toolbar it sits in.
- **`value` is added** for a controlled query.
- **`shortcut` is added**, a single key that focuses the field.
- **No suggestion panel.** Recent searches and results grouped by type, as the
  spec's global search shows them, are the
  [Command Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-commandpalette--docs)'s
  job; picking one value from matches is the
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs)'s. Search stays a
  field, so there are not three lists that behave alike.
- Native `disabled`, `readOnly` names.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Search to find or filter: a list of components, a table, the whole
site. Say in the placeholder what is searched.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SearchStories.DoSaySearchWhat} />}
  doCaption="A Search field: a searchbox to assistive tech, with a clear button and Escape to clear."
  dont={<Story of={SearchStories.DontTextInputWithIcon} />}
  dontCaption="A Text Input with a search icon looks the same but is a plain textbox, with no way to clear it."
/>

When it searches the site, put it inside a `<form role="search">` (or
`<search>`) so it becomes a landmark people can jump to. The component is
only the field: filtering a list in place does not need a landmark.

Above a list page, Search goes in the
[Filter Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-filterbar--docs)'s `search`
slot, which is already the `role="search"` landmark. Give the page's main
search `shortcut="/"`, and only that one.

## When not to use

- **To find anything from anywhere in the app**, with recent items and
  results grouped by type. Use the
  [Command Palette](?path=/docs/components-navigation-commandpalette--docs),
  opened with ⌘K or from a search button. Do not bind ⌘K to a Search.

- **To choose one value from a list.** Use a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs): it shows the
  matches and keeps the choice.
- **For other free text.** Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs).

## Accessibility

- `type="search"`, exposed as a `searchbox`, named by the visible label
  or "Search". A placeholder is not a name.
- **Clearing works the same everywhere:** the button, and Escape in the
  field (Chrome and Safari do this natively; Firefox did not). Either way
  `onChange` fires with a real event.
- The clear button is a real `<button>` named "Clear search", reached
  with Tab after the input. Pressed from the keyboard, it hands focus
  back to the field instead of losing it; a mouse press leaves focus
  where it was.
- The clear button's hit area grows to 44px on touch screens.
- The search icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers.
- **`shortcut`** focuses the field from anywhere on the page, without typing
  the key. It does nothing while focus is in a form field, or with ⌘,
  Ctrl or Alt held, or while the field is disabled or read-only. The input carries `aria-keyshortcuts`; the key cap is
  hidden from screen readers so the key is not read twice.
- The edge is the light `--field-border`, the approved exception to WCAG
  1.4.11 described on Text Input.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Select as BaseSelect } from '@base-ui/react/select'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  popupInset,
  inputStyles as s,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'

export type SelectOption = string | { value: string; label: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }

/** Strings are their own label; objects carry one. */
export function normalizeOptions(options: SelectOption[]) {
  return options.map((o) => (typeof o === 'string' ? { value: o, label: o as ReactNode } : o))
}

export interface SelectProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>
  options: SelectOption[]
  value?: string | null
  defaultValue?: string | null
  /** The spec's `onChange`. `null` when nothing is selected. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string | null) => void
  placeholder?: string
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Options are still arriving: a spinner replaces the chevron. */
  isLoading?: boolean
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  autoFocus?: boolean
  id?: string
  /** Where the popup renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen or a scope with its own density. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

export function Select({
  ref,
  options,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  placeholder,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  isLoading,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  autoFocus,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: SelectProps) {
  const items = normalizeOptions(options)
  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      hasButtonControl
      className={className}
    >
      <BaseSelect.Root
        items={items}
        value={value}
        defaultValue={defaultValue}
        onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next as string | null))}
        readOnly={readOnly}
        required={required}
      >
        <BaseSelect.Trigger
          ref={ref}
          id={id}
          autoFocus={autoFocus}
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          aria-busy={isLoading || undefined}
          className={cn(boxClass(size), s.trigger)}
        >
          <BaseSelect.Value className={s.value} placeholder={placeholder} />
          {isLoading ? (
            <span className={cn(s.icon, s.spinner)} aria-hidden="true" />
          ) : (
            <BaseSelect.Icon className={s.icon}>
              <Icon name="chevron-down" />
            </BaseSelect.Icon>
          )}
        </BaseSelect.Trigger>
        <BaseSelect.Portal container={container}>
          {/* Opens below the field like a list, rather than laid over it
              with the selected option aligned to the trigger. */}
          <BaseSelect.Positioner className={s.positioner} sideOffset={4} alignItemWithTrigger={false}>
            <BaseSelect.Popup className={s.popup} style={popupInset(size)}>
              <BaseSelect.List>
                {items.map((item) => (
                  <BaseSelect.Item key={item.value} value={item.value} disabled={item.disabled} className={s.option}>
                    <BaseSelect.ItemText>{item.label}</BaseSelect.ItemText>
                    <BaseSelect.ItemIndicator className={s.check}>
                      <Icon name="check" />
                    </BaseSelect.ItemIndicator>
                  </BaseSelect.Item>
                ))}
              </BaseSelect.List>
            </BaseSelect.Popup>
          </BaseSelect.Positioner>
        </BaseSelect.Portal>
      </BaseSelect.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Select Chooses one option from a list that opens below the field. The field is [Text Inp...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Select } from './Select'
import * as SelectStories from './Select.stories'

<Meta of={SelectStories} />

# Select

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Chooses one option from a list that opens below the field. The field is
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s.

<Status of={SelectStories} />

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Default} />

## Variants

One appearance, the white outlined box. What changes is the size and the
validation state.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and dialogs: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: toolbars, table filters. The list keeps 32px options. |

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Validation} />

| Validation state | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Before anything is checked. |
| `error` | Nothing chosen where a choice is required, or a choice that cannot be accepted. `helperText` says which. |
| `success` | Rare: a choice checked and accepted elsewhere. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Select } from 'zweihander/select'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/select.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/Select.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Select.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/select](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/select)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Select](https://base-ui.com/react/components/select)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SelectStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SelectStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The **options list** opens below the field, 4px away, at least as wide as
the field. It renders in a portal at the end of `<body>`, so it is not
marked above. Each **option** is inset by the field's own padding, so its
text starts where the field's text does; the chosen one has a check
before its label, in the brand colour. Open the list in the example at
the top of Overview to see it.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier, as on Text Input.

The list is at most 20rem tall, about ten options, and scrolls beyond
that. The check sits in a column of its own that is kept whether or not
the option is chosen, so labels never shift.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Chosen', content: <Select label="Priority" options={['Low', 'High']} defaultValue="High" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Select label="Priority" options={['Low', 'High']} placeholder="Choose" validationState="error" helperText="Choose one." required /> },
    { label: 'Loading', content: <Select label="Priority" options={[]} placeholder="Choose" isLoading /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Select label="Priority" options={['Low', 'High']} defaultValue="Low" disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <Select label="Priority" options={['Low', 'High']} placeholder="Choose" />
</States>

- **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the cursor turns to the button cursor.
- **Focus** is the field's 2px `--ring` outline, shown from the keyboard,
  and kept while the list is open: focus moves into the list, but the
  field is still the one being chosen for.
- **Highlighted option** is where the arrow keys or the pointer are:
  `--accent` behind it. Disabled options are dimmed to 60% and skipped.
- **Loading** swaps the chevron for a spinner in the same place.
- **Read-only** fills the field with `--surface-filled`.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SelectStories} />
</div>

`ref` goes to the field's button. `id` and `className` are passed through
too; no other attributes are.

### Differences from the spec

- **Outlined only.** The spec's filled, underlined and unstyled appearances were dropped to match the Claude apps, where every select is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`onValueChange` with the value**, Base UI's name, instead of
  `onChange`.
- **Native names** for `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`.
- **Options are strings or `{ value, label }` objects.** A bare component
  is not an option: an option needs a value to submit and compare, so a
  component goes in `label`.
- **The list opens below the field** instead of Base UI's default of
  laying it over the trigger with the selected option aligned: the
  spec's anatomy shows a list below.
- **The field keeps its focus ring while the list is open.** Focus moves
  into the list, but the field is still the one being filled.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Select to choose one option from five to about fifteen, when the
choices do not need to be compared side by side: a priority, a country
among a short list, a team member.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SelectStories.DoAHandful} />}
  doCaption="A handful of options, chosen once and then out of the way."
  dont={<Story of={SelectStories.DontTwoOptions} />}
  dontCaption="Two options hidden behind a click. A Switch or two radios show both at once."
/>

Give it a placeholder that says what to choose, and order the options in
a way people expect: by size or frequency, or alphabetically for names.

## When not to use

- **Two to four options.** Use radios, which show every choice at once,
  or a Switch for on and off.
- **More than about fifteen, or when people know what they want.** Use a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs), which lets
  them type to filter.
- **Several choices.** A Select picks one. Use checkboxes or a
  multi-select Combobox.
- **To run an action** such as Export or Delete. Use a Menu: a Select
  keeps a value, a Menu does something.

## Accessibility

- The field is a `<button>` with `role="combobox"`,
  `aria-haspopup="listbox"` and `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox`
  of `option`s, with `aria-selected` on the chosen one.
- **Keyboard:** Space, Enter or Up/Down open it; the arrows move, typing
  jumps to a matching option, Enter selects, Escape closes, and focus
  returns to the field.
- The label is associated with the field (`aria-labelledby`). It is a
  `<div>`, because a `<label>` would also click the button and open the
  list.
- `helperText` is the field's description; `validationState="error"`
  sets `aria-invalid`, and `required` sets `aria-required`.
- **Read-only** locks the value, not the list: it still opens so the
  options can be read, but choosing one changes nothing. The field has
  `aria-readonly`. Use `disabled` when the list should not open at all.
- `isLoading` sets `aria-busy` on the field.
- The list renders in a portal at the end of `<body>`: it reads the
  root's tokens, so a `Theme` scope around the field does not restyle it.
- Options are 32px, 44px on touch screens.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, CSSProperties } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Skeleton.module.css'

export interface SkeletonProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  /** A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length. */
  width?: string | number
  height?: string | number
  appearance?: 'circle' | 'square' | 'rounded'
  /** Several lines of text: stacked bars, the last one shorter. A circle's rows are rounded bars. */
  rows?: number
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** A gentle pulse. Off by default: many pulsing shapes are noise. */
  hasAnimation?: boolean
}

const length = (v: string | number | undefined) => (typeof v === 'number' ? `${v}px` : v)

/**
 * A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading. Decorative:
 * put `aria-busy` on the region it stands in for, and announce the load
 * elsewhere if it matters.
 */
export function Skeleton({
  width,
  height,
  appearance = 'square',
  rows,
  isFullWidth = false,
  hasAnimation = false,
  className,
  style,
  ...props
}: SkeletonProps) {
  const inlineSize = isFullWidth ? '100%' : length(width)

  if (rows && rows > 1) {
    // Lines of text are bars: a circle would stack into a column of dots.
    const line = cn(styles.bone, styles[appearance === 'circle' ? 'rounded' : appearance], styles.line, hasAnimation && styles.animated)
    return (
      <div aria-hidden="true" className={cn(styles.rows, className)} style={{ inlineSize, ...style } as CSSProperties} {...props}>
        {Array.from({ length: rows }, (_, i) => (
          <div key={i} className={line} style={{ blockSize: length(height) }} />
        ))}
      </div>
    )
  }
  // A circle takes its height from its width, so `height` is ignored.
  const blockSize = appearance === 'circle' ? undefined : length(height)
  return (
    <div
      aria-hidden="true"
      className={cn(styles.bone, styles[appearance], hasAnimation && styles.animated, className)}
      style={{ inlineSize, blockSize, ...style } as CSSProperties}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

# Skeleton

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading, so the page
keeps its layout and the reader sees what is coming.

<Status of={SkeletonStories} />

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.CardPlaceholder} />

## Variants

`appearance` sets the corners, to match what the shape stands in for. Any
appearance takes any size.

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Appearances} />

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `circle` | An avatar or a round icon. Its height is its width. |
| `square` | The default: an image, a media block, anything with square corners. |
| `rounded` | Text, buttons and cards: anything with the kit's rounded corners. |

`rows` stacks lines of text, the last one shorter so it reads as a
paragraph rather than a block.

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Rows} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Skeleton } from 'zweihander/skeleton'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/skeleton.json
```

- Source: [src/components/loaders/Skeleton.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/Skeleton.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/skeleton](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/skeleton)
- Behaviour: a plain element; there is no behaviour here worth Base UI
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SkeletonStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SkeletonStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

A skeleton is built from shapes like these, placed by the page in the
layout of the content that will replace them.

## Measurements

A skeleton has no sizes: `width` and `height` copy the content it stands
in for. These are the defaults, and the parts it sizes itself.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every appearance"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Shape', property: 'Default height', token: '--space-4' },
    { part: 'Circle', property: 'Default width and height', token: '--space-10' },
    { part: 'Lines', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Rounded', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-md' },
    { part: 'Circle', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
  ]}
/>

The default width is the container's. The last of several `rows` is 60%
of the width.

## Color

Every shape is one colour, the same subtle surface as a hover. It is below
any contrast floor on purpose: a placeholder should read as "something
goes here", not compete with content that has arrived. Switch the theme in
the toolbar: the value follows.

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Shape', property: 'Background', token: '--muted' }]} />

## States

A skeleton is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Static' },
    { label: 'Pulsing', content: <div style={card}><Skeleton appearance="rounded" rows={3} height={12} width={200} hasAnimation /></div> },
  ]}
>
  <div style={card}>
    <Skeleton appearance="rounded" rows={3} height={12} width={200} />
  </div>
</States>

- **Static** is the default.
- **Pulsing**, with `hasAnimation`, fades to 50% and back every 1.6s. It
  stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SkeletonStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through to the outer element.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Skeleton when you know the shape of what is loading: a list, a card,
a profile. Match the shapes to the content that will replace them, with
the same sizes and the same gaps.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SkeletonStories.CardPlaceholder} />}
  doCaption="Shapes of the content that is coming: the layout holds when it arrives."
  dont={<Story of={SkeletonStories.DontOneBlock} />}
  dontCaption="One block for a whole card jumps to a different layout on load, which is worse than a spinner."
/>

Animate the few shapes that matter, or none: `hasAnimation` is off by
default because a screen of pulsing shapes is noise.

<Canvas of={SkeletonStories.Animated} />

## When not to use

- **When you do not know the shape of what is coming.** Use a
  [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs).
- **For a long task with a known size.** Use a
  [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs).
- **For a load that is usually instant.** A skeleton that flashes for
  200ms is noise; show nothing, or a Spinner with a `delay`.

## Accessibility

- **A skeleton is decoration** and is `aria-hidden`, with its `rows`
  hidden as one. It says nothing to a screen reader.
- The region it stands in for has to say it is loading: put
  `aria-busy="true"` on it, as the CardPlaceholder story does, and remove
  it when the content arrives.
- If the wait matters, announce it: a visually hidden status, or a Spinner
  with a label.
- `--muted` is below 3:1 on the page in both modes, on purpose. It is not
  content, and should not compete with content that has arrived.
- The pulse stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Slider as BaseSlider } from '@base-ui/react/slider'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Slider.module.css'

type Value = number | readonly number[]

export interface SliderProps<V extends Value = number> {
  /** A number for one thumb; an array of two for a range. */
  value?: V
  defaultValue?: V
  /** While dragging. */
  onValueChange?: (value: V) => void
  /** Once, when the pointer is released or a key is let go. Use it for anything expensive. */
  onValueCommitted?: (value: V) => void
  min?: number
  max?: number
  step?: number
  /** Page Up / Page Down and Shift+arrow step. */
  largeStep?: number
  /** Visible label; also the accessible name of a single thumb. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Show the current value (or range) after the label. */
  showValue?: boolean
  /** How the value is written, e.g. `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }`. */
  format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions
  /** One name per thumb for a range, e.g. `['Minimum price', 'Maximum price']`. */
  thumbLabels?: string[]
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  disabled?: boolean
  name?: string
  /** The accessible name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function Slider<V extends Value = number>({
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  onValueCommitted,
  min = 0,
  max = 100,
  step = 1,
  largeStep,
  label,
  showValue = false,
  format,
  thumbLabels,
  size = 'md',
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  disabled = false,
  name,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  className,
}: SliderProps<V>) {
  const current = value ?? defaultValue ?? (min as V)
  const thumbs = Array.isArray(current) ? current.length : 1
  return (
    <BaseSlider.Root
      value={value as number | number[] | undefined}
      defaultValue={defaultValue as number | number[] | undefined}
      onValueChange={onValueChange && ((v) => onValueChange(v as V))}
      onValueCommitted={onValueCommitted && ((v) => onValueCommitted(v as V))}
      min={min}
      max={max}
      step={step}
      largeStep={largeStep}
      format={format}
      orientation={orientation}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      thumbAlignment="edge"
      className={cn(styles.slider, styles[size], styles[orientation], className)}
    >
      {(label || showValue) && (
        <div className={styles.header}>
          {label && <BaseSlider.Label className={styles.label}>{label}</BaseSlider.Label>}
          {showValue && (
            <BaseSlider.Value className={styles.value}>
              {(formatted) => formatted.join(' – ')}
            </BaseSlider.Value>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
      <BaseSlider.Control className={styles.control}>
        <BaseSlider.Track className={styles.track}>
          <BaseSlider.Indicator className={styles.indicator} />
          {Array.from({ length: thumbs }, (_, i) => (
            <BaseSlider.Thumb
              key={i}
              index={i}
              className={styles.thumb}
              // A range needs a name per thumb; a single thumb takes the
              // label, or aria-label when there is none.
              getAriaLabel={thumbLabels ? (index) => thumbLabels[index] ?? '' : label ? undefined : () => ariaLabel ?? ''}
            />
          ))}
        </BaseSlider.Track>
      </BaseSlider.Control>
    </BaseSlider.Root>
  )
}

# Slider Picks a number, or a range, by dragging along a track: volume, a price range, a b...

# Slider

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Picks a number, or a range, by dragging along a track: volume, a price
range, a brush size.

<Status of={SliderStories} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Default} />

## Variants

One value or two: a `defaultValue` (or `value`) that is an array of two
makes a range, with a thumb at each end.

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Range} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | The default: a 20px thumb on a 6px track. |
| `sm` | Dense panels and toolbars: a 16px thumb on a 4px track, 12px label. |

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Steps} />

<Canvas of={SliderStories.Vertical} />

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SliderStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SliderStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The control strip is as tall as the thumb, so the whole strip is the
target, not just the track: a press anywhere along it moves the nearest
thumb there.

## Measurements

The thumb has a 2px ring. A vertical slider is 12rem tall.

## Color

<SpecTable
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--secondary' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--primary-text' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Ring', token: '--primary-text' },

  ]}

The fill is a text colour, as on Progress Bar: `--primary-text` clears
3:1 on the `--secondary` track for every accent, where the solid
`--primary` does not.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={SliderStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Slider label="Volume" defaultValue={40} showValue />
</States>

- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the thumb.
- **Dragging** changes the cursor to a closed hand.
- **Disabled** dims the track and thumbs to 50%. The label turns
  `--muted-foreground` and the value stays as it was, so both still read
  at 4.5:1: they are not a native `<label>`, so faded text would fail
  contrast rather than be exempt as part of a disabled control.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>

</div>

`className` passes through to the root.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a slider when an approximate value is fine and seeing it change helps:
volume, brightness, a price range to filter by. Show the value with
`showValue` so the reader knows where they landed.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SliderStories.DoApproximate} />}
  doCaption="An approximate value, with the number shown as it moves."
  dont={<Story of={SliderStories.DontExactNumber} />}
  dontCaption="An exact figure on a long scale: 137 out of 500 is fiddly to hit by dragging. Use a Number Input."
/>

## When not to use

- **For an exact number** (a price, a quantity). Use a Number Input, or
  pair one with the slider.
- **For a few named options.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group, so each
  option says what it means.
- **For a score out of five.** Use a
  [Rating](?path=/docs/components-controls-rating--docs).

## Accessibility

- Each thumb is a `role="slider"` (a real range input) with
  `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and a formatted
  `aria-valuetext`.
- A single thumb is named by `label`, or `aria-label`; a range needs
  `thumbLabels` so each thumb says which end it is.
- Keyboard: arrows move by `step`, Page Up / Page Down and Shift+arrows
  by `largeStep`, Home and End jump to `min` and `max`.
- The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every accent.
- Thumbs keep their size and grow a 44px hit area on coarse pointers.

<Canvas of={SliderStories.WithoutVisibleLabel} />

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { colorVar, type ChartColor } from './chart-utils'
import styles from './Chart.module.css'

export interface SparklineProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  /** Values in order, oldest first. Empty or null shows "No data". */
  data: number[] | null | undefined
  color?: ChartColor
  /** `area` fills under the line. */
  appearance?: 'line' | 'area'
  /**
   * Off by default: next to a figure and its change the trend is decoration.
   * Give it a name when the spark is the only place the trend is shown.
   */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/**
 * A trend with no axes, sized by its container. The viewBox stretches to any
 * width without measuring, and non-scaling-stroke keeps the line 1.25px.
 */
export function Sparkline({ data, color = 'chart-1', appearance = 'area', className, 'aria-label': ariaLabel, ...props }: SparklineProps) {
  const isEmpty = !data?.length
  let line = ''
  if (!isEmpty) {
    // A zero baseline: a spark that starts at its minimum exaggerates small swings.
    const max = Math.max(...data, 0) || 1
    const step = data.length > 1 ? 100 / (data.length - 1) : 0
    line = 'M' + data.map((v, i) => `${(i * step).toFixed(2)},${(29 - (v / max) * 27).toFixed(2)}`).join('L')
    if (data.length === 1) line += 'L100,' + line.split(',')[1]
  }
  return (
    <div {...props} className={cn(styles.spark, className)}>
      <svg viewBox="0 0 100 30" preserveAspectRatio="none" {...(ariaLabel ? { role: 'img', 'aria-label': ariaLabel } : { 'aria-hidden': true })}>
        {isEmpty ? (
          <path className={styles.sparkEmpty} d="M0,20 C25,14 40,24 60,18 S90,12 100,16" />
        ) : (
          <>
            {appearance === 'area' && <path className={styles.sparkArea} d={`${line}L100,30L0,30Z`} fill={colorVar(color)} />}
            <path className={styles.sparkLine} d={line} stroke={colorVar(color)} />
          </>
        )}
      </svg>
      {isEmpty && <span className={styles.badge}>No data</span>}
    </div>
  )
}

'use client'

import { useEffect, useState, type ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Spinner.module.css'

export interface SpinnerProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'span'>, 'children'> {
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Colour of the indicator. `accent` is the foreground, as on Button. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary'
  /** Wait this many milliseconds before showing, so a fast load never flashes a spinner. */
  delay?: number
  /** 0–100. Omit for an indeterminate, spinning indicator. */
  value?: number
  /** Spin even when `value` is given. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  /** Shown under the indicator and used as its accessible name ("Loading" when omitted). */
  label?: string
}

// Circle of radius 10 in a 24-unit viewBox: the stroke scales with the size.
const R = 10
const C = 2 * Math.PI * R

export function Spinner({
  size = 'md',
  variant = 'accent',
  delay = 0,
  value,
  isIndeterminate = false,
  label,
  className,
  ...props
}: SpinnerProps) {
  const [elapsed, setElapsed] = useState(false)
  // Always after mount, even with no delay: the live region below has to be
  // in the page before its text arrives for the text to be announced.
  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => setElapsed(true), Math.max(0, delay))
    return () => clearTimeout(timer)
  }, [delay])

  const determinate = value !== undefined && !isIndeterminate
  const clamped = determinate ? Math.min(100, Math.max(0, value)) : 0
  const name = label || 'Loading'

  const indicator = (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" className={cn(styles.svg, !determinate && styles.spinning)} aria-hidden="true">
      <circle className={styles.track} cx="12" cy="12" r={R} />
      <circle
        className={styles.indicator}
        cx="12"
        cy="12"
        r={R}
        strokeDasharray={C}
        // Indeterminate shows a quarter arc; determinate shows the value.
        strokeDashoffset={determinate ? C * (1 - clamped / 100) : C * 0.75}
      />
    </svg>
  )

  // Determinate: a progressbar that says how far along it is.
  if (determinate) {
    if (delay > 0 && !elapsed) return null
    return (
      <span
        role="progressbar"
        aria-valuenow={clamped}
        aria-valuemin={0}
        aria-valuemax={100}
        aria-label={name}
        className={cn(styles.spinner, styles[size], styles[variant], className)}
        {...props}
      >
        {indicator}
        {label && <span className={styles.label}>{label}</span>}
      </span>
    )
  }

  // Indeterminate: a polite live region that is in the page from the first
  // render, empty through the delay. Screen readers announce text inserted
  // into a live region that already exists, not a region that mounts full.
  return (
    <span
      role="status"
      aria-label={name}
      className={cn(styles.spinner, styles[size], styles[variant], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {elapsed && (
        <>
          {indicator}
          <span className={label ? styles.label : styles.hiddenLabel}>{name}</span>
        </>
      )}
    </span>
  )
}

# Spinner Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will take, o...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Spinner } from './Spinner'
import * as SpinnerStories from './Spinner.stories'

<Meta of={SpinnerStories} />

# Spinner

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will
take, or, given a value, how far along it is.

<Status of={SpinnerStories} />

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.WithLabel} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the indicator. The track and the label are the
same in all three.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Spinner variant="accent" /> `accent` | The default: a quiet placeholder in `--foreground`, inside content that has its own colour. |
| <Spinner variant="primary" /> `primary` | A load the page is about, where the brand colour helps it be found: the first load of a view. |
| <Spinner variant="secondary" /> `secondary` | Low emphasis: a spinner beside other muted text, or in a dense list. |

With a `value` it stops spinning and becomes a progress ring, which reads
better than a bar in a small space such as a thumbnail.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Determinate} />

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Sizes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Spinner } from 'zweihander/spinner'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/spinner.json
```

- Source: [src/components/loaders/Spinner.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/Spinner.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/spinner](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/spinner)
- Behaviour: a plain element; there is no behaviour here worth Base UI
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SpinnerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SpinnerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

While spinning, the indicator is a quarter of the ring turning once every
`--duration-spin`. With no `label`, a visually hidden "Loading" stands in
for it.

## Measurements

The ring is an SVG drawn in a 24-unit box and scaled to the size, so the
stroke (2.5 units) scales with it: 1.7px at `sm`, 3.3px at `lg`.

<SpecTable caption="sm" rows={[{ part: 'Ring', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-4' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="md" rows={[{ part: 'Ring', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-6' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="lg" rows={[{ part: 'Ring', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-8' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Ring to label', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'One turn', token: '--duration-spin' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'One turn, reduced motion', token: '--duration-spin-reduced' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

The indicator is the part that has to be seen, so each variant takes a
colour that clears 3:1 on the page. Switch the theme and the accent in the
toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable caption="primary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Stroke', token: '--primary-text' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="accent" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Stroke', token: '--foreground' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="secondary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Stroke', token: '--muted-foreground' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Stroke', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

## States

A spinner is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Spinning' },
    { label: 'Progress', content: <Spinner value={40} label="Uploading" variant="primary" /> },
    { label: 'Complete', content: <Spinner value={100} label="Uploaded" variant="primary" /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={SpinnerStories.WithLabel} />
</States>

- **Spinning** is the default, and what it shows with `isIndeterminate`
  even when given a `value`.
- **Progress** fills the ring clockwise from twelve o'clock, easing
  between values over `--duration-slow`.
- **Delayed**: with `delay`, nothing shows until it has passed. The live
  region is in the page, empty, from the start.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SpinnerStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the outer element.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Spinner when something is loading and you cannot say what its result
will look like or how long it will take. Use one per region that is
loading, labelled with what is coming.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SpinnerStories.DoOneForTheRegion} />}
  doCaption="One spinner for the region, named for what is coming."
  dont={<Story of={SpinnerStories.DontOnePerItem} />}
  dontCaption="A spinner per card says the same thing three times, and three screen-reader announcements."
/>

Give a load you expect to be fast a `delay` of 300–500ms. The spinner only
appears if the wait turns out to be long enough to notice.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Delay} />

## When not to use

- **When you know the shape of what is coming.** A
  [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the
  layout and says more.
- **For a long task with a known size**: an upload, an install. Use a
  [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs), or a
  `value` here when space is tight.
- **Inside a button.** Use the Button's `isLoading`: it keeps the button's
  width and focus and stops a second click.

## Accessibility

- **Spinning, it is `role="status"`**, a polite live region, named by
  `label` or "Loading". The region renders empty and its text (the label,
  or a visually hidden "Loading") is inserted just after, or once `delay`
  has passed: screen readers announce text added to a live region that is
  already in the page, not a region that mounts full.
- **With a value, it is `role="progressbar"`** with `aria-valuenow`,
  `aria-valuemin="0"` and `aria-valuemax="100"`. Values outside 0–100 are
  clamped.
- The SVG is hidden.
- The indicator clears 3:1 on the page in every variant: `--primary-text`
  (measured at 4.5:1 per accent), `--muted-foreground`, `--foreground`.
  The track is decoration and may be faint.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it slows to one turn in 2.5s rather than
  stopping, since a frozen arc reads as "stuck", and the progress ring
  stops easing between values.
- Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading, and remove the
  spinner when the load ends, so the change is announced.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Card } from '../../data-display/Card'
import { Link } from '../../navigation/Link'
import styles from './Stats.module.css'

export interface StatChange {
  /** As shown, e.g. "12%" or "3.2k". */
  value: string
  direction: 'up' | 'down'
  /** Whether the change is good news. Defaults to up is good; pass it for figures where down is good, like churn. */
  isPositive?: boolean
}

export interface Stat {
  label: string
  value: ReactNode
  /** Context under or beside the value, e.g. "from 71,897". */
  previous?: ReactNode
  change?: StatChange
  /** Shown in a disc before the label. */
  icon?: ReactNode
  /** A link at the foot of the card, to where the figure comes from. */
  href?: string
  linkLabel?: string
  /** A trend under the figures, edge to edge at the foot of the card: usually a `Sparkline`. */
  chart?: ReactNode
}

export interface StatsProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'section'>, 'title'> {
  stats: Stat[]
  /** A heading above the cards, e.g. "Last 30 days". */
  title?: ReactNode
  headingLevel?: 2 | 3
}

/**
 * Key figures in a row of cards: a label, a value, and optionally the
 * change since last period, an icon and a link to the details.
 */
export function Stats({ stats, title, headingLevel = 2, className, ...props }: StatsProps) {
  const Heading = `h${headingLevel}` as const
  return (
    <section className={cn(styles.stats, className)} {...props}>
      {title && <Heading className={styles.title}>{title}</Heading>}
      <dl className={styles.grid}>
        {stats.map((stat) => {
          const positive = stat.change ? (stat.change.isPositive ?? stat.change.direction === 'up') : undefined
          return (
            <Card key={stat.label} appearance="outline" className={cn(styles.card, stat.icon !== undefined && styles.withIcon)}>
              <dt className={styles.label}>
                {/* Inside the dt: a dl's groups may hold only dt and dd. */}
                {stat.icon && (
                  <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
                    {stat.icon}
                  </span>
                )}
                {stat.label}
              </dt>
              <dd className={styles.figures}>
                <span className={styles.value}>{stat.value}</span>
                {stat.previous && <span className={styles.previous}>{stat.previous}</span>}
                {stat.change && (
                  <span className={cn(styles.change, positive ? styles.positive : styles.negative)}>
                    <Icon name={stat.change.direction === 'up' ? 'chevron-up' : 'chevron-down'} />
                    {/* The arrow and the colour say it at a glance; the words say it to everyone. */}
                    <span className={styles.srOnly}>{stat.change.direction === 'up' ? 'Increased by' : 'Decreased by'} </span>
                    {stat.change.value}
                  </span>
                )}
              </dd>
              {stat.href && (
                <dd className={styles.footer}>
                  <Link href={stat.href} size="sm" underline="hover">
                    {stat.linkLabel ?? 'View all'}
                    <span className={styles.srOnly}> {stat.label}</span>
                  </Link>
                </dd>
              )}
              {stat.chart && <dd className={styles.chart}>{stat.chart}</dd>}
            </Card>
          )
        })}
      </dl>
    </section>
  )
}

# Stats Key figures in a row of cards: what is measured, the figure, and optionally how it...
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as StatsStories from './Stats.stories'

<Meta of={StatsStories} />

# Stats

Key figures in a row of cards: what is measured, the figure, and
optionally how it moved since the last period, an icon, and a link to
the details. The top of a dashboard or a report.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stats.json
```

## Simple

<Canvas of={StatsStories.Simple} />

## With trend

`previous` gives the figure to compare against; `change` says by how
much and which way. The colour follows whether the change is good news,
not its direction: pass `isPositive: true` for figures where down is
good, like churn or response time.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithTrend} />

## With icon and link

An icon on a rounded square of the primary colour, and a link at the foot of each
card to where the figure comes from.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithIconAndLink} />

## With sparkline

A trend at the foot of each card, edge to edge: pass a `Sparkline` as the
stat's `chart`. Leave out the spark where the period has no data and the
card would only say "No data" twice.

<Canvas of={StatsStories.WithSparkline} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stats` | `Stat[]` | – | Required. See below. |
| `title` | node | – | A heading above the cards. |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

Each `Stat` has `label`, `value`, and optionally `previous`, `change`
(`{ value, direction: 'up' \| 'down', isPositive? }`), `icon`, `href`,
`linkLabel` (default "View all") and `chart` (a node at the foot of the card,
usually a `Sparkline`).

<Controls of={StatsStories.Simple} />

## Layout

- As many 14rem columns as fit: three or four on a desktop, one on a
  phone. Cards in a row share a height.

  <Canvas of={StatsStories.Narrow} />

- Figures use tabular numbers, so a row of values lines up digit by digit
  and does not jitter when it updates.

## Accessibility

- A definition list: each figure is the definition of its label, so a
  screen reader reads "Total subscribers, 71,897".
- The change is read as words ("Increased by 12%"), not only shown as an
  arrow and a colour. The colours are `--success-text` and `--danger-text`
  on their subtle surfaces, 4.5:1 in both appearances.
- Each "View all" link carries its figure's label for screen readers
  ("View all Avg. open rate"), so a list of links is not three identical
  entries.
- The icon is decorative.
- The sparkline is decorative too (`aria-hidden`): the change already says
  the trend in words.

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Stepper.module.css'

export interface StepperStep {
  label: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  /** Override the status worked out from `current`, e.g. to flag a step with an error. */
  status?: 'complete' | 'current' | 'upcoming' | 'error'
}

export interface StepperProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  steps: StepperStep[]
  /** 0-based index of the step the reader is on. Steps before it are complete. */
  current: number
  /** Ignored with `appearance="bullets"`, which is always one row. */
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /**
   * `circles` shows every step's marker and label. `bullets` shows only
   * the current step's label ("Step 2 of 4: Workspace") over a row of
   * dots, for a narrow space or a longer flow.
   */
  appearance?: 'circles' | 'bullets'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /**
   * Makes finished steps (and the current one) buttons that go back to
   * them. Upcoming steps stay plain: they cannot be skipped to.
   */
  onStepClick?: (index: number) => void
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

const statusText = { complete: 'completed', current: 'current', upcoming: 'not started', error: 'has an error' }

export function Stepper({
  steps,
  current,
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  appearance = 'circles',
  size = 'md',
  onStepClick,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Progress',
  className,
  ...props
}: StepperProps) {
  const bullets = appearance === 'bullets'
  const currentStep = steps[current]
  return (
    <nav
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      className={cn(styles.stepper, bullets ? styles.bullets : styles[orientation], styles[size], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {/* Hidden from screen readers: the list already says each step's position and status. */}
      {bullets && currentStep && (
        <p className={styles.summary} aria-hidden="true">
          <span className={styles.count}>
            Step {current + 1} of {steps.length}:
          </span>{' '}
          <span className={styles.label}>{currentStep.label}</span>
        </p>
      )}
      <ol className={styles.list}>
        {steps.map((step, i) => {
          const status = step.status ?? (i < current ? 'complete' : i === current ? 'current' : 'upcoming')
          const clickable = onStepClick !== undefined && status !== 'upcoming'
          const marker = (
            <span className={styles.marker} aria-hidden="true">
              {bullets ? null : status === 'complete' ? <Icon name="check" /> : status === 'error' ? <Icon name="danger" /> : i + 1}
            </span>
          )
          // Bullets show only the dot: the label and status are said, not shown.
          const text = (
            <span className={cn(styles.text, bullets && styles.srOnly)}>
              <span className={styles.label}>
                {step.label}
                {/* Said, not shown: the marker carries it visually. */}
                <span className={styles.srOnly}>, {statusText[status]}</span>
              </span>
              {step.description && <span className={styles.description}>{step.description}</span>}
            </span>
          )
          return (
            <li
              key={i}
              className={cn(styles.step, styles[status])}
              // An error on the current step does not stop it being where the reader is.
              aria-current={status === 'current' || i === current ? 'step' : undefined}
            >
              {clickable ? (
                <button type="button" className={styles.target} onClick={() => onStepClick(i)}>
                  {marker}
                  {text}
                </button>
              ) : (
                <span className={styles.target}>
                  {marker}
                  {text}
                </span>
              )}
              {!bullets && i < steps.length - 1 && <span className={styles.connector} aria-hidden="true" />}
            </li>
          )
        })}
      </ol>
    </nav>
  )
}

        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--space-6)' }}>
            <Stepper
                steps={[
                  { label: 'Account', description: 'Email and password' },
                  { label: 'Workspace', description: 'Name and URL' },
                  { label: 'Invite', description: 'Add your team' },
                  { label: 'Done' },
                ]}
                current={current}
                onStepClick={setCurrent} />
            <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--space-2)' }}>
                <Button
                    appearance="outlined"
                    variant="accent"
                    disabled={current === 0}
                    onClick={() => setCurrent(current - 1)}>Back
                              </Button>
                <Button
                    disabled={current === steps.length - 1}
                    onClick={() => setCurrent(current + 1)}>Next
                              </Button>
            </div>
        </div>
    );
};

# Stepper Shows where the reader is in a flow of a few ordered steps: sign-up, checkout, a...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as StepperStories from './Stepper.stories'

<Meta of={StepperStories} />

# Stepper

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Shows where the reader is in a flow of a few ordered steps: sign-up,
checkout, a setup wizard.

<Status of={StepperStories} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Horizontal (default) | Three to five steps above a form. The label sits under its marker, so every step gets the same width whatever its label. |
| Vertical | Steps with long descriptions, or a narrow column beside the form. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a dialog, a side panel. |
| Bullets (`appearance="bullets"`) | A phone, a narrow dialog, or more steps than fit with labels: only the current step's label shows, "Step 3 of 4: Invite", over a row of dots. |
| Navigable (`onStepClick`) | Flows where going back to fix an earlier step is normal. Finished steps become buttons. |

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Navigable} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Bullets} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Stepper } from 'zweihander/stepper'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stepper.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/stepper](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/stepper)
- Behaviour: a plain `<nav>` around an ordered list
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={StepperStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={StepperStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The last step has no connector. Vertical, the connector runs down from
each marker, beside the text.

The marker's ring and the connector are 2px. The current dot's ring is

along the markers' centre line from one marker to the next, `--space-2`
clear of each.

  rows={[

    { part: 'Dot and ring, current', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-text' },
    { part: 'Dot, upcoming', property: 'Colour', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Dot, error', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Ring gap, current', property: 'Colour', token: '--background' },
    { part: 'Dot hit area, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--muted' },
    { part: '"Step 3 of 4"', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every status"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Description', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

Complete and current share the primary colour: the filled disc says done,
the ring says here. The current ring uses `--primary-text`, the step of
the accent that reads at 4.5:1 on the page, because it frames a number.

## States

A step's status is its state. With `onStepClick`, finished steps and the
current one are buttons, with hover and focus of their own.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Statuses', content: <Story of={StepperStories.Statuses} /> },
    { label: 'Clickable' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={StepperStories.Clickable} />
</States>

- **Hover** underlines the label of a clickable step.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the step.
- **Upcoming** steps are never buttons, so they have no hover or focus.
- With bullets, **hover** fills the dot's hit area with `--muted`, since
  there is no visible label to underline.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={StepperStories} />
</div>

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

A step's `status` is only for the exception, such as an error: the rest
is worked out from `current`. Only finished steps can be clicked; upcoming
ones stay text, because a flow that can be skipped ahead is a set of Tabs.

Bullets ignore `orientation` and draw no connectors: the dots sit close
enough to read as one line. When `current` is past the last step, the
"Step 3 of 4" line is left out. A step with an error that is also
`current` keeps `aria-current` and the ring.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Stepper when a task is split into a few steps that must be done in
order, and it helps to know how many are left: checkout, onboarding, an
import wizard. Keep it to three to five steps with a word or two each.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={StepperStories.DoFewShortSteps} />}
  doCaption="Four steps, one word each: the whole flow at a glance."
  dont={<Story of={StepperStories.DontTooManySteps} />}
  dontCaption="Ten steps squeeze every label and make the flow look longer than it is. Merge steps, or drop the stepper."
/>

## When not to use

- **For sections the reader can visit in any order.** Use
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs).
- **For progress with no steps to name**, such as an upload. Use a
  [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs).
- **For a single-page form.** Headings do the job; a stepper over one page
  promises steps that are not there.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Progress" around an ordered list: screen
  readers announce the number of steps and the position of each.
- The current step has `aria-current="step"`.
- The marker is decorative, so each label carries its status in visually
  hidden text: "Account, completed", "Invite, not started", "Workspace,
  has an error". Bullets hide every label but the current one, and still
  say each in the same hidden text. Their visible "Step 3 of 4: Invite"
  is hidden from screen readers, which hear the list instead.
- An error on the current step keeps `aria-current="step"`.
- Without `onStepClick` nothing is focusable. With it, complete and
  current steps are real buttons: reached with Tab, pressed with Enter or
  Space, showing the focus ring, and 44px tall on touch screens
  (`pointer: coarse`).

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

  isLive = false,
  className,
  ...props
}: SuccessStateProps) {
  return <EmptyState role={isLive ? 'status' : undefined} icon={icon} className={cn(styles.success, className)} {...props} />

| --- | --- |

## States

</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Success State when the screen the reader was on is finished and
needs replacing: a sent form, a completed import, an emptied inbox. Say
what was done, and lead with the next step.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SuccessStateStories.Default} />}
  doCaption="The flow is over: say what was done and where to go next."
  dont={<Story of={SuccessStateStories.DontForQuickSave} />}
  dontCaption="A quick save is not the end of a flow. This hides the form; a Toast would leave it in place."
/>

## When not to use

- **To confirm a quick action** such as Save, Copy or Move. Use a Toast:
  it confirms and leaves the screen as it was.
- **When there is nothing there yet.** Use an
  [Empty State](?path=/docs/components-states-emptystate--docs).

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading, as on Empty State. Set `headingLevel` to
  fit the outline.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title says what was done.
- `isLive` makes it a `role="status"`, read politely when it replaces a
  form or a progress view. Without it, nothing is announced.

import type { ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Switch as BaseSwitch } from '@base-ui/react/switch'

import { ChoiceField, choiceStyles, type ValidationState } from './ChoiceField'
import styles from './Switch.module.css'

export interface SwitchProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>
  /** Controlled state. */
  checked?: boolean
  /** Uncontrolled starting state (the spec's `defaultValue`). */
  defaultChecked?: boolean
  /** The spec's `onChange`. Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean) => void
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  name?: string
  /** Submitted when on; "on" by default, like a checkbox. */
  value?: string
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Colour of the on state. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'destructive'
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean

  id?: string
  className?: string

}

export function Switch({
  label,
  helperText,
  name,
  size = 'md',
  variant = 'primary',
  disabled,
  required,
  validationState,
  className,
  onCheckedChange,
  ...props
}: SwitchProps) {
  return (
    <ChoiceField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      className={cn(styles[size], className)}
    >
      <BaseSwitch.Root
        {...props}
        required={required}
        onCheckedChange={onCheckedChange && ((next) => onCheckedChange(next))}
        className={cn(choiceStyles.control, styles.track, styles[variant])}
      >

      </BaseSwitch.Root>
    </ChoiceField>
