# Switch Turns a setting on or off, taking effect immediately. ## Variants `variant` is th...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Switch } from './Switch'
import * as SwitchStories from './Switch.stories'

<Meta of={SwitchStories} />

# Switch

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Turns a setting on or off, taking effect immediately.

<Status of={SwitchStories} />

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the on state. Off is the same in every variant.

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Switch defaultChecked label="Primary" /> | The default: most settings. |
| <Switch variant="accent" defaultChecked label="Accent" /> | Neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. |
| <Switch variant="destructive" defaultChecked label="Destructive" /> | A setting that is risky to leave on: public sharing, deleting old data automatically. |

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Validation} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Switch } from 'zweihander/switch'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/switch.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/Switch.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Switch.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/switch](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/switch)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Switch](https://base-ui.com/react/components/switch) and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SwitchStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SwitchStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The label wraps the track, so the whole label is part of the click target.

## Measurements

Track heights are 16, 20 and 24px; `md` and `lg` are control tiers xs and
sm (Foundations / Sizing). Each track is about one and three quarter
heights wide, so the thumb travels most of a thumb-width. The thumb sits
2px inside the track at every size.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm, 28×16px"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--switch-sm-h' },
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Width', token: '--switch-sm-w' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md, 36×20px"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--switch-md-h' },
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Width', token: '--switch-md-w' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="lg, 44×24px"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--switch-lg-h' },
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Width', token: '--switch-lg-w' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track and thumb', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Gap from the track', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Gap from the label', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Slide duration', token: '--duration-base' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

Off is a `--control-border` track (3:1 on the page, so the control is
visible at all) with a page-coloured thumb. On takes the variant's solid,
and the thumb its label colour, measured at 4.5:1 against it.

<SpecTable
  caption="Off, every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--control-border' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="primary, on"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Background', token: '--primary-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="accent, on"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Background', token: '--background' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="destructive, on"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--destructive' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Background', token: '--destructive-foreground' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Track, error', property: 'Inner edge', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Helper text, error', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Helper text, success', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Off' },
    { label: 'On', content: <Switch defaultChecked label="Email notifications" /> },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Switch disabled defaultChecked label="Email notifications" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Switch validationState="error" label="Email notifications" /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={SwitchStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** changes only the cursor: the track has no lighter or darker
  step to move to without losing its 3:1.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the track.
- **Disabled** dims the track and the label to 50%.
- **Error** draws a 2px `--danger-text` edge inside the track, so it reads
  on and off alike and leaves the band outside to the focus ring.
- **Read-only** looks enabled, with an arrow cursor.
- The thumb slides over `--duration-base`, and stops animating under
  `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SwitchStories} />
</div>

`id`, `className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the track.

### Differences from the spec

- **Base UI's names:** `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange` for
  the spec's `defaultValue` and `onChange`; native `disabled`,
  `required`, `readOnly` for `isDisabled`, `isRequired`, `isReadOnly`.
- **`helperText` is added.** `validationState="error"` needs somewhere to
  say what is wrong; colour alone is not a message.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a switch for a setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped,
like a light switch: dark mode, notifications, auto-save.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SwitchStories.DoApplyAtOnce} />}
  doCaption="The setting applies as soon as the switch moves."
  dont={<Story of={SwitchStories.DontWaitForSave} />}
  dontCaption="A switch that waits for Save looks done when it is not. Use a checkbox in a form."
/>

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Controlled} />

## When not to use

- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a
  [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs).
- **For more than two options.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group or a Select.
- **For a toggle in a toolbar** (Bold, a filter). Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs).

## Accessibility

- `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`; Space toggles it.
- The label wraps the control, so it names it and clicking it toggles it.
- `helperText` is the switch's description (`aria-describedby`); in the
  error state the switch has `aria-invalid`.
- The off track is `--control-border`, measured at 3:1 on the page on
  every gray ramp; the thumb is 4.5:1 or more against its track in both
  states.
- A hidden `<input type="checkbox">` carries `name`, `value` and
  `required` into native form submission and validation.
- On is the end side: in a right-to-left page the thumb travels left.
- 44×44px touch target on coarse pointers.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Tabs } from '../../navigation/Tabs'
import styles from './TableChartSwitch.module.css'

export type TableChartView = 'table' | 'chart'

export interface TableChartSwitchProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  /** The records, usually a Table. */
  table: ReactNode
  /** The same records summed up, usually a BarChart or LineChart. */
  chart: ReactNode
  /** The filters both views share, usually a FilterBar. It stays put when the view changes. */
  filters?: ReactNode
  /** At the start of the switch's row: what the views show, e.g. "128 invoices". */
  summary?: ReactNode
  /** The view shown. */
  view?: TableChartView
  defaultView?: TableChartView
  onViewChange?: (view: TableChartView) => void
  tableLabel?: string
  chartLabel?: string
  /** Names the switch. Defaults to "View". */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/**
 * One set of records, two ways to look at it: a table of the rows and a
 * chart of their totals, under the same filters. Owns no data: filter once
 * and hand the result to both views.
 */
export function TableChartSwitch({
  table,
  chart,
  filters,
  summary,
  view,
  defaultView = 'table',
  onViewChange,
  tableLabel = 'Table',
  chartLabel = 'Chart',
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'View',
  className,
  ...props
}: TableChartSwitchProps) {
  return (
    <div {...props} className={cn(styles.root, className)}>
      {filters != null && <div className={styles.filters}>{filters}</div>}
      {/* A status, so a screen reader hears the new count when a filter changes it. */}
      {summary != null && (
        <div className={styles.summary} role="status">
          {summary}
        </div>
      )}
      <Tabs
        appearance="pills"
        size="sm"
        // Both views stay mounted, so the table keeps its sort, selection
        // and scroll while the viewer looks at the chart.
        keepMounted
        aria-label={ariaLabel}
        className={styles.tabs}
        value={view}
        defaultValue={view === undefined ? defaultView : undefined}
        onValueChange={onViewChange && ((v) => onViewChange(v as TableChartView))}
        items={[
          { value: 'table', label: tableLabel, content: table },
          { value: 'chart', label: chartLabel, content: chart },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}

# Table Chart Switch One set of records, two ways to look at it: a table of the rows and a...
import { Meta, Canvas, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TableChartSwitchStories from './TableChartSwitch.stories'

<Meta of={TableChartSwitchStories} />

# Table Chart Switch

One set of records, two ways to look at it: a table of the rows and a chart
of their totals, under the same filters. After the table/chart toggle of
SAP Fiori's List Report.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/table-chart.json
```

The pattern owns no data and draws neither view: it lays out the filters,
the summary and the switch, and shows the view in force. Filter once and
hand the same result to both `table` and `chart`, so the two never disagree.

## Table and chart

The table comes first. Switch to the chart and the filters stay where they
are, with their state; a change shows in whichever view is in force. The
view not in force is hidden, not removed, so the table keeps its sort,
selection and scroll while the viewer looks at the chart.

<Canvas of={TableChartSwitchStories.Default} />

The chart keeps its own View as table. That table lists what the chart
plots (a total per month), not the records, so the two do not overlap.

## Controlled

Pass `view` and `onViewChange` to bring a viewer back to the view they left,
or to keep it in a [Saved View](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-saved-views--docs).

<Canvas of={TableChartSwitchStories.Controlled} />

## Empty

Nothing matches: each view shows its own empty state, the Table's
`emptyState` and the chart's No data.

<Canvas of={TableChartSwitchStories.Empty} />

## Differences from the spec

- Fiori's toggle is a pair of icon buttons in the table toolbar; here it is
  a pair of text tabs, since the views are panels of one region and a word
  says more than a glyph.
- A `summary` slot, Fiori's "Invoices (128)" beside the toggle, gives the
  row a start and the count a voice.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={TableChartSwitchStories} />

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

## Layout

- **Filters on top**, full width.
- **The summary and the switch share a row** below them: the summary at the
  start, the switch at the end, where Fiori puts it in the table's toolbar.
- **The view takes the full width** under that row. A wide table scrolls
  inside its own box.
- **When the row is too narrow** the summary wraps and the switch drops
  under it; nothing widens the page.

<Canvas of={TableChartSwitchStories.Narrow} />

## Accessibility

- The switch is a tab list named "View"; pass `aria-label` to say what it
  shows, e.g. "Invoice view". The view in force is its tab panel, named
  after its tab.
- The summary is a `status`: when a filter changes the count, a screen
  reader announces it.
- Arrow keys move between Table and Chart, Enter or Space switches, and
  focus stays on the tab.
- The filters stay in the page when the view changes, so focus in them is
  never lost.

<Canvas of={TableChartSwitchStories.Keyboard} />

'use client'

import { useLayoutEffect, useRef, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Button } from '../../buttons/Button'
import styles from './DataTablePage.module.css'

const focusable =
  'input:not([disabled]):not([type="hidden"]), button:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), a[href], [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'

export interface TableToolbarProps extends ComponentProps<'div'> {
  /** Search, filters and the primary action. Shown while nothing is selected. */
  children: ReactNode
  /** How many rows are selected. From 1 up, the toolbar shows the selection's actions instead. */
  selectedCount?: number
  /** Actions for the selected rows, e.g. Archive and Delete. */
  selectionActions?: ReactNode
  onClearSelection?: () => void
  /** Defaults to "{n} selected". */
  selectionLabel?: (count: number) => string
}

/**
 * The bar above a table: search, filters and the page's main action; while
 * rows are selected, what you can do with them instead.
 */
export function TableToolbar({
  children,
  selectedCount = 0,
  selectionActions,
  onClearSelection,
  selectionLabel = (n) => `${n} selected`,
  className,
  ref,
  ...props
}: TableToolbarProps) {
  const selecting = selectedCount > 0
  const toolbarRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
  const wasSelecting = useRef(selecting)
  // Archive or Clear selection unmounts the button that had focus, which
  // drops it on the body. Pick it up in the tools that came back instead.
  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const toolbar = toolbarRef.current
    if (wasSelecting.current && !selecting && toolbar) {
      const active = document.activeElement
      if (!active || active === document.body || !active.isConnected) {
        const first = toolbar.querySelector<HTMLElement>(focusable)
        if (first) first.focus()
        else {
          toolbar.tabIndex = -1
          toolbar.focus()
        }
      }
    }
    wasSelecting.current = selecting
  }, [selecting])
  return (
    <div
      ref={(node) => {
        toolbarRef.current = node
        if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(node)
        else if (ref) ref.current = node
      }}
      className={cn(styles.toolbar, selecting && styles.selecting, className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {/* Always in the page, so the count is announced as it changes. */}
      <p role="status" className={selecting ? styles.count : styles.srOnly}>
        {selecting ? selectionLabel(selectedCount) : ''}
      </p>
      {selecting ? (
        <div className={styles.selectionActions}>
          {selectionActions}
          {onClearSelection && (
            <Button variant="secondary" appearance="ghost" size="sm" onClick={onClearSelection}>
              Clear selection
            </Button>
          )}
        </div>
      ) : (
        children
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

/** Put the filters' flexible part here: it takes the free space and wraps first. */
export function TableToolbarGroup({ className, ...props }: ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn(styles.group, className)} {...props} />
}

export interface TableFooterProps extends ComponentProps<'div'> {
  /** E.g. "Showing 1–10 of 57". */
  summary?: ReactNode
  /** Usually Pagination. */
  children?: ReactNode
}

/** The bar under a table: what is shown, and the pages. */
export function TableFooter({ summary, children, className, ...props }: TableFooterProps) {
  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.footer, className)} {...props}>
      {summary && <p className={styles.summary}>{summary}</p>}
      {children}
    </div>
  )
}

# Data Table Page A list screen: search and filters above a [Table](?path=/docs/components...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DataTablePageStories from './DataTablePage.stories'

<Meta of={DataTablePageStories} />

# Data Table Page

A list screen: search and filters above a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs),
what is shown and the pages below it, and, while rows are selected, what
you can do with them. Two pieces, `TableToolbar` (with
`TableToolbarGroup`) and `TableFooter`, around the kit's Table, Search,
Select and Pagination. Filtering, paging and the data are yours: the
stories show one way to wire them.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/data-table-page.json
```

## Toolbar and pagination

The footer holds a Pagination given `totalItems`, so it shows the rows on
screen ("6–10 of 12") and a "Rows per page" select from
`pageSizeOptions`. Any lone child spans the footer, so Pagination's summary
leads and the pages end the bar; the wrapping inside is Pagination's own.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.ToolbarAndPagination} />

## Bulk actions

With `selectedCount` above zero the toolbar swaps its tools for the
selection's actions and a "Clear selection" button, on the accent
surface so the change of mode is visible.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.BulkActions} />

## Empty result

When nothing matches, the Table's `emptyState` says so and offers the way
back; the footer goes away.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.EmptyResult} />

## Props

**TableToolbar**

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | node | – | Search, filters, the primary action. |
| `selectedCount` | number | `0` | From 1, the selection bar replaces the children. |
| `selectionActions` | node | – | |
| `onClearSelection` | function | – | Shows "Clear selection". |
| `selectionLabel` | `(n) => string` | `"{n} selected"` | |

`TableToolbarGroup` wraps the part that should take the free space and
wrap first, usually the search and filters.

**TableFooter** takes, as children, usually a Pagination with `totalItems`
and `pageSizeOptions`. Its own `summary` slot is for a footer without
Pagination's summary, such as "12 projects" on a list that fits one page;
do not pass both, or the count is shown twice.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.FooterSummary} />

## Behaviour to copy

- **Rows per page keeps the reader in place.** Pagination moves to the page
  holding the first row that was on screen and reports it through
  `onPageChange`; keep `page` and `pageSize` in your state.
- **Filtering returns to page 1.** A new query on page 3 would otherwise
  show an empty page, or a page the reader never asked for.
- **Selection is by id**, so it survives sorting and paging (Table's
  `getRowId`), and an action clears it once it has been applied.

## Layout

- No breakpoints: both bars are flex rows that wrap, so they adapt to the
  width of their container, not the viewport.
- `TableToolbarGroup` grows from 16rem and wraps first. On a phone the
  search takes its own line and the filters and the primary action flow
  under it, instead of anything shrinking below use.
- In selection mode the actions are pushed to the end of the bar and drop
  under the count when they no longer fit.
- The footer puts the summary at the start and the pages and rows-per-page
  select at the end; when they do not fit, they wrap under the summary.

## Accessibility

- The selection count is a polite status line that is always in the page,
  so "2 selected" is announced as it changes, and silence when it clears.
- The footer's "6–10 of 12" is Pagination's own status line, inside the
  pages landmark ("Projects pages"), so a new page or page size is
  announced too.
- Search and the status filter are named ("Search projects", "Status")
  without visible labels, since the table's caption and placeholder make
  their purpose clear on screen.
- The empty state is a heading inside the table's body, so a screen reader
  reaching the table hears why it is empty.

'use client'

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Tabs as BaseTabs } from '@base-ui/react/tabs'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Tabs.module.css'

export interface TabItem {
  value: string
  label: ReactNode
  /** The panel shown while this tab is selected. */
  content?: ReactNode
  icon?: ReactNode
  disabled?: boolean
}

export interface TabsProps {
  items: TabItem[]
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  /** `underline`: a line under the selected tab. `pills`: a filled segment, for switching views in a toolbar. */
  appearance?: 'underline' | 'pills'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /** Tabs share the full width equally. */
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Select a tab as soon as it gets focus, rather than on Enter or Space. */
  activateOnFocus?: boolean
  /** Keep hidden panels in the DOM, e.g. to preserve their state. */
  keepMounted?: boolean
  /** Names the tab list when nothing on the page does. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function Tabs({
  items,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  appearance = 'underline',
  size = 'md',
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  isFullWidth = false,
  activateOnFocus = false,
  keepMounted = false,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  className,
}: TabsProps) {
  return (
    <BaseTabs.Root
      value={value}
      defaultValue={defaultValue ?? (value === undefined ? items.find((i) => !i.disabled)?.value : undefined)}
      onValueChange={onValueChange && ((v) => onValueChange(v as string))}
      orientation={orientation}
      className={cn(styles.tabs, styles[appearance], styles[size], styles[orientation], isFullWidth && styles.fullWidth, className)}
    >
      <BaseTabs.List className={styles.list} activateOnFocus={activateOnFocus} aria-label={ariaLabel}>
        {items.map((item) => (
          <BaseTabs.Tab key={item.value} value={item.value} disabled={item.disabled} className={styles.tab}>
            {item.icon && (
              <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
                {item.icon}
              </span>
            )}
            {item.label}
          </BaseTabs.Tab>
        ))}
        <BaseTabs.Indicator className={styles.indicator} />
      </BaseTabs.List>
      {items.map(
        (item) =>
          item.content !== undefined && (
            <BaseTabs.Panel key={item.value} value={item.value} keepMounted={keepMounted} className={styles.panel}>
              {item.content}
            </BaseTabs.Panel>
          ),
      )}
    </BaseTabs.Root>
  )
}

# Tabs Switches between views of the same thing without leaving the page: Overview, Activi...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as TabsStories from './Tabs.stories'

<Meta of={TabsStories} />

# Tabs

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Switches between views of the same thing without leaving the page:
Overview, Activity, Settings of one project.

<Status of={TabsStories} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Default} />

## Variants

`appearance` is the look. Either takes either size and orientation.

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `underline` | The sections of a page or a panel. Tabs sit on a 1px rule; a bar slides under the selected one. The default. |
| `pills` | A compact view switch in a toolbar, such as List / Board. A segmented track with the selected tab lifted. |

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Pills} />

| Form | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `isFullWidth` | Two to four tabs that should fill a narrow container, such as a side panel or a phone screen. |
| `vertical` | Many sections, or labels too long for a row: settings pages, a panel beside its content. |
| Icons | Recognisable icons beside the label. Never an icon alone: the label is the tab's name. |

<Canvas of={TabsStories.FullWidth} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.WithIcons} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tabs.json

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TabsStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TabsStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The indicator is one element for the whole list. It moves to the selected
tab rather than each tab drawing its own, so a change of tab slides it
across.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). A tab is a button in a
row, so it takes the spacious inline padding.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad-spacious' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Gap between icon and label', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Tab, pills', property: 'Track corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-sm' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },

/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad-spacious' },

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Tab list', property: 'Gap between tabs', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Tab list', property: 'Gap to the panel', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Tab, underline', property: 'Corner radius (the focus ring follows it)', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Focus ring offset (inside the tab)', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
    { part: 'Panel', property: 'Focus ring offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Height on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The underline indicator is 2px. In `pills`, the track has a 2px inset
and the chip's corner is the track's minus 2px, so the two stay concentric
at every size.

## Color

Each appearance has its own label colours and indicator. Switch the theme
and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="underline"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Label colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Tab, hover', property: 'Label colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Selected tab', property: 'Label colour', token: '--primary-text' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Tab list', property: 'Rule', token: '--border' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="pills"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Tab list', property: 'Track', token: '--muted' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Label colour', token: '--subtle-foreground' },
    { part: 'Tab, hover, and selected tab', property: 'Label colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Border', token: '--border' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-xs' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' }]} />

Pill labels use `--subtle-foreground`, not `--muted-foreground`: that is
4.3:1 on the `--muted` track, under 4.5:1.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={TabsStories.StatesUnderline} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled, pills' },
    { label: 'Hover, pills', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus, pills', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={TabsStories.StatesPills} />
</States>

- **Selected**: the label takes the selected colour and the indicator
  slides under it (`underline`) or behind it (`pills`).
- **Hover** brings an unselected label up to `--foreground`. It adds no
  fill.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn just inside the tab, so it is
  not clipped by the list.
- **Disabled** (Archive, above) is the enabled look at 50% opacity. It
  still takes focus.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TabsStories} />
</div>

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Tabs to split one thing into views the reader moves between freely,
in any order: the overview, activity and settings of a project. Every
panel is about the same object, and only one is needed at a time.

Label each tab with a word or two. Labels do not wrap or shrink, so long
ones push the row past its container.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TabsStories.DoShortLabels} />}
  doCaption="Short labels, a word or two: the row fits, and each reads at a glance."
  dont={<Story of={TabsStories.DontLongLabels} />}
  dontCaption="Long labels run past the edge of the container. Shorten them, or go vertical."
/>

Use `underline` for the sections of a page and `pills` for a view switch
in a toolbar. Name the tab list with `aria-label` when no heading does.
Selection is manual by default: arrow keys move focus, Enter or Space
selects, so a slow panel does not load on every keypress. Turn on
`activateOnFocus` only for light panels.

## When not to use

- **For a sequence.** Steps that must be done in order belong in a
  Stepper.
- **To compare content side by side.** Tabs show one panel at a time; put
  things that are read together on the same view.
- **To go to another page.** Use links, a Nav Sidebar or Breadcrumbs: a tab
  changes the view, not the URL.
- **For one setting with two or three options.** Use a radio group or a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) group:
  that changes a value, not the view.

## Accessibility

- `role="tablist"` of `role="tab"` buttons with `aria-selected` and
  `aria-controls`; each panel is a `role="tabpanel"` labelled by its tab.
- One tab stop: Tab moves into the list on the selected tab and the next
  Tab moves on to the panel.
- Arrow keys move between tabs (Left and Right, or Up and Down when
  vertical, with `aria-orientation` set); Home and End jump to the ends.
- Arrows move focus without selecting; Enter or Space selects. With
  `activateOnFocus`, arrows select as they go.
- A disabled tab still takes focus, marked `aria-disabled`, so it is
  found and announced, but it cannot be selected.
- Tabs are 24 or 32px tall and grow to 44px on touch screens
  (`pointer: coarse`).
- Focus ring: 2px `--ring`, drawn inside the tab.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, MouseEvent, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Tag.module.css'

/** Status first, then every hue the accent ramps offer, for categories. */
export const TAG_VARIANTS = [
  'neutral',
  'info',
  'success',
  'warning',
  'danger',
  'red',
  'orange',
  'amber',
  'yellow',
  'lime',
  'green',
  'emerald',
  'teal',
  'cyan',
  'sky',
  'blue',
  'indigo',
  'violet',
  'purple',
  'fuchsia',
  'pink',
  'rose',
] as const
export type TagVariant = (typeof TAG_VARIANTS)[number]

export interface TagProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'span'>, 'children'> {
  text: string
  startIcon?: ReactNode
  /** Image URL for a small avatar before the text, e.g. a person in a filter. */
  startAvatar?: string
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  appearance?: 'subtle' | 'outlined' | 'solid'
  variant?: TagVariant
  hasRemoveButton?: boolean
  onRemove?: (event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void
}

export function Tag({
  text,
  startIcon,
  startAvatar,
  size = 'md',
  appearance = 'subtle',
  variant = 'info',
  hasRemoveButton = false,
  onRemove,
  className,
  ...props
}: TagProps) {
  return (
    <span
      className={cn(
        styles.tag,
        styles[size],
        styles[appearance],
        styles[variant],
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {startAvatar ? (
        // A plain image, not <Avatar>: the tag only needs a round crop, and a
        // cross-component import would not survive the copy-source install.
        <img src={startAvatar} alt="" className={styles.avatar} />
      ) : (
        startIcon && (
          <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
            {startIcon}
          </span>
        )
      )}
      <span className={styles.text}>{text}</span>
      {hasRemoveButton && (
        <button
          type="button"
          // "Remove" alone is ambiguous in a list of tags, each with its own.
          aria-label={`Remove ${text}`}
          className={styles.remove}
          onClick={onRemove}
        >
          <Icon name="close" />
        </button>
      )}
    </span>
  )
}

# Tag A short label that categorises or marks something: a status, a filter chip, a person...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Tag } from './Tag'
import * as TagStories from './Tag.stories'

<Meta of={TagStories} />

# Tag

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A short label that categorises or marks something: a status, a filter
chip, a person picked in a field.

<Status of={TagStories} />

<Canvas of={TagStories.Matrix} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour: a status, or a hue for categories. `appearance`
is the emphasis. Any variant takes any appearance.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Tag text="Neutral" variant="neutral" /> | A plain label with no status: a type, a version. |
| <Tag text="Info" variant="info" /> | Informational status: In review, Scheduled. The default. |
| <Tag text="Success" variant="success" /> | Done or healthy: Paid, Verified, Live. |
| <Tag text="Warning" variant="warning" /> | Needs attention soon: Expiring, Pending. |
| <Tag text="Danger" variant="danger" /> | Failed or blocked: Overdue, Error. |
| <Tag text="Violet" variant="violet" /> | A hue: one per category, label or owner. It carries no meaning. |

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Tag text="Subtle" /> | Most places: a tint that sits in a row of text. |
| <Tag text="Outlined" appearance="outlined" /> | Dense tables and busy surfaces, where many tints would be loud. |
| <Tag text="Solid" appearance="solid" /> | One tag that must stand out: a single status on a card. |

<Canvas of={TagStories.Colors} />

<Canvas of={TagStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={TagStories.RemovableList} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Tag } from 'zweihander/tag'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tag.json
```

- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TagStories.anatomyParts}>

## Measurements

A tag sits in a line of text, so each size reads the control tier below
its name (Foundations / Sizing): `md` is tier sm, `sm` is tier xs. A 1px
padding and a 1px border, transparent unless outlined, make up the tier's
height, so appearances never shift the layout.

## States

The tag itself is not interactive. Its remove button is:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Tag text="Design" hasRemoveButton />
</States>

- **Hover** tints the button with the tag's own text colour at 15%, so it
  reads on every variant and appearance without a token for each.
- **Focus** is the `--ring` outline every control uses, drawn inset so it
  stays inside a 20px tag.
- Pressing removes nothing by itself: `onRemove` reports it, and the
  parent drops the tag from its list.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TagStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the container, including
`ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **The spec's four variants needed new tokens.** `info`, `success`,
  `warning` and `danger` were added to the token layer for Tag and are
  shared with Alert and Toast.
- **No `isRounded`.** The corner reads the control tier's radius, so it
  follows the Theme's radius preset with every other control, and turns
  into a pill under `radius="full-rounded"`.
- **The 17 hue variants are additions.** Solid is step 600 with a white
  label on every hue, in both appearances, so a row of solid tags reads as
  one set; on the warm hues (orange, amber, yellow, lime and others) that
  label falls below 4.5:1. That is accepted on purpose.
- **`startAvatar` wins over `startIcon`** if both are passed; the spec
  does not say.
- **The tag does not remove itself.** `onRemove` reports the click and
  the parent drops the tag from its list, so the list stays the one
  source of truth.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Tag to label or categorise: a status on a row, the categories of an
item, the filters applied to a list, the people picked in a field. Where a
tag has to pass AA, use `subtle` or `outlined`: solid hue tags keep one
white label across hues, which the warm ones carry under 4.5:1.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TagStories.DoSubtleHues} />}
  doCaption="Warm hues in subtle: every label clears 4.5:1."
  dont={<Story of={TagStories.DontSolidWarmHues} />}
  dontCaption="The same hues solid: the white label falls under 4.5:1."
/>

Colour carries meaning here, so it is never the only signal: the text says
what the status is.

In a wrapped list of removable tags on touch, keep at least `--space-6`
between rows. The remove button's touch area reaches 10px above and below
a 24px tag, and neighbouring targets would overlap.

## When not to use

- **For an action.** A tag is a label; its only control is remove. Use a
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).
- **For a choice the user toggles on and off.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) or a
  Checkbox.
- **For a count.** Use a
  [Badge](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-badge--docs).

## Accessibility

- The remove button is named **"Remove `text`"** (e.g. "Remove Design"),
  so a list of tags does not read as a row of identical "Remove" buttons.
- It is a native `<button>`: Tab to reach, Enter or Space to press.
- On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) its hit area grows to 44×44px
  without changing how the tag looks. That area reaches 10px above and
  below a 24px tag.
- After a tag is removed, focus has nowhere to stay and drops to the page.
  If that matters, move it to the next tag's remove button, or to the
  field the tags belong to, in your `onRemove`.
- The icon and the avatar are decorative.
- Every label clears 4.5:1 in both themes, measured by the `Contrast`
  story, except solid hue tags (see Differences from the spec).

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import {

  useLayoutEffect,
  useRef,
  type ComponentProps,
  type CSSProperties,
  type ReactNode,
} from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  assignRef,
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'
import styles from './Textarea.module.css'

export interface TextareaProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'textarea'>, 'size'> {
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Which way the user can drag to resize. Ignored with `hasAutoSize`. */
  resize?: 'none' | 'both' | 'vertical' | 'horizontal'
  /** Grow and shrink with the content, between `minRows` and `maxRows`. */
  hasAutoSize?: boolean
  /** The starting height, in lines. */
  minRows?: number
  /** The most it grows to before scrolling, in lines. */
  maxRows?: number
}

export function Textarea({
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  resize = 'vertical',
  hasAutoSize = false,
  minRows = 3,
  maxRows,
  required,
  disabled,
  name,
  className,
  onInput,
  ref,
  style,
  ...props
}: TextareaProps) {
  const inner = useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement | null>(null)
  const fit = useCallback(() => {
    const el = inner.current
    if (!el || !hasAutoSize) return
    // Collapse first so a shrinking value can shrink the box; max-block-size
    // (from maxRows) caps the result and the rest scrolls.
    el.style.blockSize = 'auto'
    el.style.blockSize = `${el.scrollHeight}px`
  }, [hasAutoSize])
  // Controlled values change without an input event; fit to those too.
  useLayoutEffect(fit, [fit, props.value])

  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <span className={cn(boxClass(size), styles.multiline, styles[`pad-${size}`])} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
        <Field.Control
          render={
            <textarea
              rows={minRows}
              ref={(node) => {
                inner.current = node
                assignRef(ref, node)
              }}
            />
          }
          {...(props as ComponentProps<typeof Field.Control>)}
          required={required}
          onInput={(event) => {
            fit()
            onInput?.(event as unknown as Parameters<NonNullable<TextareaProps["onInput"]>>[0])
          }}
          className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.textarea)}
          style={
            {
              ...style,
              resize: hasAutoSize ? 'none' : resize,
              ...(maxRows && { maxBlockSize: `calc(${maxRows} * 1lh + 2 * var(--pad-block))` }),
            } as CSSProperties
          }
        />
      </span>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Textarea Several lines of text: a message, a description, a note. The same field as [Tex...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'

<Meta of={TextareaStories} />

# Textarea

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Several lines of text: a message, a description, a note. The same field as
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs): label, helper,
validation and sizes are shared.

<Status of={TextareaStories} />

<Canvas of={TextareaStories.Default} />

## Variants

One appearance, the white outlined box. What changes is the size and how
the height is set.

<Canvas of={TextareaStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and dialogs: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a comment box in a table row, a side panel. |

<Canvas of={TextareaStories.AutoSize} />

| Height | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `resize="vertical"` (default) | People may want to see more at once and drag the corner to get it. |
| `hasAutoSize` with `maxRows` | Text whose length varies a lot, such as a chat message: the field grows as they write, up to `maxRows`, then scrolls. |
| `resize="none"` | A fixed height the layout depends on. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Textarea } from 'zweihander/textarea'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/textarea.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/Textarea.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Textarea.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/textarea](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/textarea)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TextareaStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TextareaStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The resize handle is the browser's own, in the input's bottom corner, on
the axes `resize` allows; `hasAutoSize` hides it. The placeholder is the
textarea's, in `--muted-foreground`.

## Measurements

A textarea grows, so it has no height token: it takes block padding
instead, which puts the first line where a single-line field of the same
size puts its text. The starting height is `minRows` lines (3 by default)
plus that padding. The padding sits on the textarea, not the box, so the
resize handle lands in the field's corner.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Block padding', token: '--control-xs-pad' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius-field' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Block padding', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label and helper text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label, container, helper', property: 'Gap between', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

20rem wide, capped at its container, or the container's width with
`isFullWidth`. With `maxRows`, the input stops at that many lines plus its
padding, whether it grew by itself or was dragged.

The same colours as Text Input: no colour variants, and the validation
state changes the edge and the helper text together.

    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Textarea label="Note" minRows={2} validationState="error" helperText="Add a note." required /> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <Textarea label="Note" minRows={2} defaultValue="Ships Monday." readOnly /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Textarea label="Note" minRows={2} defaultValue="Ships Monday." disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <Textarea label="Note" minRows={2} placeholder="Add a note" />
</States>

- **Hover** changes nothing; the cursor turns to a text cursor.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline around the whole box, 2px outside
  it, on click as well as keyboard. In the error state it is
  `--danger-text`.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--surface-filled`.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TextareaStories} />
</div>

Every other `<textarea>` attribute passes through, including `ref`,
`name` and `autoComplete`.

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance**, as on Text Input: every field is the white
  outlined box.
- Native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` names, and native `onChange`,
  as on Text Input.
- **`minRows` defaults to 3.** The spec gives none; the browser's own
  default of 2 is too short to read as a multi-line field.
- **`hasAutoSize`, `minRows` and `maxRows` are added**: the spec has a
  fixed `rows` only.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Textarea when the answer may run past one line: a message, a
description, feedback, an address. Set `minRows` to the length you expect,
so the field shows how much to write before anyone starts.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TextareaStories.DoFitTheAnswer} />}
  doCaption="A starting height that fits the answer expected tells people how much to write."
  dont={<Story of={TextareaStories.DontOneRow} />}
  dontCaption="One row looks like a single-line field and hides what has been written."
/>

Use auto-size for text whose length varies a lot, always with a `maxRows`,
so a long entry never pushes the rest of the form off the screen.

## When not to use

- **For one line**, such as a name or a title. Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs): Enter can
  submit the form there.
- **For formatted text** (bold, lists, links). A Textarea is plain text;
  use a rich-text editor.
- **For a search query.** Use [Search](?path=/docs/components-inputs-search--docs).

## Accessibility

- A real `<textarea>` with its `<label>`: clicking the label focuses it,
  and the label is its accessible name.
- `helperText` is its description (`aria-describedby`);
  `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid="true"`. The helper text
  carries the message, not only the colour.
- `required` sets the native `required`; the label's asterisk is
  `aria-hidden`.
- Enter inserts a line break; it does not submit the form.
- Auto-size caps at `maxRows` and scrolls beyond it, so the page does not
  grow without limit and the text stays reachable by keyboard.
- The edge is the light `--field-border`, about 1.5:1, the same approved
  exception to WCAG 1.4.11 as Text Input; set
  `--field-border: var(--control-border)` where 3:1 is needed.
- Focus ring: 2px, 2px offset, around the whole field.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { createContext, useContext, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'

export interface TextInputProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'input'>, 'size' | 'prefix'> {
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Under the field; the error message when `validationState` is error. */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  /** Text or an icon before the value, e.g. `<Icon name="search" />` or "https://". */
  prefix?: ReactNode
  /** Text or an icon after the value, e.g. "kg". */
  suffix?: ReactNode
  /** A filled segment joined to the start of the box: text that belongs to the value ("https://", "USD") or a `TextInputButton`. */
  startAddon?: ReactNode
  /** A filled segment joined to the end of the box: text (".com") or an attached `TextInputButton` ("Apply"). */
  endAddon?: ReactNode
  isFullWidth?: boolean
}

/** Lets a TextInputButton follow the field's `disabled` without being told twice. */
const FieldDisabledContext = createContext(false)

export function TextInput({
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  prefix,
  suffix,
  startAddon,
  endAddon,
  isFullWidth,
  required,
  disabled,
  name,
  className,
  ...props
}: TextInputProps) {
  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <FieldDisabledContext value={Boolean(disabled)}>
        <span className={boxClass(size)} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
          {startAddon && <span className={cn(inputStyles.addon, inputStyles.addonStart)}>{startAddon}</span>}
          {prefix && <span className={inputStyles.affix}>{prefix}</span>}
          <Field.Control {...props} required={required} className={cn(inputStyles.control)} />
          {suffix && <span className={inputStyles.affix}>{suffix}</span>}
          {endAddon && <span className={cn(inputStyles.addon, inputStyles.addonEnd)}>{endAddon}</span>}
        </span>
      </FieldDisabledContext>
    </InputField>
  )
}

export type TextInputButtonProps = ComponentProps<'button'>

/**
 * A button inside a Text Input: an icon in `prefix` or `suffix` (give it an
 * `aria-label`), or a word in an add-on, where it fills the segment. Disabled
 * with the field; a read-only field keeps it, since copying or opening a
 * fixed value is what it is for.
 */
export function TextInputButton({ type = 'button', disabled, className, ...props }: TextInputButtonProps) {
  const fieldDisabled = useContext(FieldDisabledContext)
  return (
    <button
      type={type}
      disabled={disabled || fieldDisabled}
      className={cn(inputStyles.iconButton, className)}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

# Text Input A single line of text: a name, an email, a URL. ## Variants There is one appe...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { TextInput } from './TextInput'
import * as TextInputStories from './TextInput.stories'

<Meta of={TextInputStories} />

# Text Input

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A single line of text: a name, an email, a URL.

<Status of={TextInputStories} />

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Default} />

## Variants

There is one appearance, the white outlined box. What changes is the
size, what sits beside the value, and the validation state.

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and dialogs: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: toolbars, table filters, inline edits. |

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.PrefixSuffix} />

| Affix | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `prefix` | A fixed start the value continues: "https://", a currency sign, an icon that says what the field holds. |
| `suffix` | A unit the value is measured in: "kg", "%", "days". |

**Add-ons** are filled segments joined to the edge of the box, divided
from the value by a hairline. Use them when the fixed part is long enough,
or important enough, to need its own place: a protocol and a domain, a
currency code, or an action attached to the field.

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Addons} />

| Add-on | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `startAddon` | A fixed start that is part of the value people see: "https://", "USD". |
| `endAddon` | A fixed ending (".com"), or an attached `TextInputButton` that acts on the value: "Apply", "Check". |

**Buttons in the field** act on the value without leaving it: open a link,
reveal, clear. `TextInputButton` is an icon button sized to the field; put
it in `suffix` (or `prefix`), or in an add-on, where it fills the segment.

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.WithButton} />

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Validation} />

| Validation state | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Before anything is checked. |
| `error` | The value cannot be accepted. `helperText` says what to change. |
| `success` | A value checked against the server and accepted, such as a free username. Not for every field that passes. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { TextInput, TextInputButton } from 'zweihander/text-input'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/text-input.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/TextInput.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/TextInput.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/text-input](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/text-input)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TextInputStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TextInputStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The placeholder has no element of its own: it is the input's, shown in
`--muted-foreground` while the input is empty. With `required`, an
asterisk follows the label.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). Fields take the normal
inline padding, not Button's spacious one, so the value lines up with the
label above it, and the field radius, which never becomes a pill.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Prefix, suffix and button icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-sm' },
    { part: 'Add-on', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-md-gap' },
    { part: 'Prefix, suffix and button icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Add-on', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label and helper text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label and helper text', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Label, container, helper', property: 'Gap between', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

The label and helper stay at body size in `sm` too: only the box gets
smaller. The field is 20rem wide, capped at its container; with
`isFullWidth` it fills the container. The edge is 1px. An add-on runs
the full height of the box, and its 1px divider takes the edge's colour,
so a field in the error state is red all round, divider included.

## Color

The field has no colour variants. Its validation state changes the edge
and the helper text together. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values
follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="default"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--card' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--field-border' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-2xs' },
    { part: 'Label and input', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Placeholder, prefix, suffix', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Add-on', property: 'Background', token: '--surface-filled' },
    { part: 'Add-on text', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Add-on button', property: 'Colour', token: '--foreground' },
    { part: 'Add-on button, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--accent' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Colour', token: '--muted-foreground' },
    { part: 'Required asterisk', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="error"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--danger-text' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="success"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--success-text' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Colour', token: '--success-text' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Read-only" rows={[{ part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--surface-filled' }]} />

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Filled', content: <TextInput label="Name" defaultValue="Okami" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <TextInput label="Name" validationState="error" helperText="Enter a name." required /> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <TextInput label="Name" defaultValue="Okami" readOnly /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <TextInput label="Name" defaultValue="Okami" disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <TextInput label="Name" placeholder="Your name" />
</States>

- **Hover** changes nothing: the field is already plainly a field, and the
  cursor turns to a text cursor.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the box, drawn on click
  as well as from the keyboard, since that is where typing will go. In the
  error state the ring is `--danger-text`.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--surface-filled`: it can be focused
  and copied, not changed.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.
- **A button in an add-on** fills the segment: hover gives it `--accent`,
  and its focus ring sits inside the segment, so the box's edge does not
  cut it. An icon button in `prefix` or `suffix` turns `--foreground` on
  hover. In a read-only field the box takes the add-on's fill, so only the
  divider sets the add-on apart.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TextInputStories} />
</div>

`TextInputButton` takes every `<button>` attribute; it is `type="button"`
by default and follows the field's `disabled`.

Every other `<input>` attribute passes through to the input, including
`ref`, `type`, `name`, `pattern`, `maxLength`, `inputMode` and
`autoComplete`.

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (24px) and `md` (32px) only, the compact control scale of the Claude apps. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **Native names** for native attributes: `disabled`, `required`,
  `readOnly` rather than `isDisabled`, `isRequired`, `isReadOnly`.
- **`onChange` is the native event**, not a value: the kit's rule for
  components that wrap a real input, so it works with every form library
  as-is.
- **Changed in 0.8:** `error` became `validationState="error"` plus
  `helperText`; `forwardRef` is gone (`ref` is a prop in React 19).

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Text Input for short free text on one line: a name, an email
address, a URL, a title. Give every field a visible label, and use the
placeholder only for a hint of the format.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TextInputStories.DoVisibleLabel} />}
  doCaption="A visible label names the field; the placeholder only hints at the format."
  dont={<Story of={TextInputStories.DontPlaceholderAsLabel} />}
  dontCaption="A placeholder as the label disappears on the first keystroke, and with it what the field was for."
/>

**Errors** say what to change, in the helper text, next to the field. The
red edge only points at the message.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TextInputStories.DoSayWhatToFix} />}
  doCaption="The error says what is wrong and how to fix it."
  dont={<Story of={TextInputStories.DontColourOnly} />}
  dontCaption="A red edge and 'Invalid' leave people guessing what to change."
/>

**Prefix or add-on.** A prefix is a hint inside the box, read past
without stopping: an icon, a currency sign. An add-on is a segment of its
own, for a fixed part long enough to label the value ("https://", ".com")
or for an action attached to it. Use one start and one end at most; a
field with an add-on and a prefix on the same side has two things before
the value to read.

## When not to use

- **For several lines.** Use a
  [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs): Enter adds a
  line instead of submitting.
- **For a quantity.** Use a
  [Number Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-numberinput--docs), which
  steps and parses. For numbers that are identifiers (postcodes, card
  numbers, phone numbers) keep the Text Input with `inputMode="numeric"`.
- **For a search query.** Use [Search](?path=/docs/components-inputs-search--docs),
  which clears and is exposed as a searchbox.
- **To pick from a known list.** Use a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) or a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs).
- **For a unit people choose** (a currency, a country code). Add-ons take
  text or a `TextInputButton`, not a Select: put a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) beside the field.
- **For a date.** Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).

## Accessibility

- The label is a real `<label>` for the input: clicking it focuses the
  input, and it is the input's accessible name.
- `helperText` is the input's description (`aria-describedby`), so a
  screen reader reads it after the name.
- `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the input.
  Colour is never the only signal: the helper text carries the message.
- `required` sets the native `required`; the asterisk is `aria-hidden`, so
  it is not read as "star".
- Do not rely on the placeholder as a label: it is not reliably announced
  and disappears as soon as anyone types. Without a visible label, pass
  `aria-label`.
- Pressing the field's padding, a prefix or a text add-on focuses the
  input, as a click anywhere on a native field does.
- A `TextInputButton` is a native `<button>` after the input in the tab
  order, pressed with Enter or Space. An icon-only one needs `aria-label`.
  Pressing it does not move focus to the input.
- `TextInputButton` is disabled with the field. In a read-only field it
  stays enabled, since opening or copying a fixed value is what it is for.
- **The edge is `--field-border`, about 1.5:1, a deliberate exception to
  WCAG 1.4.11** (approved 2026-10-08), for the light hairline of the
  Claude apps. The field is a white `--card` box with a faint drop on the
  off-white page, and the label, placeholder and focus ring mark it too.
  If your audience needs 3:1, set `--field-border: var(--control-border)`.
- Focus ring: 2px, 2px offset, on click and keyboard alike.
- Heights are 24 and 32px, at or above WCAG 2.5.8's 24px minimum. The
  label is part of the target, since clicking it focuses the input.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useSyncExternalStore, type ReactNode, type RefObject } from 'react'
import { Toast as BaseToast } from '@base-ui/react/toast'
import { Icon, type IconName } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Toast.module.css'

export type ToastVariant = 'default' | 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'

export interface ToastOptions {
  title?: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  variant?: ToastVariant
  /** One button, e.g. "Undo". Keep the same action reachable elsewhere: the toast goes away. */
  action?: { label: ReactNode; onClick: () => void }
  /** Milliseconds before it closes; `0` keeps it until dismissed. */
  timeout?: number
  /** `high` interrupts the screen reader (danger defaults to it). */
  priority?: 'low' | 'high'
  onClose?: () => void
}

export interface ToastProviderProps {
  children: ReactNode
  placement?: 'top-left' | 'top-center' | 'top-right' | 'bottom-left' | 'bottom-center' | 'bottom-right'
  /** Default time on screen, in milliseconds. */
  timeout?: number
  /** Toasts shown at once; older ones wait. */
  limit?: number
  /**
   * Where the toasts render, `document.body` by default. In an element with
   * a `transform` they sit in its corner instead of the window's, and in a
   * size container (`container-type: inline-size`) they fit its width: a
   * preview, or a frame in the page.
   */
  container?: HTMLElement | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | null
}

// Base UI's promise() sets these types itself.
const variantOf = (type: string | undefined): ToastVariant | 'loading' =>
  type === 'error' ? 'danger' : type === 'loading' ? 'loading' : ((type as ToastVariant) ?? 'default')

const icons: Partial<Record<ToastVariant, IconName>> = {
  info: 'info-filled',
  success: 'success-filled',
  warning: 'warning-filled',
  danger: 'danger-filled',
}

// The toast takes the opposite appearance of the page (dark on a light page,
// light on a dark one) so it stands out from what is under it. The page's
// appearance is the `dark` class on <html>.
const subscribeToPageTheme = (onChange: () => void) => {
  const observer = new MutationObserver(onChange)
  observer.observe(document.documentElement, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['class'] })
  return () => observer.disconnect()
}
const pageIsDark = () => document.documentElement.classList.contains('dark')

function ToastList({ swipe }: { swipe: 'left' | 'right' | 'up' | 'down' }) {
  const { toasts } = BaseToast.useToastManager()
  return toasts.map((toast) => {
    const variant = variantOf(toast.type)
    const icon = variant === 'loading' ? null : icons[variant]
    return (
      <BaseToast.Root
        key={toast.id}
        toast={toast}
        swipeDirection={swipe}
        // Each toast is a (non-modal) dialog and needs a name. promise()
        // passes its strings as the description, with no title: name it by
        // what it says rather than leave it unnamed.
        aria-label={toast.title ? undefined : typeof toast.description === 'string' ? toast.description : 'Notification'}
        className={cn(styles.toast, styles[variant])}
      >
        {variant === 'loading' && <span className={cn(styles.icon, styles.spinner)} aria-hidden="true" />}
        {icon && (
          <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
            <Icon name={icon} />
          </span>
        )}
        <BaseToast.Content className={styles.content}>
          {toast.title && <BaseToast.Title className={styles.title} />}
          {toast.description && <BaseToast.Description className={styles.description} />}
          {toast.actionProps && <BaseToast.Action className={styles.action} />}
        </BaseToast.Content>
        <BaseToast.Close aria-label="Dismiss" className={styles.close}>
          <Icon name="close" />
        </BaseToast.Close>
      </BaseToast.Root>
    )
  })
}

/** Wrap the app once. Toasts render in a corner of the viewport, above everything. */
export function ToastProvider({ children, placement = 'bottom-right', timeout = 5000, limit = 3, container }: ToastProviderProps) {
  const [vertical, horizontal] = placement.split('-') as ['top' | 'bottom', 'left' | 'center' | 'right']
  const swipe = horizontal === 'center' ? (vertical === 'top' ? 'up' : 'down') : horizontal
  const dark = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeToPageTheme, pageIsDark, () => false)
  return (
    <BaseToast.Provider timeout={timeout} limit={limit}>
      {children}
      <BaseToast.Portal container={container}>
        <BaseToast.Viewport className={cn(styles.viewport, styles[vertical], styles[horizontal], dark ? 'light' : 'dark')}>
          <ToastList swipe={swipe} />
        </BaseToast.Viewport>
      </BaseToast.Portal>
    </BaseToast.Provider>
  )
}

/** Show, update and close toasts from anywhere inside a ToastProvider. */
export function useToast() {
  const manager = BaseToast.useToastManager()
  // Only the fields that were given: Base UI merges an update over the
  // toast, so an explicit undefined would wipe its variant or action.
  const toOptions = ({ variant, action, priority, ...rest }: ToastOptions) => {
    const options: Record<string, unknown> = { ...rest }
    if (variant !== undefined) options.type = variant
    const p = priority ?? (variant === 'danger' ? 'high' : undefined)
    if (p !== undefined) options.priority = p
    if (action !== undefined) options.actionProps = { children: action.label, onClick: action.onClick }
    return options
  }
  return {
    /** Returns the toast's id. */
    add: (options: ToastOptions) => manager.add(toOptions(options)),
    update: (id: string, options: ToastOptions) => manager.update(id, toOptions(options)),
    /** Closes one toast, or every toast without an id. */
    close: (id?: string) => manager.close(id),
    /** A loading toast that turns into success or danger when the promise settles. */
    promise: manager.promise,
  }
}
