export const StateRow: Story = {
  name: 'States',
  render: () => states,
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    // Storybook announces each render, and the addon rewrites the stylesheets
    // then (docs pages included). The test runner announces nothing, so play
    // Storybook's part.
    addons.getChannel().emit(STORY_RENDERED)
    const cells = within(canvasElement).getAllByRole('listitem')
    await expect(cells.map((c) => c.lastElementChild!.textContent)).toEqual(['Enabled', 'Hover', 'Focus', 'Pressed', 'Disabled'])
    const stage = (label: string) => canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-state="${label}"]`)!
    await expect(stage('Hover')).toHaveClass('pseudo-hover-all')
    await expect(stage('Focus')).toHaveClass('pseudo-focus-visible-all')
    await expect(stage('Pressed')).toHaveClass('pseudo-active-all')
    await expect(stage('Disabled').querySelector('button')).toBeDisabled()
    // The forced states actually paint: the addon rewrote :hover and friends.
    const look = (label: string) => {
      const s = getComputedStyle(stage(label).querySelector('button')!)
      return `${s.backgroundColor} ${s.outlineStyle}`
    }
    // What the addon did to the stylesheets, for the failure message.
    const rewritten = () => {
      const button = stage('Hover').querySelector('button')!
      const rules = [...document.styleSheets].flatMap((sheet) => {
        try {
          return [...sheet.cssRules]
        } catch {
          return []
        }
      })
      const hover = rules.filter((r): r is CSSStyleRule => r instanceof CSSStyleRule && r.selectorText.includes(':hover'))
      const forced = hover.filter((r) => r.selectorText.includes('pseudo-hover-all'))
      const engaged = forced.filter((r) => button.matches(r.selectorText))
      return `${document.styleSheets.length} sheets, ${hover.length} :hover rules, ${forced.length} rewritten, ${engaged.length} reach the button: ${engaged.map((r) => r.cssText).join(' | ').slice(0, 300) || hover.find((r) => r.selectorText.includes('button'))?.cssText.slice(0, 300)}`
    }
    await waitFor(() => {
      // Again on each try: a stylesheet Vite injects late is rewritten too.
      addons.getChannel().emit(STORY_RENDERED)
      expect(look('Hover'), rewritten()).not.toBe(look('Enabled'))
    })
    // No transition to wait out: each state shows its end value at once.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(stage('Hover').querySelector('button')!).transitionDuration).toBe('0s')
    await expect(look('Pressed')).not.toBe(look('Hover'))
    await expect(getComputedStyle(stage('Focus').querySelector('button')!).outlineStyle).toBe('solid')
  },
}

# Focus One ring for the whole kit: `outline: var(--focus-width) solid var(--ring)`, shown...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FocusStories from './Focus.stories'

<Meta of={FocusStories} />

# Focus

One ring for the whole kit: `outline: var(--focus-width) solid var(--ring)`,
shown on `:focus-visible` only. Its colour is `--ring`, measured at 3:1
against the page (see [Colors](?path=/docs/foundations-colors--docs)).

<Canvas of={FocusStories.Rings} />

## Outside or inside

There are two offsets and the choice is mechanical.

**`--focus-offset`** draws the ring outside the element. It is the default
for anything that stands on its own: buttons, fields, links, checkboxes.

**`--focus-offset-inset`** draws it inside. Use it when the element sits
flush against the edge of a container that clips its overflow, or when an
outside ring would run into a neighbour: tabs, table rows and sortable
headers, accordion triggers, the close button in a modal, popover, alert
or toast, the remove button in a tag, the steppers in a number input.

A third value is a smell. The one exception is a selected colour swatch,
which already carries a selection ring at `--focus-offset`, so its focus
ring sits one pixel further out to stay visible.

## Why the ring is not scaled

`--focus-width` and both offsets are plain pixels, not multiplied by
`--scaling`. A ring is a stroke: at 90% scaling it should not thin to
1.8px, and WCAG 2.4.13 measures it in CSS pixels.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect, waitFor } from 'storybook/test'
import { Button } from '@/components/buttons/Button'
import { anatomyPartFor, startInspector, type TokenValue } from './inspect'

/**
 * What the Specs tab draws inside the preview frame: the parts numbered, the
 * hovered row's redline, and the tokens resolved as the frame sees them.
 */
const meta = {
  title: 'Site/Inspect',
  render: () => <Button>Subscribe</Button>,
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

const layer = () => document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-playground-inspector]')

/** Which anatomy part a Specs row is about. */
export const RowToPart: Story = {
  play: async () => {
    const names = ['Container', 'Start icon', 'Label', 'Title', 'Previous month']
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Container, outlined', names)).toBe('Container')
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Title and description', names)).toBe('Title')
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Icon', names)).toBe('Start icon')
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Previous and next', names)).toBe('Previous month')
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Focus ring', names)).toBe('Focus ring')
    // A whole word only: "Lab" is not Label.
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Lab', names)).toBeNull()
    await expect(anatomyPartFor('Option', names)).toBeNull()
  },
}

export const Default: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    let values: Record<string, TokenValue> = {}
    const inspector = startInspector(
      () => canvasElement,
      (v) => (values = v),
    )
    const parts = [
      { name: 'Container', selector: 'button' },
      { name: 'Missing', selector: 'nav' },
    ]
    try {
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: ['--control-md', '--primary', '--nope'] })
      // One number, on the part that is there; decoration only.
      await waitFor(() => expect(layer()?.textContent).toBe('①'))
      await expect(layer()).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true')
      await expect(getComputedStyle(layer()!).pointerEvents).toBe('none')
      await waitFor(() => expect(values['--control-md']).toEqual({ kind: 'length', text: '32px' }))
      await expect(values['--primary'].kind).toBe('color')
      await expect(values['--nope']).toEqual({ kind: 'missing', text: 'Not defined here' })

      // A row's redline: the part's height, with its value.
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: ['--control-md'], highlight: { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' } })
      await waitFor(() => expect(layer()?.textContent).toContain('Height 32px'))
      const button = canvasElement.querySelector('button')!.getBoundingClientRect()
      const line = [...layer()!.children].find((el) => (el as HTMLElement).style.width === '1px') as HTMLElement
      await expect(parseFloat(line.style.height)).toBeCloseTo(button.height, 0)

      // Inline padding shades the two sides.
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: [], highlight: { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--x' } })
      await waitFor(() => expect([...layer()!.children].filter((el) => (el as HTMLElement).style.background.includes('0.25'))).toHaveLength(2))

      // The focus ring at its width and offset around the focusable element, though no anatomy part names it.
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: ['--focus-width'], highlight: { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' } })
      await waitFor(() => expect(layer()?.textContent).toContain('Width 2px'))
      const ring = [...layer()!.children].find((el) => (el as HTMLElement).style.borderWidth === '2px') as HTMLElement
      await expect(parseFloat(ring.style.width)).toBeCloseTo(button.width + 2 * (2 + 2), 0)

      // Radius marks the corner; font size shades the first line of text.
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: [], highlight: { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--x' } })
      await waitFor(() => expect([...layer()!.children].some((el) => (el as HTMLElement).style.borderTopLeftRadius !== '')).toBe(true))
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: [], highlight: { part: 'Container', property: 'Font size', token: '--x' } })
      await waitFor(() => expect([...layer()!.children].filter((el) => (el as HTMLElement).style.background.includes('0.25'))).toHaveLength(1))

      // A forced state goes on the item's root as the pseudo-states addon's class, and comes off.
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: [], pseudo: 'hover' })
      await expect(canvasElement).toHaveClass('pseudo-hover-all')
      inspector.set({ parts, tokens: [], pseudo: 'active' })
      await expect(canvasElement).not.toHaveClass('pseudo-hover-all')
      await expect(canvasElement).toHaveClass('pseudo-active-all')
    } finally {
      inspector.set(null)
    }
    await expect(layer()).toBeNull()
    await expect(canvasElement).not.toHaveClass('pseudo-active-all')
  },
}

# Layering Four layers for everything that leaves the page flow. A component picks the lay...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as LayeringStories from './Layering.stories'

<Meta of={LayeringStories} />

# Layering

Four layers for everything that leaves the page flow. A component picks
the layer by what it is, never by trying a bigger number.

<Canvas of={LayeringStories.Layers} />

## One layer for every overlay

Popovers, menus, listboxes, date pickers, modals and drawers all share
`--layer-overlay`. They are portalled to the end of `<body>`, so at an equal
z-index the one opened last paints on top: a Select opened inside a Modal
lands above the Modal without either knowing about the other. Giving the
Modal a higher layer would break exactly that case.

Tooltips sit one layer up because they can belong to anything, including a
trigger inside an open overlay. Toasts sit above everything: a toast raised
while a modal is open still has to be read.

## Local z-index

A value used only to order parts inside one component (a table's sticky
header at `1`, the tab indicator at `-1`) is local and stays a plain number.
Keep these at single digits so they stay well below `--layer-sticky`.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { TokenTable } from './TokenTable'

const TOKENS = [
  { name: '--duration-fast', use: 'Popups appearing: menu, tooltip, popover, date picker, listbox' },
  { name: '--duration-base', use: 'State changes: hover and press colours, switch, accordion, modal' },
  { name: '--duration-slow', use: 'Things that travel: the tab indicator, a toast sliding in, a drawer' },
  { name: '--duration-spin', use: 'One turn of every spinner' },
  { name: '--duration-spin-reduced', use: 'One turn under prefers-reduced-motion' },
]

// Narrative and prose live in Motion.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Motion',
  render: () => <TokenTable tokens={TOKENS} />,
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Durations: Story = {
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const value = (name: string) => canvasElement.querySelector(`[data-token="${name}"]`)!.textContent
    // Under reduced motion the three transition steps resolve to 0ms, which
    // is the point of the token; the test runner does not emulate it.
    await expect(value('--duration-fast')).toBe('100ms')
    await expect(value('--duration-base')).toBe('150ms')
    await expect(value('--duration-slow')).toBe('200ms')
    await expect(value('--duration-spin')).toBe('800ms')
    await expect(value('--duration-spin-reduced')).toBe('2.5s')
  },
}

# Motion Three transition durations and one spinner speed. Every `transition` in the kit r...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as MotionStories from './Motion.stories'

<Meta of={MotionStories} />

# Motion

Three transition durations and one spinner speed. Every `transition` in the
kit reads one of them; nothing types a number of milliseconds.

<Canvas of={MotionStories.Durations} />

## Choosing a step

The step follows what moves, not how important it is. A popup appearing
is `fast`: it answers a click, and anything slower reads as lag. A colour
or state change is `base`. Something that travels across the screen (the
tab indicator, a toast, a drawer) is `slow`, because the eye has to follow
it. If a new transition does not fit one of the three, that is a reason to
question the transition before adding a fourth step.

Easing is the browser default (`ease`) except where something grows or
shrinks: Accordion and Collapse open with `ease-out`, so the panel arrives
fast and settles. There is no easing token: two curves, each with an
obvious owner, do not need a name yet.

## Reduced motion

Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the three transition steps resolve to
`0ms` in `tokens.css`, so every transition in the kit stops in one place
without each component repeating a media query.

Two things are exempt. Toast swaps its slide for a 200ms fade, written as
a number on purpose, since the tokens would turn the fade into a jump.
And spinners: a stopped spinner says nothing is happening, so instead of
stopping they slow from `--duration-spin` to `--duration-spin-reduced`.
Each spinner opts into that itself.

Loop animations with their own rhythm (the skeleton pulse, the
indeterminate progress bar) keep their own timing: they are a single
animation each, not a step anyone else should reuse.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { withPrefersDark } from '@/test/story-helpers'

/**
 * The preview decorator's side of the Preview theme: the globals the
 * Playground sends become a `<Theme>` around the story.
 */
const meta = {
  title: 'Site/Preview theme',
  render: () => <p>Themed content</p>,
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

const wrapper = (canvasElement: HTMLElement) => canvasElement.querySelector('[data-preview-theme]')

export const Dark: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'dark' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(wrapper(canvasElement)).toHaveClass('dark')
    // Popups portal to <body>: the frame's <html> goes dark with it.
    await expect(document.documentElement).toHaveClass('dark')
  },
}

export const Light: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'light' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(wrapper(canvasElement)).toHaveClass('light')
    await expect(document.documentElement).not.toHaveClass('dark')
  },
}

export const SystemOnDarkOs: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'system' },
  beforeEach: withPrefersDark(true),
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(wrapper(canvasElement)).toHaveClass('dark')
  },
}

export const SystemOnLightOs: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'system' },
  beforeEach: withPrefersDark(false),
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(wrapper(canvasElement)).toHaveClass('light')
  },
}

export const ColorAndRadius: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'light', accent: 'rose', gray: 'slate', radius: 'full-rounded' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const scope = wrapper(canvasElement) as HTMLElement
    await expect(scope).toHaveAttribute('data-accent', 'rose')
    await expect(scope).toHaveAttribute('data-gray', 'slate')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--radius-factor')).toBe('1.5')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--radius-full')).toBe('9999px')
    // Popups portal to <body>: the frame's <html> wears the same.
    await expect(document.documentElement).toHaveAttribute('data-accent', 'rose')
    await expect(document.documentElement.style.getPropertyValue('--radius-factor')).toBe('1.5')
  },
}

export const Typography: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'light', font: 'inter', scaling: '110%' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const scope = wrapper(canvasElement) as HTMLElement
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--font-sans')).toContain('Inter')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--scaling')).toBe('1.1')
    // Headings follow: --font-heading derives from --font-sans on every element.
    const text = canvasElement.querySelector('p')!
    await expect(getComputedStyle(text).getPropertyValue('--font-heading')).toContain('Inter')
    await expect(getComputedStyle(text).fontFamily).toContain('Inter')
    // Popups portal to <body>: the frame's <html> wears the same.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(document.body).getPropertyValue('--font-heading')).toContain('Inter')
    await expect(document.documentElement.style.getPropertyValue('--scaling')).toBe('1.1')
    // The face is there: bundled with the preview (the build has no font CDN request).
    await document.fonts.load('16px "Inter Variable"')
    await expect(document.fonts.check('16px "Inter Variable"')).toBe(true)
  },
}

/** System is the token's own stack: nothing set, so the default stays. */
export const SystemFont: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'light', font: 'system', scaling: '100%' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const scope = wrapper(canvasElement) as HTMLElement
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--font-sans')).toBe('')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--scaling')).toBe('1')
  },
}

/** A value the kit does not have is dropped: the default stays. */
export const UnknownValues: Story = {
  globals: { appearance: 'light', accent: 'foo', radius: 'huge', font: 'comic', scaling: '200%' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const scope = wrapper(canvasElement) as HTMLElement
    await expect(scope).not.toHaveAttribute('data-accent')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--radius-factor')).toBe('')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--font-sans')).toBe('')
    await expect(scope.style.getPropertyValue('--scaling')).toBe('')
  },
}

/** Outside the Playground no appearance is set: no wrapper, the toolbar's theme as before. */
export const ToolbarTheme: Story = {
  globals: { theme: 'dark' },
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    await expect(wrapper(canvasElement)).toBeNull()
    await expect(document.documentElement).toHaveClass('dark')
  },
}

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { Button } from '@/components/buttons/Button'
import { TextInput } from '@/components/inputs/TextInput'
import { Theme, type Radius as RadiusPreset } from '@/theme/Theme'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

const COL: React.CSSProperties = {
  display: 'flex',
  flexDirection: 'column',
  alignItems: 'center',
  gap: 'var(--space-2)',
}

const STEPS = ['radius-sm', 'radius-md', 'radius-lg', 'radius-xl'] as const

function StepScale() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.rowWrap}>
      {STEPS.map((token) => (
        <div key={token} style={COL}>
          <div
            style={{
              height: '4rem',
              width: '4rem',
              background: 'var(--primary)',
              borderRadius: `var(--${token})`,
            }}
          />
          <span className={docs.caption}>--{token}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

const INTENTS = [
  { token: 'radius-control', label: 'control', note: 'Button, badge' },
  { token: 'radius-field', label: 'field', note: 'Input, textarea' },
  { token: 'radius-panel', label: 'panel', note: 'Card, dialog' },
] as const

function Intents() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.rowWrap}>
      {INTENTS.map(({ token, label, note }) => (
        <div key={token} style={COL}>
          <div
            style={{
              display: 'flex',
              height: '4rem',
              width: '7rem',
              alignItems: 'center',
              justifyContent: 'center',
              background: 'var(--secondary)',
              color: 'var(--secondary-foreground)',
              fontSize: 'var(--text-body)',
              borderRadius: `var(--${token})`,
            }}
          >
            {label}
          </div>
          <span className={docs.caption}>--{token}</span>
          <span className={docs.caption}>{note}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

const PRESETS: RadiusPreset[] = ['sharp', 'rounded', 'full-rounded']

function PresetRow({ preset }: { preset: RadiusPreset }) {
  return (
    <Theme radius={preset} className={docs.stack}>
      <span className={docs.caption}>radius="{preset}"</span>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', alignItems: 'center', gap: 'var(--space-3)' }}>
        <Button>Button</Button>
        <div style={{ width: '10rem' }}>
          <TextInput aria-label="Input" placeholder="Input" isFullWidth />
        </div>
        <div
          data-panel
          style={{
            border: '1px solid var(--border)',
            background: 'var(--card)',
            color: 'var(--card-foreground)',
            padding: 'var(--space-2) var(--space-4)',
            fontSize: 'var(--text-body)',
            borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)',
          }}
        >
          Panel
        </div>
      </div>
    </Theme>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Radius.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Radius',
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Presets: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.stackWide}>
      {PRESETS.map((preset) => (
        <PresetRow key={preset} preset={preset} />
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const px = (el: Element) => Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).borderRadius)
    const scopeFor = (preset: string) =>
      canvas.getByText(`radius="${preset}"`).parentElement as HTMLElement
    const parts = (preset: string) => {
      const scope = scopeFor(preset)
      return {
        control: px(scope.querySelector('button')!),
        // The field's corner is on the box that draws it, not the bare <input>.
        field: px(scope.querySelector('input')!.parentElement!),
        panel: px(scope.querySelector('[data-panel]')!),
      }
    }

    // sharp flattens everything.
    const sharp = parts('sharp')
    await expect(sharp.control).toBe(0)
    await expect(sharp.field).toBe(0)
    await expect(sharp.panel).toBe(0)

    const rounded = parts('rounded')
    const full = parts('full-rounded')

    // full pills the control...
    await expect(full.control).toBeGreaterThan(1000)
    // ...but a field must never reach a pill. The input is 32px tall, so
    // anything at or above 16px is one.
    await expect(full.field).toBeLessThan(16)
    await expect(full.panel).toBeLessThan(1000)
    // ...and it still has to be a step up from rounded, or "full-rounded"
    // would just be "rounded with a pill button".
    await expect(full.field).toBeGreaterThan(rounded.field)
    await expect(full.panel).toBeGreaterThan(rounded.panel)
  },
}

export const Steps: Story = {
  render: () => <StepScale />,
}

export const Intent: Story = {
  render: () => <Intents />,
}

const SCALES = ['90%', '100%', '110%'] as const

/* A corner that stayed put while the padding shrank would break the nesting
   rule at every scaling but 100%, so the two have to move together. */
export const Scaling: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.row}>
      {SCALES.map((scaling) => (
        <Theme key={scaling} scaling={scaling} className={docs.stack}>
          <Button>{scaling}</Button>
        </Theme>
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const measure = (scaling: string) => {
      const style = getComputedStyle(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: scaling }))
      return { radius: Number.parseFloat(style.borderTopLeftRadius), pad: Number.parseFloat(style.paddingLeft) }
    }
    const base = measure('100%')
    for (const scaling of ['90%', '110%']) {
      const { radius, pad } = measure(scaling)
      await expect(radius / base.radius).toBeCloseTo(pad / base.pad, 2)
      await expect(radius).not.toBe(base.radius)
    }
  },
}

# Radius Rounding is a **single setting**, not a value picked per component. A `radius` pr...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as RadiusStories from './Radius.stories'

<Meta of={RadiusStories} />

# Radius

Rounding is a **single setting**, not a value picked per component. A
`radius` preset on `Theme` rescales everything inside it at once, and
components follow because they reference an *intent* — control, field,
panel — rather than a fixed number.

```tsx
<Theme radius="full-rounded">
  <Button>Pill</Button>
</Theme>
```

## Presets

Three: `sharp`, **`rounded` (the default)**, `full-rounded`. The
default is set by `--radius-factor: 1` and `--radius-full: 0px` on
`:root`, which is exactly what the `rounded` preset writes — so a scope
with no `radius` prop and a scope with `radius="rounded"` are identical.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Presets} />

Look at the `full-rounded` row. **The button becomes a pill; the input and the
panel get rounder but stop short of one.** That is the whole reason this
is a system rather than a number: a fully rounded text field reads as a
search pill in a form that isn't one, and a fully rounded card stops
looking like a container. Only controls opt all the way in.

`sharp` flattens every corner in the scope to `0`, including panels.

## How it works

Two variables do the work, both on `:root`:

| Variable | Default | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--radius` | `0.625rem` | you, for the base step |
| `--radius-factor` | `1` | the `radius` preset |
| `--radius-full` | `0px` | the `radius` preset, only at `full-rounded` |

Every step is the base multiplied by the factor, so the preset scales the
whole scale rather than replacing it:

| Preset | Factor | `--radius-full` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sharp` | `0` | `0px` |
| `rounded` | `1` | `0px` |
| `full-rounded` | `1.5` | `9999px` |

The pill is a `max()`. `--radius-control` resolves to
`max(step, var(--radius-full))` — normally the step wins because
`--radius-full` is `0px`, and at the `full-rounded` preset the `9999px` wins
instead.

Fields and panels use the same shape with a ceiling wrapped around it:

```css
max(step, min(cap, var(--radius-full)))
```

`min(cap, --radius-full)` is `0px` normally and the cap at `full-rounded`, so they
step up with the preset and stop there. Concretely, at the default base:

| Preset | `control` | `field` | `panel` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sharp` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `rounded` | 8px | 8px | 14px |
| `full-rounded` | pill | 15px | 27px |

The default input is 32px tall, so a pill would be 16px. `field` at
`full-rounded` lands under that on purpose, and a test asserts it.

## Three rules

### 1. Radius is tier × intent

A control's corner is not picked per component. Its **size tier** picks
the step, and its **intent** picks what happens at `full-rounded`:

| Tier | Step | Control (pill at `full-rounded`) | Field (stops one step up) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `xs` (20px) | `--radius-sm` | `--control-xs-radius` | `--control-xs-radius-field` |
| `sm` (24px) | `--radius-sm` | `--control-sm-radius` | `--control-sm-radius-field` |
| `md` (32px) | `--radius-md` | `--control-md-radius` = `--radius-control` | `--control-md-radius-field` = `--radius-field` |

{/* docs:check allow --radius-xs -- the paragraph explains why it does not exist */}

The small tiers take the smaller step because the same corner on a box
two thirds the height reads as a pill. There is no `--radius-xs`: `xs`
parts are small enough that `--radius-sm` already reads as soft. See
[Sizing](?path=/docs/foundations-sizing--docs) for which component reads
which tier.

### 2. Nested corners are the outer corner minus the inset

When a rounded thing sits inside another, with an even inset, its corner
is the container's minus that inset, never its own token:

```css
.menu {
  --menu-inset: var(--space-1);
  padding: var(--menu-inset);
  border-radius: var(--radius-field);
}
.menu-item {
  border-radius: calc(var(--radius-field) - var(--menu-inset));
}
```

At the default that is 8 − 4 = 4px for a menu item, and the pills Tabs
chips are their track's corner minus the 2px track inset. A negative
result clamps to 0, so a square container gets square children. Both
corners then stay concentric at every preset; two independent tokens only
line up at one.

The rule is for concentric shapes. A close button 12px inside a popover's
corner is a free-standing control, not a nested shape, and keeps its own
step.

### 3. Radius scales with `--scaling`

Every step is multiplied by `--scaling`, as padding is. At 110% a 32px
button is 35.2px tall with 13.2px padding, and its 8px corner becomes
8.8px. Without this, the nesting rule above would hold at 100% only:
padding would shrink at 90% while the corners stayed put.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Scaling} />

## Always round: `--radius-pill`

`--radius-pill` is `9999px` at every preset. It is for things that are
round by nature, not by preset: a badge count, an avatar, a switch track,
a slider thumb, a spinner. `--radius-full` is the preset's pill switch:
read directly it is `0` everywhere except `radius="full-rounded"`.

## Intent tokens

What components actually use.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Intent} />

| Token | Used by | Pills at `full-rounded` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--radius-control` | the md tier of Button, ToggleButton, Tabs, Pagination | yes |
| `--radius-field` | the md tier of every field, Select and Combobox lists, menus | no |
| `--radius-panel` | Card, Modal, Popover, the date picker | no |

A new component should pick the intent that matches its shape, not a step.
Getting this wrong is invisible at the default preset and only shows up
when someone sets `radius="full-rounded"` — which is exactly the kind of bug a
token system exists to prevent.

## Steps

The raw scale — `--radius-sm` through `--radius-xl` — for anything that is
genuinely decorative rather than a control, field or panel.

<Canvas of={RadiusStories.Steps} />

These follow the preset like everything else, so a decorative corner in
application code stays in step with the controls beside it.

A genuinely circular element uses `--radius-pill` (see above), not
`--radius-full`.

## Scoping and overriding

Presets nest, and `Theme` takes a `render` prop, so a single component can
opt out without a wrapper element:

```tsx
<Theme radius="full-rounded" render={<Button />}>
  Just this one is a pill
</Theme>
```

For a value the presets don't cover, set the variables directly — `tokens`
is applied after the preset, so it wins:

```tsx
<Theme radius="rounded" tokens={{ 'radius-factor': '2.4' }}>
```

Globally, change the base in CSS and leave the factor to the presets:

```css
:root {
  --radius: 1rem;
}
```

## One caveat about the base

The steps are offsets from the base — `sm` is `base − 4px`, not
`base × 0.6` — so a base far below the default degenerates. At
`--radius: 0.25rem` (4px) the steps are `0 / 2 / 4 / 8px` and `sm`
collapses to a square corner.

The factor does not have this problem, because it multiplies the finished
step. Prefer moving the preset over moving the base, and if the base does
need to change substantially, switch the four `calc()`s in `tokens.css`
from offsets to ratios.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { Theme } from '@/theme/Theme'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

const STEPS = ['2xs', 'xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl', '2xl'] as const

function Swatch({ step }: { step: string }) {
  return (
    // The caption clears the largest step's reach rather than sitting inside
    // it: 2xl extends about 3rem below the box, so a tighter gap puts the
    // label in the shadow and both read as mud.
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', alignItems: 'center', gap: 'var(--space-12)' }}>
      <div
        style={{
          height: '4.5rem',
          width: '4.5rem',
          borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)',
          background: 'var(--card)',
          boxShadow: `var(--shadow-${step})`,
        }}
      />
      <span className={docs.caption}>--shadow-{step}</span>
    </div>
  )
}

function ShadowScale() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.rowWrap} style={{ padding: 'var(--space-6)', gap: 'var(--space-12)' }}>
      {STEPS.map((step) => (
        <Swatch key={step} step={step} />
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Shadows.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Shadows',
  render: () => <ShadowScale />,
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Scale: Story = {}

/** Both appearances at once — the toolbar can only show one at a time. */
export const Modes: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div
      style={{
        display: 'grid',
        gap: 'var(--space-4)',
        gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(auto-fit, minmax(18rem, 1fr))',
      }}
    >
      {(['light', 'dark'] as const).map((appearance) => (
        <Theme
          key={appearance}
          appearance={appearance}
          style={{
            background: 'var(--background)',
            // The light panel is the near-white page, so without this its
            // edge barely shows and the comparison looks one-sided.
            border: '1px solid var(--border)',
            borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)',
            padding: 'var(--space-6)',
          }}
        >
          <div className={docs.caption} style={{ marginBottom: 'var(--space-6)' }}>
            {appearance}
          </div>
          <div className={docs.rowWrap} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-8)' }}>
            {(['xs', 'md', '2xl'] as const).map((step) => (

            ))}

    // The point of the alpha scale: the same token is not the same value in
    // both modes. If someone copies the light values into .dark, this fails.
    const shadows = (['light', 'dark'] as const).map((mode) =>
      getComputedStyle(canvas.getByText(mode).parentElement!).getPropertyValue('--shadow-md').trim(),
    )
    await expect(shadows[0]).not.toBe(shadows[1])
    await expect(shadows.every(Boolean)).toBe(true)
  },
}

# Shadows Seven elevation steps and an off switch. They read as `var(--shadow-2xs)` throug...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ShadowsStories from './Shadows.stories'

<Meta of={ShadowsStories} />

# Shadows

Seven elevation steps and an off switch. They read as `var(--shadow-2xs)`
through `var(--shadow-2xl)`, and each resolves per appearance rather than
being a fixed value.

<Canvas of={ShadowsStories.Scale} />

## The scale is one shape at seven heights

A step is not a blur radius someone liked. Each one is a **height `h`**,
and both of its layers fall out of that number:

```
ambient  0  h     2h    -h/2     the spread of light around a raised object
contact  0  h/2   h     -h/2     the tighter dark where it meets the surface
```

Two layers because one cannot do both jobs. A single soft shadow floats
without touching down; a single tight one reads as a border. The negative
spread pulls both layers in as they rise, which is what keeps a tall step
from bleeding sideways into whatever sits next to it.

| Token | h | Light |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--shadow-none` | — | `0 0 #0000` |
| `--shadow-2xs` | 1 | 1px drop, 3.3% |
| `--shadow-xs` | 2 | 2px + 1px, 3.9% / 2.6% |
| `--shadow-sm` | 4 | 4px + 2px, 5.2% / 3.3% |
| `--shadow-md` | 8 | 8px + 4px, 5.8% / 3.9% |
| `--shadow-lg` | 12 | 12px + 6px, 6.5% / 4.6% |
| `--shadow-xl` | 20 | 20px + 10px, 7.8% / 5.2% |
| `--shadow-2xl` | 32 | 32px + 16px, 10.4% / 6.5% |

The alphas are deliberately faint: a panel separates from the page by
being lighter (white on the gray-50 page) and by its border, so a shadow
is reserved for things that genuinely float — menus, popovers, dialogs.

`h` doubles through the lower steps and eases off at the top, because the
difference between 1px and 2px of lift is legible and the difference
between 40px and 48px is not.

`--shadow-none` exists so that turning elevation off is a token rather
than a literal. `box-shadow: none` also works, but it cannot be swapped by
a `Theme` and it breaks a transition between two shadow states — `0 0
#0000` interpolates, `none` does not.

## Dark mode is derived, not retyped

Only the light values are written down. The dark ones are **computed from
them**: every alpha is multiplied by 4 and clamped at 0.6.

<Canvas of={ShadowsStories.Modes} />

Look at the dark half. The shadows are nearly invisible, and multiplying
the alpha by four is not what fixes it — nothing fixes it. Here is the
measurement, sampling the darkest pixel each shadow can produce:

| | Page | Darkest shadow pixel | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Light, `--shadow-md` | 255 | 232 | **23 levels** |
| Light, `--shadow-2xl` | 255 | 214 | **41 levels** |
| Dark, `--shadow-md` | 10 | 6 | **4 levels** |
| Dark, `--shadow-2xl` | 10 | 4 | **6 levels** |

A drop shadow works by darkening what is under it. The dark page is
already at 10 of 255, so **the entire budget is 10 levels** — even a
pure-black shadow at full opacity could not do better. Light mode has 255
to spend. That is a 25× difference in available range, and no choice of
alpha closes it.

So the multiplier is not rescuing dark mode; it is spending a small budget
well rather than leaving it unspent. What actually carries elevation in
dark mode is the surface: `--card` sits at **23** against a background of
**10**, a 13-level lift — two to three times stronger than any shadow on
this page.

**In dark mode, surface lightness is the primary elevation signal and the
shadow is a secondary cue.** In light mode it is the other way around. If
you are building a floating surface and it does not read as raised in dark
mode, reach for a lighter surface token, not a heavier shadow.

The **clamp** at 0.6 is therefore housekeeping rather than tuning — it
stops a large light alpha from generating a nonsensical dark one, and
between `--shadow-2xl` uncapped and capped there is about one level in it.

Deriving rather than retyping closes a different gap. When both modes were
written by hand there were fourteen numbers and nothing checking that they
told the same story; editing a step meant remembering to edit its twin.
Now editing a step edits both, and the `Modes` story asserts the two did
not collapse into the same value — set the multiplier to 1 and that test
fails.

## Who uses them

Controls are flat: Button, Text Input and the rest carry borders, not
shadows. **Card** is the first surface on the scale — `elevated` rests on
`--shadow-sm` and lifts to `--shadow-md` on hover when clickable. The
remaining steps are for the surfaces still to come (popover, dropdown,
modal, toast), documented now so they adopt a shared scale instead of each
inventing a `box-shadow`.

That also means the steps are **untested against real components.** The
geometry is consistent, but consistent is not the same as tuned. Treat
them as a starting point to adjust when the first floating surface lands.

## A note on rings and shadows

`box-shadow` is a single property, so a shadow and a focus ring drawn the
same way would overwrite each other — which is why systems that draw rings
with `box-shadow` need machinery to compose the two.

The kit sidesteps it: focus is drawn with `outline`, which has its own
property and its own `outline-offset`, and current browsers follow
`border-radius` with it. An elevated surface can carry a shadow and a
focus ring at once, and neither needs to know about the other.

## What is not here

**Inset shadows.** For recessed wells and pressed states. They are a real
gap, but the kit has no recessed surface and no pressed treatment yet, so
they would be a step nothing reads — and this page already carries seven
of those. Add them as `elevation-inset-*` in `tokens/semantic.json` when
the first one lands; the alpha derivation applies unchanged.

**Coloured shadows.** A shadow tinted toward the accent instead of black.
Worth having, but it needs a real decision about which token it reads and
how it behaves in dark mode, not a mechanical port.

## Customization

The raw values are `--elevation-none` through `--elevation-2xl` in `:root`
and `.dark`; the `*` block maps them onto `--shadow-*` and does not need to
change.

Change a step by editing `tokens/semantic.json` and running `npm run
tokens` — light and dark regenerate together. Overriding `--shadow-md`
directly on a `Theme` scope also works and skips the derivation, which is
the right tool for a one-off surface and the wrong one for changing the
scale.

'use client'
import { useLayoutEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { Button } from '@/components/buttons/Button'
import { Select } from '@/components/inputs/Select'
import { TextInput } from '@/components/inputs/TextInput'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

const TIERS = ['xs', 'sm', 'md'] as const

/* Each cell is a token, read back in pixels: a probe element takes the token
   as a length and the table shows what it resolves to here, so the numbers
   follow the Theme's scaling and radius preset and are never retyped. */
const ROWS = [
  { label: 'Height', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}`, prop: 'inlineSize' },
  { label: 'Padding, pad', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}-pad`, prop: 'inlineSize' },
  { label: 'Padding, pad-spacious', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}-pad-spacious`, prop: 'inlineSize' },
  { label: 'Gap, icon to label', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}-gap`, prop: 'inlineSize' },
  { label: 'Icon', token: (t: string) => `--icon-${t}`, prop: 'inlineSize' },
  { label: 'Radius, control', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}-radius`, prop: 'borderTopLeftRadius' },
  { label: 'Radius, field', token: (t: string) => `--control-${t}-radius-field`, prop: 'borderTopLeftRadius' },
] as const

/* Reads every [data-probe] in the table once it is laid out, keyed by its
   probe name. data-prop names the CSS property to read (inlineSize if unset). */
function useProbes() {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null)
  const [values, setValues] = useState<Record<string, string>>({})

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const read: Record<string, string> = {}
    for (const probe of ref.current!.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-probe]')) {
      const value = getComputedStyle(probe)[(probe.dataset.prop ?? 'inlineSize') as 'inlineSize']
      // A pill radius computes to 9999px; say what it means.
      read[probe.dataset.probe!] = Number.parseFloat(value) > 1000 ? 'pill' : value
    }
    setValues(read)
  }, [])

  return { ref, values }
}

function TierTable() {
  const { ref, values } = useProbes()

  return (
    <table ref={ref} className={docs.tokenTable}>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>Property</th>
          {TIERS.map((t) => (
            <th key={t}>
              <code>{t}</code>
            </th>
          ))}
          <th>Token</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {ROWS.map((row) => (
          <tr key={row.label}>
            <td>{row.label}</td>
            {TIERS.map((t) => (
              <td key={t} data-token={row.token(t)}>
                <span
                  data-probe={row.token(t)}
                  data-prop={row.prop}
                  aria-hidden="true"
                  style={{
                    position: 'absolute',
                    visibility: 'hidden',
                    [row.prop]: `var(${row.token(t)})`,
                  }}
                />
                <code>{values[row.token(t)]}</code>
              </td>
            ))}
            <td>
              <code>{row.token('{tier}')}</code>
            </td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  )
}

const STEPS = ['2xs', 'xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'] as const
const DENSITIES = ['default', 'compact'] as const

/* The ramp in both densities at once: each column's probes sit inside their
   own [data-density], so the table never depends on the toolbar. */
function BoxRampTable() {
  const { ref, values } = useProbes()

  return (
    <table ref={ref} className={docs.tokenTable}>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>Step</th>
          {DENSITIES.map((d) => (
            <th key={d}>{d === 'default' ? 'Default' : 'Compact'}</th>
          ))}
          <th>Token</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {STEPS.map((step) => (
          <tr key={step}>
            <td>
              <code>{step}</code>
            </td>
            {DENSITIES.map((d) => (
              <td key={d} data-density={d} data-token={`--box-${step}@${d}`}>
                <span
                  data-probe={`--box-${step}@${d}`}
                  aria-hidden="true"
                  style={{ position: 'absolute', visibility: 'hidden', inlineSize: `var(--box-${step})` }}
                />
                <code>{values[`--box-${step}@${d}`]}</code>
              </td>
            ))}
            <td>
              <code>--box-{step}</code>
            </td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  )
}

function SmallControls() {
  return (
    <div className={docs.row} style={{ flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
      <Button size="sm" startIcon={<Icon name="plus" />}>
        Button
      </Button>
      <TextInput size="sm" aria-label="Text input" placeholder="Text input" prefix={<Icon name="search" />} />
      <Select size="sm" aria-label="Select" placeholder="Select" options={['One', 'Two']} />
    </div>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Sizing.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Sizing',
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Tiers: Story = {
  render: () => <TierTable />,
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const value = (name: string) => canvasElement.querySelector(`[data-token="${name}"] code`)!.textContent
    await expect(value('--control-xs')).toBe('20px')
    await expect(value('--control-sm')).toBe('24px')
    await expect(value('--control-md')).toBe('32px')
    await expect(value('--icon-xs')).toBe('12px')
    await expect(value('--icon-sm')).toBe('14px')
    await expect(value('--icon-md')).toBe('16px')
    await expect(value('--control-md-pad')).toBe('10px')
    await expect(value('--control-md-pad-spacious')).toBe('12px')
  },
}

export const BoxRamp: Story = {
  render: () => <BoxRampTable />,
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const column = (d: string) =>
      STEPS.map((step) => canvasElement.querySelector(`[data-token="--box-${step}@${d}"] code`)!.textContent)
    await expect(column('default')).toEqual(['16px', '20px', '24px', '32px', '40px', '48px'])
    await expect(column('compact')).toEqual(['16px', '20px', '22px', '28px', '36px', '44px'])
  },
}

/* The point of a tier: a Button, a text field and a select of the same size
   carry the same icon, corner and type, whoever built them. */
export const SameTier: Story = {
  render: () => <SmallControls />,
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const button = canvasElement.querySelector('button:not([role="combobox"])')!
    const field = canvasElement.querySelector('input')!.parentElement!
    const select = canvasElement.querySelector('[role="combobox"]')!
    const parts = [button, field, select]
    const iconOf = (el: Element) => el.querySelector('svg')!.getBoundingClientRect().width
    const style = (el: Element) => getComputedStyle(el)

    for (const el of parts) {
      await expect(el.getBoundingClientRect().height).toBe(24)
      await expect(iconOf(el)).toBe(14)
      await expect(style(el).fontSize).toBe(style(button).fontSize)
      await expect(style(el).borderTopLeftRadius).toBe(style(button).borderTopLeftRadius)
    }
  },
}

# Sizing Every control's geometry comes from two facts: its **size tier** and its **intent...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SizingStories from './Sizing.stories'

<Meta of={SizingStories} />

# Sizing

Every control's geometry comes from two facts: its **size tier** and its
**intent**. The tier binds height, inline padding, the gap between icon and
label, the icon and the corner. The intent (control or field) decides two
things only: which padding it takes, and whether it becomes a pill at
`radius="full-rounded"`.

<Canvas of={SizingStories.Tiers} />

The table reads each token back from the page, so it shows what the
current scaling and radius preset resolve to. Every length here, the
radius included, is multiplied by `--scaling`.

## The box ramp

Every element is a box, and every box with a fixed height or a fixed
square stands on a step of one ramp. The same role always takes the same
step, so a close button is 24px in a Modal and in a Toast, and a nav
item is as tall as the button beside it.

<Canvas of={SizingStories.BoxRamp} />

`md` (32px) is the default. Density maps the whole ramp with one rule:
16 and 20 stay, every larger step drops one notch (24 to 22, 32 to 28,
40 to 36, 48 to 44). The control tiers below are the ramp's `xs`, `sm`
and `md` under another name.

### Which step a role takes

| Role | Step | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The default control: field, button, tab, pagination and menu item, calendar day, an icon button in the app frame (sidebar toggle, carousel arrows), a nav item | `md` | 32px |
| A small inline control; a close button inside a surface (Modal, Popover, Toast, Alert); the small Stepper marker; the medium spinner | `sm` | 24px |
| Small parts: Tag `size="sm"`, the slider thumb, the checkbox and radio box, Badge `md`, Kbd `md`, a file icon | `xs` | 20px |
| A mark that sits with a glyph: Badge `sm`, Kbd `sm`, the small slider thumb, the small spinner, a skeleton line | `2xs` | 16px |
| A leading visual: Avatar `md`, the small EmptyState icon | `lg` | 40px |
| A large visual: Avatar `lg`, the Stats icon, the EmptyState icon | `xl` | 48px |
| A glyph inside a control | `--icon-{tier}` | 12 / 14 / 16px |
| A line of text, and an icon beside it | `--leading-*` × `--text-*` | one line |
| A table or list row | `box-md` + 2 × `--space-inline` | 48px |

The rules that go with the table:

- **A component picks the step by role.** Whoever uses the component
  picks only its `size`, and `size` points at a step.
- **Composite boxes take no free number.** A row, a Tag or a top bar is
  the box inside it plus a spacing role on each side: `--row-height` is
  `box-md` plus `--space-inline` above and below (48 / 36px). Text boxes
  are a line tall (`--leading-*` × `--text-*`); an icon beside text sits
  in a box one line tall.
- **A box that grows with its content** uses `min-block-size` at a step,
  never `block-size`.
- **A box with a fixed size and padding or a border declares
  `box-sizing: border-box` itself.** The kit ships no global reset, so
  the app's own CSS decides the default.

Off the ramp, each for a reason: 1–2px strokes, dots and bars under
12px (radio dot, Badge dot, progress bar), switch track widths, region
sizes (ColorPicker, a vertical Slider, overlay widths), the 44px touch
target and icons sized in `em` inside text. `npm run tokens` stops when a
control, size or row token leaves the ramp of its density without a
listed reason, and when `--row-height` stops being the sum above.

## Who reads which tier

| Tier | Height (Default / Compact) | Components |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `md` | 32 / 28px | the default: Button, ToggleButton, every field (TextInput, Search, Select, Combobox, NumberInput, DatePicker, Textarea), Tabs, Pagination, Menu item |
| `sm` | 24 / 22px | the small inline size of the same components, Tag `size="md"`, and the Menubar trigger |
| `xs` | 20 / 20px | compact parts only: Tag `size="sm"`, the slider thumb |

Density keeps every tier and tightens each; see
[Spacing](?path=/docs/foundations-spacing--docs#density). The checkbox and
radio box, the switch tracks, Badge and Avatar have their own size tokens
(`--choice-box`, `--switch-md-w`, `--badge-md`, `--avatar-md`), which follow
density too.

A component's `size` prop points at a tier; the names need not match.
Tag `size="md"` reads tier `sm`, because a tag sits in a line of text and
a 32px tag would push it apart.

**Buttons and fields have no `xs`.** A 20px button reads as a part,
not a control.

**The 24px floor is for the hit area, not the drawn box.** WCAG 2.5.8
asks for a 24×24px target. A box drawn smaller (Compact `sm` is 22px, the
checkbox 20px) keeps its look and widens its hit area to 24px with a
`::before`. On touch screens every tier grows its hit area to
`--target-coarse` (44px) the same way, without growing the visible box.

## Intent

**Padding.** Fields and rows take `pad`, because their text is left
aligned and has to line up with the label above it. Buttons take
`pad-spacious`: a centred label reads as cramped with less. The two only
differ at `md` (10 against 12px); at `sm` and `xs` there is no room to
spend.

**Radius.** The tier picks the step (`--radius-sm` for `xs` and `sm`,
`--radius-md` for `md`, so a short box does not read as a pill by
accident). The intent picks what happens at `radius="full-rounded"`:
`--control-{tier}-radius` becomes a pill, `--control-{tier}-radius-field`
stops one step up. At `md` these are exactly `--radius-control` and
`--radius-field`. See [Radius](?path=/docs/foundations-radius--docs).

<Canvas of={SizingStories.SameTier} />

A Button, a text field and a select at `size="sm"`: one height, one icon,
one corner, one type size. The story asserts all four.

## Why these gaps

The gap grows with the tier: 4, 6, 8px. Before tiers each component chose
its own, and they disagreed at the small size: Button and the field put
8px between icon and label, Tag put 4px. `md` keeps the 8px every default
control already had, so the size most of an interface uses does not move.
`sm` takes the step between, 6px, which is the one change: small buttons
and fields tighten by 2px, and a medium Tag loosens by 2px.

## The one exception

NumberInput's stepper at `sm` is a 16px button inside the field, so its
chevron stays at `--icon-xs` (12px). A 14px chevron would fill it edge to
edge.

import { DENSITIES } from '@/theme/Theme'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

const ROLES = ['stack', 'inline', 'cluster', 'group', 'container', 'section']

/* Each role as a bar, once per density. The bars read the tokens inside a
   [data-density] scope, so they show what the stylesheet resolves. */
function RoleBars() {
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(auto-fit, minmax(14rem, 1fr))', gap: 'var(--space-container)' }}>
      {DENSITIES.map((density) => (
        <div key={density} data-density={density} className={docs.stack}>
          <strong className={docs.caption}>{density === 'default' ? 'Default' : 'Compact'}</strong>
          {ROLES.map((role) => (
            <div key={role} className={docs.row}>
              <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '5rem', flexShrink: 0 }}>
                {role}
              </span>
              <div
                style={{
                  height: '1rem',
                  borderRadius: 'var(--radius-sm)',
                  background: 'var(--primary)',
                  width: `var(--space-${role})`,
                }}
              />
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Spacing.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Spacing',
  render: () => <RoleBars />,
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Roles: Story = {}

# Spacing Pick a spacing token by **what the gap does**, not by its size. Six roles cover ...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SpacingStories from './Spacing.stories'

<Meta of={SpacingStories} />

# Spacing

Pick a spacing token by **what the gap does**, not by its size. Six roles
cover every gap and pad in the kit; a **density**, Default or Compact,
decides the number behind each one. A designer never chooses between 12
and 16 pixels: they choose `--space-cluster` or `--space-group`, and the
product's density does the rest.

<Canvas of={SpacingStories.Roles} />

## The six roles

| Token | Use for | Default | Compact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--space-stack` | Lines of text under each other: title to description, label to value | 4 | 2 |
| `--space-inline` | Small things side by side: icon to text, label to value on one line, sidebar items | 8 | 4 |
| `--space-cluster` | Controls or parts that sit together: filters in a toolbar, an avatar to its content, the parts of a page heading, inside a small card | 12 | 8 |
| `--space-group` | Items and blocks that belong together: cards in a row, toolbar to table, table cell sides | 16 | 12 |
| `--space-container` | Inside the edge of a card, panel or page heading | 24 | 16 |
| `--space-section` | Page edge and between page sections | 24 | 20 |

The scale is short on purpose: 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. In Compact each
role takes the Default value of the role below it; only section steps
24 to 20. Section and container share 24px in Default, so separate
sections with a card edge or a rule, not with extra white space. AppShell
applies `--space-section` to the page edge from 64rem up; below that the
edge stays at its narrow value.

The numeric steps (`--space-1` to `--space-12`) still exist for the few
places no role fits, such as the size of an icon disc. They do not follow
density.

## Density

Density changes four things together, and keeps every size:

- **The six roles**, as in the table above.
- **The control tier.** Every tier exists in both densities. Compact
  gives each tier the padding and gap of the tier below it; md drops from
  32 to 28px, sm from 24 to 22px, xs stays at 20px (the floor of its text).
- **Type.** Body text is 14px in Default and 13px in Compact. Text of 12px
  and below never shrinks; 13 to 16px drops 1px; headings from 20px up
  drop one step. Compact body leading is 13/18, off the 4px grid on
  purpose. See [Typography](?path=/docs/foundations-typography--docs).
- **Component sizes**: the checkbox and radio box (`--choice-box`, 20 to
  16), the radio dot, the three switch tracks, the progress bar heights,
  avatars xs to lg (`--avatar-md`, 40 to 32), badge heights and dots, and
  table rows (`--row-height`, 48 to 36). In Compact each size takes the
  size below it; the smallest switch, avatar and badge step down further
  so sizes stay apart.

| Control token | md (D / C) | sm (D / C) | xs (D / C) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--control-{tier}` height | 32 / 28 | 24 / 22 | 20 / 20 |
| `--control-{tier}-pad` (fields, rows) | 10 / 8 | 8 / 6 | 6 / 4 |
| `--control-{tier}-pad-spacious` (buttons) | 12 / 8 | 8 / 6 | 6 / 4 |
| `--control-{tier}-gap` (icon to label) | 8 / 6 | 6 / 4 | 4 / 2 |

A small control inside a component (a table's sort button, a modal's
close button, a badge, the number input's steppers) reads the control tier
of its own size, like any other control, not a spacing role.

## Setting it

Density is set like appearance: on the root of the app, through `Theme`.

```tsx
<Theme density="compact">
  <App />
</Theme>
```

`Theme` writes `data-density` on its element, and every token picks its
number from the nearest one. A nested `Theme density="default"` inside a
compact app gets Default back. Popups portal to `<body>`, so set density
at the root; for a compact panel inside a default page, pass the panel
element as `container` to Popover, Menu, Tooltip, Modal, Select, Combobox
and DatePicker so their popups render inside it.

Density and `scaling` are independent. Scaling multiplies every size by
one factor (12px becomes 11.2px at 93%); density picks each number,
keeps whole pixels and holds the 12px floor. Both can be set at once.

In Storybook, the **Density** toolbar switches every story between the two.

## Touch and rem

Controls are below the 44px touch minimum in both densities on purpose:
on coarse pointers every control widens its hit area to 44px without
growing the box, so Compact does not cost touch users. Every value is in
`rem`, so it follows the user's root font size; "32px" is 32px at the
default 16px root.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import type { CSSProperties } from 'react'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

/** A type role is a size, a line height and a weight together. */
const role = (name: string, weight: number): CSSProperties => ({
  fontSize: `var(--text-${name})`,
  lineHeight: `var(--leading-${name})`,
  fontWeight: weight,
})

const HEADINGS = [
  { token: 'heading-2xl', px: '32 / 36' },
  { token: 'heading-xl', px: '28 / 32' },
  { token: 'heading-lg', px: '24 / 28' },
  { token: 'heading-md', px: '20 / 24' },
  { token: 'heading-sm', px: '16 / 20' },
  { token: 'heading-xs', px: '14 / 20' },
  { token: 'heading-2xs', px: '12 / 16' },
] as const

const BODY = [
  { token: 'body-lg', px: '16 / 24' },
  { token: 'body', px: '14 / 20' },
  { token: 'body-sm', px: '12 / 16' },
  { token: 'body-xs', px: '11 / 16' },
] as const

function Row({ token, px, weight }: { token: string; px: string; weight: number }) {
  return (
    <div
      className={docs.rowBaseline}
      style={{ borderBottom: '1px solid var(--border)', padding: 'var(--space-2) 0' }}
    >
      <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '10rem', flexShrink: 0 }}>
        --text-{token}
      </span>
      <span style={{ flex: 1, ...role(token, weight) }}>Zweihänder</span>
      <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '7rem', textAlign: 'right' }}>
        {px}
      </span>
    </div>
  )
}

const WEIGHTS = [
  { value: 400, name: 'regular' },
  { value: 500, name: 'medium' },
  { value: 600, name: 'semibold' },
  { value: 700, name: 'bold' },
] as const

// Narrative and prose live in Typography.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Typography',
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Headings: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column' }}>
      {HEADINGS.map((h) => (
        <Row key={h.token} {...h} weight={700} />
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const el = canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder')[0]
    // A heading role carries its weight, not just its size.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(el).fontWeight).toBe('700')
    await expect(Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize)).toBe(32)
  },
}

export const Body: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column' }}>
      {BODY.map((b) => (
        <Row key={b.token} {...b} weight={400} />
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const el = canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder')[1]
    // body is 14px, one step down from the 16px many interfaces start at.
    await expect(Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize)).toBe(14)
    // Every body line sits on the 4px grid at 100% scaling.
    for (const sample of canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder')) {
      await expect(Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(sample).lineHeight) % 4).toBeCloseTo(0, 5)
    }
  },
}

export const Weights: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.stack}>
      {WEIGHTS.map(({ value, name }) => (
        <div key={value} className={docs.rowBaseline}>
          <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '8rem', flexShrink: 0 }}>
            {value}
          </span>
          <span style={{ ...role('body-lg', value) }}>Zweihänder</span>
          <span className={docs.caption}>{name}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const bold = canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder').at(-1)!
    await expect(getComputedStyle(bold).fontWeight).toBe('700')
  },
}

export const Families: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.stackWide}>
      <div className={docs.stack}>
        <span className={docs.caption}>--font-sans</span>
        <span style={{ ...role('heading-md', 700), fontFamily: 'var(--font-sans)' }}>
          Zweihänder — system-ui 0123
        </span>
      </div>
      <div className={docs.stack}>
        <span className={docs.caption}>--font-mono</span>
        <span style={{ ...role('heading-md', 700), fontFamily: 'var(--font-mono)' }}>
          Zweihänder — ui-monospace 0123
        </span>
      </div>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const sans = canvas.getByText(/system-ui 0123/)
    await expect(getComputedStyle(sans).fontFamily).toMatch(/^system-ui/)
  },
}

# Typography Type is **role-based**: you reach for `--text-heading-lg` or `--text-body`, n...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TypographyStories from './Typography.stories'

<Meta of={TypographyStories} />

# Typography

Type is **role-based**: you reach for `--text-heading-lg` or `--text-body`,
not a size. Each role carries its size, line height and weight together, so a
heading cannot end up at body weight or a body line height by omission.

The alternative — a purely dimensional scale, where a name says how big and
never what it is for — is what this replaces. Each role is three variables
that belong together:

```css
.heading {
  font-size: var(--text-heading-lg);
  line-height: var(--leading-heading-lg);
  font-weight: 700;
}
```

## The typeface

One face: the platform UI font. Nothing is downloaded, and text looks the
way the rest of the operating system does — San Francisco on Apple, Segoe UI
on Windows, Roboto on Android.

```css
--font-sans: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …
--font-mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, …
```

Components read two role tokens rather than the face directly, so a
product can give headings or prose their own face without touching a
component:

| Role | Default | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--font-heading` | `var(--font-sans)` | Page titles, `Modal` and `EmptyState` titles |
| `--font-prose` | `var(--font-sans)` | long-form reading text; no component reads it yet |

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Families} />

**There is nothing to load.** To use a brand face instead, load it yourself
and point the tokens at it (see **Customization**).

## Headings

Seven steps, all bold. The line height tightens as the size grows, which
is the thing a single ratio applied across a whole scale gets wrong.

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Headings} />

| Role | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--text-heading-2xl` | 2rem / 32px | 36px |
| `--text-heading-xl` | 1.75rem / 28px | 32px |
| `--text-heading-lg` | 1.5rem / 24px | 28px |
| `--text-heading-md` | 1.25rem / 20px | 24px |
| `--text-heading-sm` | 1rem / 16px | 20px |
| `--text-heading-xs` | 0.875rem / 14px | 20px |
| `--text-heading-2xs` | 0.75rem / 12px | 16px |

Note that headings go *below* body size: `--text-heading-2xs` is 12px. Those
bottom steps are for labels and section eyebrows — a heading role is about
the semantic weight of the text, not about being large.

## Body

Four steps. `--text-body` is the default at 14px — one step down from the
16px a lot of interfaces start at, which is deliberate for dense product
UI and worth knowing before you reach for it in long-form content.

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Body} />

| Role | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--text-body-lg` | 1rem / 16px | 24px |
| `--text-body` | 0.875rem / 14px | 20px |
| `--text-body-sm` | 0.75rem / 12px | 16px |
| `--text-body-xs` | 0.6875rem / 11px | 16px |

**Every component uses these.** Button, the field label, the input itself,
and the helper and error text are all `--text-body`; only the large Button
steps up to `--text-body-lg`.

`--text-body-sm` is the label of every small control (the `sm` and `xs`
size tiers, see [Sizing](?path=/docs/foundations-sizing--docs)), and
secondary text: helper text in a menu, shortcuts, captions.

`--text-body-xs` is for dense metadata only: badge counts, timestamps,
table footnotes. Badge is the one component that reads it. Nothing a user
has to read in full or act on belongs at 11px.

Every body line height is a multiple of 4px (24, 20, 16, 16), so body text
of any size sits on the same 4px grid as the spacing and control heights.

## Weights

Four. Anything outside this set is not part of the system.

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Weights} />

| Weight | Value |
| --- | --- |
| regular | 400 |
| medium | 500 |
| semibold | 600 |
| bold | 700 |

{/* docs:check allow --font-weight-medium -- the paragraph explains why weights are not tokens */}

Weight is written directly rather than tokenised — there are four of them
and they are the same four everywhere, so a `--font-weight-medium`
indirection would buy nothing. Button is `--text-body` at `font-weight:
500`; the role supplies the size and line height, the rule supplies the
weight.

With a system stack, the weight you ask for is not guaranteed to be a
drawn face: where one is missing the browser synthesises it, and
synthesised weights look noticeably worse. 400 and 500 are safe
everywhere; verify 600 on the platforms you support.

## Scaling

Every size above is `calc(<base> * var(--scaling))`, so the
[`scaling`](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs) setting moves type and
spacing together. Line heights are stored as *ratios* — `calc(20 / 14)`
rather than `1.25rem` — so they follow the font size instead of having to
be rescaled themselves.

The 4px grid above holds at 100% only. At 110% a 16px line is 17.6px: the
ratio keeps type in proportion to the controls around it, which matters
more than whole pixels, and it is the trade-off Radix Themes makes too.

## What is not here

**A metric role for large figures.** Its sizes would be identical to three
of the heading steps; the real difference is tabular figures, which
`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` already covers. There is no stat
component yet, so it would be a role nothing reads.

**A code role.** Same size as `--text-body-sm`, differing only by family.
`var(--font-mono)` covers it until a Code component exists.

## Customization

The family is a token like any other:

```css
:root {
  --font-sans: 'Geist Variable', system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-heading: 'Newsreader Variable', Georgia, serif; /* serif headings */
}
```

Every rule that reads `var(--font-sans)` picks it up with no component
change — which is all of them, because components set the family
explicitly rather than inheriting it from the page. Re-check the weights when you do — a real typeface
usually ships fewer weights than the four above, or different ones.

To move the scale itself rather than the face, override the role tokens
directly — each is a `--text-<role>` and its `--leading-<role>` partner.

interface Project {
  id: string

  owner: string
  status: 'Active' | 'Paused' | 'Archived'
  files: number
  updated: Date
}

const projects: Project[] = [

  { id: 'p2', name: 'Billing revamp', owner: 'Mia Chen', status: 'Paused', files: 38, updated: new Date('2026-08-02') },
