# Templates

Page frames and whole pages, assembled from Patterns and Components
(atomic design's "templates"). Where a pattern is one section of a screen, a template is
the screen: an app shell, a heading, a toolbar and the content, wired
together on sample data so you can click through it.

Templates are meant to be **copied and edited**, like Patterns. They ship
through the registry only, not the npm package: install one and its files
land in your project, next to the patterns and components it uses, as
code you own.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/projects-template.json
```

Each template is one React component plus a sample data file. The state
(tabs, search, sort, selection) is local, so it runs as it is; replace the
data and the handlers with your own source when you copy it. Every
template is checked for accessibility in light and dark mode, like any
component.

## Application frame

| Template | Shows | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) | The frame of an app: places the Top Bar, Nav Sidebar and App Content patterns on the Theme's canvas, in a sidebar or top-bar layout | ✅ |
| [Home](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-home--docs) | The page an app opens on: a greeting and a period, key figures, a chart and your tasks in cards, recent activity in the aside, and a setup guide while the workspace is new | ✅ |
| [Settings](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-settings--docs) | The user's settings: a Vertical Nav of sections beside the one shown (above it on a phone), Form Sections with a save bar that stays in view, change password, and a Delete account danger zone | ✅ |

## Auth

| Template | Shows | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-in--docs) | Email and password in the Auth Layout, the frame every auth screen shares: single sign-on, Show / Hide, Keep me signed in, Forgot password, Sign up, in a card, plain or beside a panel | ✅ |
| [Sign Up](?path=/docs/templates-auth-sign-up--docs) | Full name, email and a new password with its rules ticked off as you type, in the Auth Layout: single sign-on, a terms checkbox, Sign in | ✅ |
| [Forgot Password](?path=/docs/templates-auth-forgot-password--docs) | The email, then "Check your email" with Resend link and Use a different email; and Reset Password, the page the link opens: a new password with its rules, then Password changed | ✅ |
| [Progressive Sign In](?path=/docs/templates-auth-progressive-sign-in--docs) | The email first, then a password (the email with Change) or the account's single sign-on provider, as `onContinue` decides; Remember my email | ✅ |
| [MFA Challenge](?path=/docs/templates-auth-mfa-challenge--docs) | The second step of signing in: a one-time code from an authenticator app, a text message or an email with Resend code, Remember this device, Try another way and a backup code | ✅ |

## Object Management

| Template | Shows | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Projects](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-projects--docs) | An index page (list report): saved views, search and filters, a paged table or a chart, sort, columns, bulk archive, a row's activity | ✅ |
| [Project Detail](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-project-detail--docs) | One project: breadcrumb, header with status and actions, tabs, a summary and activity aside, an Edit drawer | ✅ |

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Internal/Docs blocks demo" />

# Docs blocks demo

The blocks a component docs page is built from, each in use on Button, so
every one can be checked here in light, dark and at phone width. This page
is not Button's docs; it passes the same `docs:check` a migrated page must.

Import them in a component's MDX:

```js
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
```

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Overview: what the component is, its main example, its variants, and where
to get it. `<Canvas>` is Storybook's own block.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Default} />

## Resources

`<DocTabs>` takes exactly three `<DocTab>` children: `overview`, `specs`,
`guidelines`, in that order. The selected tab is kept in the address bar as
`&docTab=specs`, so a link can open on it.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

`<Anatomy>` takes the real component as children and a list of parts, each
found by a CSS selector inside it. A selector that finds nothing is called
out in the key.

<Anatomy
  parts={[
    { name: 'Container', selector: 'button', description: 'The box: fill, border and label colour.' },
    { name: 'Start icon', selector: 'svg', description: 'Decorative, sized to the button.' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ButtonStories.WithIcons} />
</Anatomy>

## Measurements

`<SpecTable>` reads each token's value from the CSS as the page renders, so
the numbers cannot drift from the code.

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad-spacious' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad-spacious' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="primary, contained"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--primary' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--primary-foreground' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--ring' },
  ]}
/>

## States

`<States>` shows one example per state. Hover, focus and pressed are forced
by storybook-addon-pseudo-states; a state that needs other props, like
disabled, passes its own `content`.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={ButtonStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ButtonStories.Default} />
</States>

## API

Storybook's `<ArgTypes>`, from each prop's `argTypes.description` in the
stories file.

<ArgTypes of={ButtonStories} />

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

`<DoDont>` sets a right and a wrong example side by side. In a real page both
come from stories (`<Story of={…} />`), the Don't one tagged `!dev`.

## When not to use

These blocks are for component docs. Foundations and Patterns stay single
pages.

<DoDont
  do={<Button>Save</Button>}
  doCaption="One primary button: the thing to do next."
  dont={
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--space-2)' }}>
      <Button>Save</Button>
      <Button>Publish</Button>
    </div>
  }
  dontCaption="Two primary buttons compete for the same click."
/>

## Accessibility

Each block's own behaviour is tested in `DocBlocks.stories.tsx`: the tabs by
mouse and arrow keys, the anatomy markers by name, the token values across
themes, the state labels, and the Do / Don't words.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>
